This part is the real paid content!
I said it's paid content. Do you really still want to see it?
...Hmph.

(You thought you might see some incredible secret, but the content that appears on the screen does not seem particularly riveting. What you see is a long reading list, spanning a broad range of fields from pharmaceutical manufacturing, to precision industry, to civil engineering, to interior design. You know these are all things she has read. No one starts out as a multidisciplinary engineering expert, not even an unconventional Vampire, and Closure most likely really did spend a considerable amount of money on these journals, magazines, and books, or at least their digital editions. Looking further down, you also see all manner of experimental equipment she has purchased. It really is quite a sizable expense, you think, sighing as you scroll the list straight to the bottom.)

Payment Successful...

(?)

...You have spent 180,000 LMD via ZOOT Pay.
archives:
This document contains paid content and is currently locked. Please contact Closure to purchase reading access.

If you actually pay, she will refund your money, then show you the main text. If you find Closure—assuming you can catch her—she will readily admit that charging fees violates Rhodes Island regulations, then show you the main text.
If you neither pay nor manage to find her, but still somehow see the main text, she will appear behind you of her own accord, interrogate you on how you did it, then spend several nights fixing the security flaws.
—■■■

(After that, the head of HR readily told you several methods she knew for bypassing the lock. You chose one of them and successfully viewed the locked content. However, while you were browsing, a desktop pet shaped like a drone appeared on your screen. You cannot close it, and every so often, it pops up little speech bubbles saying things like 'You cheat!' and 'Pay your fine!'... But Closure never cut off your connection to this file in the end.)

Without a doubt, Closure is one of the most senior old-timers aboard Rhodes Island.
Generally speaking, old-timers often develop impressive quirks, such as Warfarin and Medical's late-night horror stories. Compared to that, Closure is fairly normal. What she does generally does not exceed the scope of her duties as Chief Engineer and head of the Procurement Department.
It is worth noting that while Kal'tsit was absent, Closure also had to make the final call on important decisions for Rhodes Island's various departments (usually excluding Medical). This part of her responsibilities has indeed been lightened after Kal'tsit's return, but a considerable portion of them continues to fall to her for various reasons. Closure is rather conflicted about this: even to an outsider, the work of Engineering and Procurement is already heavy enough, but beneath that glib exterior, her sense of responsibility makes it difficult for her to toss these burdens back to Kal'tsit, who has only recently returned.
Still, why Closure, of all people, became one of Rhodes Island's old-timers, and why she holds such an uncharacteristic sense of responsibility toward Rhodes Island, remains an interesting question. We could certainly trace it back to the day Theresa opened the door to her room. We could say her intense curiosity drove her to follow in the footsteps of Babel, Theresa, and even the Doctor. We could also attribute it to the deep bonds she formed over a long period of time with members of Babel or Rhodes Island. Another part of the reason is clearly that being at Rhodes Island gives her access to a great deal of advanced technology that ordinary people have never even heard of...

Haven't you already explained all the reasons?
—Closure

...All of these are true, yet they still do not fully explain her current state. Emotional bonds and opportunities to access the latest technology are indeed enough to keep her here, but they hardly seem enough to make someone who is clearly not diligent by nature take such genuine pleasure in the work of a pharmaceutical company, especially the parts that are, in truth, extremely repetitive.

Ugh, how annoying.
—Closure

Even today, Kazdel's infrastructure remains quite underdeveloped, and the newly built intercity network has yet to become widespread. This inevitably raises a question: in that era, one that was plainly even more chaotic and derelict, did Kazdel really have an information realm where Closure could run wild?
Closure's answer to this is, 'If there isn't one, just build one yourself.'
Of course, the reality was nowhere near that simple. At the time, Kazdel had no soil in which an intercity network could take root, and Sarkaz had essentially only one way to come into contact with electronics: taking them from Sanktas by force.
What ordinary Sarkaz wanted most were naturally patron firearms, followed by the currencies of various nations, Originium Ingots, and precious metals, then things that could be eaten, drunk, or put to practical use. Most advanced electronics were, to them, honestly baffling things: heavy, complicated, and not worth much even if taken apart. Some people would bring these things back to Kazdel and sell them with a waste-not mindset, and that was what gave the Sarkaz in the city the opportunity to come into contact with electronics. Closure was one of the first to do so.
But whenever she went outside, she had to face relatives with whom she had strained relations, and she had no one to share all her strange knowledge and new discoveries with. During that period, Closure probably craved communication more than at any other time in her life... until she successfully used a specific frequency band to contact another electronics hobbyist nearby. Everything that followed needs no telling.
Recently, engineers working to set up Kazdel's intercity network infrastructure can still find homemade base stations and repeaters tucked away in all sorts of nooks and crannies—the handiwork of Closure and her friends from back then. Closure was responsible for design and communications from the attic, while her friends handled installation in the field.

As an aside, in the sentence 'I was tinkering with circuits in the attic back then,' the most important piece of information is not anything else, but 'attic'—being able to afford a house with an attic, where locking the door could shut out almost all interference, was honestly a decent luxury in Kazdel at the time.
As another aside, the first electronic device I got my hands on had been modified by the Sankta who was robbed... who was killed. I wanted to talk to that person, and I thought about it for a long, long time.
That person should not have died like that. Neither should the Sarkaz who died to kill that person.
—Closure

After building up Kazdel's little circle of technology pioneers, Closure and her friends soon encountered their first disagreement—what they had already done, what they could do, and what they might someday be able to do were all enough to earn money in Kazdel, and even in most parts of Terra. A whole lot of money.
Several cash-strapped partners proposed a plan to monetize it. Naturally, the already loose circle had no way to stop them, and these partners immediately became hot commodities in the Scar Market. Later, some who truly could no longer stand Kazdel's environment left for distant lands, and coupled with Kazdel's excessively high population turnover rate, Closure became a loner once more. The only people she could still talk to were a few friends she knew inside and out—or at least she believed she knew them through and through.
It was also during this period that the infamy of a certain saboteur began to spread through Kazdel. This person would hack indiscriminately into any database they could get into (mostly ones her former friends had built for someone), servers (rare treasures among rare treasures), and even stolen personal terminals. Sometimes they left after leaving a trace; sometimes they wrecked everything inside as if venting. Outside the attic, Closure's family even, in a rare show of concern, began to worry whether this deviant little brat had recently suffered some sort of mental blow—and their concern was not exactly wrong.
It was only much, much later that Closure realized that the person she was back then had probably been yearning for something called the 'open-source spirit' in Columbia, something utterly at odds with her identity as a Vampire.
Closure had long since desensitized herself to both her identity as a Vampire and 'what Vampires are supposed to be.' Ask her now, and she will clearly list the Vampire she does not dislike (Warfarin), the Vampire she does not dislike all that much (Entelechia), the Vampire she dislikes (Duq'arael), and the Vampires she would rather die than meet (her parents). But before she fully thought it through, her identity as a Vampire did trouble her for a long time—why had she been born into a race that pursues 'purity' and 'perfection,' and used clearly loaded words like 'filth' and 'debasement' to mark out its hierarchy?
Program development requires trial and error, and engineering construction must allow for error and redundancy. Between her and her first group of friends, nothing was off-limits; just recalling all that Vampire nonsense while chatting was enough to set her teeth on edge. That was why she wanted open source, why she wanted a place that everyone could freely use, freely study, and freely contribute to. At the very least, she wanted to create the conditions for such a place.
Perhaps, to her, this was the most direct understanding of 'breaking through the shackles of tradition.'
The barriers between races, discrimination born of differences in seniority, a hierarchy based on bloodline... all of these were traditional shackles that bound her, and every one of them was something she broke through.
From this perspective, her reason for moving forward together with us has never changed from the very beginning.

[Procurement Department Special Acquisitions List]

Rosin, violin cleaner and maintenance set, Leithanien. Purchase Price: ■■■■. Sales Price: -
Good to see that Amiya's been playing the violin more since we got back from Zelgrad. She used to say she didn't need any expensive maintenance equipment for it, and I didn't know any better. Only after talking to some Leithanian operators did I learn that good maintenance is always better, no matter the quality of the violin. She deserves it after all this Ursus stuff.

Compilation of various newspapers from across Terra. Purchase Price: ■■■■. Sales Price: -
Auto-scanner and reader, Kazimierz. Purchase Price: ■■■■. Sales Price: -
Kal'tsit didn't say anything, but of course she'd want to know what happened while she was gone.
The scanner and reader are gifts from me. So the Kazimierzians CAN make something useful once in a while, a scanner that can automatically turn pages, scan documents, and organize them is hard to find... maybe it was invented by a desperate secretary.

Smart Kettle Modification Kit, Columbia. Purchase Price: ■■■■. Sales Price: -
Basically a Tkaronto smart water purifier refit as a kettle. Because I couldn't find a 'smart kettle' anywhere? What do the Columbians have against kettles, anyway?
...Wait, what's so great about kettles, anyway?
Long story short, it's now operable by voice commands, and can control the water temperature and dispense cold, filtered water directly. Basically a compact water purifier. Like it or not, it's all yours, Doctor.

Handheld Electronic Game Dev Master V10.0, Higashi (Southern Court). Purchase Price: ■■■■. Sales Price: -
......

The recipients of these gifts were concerned that Closure was so busy that she forgot to treat herself, so they prepared their own gifts and went to thank her together. Their worries turned out to be unfounded, however, as they found her snoozing on her desk with a little trophy—in true Closure style—right next to her.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Sentry duty, yeah, I get it, that's what the F.N.G. always gets, no matter where… it's not that? Well, you say that, but I find it hard to believe that you won't need protection.

Come, open your palm face-up. That's right, here you go. Yup, I made it myself. Making filled candy is quite a bother, and this is all that I made. Maybe it's not that rare on the outside, but you should understand its worth—are you done? Good. I have something to ask you. I won't take silence for an answer.

That Sarkaz was really something. I didn't have to hold anything back, and my blade's still warm, even now… no, it's not so dangerous. It's a bad day if you rip your clothes in the training room. Yeah, ranged caster duel. What were you thinking it was?

'I'm here, Doctor.' Voice imitation Arts, a staple for any war caster. Not close enough? Check this out then, at the tip of my blade—no playing with fire in the office? It's just an Arts illusion, there's no real fire. You draw a strange line for what spooks you.

The Armies have a clear delineation. If you're not with the Second Army, you're with the Fourth. No one asks what the shashka thinks. My Sechin was one such weapon. No, what's between Evgeny and I isn't personal. It's not that complicated.

My comrades believe I'm favored by fate, toying with my prey before dragging it into hell, just the monster with long-drooped eyelids that my code name represents. But the true monster is war itself, toying with and destroying everyone, making no distinction between noble and commoner, hero and villain.

Yes, I know that ignoring orders is a major dereliction of duty, I just didn't think you, of all people, would be criticizing the mistake I made in the Far North… you want to thank me? It's not like I meant to spare those people. There's nothing to thank me for.

What does this mean? And this? And this? How do you manage to read these scribblings? They're like worms crawling on the page. I used to have someone to read stuff like this to me. Sirka could read anything like singing a song. Maybe you can too. Audiobooks? Not interested.

Brewing, sugarmaking, woodworking and smithing. We began to learn these things as soon as we learned to walk. That's all we're allowed to do to pass the time off the battlefield. Here, give it a try. Homebrews don't pass security checks; I had to smuggle this kvass in.

handbook.profile: Scioppa Razin, leader and commander-in-chief of the Ursine Independent Tactics Formation 'Sechin,' and leader of the Volniki. In early 1102, he led his unit out of the jurisdiction of the Ursine military. After the Deity Grypherburg Incident, 'Sechin' became fully independent. Later, through an introduction by a branch office operator, he began making contact with Rhodes Island on behalf of 'Sechin.'

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this Operator is believed to be non-infected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Viy currently shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.19u/L
Due to the significant fluctuation in the readings, the final value is taken as an average; even so, it remains relatively concerning. Continued observation is recommended.
The problem may lie with the Arts Unit Operator Viy uses. It contains a complex Originium circuit that defies conventional analysis, perhaps derived from some Ursine military research, or from an undocumented tradition of the 'Volniki.' At present, we only know that this circuit can amplify the energy of the Originium embedded in the Arts Unit to extreme levels, thereby achieving the best possible Arts performance. Correspondingly, this type of Arts Unit places an immense burden on the caster's body, and the slightest lapse could cause irreversible damage to the nervous system, or even cause the caster to contract Oripathy. If possible, I hope Operator Viy can try to reduce his reliance on this type of Arts Unit, and gradually transition to similar products with more moderate performance.

Leithanien's research into Originium Arts is not all-encompassing. I truly cannot make sense of this thing. Because not even spire casters would use something this suicidal! They value their lives more than anyone. ...Hm? You say Ursines developed this? W-Well, that does make sense.
—An anonymous caster operator
handbook.promotionRecord:
Looking back on it now, every time the chiefs of our villages led us to 'fight for Ursus,' it was probably just a repeat of that very first promise. Strange, isn't it? We were deceived so many times, yet we still never learned. It makes you feel like people like us were maybe just... meant to be treated that way. Damn it all.
Oleg always says that Vladimir really would have relented and given us autonomy, if only he hadn't died so soon. But then our parents' generation soon died in great numbers too, and among those who survived, nobody knew if that had ever been true at all. And Sirka never believed it. Not for a second.
But none of that matters now. After all, we no longer place our hopes in the Emperor. Ursus as a whole doesn't even need an emperor anymore, so who would still expect someone who no longer exists to fulfill a promise from the past?
Choosing sides, taking a stand... Everyone was sick of it, but I still believe I did the right thing back then. Perhaps when people look back on history in the future, they may find the names of the 'Volnov' or 'Sechin' written there. I only hope that when they look closely through this unit's record, they find that the ones more worth remembering are actually those who chose resistance even earlier, before we did.
It was they who taught us that we must always stand up and walk, not bend down and crawl. That is the path of the 'Volniki,' an outcome countless lives were spent to secure—
...It may not be the best one, but I will not betray it.
archives:
Based on Operator Viy's own account, as well as HR's subsequent interviews with certain operators who were born in Ursus or otherwise understand the situation there, we can roughly trace the origins of the 'Volniki,' a unique group long unrecognized by the Ursine government and unknown to the general public.
'Volniki' was initially a title promised by the founder of Ursus to the non-Ursus races within its territory at the time. Igor exchanged the right to self-government for their support in the war against the Hippogryphs, but after the nation was founded, this promise was never fulfilled. Instead, the Volniki's ancestors were driven into the wilderness under the pretext of being 'granted land,' then forced to migrate repeatedly due to Catastrophes. They gradually split apart, forming different settlements with no ties between them beyond their shared identification with the same name. In wartime, they were conscripted as a source of soldiers; in peacetime, they farmed their separate barren lands, living lives of bare self-sufficiency. Because they had always been excluded from society's progress, they gradually grew used to separating themselves from the nation and the people through the concept of the 'Volniki,' then struggling on within this isolation that resembled 'fate.' Just as the lyrics of that song often sung among their communities say, they show a persistent need to seek paths and answers from their forebears and their myths.

If everything is truly as he says, then the 'Volniki' can indeed be regarded as a significant microcosm of Ursus's racial issues.
...Considering Simonch, that city sunk by the Royal Guard, there is also a possibility that it belonged to a certain group of Elafia Volniki. If so, why such utter disaster befell them so easily has a more readily comprehensible explanation: A nomadic city belonging solely to them should have represented meaningful progress and a rare home for the long-displaced Volniki. However, judging from the Ursine government's long-standing policy tendency of forbidding any mention of the 'Volniki,' they would naturally only interpret this as some attempt at separatism.
This is not a defense of the legitimacy of Ursus's actions. It is only that, when looking back on the past, even if these brutal incidents have no direct connection to Rhodes Island, we should still attempt to understand them and learn from them. This will also be of considerable help in our future dealings with 'Sechin,' and even with the various forces in today's Ursus, which are by no means united.
—Kal'tsit

Unlike many legally recognized organizations that maintain stable external partnerships with Rhodes Island, 'Sechin' is a paramilitary armed force currently in transition. It is neither a mercenary group, nor can it be defined as a 'security company.' It exists in a 'gray area' that Rhodes Island does not readily engage with, and we must carefully gauge the extent of our dealings with it. Furthermore, the attitude displayed by the leader of 'Sechin,' who is often seen around Rhodes Island HQ, is just as ambiguous. Continued observation is recommended.

[Audio Record]
'Oh, are you asking about that big Kuranta guy with the Ursine accent? He does show up in the library a lot. Sometimes when the books on the shelves are too high up and the ladder's been borrowed, he'll even offer to help get them down—no, not just for ladies. He helps anyone who needs it. ...I know he's good-looking, but that's not why I remember him! He has a lot of scars, on his neck and on his arms, and he never covers them up. Anyone would notice that, wouldn't they?'

[Borrowing Records]
'The Guide to Fincatching'
'Illustrated Guide to Abdominal Breathing'
'Drinking Your Own Homemade Wine'
'Three Thousand Ursine Folk Songs'
'Toe Care for Steed Burdenbeasts'
...
The above books and accompanying videotapes were all returned within the borrowing period. No abnormalities were found.

[Audio Record]
'Oh my, looks like I acted a bit too much on my own. I should've said hello to one of you first. I heard people in the cafeteria say your library had all kinds of things, so I figured I'd go find some books with pictures to read and pass the time. This place isn't like back in the village, where someone would teach you how to do those family trades step by step, but the videotapes are pretty convenient too. This week, I learned more than I used to in a whole month of summer break.
'It's comfortable staying in Rhodes Island, so that's why I keep coming back. Of course 'Sechin' is good too, but during the break, those guys all go their separate ways. Some go back to Ursus to see their families, and some blow their money on booze. We don't have much in the way of entertainment. Once we're off the battlefield, we pretty much just keep spinning in place. I'm trying to break out of that cycle now, and I suppose that can set an example for them.'

Operator Viy shows an extremely strong desire to protect his colleagues in 'Sechin', as well as an unbelievable degree of tolerance. As their leader, he seems unconcerned by the possibility that this approach may ultimately lead to lax discipline and even the unit's destruction on some battlefield. 'We should get to decide how we live now,' he says. After evaluation, we can determine that they are capable of taking responsibility for their own actions, and since we seek cooperation with them, we should also bear the necessary risks.

He considers protecting the comrades under his command as his own responsibility, yet also grants them his trust without reservation. The degree of unity shown by 'Sechin' would be difficult to find even among the most decorated Ursine Formations of the past. Stay vigilant, Doctor, but there is no need to be too harsh on these young people.
—Hellagur

After a period of observation, we have noticed that Operator Viy is relatively unfamiliar with paperwork. This does not mean he is illiterate or unable to write; he simply finds this sort of work 'annoying' and has a psychological resistance to it, which makes him seem inefficient when he needs to handle paperwork independently. After we noticed that his second-in-command was unable to offer much assistance in this regard either, to ensure smooth cooperation, we assigned an operator who works at the reception and specializes in drafting documents to assist him during working hours with filing reports and other such matters in a timely manner. At present, Operator Viy has accepted this arrangement well, and the two have developed a good working rhythm.

[Report on Disturbance at Rhodes Island Headquarters Reception]
According to our information, the banner that appeared at the reception the day before yesterday, bearing text such as 'I'm sorry, please forgive me,' was sent by a patient's family member who had long been involved in a financial dispute with Rhodes Island. It was meant to express recognition of and gratitude for the reception's service, not to resolve a relationship conflict. According to this family member, he has fully realized how inappropriate his previous harassment was, and stated that he will cooperate with Rhodes Island to settle his outstanding debts as soon as possible.
In subsequent interviews, the operator who was at the reception when the banner was hung up expressed his view of the matter: this was not his achievement. While he does not know who helped resolve this troublesome problem, at least there is no longer anyone constantly shouting 'Pay me back!' and 'Frauds!' at the reception while our security personnel are unable to forcibly drive them away. Order has been restored at the reception, which is a cause for great celebration for everyone who visits Rhodes Island.

...I knew it was him the second I heard! Always looking for things to do. There was this one time when we were camped out in the wasteland with some other formations, and some snot-nosed orderly said that if we weren't Ursines, we were nothing. That night, the guy's boots got taken and hung up on an old tree 800 meters away, soaked through, dripping nonstop, heavy as rocks! Plenty of other things like that happened after. He never said anything, and he never got caught doing it, but everyone knew it was him. At the end of the day, we didn't actually want to make trouble. The Armies all treated us as expendables, and what respect do expendables need? People just follow the example set from above, that's all. But he refused to put up with it. Every time someone came looking for trouble, he had to bite back.
—Oleg, Operator Viy's second-in-command

[Audio Record]
'Bad memory, you know. Can't be helped. If you've got a score to settle, you have to settle it then and there.'

More than thirty years ago, a painter passed through a small village in the southern wilderness of Ursus, and painted a family portrait for a household that had just welcomed a newborn with thin Nightzmora blood. With the same brushwork he usually reserved for depicting Emperors and Yurodstvo, he rendered an utterly ordinary family of four from the wilderness.
More than twenty years ago, Catastrophe Messengers arrived. They pushed open the wooden fence and informed the village chief of the terrible news that a Catastrophe was coming. As the village raised great herds of steed burdenbeasts, its inhabitants should have been able to evacuate in time. Only one family of three, with a paralyzed father and a blind mother, could not manage it. Faced with the dark mass of people stepping into their home, the boy raised the curved blade that had broken on the battlefield along with his father's legs, and pointed it at the noble who emerged from behind the 'Catastrophe Messengers.' His hands did not tremble in the slightest. The noble asked: You served. A child soldier? The boy said: Don't come any closer.
The 'Catastrophe Messengers' took his parents away, the noble took the boy away, and the boy took his sister's belongings away. The village itself was destroyed by the Catastrophe that arrived as expected the next day. In exchange for his family's protection, the boy began to undergo grueling training, forcing his body to adapt to those violent weapons. He had been cast into the Empire's war factory, where the title of 'War Caster' would be granted to the 'luckiest' child among hundreds.
More than ten years ago, the boy obtained that title and began to operate in border conflicts never recorded by the authorities, as a spy, as an assassin, as a commander, as the name he had finally been given. And when every uprising he put down was ultimately revealed to have been the result of factional purges, when soldiers who were supposed to sacrifice themselves for some great cause instead used civilians as shields, he began to question, and then defected.
A few years ago, he all but carved the flesh from his own body, and finally left the army under the identity of a dead man. He returned to his homeland, already destroyed by Catastrophe, and picked a broken picture frame from the ruins. There, he began to rebuild his life, drawing on what he had learned and thought about in the army to gather a team of his own.
Yet even now, he still wears the medal the army gave him, not because he believes in the ideals or loyalty it represents, but simply because he wants to. If he wanted, he could certainly sell the medal for a good price and use the money to buy some wine for his comrades. Things are unpredictable, he often thinks. When others ask him why he left the army, he simply says, 'I got tired of it.' When others finish singing a pleasant little song with vulgar lyrics, he simply says, 'Sing it again.'
The boy grew from a child into a young man, and that young man brought along those who believed in him, continuing onward across this vast land.

All right, nice story, but wasn't there some setup that never paid off? And what does any of this have to do with Durin? If you keep talking about Ursus, I'll have to ask you to leave.
—Head of the Durin Story Circle

modules.moduleDescription:
He steps into the wide yet shallow creek, wading through the reeds towards the other side. Behind him, the campfire burns bright, surrounded by song under the clear night. The kid whose ancestors were Catastrophe Messengers swore on his mother's name that there would be no trouble for at least another week, so this is where Sechin made camp. The soldiers sit together in small groups, all except for one rookie recently reassigned from the Vanguard Battalion, who crossed the creek on her own for reasons unknown.
As their Ataman, it was Scioppa's job to know, so he follows the bootprints in the mud. They are smaller than his own, leaving marks of varying depths, and lead him to a small Originium lamp.
Scioppa sits down on the ground, a pair of eyes fixated upon him.
'Nervous about tomorrow?'
'Just some bandits. Not a problem.'
'Still, it's your first mission since you joined us. So, can you sing or not?'
The eyes upon him suddenly grow fierce. Scioppa rubs his head—he'd meant to apologize for his comrades' earlier heckling, only to almost repeat the same standoff.
'Guess not. It's alright, you know. I can't hold a tune either. Next time they want you to sing, just recite the words like I do.'
'Our Baba put a glass house upon the legs of a fowlbeast.'
'Not to move from place to place like us, but so that she could turn around—'
Scioppa's 'demonstration' is interrupted by actual singing, which grows softer after a couple of phrases, before stopping.
'So you CAN sing.' Scioppa laughs, unconcerned by the misunderstanding. 'If you didn't want to sing, you could have just said so. We don't have all the rules and taboos of the regular forces.'
'I'll get used to it.'
The Originium lamp is turned off with a crack. The Volnik's blade gleams in the dark like an eye as its wielder stands up and gestures for the soldier to follow him.

The Ataman's tent is surprisingly tidy. A jacket is spread over the bunk, and various weapons are lined up on the sturdy fabric, with a water basin and a dirty towel next to them indicating that their owner was cleaning his gear.
'Give me a moment.' Scioppa grabs the jacket and begins digging through its pockets. It takes a while for him to find what he was looking for—an oval-shaped piece of metal.
'I should've done this sooner, but I was busy with route planning. It's finished now. Here.'
The gray-haired young woman silently touches the words on the metal plate.
'Irina Arianovna... I hope I spelled it right. Take this too. I put a spell on it.'
Scioppa takes out a silver dagger.
'While I still live, the enchantment will protect you from one fatal blow, so long as you don't lose it. Everyone here has one.
'It might be a little late, but let me say this: Welcome to Sechin.'
The soldier nods and takes the dagger. She stares at the piece of metal in her hand, then at the ones just like it hanging from the chain that Scioppa is wearing. She answers in her usual, unemotional tone,
'Thank you.
'But that's not such a bad ending for a soldier.'

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: You do know this isn't my kind of work… right?

I didn't think something this big would happen to Rhodes Island while I was away. You still hanging in there—Oh? Sounds like you never forget how I said I'd replace you. You need to keep working twice as hard, then, because I didn't forget either.

Medical decided we weren't ready when we first showed up, but this time, I brought everyone back without a scratch, and the Ursine office is all set up. I wasn't so optimistic myself, you say? Look, the job's done, so why can't I be a little happier now?

Istina gave me a new list of books to read. She says if you want to unite more people, you need to learn lots of different things, and she's right. You're just about to head to the library? Then you tell the librarian I'm still reading those dozen or so books I borrowed last time. It's slow-going, but I will return them before the due date.
Oh, this is my new weapon, took it off an absolute scumbag. Using power that's not even his to bully the weak… I get a lot of joy breaking the noses of bastards like him.
There was a time I was gonna break up the USSG, but then I thought: it's good to have a place where everyone can relax. Hmm… Rhodes Island is kinda like that for us too.

Don't worry, we might have run into some trouble, we handled it fine. Zoya even officially joined the USSG. But Gummy has been pretty distracted lately, some thing with her parents, and we're all thinking of a way to help her… If you have any ideas, remember to tell us.

When did I start thinking about going back to Ursus? That place buried my parents, and it nearly buried us too. I used to hate… no, hide from it, but there was always going to be a point where you can't run anymore, and that's when I knew I had to get up and face it.

You're like Istina, always lecturing us on grand truths before doing something stupid. Sure, I don't really listen to you two when you talk about that stuff, but I know we've always seen eye-to-eye on what is to be done. Let the truth be as grand as it wants. It doesn't matter how high the walls they built are, we'll tear them down.
I'm going out for a walk. If you feel like stretching your legs, come and find me.
Here's my report: the mission to set up an office in Ursus was a success… I need to actually write a report? What a pain…
When's the real fight?
My medals need re-issuing? It's standard procedure? Man, if Ursine nobles were half as strict as you, I'd have never gotten out of their lockdown.

By the way, who actually makes Rhodes Island's medals? I'm thinking of getting some with the USSG's insignia on them. The first batch goes to Istina and the rest, of course, but after that… A few extra wouldn't hurt.
Fighting is still the easiest option.
Same old, same old?
C'mon, let's go already.
Hmph, hope those scumbags are stronger than they look.
Send me where the biggest fight is.
So, what's the plan?
Steady, everyone. I'm here.
Here I come!
Get over here, if you want to die!
Who's next?
All for one, one for all!
Charge! CHARGE!
Ah… That felt great!
That was just enough for a warm-up.
Damn, they run fast…
Leave the rear to me. Don't mess things up next time.
Phew, I'm back…
You really got nothing to do, huh… Whatever, do what you want.
It's good seeing everyone like this.
Arknights.
Man, Rhodes Island is so damned rowdy today… Oh, you're here. Come, try some blini. I made them with Gummy. We're heading out to mess around once we're done eating, you want to come along?
Hey, you doing alright?
Here, a leather jacket I brought back from Ursus. Think it suits you—See the USSG insignia on it? Drew it myself. What, you not happy with it, or…? Okay, that's good… Happy birthday, Doctor.

The Self-Government Group used to just be about survival, but now that we're on Rhodes Island, we can't stop ourselves from thinking about the future… And for me, I think, when everyone is happily walking their own paths, I'll be there to make sure nobody stumbles.

When did I start thinking about going back to Ursus? That place buried my parents, and it nearly buried us too. I used to hate… no, hide from it, but there was always going to be a point where you can't run anymore, and that's when I knew I had to get up and face it.

You're like Istina, always lecturing us on grand truths before doing something stupid. Sure, I don't really listen to you two when you talk about that stuff, but I know we've always seen eye-to-eye on what is to be done. Let the truth be as grand as it wants. It doesn't matter how high the walls they built are, we'll tear them down.
I'm going out for a walk. If you feel like stretching your legs, come and find me.
Here's my report: the mission to set up an office in Ursus was a success… I need to actually write a report? What a pain…
When's the real fight?
My medals need re-issuing? It's standard procedure? Man, if Ursine nobles were half as strict as you, I'd have never gotten out of their lockdown.

By the way, who actually makes Rhodes Island's medals? I'm thinking of getting some with the USSG's insignia on them. The first batch goes to Istina and the rest, of course, but after that… A few extra wouldn't hurt.
Fighting is still the easiest option.
Same old, same old?
C'mon, let's go already.
Hmph, hope those scumbags are stronger than they look.
Send me where the biggest fight is.
So, what's the plan?
Steady, everyone. I'm here.
Here I come!
Get over here, if you want to die!
Who's next?
All for one, one for all!
Charge! CHARGE!
Ah… That felt great!
That was just enough for a warm-up.
Damn, they run fast…
Leave the rear to me. Don't mess things up next time.
Phew, I'm back…
You really got nothing to do, huh… Whatever, do what you want.
It's good seeing everyone like this.
Arknights.
Man, Rhodes Island is so damned rowdy today… Oh, you're here. Come, try some blini. I made them with Gummy. We're heading out to mess around once we're done eating, you want to come along?
Hey, you doing alright?
Here, a leather jacket I brought back from Ursus. Think it suits you—See the USSG insignia on it? Drew it myself. What, you not happy with it, or…? Okay, that's good… Happy birthday, Doctor.

The Self-Government Group used to just be about survival, but now that we're on Rhodes Island, we can't stop ourselves from thinking about the future… And for me, I think, when everyone is happily walking their own paths, I'll be there to make sure nobody stumbles.

handbook.profile: Zima, leader of the Ursus Student Self-Government Group, has served as a combat squad leader since joining Rhodes Island and recently contributed to the establishment of our Grypherburg branch. Her skills have improved considerably through both training and field experience, giving her a mature combat style that is all her own. She currently participates in Rhodes Island's operations in Ursus as a guard operator.

handbook.promotionRecord:
[Classified Log]
Operator Zima's after-action report from their rescue of the student Rania mentioned various accidents in the course of the operation, such as a shadowy figure that flashed by the window at a secret meeting, or a schedule that went mysteriously missing from a locked cabinet. Even on the day of the operation, some students in charge of logistics were interrogated in the alleys by police with their epaulettes removed, as though there were eyes from up high seeing through all their plans, even if they had managed to pull wool over the eyes of the nobles at the hearing.
Zima emphasized, however, that all these accidents seemed to amount to nothing. Even the stamped warrant for their arrest seemed to have quietly disappeared. She initially thought it was the result of Rhodes Island's lobbying, expressing surprise at how we were able to take care of such matters, while still being unable to deliver long-range communications equipment.
As a matter of fact, Rhodes Island's activities in Ursus have encountered tremendous resistance ever since the Far North Incident, as though there were a pair of invisible eyes constantly watching our every move from atop Grypherburg.
The intentions of Ursus's regime remain unknown at this time, and establishing direct communications would be premature. In the wake of the ■■■■ Incident, we must reassess this ancient nation and its sprawling, convoluted organization.
archives:
Sonya Mikhailivna could hardly have expected the twists and turns their journey would take when she and the rest of the Ursus Student Self-Government Group signed their off-boarding checklists in the summer of 1101.
The road to Ursus was not nearly as smooth and steady as the temperature in the car. It did not take long for them to reach their first stop: the snow-covered land of Kjerag.
Zima recalls that Leto wasted little time in dropping off their tagged luggage at the station before taking the group on a tour of Kjerag's favorite tourist spots, disturbing numerous communal burdenbeasts basking in the sun with their rowdy shouting. Instructor Dur-nar had tried to warn them to stay away from the cliff to no avail. In the end, she had to tie them to her with safety ropes. For Zima, however, it was the departure that left the deepest impression. When the station staff came bearing the bill for luggage storage, Leto simply signed the name 'Paleroche' and said, 'Hand out the presents for me.' As the train departed the station, Leto laughed her ass off at the tall figure standing on the platform with chagrin on his face. When she finally stopped laughing, she told Zima that the 'presents' were not just the junk she had intended to throw away from the start, but also the warm clothing and snacks intended for the journey.
As such, when the USSG arrived in Grypherburg, the first thing they did was not submit their university applications, but purchase clothing. Zima never forgot her mission for Rhodes Island, even as she began her studies at a Grypherburg university. A prognostic sense of anxiety and excitement had come over Grypherburg society. Changes in foreign countries had become evidence for various ideologies, and everyone wanted to have a voice in Ursus's future. She felt that public opinion in Grypherburg was too complex and too far removed from the realities of everyday life. Accompanied by Instructor Dur-nar, she began to travel to nearby nomadic cities and settlements whenever school was not in session, investigating how the people there lived, what problems they faced, how they saw things, and whether their opinions were homegrown or had come from abroad.
But Zima's investigation was cut short by the incident in the Far North. The empire quickly cracked down on public opinion, the Armies' battleships were on the move, and snow had begun to fall across Ursus... Zima brought her thoughts and insights from that period back to Grypherburg. Little did she imagine that it would be far more than the Student's Assembly awaiting her.

The conclusion of the Katorga Incident did little to mitigate the tension in Grypherburg. If anything, it has intensified. For the people of Grypherburg, some of the changes were visible. The power supply had become even more inconsistent, Katorga Raion was still firmly attached to Grypherburg's power deck—though white smoke had begun to rise from a few chimneys—and the fallen statue of Igor Velikiy lay untouched, just like the broken walls. No one repaired it, no one scrawled graffiti on it, and no one even dared glance at it as they passed. Meanwhile, other changes happened beneath the surface. Zima and the Ursus Student Self-Government Group were not charged with any offenses—their actions seemingly covered up by certain parties—and they were unable to travel with Crownslayer to where Gummy's parents were located. Amiya spoke directly to Zima and Gummy to explain, while the Doctor personally signed the documents appointing Zima as director of Rhodes Island's Grypherburg office. [Audio Log] 'I understand Rhodes Island's current circumstances. The company stands out in Ursus like a drop of blood on the snow, and is in no position to openly establish a communications network or send large numbers to Grypherburg. That's what makes our work even more important. The Grypherburg office needs more than a location—but yes, thanks for cleaning the rehearsal rooms, Gummy—we need funding and connections. We need something to keep the nobles from coming after us. We need a front business, as well as reception and communication staff, and we need to do all of this ourselves. Sounds tough, doesn't it? Thankfully, we have some experience in these matters, and we all have our own strengths... Wait, you want to be the receptionist? No, Ukusik, anyone but you! We wouldn't last a week if—say, who let you in anyway? This meeting was supposed to be private! Oh no you don't, you're not getting away when you've already heard our secret. You better sign this application form here and now... Uh, we're not breaking any rules, are we, Istina? Good.' Look, I'm busy enough as it is—I'm just going to mail in this brief report, because I don't have the time. You have no idea how much trouble it is to register and operate a pharmaceutical company branch in Grypherburg! Just today, we got a notice that the fire safety inspection had been rescheduled because of a violation. We spent the whole day trying to find it. Guess what it was? That big hamaxe of mine, which was apparently 'too frightening' and therefore unsafe—what kind of nonsense is that? You'd never guess how we dealt with it either. We found a glass case, put it over it, and called it an exhibit. And guess what? It was approved. Somehow. Honestly, if I'd known this would be such a pain in the ass, I'd have taken my hamaxe to ■■■■ and picked a few fights instead! —Operator Zima's 'brief report'

A particular conversation occurred between Zima and Istina. They both independently reported it to Medical, for their respective psychological health records. I was never good with words. I wasn't sure what I was going to say, even as I opened my mouth. So I told Istina about Katorga, about what I went through in there, and she told me what she went through on the outside. I told her about what happened to Leonid, about how Faddey opposed the rescue of our fellow students, about how angry I was and how I wanted to punch him and go do my own thing. But I didn't. At the time, I thought, 'what would Istina do if she were here?' I didn't know. Maybe she would've already come up with four or five reasons to shut those mudak up, but she wasn't there. I resisted the urge to swing my fist or slap him. I forced myself to calm down and solve the problem like Istina would. I couldn't spin my words like she could, so I spoke slowly and talked about my most resolute beliefs, trusting that they would convince the others as well. Looking back, I think I did the right thing. But did I? That's what I asked Istina. I said I kind of regretted not slapping Faddey. She said she was glad, but not because of what I did. Because I regretted it. She said that proved that deep in my heart, I was still determined to be myself. I didn't know what she meant. It sounded like she was mocking me, but part of me agreed with her. For whatever reason, I even feel a little touched when I think back to that conversation with her. —Interview with Operator Zima 'Touched'? No, not at all. I wouldn't have even been locked in the kitchen prep room with Sonya if she hadn't felt the need to steal the cupcakes Instructor Dur-nar was baking. It was the most embarrassed I'd felt in a long while, having the instructor come free the two of us 'thieves' when she heard the alarm. As for what she said... I did say that, but I was not mocking her. When I did what I did outside Katorga, I often forced myself to step into Sonya's shoes, and asked myself what she would do if she were there. And just like her, I have regrets. But regret doesn't mean we did anything wrong, it's simply a reaffirmation of our self-identity. Sonya could have let loose her slap, of course, and I didn't have to force myself to do those things. But who can say whether the things we didn't do would have been better or worse? At least we're asking ourselves the question. That's good enough. There was something else I didn't get to say to Sonya, who left as soon as the instructor arrived. I'm sure you're aware that some things are hard to say once the moment has left us, so I thought I might as well say it here: I'm glad we both chose to affirm who we are, Sonya. I think that's why we trust each other. —Interview with Operator Istina They'd gone through almost the entire batch of cupcakes by the time I arrived. It's all good, though. This is why I like baking. —Operator Dur-nar

We brought down those mudak. We are free. Now we must gather people, everyone who would join us, and show Grypherburg who its true master is! —Words on a page I saw the people whimpering in pain. I saw the scarred soil. Not another drop of milk could be squeezed from it, yet the greedy nobles and vile bureaucrats continue to torment it like leeches, torment our motherland. I must resist. I must take up the sword! I am not the only one who thinks this. —Words on a page We cut off the commissioner's head! We will cut off more! This rotten nation will fall! Victory shall be ours! Nika, Sonya... I fight for you. —Words on a page Zima and Gummy found a large pile of papers in the basement of the abandoned theater that served as the Ursus Student Self-Government Group's temporary base of operations. At first, she thought it was the script of a particularly incoherent play, but Absinthe's examination of municipal archives revealed that the basement had existed from before the theater was even built. It had been part of the prison system centuries ago, used to store and destroy the possessions of executed inmates. Zima began to examine the papers again. The inmates who wrote them had likely been put on death row for treason, suppressed and arrested by the enforcers of Ursus. Each sheet was subtly different from the others in texture or color, and each was written by a different hand. They mark the countless acts of resistance over the centuries, big and small. By farmers, poets, soldiers, and madmen. Their dates are often many years apart. Some wrote in factories driven by Originium External Combustion Engine, while others had only recently heard about that new invention. Ultimately, however, all their final letters ended up in the same dark corner. Zima tried to identify the writers, but unsurprisingly neither these 'rebellions' nor those who carried the flag of resistance had left their names upon the vast history of Ursus. The first thought I had might seem childish. I was thinking about how many Sonyas there have been over the centuries, how many Annas, Rosalinds, Natalyas, and Zoyas... how many Peters and Ivans. I felt a chill when I saw the name 'Sonya' on that piece of paper. Was it fate or coincidence that I came across it? I put down the papers and looked over the dust-covered basement, filled with history. This time, I thought, it would be different. I'd make sure it was different. —Operator Zima

modules.moduleDescription:
...It's getting dark. We have to leave.
But before we go, take a look at the white vapor of our breath. That's proof that we're alive. And take a look at our friends, buried beneath the damp dirt.
The air is filled with the smell of iron and saltpeter. This is no lecture hall in Grypherburg. Look to your left, at the empty spot where Pencil Stub once sat. He always carried his pen and paper, mulling over the flowery prose of his dramatic scripts. But he was the first to answer my call to raise his fist and resist.
Nika and Yeremey used to sit side-by-side in that empty spot in the middle. I can still see Nika patting Yeremey's back, blushing slightly, singing their school song out of tune after they'd had a few drinks.
And Faddey, too. Whatever his mistakes, he never forgot his duty, and in his last moments, he gave the chance to live to another.
......
There are so many more names. I could go on and on, until we've etched every one of them into our hearts.
Our sorrow is not weakness. It is not cowardice. It is a scar that marks our struggle, and our rebirth, over these ten days. It tells us that there's something that can never be taken away.
We will remember that we each held someone else's hand in ours on that cold winter day, in that all-consuming inferno.
The clouds of dust, the songs that never end, the tears in the snow, the battlefield on which we fought... As long as any of us still remembers—
They will continue to live. We will continue to live.
Ursus cannot kill us, just as life can persist and grow beneath even the frozen earth.
We must remember their faces, remember their fights, and remember that we will meet again, in the future that they died for.
Come and speak their names with me, for those who fell and for those who live, for yesterday and for tomorrow.

Some time later, Sonya found a few battered school uniforms as she was organizing her things. They were wrapped up tightly, not a speck of dust on them.
She touched her burning cheeks, her fingertips numb and trembling as she recalled her speech before the graves in Katorga that day, the words rushing back like snow upon the window.
'What are you doing here, General Zima? Everyone's waiting for you.'
'Don't rush her, Leto. Sonya needs to prepare for the victory banquet.'
They will meet again, in a better place... It wasn't perfect, but they achieved a lot, didn't they?
Sonya gave a subtle smile, and complained to the others about the Ursine winter as she rubbed her hands together.

summons.name: Bond
summons.description: When skill ends, Bellone returns to this position and no other Operators may be deployed

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Sort these files? Fine, but before we begin your trivial task, you might have a look at these plans I've mapped out for you.

There are no famiglie in Nuova Volsinii, not a single one. A famiglia must flip into a corporation before it can enter the city, and that's hardly a bother. Indeed… and there's not much difference between a mafia and a corporation, whether Siracusan or foreign.

The Bellones took me in when I was five, and trained me to become Leon's consigliere. With this bulky suitcase in tow, I went to many places and met many faces as I ran errands and collected intelligence. Even now, I still do many things myself.

You want to learn to knuckle-roll a lighter as fast as I do? It's easy, here. Don't worry, just try again. I practice these tricks to keep my hands nimble—after all, there are times when you can't just draw a blade, even in Siracusa.

At first, the famiglie were just packs of runts keeping each other alive, while the dons used them as tools to grab power. But in Nuova Volsinii, under Leon's rules, a famiglia does imply a real family now—at least, that's how it is for the Bellones.

You think the Bellone name is important? No, what's important is our people and our bond. As for Rhodes Island… we have an excellent working relationship, but if you hope to advance our working relationship even further… you'll have to prove a familial bond exists between us first, Doctor.

You were told that enjoying authentic Siracusan cuisine is a proper show of respect to a Siracusan? No, I differ on this. You come to my home, and I make sure you're sated. Finishing the food on your plate is a show of respect to me, è così semplice.

Of course, you may overlook my concern and kindness, as many do when they first meet me. But soon, you will meet something you can't manage on your own, and then, well… Someday, and that day may never come, I will call upon you to do a service for me. And you will say sì.

Passively carrying out orders isn't my style. Taking control, eliminating all obstacles when the opportunity strikes, and achieving my objective, by any means—That's how I do things, so you'll want to get used to it, Doctor.
You're looking a little sluggish… it's time to rest. Here's a cocktail. Salute.
So Leon's codename is 'Vigil'? Abandoning both his family and his name… I see. Well then, Operator Bellone, reporting in.
Violence is only the means, and not the end. But these pups are too inefficient at it.
A promotion… It's been a long time since someone's used this word with me. Feels fresh.
Titles and tokens don't necessarily equate to trust, but at least they show how you see me. È un onore.
Let's go. It's time we witness the fruition of our plans.
Do as I say, and ask no questions.
I don't need so many hands with me. Those on standby, just watch us work.
Stay silent and wait.
You're asking me? I say it's time to move.
Don't hesitate.
Leave it to me.
I'll handle it.
The Bellones say hello.
It's time to repay your debt.
This is the price you pay for offending the famiglia.
Don't worry. I'll take care of your family when you're gone.
Meticulous plans, finely executed. You'll get used to these splendid triumphs with me around, Doctor.
Not all donuts come out with a hole. I'll review it when we get back.
Stragglers will return for revenge, so we'll have to devise a plan to eradicate all possible threats.
Let's see… how can we flip the situation to our advantage?
You have a big famiglia of your own. That's no easy feat, making sure they're all cared for.
Did I miss something important?
Let's go for a walk and inspect our territory.
Arknights.

The new year is a time for family gatherings. I should go eat with my famiglia. An unshakable tradition. We'll have dinner together after that. It might be a late one, but I'll make it back before the clock turns over.
Demetri Certaldo Bellone, happy to serve.
Birthdays only come once a year. So, what would you like to eat? Anything you fancy. Yes, even a pineapple pizza, if you dare—though I'm sure you know you'll pay for it someday.
Your eyes… remind me of a friend. Idealistic eyes, shining bright. Don't worry, I'll help you out—by my rules.

EN.voiceText: Sort these files? Fine, but before we begin your trivial task, you might have a look at these plans I've mapped out for you.

There are no famiglie in Nuova Volsinii, not a single one. A famiglia must flip into a corporation before it can enter the city, and that's hardly a bother. Indeed… and there's not much difference between a mafia and a corporation, whether Siracusan or foreign.

The Bellones took me in when I was five, and trained me to become Leon's consigliere. With this bulky suitcase in tow, I went to many places and met many faces as I ran errands and collected intelligence. Even now, I still do many things myself.

You want to learn to knuckle-roll a lighter as fast as I do? It's easy, here. Don't worry, just try again. I practice these tricks to keep my hands nimble—after all, there are times when you can't just draw a blade, even in Siracusa.

At first, the famiglie were just packs of runts keeping each other alive, while the dons used them as tools to grab power. But in Nuova Volsinii, under Leon's rules, a famiglia does imply a real family now—at least, that's how it is for the Bellones.

You think the Bellone name is important? No, what's important is our people and our bond. As for Rhodes Island… we have an excellent working relationship, but if you hope to advance our working relationship even further… you'll have to prove a familial bond exists between us first, Doctor.

You were told that enjoying authentic Siracusan cuisine is a proper show of respect to a Siracusan? No, I differ on this. You come to my home, and I make sure you're sated. Finishing the food on your plate is a show of respect to me, è così semplice.

Of course, you may overlook my concern and kindness, as many do when they first meet me. But soon, you will meet something you can't manage on your own, and then, well… Someday, and that day may never come, I will call upon you to do a service for me. And you will say sì.

Passively carrying out orders isn't my style. Taking control, eliminating all obstacles when the opportunity strikes, and achieving my objective, by any means—That's how I do things, so you'll want to get used to it, Doctor.
You're looking a little sluggish… it's time to rest. Here's a cocktail. Salute.
So Leon's codename is 'Vigil'? Abandoning both his family and his name… I see. Well then, Operator Bellone, reporting in.
Violence is only the means, and not the end. But these pups are too inefficient at it.
A promotion… It's been a long time since someone's used this word with me. Feels fresh.
Titles and tokens don't necessarily equate to trust, but at least they show how you see me. È un onore.
Let's go. It's time we witness the fruition of our plans.
Do as I say, and ask no questions.
I don't need so many hands with me. Those on standby, just watch us work.
Stay silent and wait.
You're asking me? I say it's time to move.
Don't hesitate.
Leave it to me.
I'll handle it.

handbook.promotionRecord: You wish to mediate between me and Leon, Doctor? I appreciate it, but that will not be necessary. I understand that it concerns you that he is avoiding me at Rhodes Island, but I assure you it is simply because he does not know how to treat me in an informal setting. We were family, after all, brothers who grew up together, the future Don and his advisor. Now, we are partners, friends who speak to each other as equals. It will take some time for him to get used to it, as well as hearing the name 'Bellone' in his ears, but he will get used to it. He must. We must all accept certain things that we cannot change, must we not? Leon has, after all, chosen a different path. No, I do not oppose Lavinia's ideas. They are very fine ideals, light and justice and all that. I fully believe that they will guide Nuova Volsinii and Siracusa toward a better future. You must understand that I was in charge of his education long before Lavinia came to the Bellones. The famiglia and Signor Bernardo groomed me to be its advisor, and I taught Leon everything I knew, raising him to be the leader I wanted the famiglia to have. Yes, we've had our disagreements, but what he believes in is essentially no different from what I believe in. I have simply walked too long in the rain, which is the reason for our differences. I could never abandon my famiglia, so long as they consider themselves that. On this, both Signor Bernardo and Leon have a leg up on me, possessing the resolve and determination that I lack. Still, I firmly believe that the Bellones and I have the right to exist, that we are needed. Where there is light, there is shadow. If you wish to breathe the fresh air after a rain, you must first accept the rain. It is true that I am a long way from the ideal leader I dream of. This doesn't matter. It was never what I aspired to be, and I will not change who I am now. I once placed all my hopes on Leontuzzo Bellone, but he will not become Don, and I will not be his advisor. This, I have accepted. In the distant future, I may become an advisor again—if someone proves that they will make a better Don than I am.
archives:
A young Lupo who always has a smile on his face, yet is nevertheless somehow quietly intimidating.
Operator Bellone's first visit to Rhodes Island caused a small uproar within HR, as we had previously written in Operator Vigil's file that Vigil was the 'last leader of Siracusa's Bellone Family'.
This misunderstanding was quickly cleared up: according to Operator Bellone's statement, the Bellones almost dissolved when Don Bernando died, and his heir Vigil left the old city to build Nuova Volsinii. The Family's power structure had fallen apart, and the remaining former Bellones were barely scraping by under pressure from other Families, unable to either return to a normal life or join another family and thus betray Bellone. That was when Demetri Certaldo decided to take up the mantle of the Don of the Bellone Family, taking those who had lost the family's protection under his wing.
Based on our current understanding of Siracusa, we are aware that his statement is missing quite a few details. Someone who was not the designated heir could hardly have inherited a family—even a declining one—without facing opposition both within and without. When asked about this, however, he deflected our questions with a smile.
'I grew up in the famiglia. The people there are like blood family to me, and I could never abandon them no matter what,' he said, and declined to elaborate further.
It is perhaps worth mentioning that Bellone ran into Chiave's gang at lunch that day. The always-jolly Chiave welcomed Bellone's arrival with his gang—to Bellone's apparent surprise, though he eventually assented to Chiave's eager (and rather physical) show of friendship with a smile. The scene seemed familiar, but also quite different from when Vigil first arrived.
An operator who was present recalled, 'It makes you realize how easy-going Vigil is by comparison. The smile never left Bellone's face, but for some reason I was really worried for Chiave the entire time.'

The Bellone Family staked a foothold in Nuova Volsinii through the Saluzzo Vino winery. Soon after Demetri Bellone and Alberto's deal, Alberto was arrested, and control of Saluzzo Vino fell into Bellone's hands. He has since made Saluzzo Vino stronger, establishing a dominant position in the local wine market following the Kazimierz-sponsored Red Wine Championship, and demonstrating the ability to compete with international brands from outside Siracusa.
In addition to wine, the Bellone Family has also invested in various industries in Nuova Volsinii, which are also growing at a breakneck pace. Although public data is not available, it is estimated that they are bringing the Bellone Family roughly the same revenue as Saluzzo Vino, perhaps even more. Yet there are also issues: most of these investments are in traditional mafia industries such as restaurants, bars, hotels, and moneylending—rarely involving the production of physical goods—inevitably leading to speculation that the Bellone Family is going back to the old ways in Nuova Volsinii. Furthermore, while Bellone's new investments are heavily staffed with Bellone members, Saluzzo Vino maintains a strong Saluzzo presence. Even setting aside potential problems caused by mafia members in corporate leadership, one cannot help but feel concerned as to whether the Saluzzo members truly accept Bellone leadership, and whether this arrangement will impact Rhodes Island's partnership with the Bellone Family.
An HR operator made a secret visit to Saluzzo Vino with these concerns in mind.
'Signor Bellone? He's a good man!
'We're still called Saluzzo Vino, aren't we? He said Saluzzo's only working with Bellone on a temporary basis. We're still Saluzzo, of course, and he even praised us for our loyalty, saying he was honored to be working with a famiglia like ours that respects tradition!
'Of course, we're in Nuova Volsinii now, and Signor Bellone told us to respect City Hall's policies, work hard, and follow the rules of the New Urban Management Act. I can tell you it took some getting used to. Back in the day, whenever I heard my terminal ring, the first thing I did wasn't pick up the call, but check my knife and gun. But I'm not even doing any brawling these days. I work fixed hours and go home for dinner with my wife and kids. I've got to admit, it's not such a bad feeling after all.
'Oh, of course I'm still part of the famiglia. We're all waiting for Don Saluzzo to get out of prison! I even asked Signor Bellone if there was a way to get him out. He said it would be hard to get his sentence reduced under the New Urban Management Act, but he would pull a few strings and make things more comfortable for him. Sure enough, when I visited the Don a couple of days ago, he had a cell to himself and seemed to have gotten a little plumper. I'm so grateful to Signor Bellone!
'I wasn't able to talk to the Don too much in the allotted time, so I just told him about how things had been going with us. He didn't say anything, but ended the visit with a smile. I'm sure he's very grateful to Signor Bellone too!'
The HR operator could not help but feel that something was not quite right. Seeing the Perro's bright smile, however, he could only follow Alberto Saluzzo's lead and smile back.

We are well aware that Demetri Certaldo was not groomed to become the next Don of the Bellone Family. His father had held an advisor position in the Bellones, and when he was killed in a mafia struggle, young Demetri was taken in by the Family and raised alongside Operator Vigil. This sort of arrangement is in line with what we know about Siracusan mafia tradition: having core members live together helps instill loyalty in those pegged for important Family positions in the future.
Demetri quickly accepted his role as Leontuzzo's advisor, taking care of his daily needs and teaching him everything he knew about the mafia, business, and fighting—essentially grooming the boy four years his junior to become the perfect leader, one who could take care of every member of the Family and protect their interests.
This should have ensured a smooth transition of power to Leontuzzo, until Bernardo's views on the Family began to change and he brought Lavinia—Operator Penance—into the Bellone Family. Under Lavinia's influence, Leontuzzo began to deviate from the path that Demetri had set for him. This was seen as a regrettable development, but an understandable one: for Leontuzzo, the scope of the 'family' had grown from a single Family to what is today all of Nuova Volsinii, and perhaps eventually all of Siracusa. The rules of the Family that he used to value had became the law and justice that Lavinia upheld.
Again, Operator Bellone's statement here seemed to omit many details, which we do not feel the need to delve deeper into, but there was a question we could not help but ask regarding Siracusan mafia tradition: is the Family's advisor normally expected to take care of the Don's daily needs?
Bellone did not answer.
We did, however, receive a valuable reference from another 'party concerned':
'Most advisors don't, but Demetri and I grew up together. He was a few years older, and he was used to taking care of me, while I was used to being taken care of. Or maybe... he was already showing his potential to become the Don, by seeing me as his famiglia and finding it perfectly natural that he should take care of me. He used to tell me that a Don should take care of his famiglia. I think he's doing a fine job of it.'

The announcement of the amendment to the New Urban Management Act sent shock waves throughout Nuova Volsinii. Most heavily impacted were the foreign corporations in the involved industries, whose stakeholders and investors expressed their dissatisfaction to City Hall. City Hall stood firm, however, and as a result some corporations have begun to adjust their business strategies based on the amendment's provisions. It was met with a generally positive response from local enterprises, who were long clamoring for its policies, as well as the general populace of Nuova Volsinii. Although some have noted that the amendment represents a form of protectionism, which could cause Siracusa's mafia traditions to once again rear their heads in the guise of local enterprises.
The full impact of the amendment on Nuova Volsinii remains to be seen, and we are keeping a close eye on further developments.
—Central Journal, International Edition

When Bellone finally stood before Signora Sicilia, he felt nothing but fear.
It was not her power that he feared. On the contrary, when he stood before her and saw her face clearly for the first time, he saw her sagging cheeks and sunken eye sockets, and the spots on her skin that not even heavy powdering could disguise. That was when he realized that the legends of Signora Sicilia he was so familiar with took place sixty years ago, and that the legendary matriarch had already entered her twilight years.
Her gaze was still strong, her movements elegant and confident, and her words soft yet impossible to refute or defy. The authority of Siracusa was still concentrated in her, but this only served to amplify his fear: all this power was centered on her, yet she was merely mortal. The order that she represented, the influence she wielded over the many Siracusan famiglie, and the deterrence her presence represented to other countries would all inevitably vanish upon her death. When the time came, would the famiglie still sit together and negotiate in the Grey Hall to resolve their conflicts? Or would Siracusa fall into chaos and desolation again?
'I don't give a damn what happens to Siracusa after I die,'
Signora Sicilia said as she ascended the steps of her manor. Her steps were slow, and seemingly steady, but she grabbed Bellone's arm with such strength that all he could say in response was, 'Please do not mention that word, Signora. You still have many years ahead of you.'
'The only people who love to bring up that word are the young who've never known death and the old for whom death is near. I know my own body best,' she smiled. 'The future does not belong to me. Whether it belongs to you—all of you—depends on you. Your idea is interesting, and you have shown respect by coming to see me before you act. Go. Go and try it out in Nuova Volsinii.'
His fear prevented Bellone from answering, but in that instant the faint notions in his mind became concrete and firm. He had wanted someone to show him a path he could simply follow. Now, he had to become the one leading the way, the one who saw it through to the end. He must build a new order.
There is little time left. For him, for them, and for Siracusa.

modules.moduleDescription:
Even now, as he blends drinks in his private bar in Nuova Volsinii, Demetri occasionally thinks back to the last time they were gathered around the dinner table of the Bellones' house.
He had met with his informant in the Famiglia Rossati earlier that day, and returned home to see the dinner table already set up. It was not a particularly special day, but it was a rare one: Leon was back from the Ministero dei Lavori Pubblici, and both Bernardo and Lavinia were home. Such occasions had become hard to come by.
He sat down in his usual seat and began to talk about the information he had garnered, but Bernardo took a glance at the look on Lavinia's face and interrupted him. He knew that Lavinia, unlike the other famiglia-backed judges, had her own ideas about the mafiosi of Siracusa, but assumed the day would eventually come when she truly became a part of Bellone. That Bernardo only meant that now was not the time.
He decided to give his report later that night. The information gathering operation had been Demetri's own idea. Bernardo had been giving him fewer orders recently, allowing him to act on his own judgment most of the time. The famiglie were stirring as the new city neared completion, and he felt the need to be aware of their movements. It was his duty as the advisor to the Bellones, after all. He would prove to Bernardo that he was worthy to carry the famiglia's future.
He carved the stewed meat with his knife and served the soup for the others. The heavy atmosphere brought about by his news of Rossati's movements had dissipated—Leon was chatting excitedly about what he saw at the Ministero dei Lavori Pubblici, with the occasional comment by Lavinia. Bernardo said little, but nodded from time to time. The Ministero dei Lavori Pubblici has long been closely watched by the famiglie, and those experiences were of no doubt mixed with bloodshed and violence, yet Leon's words seemed to carry hope and expectation, as though they were heralding a brand-new future that was completely different from the past.
Demetri thought his words were naive. Not that there was anything wrong with naivete, of course. It was only natural that the future Don should expand his horizons, so that when the time came to take over, he would have the vision to see the big picture and choose the best course of action. He would have to understand and take care of all of the famiglia's members, and ensure Bellone's continued prosperity. Though Leon's path had deviated somewhat from his expectations, Demetri had believed that he would groom Leon into the perfect Don, at which point he and his knife would become the Don's perfect tools.
Thinking back now, perhaps he was the truly naive one.
Demetri cuts the ice cube into a sphere with his knife, and places it into the glass. This knife has been with him for so many years and remains a useful instrument to this day; he is much the same.

Passive Effect: When a stone is triggered, deals <@ba.vup>{attack@atk_scale:0%}</> ATK as Arts damage to all enemies within 3 tiles, but only in directions parallel to any links said stone has, and reduces their Movement Speed by <@ba.vup>{display_move_speed:0%}</> for <@ba.vup>{attack@duration}</>s
Active Effect: Gain 2 stones

levels.name: All-Dominating Fight
levels.description:
Passive Effect: Stone trigger range and damage range expand, dealing <@ba.vup>{atk_scale:0%}</> ATK as Arts damage
Active Effect: <@ba.vdown>Stops attacking</> but <@ba.vup>Attack Range expands</>; grants <@ba.vup>{cnt}</> stones, then any stones above the limit <@ba.vup>are placed within Attack Range, prioritizing tiles with enemies</>; when manually placing stones within Attack Range, stones can be placed <@ba.vup>on tiles with enemies</> and <@ba.vup>Talent 1 deploys up to 3 additional stones</> at the cost of an equal amount of ammo
<@ba.rem>Skill activation grants {trigger_time} ammo, skill ends when manually deactivated or stones are depleted, any ammo remaining is refunded as stones</>
