CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: It has been centuries since the post of Great Yan's Weiqi Attendant was discontinued, and yet you… You simply wished for me to help you in managing these documents? No, I do not understand what you mean by 'can't be in two places at once'.

If you require someone to share your burden during my time on Rhodes Island, I shall do my utmost. Though there is no need to ask me for advice on medical company work... You wish for a round of hand-talk? There is no need to rush, until the day you take your first step on the Dao of weiqi.

The Dao of weiqi is abstruse, but in the end, it is merely a game. You will not learn of military tactics or political maneuvers upon the gridded board. I have seen no small number of people who enjoy making such fantastical claims. As for the story of the general sitting in his camp, breaking his enemy with ease during a game of hand-talk… According to the Laws of Yan, a general making such merry during wartime is to be beheaded.

I have never seen my younger brothers and sisters act in so ridiculous a fashion before. It seems they have plenty of time to waste now that this affair is over. No need to inform them I am here. So long as they can live together happily like this… You have already informed them?

Through a thirst for victory, seek peace. In this point, and this point only, can it be said warfare is connected to weiqi. People seek egress from all sorts of unbearable struggles, yet it is thus that they can speak of their future. I cannot read your future, but I believe the choices you make are in accordance with the proper moves on the board.

That game with It has come to a close, all resentment, gains, and losses stricken from the ledger. Can it be considered victory? We have paid a bitter enough price simply to find our place upon this earth. Surely you too understand the weight of the word 'decision'… One must have no regrets after placing a stone, but can one truly be free of regret?

We no longer obsess over leaving something behind. The exception is our masteries, which each of us has spent more than a thousand years honing. They are worthy footnotes in the fickle realm of humanity, and it would be a pity to lose them to oblivion... The fact that they may leave things behind is, for most parts, a treasure, though far be it from me to pass down knowledge.

Quibbling over seniority is inherently ridiculous for us. Not even in ordinary families would you see an elder brother make every single decision for his younger siblings. You do not need to act as my elder brother's messenger. Once this game is over, I shall go to dinner. I am aware Yu is manning the kitchen today.

I have calculated every possible outcome, yet I cannot see a conclusion where these muddy waters run clear once more. But I know she is still there. A move in a weiqi record, a page in a history book. This simple faith shall suffice… You do not need to question my determination. Surely you too have people you care for.
…After our parting, the blizzard-lashed night outside my window…

You are Dr. {@nickname}? I am honored to finally meet you. As you've already met many of my siblings, I shall not belabor my introduction. I am Wang, a former strategist. As for our earlier encounters… Let us consider them not worth mentioning.
Do you truly wish for me to point out all the flaws I see here?

The weiqi players of Yan are divided into nine ranks, from the Ninth Clumsy Defender Rank to the First Nearly Divine Rank. As you are now, your prowess should grant you the rank of… This is meant to denote my rank? Preposterous…
There has only ever been 'me'.
Have your strategies plotted beforehand. You should know how the battle will end before it begins.
You truly wish to entrust this authority to me…?
Three Armies, heed these orders: we march.
Come, take your seats.
Spare them or slay them. The choice is yours.
Simply place your stone. Why ask me?
Observe the entirety of the board. There is no one point that decides victory.
You have been drawn into my plans.
Warmongering as ever. Even now, you have learned nothing.
You will not escape this jie so easily.
Admit defeat now, and spare yourself the embarrassment.
…Why must you insist on struggling?!
…I am content.
Take it away. I have no need for battle reports.
Such blunderous command.
Guileful moves indeed… Another game, what say you?!
…This is much more spacious than my last dwelling.
…Remain silent while you spectate.
I have some spare time today, so I do not mind a game.
Arknights.

Its name is Sui, or 'age'. It seems the people of antiquity knew that time is a terrifying, evil beast. All things are worn away by its passage. I too do not know how much longer I will remember her. Before my memory leaves me… Yes, no need for further urging. I shall come and eat now.
Doctor. I have heard from others that you are not accustomed to rising early.

I have not prepared any curios to offer you upon your birthday. Some seek out pearl shells from the southern depths to make stones and fragrant nutmeg-yew wood from the northern ridges to make boards, but such luxuries will not help them play any better… I grant you this ancient record of a game. Since you now understand the Dao of weiqi, you shall be able to discern the thoughts present on the board. The player? Nothing more than an obsessive like yourself.

You have chosen the most difficult game in this realm to play, but if this is enough to make you consider a retreat, then you have surrendered all chance of victory… Merely a warning from someone who once walked the tightrope and lost it all, whatever that may be worth. Do not fret. By my reckoning, this game is still far from over, and there are still many variables at play.

handbook.profile: Wang, former military advisor to Yan, now an unemployed weiqi player. Younger brother to Chongyue, and older brother to Nian, Dusk, Ling, etc. He came to Rhodes Island to recuperate at Chongyue's recommendation, and is occasionally consulted on tactical matters.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.00u/L
Look! The readings just went off the charts, before dropping back to zero... the instruments were working just fine a moment ago. What happened?
—Surprised Medic

...I asked the Doctor. Just write a zero.
—Warfarin, looking up at the ceiling with despondent eyes
handbook.promotionRecord:
'A beast shrinks long and lone. A miser's shadow cold.
It takes its number second. Black and white at odds.
Finds solitude in stone. It dwells on countless paths.
But its schemes are finite. Desolate out and in.
Alas, alack. Its stones could be no gems, its wood is no fine grain.
All thought and schemes. It seeks a life in death.
How could it not know? A part fights the whole, defying the land's law. It may endure awhile, yet peril will come.
It writhes and wracks in ruin. Its spirit thin, it leaves its kin, it takes rebuke.
It breaks its flesh; now the tide is turned. A thousand years; the wish is fulfilled.
Now scattered to the winds like mist. Haze waters far and still.
Through the turning of day and night, between heaven and earth, only cold stones and a broken board.'

The text of the rubbing is often corrupted in its frequent transcriptions. At the time of the most recent comparison, a slow yet irreversible change was found to have already begun in the stele's physical material.
archives:
Following the monumental event that occurred in Baizao, Nian and her siblings began to spend more time on Rhodes Island, with a marked improvement in their moods—Chongyue being the sole exception. He spent little time on the ship, only coming back to check on his siblings from time to time before setting out again.
It was during this time that Wang showed up at the reception, on an otherwise completely unremarkable afternoon.
'I would like to speak to the supervisor here,' he said.
The impression he gave was that of a quiet, peaceful, and polite man, very different from the sinister and dangerous image from the rumors.
Wang remained on Rhodes Island as a guest, and we agreed to his request not to tell his siblings. After all, Rhodes Island is much bigger now, and surely it was not so likely to accidentally run into someone... until one day Wang vanished into thin air as he was walking along a corridor. It turned out that he had walked right into a painting that Dusk had planted, and emerged an hour later with his head hanging dejectedly, followed by Nian with a gleeful smile on her face, Dusk with her eyes red, Shu with a worried look, and Yu whose sleeves were wet with tears...
We do not know if Wang could have seen through Dusk's little trick, nor did we witness their reunion. All we know is that Wang stopped avoiding his family from that day forth.
Families inevitably have their little squabbles, of course. One day, someone overheard the normally carefree Ling berate Wang, saying, 'You want to hide, that's your own business, but couldn't you have had the decency to at least write to Chongyue? Have you any idea how hard he was looking for you?'
That was when Chongyue showed up and said something to her, which seemed to calm her down a little. Finally, she sighed and turned around to leave with a flick of her sleeves. No one knew whether she had let it go or meant something else.
Wang is rarely disturbed on Rhodes Island, other than for important festivals, family reunions, or when a sibling forces his dorm door open, and he rarely speaks even at such occasions other than when spoken to, seldom answering questions not from family members unless they are to his liking. He usually sits in his room, gazing at the weiqi board in front of him. It looks as though he is daydreaming, but one can plainly see his thoughts stirring in his heterochromatic eyes.

We thought he had fulfilled his dreams, but it seems like he has even more to worry about now, both for the greater good and for personal interest. He can't let either go... Bring him this rice cake. He seems to have gotten even thinner lately.
—Shu

Wang's fame as the greatest weiqi master in Yan is known to many on Rhodes Island even before his arrival, and quite a few of them can hardly resist the urge to have a game of weiqi with him. Fortunately, though he usually looks unapproachable, he rarely turns down an invitation to play weiqi. Even if he has been lost in thought just seconds before, all you need to do is knock on the door and ask if he'd like to have a game. By the time you step inside, the board is already set up.
Many operators have challenged him, but few have sniffed even a single victory—hardly surprising, considering Yu's skill in cooking and Dusk's skill in painting. Closure once tried to challenge Wang by connecting all of Rhodes Island's support robots in parallel (Friston-3 declined to participate out of dignity, but spectated the match with great interest). When faced with the choice of tapping ZOOT's reserve computing power and just pulling the circuit breaker, she wisely chose the latter.
Outside of Closure, there is someone else equally obsessed with challenging Wang, and that someone is none other than Zuo Le. Although he was no longer required to keep a close eye on the proxies, Zuo Le felt obliged to play a round with Wang. A few months later, when Grain Buds asked him about the result, he scratched his head abashedly, saying he was not yet ready. It turns out that he only knew the basics of of weiqi, and had never had the time to truly study it. Compared with Wang who had pursued the art of strategy for nearly a thousand years, he was naturally outmatched.
Finally, Nian arranged for a game between Zuo Le and Wang handicapped at nine stones in Zuo Le's favor. Unsurprisingly, Zuo Le lost handily, but there were more twists and turns than expected. Wang started out playing aggressively, but he began to tone it down once he realized that Zuo Le had no answer, nor was he attempting to duel as equals—he was simply there to learn from the superior player. Wang ended up giving Zuo Le a small spot in the corner, so that the final score would not look too bad.
Wang became less guarded against operators from Yan after this game of weiqi.

To Wang, playing weiqi with someone is like being in a fight to the death, or living together with the opponent for years. He can tell all your secrets, as well as what you're thinking. Perhaps he saw in the Candleholder's moves that Yan's current stance toward us is genuine, and was thus convinced to let down his guard. Good news, I say.
—Ling

[Classified Log]
I never thought the problem would be solved in such a manner... or at least delayed from a pressing threat to one we will not have to worry about again for another millennium or so.
'Wa Stone', 'Bu Fan', the Jingyu Prime Vein... the first Originium gave Yan the power to vassalize the gods and contain the Feranmuts, and the capital to catch up during the Crystal Age. These gifts should have blown up in Yan's face just as what happened in Ursus, but that was nullified by a Feranmut with inextricable ties to the nation. With the first Originium gone, the Jingyu Prime Vein's Originium growth rate has entered an irreversible decline, but overall, it remains far more stable than the Kolossal Prime Vein, giving Yan's industry plenty of time to transition, and helping Yan avoid the same chaos that engulfed Ursus. A stable Yan is good for the stability of Higashi, Rim Billiton, Kazdel, and Ursus as well. This does not even take into account the turmoil that was successfully avoided, the calamity that the first Orignium should have caused... He really did achieve the greater good, and bought valuable time for the land.
As natives of Terra, the paracausal nature of Feranmuts is inherently incompatible with how Originium stores information. The Feranmut will eventually succumb to the Originium, but until then, there is no safer box than the interior of a Feranmut for storing Orginium and cutting it off from its controller.
This does not come without a price, of course. Kroos's report, official Yanese communications, and Ju's statement all indicate that it took all of Ya's lifeforce to plant the first Originium into the bestial Sui. In addition, whatever consciousness it is that is now in control of the bestial Sui will suffer from extreme, unbearable, endless pain.
Wang as he is on Rhodes Island is currently no more than a weiqi stone. I'm not saying he's incomplete—after all, these are Feranmuts we are talking about, and the Wang we see is certainly Wang in his entirety. What I'm saying is that, as he plays weiqi with you, he is also being constantly tormented deep beneath Baizao, which explains the abnormal crystal density readings from his checkup: at times, it was the weiqi stone you saw; at others, it was the Feranmut, slowly but surely crystallizing from the wound.

[Audio Log]
The writing knife?
Do not ask me. It does not belong to me. It is none of my business that she entrusted it to Jun, who entrusted it to the young lady. There is only one thing that I regret about the knife, and I found the answer in the Tomb of Sui.
As for the powers of the knife... most of us do not intentionally create objects of power, with the exception of Nian. The objects associated with us came to be as a result of our influence over a long period of time, just like It unconsciously created the geists from inside Its tomb... It would not have suffered mundane wine cups, paperweights, and cutlery to be imbued with the power of evolution too, if It were awake and aware.
Yes, this box for storing weiqi stones is similar to the writing knife. Once, it was no more than an ordinary box. The influence of Sui caused it to take the form of a beast a century ago, making it the perfect container for the hundred and eighty-one black stones. All the stones are gone now, save for the one in front of you, but it sought me out after my awakening and would not leave my side after it found me, so I allowed it to stay.
Let us speak of things that are truly worth our time. I do not need your hollow praise—all I want to know is who made Originium, and who is trying to take away everything that Originium gave to this land. What is their ultimate goal, and how will it affect me and my family?
(Recording interrupted)
...I appreciate your candor.
I will continue my calculations based on the information you provided. Come to me immediately if there is any new development.
Why do I do this?
I believe my siblings have already told you the answer, or demonstrated it through action. For my part, I have unfinished business—
You wish to help?
...
That's enough talk. We can continue the game if you want to play. If you've had enough, surrender, and we'll do it another day.

modules.moduleDescription:
The 'cloudbeast' picks up a white piece, drops it on the board, then leaps onto the incense burner, looking at Wang with a meow.
This is his new weiqi partner, formerly the container for his weiqi stones. Though now in beast form, it is well-versed at the game after spectating matches for centuries. However...
After a few turns, Wang captures a major piece and secures a victory. The 'cloudbeast' immediately jumps down from the burner, crashing onto the board and sending the stones flying everywhere.
Wang rarely bothers trying to handle it. Once it is done venting its anger, it picks up the pieces before finding a suitable napping spot—as a mere container, it is only natural for it to act like this.
......
Yet, it is the only source of noise in the room.
The cloudbeast falls asleep on Wang's lap, and only silence is left, a silence he is more than familiar with.
All is silent, as if imprisoned in the old temple.
With the board before him and the container beside, he finds himself stricken with countless sorrows and worries.
In his heart there is only the occasional pain from the crystals, that turn into clock hands moving in slow motion.
The 'cloudbeast' rolls over and stretches inside the sleeve of Wang's robe, using his hand as a pillow as it returns to its dreams.
He had given life to the container and stones, but how they perceive the realm could not be any more different.
Perhaps its life on the sidelines as an outside observer has granted it a sort of optimism.
While even the most careful of strategists can find themselves lost in a labyrinth, one can save oneself from such a fate with an outsider's view of the situation.
It has still managed to find this solitary stone, ever since Wang replaced Sui. Was it because the container would lose any significance and struggle to take form without him?
Or is it only by leaving the stones inside the container that he can calm himself down and stay composed?
The stone stays silent as the container warms his cold hand.
The warmth is its answer: he was never alone.
Not only it, but everything in his room on Rhodes Island also serves as a constant reminder: Yi personally placed the potted plant on his desk, Dusk painted the ever-shifting patterns on the curtains, the burner was Nian's work, the incense within chosen by Fāng, and the box of food next to it was full of tangerine cakes made by Yu...
After centuries of solitude, his siblings and even his own creation implore him to change.
This match, he gladly concedes.
His hand, now warm from the 'cloudbeast' earlier, reaches out to open the box of food, and he takes out a cake. He eats most of it and gives the rest to the 'cloudbeast' still fast asleep on his lap.
It opens its eyes and sniffs the pastry before it, before giving the treat a cautious lick. It then buries its head in Wang's palm, eating it all and leaving no crumbs behind.
Wang has never shown any kindness to geists, but when this abandoned waregeist returned to his side, all his thoughts and plots turned only to sighs, and he has never managed to shake off or escape from this 'helpless' thing since.
With a soft sigh, he leaves his hand on the now-snoring 'cloudbeast' as he returns his gaze to the board, beginning his endless plotting.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: So, do you want a bodyguard, or a cop to watch you work 24/7? Just joking. I haven't forgotten how you do things here.

It's Rhodes Island's visitor logs? Swire, Hoshiguma, and Lin too… Right, assuming they're always asking about me, but there's no way they're coming this much for—Hm. I know a lot of people are waiting for me. It's not too bad, being on someone's mind.

Worried about my health? Guess we ought to be checking up on each other, Doctor. I've been through a lot these past few years, time sure does fly. The more you experience, the easier it is to fall into confusion and helplessness. Sometimes I do need a reminder… my time is not infinite.

Oh, you've noticed my blade? I was told it can erase history's mistakes, but that's practically half of whatever's been archived in the last thousand years, and there's no way a single blade could clean that all up. Let's look to the future instead—the ideals we seek still lie ahead.

I followed her and Reunion to many places, and saw many sacrifices made. The people went from being lost and fragmented to becoming united and awakened—on that long and winding road. Many of them were left behind in the huge blaze in Deity Grypherburg, yet it was this very fire that ignited their hope.

We're a long way from a place where everyone is treated equally, and I have no clue if I'm any nearer to this goal. But I've never doubted the equality I envision is real, for when we step up to rage against the injustice we see, we prove it exists.

I've been back to Lungmen a few times. Other than the loss of my favorite cheongfun shop, the changes are nice to see. There are fewer L.G.D. patrols on the streets, and you hear less talk of the slums… There's no lying to myself and pretending I don't care for the city.

I asked that man why my mother and sister had to suffer, and unsurprisingly, I didn't get the answer I was looking for. It's too bad Chi Xiao can't sever blood ties, and this writing knife can't scrape away recorded history either. There's no granting any forgiveness in their stead, no one is worth sacrificing for any 'greater good', ever.

When things calm down, it would be nice to take you around Yan. Not just Lungmen, and not for any investigations either. Just a trip to watch the people make something from nothing in that beautiful land. There's nowhere else like it. You won't have to pack anything either. A sword and a boat. That's all we'll need.
Need a break, but can't sleep? Yeah, you have a lot of pressure on your shoulders. Sit up straight. I'll teach you some Yanese breathing exercises.
Long time no see, Doctor. I know things have gotten pretty serious, so I'm back to lend a hand. In case you need a reminder, I'm still with Rhodes Island.
This battle… Rhodes Island was there too?
You have a lot of people who trust in your command, and depend on you to direct them… that's important to keep in mind.
I spent a long time mastering Chi Xiao's techniques, but the answer I got was different from the lessons I was taught. Chi Xiao has seen my determination, and when you need it, it will never waver.
Doesn't feel too unfamiliar yet.
Don't worry, I wasn't always on my own these past few years.
Move out. I'll make sure no one gets left behind.
Suppression by force isn't an option on this field.
Fear not the power of this blade.
I know very well why I draw this sword.
I'll stop all evil in its tracks.
Chi Xiao, unsheath—
As move unsheathing blade, cleave now as cleft.
As move at teardrop's point, once known be deft.
As sword of stratus rent, once stood stand fast!
As sword of heaven's plaint, bid dawn as cast.
Nicely done, Doctor… you're mistaken. That light in the sky wasn't from my swordplay.
One day, we won't have to make right with might.
They'd best take this chance to repent.
Come on, don't lose heart over one setback.
Furnishings haven't changed. Nice.
Doctor, careful you don't poke yourself with the end of my blade.
You don't have to ask—I'm the same old Ch'en, haven't changed one bit.
Arknights.

I've seen many different kinds of new years. Once, I watched a group take shelter under huge Originium clusters, promising each other everything would get better while they clinked muddy cups of water together, silently waiting for the sunrise… it's nothing, Doctor. This day only comes once a year, so let's go celebrate with the others.
Doctor, you haven't changed one bit.

Perfect timing, Doctor. Here's a Bolívarian wood carving, a Victorian tea set, and an Ursine... I'm not asking you to choose, they're all for you. It's been a few years since we've seen each other, so I owe you a few birthday presents. Don't be shy. Happy birthday, Doctor.

I remember the first time I collaborated with Rhodes Island. A difficult fight, but a single Black Snake is nothing to worry about. What's scary is the countless villains out there who use despair to force people into doing their bidding. There's no winning our fights with brute force alone, so we have to keep improving ourselves.

Once, I watched a group take shelter under huge Originium clusters, promising each other everything would get better while they clinked muddy cups of water together, silently waiting for the sunrise… it's nothing, Doctor. This day only comes once a year, so let's go celebrate with the others.
Doctor, you haven't changed one bit.

Perfect timing, Doctor. Here's a Bolívarian wood carving, a Victorian tea set, and an Ursine... I'm not asking you to choose, they're all for you. It's been a few years since we've seen each other, so I owe you a few birthday presents. Don't be shy. Happy birthday, Doctor.

Worried about my health? Guess we ought to be checking up on each other, Doctor. I've been through a lot these past few years, time sure does fly. The more you experience, the easier it is to fall into confusion and helplessness. Sometimes I do need a reminder… my time is not infinite.

Oh, you've noticed my blade? I was told it can erase history's mistakes, but that's practically half of whatever's been archived in the last thousand years, and there's no way a single blade could clean that all up. Let's look to the future instead—the ideals we seek still lie ahead.

We're a long way from a place where everyone is treated equally, and I have no clue if I'm any nearer to this goal. But I've never doubted the equality I envision is real, for when we step up to rage against the injustice we see, we prove it exists.

handbook.profile:
Ch'en, former Lungmen superintendent and former head of the L.G.D.'s Special Inspection Unit, graduated from the Victorian Royal Guard Academy with superb marks and outstanding achievements. During her time with the Department, she cracked down on crime, fought violent offenders, tracked down armed fugitives, and brought down international criminals.
Having resigned from the L.G.D., she is now officially a member of Rhodes Island. In accordance with her wishes, she is mainly assigned to provide field operators adequate support and on-location guidance.
She continues to fight on the frontlines as a Rhodes Island Operator.
handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 6%
Small traces of crystallization are visible on Operator Ch'en's body surface.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.21u/L

Ch'en's condition has deteriorated since her last checkup. We know her resolve and understand her reasons, but she must take better care of herself...
—Sussurro

You know how she is. Oripathy or not, she'll never listen.
—Warfarin
handbook.promotionRecord:
I saw a village burned to the ground in the north. The charred remains stood out in the white snow. There were signs of fighting, and bodies of both uninfected and infected people. I'm not sure what happened there.
Are such scenes a regular sight in Ursus?
Did you see the same thing when you were in Ursus, all those years ago?

Received communication from Rhodes Island. Something has happened to the Doctor's team. HQ has sent a special task force to Ursus, and I have a feeling you'll run into them again.
Security is really tightening in the Far North. I was thoroughly questioned and searched just walking into an ordinary hotel today.
There are a lot of movements from many different directions. I do not yet have a clear view... but I'll get to the bottom of it.

Received a letter from Madam Fumizuki yesterday...
The events in the Far North were just the beginning. Ursus is facing an even greater crisis. If the events truly have implications across all of Terra, as the Doctor predicted, Yan will not stand idly by, and Wei Yenwu certainly will not. He will do something.
Should I...

Back in Victoria, you encouraged me to do what I had already made up my mind to do. I found you again, but we still do not know the truth. Mother, your father, that pathetic man, and Wei Yenwu... We should have been told the truth about what happened. We have a right to know. Perhaps you don't care anymore, but I can't cast it aside so easily.
Someone told me that those old folks were young and ambitious once. What happened to them? Their ambitions grew rusty, and the only thing they have left is silence, keeping them from telling the truth... I must go back, to Lungmen, to Baizao. If they will not tell the truth, I will find it myself.
I ran away many times, but I don't plan on running away forever—you didn't run away either, did you?
Heaven burned red over Grypherburg that night... the fire on the ground burned for a long time. Buildings were collapsing, and other things were collapsing with them. The stubborn stone split apart in the fire, and light shone out through the crack... I still see the fire when I close my eyes, and it gives me the courage to walk toward the truth.
I think I'm ready. I'm going back.
...Can you hear it, Tal?
I'm going back.

[The letters are neatly folded, but were never sent.]
archives:
'Broken shields have been melted down into plowshares. The fire in the furnace has changed.
'The name Reunion is increasingly used to refer to a village, rather than a group of Infected.
'Oversight? I have my duty as an operator of Rhodes Island, but this is also a personal commitment for me. What is different about Nine's 'fairness'? What judgment will Talulah receive? Will a reborn Reunion truly light a lasting fire of hope in the snowstorm? Someone must bear witness, and it should be me. It must be me.'

Following the Londinium incident, Ch'en traveled throughout Ursus, from the disputed region at the Ursus-Kazimierz Border, to the Grypherburg region, to the distant north... We later learned that Ch'en operated like a Messenger, braving martial law, harsh weather, and magnetic storms to cross the tundra, establishing the basic framework of an intelligence network for Rhodes Island. Outside of the task force that the Doctor and Amiya personally led, Ch'en was our most reliable and stable source of information in the Ursus region. Ch'en's aptitude in intelligence gathering, already on display in Lungmen, provided invaluable help to Rhodes Island.

[Classified Log]
Ch'en did not conceal the fact that she met with Talulah's group, witnessing them unite a group of Infected on the tundra and establish a village by the name of Reunion. To Reunion, she was candid about her role, exercising oversight in her personal capacity, procuring necessary supplies, and sharing some Rhodes Island-compiled intel with them... Her stance raised some concerns amongst the operators—when the one we need to trust is the controversial figure at the heart of the Chernobog Incident, any interaction should be subject to greater scrutiny.
In the end, we gave Ch'en our tacit approval after extensive discussion. Ch'en has undoubtedly become an important and trustworthy member of Rhodes Island, demonstrating her oversight responsibility with concrete action, and helping the new Reunion take crucial first steps toward winning trust.

'The children look forward to Hui-chieh's visits. Although supplies are never plentiful, they have been learning to sew teddy bears because they think she loves them after she was seen gazing at a teddy bear, lost in thought.'
'I know a lot of the resources and news that Ch'en brought came from Rhodes Island, and I understand your reservations about me. I can't guarantee that there will be a perfect ending, nor do I expect us to truly understand one another, but I guarantee that Reunion will not repeat its old mistakes. Your torch is not the only one that burns bright. There are those who carry it into the darkest night, so that it may illuminate others.'

A great snowstorm struck many places in Yan, the likes of which had not been seen for a century. The snow lasted months, covering the land in white, and making the bright red figure traveling upon it particularly conspicuous. Rumors speak of a swordswoman who has been journeying across the land since last year, fighting for justice with her sword. She helped rebuild ruined houses in Baizao, punished bandits in Danyan, and cleared clogged water channels in Jiangqi... is she on some sort of quest? There are many differing opinions: some say she often asked those she helped where the local library was, and infer that she was seeking some secret tome that would allow her to break through a bottleneck in her training; others have seen her visit cemeteries, and believe her to be following the trail of a departed friend; and others claim that she often visited the sites where schools and colleges once stood, and hypothesize that she is a Tianshi, sent by the Ministry of Rites to investigate ancient sites... The only consensus is that there is no consensus. Some martial arts schools claimed her to be one of their students, only for the claim to be immediately shot down—'You're full of crap! She doesn't even know your dialect. How could she have studied there for decades?' Others have tried to challenge her to a duel. The first challenger recalls that she readily accepted his challenge, but he was stunned when she spoke a line straight out of a kung fu film. She was clearly unfamiliar with the modern-day martial arts landscape of Yan. Subsequent challengers were no longer met with the same flowery lines. My investigation indicates that our heroine has moved north, and it remains to be seen whether we will see her emerge in Dahuang or Lungmen next. I would like to close this column with a word of advice... challenging her is really not for the faint of heart, or anyone who is not supremely confident in their skills! —Excerpt from Jianghu Monthly, Issue 02, 1103 [Classified Log] Ch'en's request for field assignment in Yan is hereby approved. The Tomb of Sui incident carries tremendous significance for both Yan and Terra as a whole. For Yan, it meant the resolution of a thousand-year affliction; for Terra, it was a relief to know that the Jingyu Prime Vein was not being depleted at nearly the same rate as the Kolossal Prime Vein, even though neither Rhodes Island nor Yan has been able to conclusively determine the current state of the first Originium. That does not mean, however, that Yan can fully escape this Terra-wide crisis. We had not previously made any association between Ch'en's matter and that of the Feranmuts. It was only when her identity and her 'family matter' became known to us that we realized her 'family matter' was, essentially, the family matter of Yan... Ch'en did not return to Yan's center of power following the resolution of the crisis at Baizao, instead opting to wander the lands in search of traces of a departed Sui proxy. Her reasons for taking up this responsibility are clearly linked to the writing knife that she obtained during her trip to Baizao. 'From Baizao to Shangshu, to Yumen and Lungmen... from south to north, from the heartlands to the frontiers, I discovered many traces that the proxy left behind. If she managed to bring writing and history to such distant lands back then, perhaps the land of fairness and justice we are seeking really does exist after all.'

In the reports about the Tomb of Sui incident that the Yanese operators submitted, nothing caught our attention more than the account of Ch'en stopping Yumen with a single swing of her sword. According to Zuo Le, Ch'en cut power to all of Yumen in an instant using nothing more than a tiny writing knife, buying crucial time for him to neutralize the remaining artillery positions. Nian's account, on the other hand, was rather different: 'She was muttering something like As sword of heaven's plaint, bid dawn as cast, then there was a gust of sandstorm, and then Yumen just stopped. What do you mean my statement was as vague and incomprehensible as my films? You can ask the others if you don't believe me—did you hear that, Shu? They don't believe me!' Her shouting caught the attention of the other Yanese operators present. Mr. Nothing heard the story, waved his fan, and walked away with a profound expression on his face. It took only a few days for the legend of how Ch'en stopped Yumen with a single swing to spread throughout Rhodes Island. And so, the next time Ch'en returned to Rhodes Island and walked into the training room, she saw every pair of curious eyes in the room fixated on her... After learning what had happened, Ch'en agreed to do a demonstration in the outdoor training grounds. But she did not draw Chi Xiao—instead, she made the gesture of a sword with her fingers, turned her wrists, stepped forward, lowered her shoulder, and swung upwards lightly—there was no breathtaking aura, but the wind began to blow, stirring up sand and dust. A few seconds later, the sandstorm cleared, and the clouds parted to reveal the sun. It took a little while for the spectators to process what had just happened. The move seemed utterly unremarkable, yet clearly extraordinary. What made it so powerful? No one dared ask, seeing the solemn expression on Ch'en's face. Observing from the side, Qiubai and Yun Qingping revealed the secret— 'It was like a ray of light breaking through the clouds, but still connected to the soil on the ground.' 'My master once said that mindset was the most important thing to the Chi Xiao style. The swing just now was very different from the traditional finishing move of Chi Xiao. If the philosophy of Lord Wei's sword is to strike with no regret, Miss Ch'en's sword represents the admission and acceptance of regret, to press forward regardless of regret.' 'That's what makes Ch'en different from Chief Wei.' 'What's that supposed to mean? Did you understand a word of that, stinking rat?' '...There was already a hint of that move in her sword when she was in Yumen.' 'Yumen? She was in Yumen when you were there? ...Hey, why aren't you saying anything? Why are you walking away? Did you really understand that? Wait up!' 'Take it easy, Missy—the move sends the message that Ch'en never gives up partway.' As sword of heaven's plaint, bid dawn as cast. Never fear, never waver, long though the journey be. The light shines through when the clouds part. One must overcome the obstacles of one's own heart to fully comprehend the way of the sword. The sword begins and ends with the heart, but the spirit of the sword lingers. Those who fail to act because something seems impossible shall lose their spirit, and their sword lose its soul. —This segment has been rewritten many times; Ch'en says she is still working on it

As Ch'en sent back more and more reports during her time in Ursus, we set up a dedicated storage area for them at the Doctor's suggestion. Reviewing these reports made us realize just how long Ch'en has been with us. From Summary of Conditions in Lungmen Slums and Tripartite Investigation Report of the Governments of Dossoles and Bolívar, to Development of Law and Order in Columbia and Challenges in Implementation and Overview of Victorian Dukes and Tara, to the recent reports on Ursus and Yan, these are not just raw intelligence collected by Ch'en, but also focused and astute observations and commentaries made by someone embarking on a long journey. They are of great significance to both Rhodes Island and Ch'en herself. The fact that Ch'en is part of Yan's imperial bloodline is no longer a secret on Rhodes Island, but she has not been shunned or approached because of it. Perhaps it is because she has already left a deep impression fighting alongside the others as a former Lungmen cop, or perhaps it is because the significance of her bloodline pales in comparison to her experiences across Terra. While Ch'en keeps her distance from the Yanese government, it does not mean she no longer cares about the country. She has never truly left Yan—or rather, she has never truly left Lungmen. She is still searching for a land of fairness and justice, and she hopes that she will find it in the soil that she stands upon, but she is not bound by this land, nor by any other. For us, the most valuable thing about Ch'en has never been her position, but her will and direction. She does not belong entirely to Rhodes Island, but her goal of seeking a land of fairness and justice aligns closely with Rhodes Island's mission. Operators who have gone on field missions with her say that there is a sort of certainty about Ch'en that is reassuring—she understands what she is seeking, and has never wavered. While the concepts of fairness and justice may differ somewhat from language to language and context to context, they ultimately point toward the same conviction: a belief in a better tomorrow. We all believe that Terra will become better than it is today. 'Officer Ch'en—no, Ch'en is our comrade and kindred spirit, one of Rhodes Island's most important partners. Of that there is no doubt. Elite operator? Ahem... she understands what she wants all too well, and our paths will not necessarily always be aligned—of course, a consistent presence at headquarters or squad operation has never been a criterion for elite operator selection... Perhaps you could ask her yourself the next time she comes back?'

modules.moduleDescription:
As the chaos from the Sui incident subsides, the scriptgeists vanished, though the damage done to the city remains.
Collapsed walls are moved away, and overturned shelves propped upright, as scrolls of artwork and calligraphy sit in a neat pile near the rubble. Right beside is a plaque split into two, bearing characters that read 'Study of the Wordseekers'.
According to Ch'en Chao-ch'ien, this is one of Baizao's finest book repositories, and something of a historical gem. More importantly, rumors say it houses a vast collection of works discovered by those seeking the truth behind the bestial Sui's incident a hundred and twenty years ago that caused the characters on the ancient records to vanish. The owner Mr. Huang is also an antique connoisseur, and despite Baizao's many changes, he still keeps this placed unchanged even today.
'So, which books among the remainder do you consider a vestige of her?'
After digging out so many books from the ruins that she had lost count, Ch'en cannot help but pose the question as she catches her breath.
'Maybe all, or maybe none.' After hours of physical labor, Ch'en Chao-ch'ien mutters her reply, a trace of irritation in her voice. 'Maybe the traces she left behind aren't in any book or scroll, and we'll only get to see her again once every hole in history has been patched up.'
'Every hole in history...'
Ch'en Hui-chieh, new to Yan's extensive history and literature, does not quite grasp how heavy that sentence is.
After the recent turmoil over the past few days, Ch'en Hui-chieh now holds a genuine respect for the individual who has guarded Yan's writings and history for nearly a thousand years, but a doubt still flashes through her mind—should people even be bringing a deceased person back to life? And by going to such lengths?
Ch'en picks up another scroll from the ruins. A simple yet ancient painting of a mountain village. Huge splashes of ink depict a village surrounded by lush mountains, but a huge empty sky leaves the composition somewhat unbalanced, making her wonder if the negative space was left deliberately for something to be written in.
'Good work, ladies. Please, take a break.' Mr. Huang comes over with two cups of tea and snacks to reward the two women helping him out.
'Sir, do you know what scenery this painting is meant to be depicting?'
'Hmm... now this is a strange one. The trees look like those you'd see in the north, but the design of the homes is what you'd find in the south. As for where you might find this particular view...'
Perhaps this is what the study before her looked like, before it was reduced to ruins.
That is the nature of history—it is not passed on so easily. It can be unconsciously forgotten, or even consciously erased. And sometimes, it is more than just a view or a few names lost.
The past is not as important as the present, and while a place fit for 'righteousness' may lie behind us, the road there is bound to be found in history.
Perhaps she should start by finding the name of this painting.

The next day, Ch'en Chao-ch'ien wakes up after an all-nighter at Sky Mirror Pavilion to find a farewell letter on her desk:
I dare not stay idle with a thousand matters to attend to, but the search for history's traces is not limited to just the pavilion. The land is vast, and we will meet again.
Sincerely, Ch'en Hui-chieh

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Help you with work? Sure. Does that mean I can set Rhodes Island's course? There's a tribe nearby just about to hold an unusual ceremony, and I was thinking of going to see—I can't? Why not…? It'll barely be a detour…

This thing on my bangs? Yes, it's a relic. Its original use was most likely as a buckle. It was just sitting there in my family's storehouse with nobody to see it, so I took a page out of the Columbians' book and stuck it in my hair like sunglasses. See, even antiques can be fashionable.

Historical relics aren't the only thing the museum puts on display. As long as an exhibit broadens the visitors' horizons, it's a good exhibit, right? You nodded! Good, because I've got this proposal for you—drumroll please: The Life of a Sarkaz Boiler Worker! If you see no problem with it, then sign here!

Psychology, architecture, artifact appraisal and restoration, exhibit design and crowd dynamics… Museum studies require me to understand these things, and I do. But I'm not a master of any of them? Well, sure, but a decent understanding is enough for my work, and I'm also always learning new things…

My family's fortunes had waned by the time my father's generation came around, so we're nowhere near as illustrious as Pepe or Anat's families. Now I see that as a blessing. I could have gone to study in Columbia, as I wanted, just as I've come to Rhodes Island. If you need me to do anything, just say it straight, no need to beat around the bush like you do with those two.

'In Sargon, Padishahs are as numerous as the stars in the sky; anyone who feels like it can reach out and grab one.' That's my favorite quote from the Thieving Padishah Merit—No, no, I'm not saying I want to be one, I just think her 'I want it so I'll go do it' attitude is super-cool, you know?

Doctor! DOCTOR! Quick, there's no time to explain! Help me write a description for this artifact from the South Sargon Marshland Tribal Customs exhibit! Huh? You can't describe something you know nothing about? Whoa… So there are things you don't know… Alright, new plan, I do the writing now, and you check if what I've written makes sense.

I know Mio's no ordinary Feline Beast Steward… and you're no ordinary human either, Doctor. That's all right. You can keep hiding your identities, I'll still be friends with you both. Of course, if you ever feel like sharing your 'secrets', I'd be happy to lend you an ear.

Close your eyes, get in the car, and come with me! It's hot? Enough complaining. Okay, you can open your eyes now. Look at this desert expanse. This is where the Shah set out on his expedition. Who knows? The wind might uncover some of the footprints he left behind. Don't speak, Doctor, or you'll disturb the flow of time…
Nothing to do… Hmm… Why not try to sleep standing up like I hear Pallas can…? Zzz… Zzz… Ow! My head! That hurts!

Hello, Doctor, my name is rather tricky, so you may call me Titi, like all my friends do—but what you call me isn't important. I'm here to prepare my museum's new special exhibit. Are you and Rhodes Island interested in participating?

Hmm, these are something like the artifact restoration tutorials I watched in Columbia. It looks easy when someone else does it, but the moment you try it yourself, you realize you have no idea where to even start.
This is a Rhodes Island promotion? Using ancient investiture ceremonies in modern business management… Fascinating. I could try something like this in my museum.
I feel like I could go even higher from here—Wait, what do you mean this is the peak?
There's some new artifacts that need to go into storage, shall we go see?
Okay, everyone have a look at the plan—It's different from yesterday's? Well, I just now got a new idea. So? Any issues?
Let's go, time to see what new stories this round of relics has to tell us.
We're in the storeroom, so everyone tread a little lightly, okay?
Cleaning, conservation, repairing, restoration, I can do it all.
Just relax and leave it to me.
Remember, patience makes perfect.
Easy does it.
Brush off the dirt, revealing the rich tones of the pottery glaze.
Remove the mold, restoring the flexibility of the fabric.
Clear away the crust, returning the marble sculpture to its full glory.
Phew! No new ceramic artifacts coming in? Not much for me to do, then.
This is from a much older period than we thought. You sometimes find a major discovery like this when tidying up the storeroom. Let's celebrate with a big cup of tangerine sahlab!
And that's storage sorted. If we made a themed exhibit out of these items, the tourists would be happy to queue for at least two hours.
It's fine. I'll help you mend it with epoxy and touch up the seam. You won't even notice.
I was exhausted the moment I got out the door. Today's really not a good day for work. I'll do it tomorrow.
You have much more… intriguing furniture than I thought. Is there some sort of theming to it all?
Hey, I saw that. Your itchy finger was trying to pull my straps.
You want me to go shopping with you? Alright, I'll have a mango and carob slushie, with crushed nuts on top. Oh, and a hibiscus juice too. And it's on you, right?
Arknights.

Happy New Year. Want to try some fermented carrot cakes? All the rage in southern Rim Billiton. A Cautus patient in the infirmary gave me some, said it's how they celebrate the new year. Don't want one? It smells weird? Eh, a little I guess, but that's no reason not to try it.
Oh, Doctor. Did you also come to this corner of the bridge for a view of the city? Come, stand right here, this angle's spectacular!

Happy birthday, Doctor. Here, I found this while tidying up the family storeroom. It used to be an ornament for a chariot, but you can take it to keep your hood buckled, no matter how hard the wind blows. The moment I saw it, I knew it was meant for you.

The wear and tear on an artifact are proof that its former owner once lived. We're the same… So long as our brains are running and limbs moving, we'll leave our own marks on the land. Those who come after will bear witness.

handbook.profile: Medjehtiqedti, Curator of Varjavandabad Museum. Only her friends can call her 'Titi'. Currently works with Rhodes Island as a field operator, and strives to repair relations between Sargon and Minos.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Titi shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.021u/L
Operator Titi rarely comes into contact with Originium.

Operator Titi has quite the sweet tooth, possibly as a result of the traditional diet of her native region. I tried getting her to make some changes to her diet, to no avail.
I asked Operator Papyrus for advice, and she came up with a list of names which she told me to give to Titi. Titi spent some time looking at the list, then became extremely pale. She stayed away from high-sugar candied fruit for a long time afterwards.
Later, I learned that Papyrus had given me a list of famous padishahs who all lived to an old age, but suffered from tooth decay because they ate too many sweets.
—Hibiscus
handbook.promotionRecord:
Operator Titi's time in Minos clearly left a deep impression on her, but when we asked for her thoughts on the trip, her answer was not what we expected.
'For a long time I've been thinking about a question, one that my mother and teachers have asked me as well: where will my curiosity take me?
'The incident at the museum planted the seed of an idea in my mind, and the journey to Minos made it sprout. My curiosity about history, society and how it works, science and how it develops ultimately comes from a desire to learn the reasons behind things, the things that shape us and our society, and make us who we are today.
'Having visited Athenius, I now know that stories of heroes form the roots of Minos, the desires of all Minoans converging upon the concept of 'hero'. What about us? What are the roots of Sargon, and what is our common goal, our shared aspiration? I'm afraid I don't know the answer, yet.
'But I think I'll find the answer one day, when I've gained sufficient knowledge. Or when the day comes that I visit the ancient city with over a thousand years of history.'
archives:
Operator Titi almost immediately became integrated into the Rhodes Island community.
Her adventure began as soon as she parted ways with the HR operator who showed her the main facilities. There was hardly a corner of Rhodes Island that she didn't explore. After dining at the cafeteria, she exchanged a rare photocopy of an old Vine-Bead Court cookbook for Operator Matterhorn's collection of Kjeragi recipes. While visiting the Engineering Department, she expertly repaired an important part using glue meant for relic restoration. She even wandered into the mobility layer, making friends with the Sarkaz boiler workers on her first day.
As we got to know her, however, we grew even more perplexed. The seemingly insignificant accessories she wears are in fact valuable ancient relics, which she seems to treat with complete nonchalance. Her white ribbon in particular is more than decorative: driven by Originium Arts, it practically serves as an extra arm, allowing her to grab distant objects, and move or support herself during activities such as climbing. It is also a medium for her to take notes, record her discoveries and data, or even act as a cheat sheet for public speaking.
We soon learned that, while making friends with Titi is easy, truly getting to know her is a different story.

[Weapon Evaluation]
Titi's staff stands in contrast to her short stature. At her checkup, we immediately found that the staff amplified her Arts considerably. The antiques she wears and the classical design of the staff gave us the impression that it was a family heirloom passed down through generations, but she had in fact designed and assembled it herself.
Titi says that its design was inspired by ancient Sargonian artifacts. The scarab sealed inside a piece of golden amber in the middle represents eternal life and resurrection, an ancient symbol dating back to Lugalszargus, the 'Shah of Past and Future,' making it an ideal fit for her conservation Arts. Our discussion turned into an impromptu semiotics lecture, as at one point we thought the symbol represented some kind of power boost Arts, a misconception that she soon dispelled.
'Power boost? Oh, that's because of the seven amplifiers I installed on the staff, on the ring around the amber.'

[A Trimounts University Transcript] Museum Design: A- Instructor Comments: Student demonstrates a thorough understanding of modern museology theory, as well as a mind open enough to effectively implement new media to enrich the exhibition experience. Can sometimes be overly fixated on new forms, in particular conceptual interaction designs advocated by the Columbia Art and Design Center, leading to the exhibition's content being overshadowed by the presentation. Archaeological Analysis and Technology: A- (Joint course with Trimounts Academy of Technology) Instructor Comments: Student demonstrates high proficiency in technological methods for analyzing the materials and techniques of relics. Occasionally prone to spur-of-the-moment ideas, resulting in outlandish experiments, and insists on analyzing the failed results. Conservation and Restoration: A- Instructor Comments: Student demonstrates excellent grasp of conservation and restoration techniques for relics of various materials. Capable of independently coming up with restoration proposals for working with heavily damaged artifacts, plans that are often risky, but the results have generally exceeded expectations. The only issue being occasional violations of lab rules and protocols—do not use the lab's specially blended glue to stick your classmate's shoe soles back on! ... The transcript is a long one, with far more credits on it than needed to graduate. It includes her compulsory coursework, subjects tangentially connected to her major like international history, languages, art history, architecture, and folklore, but also courses like 'Ingredient Analysis of Sami Herbal Remedies', 'Principles of Automated Flying Machine Control', and 'Literary Analysis of Flowers of Quinde and Kerespereia', taken for reasons unknown. Even more surprising is that she got an 'A-' in most of her coursework and excelled academically by any definition, yet had very few full marks in any of her courses: the instructors usually docked her points here and there for unusual reasons. Titi did not seem especially concerned with her grades—what mattered more to her was whether the course was interesting, and her definition of an interesting course was very different from others. While most look for variety, lively pacing, and humor, she judges courses by whether they satisfy her curiosity and stimulate her desire to explore further. 'I went to Columbia because I thought it would be fun. I had just graduated from school in Menat-Ha'mait when a Columbian merchant showed up with a bunch of newfangled things and told me that Trimounts University accepted students from all over Terra. It made me want to check it out for myself. I didn't think much about the distance from Menat-Ha'mait to Trimounts, or how I was actually going to get accepted and enroll. I just thought I would cross that bridge when I got there.'

Operator Titi describes her younger self as a 'free range wild child'. Her father was known as a ne'er-do-well amongst Menat-Ha'mait's nobility, having no interest in fame or fortune, only literature, and in particular in collecting books brought back to Sargon from occupied Minos. Never in great health, he fell ill when Titi was young and virtually stopped leaving the house altogether. To Titi, her father was like a plant that grew on the chair of his study. He would tell her stories if she went to find him, and if she did not, he did not concern himself with what she was doing. As such, she enjoyed more freedom than most noble children. She had plenty of room to explore, think, and imagine, and to reveal the laws and truth behind what she saw, what she was interested in. Her conclusions were not necessarily correct, and her ideas young and naive, but she had arrived at them on her own. The process of thinking helped her build trust in her own judgment, taught her how to obtain the information she wanted, and opened doors to new horizons. It took a long time for her to understand that there were many things that did not need to be said. How to explore, how to study, how to defuse hostility, how to help friends, how to find one's path forward, how to commit to what one thinks should be done... she had already learned all these things from the stories her father told her, and her mother's tacit approval and indulgence. [Book Excerpt] ...And so the silent Siopi returned to his homeland, but still he never spoke. 'You are friendly and outgoing. You never know if you might accidentally reveal the secret you are trying to keep in conversation.' The safest way, therefore, was to never speak. Once full of vigor and spirit when he left home, the young man now shut himself away, shunned contact with others, and died as silently as he lived. It was only a long time later, when the news of victory came from afar, that his fellows learned the secret he carried, and thus he became known as Siopi, the Silent Hero. —Excerpt from Vol.3 of Minoan Heroic Legends, New Edition, 1101, Varjavandabad Museum Press [Book Review] Scholars are excited about the publication of Minoan Heroic Legends, New Edition, and for good reason. Mr. Khnum Nasutu Mashayer has long been known for his extensive collection of Minoan literature, and this six-volume collection, totaling more than three thousand pages, is more than just a compilation of the famous legends collected in the Mashayer Archives and their many variations, but also of rare oral traditions that he personally collected during his time in Minos. It is a landmark in scholarship that will undoubtedly be cited by researchers for decades to come. It is perhaps also worth noting that the publication of this work was sponsored by Mr. Mashayer's widow, and it was compiled and edited by their daughter. This is itself something of a legend.

We initially thought that the entity known as 'Mio' who accompanies Operator Titi was simply an ordinary Feline Beast Steward, although in hindsight there were certainly telling signs. Mio is very similar to Titi in its sociability, and its investigation of Rhodes Island took place concurrently with Titi's explorations. Mio quickly found its turf, claiming the best fresh fin belly from the cafeteria every morning, as well as a cushion on the sunniest spot on the bridge, though it does not visit every day.
Other operators claim to occasionally see a small, strange-looking Feline who often accompanies Titi, at times getting her out of tight spots, while at others getting into arguments with her, like two close yet bickering friends.
This has led to us theorizing about Mio's true nature... by now, we have grown rather familiar with such beings. For now, at least, there seems to be little cause for concern, since Mio's intervention has been limited to providing occasional assistance to Titi and filling its own stomach.

[Classified Log]
Hey, I picked the girl myself, I can't very well let her fend for herself. I like her personality, and she's not burdened by stuff like legacy or history, like so many other humans. Getting out of the Grand Bazaar wasn't easy, and I'd like nothing more than to have some real free time with nothing to worry about, but I guess the girl's not gonna stay put.
She and that damn curiosity of hers. Yeah, I know where she wants to go, but the depths of the desert is just not a nice place. The old Shah... yes, interesting fellow. Woof and I liked him, but his one-time dream, his discoveries in the south, his invincible army, and all his outlandish ideas, have all been twisted beyond recognition. As for the current Shahanshah, the lion who has lain low in the depths of the desert for many years... Has his silence and inaction been by choice, or has something happened to that ancient city in the sands, something beyond the control of puny humans? I don't know, and I don't particularly care to know. Frankly, I would prefer not to return to Shar-Agade, if I had a choice.
You're an interesting one too, Doctor... There are many of my kind here. I know they are uneasy too. It's a fresh, unfamiliar feeling, and I don't like it one bit.

modules.moduleDescription: Returning to Menat-Ha'mait from Trimounts takes at least three months. She could hitchhike with mercenary caravans in Columbia, but the journey home got harder once outside the country. Only after wasting several days at a border town does she finally find a caravan headed the right way back. Titi makes friends with the caravan leader in just a few days, a dark-skinned Liberi called Inam. She is quite curious about Titi's solo journey, as well as her past experiences. 'A Sargonian going to Columbia to study is rare enough, but for such a niche major? And now you're even headed home? Why?' 'Well, I did get scouted by a few Columbian museums after I graduated, but... I still feel 'Sargonian'. Besides, all my best friends are back home.' 'But you haven't seen them in years, have you?' 'We grew up together. We would play pranks on each other, but also help each other sneak out to play. They've kept in touch with me during my time in Columbia too. I know Pepe's an archaeologist now, leading a dig in the south, while Anat's life has probably been arranged by her father, but I'm sure she'll break free from that and do what she really wants—she's always talked about traveling the land and seeing what's outside Sargon.' 'So everyone has a goal in mind.' 'Well, they do. As for me, my family likes to say my heart's as fickle as the sands, easily swayed by a gust of wind. I went to study in Columbia on a whim, but to be honest...' Titi can still remember the night of her father's funeral. Her mother went to rest once all the guests were gone, leaving her alone in her father's study. The chair he used to occupy was now empty, and she realized for the first time how scary the bookshelves she used to take lightly were. Every shelf was crammed with tomes, as if they could burst free at any moment and crash down on her bewildered self. At that moment, she heard a familiar knocking sound from the window. A secret code used with her friends. Then, Pepe nimbly opened the window and climbed into the study with Anat in tow. With a surprised expression, Titi recalled her mother bidding farewell to them earlier, along with their parents. 'Titi... you didn't eat much earlier, did you? We got you some food.' Anat took out two pieces of sun bread, handing one each to Titi and Pepe. 'You have one too.' The sun bread was filled with Titi's favorite orange flavor, and reminded her of her empty stomach. When she finally took her first bite, Pepe seemed to heave a sigh of relief, and took a bite from her own as well, although she immediately grimaced. 'Anat, you jerk! What did you stuff into mine?!' Anat smiled shyly. The two began to squabble with exaggerated, almost theatrical movements. Titi could see they were clearly acting it out. Amidst their laughter and playful antics, a warmth seeped back into the study. 'I think... I can help them realize their own dreams first. Then I'll figure out what I want to do myself.'

levels.name: 'Execute'
levels.description:
When this skill is equipped, restores device HP over time after the device is deployed. On activation, the device loses 1 HP every 0.5 seconds, and grants the Operator in front <@ba.vup>1</> SP and a <$ba.barrier>Barrier</> equal to <@ba.vup>{talent@shield_each_hp_rate:0%}</> of Nasti's Max HP.
Immediately activates the devices on the field. Stops attacking and gains a <$ba.barrier>Barrier</> equal to <@ba.vup>{attack@nasti_s2[update_shield].shield_each_hp_rate:0%}</> of her Max HP every 0.5 seconds. (Barrier cannot exceed {talent@shield_max_hp_rate:0%} of Max HP)
<@ba.rem>Gains 1 Device when skill ends</>

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Here, construction project plans and data reconciliation sheet. Why the face? I share the same twenty four hours a day that you do, so there's no reason I should work for you alone.

Please grab these 'branches'… good. I've obtained your height, weight, and bone density. In ten minutes, a robot will deliver safety equipment tailored to you. Why the surprise? Were you not planning to follow me to the construction site?

Ho'olheyak? A K'uk'ulkan not even trying to hide her probes and provocations. She has a talent for making trouble. She calls herself my friend… Yes, I'm aware of such rumors. I will temper my hate for her as long as she doesn't interfere with my work, and the same goes for you, Doctor.

I won't join Rhodes Island's engineering optimization efforts—no, you wouldn't manage to steal Rhine Lab's tech either way, but as a fellow engineer, I know the look on that Vampire's face when she stays up all night drawing blueprints. This is no prime-time Trimounts home renovation show, and I have no interest in commentating on someone else's home.

The so-called 'Rhine Lab Ten' seldom came together, even when Kristen was still around, so the few empty seats at the round table now do not imply much of a crisis. As Director of Engineering, I know how much longer this machine we call 'Rhine Lab' can operate.

Correct. Countless Columbians bore witness to the fall, and the spectacle left them disheartened. Was there a need to cool their fervor? I have no interest in discussing this, Doctor… Fowlbeasts learn to fly by falling, and one day Kazdel will float in the sky.

I invited you to dance on the sky bridge yesterday? *sigh* I see Muelsyse has taken to this impersonation game. Doctor, I will, for now, take it you failed to recognize that was a water clone, so—who is it you do not know well enough—Muelsyse or myself?

You must have misheard, I was not singing—if you take the Logos you know as a reference, I am no qualified Banshee, nor do I belong to the Convallis any longer. Though elegies still mean the same to me. You're tired? If you're unused to falling asleep to the rumbling of construction noise, I can write you a curse.

Look at the barrier above our heads. Do you think it's out of our reach? Or perhaps I should be asking if you know how it was formed, how to break it down? Kristen absolutely believed her choice held meaning, while I will see it through. Where do you stand on this, Doctor?
At last, the muddled dream is about to settle…
So we meet. Nasti Lunorey, Director of Engineering at Rhine Lab. I've heard a lot about you from some of my colleagues. Pleased to make your acquaintance.
Rewind three seconds. The terminal on the left was displaying incorrect data… Alright, problem solved.
Are you expecting a speech…? Sorry, abstract topics only leave me feeling hollow.
I'd like to thank Rhodes Island and you for the recognition, Doctor. Our cooperative efforts have been reassuring.
Rhodes Island's many Operators working multiple jobs is a common sight at Rhine Lab as well.
Saria. She will break through the enemy's encirclement; and Muelsyse will manage any mediation efforts as necessary. Both are indispensable.
Silent words work all the same.
Ensure the construction site is safe before we begin.
If the plan is too vague, I will revise it.
An error message? Nothing out of the norm.
You don't have to reiterate the project goals. Work has already begun.
Don't trip on my tape.
Listen again. Did you think it was just construction noise?
A confession? All I hear is the babbling of souls.
'Elegies are no final respite.'
'The realm has naught for your perch.'
Project done. Good work, everyone.
Do another round of checks… 'Perfect' to us is but a standard to reach.
'Expectations' met. Expand on that? We always leave room for improvement.
Angry? Why? Would you like to guess how many Rhine Lab blueprints I've had to revise before they were officially greenlit?
The elevator bulb was loose, so I changed it.
'Stasis'—I consider this legitimate self-defense.
Don't pull on the mechanical leaf… Fine, I'll teach you to whistle Mother's melody.
Arknights.

One last cable, and three, two, one, go… Times like these, the researchers would excitedly scramble over to the cable sparks and call them 'fireworks', but you seem quite calm still—Happy New Year, Doctor. We won't make it to the celebrations back on the island.
You bumped into my 'branches'.

You're still alive, so leaves are more suitable than bone for the whistle. A melody I know…? No, the Mama John's jingle wouldn't fit… Once upon a time, a group of Pioneers lying on a scaffold hummed a tune to the setting sun to welcome a Banshee into their group. Would you like to hear it?

A Banshee does not forget the Convallis that nurtured her, while a Pioneer will not forget the barrens she trekked through—it was how I joined Rhine Lab, and the antecedent to my future. Doctor, what does Rhodes Island mean to you, and how will you guide it? Our cooperation will continue.

The so-called 'Rhine Lab Ten' seldom came together, even when Kristen was still around, so the few empty seats at the round table now do not imply much of a crisis. As Director of Engineering, I know how much longer this machine we call 'Rhine Lab' can operate.

Correct. Countless Columbians bore witness to the fall, and the spectacle left them disheartened. Was there a need to cool their fervor? I have no interest in discussing this, Doctor… Fowlbeasts learn to fly by falling, and one day Kazdel will float in the sky.

I invited you to dance on the sky bridge yesterday? *sigh* I see Muelsyse has taken to this impersonation game. Doctor, I will, for now, take it you failed to recognize that was a water clone, so—who is it you do not know well enough—Muelsyse or myself?

You must have misheard, I was not singing—if you take the Logos you know as a reference, I am no qualified Banshee, nor do I belong to the Convallis any longer. Though elegies still mean the same to me. You're tired? If you're unused to falling asleep to the rumbling of construction noise, I can write you a curse.

Look at the barrier above our heads. Do you think it's out of our reach? Or perhaps I should be asking if you know how it was formed, how to break it down? Kristen absolutely believed her choice held meaning, while I will see it through. Where do you stand on this, Doctor?
At last, the muddled dream is about to settle…
So we meet. Nasti Lunorey, Director of Engineering at Rhine Lab. I've heard a lot about you from some of my colleagues. Pleased to make your acquaintance.
Rewind three seconds. The terminal on the left was displaying incorrect data… Alright, problem solved.
Are you expecting a speech…? Sorry, abstract topics only leave me feeling hollow.
I'd like to thank Rhodes Island and you for the recognition, Doctor. Our cooperative efforts have been reassuring.
Rhodes Island's many Operators working multiple jobs is a common sight at Rhine Lab as well.
Saria. She will break through the enemy's encirclement; and Muelsyse will manage any mediation efforts as necessary. Both are indispensable.
Silent words work all the same.
Ensure the construction site is safe before we begin.
If the plan is too vague, I will revise it.
An error message? Nothing out of the norm.
You don't have to reiterate the project goals. Work has already begun.
Don't trip on my tape.
Listen again. Did you think it was just construction noise?
A confession? All I hear is the babbling of souls.
'Elegies are no final respite.'
'The realm has naught for your perch.'
Project done. Good work, everyone.
Do another round of checks… 'Perfect' to us is but a standard to reach.
'Expectations' met. Expand on that? We always leave room for improvement.
Angry? Why? Would you like to guess how many Rhine Lab blueprints I've had to revise before they were officially greenlit?
The elevator bulb was loose, so I changed it.
'Stasis'—I consider this legitimate self-defense.
Don't pull on the mechanical leaf… Fine, I'll teach you to whistle Mother's melody.
Arknights.

One last cable, and three, two, one, go… Times like these, the researchers would excitedly scramble over to the cable sparks and call them 'fireworks', but you seem quite calm still—Happy New Year, Doctor. We won't make it to the celebrations back on the island.
You bumped into my 'branches'.

You're still alive, so leaves are more suitable than bone for the whistle. A melody I know…? No, the Mama John's jingle wouldn't fit… Once upon a time, a group of Pioneers lying on a scaffold hummed a tune to the setting sun to welcome a Banshee into their group. Would you like to hear it?

A Banshee does not forget the Convallis that nurtured her, while a Pioneer will not forget the barrens she trekked through—it was how I joined Rhine Lab, and the antecedent to my future. Doctor, what does Rhodes Island mean to you, and how will you guide it? Our cooperation will continue.

handbook.profile: Nasti Lunorey, director of Rhine Lab's Engineering Section and one of Columbia's foremost authorities in engineering, as well as an expert in applied linguistics. With a reference from Saria, she has entered into a long-term memorandum of cooperation with Rhodes Island and provides support for various projects as a special consultant to the Engineering Department.
