handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be non-infected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Nasti shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.13u/L
Operator Nasti lived in Kazdel for five years during her childhood and spent more than a decade traveling across Terra. That she has been able to avoid infection is a combination of good luck and extreme care taken with protective measures.

'My goals require a healthy body, that's all.'
—Nasti

'But your calluses are too thick!'
—A passing Elf
handbook.promotionRecord:
Countless cables were laid across the floor. There was a terminal screen in the middle of the room, with data flushing across it like a waterfall. The Banshee buried her head in the equipment in front of her, her jacket tied around her waist. You wondered whether you should just leave quietly; this was an impromptu visit, after all, and the matters about future cities in the sky and 'trees' in ships and among the stars could wait for another day.
Just as you were about to walk away, the Banshee said, 'One moment. Check the result for me, please.' She did not turn around.
Only then did you notice two branch-shaped robots wearing safety helmets standing behind the Banshee, less than a meter away from you. They were faced off against each other, each solving an extremely difficult variation of the rubik's cube, with sparks flying between their 'fingers' despite their lack of facial features.
Was this a competition? For what? You knew the Banshee well. What kind of engineering problem did she run into that called for such a solution? You could not help but feel curious.
'Mama John's happy meal set if the left one wins. Compressed biscuits if the right one wins...'
'Do you have another cube?' You asked the Banshee. Perhaps there could be a third outcome.
archives:
Nasti accepted our offer to act as a special engineering consultant soon after we established contact through Saria.
According to the operator from the Trimounts branch who brought the contract to Nasti, Rhine Lab did not prepare any ceremony or even an office room for the signing of this important agreement. A haughty Forte researcher by the name of Sky Jagger led him to an underground facility, pointed at a door, and said, 'The director is inside' before leaving. The operator opened the door, his head filled with question marks, and was met with a shocking sight: hundreds of giant ants wearing yellow safety helmets barreling around the room, charging at him the moment they saw him. He dropped the contract, which was immediately stampeded into pieces. Then Nasti emerged from amongst the ants and approached him, saying, 'Sorry, I had inspection work I couldn't get away from.'
Having gotten over the fright of Rhine Lab apparently turning on Rhodes Island, the operator noticed that the giant ants were in fact branch-shaped robots, sharing the same origin as the device on Nasti's belt. A masterpiece by Rhine's Director of Engineering, these incantation-driven creations were inspecting the energy supply system using their dexterous branches to complete various delicate tasks, while the safety helmets protected their cores.
With the contract badly damaged, the operator apologized to Nasti and offered to reschedule the signing, only to be surprised again by the reaction of the impassive director. Nasti took a section of a paper tape floating around her and had the operator dictate the general outline of the contract. As he spoke, words appeared on the tape, then a robot stepped on his foot, gave him a pen, gesturing for him to sign it.
The operator would later describe the scene in vivid detail to others whenever he had the opportunity: complex pipelines arranged like a witchcraft array in a strange underground space, signing one end of an incantation-woven paper tape as the aloof Banshee signed the other, while hundreds of giant ants wearing safety helmets hustled around them. For a moment, he thought he had entered the territory of some mysterious Sami tribe. It seems there is still much on Terra that he does not know about.

'An incantation is a Banshee's promise. It will never fade, as long as I exist.'

When speaking of the 'Rhine Lab Ten', Nasti is seldom the first name to come to mind. Kristen is an icon unto her own. Muelsyse has as many friends as she has water clones. Ferdinand is so strict he can scare a crying intern into shutting up with a single look. Maryam's exploits have won him many fans in Columbia's extreme adventuring community. Meanwhile, there is little to even say about the Director of Engineering, who spends her time moving from construction site to construction site, rarely showing her face in public. Even in her rare appearances, she hardly talks or shows any expression on her face.
That is, until a junior researcher from the Ecological Section repeatedly came across Muelsyse, the director of the Ecological Section, watching the same home renovation show with great interest. Among the many interests of Muelsyse, from games to fashion to photography, home renovation was not known to be one of them. The Rhine Lab gossip mill quickly ramped up and soon discovered the truth: Muelsyse had her eyes on a special guest who participated anonymously across multiple seasons, fascinating the audience with bold, avant-garde designs that emphasize unconventional spatial order. In a season themed around future living, the designer built a home based on the concept of musbeast wheels, with seven living spaces in different styles rotating on a wheel, maximizing both usage and fun. Muelsyse made a compilation of episodes featuring that designer and sent it to the designer herself: Nasti.
This discovery soon became the talk of Rhine Lab from the corridors to the break rooms. Everyone had a hard time connecting that paragon of avant-garde architecture on the show to the reserved, pragmatic, and meticulous head of Engineering. Later, it was revealed that it was Jara, head of HR, who initially arranged for Nasti to join the show to 'maintain activity'. Contracts for subsequent seasons, however, were signed by Nasti of her own accord.

'Unlike the research sections, Engineering has a limited budget for creative experimentation. I saw no reason to turn down an offer to pay me to build weird houses.'
This was Nasti's answer when someone mustered the courage to ask her.

[Audio log of a lecture to new employees by Nasti, Director of Engineering for Rhine Lab]
'Engineering is Rhine Lab's busiest section. We have to coordinate with the other operational sections, while also providing engineering support for Structural, Ecological, Energy, Originium Art, and Scientific Investigation Section, in an endless journey to fulfill their demands. This is my advice: don't think of yourself as the scientists' friend. Read every word on those proposals and blueprints carefully, and tell them which are a matter of laying the bricks and tightening the screws, and which are pipe dreams they need to wake up from.
'Energy's facility proposals are generally properly validated. Ferdinand may be an arrogant asshole, but he knows what he's doing.'
......
'Be on your guard when dealing with Ecological. Don't let Muelsyse find your weakness.
'Defense... Saria's former department. A bunch of tough customers to deal with. In its role in assuring the safety of Rhine Lab's projects, the Defense Section has more concerns to consider, and its methods are more resolute. Saria is the new Control now, but their style has not changed. Saria herself has a serious case of OCD. I was in charge of renovating her office, and it was a long, arduous process.
'Power supplies and emergency equipment for Originium Art must be built to the highest standard. As for Dorothy, I am very familiar with people like her. They have too many people to worry about, too many things they want to do, and too many things to lose, but they deserve respect.'
......
'May I ask a question, Director Nasti?'
'Go on.'
'When you described the other directors, it sounded like they are more than just co-workers to you...'
'...Is that so? I suppose I talked a little too much. Anyway, Rhine Lab has changed a lot. Some names aren't talked about so much anymore, while others will come to be remembered. Change is a constant in science and engineering, but the walls of Rhine will remain strong. It welcomes you.'

To Kazdelians, burying a dead body is no different from burying potatoes in winter. The true farewell happens after the dead turn into Originium crystals sprouting from the ground. Then, those who remember the departed gather to carve their name, their nicknames, the events of their life, and words of gratitude or grudges on the crystals.
'I was three at the time. A sickly man was carefully knocking on a crystal on the ground. I asked him what he was doing. He said his wife's crystal was too small for all the things he wanted to carve into it, so he decided to take it home and use it as a hanger. That way, he could talk to her every morning and night.'

The Pioneer caravans of Columbia are always moving forward, even during a funeral. Whether the departed left behind ashes or Originium dust, it gets scattered behind the procession when the others set out the next day. The urn is passed from one hand to another, each person scattering a handful of ashes while saying their goodbyes.
'I tried to sing an elegy the night before. I sang awfully and they didn't understand a word of it, so I was surprised when they passed me the box of ashes the next day. It was a simple plastic lunchbox, with one last handful of ashes inside. 'If you're willing to sing that song one more time,' they said.'
—Nasti, on the funeral customs she had witnessed

['Great Server' Visit Notes]
In Professor Aefanyl's class, we listened to the voices of the myriad souls in centuries past. When asked about the new myriad souls and their new voices, he instead brought us to this enormous tree that took up nearly an entire floating plate. The Great Server's main structure was built upon its main trunk in many layered stacks.
We were greeted by Director Nasti Lunorey, who complained about how Professor Aefanyl kept interrupting her work by sending students to visit, while patiently guiding us through the internal structure of the Great Server's facilities. As I crawled out of the labyrinthine maintenance pipelines with a safety helmet on my head, I almost felt like I had changed my major from vocal techniques to civil engineering. Then, some branch-shaped robots crawled out from a corner of the tiny storage room, giving each of us a small cardboard box.
'This is the answer Aefanyl wanted you to discover here.'
As though the five-hour visit wasn't enough to demonstrate how inscrutable Director Nasti was, the cardboard box contained neither writings nor drawings, but an elaborate cupcake.
Director Nasti began explaining the nature of the 'Great Server', seemingly oblivious to our confusion.
'I've been to many places and seen many funerals. No matter the occasion, no matter what form it takes, those left behind try to wrap all their love and hate, relief and regret, into a few words of farewell. But the departed have had no such opportunity. Now, the 'tree' has given them that opportunity, and the Great Server stores their words of farewell.
'I love you, I hate you, thank you, sorry.... Besides the countless messages like these, some have left behind more unusual words: a report on the near-death experience, a melody that has never been written, a wildly imaginative blueprint, or a joke...
'The recipe for this cupcake was one such message. I might never have tried my hand at baking if someone I've never met hadn't left this recipe behind. Now, you've heard the voices of the new myriad souls that Aefanyl wanted you to hear.
'Or tasted them, to be precise.'

modules.moduleDescription: 'Director Nasti, I heard it took you only six months to go from joining Rhine Lab to leading Engineering?' 'Three.' 'Just... three months?' 'To be precise, Rhine Lab only established an official Engineering Section after I joined, to provide engineering support for the mountain of proposals from Muelsyse, Ferdinand, and the others. I joined the company in its early days, but after it had already attracted quite a lot of attention. And given my background... you could certainly say that three months was an especially short period for a Sarkaz who showed up out of nowhere to assume a regular role here.' 'You mean the vetting process went smoothly for you?' 'One of my people over at Maylander secretly helped me out. Of course, I only found out about that later.' 'Hiding your history must have been difficult.' 'Maybe you've been spending too much time listening to water-cooler rumors. The more time you waste on this routine interview, the more time I'll have to spend later 'hiding my history', as you put it. A young company like this—a young country like this—has always derived its nutrients from age-old secrets.' 'My apologies, Director Nasti. I-I'm just a little nervous. I thought you'd have declined the interview, or responded the way Director Muelsyse did. Only halfway through my interview with her did I realize I was talking to a water clone the whole time...' 'They don't have any function like that.' 'They? Oh, you're referring to the robots by your feet? According to HR's surveys, many of our employees are very interested in them... What should we call them?' 'Branch-type fully-loaded hybrid precision work robots. Each of them bears a unique eight-digit serial number indicating the scope of their respective duties. I have incantations inscribed on their core components so they can seamlessly adhere to my commands.' 'So I take it you're like their mother, Director?' 'No. They do whatever I want. They're merely the bricks and bolts of whatever project needs them. Just like me. Also, don't casually project such precious emotions onto inanimate objects.' '...' 'Alright, kid. You don't have to force yourself to think of any more questions to ask. Just leave the rest to me.' —Excerpt from a Rhine Lab HR Audio Log Thank god Director Jara showed up in the nick of time, before the mood in the room dropped below zero. To be honest, the Director of Engineering isn't that hard to get along with, other than her schedule being difficult to squeeze into. She's just focused on efficiency and her work, and I could be myself for the most part. The two of them soon shifted topics and began discussing Control. Probably Director Jara was subtly asking where Control was. 'This was your true motive for the interview, wasn't it?' The conversation continued, and I heard Director Nasti switch to an unusually gentler tone. 'Kristen doesn't want you to know too much. I understand her reasons, so I'll say nothing more on the matter.' It seems like I'll never get the chance to apologize to her. —Supplementary explanation from HR staff Jennifer

<@ba.rem>Can store 2 charges</>

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Your time and sanity should be left to more consequential matters. Surely you can find someone suitable to handle these trifles in your stead? Very well. For you, I shall happily serve.

Gnosis and Degenbrecher have taken over my Karlan Trade duties. Since this was not what I originally promised for their careers, they understandably have some complaints. There is not always a clean boundary between method and aim, but when I used this sword of mine to cleave the bridges behind me, I saw it, clear as day.

When I was surveying the land to find a suitable site for the observation station, I already understood the sight of it would attract numerous gazes. In this era of radical change, those timid conservatives and ignorant opportunists will meet similar fates in the dustheap. But I, SilverAsh, must ensure Kjerag is never again left behind by the times.

I've met with the Speaker, yes. Those of similar ideals face similar issues, perhaps even similar… kin? When Father left for Victoria, he would never have imagined a future where that nation was to be our enemy. It was indeed a simpler time, one to which we may never return.

Those who seek power out of cowardice shall find nothing at the apex of authority. As for me? My friends and enemies both ensure I am unlikely to forget the importance of how I conduct myself. But I am dearly looking forward to the day I take the final step towards the peak, and find myself standing opposed to you.

Kjerag seeks to build ever-greater institutions, but we shall not stand tall among the nations because of them. When we faced a true crisis, I began to believe in the strength inherent in the people of the Snow Realm. I must admit, Enya is right. It is not that I do not care for faith. I have simply long since found a belief of my own.

There is no such thing as a chessboard without uncertainty. In a sense, every move we make is a gamble. Only when maximizing one's odds of success do one's wits come into play. Ah, the burdenbeast I bet on crossed the line first. According to custom, you are to down your glass.

Ensia cherishes her friendship with you. Asking you to take care of her was, at the time, a somewhat unreasonable request of mine, but now I see that there could not have been a better choice. Let us not speak of the barriers between her and me. Rather than reaching any so-called understanding, I would much rather see which peak she decides to conquer next.

Ohh? You are worried. Those in power cannot take the weight of responsibility lightly, but neither can they allow it to hold them back. At times, you need only make decisions, then entrust the rest to others. There is nothing simpler, yet more difficult. A lonely life? No, though I do look forward to having an opponent who could stand shoulder-to-shoulder with me.
…The snowfall hath relented. Let us go for a walk outside.

It has been quite a while. The land teems with misfortune, but neither Kjerag nor Rhodes Island have fallen to the floor just yet. Are you ready? I believe we can re-establish our old rapport rather quickly. I, SilverAsh, have joined your cause as a sworn ally.
I have always found Rhodes Island's methods quite… refreshing.
When you accepted my proposal, did you not suspect Rhodes Island was becoming part of my schemes? Then again, you rather enjoy this sort of challenge.

How shall this cooperation of ours end? Will the two of us conquer all of Terra together, or will we face each other across a board near-finished, our conflict inexorable? No matter where the dice may fall, we await the outcome with bated breath.
I have learned some new tricks, since the last battle.
They shall learn whom they face.
How nostalgic…
The outcome has already been decided. They simply cannot see it yet.
Great minds think alike.
Make your decision, fast.
The situation is crystal clear.
Everything is under control.
Hark! Ne'er hast thou questioned the road thou'st strayed upon.
Thy trampling of this hallowed ground shall beget bitter rue.
Wait, for the snow shall bury this all…
…As ice yields to gentle warmth's embrace.
Has this battle left you unsatisfied? I eagerly anticipate seeing you dictate the flow of an even grander chessboard.
An astonishing result. And here I thought myself inured to you bringing home victory.
Am I to believe you did this intentionally…?
Ultimate victory will not be decided by a single check. Do not miss the chessboard for the squares.
A new beginning, yet not an unwelcome one.
If you are ever in the mood for some chess, I shall be happy to oblige.
…I am awake.
Arknights.

Enya is very happy aboard Rhodes Island. With Ensia to accompany her, I daresay it might be the happiest time of her life… I shall avoid intruding upon them. I will say, you are the only one who could make such a suggestion without crossing a line. Let us head out to enjoy the snow. Happy New Year, my ally.
You haven't weathered one bit, my friend.

A meeting between Karlan Trade and the General Chamber of Commerce? You are frightfully knowledgeable about my schedule. But it is clear that today, I, SilverAsh, have much more important plans. There is no doubt you are worth a blemish or two upon the Silverash name. Happy birthday, my ally. How do you wish to spend the day?

Rhodes Island's cause will reshape the fabric of this land. This point may be beyond the comprehension of most, but I am not most men. I believe we have both heard our fair share of similar comments, but remember: those who truly have the ability to change this land are often those arrogant and conceited enough to think themselves able to do so.

handbook.profile:
Enciodes Silverash, former chairman of Karlan Trade and current Chief of the Silverash Family. He has unique views on economics, trade, international politics, diplomacy, and strategic planning.
Considering his exceptional status and the complex situation in Kjerag, we should be judicious in our cooperation with him, to avoid unnecessary risk.

handbook.promotionRecord:
He stopped at the edge of a snow-covered plot of land, and turned around to look at you.
'A hospital will be built here, the most advanced hospital in Kjerag, one that will accommodate both normal patients and the Infected.'
You knew this was both a gift and an invitation, with a hint of remorse for dragging Rhodes Island into the next phase of his plan.
And then he said, calmly, 'I know your abilities, my friend. Fewer would die if you intervened. Perhaps things would go smoother, and we'd reach a more 'proper' conclusion. But such a victory would not belong to Kjerag. The people of Kjerag would continue to think that we can rely on outside powers, some hero or ally to overcome our crises. That is the illusion I seek to shatter. The people of Kjerag need to see for themselves how the old clans, old faith, and old order are reduced to ashes on their land, and build from those ashes something new with their own hands, something belonging only to them. These are growing pains that no outsider can stand in for.
As such, what I wanted to talk about is something else.
When I signed my resignation, I kept thinking back to the question you asked me: is it really worth going so far? For a long time I avoided the question, because I could not answer it. Now, I have finally taken this step, and found my answer.
I am filled with complex emotions: the joy of fulfilling my childhood wish, the weight of responsibility, the excitement of defending home and country. In the end, however, they are wrapped in a feeling of emptiness.
You know its name. Loss.
It is as though everything I lost over the decades has found me, many of which I pushed away with my own two hands.
They asked me the same question that you did, and I answered: yes, it's worth it.
But not because Kjerag won a key battle, or because of anything I achieved. But for all the changes others may see in Kjerag, in my eyes she has always been the same land I looked back at when I first set out for Victoria that day.
Degenbrecher always accused me of being a perfectionist. I don't deny it. A perfectionist does not tolerate loss, nor does he have the patience to wait for new things to arrive on their own. It is my own selfish little hope to prove to that which was lost that the future will be even better.
This hospital is the first step.'
archives:
No child of Kjerag who was there for the winter of 1101 will ever forget it.
'Eventful' does not even begin to describe it. Scientists from Columbia built an observation station on Karlan soon after people began hearing rumors that the sky above their heads was fake, but how could that be? Then, the first ever Catastrophe in Kjerag's history, at a time when its people hardly knew what a Catastrophe was. Even the Saintess's Pilgrimage could not fully calm the people. After that, the clash between Clan Silverash and the Vine-Bead Court, and the Victorian invasion... Those days of chaos seemed as long as Kjerag's winters.
During a time like that, the changing of the guard at Karlan Trade seemed little more than a footnote.
Only those closely associated with the company understand the true magnitude of this change. It was founded by Enciodes Silverash, and for all intents and purposes he WAS Karlan Trade. Yes, he was indeed involved in some controversies connected to the Victorians, but what child of Kjerag would ever trust the word of a Victorian over Mr. Silverash, who built railroads and factories for their homeland? And no one knew why he chose that particular moment to resign.
But it did happen, with the new president Gnosis announcing Enciodes's departure. After several months since the former president disappeared from the public eye, it was soon business as usual at Karlan Trade, as though nothing had changed.
Yes. Nothing seemed to have changed at all. A transition as smooth as a hot knife through crystymilk butter. There can only be one explanation—
The one who handed over his power had long planned to do so.

One day in the winter of 1101, the Glorious Post, based in the dukedom of Caster, published a report that few paid attention to. 'The military drill Her Grace the Duke of Caster personally oversaw concluded yesterday. This marked the first appearance of the Caster fleet since the end of the Londinium War, with the newly-overhauled Gloriana once again serving as flagship. It was a clear proclamation that Victoria has escaped the shadow of war, the light of her glory fully restored. This report was quickly buried under news of rising inflation, as well as the latest gossip. The people of Caster showed little surprise when goods from Kjerag quietly began showing up on their stores' shelves, and few if any associated it with the report, if they remembered it at all. Classification Level: Top Secret Title: On the Current Situation in Kjerag and Supplemental Review of the Duke of Caster's Actions ...Once again, it must be emphasized that it would be dangerous and short-sighted to attribute the failure of the Snow Realm Campaign to the Duke of Caster's rash military strategy. In our review, we discovered that the duke's military actions were, in fact, an irrational attempt to salvage well-laid plans of subversion that were derailed by unexpected factors. The true failure occurred well before the Gloriana arrived in Kjerag. Information we obtained through various sources paints a far more complex picture than publicly reported. The Duke of Caster's initial plan was to bring Kjerag into Victoria's sphere of influence without firing a single shot: through economic assistance, cultural infiltration, and fostering local pro-Victoria factions. The plan began smoothly, at one point successfully turning both the Vine-Bead Court and public opinion against the reformist leader, Enciodes Silverash, but spontaneous resistance from various Kjeragi factions ultimately turned the tide. When her plan failed, the Duke of Caster attempted the path of military intimidation, only to find that the nation she faced was not even closely as backwards as she thought, putting her at risk of losing a large portion of her fleet as well as significant embarrassment with the rest of Victoria's eyes upon her. While we do not know the details of Enciodes's negotiations with her on her ship, the fact that Karlan Trade was able to obtain favorable terms in its subsequent agreements with the dukedom tells us all we need to know. From an economic perspective, Karlan Trade has a monopoly on communications with the outside. From a spiritual perspective, Enya maintains her absolute authority as Saintess. From a military and political perspective, despite resigning from his position at Karlan Trade, Enciodes Silverash retains control over armed forces sufficient to present a credible threat to a Victorian fleet, and Kjerag has also established close relations with Columbia by way of Rhine Lab. While Kjerag's military might is not yet enough to pose a threat to other countries, its unique environment and political advantages have cemented its position as a faction that is relevant, potentially even dangerous, should they express even greater ambitions. We must continue to observe and assess Kjerag's diplomatic stance with prudence. Compiled by: Sharp

Undeniably, Enciodes plays a pivotal role in the affairs of Kjerag in this delicate transitional period.
It would be a dangerous mistake to view him through the lens of other countries' systems and understand his role as that of a local warlord or head of government. The authority of the former is rooted in fragmentation and greed, and the latter in constitution and popular opinion, while Enciodes's authority comes from bloody victory and a massive, unsettling void. He does not hold any office, for there is no office that can define his authority in Kjerag.
The ambiguity of this power structure gives Kjerag a strange sense of fragmentation. It has a nominal parliament, a Karlan Trade back on track in its commercial role, and an independent religious institution, but everyone knows full well that behind the clearly defined roles of these gears, there is a ghost without any formal responsibility who can bring any or all of them to a halt on a whim.
But just as everyone believed he was about to centralize all the power in his hands and become the shadow leader of Kjerag, incomprehensible changes began to take place across the country, changes that were diametrically opposed to the narrative that was supposed to unfold.
It used to be that only the best and brightest had the opportunity to study abroad under Karlan Trade's sponsorship. Now, new schools are emerging in every corner of Kjerag, including the most remote mountain villages. Even more noteworthy are their textbooks: the teachings and prayers of Kjeragandr are still present, to be sure, but there are also new subjects such as 'Physics', 'Chemistry' and 'Mathematics'.
No one knows if the 'shadow leader' is behind these changes. Some call it the enlightening mercy of the Saintess Enya, while others see it as an investment by President Gnosis of Karlan Trade, but even more speculate that it is the silent leader without office who has been pushing these reforms behind the scenes.
It is true that he possesses great power. But he has also carefully groomed his enemies and given them weapons more powerful than his own authority, weapons that can be used to end his reign.
He is not building his throne, but a sword for Kjerag that can cut a throne in two, even if he is slated to be that sword's first target. It is a temporary despotism, and a necessary one, a transition that is scheduled to end with his fall. His reign began with a storm, and it will end with the birth of a stronger, more resilient Kjerag, one which he has nurtured, and one which will end his reign.

Enya chose to walk a difficult path to find an answer that could convince her. I understood and assented. Someone needed to be the final and most pious martyr of the old faith, and give a thousand years of tradition a proper, dignified ending.
As for Ensia... she has already seen the cruelest side of this nation. In the coming days, she will truly understand the nature of what she wants to protect, and the price it will take.
The girls have far exceeded my expectations, and I expect they will continue to. I'm pleased.
I'm glad to have a colleague like Gnosis. I expect he will settle into his chair as Karlan Trade and Rhine Lab continue to expand their cooperation.
Degenbrecher is the one I'm concerned about. Not because I expect her to leave, but because I'm not sure how to deliver my apology to her, though I know she doesn't need one.
Weiss asked if I wanted to hold a nominal position at his new logistics company, now that I'm out of a job. I recommended Matterhorn instead. It's about time he took a break, after all that he's done for me.
As for the name Silverash... it has long become a shackle that binds the snowy mountains, as are Paleroche and Browntail. Kjerag will never truly belong to its people while these three ancient names are still revered by all. It is only a matter of time until the Tri-Clan Council becomes obsolete.
Therefore, I have made the following arrangements for the future of Kjerag: I gave Gnosis a commercial empire, Enya a spiritual symbol, and Kjerag a sword sharp enough to protect itself.
I will not be so arrogant as to proclaim myself Kjerag's protector. I've made too many decisions for its people, decisions that they should have made for themselves. But I will continue to do so, until a new order is truly born upon this land, until it gains the power to judge all that it should.
When that day comes, I will gladly stand trial, and accept whatever judgment it proclaims.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Serve as your assistant…? Hm, from what I have seen, there is not much difference between administrative work and organizing the scriptures of the Vine-Bead Court. I know how to do it, but… are you sure there are not more important things for me to do?

During my days at the Vine-Bead Court I would clamber up and down ladders to consult ancient records and scripture as thick and heavy as bricks. Based on past Saintess selections, the girl who is to become Saintess must have a strong, healthy body. Hm, I believe I've figured out the reasoning behind these traditions.

Hm? Oh, this? This is something I knitted for Ensia's birthday in my spare time. It's like when I was little, Father and I would knit new cloaks or scarves for the entire family every three years… I know what you want to ask, but please don't.

Why do foreign envoys still believe Kjerag to be a land of spirits and sprites…? Hmph, it leaves me no choice but to meet their expectations, and take on a most fearsome form. 'If you do not wish to be snatched away by the Tschäggättä, then you must show some sincerity.' That will make them good little ambassadors who sign our agreements.

What is a miracle, you ask? Hm, who knows? Perhaps a gust of night wind, or a beautiful rainbow, so long as it inspires the devout and puts fear into the heart of sinners. When you feel troubled and know not what to do, pray, and the divine in your heart shall give you strength.

It is not that Kjeragandr taught us virtue, but that She is made manifest through the virtue in our hearts. So too does all sloth and sin find release through this understanding. She shall not scold you, for recognizing oneself is a difficult thing, and She will always show a path through the wind and snow for her children.

There aren't enough funds for dormitory maintenance? Allow me to make a donation in the name of the Vine-Bead Court. The funds shall come from the personal account of the president of Karlan Trade—ah, no, no need for that. The medical support Rhodes Island has given the people of Kjerag is plain for all to see. Sir Enciodes won't utter a single complaint.

You'd like to help me comb my hair? Nmph… it wouldn't be an easy job. If it weren't for Kjarr and the other maids, I don't know how much time I'd have to spend each day caring for it. I've considered cutting it short, but I understand some of the people would be sad if I did, so…

'Merciful Kjeragandr'… She has clearly run off to that snowy mountain to fool about… Perhaps once Her spirit has recovered, She will awaken once more. How will Kjerag have changed in that time? If there really are gods, then please, help her find a way back home.

Hm? Documents that need to be signed? Err… The Doctor is currently in an emergency meeting, would it be alright if these got back to you later? Alright, I shall pass them on for you… *phew* Getting an afternoon nap is no small task for Dr. {@nickname}.

Amidst the undying winds of the Snow Realm and the unending fall of snow, Pramanix of Kjerag now stands before you… How's that for a preamble? Now let me in already, we'll have plenty of time for greetings later.
'When in snow, seek the footprints of those heading forward'. This is the simple wisdom of Kjeragandr.
No, no more gifts or ornaments, please. A Saintess's garb is heavy enough as it is. You want me to feel light and breezy, don't you?
'Of what has been gained, renounce it all. Of what has been lost, forget it all. We need only strive for truth and question ourselves, and in the end, we shall return to Her embrace.'
Victory belongs to the faithful.
I shall guide you in Her stead.
May the unclean be purified, and the blizzards dispersed.
You shall go no further…
She is omnipresent.
She cannot be sought.
Hear Her words.
Pray with all your heart.
Cold winds care not for whom they chill.
Ice and snow know not mercy.
Behold the power the mountains pledged to me.
Your struggles are feeble.
Karlan has witnessed this victory. O warriors clad in frost and gale, let us return home.
'After hard work comes a good night's rest.' The Saintess decrees it so.
…In the end, our gain is greater than our loss. Before the snow hides their footprints, we must discern which bad habits it is time to let go.
…The snow shall cover our tracks, and grant us the chance to return.
Have you widened this place since last time?
'Kjeragandr on high, smite those who play pranks by depriving them of snacks with their afternoon tea.'
Here, a pat on the head… A blessing? No, this is not the Saintess's blessing, but Pramanix's. It is, in a sense, the rarer of the two.
Arknights.

Happy New Year, Doctor. Old Kjerag custom dictates that I spend the entire night atop Mount Karlan praying for Kjeragandr's blessings, but… It's a rare day off for me, so let's not speak of work today, shall we? Hm?

The same arrangement as last time. You don't tell anyone I'm here, and you provide me with a blanket… Oh, this one's my favorite. You actually remembered…? Haha… It's like we're of one mind, when it comes to sneaking away for a nap.

I expect the gifts you receive will be enough to fill a small dormitory, so… Hold out your hand. The first snowflake to descend upon Rhodes Island shall fall into your palm. Before it melts away, it shall be my gift to you.

The snow atop the Matterhorn's peak did not fall in a single day. The road ahead is much the same. Rhodes Island has been following this path for so long, what could possibly be left to bar your way? Forge ahead. My blessing shall be with you forevermore.

handbook.profile: Pramanix, native of Kjerag and the Saintess of Karlan. She is the religious leader of Kjerag and plays an important role in its development and transformation. She is currently at work developing a basic education system in her homeland. Some reports claim that she successfully dispelled a looming Catastrophe in Kjerag.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be non-infected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Pramanix shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.11u/L
Operator Pramanix rarely operates in high-Originium environments.

There have been no significant changes to Operator Pramanix's data since her previous checkup, even demonstrating a slight increase in physical ability and reaction times. This is likely a result of keeping up a regular schedule and daily morning exercise required by the Vine-Bead Court. Perhaps we can implement similar activities on Rhodes Island.
—Medical Department Notes
handbook.promotionRecord: The temporary absence of some of the clerics and elders means that other clerics must step up to fill the vacancies in the central chapters, and the Vine-Bead Court has recruited a group of young people from both the clan domains and the Court's local chapters. Two-thirds of them were assigned to basic tasks such as cleaning and organizing the scriptures, while the rest were assigned as assistants, to help the busiest clerics with their work. Nine maidens of appropriate age were assigned to attend the Saintess, from which the new head handmaiden will be selected. The head handmaiden is customarily selected from the most experienced existing handmaidens, but with all of them already slated to teach in rural schools, the new head handmaiden will be selected from the new ones, at the Saintess's recommendation. —Vine-Bead Court Personnel Memorandum At first, I thought it wouldn't make much of a difference who had the job of head handmaiden. After all, no one can possibly compare to you. So I simply picked the girl who looked the brightest. The idea was that I would have her start out doing simple tasks like putting away clothes and passing on messages, and slowly ease her into more advanced duties like managing the other handmaidens and coordinating different departments. But she turns out to be even brighter than I expected. She is still young, but she is a quick learner with keen perception. When I was her age, I still liked to sulk by climbing mountains... What did you think of me when you saw me back then? I should have asked. But seeing her reminds me of the previous Saintesses I saw in the cave. Some of them were even younger than her. When I'm gone and it's time to pick a new Saintess, will they still make such young girls walk the mountain path? Never mind. I hope you'll like the way I changed Kjerag, the next time you wake up. —Excerpt from Pramanix's diary The Vine-Bead Court has announced that future Saintesses will no longer be chosen by trial, and the obligations and ordeals of the candidates be abolished. Future Saintesses will be picked from eligible volunteers based on character and aptitude, and raised in the Vine-Bead Court under the instruction of the incumbent Saintess, nurturing their learning of scripture, etiquette, and virtue. —Front page of Kjerag Daily
archives:
[Diary of a Vine-Bead Court Cleric]
Terran Calendar 1101
Winter, Kjerag.
The Saintess put forward a proposal to build schools across Kjerag and establish libraries that the Hall of Writings will gradually share its collection with.
It was considered unlikely to pass due to the opposition of conservative elders, but most of the conservative faction was sent to work in the fields for colluding with Elder Adso in the recent incident, and it passed with the support of the reformist faction.
By Kjeragandr, the old clerics will not recognize the Vine-Bead Court from this day forth. Perhaps all of Kjerag will become unrecognizable.
I did not choose a side in this, and there are many others like me. When we left the room, we looked at each other with the same question on our faces: Will it be a good thing?

[Excerpts from the Vine-Bead Court Letters, 1101-1102, Vol.2]
...I was young when I first came to the Vine-Bead Court, young enough to dream about the miracles depicted in the legends and scriptures coming true before my eyes. However, when I was dispatched to this remote town, I had to bow my head in humility and learn the wisdom of living in such a harsh environment from the locals, eating and living with them. I learned to mend clothes, repair windows, identify herbs, but I forgot how to dream... Indeed, I even forgot how to pray and serve Kjeragandr. She faded from my mind along with the words of the scriptures...
Until you sent those trucks and construction teams here. I never thought I would once again have the chance to sit in a warm room with the children, reading to them the ancient words of wisdom. For the first time, I saw something other than ignorance or mischief on their faces. It was a desire, a thirst for knowledge and the future.
Your workers repaired our houses, and built a school in the dilapidated temple. You delivered dictionaries, novels, even the latest books from abroad... You've shown the children and myself a dream, of a Kjerag that we've never seen before. This is the miracle of Kjeragandr, and the fruit of your love...
By Kjeragandr, Her most humble child remembers your kindness and prays for your health... For you, Saintess, I give my most sincere gratitude, not as a cleric in the field, but as a teacher in Kjerag.

With Elder Adso's fall from grace, it soon became apparent that the Saintess would become the Vine-Bead Court's sole decision-maker. It stood to reason that a single voice would speak for Kjerag from then on. The Saintess was Enciodes's sister, after all.
It is certainly true that the Saintess has grown closer to Enciodes than ever, but to everyone's surprise, the Vine-Bead Court and Karlan Trade soon got into a public feud over their joint school-building venture. A Vine-Bead Court cleric wrote to the newspapers, accusing Karlan Trade of delaying construction of the new schools and prioritizing other post-war rebuilding efforts. There were even anonymous tip-offs that Karlan Trade had, without communicating with the Saintess, reduced the priority of the school construction project.
Some have speculated that the Saintess actually wrote the strongly-worded letter herself under a pseudonym. At the very least, there is no doubt that she had at least tacitly approved of its publication, if not outright instructed it. As public discussion turned to the apparent discord between the two, the Silverashes' family dinner became the center of attention. On the day of the dinner, the Saintess showed no intention of leaving for Silverash Manor, until Enciodes personally drove to the Vine-Bead Court to request her attendance.
No one knows what the siblings discussed over dinner that night, but the construction teams that were previously working on Karlan Trade's factories showed up to the sites of the schools the following morning.

[Karlan Trade Construction Division Internal Memo]
In accordance with communication with the Vine-Bead Court and the Saintess's request, this team is hereby assigned to the Kjerag Basic Education Development Project for the next 6 months.
Current milestones are to complete repair work in rural regions on 11 temples designated by the Vine-Bead Court. Scope of work involves reinforcing and repainting the walls, and the provision of basic facilities and equipment necessary to operate a school.
After discussing with the Saintess, Karlan Trade has agreeded to provide all necessary funding for the project. Construction is expected to begin in October.
Note to all staff: Do not spread unsubstantiated rumors that the Saintess only agreed to attend dinner in exchange for expediting the school construction project.
Project Director Adler

[Health Examination Summary of Operator Pramanix]
Subject: Pramanix
Result: This examination included a number of extra items as Operator Pramanix already has a recent standard checkup on record. Results indicate that she is in good health, with all numbers within normal ranges. A slight improvement was noted in liver and kidney function, eyesight, reaction speed, and cardiorespiratory function.
Two issues were noted in advanced Originium Arts testing and brain imaging scans:
1. Pramanix has demonstrated a slight increase in Originium Arts Assimilation compared to when she first joined Rhodes Island;
2. Brain imaging scans reveal occasional irregularities in her brainwaves, briefly exhibiting slow delta waves characteristic of a slow-wave sleep state before returning to normal, while she remains lucid throughout the process. This unusual activity calls for long-term observation.
Supervisor: Warfarin

One week after receiving her health checkup report, Pramanix sent it to Astgenne. It did not take long for her to receive a long reply letter, despite Astgenne's busy research schedule.
The Liberi's letter filled an entire sheet with recent news about a similar case to Pramanix's: a group of field researchers who were rescued also demonstrated symptoms of amnesia and irregular brainwaves. The letter showed the care and concern of a friend, but also the unique excitement of a scientist.
Pramanix chuckled as she recalled the face of the young woman who sneaked into the Vine-Bead Court. The new head handmaiden questioningly poked her head out from behind a screen.
'Is there something on your mind, Saintess? The look on your face is... different from usual...'
'It's nothing.' Pramanix closed her eyes. 'It's just...'
A cool breeze blew in from the slightly ajar window on the other side. It was as though her friend was always there, the one whom she had spent so many days and nights with. She could feel her thoughts slowing down, as though drifting into a light sleep.
'I'm glad I still have all those precious memories.'
The Saintess dismissed the handmaiden, and sighed again in solitude. She touched her own forehead with her middle and ring fingers. Loss was a feeling she knew well, and she was acutely aware of how fragile and fleeting memory can be.
She had lost eternity... Would there come a day, then, when the people who walk the snow realm forget faith and goodness, forget the path from whence they came?
Will you ever wake up again... and what can I do until then?

Times may be changing in Kjerag, but the work of the Saintess goes on.
Pramanix spends about a third of her time in the deepest reaches of the Hall of Writings, translating scriptures that have yet to be deciphered.
An elder suggested it would be understandable to take some time off, given the present circumstances, but she declined, which earned her respect even amongst the stoic ascetics of the Vine-Bead Court.

She flips through the tomes like she has done countless times before, but now, her head handmaiden is no longer there to give her the correct answer. She must rely on herself.
[You have awakened me together. She said as She walked out from the water. I know you (crossed out) I saw that you have come from different places, and reached here after much hardship.]
I remember this passage about the first time she revealed herself to the people. Come to think of it, she appeared just as suddenly the first time we met. I should have realized she made no sound with her footsteps...
[Then She demonstrated her (left blank with the comment 'meaning unknown' next to it), and fruits and grain began to grow from the soil, and the people learned sweetness and satiation for the first time.]
I don't recognize this word. I'll have to discuss it with the other clerics later. Kjarr used to bring me candied fruits when I was in a bad mood. 'Eat something sweet, and you'll feel better!' She always said that.
[And thus it all began. She walked amongst the people, showered miracles upon them, and reconciled their differences. The three clans began to live upon this land, and so the land came to have a name.]
[She told the people: Remember that this is not eternal. When there is a name, there is a meeting, and each meeting must have a parting.]
The Saintess's fingertip lingered at the end of this line... You may look muddle-headed, but your mind is clearer than anyone else's. Taking me away from the memory before the words are said... what a cunning girl...

'Saintess!' Youthful voices broke Pramanix's reverie. A group of children dressed in simple, neat matching outfits were standing outside her door.
'The students you put into the schools. They take an annual field trip to the Vine-Bead Court, and they're waiting for an audience with you.' Her new head handmaiden reminded her. Pramanix nodded and walked towards the excited children.
One girl, however, stayed away from the crowd, hiding behind a tree in the distance.
'Saintess...' a boy whispered to the Saintess, 'She's really timid, and she's never left the village in her life...'
Pramanix approached the girl with a smile and extended her hand. After a moment of hesitation, the girl timidly took her hand. Pramanix felt the warmth of the girl's palm, and a tinge of nostalgia.
Is it you? No, but...
They are the future of Kjerag... I can feel you through them, and see their kind and pristine souls, just like yours.
Perhaps this is how Kjerag and I will remember you, Kjarr.

modules.moduleDescription:
Technically, I have met Enya 'for the first time' three times.
Our very first meeting was when she was born. She was tiny, curled up in the bosom of her mother who she so resembled, a near carbon copy. The most adorable of miracles.
The Silverash couple had prayed for her, praying with all their heart that blessings, health, and everything bright and beautiful they could think of would fall into her lap. Across the bed, a young boy, only slightly older, struggled to stand on his tiptoes. His outstretched finger was grasped by the babe, leaving an innocent smile on his face.
The second time was when I saw her during the Saintess selection, and heard her voice amidst the devoted, humble prayers. An interesting voice. I noted how different it was, and saw a fleeting chance.
Long had it been since the Snow Realm saw one with such anger, with such a lively, raging heart. With the winds of Kjerag enveloping her at every turn, she would surely go further and do better. I knew that the melting snow would drip upon her nose, for what Kjerag needed was a Saintess who stood above the crowd.
As for the third, final time, I was the head handmaiden by her side, recommended to her by the elders of the Vine-Bead Court.
At the time, I was already rather familiar with her, and regarded her with dearest curiosity. She, for her part, greeted me politely, maintaining her stiff, unnatural posture.
Of course, Enya was never a timid child. Her many particularities soon made themselves apparent, and with each passing day, we got closer and dearer to one another.
Until the time came to say goodbye, as she held my hands tight, asking question after question.
I could not help but be reminded of her mother. A Feline from Victoria. She loved to pray, but unlike the veneration of the people of Kjerag, she used her prayers more as a diary, pouring out everything going on in her life. I heard about how her children grew, about all her joys and elations, and amidst that joy, a thread of compassion. She said, 'Kjeragandr above, if I must leave my children one day, I ask that you guide them. If they ever stand alone upon this land, lost and confused, support them and show them the road ahead through the ice and snow.'
Prayers were never certain to come true. Most times, it is the efforts of people that are more important.
By the time I had come to Kjerag's border, the Court's reforms and the Saintess's edicts had finally reached even a countryside herder boy.
He asked me inquisitively: 'What is studying? Do I need to do it too? Will they teach me how to read? Can I be like those researchers I saw a while back, staying in a nice big house while looking at the stars?'
The chill wind blew away the dusting of snow on his shoulders. I did not look back. I knew the child who once grabbed hold of my finger, bound in her blanket, had taken her first teetering step.
If I were still by Enya's side, she would most likely be rather pleased with herself, and ask me if I liked these changes.
Oh, Enya, my sweet Enya. The little burdenbeast who dared to jump the fence, of devoted heart and stalwart spirit.
The road ahead shall open up for you, and my blessing shall be with you forevermore.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: I'm used to being your assistant, so I bet I can take care of any work you throw at me. But don't you pile everything on me just because I said that!

It's so much easier working at Rhodes Island than the observation station. You have no idea how busy things get there! Not only do I have to pull all-nighters, but everyone's always coming to me for help. They even said they'd push for me to become a section director… You think I'll make a good director? Hehe, it's still too early for me to think about that.

Kjerag? I like the place. Everyone there takes really good care of me. When I was testing Originium samples with my local assistants, they all suddenly bowed their heads in unison. It kind of freaked me out, and it wasn't until later that I found out they were praying to Kjeragandr for me and the experiment.

My coworkers at Rhine Lab like to tell our new staff how I used to be, half-jokingly. Stuff like how I insisted on recording data even during a liquid Originium leak, but that 'just because something is dangerous doesn't mean it's important.' Gotta say, I'm actually pretty miffed about that. Whether it was actually important or not is something we'll have to wait for the future to find out.

Pramanix's a really good friend. I doubt I'll ever revere Kjeragandr as much as she does, or anyone from Kjerag, but I can feel just how crystal clear and resilient their minds are. For real, this is god's presence.

There was a researcher in Kjerag who told me he's afraid of new discoveries now, because of how they always shatter the framework of current science. I know not everyone who believes in science looks forward to its changes, but me? I always love seeing the new possibilities.

Not long ago, my parents sent my sister a long letter and a whole bunch of goodies from our hometown, meant for me. I may not have made up my mind yet, but… Doctor, do you have any gift ideas for old-fashioned types?

Hm… Oh, hey, Doctor. This is an astrological star chart I got from Sia. I wanted to make some adjustments based on the observation data I got at Kjerag… Since when have I been interested in astrology, you ask? This too, is a field that those who walked before us explored. It may be riddled with errors, but that doesn't mean it's completely devoid of value.

In Kjerag, I witnessed a power that I couldn't comprehend for the first time. The further I walk down this path of science, the more I am pushing the boundaries of the unknown... Don't worry. I respect all explanations for the unknown, and I know I will one day demystify it.
Huh? Is the Doctor asleep? Then I guess I'll take the chance to get a nap in, too.

It's great to see you again, Doctor. I reviewed my time onboard and my workflow at Rhodes Island. I'm pretty confident I can handle anything that comes my way. Hm? You've always been satisfied with my work? Hehe…
There's still room for improvement. Looks like I will have plenty to do once I get back.
Huh, still the same medals as before. So pretty.
Nothing exists independently of us. Rather, we observe and change everything. That's why I believe in science.
Long time no see, everybody. Time to work together again.
'Switching firing position!'… Got everything memorized. We'll be fine.
Don't worry. I know our departure time.
In position to engage the enemy. Ready your weapons.
Yep, I'm here.
Same tactics as before?
In position.
I'll do my best!
I convey my starlight to the darkness.
I have charge of this sector.
I will stop you.
There is no limit to the power that mankind may realize.
Incredible commanding, Doctor! Hm? My performance is incredible, too? That's giving me too much credit. I came prepared, that's all.
A victory meeting expectations after careful planning. Now we can all relax.
Huh? This variable…
Oh, don't worry. Once we identify the source of the problem, we'll get this taken care of, easy.
Let me set my alarm.
Whoa?!
Don't let anybody know I'm slacking off—wait, you didn't know? Drat...
Arknights.

Hello Doctor. The lab's too suffocating, so I came out here for a little fresh air. Are you here for a break, too? Hm? Happy New Year? Wait, is it past midnight already?! I was gonna head out with Sia and get some snacks… Oh well, it can wait. Happy New Year, Doctor!
Hey, Doctor. Do you have time to come to the lab and check out my latest breakthrough?

Happy Birthday! I have a present for you—a planetarium I made myself, by hand! When I was a kid, my parents wouldn't let me make them, and it took me so much work just to fix one myself. Come, switch off the lamp and check this out. It even lights up! You think it's a little cliché? Come on, Doctor. Don't say that, even as a joke.

Anything that mankind can gain from these stacks of paper pales in comparison to the reality offered by planting your feet on the ground or gazing up at the stars. I look forward to witnessing more miracles in the mists of the unknown… both at Rhine Lab… and at Rhodes Island.

Stuff like how I insisted on recording data even during a liquid Originium leak, but that 'just because something is dangerous doesn't mean it's important.' Gotta say, I'm actually pretty miffed about that. Whether it was actually important or not is something we'll have to wait for the future to find out.

Pramanix's a really good friend. I doubt I'll ever revere Kjeragandr as much as she does, or anyone from Kjerag, but I can feel just how crystal clear and resilient their minds are. For real, this is god's presence.

There was a researcher in Kjerag who told me he's afraid of new discoveries now, because of how they always shatter the framework of current science. I know not everyone who believes in science looks forward to its changes, but me? I always love seeing the new possibilities.

Not long ago, my parents sent my sister a long letter and a whole bunch of goodies from our hometown, meant for me. I may not have made up my mind yet, but… Doctor, do you have any gift ideas for old-fashioned types?

Hm… Oh, hey, Doctor. This is an astrological star chart I got from Sia. I wanted to make some adjustments based on the observation data I got at Kjerag… Since when have I been interested in astrology, you ask? This too, is a field that those who walked before us explored. It may be riddled with errors, but that doesn't mean it's completely devoid of value.

In Kjerag, I witnessed a power that I couldn't comprehend for the first time. The further I walk down this path of science, the more I am pushing the boundaries of the unknown... Don't worry. I respect all explanations for the unknown, and I know I will one day demystify it.
Huh? Is the Doctor asleep? Then I guess I'll take the chance to get a nap in, too.

It's great to see you again, Doctor. I reviewed my time onboard and my workflow at Rhodes Island. I'm pretty confident I can handle anything that comes my way. Hm? You've always been satisfied with my work? Hehe…
There's still room for improvement. Looks like I will have plenty to do once I get back.
Huh, still the same medals as before. So pretty.
Nothing exists independently of us. Rather, we observe and change everything. That's why I believe in science.
Long time no see, everybody. Time to work together again.
'Switching firing position!'… Got everything memorized. We'll be fine.
Don't worry. I know our departure time.
In position to engage the enemy. Ready your weapons.
Yep, I'm here.
Same tactics as before?
In position.
I'll do my best!
I convey my starlight to the darkness.
I have charge of this sector.
I will stop you.
There is no limit to the power that mankind may realize.
Incredible commanding, Doctor! Hm? My performance is incredible, too? That's giving me too much credit. I came prepared, that's all.
A victory meeting expectations after careful planning. Now we can all relax.
Huh? This variable…
Oh, don't worry. Once we identify the source of the problem, we'll get this taken care of, easy.
Let me set my alarm.
Whoa?!
Don't let anybody know I'm slacking off—wait, you didn't know? Drat...
Arknights.

Hello Doctor. The lab's too suffocating, so I came out here for a little fresh air. Are you here for a break, too? Hm? Happy New Year? Wait, is it past midnight already?! I was gonna head out with Sia and get some snacks… Oh well, it can wait. Happy New Year, Doctor!
Hey, Doctor. Do you have time to come to the lab and check out my latest breakthrough?

Happy Birthday! I have a present for you—a planetarium I made myself, by hand! When I was a kid, my parents wouldn't let me make them, and it took me so much work just to fix one myself. Come, switch off the lamp and check this out. It even lights up! You think it's a little cliché? Come on, Doctor. Don't say that, even as a joke.

Anything that mankind can gain from these stacks of paper pales in comparison to the reality offered by planting your feet on the ground or gazing up at the stars. I look forward to witnessing more miracles in the mists of the unknown… both at Rhine Lab… and at Rhodes Island.

handbook.profile: Elena Urbica, PhD, is a researcher from Rhine Lab's Energy Section, and currently their team leader at the Kjerag Observation Station. One of the primary investigators of the Kjerag Catastrophe.
handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 6%
Originium crystals have begun to appear on Astgenne's lower right leg.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.24u/L
Isolated Originium crystals have appeared on the surface of Astgenne's body, in the shape of a four-pointed star. Symptoms are currently under control via medication.

Comparative analysis indicates significant difference in blood sample data obtained from Astgenne and Astesia. The chance of sympathetic Oripathy deterioration is deemed minimal. Please note that this document is to be archived under confidential files for reference.
—A Medical Department Operator

'Good thing I brought...'
