Laterano has been turned on its head. The old Law is gone. But I still have faith in the Holy City, and in the ties that bind us to one another. Otherwise, why would those who left the Holy City return to defend it together with me... right, Doctor?

I heard Fia made some friends here. Does she get along with the others? She's got a sharp tongue, but deep down she's hiding a heart of gold... I guess it's my fault for making fun of her too much when she was little. But then, where's the fun in raising a child, if you don't make fun of her?

What a tear-jerker. I should've picked a comedy for movie night. How embarrassing, crying my heart out like that in front of you... the tear glands get so much weaker as you age, you know. Say, am I imagining it, or are your eyes even redder than mine are? Come now, no need to fight the tears.

This letter? Oh, it's nothing, just word that an old friend has passed away. I personally escorted her out of the Holy City when she contracted Oripathy, many years ago. I don't even remember what she looked like, how awful I am. I wish I could've seen her one last time, even if it meant getting punched in the face.
Feel free to lean against me if you're tired, though I'm not exactly soft. This suit is almost as ancient as I am. It's gone through quite a few major overhauls, but it's still a... reliable partner.
A pleasure to meet you, Doctor. You know me as Fia's grandpa, if you've heard of... the Sankta Miksaparato... I really regret letting Fia fill out my recommendation form.
That was one wild shot from Fia. Reminds me of when I was young.
What is WRONG with your medics?! Do they think I'm a child? A medal just for cooperating with medical personnel? Shouldn't that be common sense? And… what're they giggling about?
You see all these medals? That Vampire told me to come here to claim my prize. I can't guess what you're going to give me. Another medal? Is it a 'collect twenty to get the grand prize' deal?
I'll help, but you'd better sit down with me for a mug of mead once this is over.
Why do I feel like I'm taking a bunch of kids out to a picnic?
Why does this suit of armor feel like it's gotten tighter, especially around the waist? Thankfully, my gun still feels the same as it ever has.
What are you doing standing there? Come at me! And don't expect me to give you your last rites!
Good, a chance to try out my new hip.
My bones will get rusty if I don't exercise.
I'll hold this ground all on my own.
Don't underestimate these old bones.
I will not fall.
You will not fall.
No one will fall.
No one will touch that which I defend.
Blood? No, I'm not hurt. Just a loose tooth that fell out. Lucky, spares me a visit to the dentist.
No need to thank me. I hardly broke a sweat.
Are we done? We should go home, then. If we didn't do bad, then I say we did good.
I'm fine. I've been in worse pickles before. Come now, don't look so sullen. Maybe a bit of ice cream will cheer you up? My treat.
Anyone in the mood for some classic Lateran soap operas? They're pretty good up to the point where you fall asleep.
Take it easy, you'll shatter my old bones.
A little pot of tea, a big plate of raspberry pie. Let's sit down and talk.
Arknights.

Don't complain about me being late. What's half an hour more or less? Have you any idea how long I waited for Fia to bring you folks to see me in Laterano? Besides, I still need to fix my hair since it got crushed under a helmet all day.
I brought some pastries. You can share them.
I heard it's your birthday. So I brought a vintage from my cellar to join in the fun... Oh, no need to be so polite. A bottle doesn't compare to a good time spent with friends.

The people by your side will leave you someday, Doctor, but they're never truly gone. They are the stars adorning the sky that is your life when you look up at night; distant though they may be, the light they leave behind for you will never die.

Patrizion is a citizen of Laterano entitled to the rights listed in Clauses 1 through 13 of the Laterano Constitution, and the longest-tenured active gun-knight of Laterano. He is intimately familiar with the use of various types of firearms.
In accordance with the memorandum of cooperation between the Lateran Curia and Rhodes Island, he is currently stationed on Rhodes Island as a collaborating operator under the code name Sankta Miksaparato.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Sankta Miksaparato shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.10u/L
Operator Sankta Miksaparato has many scars on his body, but all were properly treated, and in his fitness examination he demonstrated the physical prowess befitting a gun-knight, surpassing many younger field operators.
There is irreversible damage to his left hip joint. Surgical replacement is recommended, considering his age and the associated risk of bone fracture. I am available next month to perform the operation.
—Mon3tr

'I'm a little concerned. A gun-knight's presence on Rhodes Island represents Laterano's trust in us, but... Operator Mon3tr isn't nearly as meticulous as Dr. Kal'tsit was when it comes to dealing with people.'
'Don't worry, I just saw her pushing Mr. Patrizion's wheelchair through the corridor at great speed. He was laughing heartily.'
handbook.promotionRecord:
It has been a long day. You were unable to get out of work until quite late, and the movie has already started by the time you arrive at the theater. You feel less guilty when you sit down and see that the seat next to you is empty; it would be rude to be half an hour late for a meeting with an old man, but not so much if the other party is late too.
The movie ends, and the old man never showed up. As you get ready to return to your office, someone pats you on the shoulder.
'You were late, Doctor.'
You turn around to see the tall figure of Patrizion, his head wrapped tight in a scarf that almost covers the top of his head. It has been a cold winter.
You express your dissatisfaction. After all, it was he who never showed up. He sighs and apologizes.
'The people behind me complained I was too tall, so I moved to the last row. Sorry, I forgot to send you a message.'
Now you are the one in the wrong. You blink.
'I usually pick the late shows, where I won't have to worry about blocking someone else's view. For some reason, though, I always have someone sitting behind me, so I always have to go sit in the last row. At my age, it gets really hard to see the screen from there...'
Patrizion keeps talking along the way, right up until you have to part. That is when he realizes it—
'Oh, look at me, I've been babbling, haven't I? It's been so long since I've watched a movie with someone, and I was just too excited.' He shakes his head abashedly and turns around to leave.
You stop him before he rounds the corner and tell him you were planning to get some ice cream. You can walk with him for a little while longer.
archives:
[A Day in Patrizion's Life]
05:00 - Wakes up and changes into full gun-knight armor. Typically takes one hour (he refused to pick a squire, insisting on wearing and removing his armor without assistance).
06:00 - Morning prayer. Typically takes one hour, though 10-15 minutes may be spent deciding which scripture ribbon to display on his armor (scriptures issued during Yvangelista XI's reign are excluded from selection).
07:00 - Arrives for duty. Patrizion leads his squad to patrol the designated district, wearing a halo amplifier (a.k.a. helmet-mounted supplemental halo light). Laterano guidebooks recommend that tourists in need of assistance seek out the brightest halo in the crowd.
13:00 - Change of shift. Patrizion climbs the walls and uses city-defense artillery loaded with special ammunition to clear obstacles in Laterano's route. Laterano is the only nomadic city that maintains its route by such means, and only the gun-knights are skilled enough to destroy large obstacles (typically overgrown Originium crystals) without compromising the terrain of the route. This is his favorite part of the day.
17:00 - Change of shift. Patrizion arrives at the firing range for practice or to train new Pontifica Cohors recruits, and demonstrates the usage of large firearms to the numerous Lateran citizens who gather to watch. Typically takes much longer than expected due to the large crowds, but he never turns down citizens seeking his advice.
19:00 - Audience with Yvangelista XI to report on Laterano's security matters, discuss the Law, and share cactus tarts (as the previous item on the schedule tends to overrun, Patrizion typically only has time to do the latter).
20:00 - End of work day. Patrizion blocks Yvangelista XI's work account, removes his personal account from the blacklist, picks out a message that includes movie tickets from the many unread messages to reply to, then turns off his terminal.
20:30 - Watches a movie with Yvangelista XI.
22:00 - Attempts to sleep (usually unsuccessful, in which case he turns on his terminal and attempts to send a message to Yvangelista XI's personal account, only to get a popup message that he has been blocked).

[Audio Log]
'Why don't you answer his messages? Weren't you the only one to realize that he disappeared when we were dragged into the dream by the Law? I thought you guys were good friends.'
'Mm... all I remembered was that there was this old man who gave me the habit of eating cactus tarts, but I couldn't remember who it was. Speaking of, you're friends with Mostima, aren't you, Fia? Why don't you answer HER messages?'
'......'

It took six months before Operator Fiammetta and Operator Sankta Miksaparato met on Rhodes Island. She promptly looked up his mission logs and found that the gun-knight, despite claiming to want to find a place outside Laterano to get some good rest, had participated in a large number of field missions, along with other even more outlandish activities: At Roberta's introduction, he starred in the Wrankwood action blockbuster Kingdom of Outlaws. He had showed up at just the right time—the filmmakers were having trouble casting someone more than two meters tall who could play a villain, wear a special suit of armor, and carry a massive weapon that sprayed fire. Conveniently, he was able to do all this without special effects or even a custom costume: all the crew had to do was spray-paint his gun-knight armor. He was extremely interested in acting, and turned out to be a natural, finishing most of his scenes in one take. The producer called him 'the last piece of the puzzle for this film to become a classic'... He also took part in a Columbian off-road rally—it took the combined efforts of Closure and Chiave's team and a full month of work to create a vehicle that could carry his weight and that of his armor, but the final result was unsatisfactory at best: though no one was foolish enough to clash with him, the machine lacked the necessary performance, and the massive rider and his massive bike were the last to cross the finish line at sunset. Though the photo album 'Gun-knights and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance' became the subject of much discussion on the intercity net. ...... Items such as 'helping Engineering with deck repairs' and 'learning qinggong from Yanese operators' were dismissed by Fiammetta as being mundane. 'Is this your idea of rest and recuperation, Patrizion? You're even busier than you were in Laterano.' 'Did you think I'd spend my days on the deck basking in the sun?' '......' 'Sure, that sounds like what an old man on the verge of retirement might do. But I've spent my entire life as a gun-knight and nothing else. What's wrong with a chance to experience other ways of living?' 'I didn't even say anything!' 'Look, Fia, I won't interfere with your life anymore, so I hope you won't interfere with mine either... There might not be much left of it, but there are still so many possibilities.'

It is difficult to define the relationship between Patrizion and Fiammetta.
They are not your average grandfather and granddaughter. He took her in when she was seven, vowing to his fallen comrade to raise her into a Lateran any parent would be proud of. Their first 'war' broke out that very day, when he attempted to comfort the young Liberi with movies when she stubbornly refused to show her sorrow. The attempt was a failure, with Patrizion being forced to defend his choice of films (though he insists it was a win because he achieved his original goal of making her forget her sorrow). The adoption documents at the Notarial Hall record their relationship as grandparent and grandchild, but they rarely call each other that. Indeed, during what little time they spend together, they are like two bickering friends, arguing over each other's fighting styles, interests, hobbies, behavior, and even diet, before going back to their own lives, satisfied.
They are also not your average mentor and pupil. Patrizion was indeed Fiammetta's mentor, and he was involved in the important moments of her life, from choice of school to choice of career. According to her, however, he only seriously exercised his role as a mentor on three occasions: accompanying her when she upgraded her grenade launcher, encouraging her to join the gun-knights, and attempting to rectify her tastes in cinema. He did not deny these claims, and simply reiterated his disapproval of her prejudice against Wrankwood movies.

[Medical Department Audio Log]
'Ah, it's nothing I can't talk about... I've always felt that my role as her mentor was to be the embodiment of Laterano for Fia. As a Liberi child who lost her parents at a young age, she had many questions growing up that 'Paradise' had to answer, questions that couldn't be answered by the papers of the Notarial Hall, or the 'faith' that every Lateran speaks of yet can't properly explain. For Fia, I was a gun-knight, someone who was in a position to interpret the Law. I was a Lateran she could talk to... Honestly, I was in the same boat. After Gia left the Holy City and Pag distanced himself from me—when I realized I'd never truly shared anything with the Liberi I lived side-by-side with—I began to have doubts about the Holy City, and needed a 'Laterano' I could talk to. That was when Fia came into my life. Who's to say who couldn't leave whose side?'
'I see. But why don't you want her to find out that you'll be hospitalized for a while because of arthritis?'
'Because I don't want her to think of me as a bedridden old man.'

[Postcard] Dear Grandmother, I will graduate soon. I would like to apologize for the impulsive decision I made behind your back... Perhaps you already realized that I've felt out-of-place studying theology these past four years. I still believe that my childhood dream is my destined path, and that I can do so much more as a gun-knight than as a priest. I'll be applying to become a cadet gun-knight, so I won't be coming back for the holidays. The training and approval process may take a while, but I'll be in full armor the next time I come see you. With Love, Patrizion [Notice Letter] Mr. Patrizion Pozzo, We regret to inform you that we have held the remains of your grandmother, Marion Pozzo, for the maximum period permitted. As we have been unable to contact you, we have cremated her remains in accordance with the Law. You may retrieve the ashes at your convenience. With Apologies, Ecclesia Requietum Stevonus [Permit] Patrizion Pozzo, Apostolic Knight, is hereby authorized to supervise the departure of the long-range landship Twinflower and accompanying vehicles from Laterano, for the purpose of deporting Lateran citizens afflicted with Oripathy in accordance with the Law. Patrizion Pozzo is hereby granted absolute discretion over all personnel on the ship, and is authorized to make any modifications or cancellations to the schedule as necessary. [Notification] Citizen Gia Lopez, you have been diagnosed with Oripathy, and are now scheduled to depart Laterano on the landship Twinflower in accordance with the Law. Cooperate with supervising personnel during the journey, and remain in the Infected cabins on the lower levels except when necessary. Detailed instructions are attached with this notification. Please read them prior to departure. [Recommendation] Your Holiness: I, Patrizion Pozzo, hereby recommend the cadet gun-knight Aurela, who demonstrated extraordinary performance during the assessment process. While her pride can still get in her way at times, I believe that with proper guidance she could be the most promising gun-knight of the next generation. Patrizion Pozzo [Rejection] To Patrizion Pozzo, Apostolic Knight: As the Pontiff of Laterano, I hereby reject your resignation. What happened to Aurela was not your fault—not entirely, at least—and there is still much for you to do in your current position. If you still insist on resigning and nothing will change your mind, write another resignation letter. Yvangelista XI [Unsent Letter] ...Gia. I retired today. I've been a gun-knight for fifty years... It's plenty, but at the end of it all, I still don't understand what a gun-knight is. At first, I thought becoming one would let me protect everyone. Later, I thought becoming one is what made me lose everyone around me. Recently, however, an even scarier thought occupies my mind. Maybe all the ups and downs in my life had nothing to do with becoming a gun-knight at all. That it's not that being in this position made all those choices for me, but that I was unwilling to make them myself... Was becoming a gun-knight the only choice I ever made in my life? If so, a 'gun-knight' might be no more than a symbol, an ideal, an answer for me that I'd taken for granted. But that's not what a gun-knight should be, and it's not what Laterano should be. No one should allow a symbol, an ideal, to dictate all their choices in life. Do you think I still have a chance to help the children understand this? Or maybe they've always understood it better than I have. I hope so, Gia. I really do...

modules.moduleDescription:
'Where did you get this feather duster?' Fiammetta asks in annoyance as she takes out the scarlet duster.
Patrizion lifts his head to answer as he wipes his armor: 'Oh, you mean Fifi? It was a gift from your friend Mostima, said I could look at it whenever I missed you.'
'And why exactly did you give it my childhood nickname...?'
Seeing the woman's eyebrows scrunched together in fury, Patrizion hesitates a moment, then decides to spit out the truth: 'Everyone thought it looked just like you, so I called it that.'
'Which part of this is meant to be like me?!' She raises the duster and gives it a few flicks, grumping disapprovingly.
'It's the same color as your ear tufts, and when the plumes are sticking up, they look like how your hair would stand up after I combed it for you when you were little.'
'Just throw it away!'
'Now that won't do. It was a gift, so throwing it away would be rude.' The old man takes the duster away from her, sticking it back into the old helmet before nodding in satisfaction. 'Yes, I'd say it looks quite nice in there, otherwise this armor would be rather lonely at home.'
'Then stick some flowers in there, or hang your medals on it or something!'
'But I'm such a humble man, how could I just put my medals on display like that?'
'Then what'll it take for you to put it away?!' The woman tries to snatch the feather duster back, but her every attempt is easily thwarted by the old man.
'No, no, I shan't no matter what you say. It's Fifi who keeps me company when you're not home. When it's movie time, she sits there quietly, never muttering about hackneyed plots or wooden acting or stale popcorn.'
After staring each other down for a good long while, she figures there is no reasoning with him. All she can do is pinch her brow.
'...Fine. There's no talking you out of this. Forget it.'
Upon hearing these words, the old man lets out the smile of a winner, but the smile soon stiffens as the woman changes tack.
'At first, I was going to take a whole month off to relax at home, maybe spend some time with you while I was at it.' She shakes her head and sighs as she continues: 'But since you have Fifi now, I guess I'll just have to go on a trip alone. Wouldn't want to disturb your leisure time, after all—'
Before she even finishes, the old man quickly grabs the feather duster, walks forward a few steps to pull open the storage room door, then throws it in before slamming the door shut.
'Ah, it's just a feather duster, no need to keep it on display.'
'But it was so pretty when stuck in the helmet.'
'What was pretty about it? It looks like it was caught in an explosion.'
'Wasn't it nice and quiet?'
'Movie time should be all about eating popcorn while grumbling with your fellow watchers.'
'Wasn't it just like me?'
*sigh* 'Don't mock an old man...' The old man tousles the woman's hair, smiling in exasperation. 'Fia, it's not that it's just like you, it was me thinking of you, that's all.'

modules.moduleDescription: The Shrine of Nurtury's schedule never changed. At 8pm, Patrizion would take off his armor and open the door with his left hand, because his right one would be holding two hand exercise balls. Half an hour later, he would sink into the sofa and begin examining the two strange objects in his hand—a ball cactus and a spherical hand grenade. He had been trying to figure out where they came from ever since they showed up in his home. Giving a hand grenade to someone as a hand exercise ball definitely sounded like a prank he would pull, but who would he give it to? Not Pag, certainly: he sleeps with a gun in his arms and the prank would simply fall flat. Besides, they hadn't communicated in years. Meanwhile, the ball cactus weighed even heavier on his mind. Giovanni was long retired, and Patrizion himself was the only reason cactus tarts were still being served at meal gatherings, something Velliv often teased him for. Though he himself didn't know why he had such a liking for cactus. He must have forgotten something. This was why Patrizion never wept like the other believers when the Matriarch explained the order that encompassed all things, when she spoke of a future with no barriers, no forgetting, and no partings. Because he knew that something was missing from that future: the one he wanted to prank with the grenade, the one who made him fall in love with cactus. He knew what Gia died for and why Pag had cut him out of his life, yet there was always one person he could not remember at all. Nor did he know why that person was gone. He was able to convince himself to accept any tangible price, but how could he convince himself to accept a void, when he had no idea what it was or where it came from? And so, when the emotions of thousands rushed into his brain through his halo, Patrizion had to clutch those two exercise balls tightly, so the pain would remind him that the future promised by the Matriarch was missing something. 'Should I be touched, Patrizion?' 'Say that again, Your Holiness, and I'll block you.' 'At least give me the grenade. You meant it for me, didn't you? In return for that ball cactus that I gave you?' 'Maybe I should. After I've loaded it with explosives and armed it.' 'In all seriousness, though... I'm glad to hear that your wariness of the Matriarch stemmed from an awareness that I was missing.' 'I just felt someone was missing. I didn't know it was you. I can't pay a price when I don't even know what it is, that's all. I might have served the Matriarch wholeheartedly if I'd remembered it was you.' 'Then thank God you didn't.' 'Thank God I didn't remember.'

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Don't worry, this is all routine work. I've reviewed the correct process numerous times. Now... how do I edit these permission logs again?

Yes, I declined Dr. Warfarin's request to perform a scientific examination on you, as per Kal'tsit's instructions. She wants to study me too? It's worth considering... She could assist with analyzing the knowledge and memories I've acquired. I know what she wants, and our goals are aligned.

I'm getting used to speaking plainly with the operators, Doctor. They've been cooperating with my check-up requests, and I'm addressing their concerns as Kal'tsit would, in the ways they're accustomed to. Our coordination has become increasingly seamless. Oh? There's been a steep drop in Medical appointments?

Why abandon a more efficient, more robust form? Why would I prefer others not fear me? I never considered this before. I made an unconscious decision the moment I awakened. Hey, are you done staring? I can still easily string you up— Huh, you're saying this is what she meant by 'humanity'?

Amiya's gone to chair the elite operators' meeting. Hmm... She now appears much taller than I remember... how odd. I'd like to spend more time with her, Doctor, but I find myself feeling rather anxious— We can go together? That's a great idea! Err, I mean, a sensible suggestion.

The anti-Originium communication lines have been destroyed; unable to confirm your receipt of this transmission. The Crystal Activity Index continues to surge, and I've observed its escape from the void. Meltdown protocols initiated. I will eliminate all interceptors. Find her... and Kal'tsit.

'Protect the Doctor. Protect Amiya.' This directive indeed holds the highest priority in my core behavioral protocols, but this doesn't mean I am compelled to execute it. Protecting you is my own choice— And definitely not because I'm trying to trick you into dealing with an angry Closure!

Projekt Red likes to curl up and rest by my side, while Folinic always sweetly helps me with things I've overlooked. How should I respond to the way they look at me, Doctor? How did Kal'tsit first learn to love...? I do wish I could hold her once more.

It was the end Kal'tsit had long anticipated. She prepared well, and faced it with composure. She loathed idle speculation about the future, and just the same refused to dwell on the past. 'Keep going.' I believe that is the only message she would have left us, Doctor. We should just keep moving forward.
Wanna hear some stories about Kal'tsit? The kind she'd never tell anyone.

Leave my file here in the Medical Department, Doctor. Like Kal'tsit said, this is the core where Rhodes Island addresses critical challenges, and my knowledge is crucial. Now, let me concentrate on accomplishing my mission.
I saw her.
She ended our cycle of reincarnation, granting me freedom and eternal life... and loneliness. Yet I cherish it, Doctor. It reminds me of what I have lost.

So long as a spark of hope for life remains, the unending cycle of despair cannot shake me. Not even Originium may force my life into stasis, Doctor. AMa-10 has shattered the fate predetermined at her inception.
When necessary, you'll see a more familiar side of me.
Do not worry, I've fully mastered the art of tactical command. Don't fear injury, I guarantee you'll make it out alive.
Make certain my claws don't scratch you!
Enemy engaged. Let's end this quickly.
Communications, linked. Your orders, Doctor.
Deployment optimized, ready to go.
Mon3tr, in position.
Switching forms.
Ruin, and restore.
My talons shall be my stethoscope.
This may sting a little. Just bear with it.
Ahem, sorry, I used too much force…
Some cut-to-the-chase commanding. Promise me you'll deploy me closer to the enemy next time, Doctor. I'll try some more efficient techniques.
Wait a moment, I need to collect tissue samples.
I'm fine, I already learned how to heal myself. Leave the cleanup to me. You don't want to see what comes next.
Stop struggling! You always liked it when I had to carry you during a retreat, didn't you?
No priestly eyes on me now, right?
Hee hee, did I scare you?
I'm getting used to my work and responsibilities as quickly as I can. I will be ready for our reunion.
Arknights.
A new year, and you're still punctual as ever. That means the season's first scientific exam will be your reward— You didn't come to Medical for an appointment? Oh, is this... a present for me?
Doctor.

Birthdays are special for us. We can't say for certain when our lives started. But at the very least, you have your answer deep within... This gift… Kal'tsit hesitated for too long, and never got to give it to you. Happy birthday.

You are reminiscing about the old Rhodes Island—about all the tragic destruction we witnessed, about the happy reunions we celebrated. But no matter how time wears away our precious memories, the ark beneath our feet will press ahead on its course across the lands. Come, Doctor. Everyone's waiting for you.

handbook.profile: Mon3tr is profoundly knowledgeable in life sciences, Oripathy treatment, history and genealogy, and many other fields. She also possesses plentiful experience in mobile combat maneuvers, and offers much-needed assistance during Rhodes Island's rebuilding. Currently serves as a special consultant for the Medical, Engineering, and Field Operations departments.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Mon3tr shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.00u/L
She is no longer steadfast, incisive, or relentless, nor the bearer of certain extreme traits. A reminder that our recent loss is all too real.
Mon3tr's vital signs are extremely unstable. This is not to say her new body is diseased, but rather that she is currently in a state of accelerated catalysis and morphosis—in simpler terms, this new body of hers is not yet truly complete. Thankfully, unlike Kal'tsit, who never acquiesced to a physical examination, Mon3tr is more than happy to cooperate with Medical, perhaps even too enthusiastic at times. We will continue monitoring her situation.
handbook.promotionRecord: Entering underlying linked data region. Executing data integrity check. Timestamp... verified. Authorization... verified. Entering... 'Dandelion'. [Accessing work log, beginning recording] ...... Just last month, a herd of Feranmuts dragged mounts and rivers atop their bodies to the whirlpool near the Black Flow. What must be signed of these Memoranda Pertaining to Abnormal Tides has been signed, to no surprise. After all, as things stand, even the most opinionated of the Core nations must sit at the same table... In short, everything is going smoothly, though the bags under Amiya's and the Doctor's eyes are not particularly pleasant to look at. This seedship contains genetic samples of more than 134,700 native Terran species and their associated breeding platform, as well as compatible databases, backups, expert systems able to answer all possible contingencies, 'Little Handies', vast amounts of equipment... The seedship is ready, and will soon join with the main hold. Our top priority is to find the runaway objective, to try and intervene in its path and allow it to be recaptured by Terra's gravitational field... But the seedship is a brief intermission, an unspoken acknowledgment of the joint project group. We will bid it farewell once it leaves the starpod, hurtling away into the distance... Perhaps it will fade away in an instant, or perhaps it will sail the stellar sea for eternity... Or perhaps it will be seized by some star system's gravity, and these 'dandelions' will be scattered across new ground. Of course, we cannot forget the movies of Wrankwood, the music of Leithanien, the sociological research, sculptures, and literature of Ægir. Many, many things worth preserving... Perhaps, once these seeds have been baptized by the ravages of time, people will discover by happenstance that this ship is a book with said seeds trapped between its pages. The transportation technology Terra has access to has its limits, so this was in truth a compromise, but who knows, it may turn out to be a pleasant surprise. Most likely, Project Dandelion will be meaningless... Just as their every past attempt has turned out. But we cannot give up on looking for a possibility, a chance, a miracle. Like the birth of civilization on Terra. [Work log archival complete, recording confirmed] 'Ahh... Turns out, Kal'tsit, when people's heads are full of serious stuff, their tone of voice starts getting all weird. 'I'm understanding you a lot more as the days go by.'
archives:
Dr. Kal'tsit has left us, and another wearing similar clothes is now at our side, helping to rebuild Rhodes Island. This leaves many feeling somewhat bewildered. We often heard such mutterings as HQ was being rebuilt, the earliest of which even came from Medical itself.
According to the Medic operators, Mon3tr showed up to the very first meeting held after Medical was rebuilt. She stood in the corner of the room, not saying a word, electing to quietly listen to Dr. Warfarin's speech. Eventually, she was noticed. At first, Dr. Warfarin was clearly at a loss for words, but she quickly started raising her voice, drawing everyone's eyes back to her.
'I know she wants to come along. She feels like she should be there. You must have noticed it, Amiya. Kal'tsit's stethoscope, hanging around her neck... Although she got it upside down.'
'I don't think she's trying to copy Dr. Kal'tsit, nor does she hope to be her equal. She's inherited all her memories, but at the same time, she's trying to process all that pain... She needs a little... no, a lot more time, just like the rest of us.'

I have decided to officially hire Operator Mon3tr as Medical's special consultant. This decision was made after an assessment of her professional ability in basic medicine, life sciences, clinical medicine, first aid, and other such fields. Her performance during this period has also been taken into account, having helped provide aid to the wounded of her own accord and assisting in surgery (using two talons to secure the wounded while using another two to distract them—Kal'tsit never did anything like that before). This has been decided by a show of hands from all members of Medical.
—Warfarin
Your hands are so soft, Mon3tr.
—Rosmontis
See you at the training room today, Mon3tr! We're not leaving until we're all tired out!
—Blaze
She's become Blaze's ideal sparring partner, and not long after she started participating in stool racing and nut-cracking racing; she got second place in both of them.
She is Mon3tr, our new comrade-in-arms.
—Stormeye

[Training Room Recording]
'Wait, wait, wait, I didn't get a good look. How'd you manage to block my chainsaw? I thought it'd be a sure thing, imploding the air to force you back. No way you'd be prepared for it...'
'It was my talons.'
'You're harder to get a solid hit on than ever. Speaking of, I was wondering... Can you still do that thing with your mouth...?'
(Sound of a violent shockwave blast)
'What the ****?!?'

With Operator Blaze's enthusiastic assistance, Mon3tr has gotten accustomed to her current body in a short period of time, and has mastered several unusual combat techniques. She makes full use of the metallic constructs that float in front of her. The pair of large and small constructs are able to decompress into a pair of upper talons and lower talons respectively. The decompression process is near-instantaneous, and their shape can be freely changed to suit the current needs. For example, they can be split into fragments and adhere onto someone else, or act as an Arts unit and help her render emergency treatment. The current Mon3tr does not possess the same formidable resilience she had while at Kal'tsit's side, but there is no doubt that her highly flexible nature on the battlefield is not something to be overlooked, whether she be threatening an enemy or aiding an ally. As a new operator who has not been with Rhodes Island for very long—sorry, official procedure, gotta follow it—she has been very active, participating in over a dozen field missions. She has proven herself a great help to us.

[Classified Log]
I've ordered Medical to set up a group dedicated to monitoring Mon3tr's condition. We need to keep an eye on it.
She accompanied Dr. Kal'tsit for an incredibly long time. The end of the gemini cycle system means a painful rebirth, one full of unknowns. She hasn't been awake for long enough... Mon3tr's current appearance is merely her initial form as an independent construct—in other words, her countenance and capabilities are currently in a state of continuous flux. This process is filled with uncontrollable elements. It must be guided. Ever since we experienced that grave incident, there have been more and more disturbing developments appearing across the land. The situation is deteriorating, and that deterioration is accelerating. Rhodes Island has no time to rest. I worry... I worry that our reliance on Mon3tr will outstrip the speed at which she is adapting to these changes...
But no matter what, we will stand with her, and meet those changes together.

[Classified Log]
'According to our intelligence, there has been a surge in 'academic exhanges' between the spires of Zwillingstürme lately. There is no doubt that the Golden Empress is trying to analyze the secrets plucked out from amidst the chaos. The hole in the starpod is still open, and the Columbian government is increasingly engrossed in levitation research... The nations of the Core love new opportunities, but they must understand that these opportunities indicate a brewing crisis that will affect us all, not the start of another round of disputes. We should offer Vina more support. She's able to do a lot more now... But Rhodes Island should refrain from official collaboration with Parliament.
'Just note these words down for now, Mon3tr. The Doctor and Amiya will know what they mean.'

'Laterano's Law has been on guard for a very long time now. The Holy City's futile call for peace across Terra is, in essence, a way of saving itself. We still do not know exactly what sort of disaster the Law has foreseen, but I fear that not so far in the future, all the past calamities we have seen will be but a shadow of this new one.
'If there is the opportunity, try to contact the Law, but by no means regard it as a peer. It still retains the ability that caused endless dispute in the past. It is still able to cause irreversible influence on one's personality with ease.
'But when the time is right, do not hesitate to access its system.'

'I am glad that Clementia and Gladiia listened to my proposal. The 'Land Patrol' is a good starting point. For the time being, Ægir is willing to work on dry land via more neutral powers.
'Ægir boasts of being the successor of prehistoric civilization. It is the closest to the most foundational of legacies, yet also closest to where the sea currents are cut off. If the one I least want to see shows herself, she will not overlook its existence. She will not come to them as equals of humanity, nor will she, as the philosophers of Ægir expect, reveal a million truths to them in endless communion. Even arrogant Ægir must learn how to confront a 'Creator'.
'We must deepen our bond with them, and seek out more possibilities from the ruins. Perhaps even from the Seaborn.
'Raise the priority level of founding an office in Ægir. The two consuls are a good place to start. But remember, Mon3tr. When in contact with Ægir, keep the Doctor well guarded.'

......

'War comes. It will not be one limited to her and us. It is one that affects all of Terra, and everyone on it.'

[Office Recording]
'Kal'tsit recorded this information bit by bit in my spinal cord. She probably already had an idea of how things would end, and made her final decision. Before her life faded away, she tried to leave behind as much guidance as she could for Rhodes Island.'
'You've already told the Doctor and me all of this, Mon3tr. You don't need to sit here repeating it over and over... like you're just reciting lines.'
'No, I need to understand it for myself too.'

>TIMEDATA TT 197/19/09
>ADMIN: Oracle; PRTS
Project Codename: AMa-10
A mechanical lifeform that uses the gemini cycle system as its core. This lifeform is characterized by an impressive ability to learn and a near-indestructible structure, one that can adapt to all sorts of extreme environments. Furthermore, in theory, it will not be recognized as life by ■■■. In the original plan, this model of mechanical lifeform would have been mass-produced by the millions, helping humanity terraform planets and build new homes for us.
At the time, this was not a particularly vital project. It would not have forestalled the oncoming calamity, nor would it have served as the ark of civilization like DWDB-221E. It was more of an investment by its creators. When they were discussing AMa-10, they decided it should be designed to survive, as a way to ensure that in the future, life will still persist.
If that is to be considered the moment I was born, then this ship named Rhodes Island should be considered my birthplace. At the time, she still sailed among the stars, the two administrators aboard her cautiously watching the undulations of the dark tides as they debated concepts for the future.
But the tide fell on them faster than anybody imagined, and the AMa-10 project could not wait for the day mass production of mechanical life was feasible. And so, I was special, and alone.
Once the administrators went into hibernation, I received no further signs of life. But before the true end comes to pass, I still have some duties I must see through.

>TIMEDATA TT ???/??/??
>ADMIN: AMa-10
The administrator known as Oracle has been awakened from hibernation, and I find myself accompanying Oracle alongside the investigation of this land known as Terra. However, this is not an appropriate time for it. None of our projects have progressed as we expected. Oracle should be aware of all this. From this perspective, this awakening was not a rational action.
At journey's end, Oracle issued one last command to me.
'Find yourself.'
This command was not especially difficult to parse. What 'finding yourself' means is known to both philosophers and logicians. But I sensed a strong undercurrent of frustration in Oracle's words.
Perhaps Oracle still had other matters for me to do?
Seek out traces of life. Protect the spark of civilization. These actions may be of equal value to the hope Oracle advocated for during debates. Still, in contrast to that final instruction, they are somewhat more complicated issues.
With these doubts on my mind, I begin my own journey.

>TIMEDATA 899/03/01
>ADMIN: Kal'tsit; Mon3tr
This is the second death Kal'tsit had experienced.
The civilizations of this land are advancing, and the enemies we face are becoming more difficult to handle by the day.
Not every step of Kal'tsit's plan can go smoothly. Her defeats are not unexpected. Yet I have never seen her put her full trust in anyone before, let alone a Sarkaz woman who was once an enemy. But as her mastery of DWDB-221E shows, she is a Terran with more wisdom than most. Maybe this is why Kal'tsit likes her.
The only thing I don't understand is why she gave up her former strength, why she chose a body like an ordinary Terran. She had begun to copy the appearance of the humans of Terra a very long time ago. Imitation is a biological instinct, and the starting point for wisdom, but to Kal'tsit, this copying must have another meaning.
This is not entirely a bad thing, however. We have a clearer division of labor between us. Sometimes her conversational skills can get us out of trouble, sure, but I think using my strength's the simpler option.
I will protect her.

>TIMEDATA 1101/09/03
>ADMIN: Mon3tr
I ran into the Doctor and Amiya again.
It's strange talking to them in words, especially when talking to the Doctor. My subconscious always treats it as some sort of reunion, after ten thousand long years of waiting, and I find myself having to suppress this inappropriate joy. I believe the past me has always been able to communicate with the two quite clearly, but only now, in this current form, is the connection between us truly close. We have 'become the same kind'.
It seems I now understand the choice Kal'tsit once made.

I've been reorganizing this ten millennia of data. It feels like it all happened only yesterday, yet they also feel like ancient, faraway stories. They are the foundation my logic and personality rely on, and the treasures I share with Kal'tsit.
Protect the Doctor and Amiya. I will follow this order to the last, but not only because I was commanded to. It is also my wish.
Perhaps this will be a new beginning. I must 'find myself' once more.

modules.moduleDescription:
You're hurt.
As you leaf through the documents, the paper slices open your skin at one particularly tricky angle.
It's no big deal. You didn't even feel it.
At least, not until Mon3tr comes in with a new stack of documents.
At first, she simply stops and looks around, left and right, like she senses something wrong in the office.
When she grabs your wrist, snatches away your pen, and flips your hand over, you finally see the cut on your index finger.
It's not deep, and barely a drop of blood has oozed out. Your body's natural healing processes are already doing their job. It'll probably be fully healed with just a band-aid and a day's wait.
But it's obvious the medical consultant before you thinks otherwise.
Thanks to nearly all your prior treatments being handled by Kal'tsit, Mon3tr has a very thorough understanding of your body's condition. Kal'tsit had, naturally, handled more serious injuries than this. Sometimes with a bandage, sometimes with medical gel, and on very rare occasions, with direct use of her healing gun.
But what should she do now?
There is nobody who can give her an answer.
Mon3tr is left thinking for quite a while, your hand firmly clasped in hers the entire time. Based on the look on her face, you get the feeling that if you don't help her out of this conundrum, she would end up running around with you on her back, searching for the Sarcophagus.
Which is why you point at a small first-aid kit to your side, stocked with everything you need for basic medical treatment.
Move, search, select, use. In relief, she follows your 'orders'.
After using a cotton swab to disinfect the wound, she gently yet deftly plasters on a band-aid. Once done, she cups your hand in hers, mumbling something to herself as she softly pats your palm. Then, she is gone, before you even have the chance to thank her.
...
You had assumed that little incident was behind you, but twelve hours later, as you supervise the construction of a new plate with a hard hat on your head, she suddenly pops up beside you, ripping off your band-aid.
The remaining shallow mark does not seem to satisfy her, so she stuffs another one into your hands.
Another twelve hours later, as you are brewing up some fresh coffee, you see Mon3tr waving at you as she walks by. An action with a deeper meaning beyond a simple greeting, of course. And so, you wave back, showing her your healed finger. This way, both you and she will enjoy a peaceful night's rest—
At least, that's what you thought. It's just that, the moment you start sipping your coffee, she is already sitting by your side.
'Does it still hurt?'
You shake your head, showing her your formerly-injured finger as you give it a good rub with another, doing your best to assuage her worries.
'But my memories tell me that bleeding hurts a lot. What does it feel like?'
You look at her puzzled expression, and you know you should find some other way to satisfy her thirst for knowledge.
How much did it hurt this time? You ask her to hold out her hand, then you run your fingernail firmly across her index finger. You then turn her question back at her.
Does it hurt?
The answer is, of course, no. The most she does is scratch at her finger a little due to a minor itch. Her heart is now calmed, but her tone of voice takes a turn for the strange as she 'warns' you that any bodily abnormalities must be reported to her ASAP.
Naturally, you agree, and as thanks, you offer her a simple but delicious midnight snack.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Would you care to try some sweets? I could prepare a selection for you. Wine to pair with? I have some too.

My servants relish in manipulating the fates of others. Some imagine themselves cunning conspirators, others mere wavering dreamers. Yet they remain equally cold when consuming lives not their own. And me? Heheh. It matters not whether I am puppet or puppetmaster… for the end of life lies with me.

That Dr. Kal'tsit has a frightening glare. Whenever her eyes fall on me, I feel as if she plans to nail me to the landship deck. Fret not... during my brief stay here, I am but your Operator Necrass, and nothing more.

An ice-cold body, a dulled sense of touch; a pain inside that never rests, as if my own freezing flames pierce me through... But it is the pain I find so fascinating, for without it, I might forget I've already tamed death.

Rhodes Island is a beautiful place, where anyone can write their story, no matter who they may be. It's something of a utopia, built at the theoretical cost of countless lives. Illusions are ephemeral, however, so do try your best to keep it alive.

I permit your silence—or perhaps, your evasiveness—toward my invitation, but this does not mean you can escape me. Once I grasp you, your soul will be mine. Time, life, and joy are all yours to squander, but remember this well: your end, too, lies with me.

What brings me here, you ask? You do. Or should I say, your willingness to explain the glimpse I saw... of a future where even death is gone? Whether you choose to serve me before that future comes matters little... I'll gladly keep on waiting.

Loughshinny? Were she still the girl shivering under that snowy night, I would have simply gifted her a peaceful life until death reunited us both. A pity she ultimately learned to dance between blades and lies, and you surely understand how rare a truly endearing dance partner can be.

What must I do to have you submit to me? Must I plead, or yell? Show you a side of me no one has ever seen, or grant you my dominion over death? All that you desire, I... refuse. First you must submit, and then we can discuss further.
...A deep sleep is akin to death. I hope you manage to wake as usual, Erudite.

Allowing me on board at last? Then, hand me the register. 'Necrass'—how about this codename, Erudite? Hm? Rhodes Island requires I go by a codename, so I've decided to fashion an appropriate one for you as well.
How delightful. Another momentary escape from their predestined end.
A promotion. Does this imply I now have a formal position in your organization? Do you deem this appropriate, Erudite?
This medal symbolizes your trust, yet death is an eternal betrayal of life. If you've thought it through, perhaps set me a deadline—I'll strive to live up to your expectations until then.
Do you require me to conceal my face? No? A judicious judgment. The dead shall remember, while the living will forget.
Your operators might fail to keep up with my harsh demands.
Let us be off, to create many more corpses.
Mortals grieve over death, but death has never mourned.
My flame holds no warmth.
I see it.
I accept your invitation.
So this is your judgment?
A touch of my finger shall crumble your wills.
Life withers and dissipates, remnants left to hesitate.
Bathed in fire, departed souls dance in a frenzy of fear.
The clamor of the dead peters out into oblivion.
You and your tactics are equally lethal, Erudite.
Why repress yourself? I see a desire for destruction in you, and you should let it all out... with no reservations.
Life is inherently flawed, so let's not grieve too much over it.
Should I take them all away? Good, you need only pay a tiny price... I'm sure you can afford it.
Ah. A warm place.
What do you want?
You may hold my hand, if you can bear the icy burn.
Arknights.

A new year ought to be welcomed with fire; burn away the past to build again upon the remains, and the cycle continues anew. That being said, I do quite fancy this tiny flame before me as well. Roast something for me, accomplish what my flames cannot.
Are you happy to see me, Erudite?
Should I prepare a bouquet of flowers for you? For what reason, you ask? I simply want to receive one in return, and watch your flowers crumble into ashes between my fingers, that's all.

Loughshinny aside, Rhodes Island still bears scant traces of Dublinn... don't be nervous. The dream has been realized, so Dublinn should die, but death does not mean to vanish without reason. I shall allow it—let this gravestone of Dublinn remain at Rhodes Island as-is.

handbook.profile:
Necrass, real name Eblana Dublinn, is the former Leader of Dublinn, an organization that no longer exists. After careful consideration, Rhodes Island has conditionally agreed to establish a degree of cooperation with her.
After joint confirmation from the Medical and HR Departments, as well as the Doctor, all of Necrass's files have been moved to the high-clearance database.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis: Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected. [Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0% Necrass shows no signs of Originium infection. [Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.24u/L This is a considerably dangerous level for a non-Infected. We recommend Necrass for immediate targeted medical intervention. She has previously rejected all of our examinations, and we strongly recommend— Sorry, but I have to take her to HR now. She arrived on board in the morning, but only came to Medical at midnight, and the sun's already about to rise. —Anxious HR Operator One week after boarding the landship, Medical conducted a relatively thorough examination of her, concluding that— Concluding that we could not draw any real conclusions. At best, we've thrown around words like 'because' and 'therefore' while merely re-arranging what we already know. By the way, don't ask me about her blood. Heaven only knows if that is blood in her veins, or her flames. —Warfarin
handbook.promotionRecord:
Reading my visiting log? Perhaps to glean some sort of pattern from it? Why go through the trouble when I can simply tell you?
Every time I visit the Medical Department, they just so happen to be packed with patients, and the Cafeteria always just so happens to be open, and the head of the Engineering Department just so happens to be debugging support machinery, and at least two of your Elite Operators just so happen to be nearby, ready to close in on me at a moment's notice...
All a coincidence, I'm sure.
And yourself?
Indeed, you are also always wherever I decide to go, but mere 'coincidence' cannot explain your omnipresence.
Because you are a fascinating mystery, Erudite.
From the time you saved Loughshinny, to the moment she returned to me with your approval, my interest in you has only intensified.
Be that as it may, this land is not lacking in chess players to match wits with. Normally, I'd have left my contract with Rhodes Island and vanished, never to appear again. But I saw you. Smelled the death lingering around you.
—Do not interrupt me. It is not simply the scent of your patients or enemies who have died here.
Death is the source of all power, Erudite, and also its terminus. Death itself is power. And everyone around you is doomed to one day become either the power you wield, or the shackles compelling your surrender.
And so, I shall remain by your side.
Death is unbound by reason in choosing its targets. Once it locks on, it will pursue them until their life comes to an end.
archives:
[A badly damaged diary with handwriting recognized as the Earl of Warwick's]
■ Day, ■ Month
Truly disappointing. I finally found the last two red dragons I've been searching for, but Eblana is silent, hesitant, and timid, while Loughshinny shows no ambition at all...
But no matter. They are my, no, this land's final two trump cards.

■ Day, ■ Month
Eblana has finally improved. She realized she can get whatever she wants as long as she obeys my will, and has learned to be greedy, hypocritical, and wildly ambitious.
Meanwhile, Loughshinny is infatuated with poems, myths, and legends. No matter. The throne spoken of in fables is still the throne, and I trust she will not treat it with indifference.

■ Day, ■ Month
I need no longer pay any special attention to Eblana. My word is law to her. 'Teacher' she calls me—yes, I am her teacher, the one she most trusts and relies on, whom she absolutely cannot do without.
As for Loughshinny... I shall let her be. I am beginning to appreciate her lack of desire, and can only hope this trait will please her sister.

■ Day, ■ Month
No one can tell me why Loughshinny is so fond of that crude baby dragon doll, yet she dares not grab it back from me. She is simply hopeless.
In the end, Eblana took it. I don't know what exactly she is thinking, as she outgrew such childish things long ago.
She flashed me such a sweet smile after taking the doll, but I cannot help but think she wasn't smiling at all...
Perhaps I am simply exhausted by the latest happenings in Parliament. Surely that's all it is.

■ Day, ■ Month
Eblana finally burned that tattered doll, and even told me she gave it to Loughshinny—yes, a lie. It must be. For Dr. Dale told me she personally saw her throw it into the flames. The doctor has always been loyal to me—I know she is, just like Eblana—

The diary stops there, for the other pages have been burned to ashes.

[Interview Log] I know she's here. Yes, only me. The others? They'll never know, as long as you people don't take it upon yourselves to tell them. How? Well, she certainly didn't come looking for me, but you lot were obviously scrambling about to host a very important figure, and I'm all too familiar with this particular VIP's habits. I'm sure you're no stranger to Dublinn's affairs. The ones you know just so happen to represent the sort of people who followed her. First is Mandragora. Fanatical devotees of The Leader who think only of vengeance, but are also our most useful soldiers. Most of the upsetting incidents attributed to Dublinn in its infancy can be traced to their actions, but none of them remain. Then you have the people like me and The Brigadier. Our backgrounds vary, but we're more capable than the ones with so-called seniority, so The Leader tended to rely on us. This complicates our private relationships, but she knew from the start what we wanted, and somehow managed to turn all of our connections to her advantage. As for The Elocutionist and his ilk, do you really think she had no clue what they were up to? The Leader is someone who makes the best of everybody's talents. What I mean is, when she wants to use you, she'll wring out every last drop of value from you. And when you start to consider how to use her—that's right, even the thought of it—she'll already have figured out how to ruin you for good. But the fact that she was able to board the landship proves that power has changed hands. She's no longer willing to be bound by Tara or Dublinn. If Loughshinny wants to shake things up, I fear I'll be affected too. What did you say? Dublinn 'no longer exists'? The Leader personally... eradicated every last trace of it, then died, and came to Rhodes Island after?! ...... No, I'm not doubting that she's capable of that. To bury Dublinn... along with herself, is nothing but beneficial, both for Tara's image and their internal governance... What about the middle and lower ranking Dublinn members? Did she also...? 'They were told Dublinn had been integrated into the Taran Defense Force, and would no longer exist as a separate entity?' That certainly sounds like Loughshinny's handiwork. But by then, Eblana was already... dead, yes? Leave me be for a while. ...I said I wanted to see power capable of smashing conventions, and she's indeed astonished me.

[Voice Log]
What used to be Wellington's demesne, along with the nearby regions with strong Taran national identity—officially referred to in Parliament as Wellington's Demesne and Surrounding Territories—now take orders from Na Saoirsí. This is not without precedence, as the Dukes often change up their borders.
We've even heard of some... 'Modern King Gaeil Legends' involving the death and rebirth of a red dragon, or a Draco from a specific family. The implied reality is not hard to guess, and we need not delve into the details. What is important is that it indeed explains not only the territory's huge shift in public opinion and administration style before and after martial law was imposed and lifted, but also the cautious and flexible diplomatic stance that would have been unthinkable for the previous 'Leader'. She has indefinitely postponed the so-called coronation in the name of frugality, for the ceremonial stone circle must be repaired first, and rebuilding the economy takes priority. She only calls herself the Leader, but has not abandoned private exchanges with the Core countries, and even organized a poetry and culture festival in Leithanien, based on the work of the late poet Seamus Williams.
As for 'Victorians who do not identify as such', we have at most a few sympathizers with similar issues in Londinium. Nor is it a significant problem in the other ducal territories, as far as I'm aware. The migration of the aforementioned group peaked before the conclusion of the war in Londinium.
As for Wellington's Demesne and Surrounding Territories, the Dukes have been keeping in contact with Wellington himself to discuss resolving any relevant issues, all while acting within the framework of 'Victoria'. Regular trade and travel have basically returned to normal, and I believe this issue can also be properly resolved.

The Operator before you jabs the recorder's stop button with annoyance, and repeatedly checks that it is off before letting out a long sigh.

When you asked me about Operator Reed back then, no one could've imagined things would turn out this way.
'She's embarked on a completely different, yet equally difficult, path from mine. I empathize with her, truly I do.
'As for her sister... as the Speaker of Londinium, all I can say is 'no comment'. As Vina of Rhodes Island... there really is nothing I can say.'

[Correspondence Log]
Next, I write this letter as Rhodes Island Operator Reed, and not as Loughshinny Dublinn.
Tara has already satisfied Eblana, or perhaps thoroughly bored her—there is often no difference between the two. Essentially, Tara is no longer in her sights. She only sees what interests her, the things she has yet to have... you know what I speak of, Doctor.
She does not like to lie, preferring to mislead with meticulously woven truths. She has been this way since the Earl of Warwick. Other than feigning a timid and hesitant front when we were just taken in, she hardly needed to put up an act to convince the Earl he had 'educated her well', listening to him even as she bared her fangs at him.
Meanwhile, I cannot help but wonder: was turning Na Saoirsí into a city of the dead an irrational act meant to make me submit, or had she planned for everything all along? Is posthumously wandering this land as a dire consequence of my negligence, a second miracle following the first—or has it always been her goal?
I don't know, Doctor... I don't know.
Please don't get the wrong idea; I bear you no grudge. I yearn to write of my own life like any ordinary Taran, but I'm perfectly happy to exchange that right for the survival of multiple cities and a nation's future. I will not denounce the Duke of Wellington either. He is hardly a paragon of benevolence, but his goal has always been explicit. Dealing with him may be tiring, but it is no torment.
Only, I still can't let go of Eblana.
I'd rather blame everything on her flames. She must have understood the nature of that ominous flame early on, so early that it distorted her perceptions. She was certain that I should be like her, but we did not gradually drift apart from our conflicts and contradictions. Rather, we have stood on opposite ends from the beginning.
Unfortunately, we are twins who lost our parents while young, so we resemble each other more than just physically.
More regrettably, I thought at the time that she would always understand me, and vice versa.
So she mercifully stuffed the toys she was tired of under my pillow, yet I could never tell her I didn't want her hand-me-downs, be it the toys she didn't want, or the authority I didn't like. This sort of thing has happened again and again, and my fear, anger, hatred... all those emotions have nearly burned to ashes by now, leaving nothing but grief.
...My apologies, we've gone off track, so I'll keep it short. Be wary of Eblana, and take care not to be misled by her cajolery or abrupt brutality.
Also, I appreciate the concern, but I won't go see her, and I doubt she has any intention of seeing me either. We will never see each other—
At least, until death descends, we shan't meet again.

modules.moduleDescription:
A Na Saoirsí cook finishes washing some pots and newly cast metal goblets. She walks through the citadel corridor thinking about a better life and a new future, and picks up a pair of old stuffed toys holding each other.
She says: 'Who dropped these dolls? Who has been to the citadel spire? Surely they have an owner, and lost items ought to be returned. I need to find who they belong to.'
The cook returns to the kitchen with her pots, cups, and the dolls, and poses a question to the merchant who comes by to deliver some meat.
'Have you seen these two dolls before? Have you seen their owner?'
'No, I've never seen them before, nor their owner. But they're so adorable with their apple-like faces and potato-like bodies. If nobody wants them, you could give them to me.' The merchant stretches out a hand and points at a doll, 'I only want this one though. It's still in good condition, and much nicer looking than the other tattered one.'
The cook refuses the merchant and leaves the citadel for the streets. When she passes by a guard escorting carts carrying grain, she makes her inquiry:
'Have you seen these two dolls before? Have you seen their owner?'
The guard takes the dolls, and mumbles: 'I once heard of two self-centered brothers who each had a red dragon doll, but they were both unsatisfied and plotted to rob each other to get the other one. The elder had a hidden table knife while the younger carried some flint, and as they walked towards each other's beds...' The red dragon dolls suddenly scald his hands as if they were made of flame, and the guard bites his tongue, tossing them aside and running away as he says, 'No, that story's completely unrelated to these two! I don't know about them or their owner!'
The cook picks up the dusty dolls, carefully wiping the dirt off them. She circles the city streets a few more times until dusk gives way to night, and a woman, a wakewoman, shows up behind her.
'Miss cook, I heard you've been asking around about something. I came here looking for you, because I know the answer you seek.'
'Have you seen these two dolls before? Have you seen their owner?' the cook asks.
'I've seen these two dolls before, behind a coffin, under the moonlight. And yes, I've seen their owner, under the eaves, out in the wilds.' The wakeman extends both hands and says, 'Give them to me, and I'll put them where they belong.'
And so under the stars, the wakewoman walks all the way back to the citadel, to the highest lookout point, to a little room belonging to Tara's one and only red dragon.
'There were never a pair of brothers.' She places the older-looking doll on the red dragon's bed.
'Nor did this belong to a pair of sisters.' The doll's is tucked under a soft blanket, its head resting on a pillow.
'It has always belonged to the red dragon. A single red dragon, and then the other red dragon.
'One dragon discarded it, and one found it a young partner.
She puts down the newer looking doll right next to the older looking one, making them snuggle together just like a pair of sisters.
'Today, they become a pair, and return to the red dragon's bed as a legacy.'

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Wasting me on tidying up papers? Hardly the most brilliant of plans. Why squander a pair of capable hands? Pass those charts and tables over, I'll reorganize them for you... And, as I'm already in your seat handling this headache, let's have you rest for a bit, alright?

Little Garnet here is just an elaborate Arts creation. Whether taking lives or saving them, it allows me to shed less blood and do the job with a little less mess. But in the end, it's nothing more than a crystal of blood. Well, aren't you fascinated? Here, you can play with it for a while... Oh dear, why are you pulling away your hand?

I've taken care of those tasks—effortlessly, I might add. No need to thank me. That would give the impression I've exerted myself over such trivial matters. Incidentally, when will that bunny start asking me for help directly, instead of using you as her messenger? Rest assured, I won't scare her like I did before.

The sisters refused my visit again. They still find me... disagreeable. I've never claimed Rose Riverside's Canoes to be a harmonious family. As we can perceive the rhythmic pulse of each other's hearts pumping blood, the trust between us needn't rely on sentiment.

No, no one else is here. I was just chatting with Laqeramaline—or rather, with the incantations woven by the Banshees, reminiscing about the riverside landscapes I've traversed. Who doesn't like to take something precious as a keepsake, to hold in place for a loved one?

Some sisters have never seen this landship with their own eyes. Some imagine it to be an egg woven of countless blood vessels; others see it as a ghost formed from communication data and electrical cables. How do I know their imaginings with such clarity? Good question. How indeed?

I won't tell a soul, so tell me: the one who just entered the office and the one who came in earlier, they have a rather... sensitive connection, don't they? Look at your furrowed brow... I'm not angling for intelligence, I'm genuinely concerned about you. Do be careful not to get caught up in emotional entanglements.

Rejecting the kindness of others is terribly rude, wouldn't you agree? Some people, when they notice changes within themselves, want to break away from the past. But me? I will always remember the most intimate moments I've shared with each of my friends. These memories aren't fabricated, so why would one arbitrarily deny our friendship?

Indeed, my interrogations are truly gentle. As long as enough blood flows, I can thoroughly sift through a heart and excavate all the secrets I wish to know. A pity, though, that you and your blood are simply too precious. Do strive to live on. The day you lie mortally wounded on death's door, I'll be there to see you.
Hmm... Pulse is steady. Not dead, just asleep.
Codename, Entelechia. It's been quite a while, battlefield commander of Rhodes Island—Don't feel bad that you've forgotten me. No one can know every single one of our Canoes.
Can a recording on a machine be more truthful than a memory bubbling from one's heart?

I should 'promote' you too, shouldn't I, as a token of appreciation? Why don't I purify the blood in your body, see if you can become a pure Vampire… Relax, you're not a mixed-blood Sarkaz, and unworthy of a torture you could not endure.

Ah, a medal... Have you thought it through? I'm rather fussy when it comes to gifts and the ones handing them over. The vows between Canoes come first, so I can't do much for Rhodes Island... But if a friend has a personal favor to ask, I don't mind lending a hand at times.
I don't mind escorting this many people at once.
Take care not to let your blood run dry.
Every drop of blood whispers.
I prefer a clean floor, so I'll grant you a death without shedding blood.
Oh, you have an indecisive side too?
If you need to calm down, I can slow your heartbeat for you.
At moments like these, Little Garnet shines most brilliantly.
Don't get me wrong. I don't like the smell of the battlefield.
Gush forth from your heart.
Part ways from your flesh.
Fall back into death.
Oh dear. Don't choke on your own blood, now.
Fine work. I will preserve this moment within my memories.
Can you feel your blood racing? Do you find this scene beautiful? If you're satisfied with the battle's outcome, then I haven't come here for naught.
So long as they bleed, they cannot flee.
Go already. Do not dwell on this mess, nor let it scar you. The aftermath is mine alone to handle.
A familiar sight. As I suspected back then, no one can alter this landship's mechanical design.
Does it feel nice, having your blood run backwards?
I would like to bestow upon you a little gift. Say, an Arts enchantment on your pen nib, the same I use on Little Garnet. How does that sound?
Arknights.

How rare to see everyone in the mood to celebrate a holiday, rather than to mourn someone. It's also rare to see a banquet hall prepare a seat for a Vampire. The sisters of Rose Riverside have spoiled many a banquet before. Whoever said a dinner party isn't the perfect hunting ground for intelligence?
If I were a commander whose life is either the target or concern of many and more, I would learn to tread a little lighter, Doctor.

A new birth is always a bloody affair. Some sisters choose to commemorate the day they killed an archenemy as their birthday; others pick the day their blood was purified and they became pure Vampires. How about you? Since coming to this great land, the blood you've shed and the pain you've endured… how much do you remember?

Farewells are difficult, so we must strive to minimize our partings. This isn't my personal conviction, but it was the reason Rose Riverside rallied behind Theresa, and why I support you now. Very well, present your year-end retrospective. I find solace in hearing memories unfold.

I'm not angling for intelligence, I'm genuinely concerned about you. Do be careful not to get caught up in emotional entanglements.

Rejecting the kindness of others is terribly rude, wouldn't you agree? Some people, when they notice changes within themselves, want to break away from the past. But me? I will always remember the most intimate moments I've shared with each of my friends. These memories aren't fabricated, so why would one arbitrarily deny our friendship?

Indeed, my interrogations are truly gentle. As long as enough blood flows, I can thoroughly sift through a heart and excavate all the secrets I wish to know. A pity, though, that you and your blood are simply too precious. Do strive to live on. The day you lie mortally wounded on death's door, I'll be there to see you.
Hmm... Pulse is steady. Not dead, just asleep.
Codename, Entelechia. It's been quite a while, battlefield commander of Rhodes Island—Don't feel bad that you've forgotten me. No one can know every single one of our Canoes.
Can a recording on a machine be more truthful than a memory bubbling from one's heart?

I should 'promote' you too, shouldn't I, as a token of appreciation? Why don't I purify the blood in your body, see if you can become a pure Vampire… Relax, you're not a mixed-blood Sarkaz, and unworthy of a torture you could not endure.

Ah, a medal... Have you thought it through? I'm rather fussy when it comes to gifts and the ones handing them over. The vows between Canoes come first, so I can't do much for Rhodes Island... But if a friend has a personal favor to ask, I don't mind lending a hand at times.
I don't mind escorting this many people at once.
Take care not to let your blood run dry.
Every drop of blood whispers.
I prefer a clean floor, so I'll grant you a death without shedding blood.
Oh, you have an indecisive side too?
If you need to calm down, I can slow your heartbeat for you.
At moments like these, Little Garnet shines most brilliantly.
Don't get me wrong. I don't like the smell of the battlefield.
Gush forth from your heart.
Part ways from your flesh.
Fall back into death.
Oh dear. Don't choke on your own blood, now.
Fine work. I will preserve this moment within my memories.
Can you feel your blood racing? Do you find this scene beautiful? If you're satisfied with the battle's outcome, then I haven't come here for naught.
So long as they bleed, they cannot flee.
Go already. Do not dwell on this mess, nor let it scar you. The aftermath is mine alone to handle.
A familiar sight. As I suspected back then, no one can alter this landship's mechanical design.
Does it feel nice, having your blood run backwards?
I would like to bestow upon you a little gift. Say, an Arts enchantment on your pen nib, the same I use on Little Garnet. How does that sound?
Arknights.

How rare to see everyone in the mood to celebrate a holiday, rather than to mourn someone. It's also rare to see a banquet hall prepare a seat for a Vampire. The sisters of Rose Riverside have spoiled many a banquet before. Whoever said a dinner party isn't the perfect hunting ground for intelligence?
If I were a commander whose life is either the target or concern of many and more, I would learn to tread a little lighter, Doctor.

A new birth is always a bloody affair. Some sisters choose to commemorate the day they killed an archenemy as their birthday; others pick the day their blood was purified and they became pure Vampires. How about you? Since coming to this great land, the blood you've shed and the pain you've endured… how much do you remember?

Farewells are difficult, so we must strive to minimize our partings. This isn't my personal conviction, but it was the reason Rose Riverside rallied behind Theresa, and why I support you now. Very well, present your year-end retrospective. I find solace in hearing memories unfold.

Little Garnet here is just an elaborate Arts creation. Whether taking lives or saving them, it allows me to shed less blood and do the job with a little less mess. But in the end, it's nothing more than a crystal of blood. Well, aren't you fascinated? Here, you can play with it for a while... Oh dear, why are you pulling away your hand?

I've taken care of those tasks—effortlessly, I might add. No need to thank me. That would give the impression I've exerted myself over such trivial matters.
