handbook.profile: Former Rhodes Island frontline combatant Thorns, now a captain aboard an independent exploration-ship/scientific-vessel/finning-boat/cargo-hauler/pirate-ship. As the captain of the Cuna de Nene, he maintains a cooperative partnership with Rhodes Island. We provide medical and supply services, while he in turn offers us many ocean-related conveniences, as well as the means to contact remote Iberian settlements outside the jurisdiction of the Inquisition.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Thorns shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.17u/L
The moment we stepped aboard the Cuna de Nene, Operator Thorns handed us a piece of wrinkled cloth. It was only later that I noticed the numbers painted on it. To my surprise, it was data on his vital signs, but more surprising was how closely the numbers matched our official examinations. It was like magic.
I asked him about it, and he said it was something he came up with while darning the sails. He used the alchemical substance coating his arm he calls the 'Corazonix' to give himself an examination, ran the numbers himself, then jotted them down on a nearby scrap of sail canvas.
It's fine, I suppose. Maybe a bit haphazard, but it's never a bad thing to be thinking about your own health.
—Medical Operator's report after the Doctor visited the Cuna de Nene
handbook.promotionRecord: No need to rush. This question, I leave to you. There will come a day you can answer in your own words... Or rather, when the time comes, your answer will be your own. —The final words Aulus left for Thorns as they parted [Captain's Log] The sea's much calmer than I imagined. The day I set out to sea, the voices that once called my name from the depths no longer echoed in my ears. I observed every school of Seaborns along our course, yet they all seemed compelled by instinct—relentless expanding and devouring. I couldn't hear their murmurs or calls. Now, all I hear is my own voice. Every time I call the Corazonix back to me, I can hear the rushing of my blood spreading further and further into the distance. At last, it is not the sea calling to me, but me calling to it. I am trying to extend my searches further. At its distant limits, it takes an incredibly long time to recall the Corazonix, and I fear the accuracy of its information will be diminished somewhat. The further I go, the more the sea warps and mutates. Some of these oddities can be explained by large-scale Seaborn activity. Others, I believe may be due to Ægirian technology controlling things behind the scenes. But even further in the distance, there are phenomena I have no explanation for. There is some sort of abnormal 'tide' (for lack of a better word), completely unlike the one near the coast. As if the water of this distant stretch of sea is being pulled away by some unknown force. I want to know what it is. I will discover the truth of the matter.
archives:
[Crewmate's Petition #1]
Captain! Next time we're repairing the ship, d'you mind not using your Corawhatsit?! Sure, it fixes things up great, but whenever you've got something on your mind that silver goop starts flying everywhere and dragging along all the stuff you fixed with it! The crapper door keeps smacking into the crapper, and it's a real pain in the ass, so to speak...
[Captain's Response]
Agreed.
Logically, the simplest solution would be to train myself to keep a cool head, while the most thorough would be to cut off the Corazonix I use as an adhesive to prevent it from reacting to my thoughts.
But my personal decision is to start developing a new quick-drying, waterproof, and high-strength multi-purpose adhesive. I think it would be a fascinating research project.

[Crewmate's Petition #2]
Captain! That knucklehead Fabian dropped the mooring rope and half a mast cracked off! Nearly squished little Nene in the process! So why's he still swaggering about like nothing happened?! He deserves to get flogged or something!
[Captain's Response]
Agreed.
I've ordered Fabian to do strength exercises ten times a day, so the next time he's fastening the rope, he won't get tired and let it slip.
To ensure he follows those orders, I'll do them with him.

[Crewmate's Petition #3]
Captain!!! This ship used to be the La Conquista, so why the hell is it the Cuna de Nene now?! Before asking if it's dapper or not (it's not), we're a ship sailing the seas by our lonesome. Without a fearsome name to shout, how're we supposed to scare off any slimy curs up to no good?
For the crew's safety, I beg you to reconsider the new name! We're looking at a mutiny here!
[Captain's Response]
Denied.
Cuna de Nene was decided by drawing lots, as usual. As a saltfin, I highly doubt Nene used any underhanded tricks to rig the results. Besides, the Seaborn seem unlikely to respond differently to different ship names.
But if you do wish to mutiny, be sure to inform me ahead of time.

[Audio Log]
'You've been out to sea before, Señora Juana. Tell me, was being the captain always like this? Did Captain Cruz have to handle this sort of thing? I always feel like I'm doing something wrong.'
'Why ask? Are you unhappy with it? Would you rather be tied up and dragged behind the ship whenever there's a complaint?'

You the new guy the first mate recruited? She tell you about the situation aboard the ship?
Fine, I guess I'll do it. No secrets on this ship—our captain knows all.
Hah, take it from me. One time he was charting our course with the first mate. One moment, he's talking about the ocean currents, next, he's calling my name, saying my tattoo's starting to swell and to put some ointment on it... I swear to Nene, I never told anyone I got a tattoo in the first place! Since it's of, uh, Nene's beautiful fin-spinning dance... Then there was another time he was adjusting the helm when all of a sudden, he pokes his head out from behind the wheel and hands me a bottle, told me to rub it on if I wanted Nene to play nice with me... How'd he know Nene nipped me?
Oh, but don't you worry! He don't really care about dark grudges or lurid affairs, and he's not one for teasing or blackmail either. It's just crazy how much he knows, and that lets him spot a whole lotta problems... Not that any of us can say when he'll decide to do something about 'em.
—An old sailor's warning to a new crewmember in a tavern in an unnamed town

In the early morning, if it's a clear blue sky, you can see the Cuna de Nene entwined in shimmering silver threads. This is the only time of day you'll have the chance to actually see them in all their near-imperceptible glory. They are the handiwork of Operator Thorns, woven out of the alchemical substance called 'Corazonix' he bears on his arm. According to him, he can release this Corazonix to have it enter any sort of natural fluid (ie: air, seawater, or even flowing blood), inserting itself into the circulation and sending innumerable data points back to his arm.
When I say 'innumerable', I mean 'innumerable'. If I understood Thorns correctly, it feels like your ear is subjected to a foreign language, classical music, and a burdenbeast braying all at once, while your mouth is being stuffed with candy, chilies, and mud at the same time, not to mention the documentary, children's cartoon, and dance lesson being beamed into your eyes... How does he process all that information?
—A Caster's report after the Doctor visited the Cuna de Nene

My dear colleagues, it has become clearer than ever that the Corazonix is itself a paradox.
The 'compass'—the most direct apparatus we can use to decipher it—is the product of many years of research, yet even with its aid we cannot know which of the Corazonix's tremblings tells the temperature of the air, which of its undulations mirrors the ocean's flow, or if its churning conveys of the average blood temperature of a school of fins or the direction of the next geyser to erupt. The way I see it, there is nobody who can interpret the irregular behavior of the compass's Corazonix... unless that interpreter already has a clear image in mind of what data they'll need.
For you see, a tool that can gather endless data has finally manifested itself, but it can only ever show us what the heart of man yearns for... Ah. Perhaps the rumors of a so-called 'guiding desire', as well as the name 'Corazonix' itself—thought up by the court poets to show off their skills—are rather fitting after all.
—A letter from Golden Age alchemist Aulus to his colleagues, kept in the archives of the Inquisition

'Hey, Elysium, what happened to the captain after that?!' 'Ah, right, where was I... Our Captain Valourchin defeated the scoundrels, and finally managed to take his trusty crew out to sea. With a wave of his silver arm, he could see the positions of every sea monster, letting him slip through their territory before they even noticed. He also recovered basketfuls of fins snatched away by the monsters, meaning nobody had to go hungry. And just so you know, he was only able to learn any of these skills because I was there to support him, as his constant companion and closest friend—' 'But if the Captain Valourchin's always out at sea, doesn't that mean the two of you have split up?' 'Err... It's true that I didn't follow him to sea...' 'Then why do you look so happy? Didn't you say you were the best of friends?' 'I may not be out there among the briny waves with him, but we're still partners! Before he set sail, I thought about everything he might encounter during his adventure! Everything he needed out there was prepared by yours truly! I'm willing to bet that even as we speak, he's eating one of the vitamin pills I gave him!' —A tale Elysium recounted about himself and the Captain at a signing for the 'Saga of the Captain Valourchin: Volume 3' 'You sure you're looking for Rhodes Island?' That's what the sailor, beard festooned with clattering bone ornaments, asked me. My heart was leaping out my chest, but since I had already stepped aboard, all I could do was tell the truth. 'I-I was told there were people here who took applications for R-Rhodes Island supplies.' He squinted his eyes, then led me into the depths of the ship's hold. It was like a ramshackle maze in there. Sometimes we'd have to crawl under Golden Age era steel frames, some still partially gilded. Other times, we'd have to climb up and down ladders fashioned from bone and finleather. I was led to a dark room, where a pair of golden eyes stared at me from the other side. The sailor pushed me in, telling me I was on my own. 'Could you turn on the light for me? The switch is 23 degrees to your right, and 40 centimeters ahead.' With the lights on, I could see who was talking to me. He had messy hair and unkempt clothes, yet gave off a vigorous, youthful aura. He examined me carefully in silence as he fiddled with some strange device in his hand. To tell the truth, this was not what I had in mind when I pictured a Rhodes Island office. All sorts of symbols were scrawled across the wall, while bottles hung down from the ceiling. As strangely-colored lights shone from them, I could faintly see fine threads running through the air. It reminded me more of a sorcerer's lair than anything else. 'I, err, think I might have gotten the wrong place. Seeing how this isn't a Rhodes Island office and all. I don't suppose you could just let me go in peace? I've got no money on me, a-and there's no one who can pay a ransom either...' I clutched my autographed copies of the 'Saga of the Captain Valourchin' trilogy in my bag, trying my best to think of a way out of there. If I had really fallen into the hands of pirates, I thought, then the righteous Captain would surely come to my rescue, but until then, I'd have to rely on my own wits... 'Oh, what am I saying, this must be Rhodes Island... O-Oh! Terribly sorry.' Upon hearing the name 'Rhodes Island', the young man's eyes lit up. He stood up all of a sudden, painstakingly dragging a plank covered in draft paper over from behind him. On the back of the plank was an impressively-carved rendition of the Rhodes Island logo. 'Sorry, there's not much space aboard, so rooms have to pull double-duty. This is Rhodes Island. Specifically, its high seas office. Trust me, we're the real deal. Now hand me your application form, and I'll see what we have available...' —The recollections of a villager who, after introductions from Rhodes Island's Iberia office, came aboard the Cuna de Nene to receive supplies

'You met with that youth, the so-called 'Captain Valourchin' again, Lord Carmen.'
'I did.'
'You need not attend the meetings personally. He is of far less importance than our dealings with Ægir.'
'It has been a very long time since tales of any 'sea captain' have made their way around Iberia.'
'...A 'captain' who has looted towns and conspired to murder our civil servants. His tale should be brought to an end by the Penal Battalion's poleaxes.'
'His crimes will not be forgotten, but do not be so eager to bring him to trial. His current conduct is still of use to us.'
'A few barrels of fins to some remote villages we do not have the leisure to look after, and opening up trade routes to such regions... Hardly anything groundbreaking. The past few decades have seen the remnants of the Defensa voluntarily look after dozens of hamlets near our land border.'
'Yet they have not seen anyone from the Defensa sung of as a folk hero. I saw the eyes of those villagers as they praised the 'Captain Valourchin'. I've seen that look before.'
'What sort of look?'
'Sixty-odd years ago, whether aboard the Church's seaborne basilica or Alfonso's Stultifera, every time I returned, I could see their shining lights—Cerro del Faro, Ciudad de las Olas Doradas, sometimes Puerto Orgullo. Even in the middle of the night, the people would look out to sea with expectant gazes, eager to see what curiosities we had brought back from distant waters. I see that same eagerness, the same expectation in the eyes of those praising the 'Captain Valourchin'... I am afraid the people no longer fear the sea.'
'You mean to say he has led these innocents to cast aside the sanctuary of fear and embrace desire instead. Desire that will only invite disaster. All the more reason to punish him as soon as possible.'
'Or maybe what we actually need is someone to light a fire amidst the ashes. We will not find the answers we seek on land. No matter how much we fear it, Iberia's lifeline lies out at sea. If he were to submit to Inquisition supervision and act in our name... he would no longer pose a threat to us. Quite the opposite, in fact.'
'And how did he respond?'
'Ah. He refused.'
—A conversation between Saint Carmen and a senior Inquisitor

modules.moduleDescription:
'We'll reach shore soon, Captain. I can smell the wheat drying out in Finscale Town.'
'What we brought there was sugarcane seeds—they won't grow into wheat in any case.'
'Er, I was just wondering... When we go ashore, Captain, can I quit?'
'I understand. Hold out your hand.'
'...A gold coin? A coin with... arms and legs?! What's this about, Captain?'
'Let me explain.'

More than a decade ago, in a dark and gloomy church, a boy warily sneaks a glance at the soft-spoken priest. Once, as he was held by that priest, he would force open the man's eyelids, trying to see what secrets he hid within his ever-narrowed eyes. Now, however, the boy shudders at the cold glint occasionally shot from them like bullets.
'I know you can hear me, Isidro.'
The boy does not reply. Blood seeps from the wound on the priest's cheek, as the boy stumbles backwards in fear.
'You have tried to kill me. You have made up your mind, I see. If that is the case, you should make the same choice your fellow students did.'
The boy tightens his grip around his Arts unit as he looks away. He remembers how sick he felt as one of those students squirmed on the ground, before a single cold eye was plucked from the depths of their skull.
'You are well aware, Isidro, that those children who chose to become my kin did not do so unwillingly. If you do not wish it, I shall not force you.'
The boy continues to keep his mouth shut. He remembers the final words spat out by that other student before their life as human ceases: 'Why, Maestro? Why won't you teach me swordplay and alchemy like you do Isidro? Why is this the only path I can choose?' It was then the boy realized the priest's so-called choice was no choice at all. He was the one who dictated the options available to everyone, after all.
'If you do not wish to choose...' The priest holds out a gold coin. '...You may consider if you would like to leave this life-altering decision up to chance.'
The boy does not take it. Only once the priest has placed it on the ground does he reach out his hand to grab it. He knows he is powerless to resist. He knows he must make the choice the priest has given him... Or perhaps, think of a way to refuse that choice.
The boy flips the coin into the air. Its cold gleam streaks across the dark room. He holds on tight to his Arts unit, giving the coin the lightest of taps. A fine stream of silver metal winds its way around the coin, becoming its 'arms' and 'legs', allowing it to stand on the ground firmly. Not on its front, nor its back, but on the coin's 'third side'.
'Ah... I see. You believe you still have other choices. No matter. If you are so sure of this, then go and see for yourself. I leave this question and the right to choose with you... There will come a day you will answer me in your own words.'

'So, Captain, you mean that... you're leaving it up to me to choose? What are the options?'
'...No. I told you this to let you know you are free.'
'Then what about the coin?'
'Nene loves that coin. Take it, and have some fun. It's so that you won't regret not having the chance to play with Nene a little bit longer before you go... Once you're done, that coin will come running back to me on its own.'

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Leaving all this work to me? Hahahaha, I appreciate your trust.

It's Siracusan tradition to mask up and dress formally for a kill, but the people of Nuova Volsinii think such costuming means embracing a new life. But no matter the occasion, you must find the best tailor for the job, no? I certainly have.

Ah, what nice weather today—Siracusa's rainy season is over, and the Grey Hall old guy can no longer stay in their seats as all the hungry opportunists rush in. Hahahaha, could the Carnival have been such a roaring success without my help?

If the left sword drops first, we donate the wineries to the city. If the right sword falls first, then the wineries offer free admission to everyone at next year's Carnival. Hahahaha, even as that obsessive, controlling father of mine rots away in jail, the Siracusans will never forget him!

The families, the government, Signora Sicilia... every party has proved their own theories for their own gain. But how is a new city enough? What they want is a brand new country! And me? I want to see all their wishes come true, all of them!

Quiet. I won't have another 'wasteland', or 'civilization' enter my ears. Our new game is not so boring. You must learn quickly how the humans play… Oh. Hehehe, you overheard me, Doctor? Then how about you be my enemy? Come, stand against me.

Texas said I'd show up eventually? Aha! She knows me so well. Anyone would burn her prison to the ground, but how many dare to remain and see what's left in the ashes? Hehe, there is no shame in running away. But after that, you pray every day! Pray that the inferno won't haunt your nightmares!

Whiskey, on the rocks, with a mint garnish. Don't mind me, just knocking a few back while you carry on with your grand ambitions. But if I were you, I'd ease up on the goodness. Or the suffering will double when it all comes crashing down.

You care very much for Rhodes Island, much as Texas cares for her companions. Woo yeah... that serious look on your face! Very good! Why don't we make a wager, with this landship... You count me in as part of this place too? Hmmm... Very interesting, Doctor.
Oh, dear Doctor, what would you trade for the peaceful nights you once knew?
Long time no see. Oh no, did my weapon take your seat on the sofa...? A pity I was here first. What happened on the Carnival stage, you ask? Why so curious?
Bah. What a bore!
I refuse. I don't think Rhodes Island could throw a decent Carnival, even if we put a mask on each and every one of you.
Are you trying to placate me? Or do you think the game isn't fun enough...? I just can't see through you. No wonder I find your trust so entertaining!
Where stand the wilds? Where stand the cities?
A wolfpack I am.
Ah, the parade's here.
The mad lead the blind! Hahahaha! 'Tis no wonder they never tire!
The show hasn't started, and this place is already such a riot!
Look, Zaaro! See the game we humans are born playing—
Your weapons are right at your fingertips, why wait?
No need to cover up! If secrets go public, then everybody is in the game!
What should I do? I knew who you were right away.
What are you waiting for? The curtains are about to fall!
The spotlight shines on us. Hahahaha!
Do not disappoint tonight, my friends.
A grand spectacle, a perfect show, a dignified exit. Bravo, Bravo… But I won't applaud, not without an accident befalling the act, haha.
Work's over, time for a drink. Where is Texas?
Come gawp at those whose masks have fallen. Some carefree, struck with panic. Some let loose, so free and manic! Oh, what fun to prowl this ball!
Defeat? Hahahaha. That's just the end of Act One.
It's quiet in here—not afraid to miss the excitement outside?
Haha... is this how you greet Texas too?
Come here! Dance with the wolves.
Arknights.

Happy New Year! You're inviting me in? How will you introduce me? Texas's archenemy, the Saluzzo traitor, or the white wolf who would conquer all? Hahahaha... Enjoy the evening, Doctor. For tomorrow, the twin moons shall rise for the hunt... like always.
Here's a Carnival costume. Put it on.

One birthday, my father brought me to tour a vineyard in bloom. I wondered why there was no monstrous vehicle to run it down to ruin, along with the whole of Siracu— What? No, I bought this bottle of wine off some random shelf. That manor became a trash heap long ago.

Hah, the things you and the Rhodes Islanders do are quite interesting indeed. Siracusa, no, everywhere of this land is a filthy swamp, yet Rhodes Island manages to hold on still. Is it because you're so adaptable, or... did you have a hand in writing the rules of the game?

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Ohi, Zaaro, still not done washing those glasses? Enough cracking the ice cubes, Caesar… Keep your hats on tight and ears perked up—we have to hear the new Boss's stirring speech before we open.
An unlicensed bar, an omnipotent bartender, and one simple rule: You're the Boss today, free to dominate all that you see. Haha, put all your embarrassing desires onto the wine list.

Try it. It's a 'Demon Sunrise', brought here by your predecessor, a refugee Snowpriest from Sami. Good stuff, no? I know you won't disappoint us—even if the wolves tear you to shreds, your legacy will only grow.

Done for the day! The place is yours now, I trust you have the time and space to tinker with your 'secrets'. Call it the Boss's privilege. Zaaro, is the car still not ready? Ssh—a word of advice: Don't ask where your employees go after work.

Of course I like the bar. Without it, where would I find the inspiration for new games to play? It's lawless? Hmph, Agnese, why don't you tell our good Boss, how we've been waiting every day for the police to knock on our door with an arrest warrant? It can't be helped, we get either baddies, or poor things like you.

I said before I want you to be my enemy, but this doesn't stop me from realizing your wishes. Texas is no stranger to this either. This bar will be a valve for the swamp. You can decide to turn it off, or let the mud flow. Isn't this much more interesting than being boring old enemies?

Done thinking, O savior of ours? Will you share a bottle with the Church of the Deep and the Yurodstvo, or perhaps consult the revenants on how to make Rhodes Island soar past the starpod? Haha, feel free to go wild—give yourself, and your employees, a challenge!

Yes, the Cyclops in the recording was a Boss once. He tried using the 'tragic future' glimpsed through his foresight to change my rules, but what a pity—just five minutes before his shift ended, he threw up blood and died… Oh, you're an expert in this field too, no?

An ice cube? Open your eyes, Boss. That's a roccia in your glass. Do you want to see its creator, your old friend? In this bar, you can do it all. Of course I know the thing, and of course I can do it. For the low price of… suffering? Haha, I'd be glad to oblige!
Still undecided? Haha, just a friendly reminder: The ice's melted—it's rude to keep a bartender and her drinks waiting.
Haha, keep your hood on. You're the Boss of this bar now. Lappland and her merry pack of wolves, at your service.
There is nothing new under the twin moons.
Congratulations! The wolfpack and I have not lost patience with you, for now.
My gratitude, Boss. You've instilled a passion in us for our work—for now, at least.
Ohi, Vargo. Get our thirsty Boss and me a couple shots of whiskey to wet our whistles.
I'm still waiting for you to tell me what 'order' means.
Earlier opening hours? You're the Boss.
You want some ice to chew on? Keeps the pain away, and keeps you awake.
Ohi, Zaaro! Patience!
Haha, was that a yawn from me?
Interesting! Agnese, Vargo. Don't get in my way.
What a bore… Zaaro, Caesar. Sweep the place, quickly.
Here you go—a 'Civilizzato Classico'.
Enjoy—'Barrenlands' Special Brew'.
Bartender's Choice—'Custom-made Quagmire'.
It's happy hour!
All drinks on the house.
Not bad. I haven't seen the wolfpack so enthusiastic in a long while.
Is this what you wanted? You know the price of boring me, don't you, Boss?
When will a new Boss come…? Zaaro, why isn't this one gone yet?
So this is the decor you're planning to draw crowds with?
Olives for you? Yes, I've changed the specials again.
Zaaro, bite down on the Boss's head. I want to see what's inside.
Arknights.

Here, a vodka martini with five olives. Don't worry, just sample your employee's craft. Bravo. One more shot, and tell me all about your grand master plan to save or destroy Terra—this will be my New Year's gift to you.
Friendly reminder—you're running out of time to boss me around.

I get it, a wish you've pondered a thousand times, when spoken aloud on your birthday, will double the chances of coming true—ohi, my wolves and I are right before you, so why are you still making your wish with your eyes closed?

A single ark, along with the fate of millions, haha. Same little ambition as always. Though, I truly can't imagine what exactly you'll destroy and leave behind… I expect you to reward me with that pleasant surprise, Boss.

handbook.profile: Lappland, unemployed. The only daughter of Alberto Saluzzo, patriarch of the Siracusan Famiglia Saluzzo. She is currently separated from her family. Lappland excels in solo combat, and often assists Rhodes Island in tactical Arts assaults and elimination operations.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Originium crystals distributed across surface of body, confirmed Infected by medical examination.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 14%
The Originium crystals on Operator Lappland's body are still spreading.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.33u/L
Density has significantly increased compared to previous results.

'She's crazy! Patients like her are the most annoying to deal with. She's always so polite and cooperative when we're conducting tests, and even smiled while saying she'd take good care of herself as Medical suggested... And look what happened. Can we just beat the daylights out of her, so we can treat her here uninterrupted for a month?'
'You want to try?'
'...'
handbook.promotionRecord:
Luchino recognized this special client: she once opened the doors of Tailor de Montano and ordered two Carnevale outfits of the highest quality in one breath, and even personally drew the famiglia patterns she wanted on the costumes by hand. This time, she was still wearing one of the outfits, but the Carnevale mask that used to be sitting at her waist was now missing. Unlike a traditional Siracusan suit, the mask is the most important part of a Carnevale outfit, and the most unique visualization of the event. Luchino could not ignore the missing mask, and boldly asked why.
'I gave it away.'—That is how the client responded.
It was not De Montano's professionalism that led him to ask the question, but Luchino still expressed his willingness to make her a new mask and complete her outfit. After all, he knew who his client was, and it would be best if she had a mask ready for any future Carnevales. Nonno had passed a long time ago, and his current skills were already 'up to par', so as the current manager of De Montano, he was obliged to maintain any relationships with old clients, no matter who they were.
'No need, little tailor. Is there a difference between wearing one mask and wearing two?
'The outfit is clearly already complete!'
archives: Lappland did not notify anyone before returning to the Rhodes Island landship. She suddenly showed up in HR's office, taking up half the sofa while her weapon occupied the other half. She looked as if she had just came back from traversing the wastes, covered in sand and dust... had it not been her gorgeous and somewhat extravagant Siracusan attire suggesting more to her story. Before she showed up, we learned from mission logs sent by the Nuova Volsinii branch about what happened at the Carnevale, including the fact the city government had revoked all of her licenses and banned her from returning to the city. We tried to ask how she was related to the city's unrest that nearly turned into civil strife, and she did not shy away, giving us a rundown of what she did over the next two minutes. She spoke in a breezy tone, but the operator in charge of recording stopped writing, frozen with fear. According to her, what she did at the Carnevale included but was not limited to: Helping strangers put Alberto—her own father and head of Famiglia Saluzzo—in prison, driving a cargo landship loaded with weapons into a massive parade crowd, and helping a Vulpo mother exact vengeance... All of this, to 'spice up' the Carnevale. 'Honestly, shouldn't they have given me a medal?' Lappland added, after a brief pause, 'How else would they be able to boast about how Nuova Volsiii has gotten off to a good start in reforming Siracusa!' 'Though...' she suddenly stopped talking, looked at the operator recording her words, and asked, 'What do you think? If the Carnevale started like this, won't future Carnevales only get more and more boring?' With her signature smile on her face, it was hard to tell if she spoke with regret or schadenfreude. The operator was stunned and didn't know how to respond, so the conversation abruptly ended there.

Lappland and Texas bumped into each other in the Rhodes Island lounge.
We have a rough understanding of the subtle relationship between the two operators—everyone can still remember why Lappland joined Rhodes Island in the first place, after all. After the collaboration between the Lungmen branch and Penguin Logistics ended, she suddenly cornered one of our operators, handing over her resume with a smile and—while resting her two strangely shaped blades on the operator's neck—asked: 'Is Texas your employee?' Afterwards, be it a deliberate provocation, inexplicable adulation, or vague investigation, it is no secret that she has always set her sights on Texas, and thus we have prevented them from meeting directly. However, one time Texas unexpectedly returned to the landship, and by the time we were aware and trying to prevent them from meeting, she had already run into Lappland who was drinking alcohol by herself in the break room.
The operator who had rushed to 'get the situation under control' came back silently, and described what he saw with a confused look on his face: Lappland casually took a glass from the alcohol rack and poured a glass of amaretto whiskey, and Texas sat down, took the glass and drank it like it was just a normal day. Lappland nonchalantly asked Texas about her recent work as a special logistics consultant for Nuova Volsinii, and made a few casual jokes about city hall's attempt to promote the 'New Urban Management Act' to other Siracusan cities, to which Texas replied with a few words. After finishing her drink, Texas leisurely stood up and left, and they even wished each other well before going their separate ways! They seemed like nothing more than a pair of old friends who understood each other perfectly and had met up at an agreed time whilst going their respective ways.
To be honest, we have no clue what exactly happened. We only know that they had met a few times during the Carnevale, so how did their relationship suddenly turn out like this? Have they resolved their differences and reconciled, or is this another tug-of-war, with a hidden turbulent undercurrent? Who knows? One day they might cross swords and stain the deck with blood. For a while after this, we continued to observe the two, who met up a few more times, but the general atmosphere was similar to that day in the break room.

'I'm tired. Tired of guessing what's going on between them.
'I don't care if those two have let go of their grievances or not, but at least they're no longer as tense as before, which saves us a lot of trouble.'
—An HR Operator in charge of observation

Famiglia Saluzzo traces its origins to the Siracusan Autonomous Region three centuries ago. Siracusans see the family as extremely robust, even turning a mistake made at an important point in history into a story of survival.
In the late 1030s, when Signora Sicilia established the 'Guns and Order', there were many dissidents, Alberto's grandfather among them. During the most important revolution of modern Siracusan history, the head of Famiglia Saluzzo stood against Signora Sicilia, and this decision nearly spelled the end of the family. Several major opposition famiglie were practically liquidated overnight, and Famiglia Saluzzo too suffered the Signora's retaliation. To spare the rest of his famiglia from suffering, Alberto's grandfather ultimately ended his life in his own study, and the ancient family established during Lethanian rule that rose to prominence by selling bootleg liquor to Gaul almost collapsed entirely.
Fortunately, Alberto's father painstakingly brought his family into the Grey Hall and they became one of the Dodici Famiglie, though the family's prestige and power had yet to recover from the prior shock. Alberto was born into and grew up in those circumstances, and took over the famiglia's future from his father's hands.
—Excerpt from a special study on Siracusa conducted by a certain Columbian university

We once asked Lappland about Famiglia Saluzzo's situation, but she was uninterested and kept yawning in response, so we eventually abandoned our questions.
Based on information later provided by HR, we managed to make a rough analysis of what happened. Alberto did not at all trust the emotions and legacy between the generations of his family: his grandfather's mistake during Signora Sicillia's reforms had, after all, brought upon disastrous consequences, but he was also disgusted by his father's harsh denouncements of his grandfather, and this distrust was passed down and reflected in his attitude towards his daughter—He had an almost perverted desire to control her, equipping her with an elite education, but also throwing her into the barrens as a child for training, and even expelling her from the family because of her various transgressions. Of course, this analysis is meaningless, for it is difficult for us to attribute Lappland's current behavior solely to a 'failed education'. This would not explain her simultaneous 'politeness', 'aggressiveness', 'hunger for battle', and 'penchant for theatrics'. After observing her for a long time, she seems to have been 'born' mad, while her father and family's influence merely fanned the flames.
'Let's just settle Lappland's files as-is. There's no point analyzing a lunatic's personality.'

Lappland's return to Rhodes Island has provoked strong reactions in some of our Operators. In particular, Operator Lunacub who had just recently recovered from rather serious injuries suddenly began running down the landship corridors, excitedly shouting 'I finally saw Agnese again!' Or Operator Projekt Red who would on occasion suddenly tense up, muttering words like 'Grandma'. Meanwhile, Lappland would always just happen to be passing by, as if the one they were talking about were by her side. [Classified Log] Take good care of Red. The Signori dei Lupi's game is over, but this child has grown up in such unusual circumstances, and suffered so much deception and betrayal that will take a long time to deal with. I came up with many ways of stopping her from ending up like this, but still I failed in the end. Fighting with each other is natural for the Signori dei Lupi, and not every human who interacts with them can be as lucky as Lunacub, or Lappland... to naturally integrate into a wolf pack, even becoming their sovereign in the latter case. I hear she has made a deal with Emperor and Duck Lord while representing the wolf pack. Be it Emperor, Duck Lord, or the Signori dei Lupi, I have dealt with many beings like them. They are immortal, and most find a way to get along with humans and live on this land with their unique character. I've also met humans with unusual life experiences. Be it due to their ancestors' adventures or major Catastrophes, they possess powers or insights beyond human limits and are closer to the former. Lappland seems to have been born this way. She is obviously still young and her experiences aren't that out of the ordinary, but the boundaries on her are already blurred. She is embracing a certain kind of madness ordinary people will find difficult to comprehend, which is not a good thing... Continue watching over her, Doctor. Going back to our original topic, the Beast Aristocrats may phrase it differently, but it all comes down to the same thing: they felt uneasy. If even they feel threatened to the point of ignoring their respective traits so they might contact each other and figure out a countermeasure, then we must focus on what is causing their nervousness.

modules.moduleDescription: It's almost eight. She's out by the forest, and now she's getting impatient. Whatever happens, she needs to be home before nine. A rule her father made. She's allowed to die, but not to break this rule. So, she has made herself a rule too: before eight, finish everything she has to finish, and kill everyone she has to kill. But she hasn't finished her job today. The enemy's had more forces hidden than the Saluzzos expected, and things are getting bogged down. Her guys have the ride home ready. She knows her father doesn't give a shit about her results, just that she's punctual. So she chooses to get on. But the enemy choose this moment to loose a pack of trained tuskbeasts, a handful of which breach the vicinity, and charge straight aboard the wheels, aimed straight for her throat. They can't get near her, of course; she dodges easily, and decapitates them in the same motion. Still, something tells her they slashed something on her. She looks down. It was the pocket watch. They scratched the glass face and left a real deep claw mark. She can't tell the time through it. A hint of nerves immediately bolts through her. But right after that, a surprising sense of relief. The tension she felt a moment ago vanishes into thin air. 'Lemme out,' she suddenly says. Her goons push back as hard as they can, but she gets out anyway, and paces one step at a time towards the forest. Tick tock, tick tock, it's eight o'clock. She paces into its depths, vanishing without a trace. Today, it'll take her until the dead of night before she's killed them all, and only at the crack of dawn will she finally traipse back through the Saluzzos' door. Today, Alberto will fly off his goddamn handle. Today, Lappland will smile a big happy smile. ...... 'There's a story that goes like... A girl gets a spell cast on her that turns her beautiful, but then she'll turn back right at the stroke of midnight.' Idly fiddling with her watch, she throws out a sudden remark. 'Zaaro, you scared the magic'll run out? Scared you'll just die like a nameless tuskbeast out in the barrens where nobody'll ever know?' 'What a fool's question. You disrespect the Signore dei Lupi's very nature.' 'You know, most humans—the ones you see as toys—they think the same way. And in my eyes, you're all the same. 'You think the spell cast on you will last forever and forever, and then there comes a day, a moment the magic wears off, and you howl like a mutt how it wasn't meant to be this way.' 'What? And you think you're an exception?' 'No, Zaaro. I think that's when you get to see the real me.' She places the watch to her ear, shuts her eyes, and oh-so-softly taps at its shell in time with the faint second hand. 'Tick-tock, tick-tock, it's eight o'clock.'

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Have someone else handle the paperwork and filing. But if you need anyone dealt with, or protected, just give me the list of names. I'll take care of them.

These are clothes and snacks for Lisa, along with gifts for her friends. As for this box of old books her papa insisted I bring, I'm not sure what they're for. I'll just let Lisa decide what to do with them.

Uniform? No, thanks. I don't know why you people need so many pockets. Just as I can't grasp why the Higashinese stuff planks and pillows in their waistbands, making it so terribly hard to move around… Anyway, I'm fine with this outfit, and it has nothing to do with me being Siracusan.

Some of the operators here have unsteady breathing. Perhaps they could try reciting a tanka or two to adjust their breaths as they strike, like: 'Solitude seeps not from autumn shade, but from the mountain pines in red sun's fall.' Or 'I bear no off'ring branch unto the hills, for rich brocades of maple sate the gods.' You think these lines evoke a particular image? Hm. Probably.

No need to hide the Wolumonde story from me. Hm, you look nervous, but I'm not here to cast blame, my daughter knows the meaning of her work. Suzuran is no fragile flower, and I am no hidebound gardener.
My return trip to Siracusa? The perpetrator is dead, so there is little else to say. The man who, in his lust for power, deprived so many of a decent life, did not deserve a decent death.

Lost in thought? Is something wrong? Hm, some business less suited to a so-called pharmaceutical company, is it? If you need my help, do speak clearly now. You see, Doctor, I have only the patience to manage this single braid.

The wine tasting is already finished? I went to freshen up and hurried back as quickly as I could... Ah, sorry, but my work demands it. You see, precision is everything. I must be meticulous about which bastard die at which moment, not a second sooner. Hehe, but we don't need to pick a time for whiskey. Care to stay a while longer?

So much snow on the deck, and yet the corridors are not cold. I detest inconsistent weather, so the landship has been a blessing. I only just realized how long I've been here. You're right, an assassin's vacation is a good thing, for herself, and others.
I'll stay here, just call me if you need something. Hard to believe? Sometimes, I can be very patient, Doctor. Have you ever tried combing nineteen tails in one go?

Hello. You must be 'the incredible Doctor' Lisa always mentions in her letters. Hmm, I've been curious to know what you looked like, and here you are. Which reminds me, could you update me on Lisa's studies, if you have the time?
It's not often I see recordings of myself. I fought my battles in quiet alleyways, with no witnesses.
I appreciate the recognition. But this means those after the bounty on my head will come looking for Rhodes Island. You are not worried?
I accept your medal, Doctor. You needn't say more. I do know the difference between this medal, and the emblems of the Siracusan family.
Leave the toughest one for me.
Just keep yourselves safe, ladies and gentlemen.
My ears are sharp, so when I stop, you stop.
Need to parley with them? But I rarely do such things, whether I'm in Siracusa or Higashi.
I'm all ears.
So much negotiation and we end up talking with our blades.
Splendid day today.
Beautiful place.
Hate and resentment have no place, but in a burst of autumn red.
Flowers imbibed, the lady in suit and tie dance with her blade.
At least make me lose the coat.
Why the rush? The road to the afterlife is crowded enough.
Higashinese shoji screens often run a common theme. The kami created life and land to propagate themselves… A pity they didn't care for what came after. Sorting out this mess is hard work.
There's nothing to clean up. Let's go.
Crawling out of the swamp is hard enough, never mind doing it gracefully.
Leave the rest to me... it's clear why we failed, and I know how to make it even.
The soundproofing of this place is excellent. Was it done for professional reasons?
Hehe, even Lisa has grown out of this by now.
The scar on my face? I wasn't born with it... Let's just leave it at that.
Arknights.

Happy New Year. What a wonderful gathering. Dancing, chatting, making noise just for fun, instead of drowning out a struggle. Hmm… Lisa's making her way here, Doctor. That was sake in my cup and not a double whiskey shot, understand?
Hello, Doctor... Hehe, I can hear your footsteps even with my ears folded.
Happy Birthday, Doctor. Lisa's papa asked me to give you this omamori. He hopes to visit you in person, if given the chance. As for me, I offer a promise: my blade is yours whenever you need it.

I first contacted Rhodes Island because it was the best place to treat Lisa. But now, I would send her here to learn, even if she were perfectly healthy. Do not let this landship ever stop, Doctor, not after it has been sailing for so long.

handbook.profile: Ingrid, mother of Operator Suzuran, and former core member of Famiglia Venezia—one of the Dodici Famiglie of Siracusa. A veteran assassin who excels in elimination and raid missions, she has separated herself from her famiglia for various reasons. Now works on the Rhodes Island landship as an operator under the codename Vulpisfoglia.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Vulpisfoglia shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.13u/L
Operator Vulpisfoglia rarely comes into contact with Originium, but is quite familiar with Oripathy prevention and treatment methods, and has some experience with taking care of Oripathy patients.
handbook.promotionRecord:
'Orchid, was that Ingrid just now?'
'Yes. She wanted to borrow and needle and some thread to repair something on her own.'
'What was it?'
'The omamori hanging on her waist. She said it was accidentally punctured in Nuova Volsinii... I suppose it's important to her.'
'What's inside it? Hehe, I'm just curious...'
'It's empty.'
'Empty?'
'Maybe it had something inside before, and it got lost when it was struck open. Why so surprised? Someone like her surely knows what's important or not. Her hands were clumsy, but she mended it in one go, tied off the thread and got up to leave, stylish as ever.'
archives:
Over the last few years while Operator Suzuran has been receiving treatment on Rhodes Island, Ingrid and a Higashinese priest have visited the landship a few times to see her. The priest is always the one asking us how his daughter is doing, in terms of both health and studies, while Ingrid stands at the side, occasionally asking abrupt questions about the landship's defenses and how dangerous the field missions are. This has left HR with a profound, albeit limited, understanding of her, but also given them an easy job when deciding what to write on her record—'Siracusan, famiglia assassin, doesn't seem friendly.'
This time she has come to Rhodes Island on her own, and after she applied to stay on the landship, we began to supplement her files with more information. This went smoothly, and we discovered that 'Ingrid' is an infamous name in Siracusa: As a core member of Famiglia Venezia, she left no less than 27 separate homicide case files in the courts of every region she visited while the famiglia was expanding their territory. At least ten famiglie have offered a bounty for her head, and half of them have yet to expire even today. 'A Vulpo even more ruthless than a wolf', is how she's fearfully described among Siracusan famiglie.
Of course, considering Siracusa's political situation and the identities of those who have died at her hands, her past is not at all incomprehensible, and will not meaningfully affect Rhodes Island. After consulting Dr. Kal'tsit, we approved her application to stay aboard the landship. The final confirmation step also went smoothly, and the operators who went looking for her came back to HR shortly after. According to them, they had brought a large file of sorted information for her, but the other party just nodded to confirm her application, and only mentioned a small request: to erase the 'Venezia' surname from her file. She even gave each HR Operator an exquisite present before she left, and said with a smile: 'As thanks for taking care of Lisa, and also for your hard work collecting those documents.'

'Ingrid doesn't seem that unfriendly.'
'Hey now. Didn't you hear the implied threat underlining her second sentence?'
'Don't jump to conclusions. Don't you remember her smile?
'Exactly, remember that smile...'

As Ingrid spent more and more time on the landship, we got to know each other better. A few interest groups invited her to their gatherings, but were surprised when she gladly accepted, only to miss almost every single one—because she was always late. She missed a few consecutive wine tasting sessions, only languidly arriving at the venue when the event was almost over, and embarrassingly pleading the organizer to extend it by one more hour. We find it truly hard to imagine how she has no sense of time while also somewhat lacking in patience. She once again surpassed our understanding of her when she began participating in Rhodes Island's combat drills and field missions under the code name 'Vulpisfoglia'. Operators who were with her would nearly always mention feeling a great pressure, not because she was once a Siracusan famiglia assassin, has an unsociable personality, or uses cruel methods, but because her... impressive ability to execute every task with utmost precision left everyone somewhat dumbfounded. She always completes every objective in a mission exactly as stated, and even a placeholder objective accidentally left unrevised as 'I hope the target can be knocked over by an object thrown from up high, right as the new day comes in, for a most satisfactory result' was realized perfectly. Unlike how she acts on the landship, she seemed to have suddenly gained an almost obsessive-compulsive or perfectionist obsession with the finest of details. The sharp contrast stunned everyone, but someone finally plucked the courage to ask her about this gap in behavior. She simply frowned and said: 'Did you want me to slack off while working?' [Supplementary Note] I was sorting through the operator's files when I flipped to a Siracusan court case with records of what Ingrid said when she was answering the judge as a defendant. Perhaps it can explain her 'extreme separation of work and life' and her 'OCD' tendencies in battle: Some die as a warning to others, while some die in a way that cannot be remembered. How should someone undeserving of death die, or someone who should die, go? Your Honor, technical work must always be executed with utmost care.'

I imposed a strict ban on curious operators discussing Operator Suzuran's family composition, until I bumped into Suzuran and Ingrid myself, chatting on the landship bridge, and they stopped to greet me at the same time. They were just so alike in appearance and stature, as if they were carved from the same mold, but their temperaments were like night and day. I confess this was somewhat rude of me, but I honestly couldn't help wondering how a Siracusan assassin and a Higashinese kannushi met and formed ties.
Many stories quickly flashed through my mind, like a tale of a cold killer who, under orders to kill the shrine's master, traveled from Siracusa to Higashi, but her long blade shatters a bugaku mask to reveal the kannushi's clear eyes, stopping them both in their tracks as if entranced. Or another tale, of a gentle kannushi visiting the foot of a mountain for an event, but finding a Siracusan assassin leaning against a maple tree on a corner of his path, who—having fled a bloody battle and made it all the way to a foreign land—was now bleeding out, and the kannushi tenderly crouching down to check on her. By the time I came back to my senses, I realized I had already involuntarily opened my mouth to ask: 'Excuse me...'
Be it as a colleague or an HR operator, my actions were extremely inappropriate, but surprisingly they were not angry at me. On the contrary, Suzuran generously answered my question in a simple manner. She described her father meeting her mother as purely coincidence:
An armed force had infiltrated the area around the shrine where Suzuran's father works, and frequently caused trouble. Her father resolved to confront them alone at their stronghold to protect the innocent masses, and was on his way to the final negotiation. At the foot of the mountain, he passed by a foreign lady with a scar on her right cheek wearing a large coat. When he arrived at their stronghold, the boss was already dead in the snow, and everyone else left had already fled. A week later, the priest had gone into the city in civilian clothes to buy some chikuwa for a certain 'god' he serves, and went to the stall he usually frequented, only to see the same woman from before buying the last two sticks. He politely asked her to sell him one, and the cruel-seeming woman turned around, and gave him a stick with a smile. He bowed and thanked her for the chikuwa stick, as well as for their second meeting... and then everything else happened as it should.

Indeed, a truly normal tale. In fact, the meeting of two people from different countries, backgrounds, and personalities is precious in itself, but the choices and efforts they made afterwards—challenging the shrine taboos, ignoring the famiglia rules, and raising a child both parties have invested unfathomable emotions and expectations in—are far more worthy of respect, and have nothing to do with how strange their initial encounter may have been. I bid the two goodbye, and then Ingrid, who had been silent the whole conversation, smiled and stopped me in my tracks with this:
'As I recall, you'll be joining us in our special resistance training drill later this afternoon, yes?'

[Special Letter Correspondence 03]
Sender: Fabrizio Venezia (verified as the current don of Siracusa's Famiglia Venezia)
Recipient: Rhodes Island Procurement Department
Content: My granddaughter Lisa has always been undergoing Oripathy treatment with your company, and recently her mother Ingrid has also gone to your company as well, so I hope to sponsor your research on Oripathy diagnosis and treatment in the name of Venezia Trucking Co..
Response: We specifically asked Ingrid about this, and based on her attitude have made the following reply:
'Thank you for your interest in Rhodes Island, but we cannot consider your offer due to inaccurate information provided.'

[Special Letter Correspondence 07]
Sender: Nuova Volsinii branch office, Penance
Recipient: Rhodes Island Landship
Content: Operator Penance has routinely synchronized with us on mission reports and official correspondence, which included an arrest warrant issued by the Police Department of Nuova Volsnii for Ingrid on the grounds of committing premeditated injury.
Response: We informed Ingrid about this, and surprisingly, unlike the usual famiglia member attitude towards the law, she acknowledged the warrant was real.

[Classified Log]
I'm not running or looking for a sanctuary, Doctor. Of course, I'm not going back either. There are too many 'laws' on this land, so why care about them all?
...Yes, Siracusan famiglie do not need a valid reason to end someone's life. Or rather, the usual reasons not to, like 'decency' or 'hoping everyone gets a good ending'... often hold no water there, which is why I chose to leave. But I won't take off this suit, because it's comfortable to wear; I won't abandon this blade, because it's easy to wield. It's just that Lisa doesn't need me to worry over her anymore, and her papa can solve his own problems and won't need my help for the time being. So I can indeed afford a short vacation. You're right, an assassin taking a vacation isn't a bad thing. For her, or for everyone else.

modules.moduleDescription: Ingrid observes the young man's face, blood dripping through his hair and down the nape of his neck like some wretched tattoo. 'Help me,' he begs, as if he's forgotten that he tried to fling a dagger at this very lady just a day ago. Ingrid's gaze shifts past his shoulders, landing on the smoking vehicle in the distance. Oh, she thinks, so they caught up to him after all. His story was of failing to enact his vendetta against Ingrid, then running into his own foes on the way back for good measure. All too common a story. Revenge is a wolf snapping at its own tail. 'Help me.' He's still asking? Who would help an enemy? What, just because she pardoned him once before? But those thoughts don't bother Ingrid for too long, for then she answers. 'Sorry, I don't do this kind of thing anymore.' She tosses a dagger to the ground—the very same one her personal avenger left her yesterday. It's not her concern whether he still has the strength to pick it up, or whose heart he'll elect to aim it at. She turns, and steps into her Rhodes Island dorm room. The Logistics op outside reminds her that the physio appointment she booked starts in fifteen minutes. Through the porthole, she peers out into the barrens, the dagger she tossed down now six hours in the past. Who knows if that young man ever escaped the wheels of hostility after him. There's an unfinished jigsaw puzzle on her dorm table. A present. Now and then, Lisa comes by to chat while casually putting a couple of pieces in place. She carefully examines the part of the image that's already formed. An everyday landscape, an undulating horizon; one could imagine the outline of buildings, mountains, forests. Despite not having pieced a single row together herself, it's already complete—at least in her mind. It's not for lack of patience; it's just never much excited her when the start of something can give away the full picture. As if examining herself, she picks up a jigsaw piece, and places it right in the heart of a vast swathe of blank. 'That's where it belongs,' she says to herself. She doesn't even need to look for the pieces around it; she's more than sure, as if she's secretly completed this puzzle countless times before. Placing that lone little piece at the center, she can almost picture a wolf circling it chasing its own tail, round and round and round, in endless joy. With a shake of her head and a flick of her finger, she sends the piece flying off the table. 'I shouldn't be having thoughts like these on vacation.' She heads out of her dorm. Is it time for her physio appointment yet? Whatever the case, a killer on holiday can make as luxurious use of her time as she wants.

modules.moduleDescription:
一方洁白的手绢擦去剑身上尚温热的血珠，随后便被毫不怜惜地扔在桌角。
英格丽为自己包扎好伤口，将门口堆积的信件摊在桌上，逐一撕开检阅。
几封受潮的信盖着隐秘的钢印，那些是来自家族的指示。她知道里面仍旧会是一些催促她返回叙拉古的话，所以连读都懒得读。
几份账单，租金、水费、取暖费。英格丽皱起眉头，她以为在自己出远门刺杀目标的两个月里，家族的势力会替自己料理好这一切。
哦，她想，原来这是一个警告——如此幼稚而低级的警告。她不打算回复那些催促她回去的信件，她打算继续在东国待上一段日子。
来自家族的声音从来不止一种，有人盼着她回去，有人则源源不断地往她的待刺杀名单上添加新的名字。
无论怎样，她不在乎。有任务她就会去做，不过是杀人而已。
她拿起下一封信，正准备从中间撕开时，她的指尖认出了那种质感独特的纸张，以及上面花与藤的细密暗纹。
于是她在卧室里翻箱倒柜，找出一把拆信刀。
“山巅的雪开始融化了。雪水煮茶，对坐欣赏，风景很好。”
她放下信，又拿起来，分别用东国语和叙拉古语读了一遍，再从信封上找到寄出的日期——她猛然走到窗前，试图看清远处的山巅。
远峰绿意盎然，郁郁葱葱。
“请止步！”山脚下，神社的看守拦住了英格丽。
她并没有止步，只是挥出一剑。
一剑，又一剑。
敢上前拦她的人越来越少，她在这座山上爬得越来越高。
刚包扎好的伤口再度崩裂，血沁透白纱，又在外套上晕染出赤色，如同艳丽的山茶花。
终于，她抵达了山巅。
雪早已化完，但那人仍煮着一壶茶。年轻的宫司请她坐下，她却摇摇头。
她的意思是，自己身上沾满了血，血腥气味会毁掉那一壶茶。
宫司也摇摇头，他的意思是，那壶茶并不重要。英格丽看懂了，于是坐在了庭院中的一方茶桌前。
他们沉默着，目光掠过积雪早已融化的山峰，掠过庭中飘落的花瓣和山道上滴落的血迹——
那几乎全是她的血，来自于她曾经为家族杀人而留下的伤口，这些伤口迟迟没有愈合。
最后，她说：“我看腻血了，我想看看你信里的雪。”
年轻的宫司点点头，用指尖沾了些茶水，似乎想在桌上写下点什么，却又收回了手。
几日后，英格丽又收到了一封信。她用拆信刀拆开，里面同样只有一句话。
“洋服剑舞，所谓伊人醉山花。”
她折起信，盖在了那柄剑上。

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: You want me at your side to see if Rhodes Island can live up to the talk. Hmm... Alright then, so long as your security doesn't give me too much trouble.

Life in the Truckers Mutual Aid Association? We drive, we deliver, we drink, we mess around and have a good time. Nobody bares their fangs in Nuova Volsinii... But as my mentor once said, the Fangs will never truly disappear.

At first, I couldn't get used to pizza and spaghetti. My mentor was the one who taught me to mix finsauce into spaghetti, and replace the salsiccia on pizza with bacon. Had to find a way to fit in with the wolfpack, she said. So, I've eaten like this through all my years in Siracusa. Why? Because it tastes alright.

Truth and Justice... That's the book my father used to read to me when I was little. He even took me to meet the author, who was later imprisoned by some duke, died in jail, and was buried in a mine. Pretty awful, no? But that's how things were, at the time.

My father said that Sergei would become the greatest of all scientists, even if he was born in Ursus. I thought they were friends, partners, and kindred spirits... Yet Sergei stabbed them all in the back. He deserved to die, but I also doubt whether the blame was his alone.

Where did I learn to fight? From my mentor. She taught me to turn hatred into power, but not to hate. She taught me to fight, but not to step onto the battlefield... What a strange 'wolf' she was. Too bad I didn't figure out her final lesson sooner.

Director Kal'tsit, Dr. Kal'tsit. No matter what hat she wears, she's still her same, cold-blooded self. Yet, I do find it believable that she didn't betray my father. Maybe she's not as ruthless as she looks, after all. Hmm, what do you think, Doctor?

In all the time I stood behind Talulah, I watched her crush dream after dream, morphing into our very own tyrant... That was my mistake, and one I will not make again... Kill her? No. What I want is to tear off the tyrant's crown.

You've united many under your banner. This is familiar to me. I've stood with such people, and also against them... But do beware, leaders like you are known to make grave errors. When you do, I'll look you dead in the eyes, and I won't hesitate—Doctor.

She learned her song by snow, she learned her blade by rain… She learned to show her courage, by fire that swept the plain… She learned to topple crowns, by all the silent pain... Oh, you're awake. No, it's nothing. Just a Siracusan nursery rhyme.
Crownslayer. It's a name we both know well, so let's keep it. Maybe one day you'll come to understand its true meaning.
Old combat records? Got anything with me in it? Come on, let's give it a try. I won't lose this time.

Alright, alright. Enough with the formalities already. I couldn't care less about your little medals and ribbons. Do you take me for some general or noble? Or, would you prefer I test my blade on them?
