handbook.profile: Lyudmila Ilyinichna, a former Reunion squad leader who dealt in covert operations and assassinations, specializing in melee combat and breaking through defensive lines. She parted with Reunion in the wake of the Chernobog-Lungmen Incident, and approached Rhodes Island at the end of 1100. She is currently receiving Oripathy treatment while under supervision.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Originium crystals distributed across surface of body, confirmed Infected by medical examination.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 18%
Crownslayer has suffered from Oripathy for a very long time, with distinct crystallization in her upper respiratory tract. Many of her organs are heavily infected, and the organs between her oral cavity and throat also display hyperplasia. She reports no foreign body sensation, and staunchly refuses our suggestion of surgery.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.45u/L
Crownslayer has not received any systematic Oripathy treatment. Her BOCD is rather high, and seems to be trending upwards. Her organ crystallization accelerates rapidly whenever she uses her Arts, worsening her condition. Medical has already given her a proposal on how we can keep her condition under control.
handbook.promotionRecord:
A Sargonian dancer whirls lithely, her white skirts brushing past the padishah's face, a deadly tail spike following soon after.
Bolívar's Viceroy drinks a toast from a glass handed to him by a Perro waiter and soon dies amidst a lavish feast.
Victoria's tyrant closes his eyes as his servant girl strangles him in his bed.
Gaul's soldiers turn their artillery on the emperor's carriage and blast it to pieces.
...
In the story she just finished reading, a Yanese chef grabs a fintail fresh off the stove, and thrusts the dagger hidden within into some prince's throat, fin flesh and bone included. Lyudmila closes the book, and places it back on the shelf in the reading room.
Lyudmila learned to read at a very young age, but aside from 'Truth and Justice', she hasn't actually finished many books. She couldn't really explain why she was randomly flipping through a book on Sargonian history in Rhodes Island's reading room, or why she was drawn to a record detailing how a dancer assassinated a padishah. Soon after, she looked for more material, finding similar tales in the histories of every nation.
A dancer, a waiter, a servant, a soldier... Most of them left behind no name, and even less of them met a happy end. But their very existence is enough to remind kings and sovereigns about one simple fact: They can play with politics, with the people, even the order of the entire nation, but even an insignificant grain of sand can become a blade hanging above their heads—a 'Crownslayer'.
Crownslayer likes these stories.
archives:
Crownslayer's arrival at Rhodes Island left a deep impression on us. She suddenly appeared in front of the landship on its course, with Operator Projekt Red held hostage by her side. Before the ship's defensive alarms even sounded, S.W.E.E.P. had already secured Red and subdued Crownslayer.
We were quick to notice the changes in Projekt Red. She was unharmed, but had a blank look on her face, as though she had sunk into some sort of delirium. Our medical operators hurried to give her a comprehensive examination, and confirmed that this was the result of drastic emotional fluctuation. From her fragmented replies, we pieced together that something happened during a personal visit to Siracusa, and we determined that her odd behavior had nothing to do with Crownslayer, who had even helped her during a suicide attempt. During the course of our examination, the subdued Crownslayer was shouting Dr. Kal'tsit's name and things such as 'Come and take care of your wolf cub already,' along with an unending tirade in both Ursine and Siracusan. As Dr. Kal'tsit was not on the ship at the time, we temporarily locked her in a cell under strict supervision while we sent an urgent communique to Dr. Kal'tsit asking how to handle her.
A few months later, we received her reply. Surprisingly, she suggested we lift Crownslayer's confinement and allow her some measure of monitored freedom, including but not limited to access to the low security areas of the ship and the right to participate in Rhodes Island missions.
This was how a former Reunion member came aboard Rhodes Island using undisclosed means and became, in a sense, one of our members.

The following is only for staff with high clearance:
In light of Crownslayer's identity as a former member of Reunion, she is to be placed under observation by both S.W.E.E.P. and the HR department. This is to prevent her doing anything unnecessary, but also to ensure her personal safety. Though the conflict between Rhodes Island and Reunion is long over, many of our people still feel the pain of losing our comrades. Even if she does not have their blood on her hands, anger cannot be controlled once it boils over. We will keep her under surveillance until she truly becomes one of us.
We have entrusted Operator Mudrock with this task. Considering their shared backgrounds as former Reunion members, this will hopefully help us better evaluate how Crownslayer is doing aboard Rhodes Island.

'I just spotted Mudrock with Crownslayer—yes, I know she's our informant, let me finish—and she was standing right next to Crownslayer, nodding along to everything she said! I bet she was bought off! Man, this is becoming a headache—Dammit, they ran into the kitchen! I'll follow them, you go get some backup!'
'Knives? White masks? Didn't those thugs use those in Chernobog and Lungmen? Do they have an inside man in Logistics? That's real sly of them, hiding weapons in the cafeteria! Are they about to raise Reunion's flag again aboard Rhodes—N-No way!'
'They closed the kitchen doors and pulled down the curtains, I can't get a read on the inside. This is an emergency, no time to report to the higher-ups, and no time to look for a floor plan. Gonna head in first to keep things under control!'
'Those thugs are... having a culinary club meeting around the table? Some are busy by the stoves and ovens. There's a redhead kneading some dough who noticed me real quick. She stopped her kneading and cut me a slice of pizza, fresh out the oven, even though I'm holding a weapon. I think she knows me, but I'm pretty sure I've never seen her before.'
'The operators behind me stowed their weapons, and they all got a slice too. It was good pizza. Instead of the usual sausage, it's got Ursus-style salted meat. Since it's right out the oven, the heat's just right, and the bread's got just the right amount of chew. I gobbled up my slice real quick. The red-headed lady has been all over the kitchen: kneading, chopping the meat, pouring the sauce, keeping an eye on the pizzas in the oven and occasionally dealing with people trying to rush her. She seems really into it. People are calling her Lyudmila. Kind of a pretty name, Lyudmila... Wait, Lyudmila?!'
—Excerpts from a monitor's real-time voice logs

'I asked Lyudmila why she was staying aboard Rhodes Island, and she told me she was waiting for that hag Dr. Kal'tsit to come back. Her words, not mine. She wanted to ask her if she knew about her master when she was sent to live with her uncle. If she knew about the wolf pack's game. If she did, why didn't she do anything about it? If she didn't, and things were always out of her control, then why did she always act so sure of herself? In short, she is ready to give Dr. Kal'tsit a verbal beatdown in front of everyone.
'Look past her sharp tongue for a moment. Lyudmila wants answers out of Dr. Kal'tsit, but... she's gotten used to waiting here. I've seen her buying magazines from the store, killing time in the Convalescent Garden... doodling on the bridge with charcoal. Maybe life here is a rare chance for her to relax. It's not hard to understand. When I first got here, people were saying a Reunion hammer-wielder had infiltrated the landship... but all I was thinking about was that I finally had a place I could, err, go for a light stroll.'
—Excerpt from a recorded conversation between HR and Mudrock

[Field Mission Voice Log 03]
'In a few hours, I'll be meeting with the operators from the Trieste branch to help them complete negotiations with the local famiglie.'
The nomadic city out at the edge of the barrens could be faintly seen in the distance. This was the third time Lyudmila was going to Siracusa.
The first was when she was still seven. Kal'tsit had entrusted someone to take her there, to her uncle. It seems even the all-knowing Kal'tsit can still be blindsided by unexpected factors, no matter how well-thought-out her choices are.
The second was when she split from Reunion, leading a band of brothers and sisters who didn't want to follow Nine to Victoria. Over the course of two years, Lyudmila saw them back to their hometowns, one by one. For those with no home to go back to, she found them work. Finally, she walked back to her master's house in Siracusa, as though it were all one big farewell ceremony. But what came after was hardly an ending deserving of such ceremony.
Reunion, the Truckers' Union, Ursus, Siracusa... None of them were places associated with pleasant memories to her, but when the Field Operators Department was discussing who to entrust this mission to, there were eyes that fell on her. She doesn't know why she didn't refuse.

[Field Mission Voice Log 05]
'This would be easy to settle if you just took out a few famiglia dons—problem solved. Fine, fine, I know that's not how you do things.'
The negotiating operator was murdered in broad daylight, and so the cooperation between Rhodes Island and one of the local famiglie was all for naught. The other famiglie were very satisfied with this state of affairs, and their alliance of convenience broke down back into their usual territorial selves. About a week later, the canceled press conference went ahead as scheduled, to the surprise of many. That dead negotiating operator was on TV, declaring that Rhodes Island had managed to reach an agreement with their partner famiglia, and that the supplies included in the deal had already been transferred. Only now did the other famiglie realize that it was all a trick, and that they had been scammed.
'—If they're out for blood, then we'll just have to do it ourselves before they get a chance. A killer without a target's not going to swing their knives around for no reason. Here, I'll show you. See? If I stab you with this collapsible knife, then the fake blood will—Ow, some got in my eye... Give me a sec. The bathroom's that way, yeah...?'

[Field Mission Voice Log 09]
'...I've run into a personal matter I gotta deal with.'
A truck driver on the streets of Trieste had noticed Lyudmila and called out her, trying to drag her back to Nuova Volsinii with him. He yammered on in excitement about how the drivers didn't want to move camp, and how City Hall was preparing to build the resettlement area in their camp. Eirene had brought Sommer's daughter to the new city too. Her condition is stable, and she's about to go to school... The chance reunion only ended after he forced Lyudmila into drinking three cans of salt soda.
She couldn't deny her own happiness right then. There's no doubt that Eirene, as head of the union, was able to grasp something during Carnevale that could change her fate. Change countless people's fates. The changes in her were clear, but the Truckers' Union never deviated from its original goal: to give the drivers better lives. She had a sudden recollection of the day she joined Reunion. The Infected were kicking about some nobles in the snow, gathering around the bonfires while eating meat and potato stew, even dreaming about how one day, they would demand an explanation from the Emperor himself, and let everyone on this great land breath freely for once. The Truckers' Union couldn't hold a candle to Reunion, but to her, they really were more alike than not: they both appeared along her path to vengeance, and thanks to some bitter experiences and some rather absurd changes, she chose to leave them both. It seems she has managed to make one big loop in life before learning something about herself: she is someone easily waylaid by hate. She should keep an eye on the one in the lead, while not completely denying the fact that her past comrades had, for a time, given her a reason to live, given her faith and flame.

[Field Mission Voice Log 11]
'Mission complete, heading back to the landship soon.'

To the most esteemed Director Kal'tsit:
Sergei hasn't shown up for several days now, and I cannot confirm if he has been arrested or not. For the sake of the institute's safety, we must be prepared. Our government contacts have begun their work, and I pray they will have good news for us. At the same time, we must send away our families, seal off the sarcophagus, copy or destroy our data... There's simply too much to do, and I may not have time to see Lyuda. If you do see her, please give her a kiss on the cheek for me.
Ever since Sophina passed away, Lyuda's hate for Chernobog has grown by the day. Staying here will only cause her to suffer more. As her closest family, I should be with her right now. But I am a selfish man. Our progress at the institute has reached a rate where I do not wish to take even a single day off to go home, slice some bread, and make breakfast for her. I truly wish I was the type of person who could give up everything in the name of science, but I love my little Lyuda so. It torments me, and makes me tarry when I should be sending her off somewhere more suited for her.
But now, Ursus has made my decision for me.
No matter if we survive this oncoming calamity or not, Director Kal'tsit, I ask you send Lyuda to Siracusa. Sophina's elder brother has an estate in a small town there, and when she was still alive, he once offered us shelter. I believe having Lyuda live there for a while is the most suitable choice. She can complete her studies in a foreign land, open herself up to the arts and sciences, become the sort of person she wants to be—a navigator who charts the course of scientific research, or a politician striving for the well-being of all.
...
I hope you can leave the city without any trouble, and that our research will see fruition soon, realizing both our plans and yours.
Yours, Ilia.

As the surveillance team rushed over to the landship's middle layer to turn off the alarm, Crownslayer slipped out of Dr. Kal'tsit's office. She held in her hand a letter as she waited for the team to come and subdue her. It was just like the first time she stepped aboard Rhodes Island, except she was calmer this time around.
'It's obvious that I'm not going to be a navigator or politician anymore, Papa.
'Tell Kal'tsit that when she gets back to the landship, I need to be the first to see her. She needs to tell me all the reasons why that research institute was set up, about the research itself, everything about her own history... All of Ursus's secrets. All of them.'

modules.moduleDescription:
'This painting is the most famed of Valentin's works, purchased on recommendation some years ago. Parted with about a million chervontsy for it,' Duke Propp effusively tells the Government Inspector as he introduces his collection.
'And here we have a precious night pearl recovered from the east mountains. Only two in the entire empire, one of them here with me, the other in the hands of Duke Beria...'
'You mean this one?' The Inspector pulls a gemstone out of her pocket the size of a burdenbeast's eyeball, glowing in faint green.
'Well, good Inspector, you certainly know your treasuries!', lauds the Duke, loath as he is to. His territory is tenth on the Inspector's rounds, and the first nine are all extravagant when it comes time for bribes. Not one Inspector hasn't been thoroughly spoiled by the time they make it here.
The Inspector strolls up to a corner of the collection, and picks up an altogether unremarkable and antiquated military saber, toying with it amusedly in her hands. Its edge is polished to a shine, reflecting her carmine eyes.
'What fine taste you have!' As if he's caught sight of prey in his trap, the Duke bustles over to ingratiate himself. 'This precious sword here was one bestowed by the previous Tsar. A perfect spoil for you to take back to Deity Grypherburg, I might think.'
'How could I repay your generosity for such a precious article, Duke?', the Inspector makes her second question.
'I simply ask that on your return to Grypherburg, you might recount my service to His Majesty, so I could take part at the capital when he grants his subjects...'
'So you're telling me, you want the Empire to know of your mines' service, ten years accident-free, accomplished by having everyone who knew of the disaster there buried in a collapsed shaft?'
The Inspector's words completely blindside the Duke, and the sycophantic smile freezes on his face.
'You want the Empire to know of the 'ten thousand bandits' you killed, when half of them were refugees starving to death in your territory?'
The color in the Duke's face goes from pale to ghastly. He has never met an Inspector like this before.
'Or maybe, you want the Empire to know that you, and the past nine Dukes, were all such devout and loyal executioners?' The Government Inspector, with the ceremonial saber at hand, has cast the night pearl worth a king's ransom straight aside. She pulls off her hood, revealing her fiery red hair. The Duke meets her eyes, and they call to mind the recent rumor—only a few years ago, the Crownslayer, whoever she was, had returned to Ursus.
'It couldn't be. Are they all...' The Duke tries to ask, but can only swallow the rest of his sentence, along with his fear.
'If there was an Inspector visiting, and if the Empire did know of all your deeds, maybe they would've given you shiny new prizes for it.'
Duke Propp is dying to run, to scream for help, but before he knows it, thick and choking smoke coiling about him has stolen his voice.
'It's a real shame the Empire can't hear your cries.' The 'Inspector' raises the saber.
'But don't worry. The Crownslayer will grant you your reward.'

modules.moduleDescription: A noisy afternoon. She buries her face in her father's arms to hide from the scorching sun. Her father makes her greet the people standing behind the glass. She cannot make out who they are from their blurry visages. 'Lyudmila.' Someone calls her. She recognizes that warm voice. Her father often quotes that person, and likes to leave a lot of comments beside their work. Watching Lyudmila doodle all over the floor with charcoal, the voice sighs, and hands the girl some paper and a wet towel to wipe her hands with. Lyudmila does not mind it, for it doesn't matter where she doodles. 'Lyudmila Ilyinichna.' Someone else calls her name, his body emanating the stench of tobacco she hates. 'What are you drawing?' 'Who let you draw these? Everything in this research institute has to remain confidential. Do you know what that word means?' 'Enough, Sergei. It's a child engaging in pure creativity.' So says the voice that handed her the paper. 'You ought to take a break, you're too tense.' 'I have a daughter too, but I prefer not to bring her here. Also, you'd best get rid of these drawings, for your teacher's sake. You know how it is out there. It'll be best for everyone.' The hateful man leaves. She raises her head, and compares her work with the structure in front of her. The warm voice approaches. 'I believe it's still possible to record your feelings about something you have no understanding of. So can you show me your drawings?' She nods. 'You have a good eye for lines and shadows. Just look at these scary shadows—you drew them like huge dark clouds, weighing down on everyone's heads. But that thing is harder, and much heavier. I can tell—this institute is oppressing you, making you afraid. The voice sighs again. 'We call it the Sarcophagus. We all feel the same way you do, but we're hoping that what we do here can change our feelings towards it.' 'You might even clear the dark clouds above with your own hands, Lyudmila.' The voice becomes a little nervous: 'Will you trust me? Give me those drawings, like you're passing on your fear to me. I'll return them to you when we're done with our work here. I believe that by the time that day comes, you'll no longer be afraid of it.' She hands over the drawings almost instantly, as if agreeing with the voice. 'Lyudmila, as long as I'm alive, I will find a way to return these to you. And if something happens to me and I'm unable to keep them safe, I'll help you destroy them. Now, your father's coming over. Don't tell him about this—there's no need to distract him from his work.' Her father comes over, and wipes the charcoal off her hands with a handkerchief. He looks into her eyes and says: 'Lyuda—' A shrill alarm sounds. Crownslayer's eyes flick open. The charcoal stick in her hand has already broken into three pieces. Papers covered in old drawings are spread out all over, with huge shadows and clear silhouettes. She briefly stays in a trance before realizing she is standing in Kal'tsit's office with no one else inside. The drawings before her are from twenty years ago, and not her fresh work of art. Tossed to one side, an envelope bears Kal'tsit's signature agreeing to seal them. The prior promise has been fulfilled, a secret promise not even Kal'tsit' knew about. Does this mean that person managed to walk out of the institute alive? 'You and the Doctor are organizing a group of Rhodes Islanders to go to Ursus, right?! I remembered something—No, Amiya, I'm not telling you for free, I want to negotiate a proper deal!'

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: A Dublinn spy, one of Caster's lackeys, the leader of the workers, plus Wiš'adel... Fancy that, a full house? In any case, I take it I can rest while you handle my business? Since you did let me tuck myself back onto the ship.

What's this? It's one of those healthy meals they hand out outside the training grounds. 'Help yourselves', they say. What's that look for? It tastes good enough, better than the emergency ration handouts in Londinium by a country mile... Tell you something I know better now, Doctor. It's bloody hard, as it were, to keep a city's worth of bellies full.

My sword here has enough legends to fill a storybook. Even my teacher had his version to tell, flourishes and all. Yet, people only seem to remember those who wielded the sword, not the ones who forged it first... I won't stand for that, Doctor. I'll be there to tell the stories of the unsung heroes.

Sometimes, after a night of dotting Is and crossing Ts, I'll climb up onto the roof of Westhaleg and watch the sun come up. Down in the street, there'll be costermongers hollering, workers delivering goods. On occasion, you'll spot my boxing gym mates, all hungover. A few of them'll look up and see me, and we'll wave at each other. I love this city a lot, Doctor.

All this regalia's from an old friend. It's not the lightest thing ever... I'll tell you what she taught me: If you've got a noble 'calling' that pisses you off, then go on and get loud about it. Give it hell, and hold nothing back. I can't argue being Speaker now weighs on my shoulders, but my spirit will stand tall, and I'll have her as my witness.

'Victoria'... I know to a lot of people, it's not me that sticks out, it's my name. But so what? The things they're so desperate to scrounge from me are the things I'm off to smash to bits. It's in my power to force that through their heads, sooner or later. The fight's only just started.

Alright, I've been coming back aboard a bit much recently, I admit. Mm-mm-mm, I'm not skiving. It's just hard to meet some of the people here otherwise. Delphine's dead set on calling it 'diplomacy'... And I don't just drag you along as a safeguard, Doctor. I have to be honest, I do want to learn a little more from you.

My face? Just a blister, nothing big, helped Indra and the lot in a fight as I was passing through Norport. Heh, even the ones challenging our turf don't come half as strong as they used to. I've seen babies punch harder than... My clothes? Oh, flip, I forgot to change into my casuals!

Can you believe it? A simple trick like that and Dr. Kal'tsit's got the whole Glasgow Gangers on Rhodes Island. Wait, you knew all along? Haha! Come on, no need to dodge. There! A playful rap on the head, that's how we boxers respect our opponents after a match is done.
Wake up, Doctor, you've got tons of business to sort out still— hah, finally I get to tell someone else that.

Doctor, to be clear, this is not official business. What it is is two old friends, reuniting now the war's over. And about my old files... I think I'll finally fill in my name. Vina Victoria. No more hiding from it.
Can't help feeling the itch... I might go and file for time off with Parliament.

I lost a lot of mine, on the way back home. Parliament awarded them all these posthumous medals, and I still don't know who to even give them to... We weren't told how heavy glory weighs. I came out knowing.

I know clear as day what's up ahead. If I'm the only one left at the end of this all, so be it, I won't hesitate. But in my heart, drinking with her best mates until we drop in the sunset, that's the happy end to the story of Vina, the story of the Siege.
I fight alongside you once again, Doctor, with a sword that's not just for show.
I'll adjust my combat style to fit you all.
Recon, strategize, deploy… then, the siege.
I've been through crueler fights.
Finally I can limber up.
It's the frontline for me after all.
Wish I didn't scare you.
Get up! There'll be no bending of the knee!
I forbid your retreat.
Who says you can't hammer with a sword?
Negotiations are useless here.
Violence too, is an effective means.
My teacher was right. With each step forward, I still learn something new from you.
Getting to lump you with the thinking work feels bloody refreshing. It's been forever since I had a stress-free scrap!
The most precious lesson war taught me was this—there's never an absolute best-case. Regret is its own kind of mercy, and that goes for us and them both.
Not time to give up yet. Follow me, I'll bring you all home.
...Really calms you down here. Think I'll get my forty winks.
Um. My cape... you're stepping on it.
Eh? Did you say something, Gawain?
Arknights.

It's the frontline for me after all.

Who says you can't hammer with a sword?

Violence too, is an effective means.

handbook.profile: Originally registered at Rhodes Island as the leader of the Glasgow Gang, she later worked alongside us as the leader of the Exemplars during the Londinium War. Now, as the Speaker of Parliament, she maintains our cooperative relationship. Rhodes Island has been supporting Londinium's healthcare system, and Vina Victoria has pledged to broaden our partnership in other areas.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis: Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected. [Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0% Vina Victoria shows no signs of Originium infection. [Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.16u/L After the war, Vina Victoria completed another physical examination. The medical report was submitted by a local operator from the Londinium branch, and contains subjective assessments (see below) which I recommend removing from the file. 'I personally saw her battle at Silverrock Bluffs, a literal mountain of Originium. She charged to the frontlines with no protective gear, but somehow avoided infection. It's been days since then, and I can't help but wonder if that was a sign that Victoria can lead us through tough times.' What, should we check if she gets food stuck in her teeth during meals too? If not, maybe that means Victoria will sweep away the old refuse and lead us into a glorious future? Maybe we're placing way too many expectations on a single person. ——Morgan
handbook.promotionRecord:
[Voice Log]
Thank you for your skepticism, Feist.
...No, of course I don't want the military-industrial complex to dominate Victoria's future—that would only turn Victoria's future into Ursus's past.
My hope is only that any new technology retains the potential for military application.
My teacher told me that Rhodes Island will guide us down a path that confronts the destiny of the land. He wasn't speaking metaphorically. It was never Rhodes Island that pulled Victoria into the Core countries' political struggles: Victoria was inevitably being drawn into a much larger vortex.
When Rhodes Island reaches the end of its mission, I hope that we, and Victoria, will stand in the right position. By that time, I don't want her to be held back by an unwieldy industrial system or outdated military technology.
And until then... I assure you, nothing born from your hands will become an extension of anyone's ambitions.
archives:
Initially, most of our operators had a limited understanding of Vina Victoria due to significant gaps in her records, which were based entirely on scant personal details leaked by the Glasgow Gang to HR.
However, when she returned to Rhodes Island as the Speaker of Londinium's Parliament, she quickly changed those perceptions.
Many noticed that, as Speaker, Vina acted with more caution, likely due to her new status.
According to the Glasgow Gang, Vina 'has a particular fondness for strange-flavored candies', but when the 'Odd-Food Enthusiasts' of Rhodes Island offered her a super-spicy star-anise-and-angelica root lollipop, Vina politely but firmly declined. There was also a rumor that she 'likes to doodle on her clothes'. However, the operators know that the intricate embroidery and patterns on her royal garments are definitely not doodles.
Many have remarked that Vina has become more laid-back and carefree after coming to Rhodes Island.
How about the claim that she is 'a picky eater who hates potatoes'? This was disproven after she was seen, on several occasions, chowing down on the nutritious meals provided by Hibiscus. The assertion that she is 'low energy and sluggish' was also quickly debunked. According to our operators, Vina actively takes part in many activities at Rhodes Island, including postpartum care for burdenbeasts and test-driving Engineering's new tractor.
What should we make of the changes in Vina Victoria's lifestyle? That's still being looked into. However, it is clear that many of the personal details leaked by the Glasgow Gang and recorded in Vina's file were simply pranks and should be removed.

Pranks?! If you remove anything, you're boneheads! You hear me, HR, official boneheads! I'll fight every single one of you!—Indra
Vina once said she liked sour lollipops because the intense sourness made her feel more alive. It's probably the same reason I enjoy the awful, nearly expired sauce from Old Hank's shop.
As for the claw marks she draws on her clothes, she said it's to let the ingrates see at a glance what kind of marks she can leave on them.
As for her hating potatoes, that part's true, but it also shows her determination and resolve. She even dragged Hannah into the boxing ring once, to get her to eat all her potatoes for her.
And the reason she can fall asleep anywhere is because she's always exhausted. I get that—if I had to be two people at once, I'd be tired too.
That's the Vina I know, and no one can tell me otherwise! These new 'records' you're adding are nothing but lies.

—Morgan
But whenever we see her, she's the same old Vina. She still shoves her potatoes onto Hannah's plate like always.
—Dagda

Hold on, Dagda, that isn't contradictory. While I no longer dislike potatoes, it's still funny to put them on Hannah's plate... But Mr. Recordkeeper sir, everything Morgan said is completely true as well! I've even fallen off the tram while dozing off...
Tch, never mind, why am I bothering to explain this? Anyway, those are all things I've done, so just leave them in my file!
—When the Glasgow Gang caused a ruckus at HR, Vina attempted to mediate.

[Classified Log]
I don't know precisely what trick Kal'tsit used, but she did manage to get Siege, who was living in fear in a foreign land, to let down her guard and treat Rhodes Island as a second home. During that time, she would even drag Kal'tsit to their Glasgow Gang dormitory to watch movies.
So, when Kal'tsit finally called her by her full name, 'Alexandrina Vina Victoria,' all her hair stood up. I remember it clearly: she smacked Mon3tr with a hammer so hard it started buzzing; you could hear it from the hallway.
But she only hit it once. This time, she didn't run away.
—■■■

[Voice Log]
Doctor, I've actually never been sure whether the path I'm on is one I've chosen for myself. From my biological father, to the dukes who sent him to the gallows, to the 'Unicorn' pulling strings behind the scenes... they've all tried to control my life, pushing me into different roles for all sorts of purposes. But I can't see what lies ahead. I really don't know what path they've put me on. To be honest, I hate it.
When I first came back to Londinium, I thought I was heading home to deal with some minor family issues. I never imagined I would end up where I am now, doing what I'm doing. But Dr. Kal'tsit did, didn't she? Right from the beginning. Even when she first brought me to Rhodes Island, she was already looking toward Londinium, wasn't she?
Ha, you won't deny it. I only just realized that Dr. Kal'tsit—and even you, Doctor—have already thought more about my life's trajectory than I had. All while leaving me completely in the dark.
What, you think I'm angry? Not at all. I think of it as you competing against those who've tried to manipulate me, and helping me defeat them. I don't regret my choices in the slightest, and neither should you.

The Holy Orb of Order, a symbol of the Victorian parliamentary system, is usually held by the Speaker (the King themself). It is made of a special alloy crafted by royal alchemists; its deep blue hue emits a mysterious, shifting glow when placed in the light. It is adorned with a golden band in the center, set with various dark gemstones. There are two different Holy Orbs of Order: one engraved with a red dragon, and the other with a lion. The former belongs to the Draco royal family, and the latter belongs to the Aslan royal family. Eventually, the orb with the red dragon disappeared along with the Draco royal bloodline, while the orb with the lion has been passed down through the Aslan royal family for generations.

Professor Briggs, 65 years old, and a faculty member at Victorian National University, tearfully recounted his experience. According to him, the current Speaker of Parliament, Vina Victoria, unexpectedly approached him one sunny afternoon, seeking information on the Holy Orb of Order. After Professor Briggs carefully explained the orb's history and political significance, as well as the process used to make it, the Speaker revealed her true purpose: she wanted to repurpose it into a voting bell to remind members to attend votes punctually! She even planned to make replicas and distribute them to every MP!
Professor Briggs deeply regretted not asking for clarification in the beginning. He tried to 'hypnotize' the Speaker with his words, hoping she would forget this absurd idea as well as what he had told her, but unsurprisingly, he failed. In his despair, he cried that a royal heirloom, the sacred symbol of Parliament, should never be desecrated like this—and if it were, it certainly would not be in relation to him.
The Speaker, however, had a different perspective. She boldly asserted that since both the Holy Orb and the voting bell are used to maintain parliamentary order, they are clearly the same thing.
—'Londinium Bi-Monthly,' Headline News, 'Parliamentary Relic or Gold-Plated Alarm Clock?'

Your Grace, we are losing Victoria.
The Duke of Wellington's stance is clear, and his will is firm. We have no way to respond by force, lest we provoke another war. While Tara's economy is imbalanced, its foundation remains strong. You would need to collaborate even more closely than you currently do with the other dukes if you want to put economic pressure on the Duke of Wellington.
On the other side, only Alexandrina and Parliament remain. As you said, there is no need to rush in and get involved; rather than seizing authority, Alexandrina seems to be building her own power base in a land where previous sources of authority have already been shattered. The power she is accumulating... we could have harvested it.
However, as I've mentioned several times in my reports, her methods are unconventional. She appears adept at dismantling established symbols of power. Though she is currently powerless against the crown, the Holy Orb of Order has already been reduced to what common folk jokingly call a 'gold-plated alarm clock.'
I don't know how she plans to establish her authority after so eagerly dismantling the existing symbols of power. I believe her approach will lead to one of two outcomes: either she will quickly be hanged by her own people, or she will create a kind of power we've never seen before and can't ever hope to harness.
—Report submitted to the Duke of Caster, intercepted by Operator Harmonie and secretly forwarded to Rhodes Island

Ha, it's happening all over again. I pass some bills in Parliament, and they remain indifferent... but when that little orb is placed on the lathe, everyone gets so worked up.
When all else fails, shake things up! That still works in politics, from time to time.
—After reading the above report, Vina laughed.

This one? This is a photo that the Count of Schutzbury gave me. Don't worry about who he is for now... Can you guess what it's of?
Right, it's just a blurry mess, I can't make it out either. The day he gave it to me, he didn't prattle on about his usual theories of justice. Instead, he looked at this blurry photo and went on and on about what he saw in it: a bakery with a red sign, selling the worst bread on the block. Yet, homeless people would gather in front of it every night, eating the leftover bread the owner had left out. There was a sunken area on the road in front of the shop, where water would collect every time it rained. The neighborhood children would pick up the bread wrappers thrown away by the adults and fold them into paper boats to float in the water, etc...
I later found out that his unusual behavior was something Vina had orchestrated.
Strange, isn't it? Morgan and the others told me that Vina used to be like all the other street thugs—she despised nobles to her core. Two months ago, I would have had a hard time imagining her speaking with any noble for ten minutes without throwing a punch. In the past two months, she's made more new noble friends than I've made new intelligence contacts. Of course, she still hates salons, fancy dinners, and balls, but at least she's willing to let a viscount talk about his family's ancestral beliefs before raising her fist, or let a scholar explain some new, emerging political theories, or let an army officer recount the social ills he's witnessed firsthand. Just like how she used to listen to me talk all night about Lynncardine. It seems like she is trying to understand the Victoria she's determined to shatter.
Victoria is dirty, but it's also proud. Over a thousand years ago, when the Draco people were still nomadic tribal leaders, they pieced together the earliest form of Victoria using a framework borrowed from Sargon. But the fundamental source of their power was still their ability to protect their people—something they took pride in. That pride has been passed down, stumbling along the way, to the present day. Every noble child still blindly recites 'Honor her glory, shield and protector,' just as their ancestors did, though they no longer can see the people they need to protect.
I think Vina must have seen that pride, which is why she's holding back her fist for now. She wants these people to open their eyes and see Victoria the way she does. So, while riding in Count Schutzbury's hot air balloon, Vina pressed his head down, making him look at the streets below, showing him that the people he treated like trash also had lives of their own. What he couldn't see, Vina described to him, street by street, until the sky began to lighten again, until the hot air balloon was frosted over.
After they came down, Count Schutzbury immediately called back those poor souls he had thrown into the boiler room without any protective gear. He started telling everyone about the sights he saw, the things he had learned for the very first time. Of course... we all know this was probably just momentary self-reflection. Vina opened his eyes, but in the end, he will most likely close them again.
But even so, for Victoria, this is a big deal.
—A conversation between Delphine and the Doctor

modules.moduleDescription:
Vina never expected her meeting with the Doctor after reboarding to take so long.
When she strolled through the Command Center doors on a whim, she never would have guessed the intense discussions the Doctor and Closure were having was about a board game of all things. Londinium's newest fad—The Adventure of the Lioness. There were only so many ways to kill time in the pubs right now, and this game for kids quickly found a home among pubgoers who loved picking at politics.
To all that, the Doctor replied: 'Closure and I see plenty of unpatched holes in the game design.'
She prepared to deploy her standard suite of excuse-mes and beat a hasty retreat, but Closure had already sealed off her escape route, and was urging her to join in. 'I can vouch. This game really takes me back to those days, you know? Underground in Londinium, fighting with the Self-Salvation Corps.'
And how was she to predict that a fun little idea from a couple of kids playing house would get snapped up, commercialized, shipped, and become all the rage in Londinium? And then the greatest surprise was Morgan gleefully bringing the game back to the landship and recommending it to everyone she possibly could.
'I'll play as you.' Taking on the 'Vina' role, the Doctor readied for the other two players' assault. Dice rolled again and again, and each time City Keeper 'Vina' came out on top, even twice succeeding in a complete counteroffensive and taking the 'Caster' territory for 'herself'.
Defeated time and time again by 'herself', Vina was somewhat exasperated. 'Doctor, this is cheating. Hardly anything you're doing is in the rulebook.'
'We never agreed to play by anyone else's rules, Vina.
'Londinium's an enormous city. There are plenty to draw on that the designers didn't know or care about. That's what I meant by holes.'
For a moment, Vina thought to herself, then threw herself decisively into the next round. The aftermath of an independent Tara, the strategic give-and-take of Caster, the Infected vanguard bearing news of Gododdin... Vina played character after character, trying with all her might to wrest the Doctor's advantage away, but always to minimal effect.
Before her eyes was a city that far surpassed her expectations. With a peculiar and twisted ambition, she sought to beat 'herself'.
But it was beyond her to read any of the strange and crafty angles by which the Doctor defused her offensives. Their tiny little board couldn't support the three's game anymore. With a flash of inspiration, Closure called directly on PRTS to simulate one that was even larger and more complex.
'Uh. Closure, are you allowed to use PRTS like that? What if Dr. Kal'tsit—'
Closure waved it off. 'She's got urgent business, she's not on the ship. Besides, I have the permissions to guarantee she'll never find out what we did.'
An absurdly protracted ten hours later, Vina finally had to excuse herself from the game thanks to an anonymous express delivery to her dormitory.
What had arrived was the yet-to-be-published first expansion for the game, including a series of all-new powers with all-new game plays. There was Normandy, Ashworth, and the Unicorn. Printed on the box was a roadmap for future expansions and updates, too.
'The Adeptus Chamber Knights, the Empire's Blades, the Agents of Operation Boulder, the Twins' Voices, and the Angels of Judgement...'
And finally, a message that left Vina silent.
'I hope you like it! Looking forward to your feedback. —Eleanor'

modules.moduleDescription:
'Madam Speaker, please accept this... humble gift of mine.'
Inside the Slobberknocker boxing gym, a paunchy nobleman stands in front of Vina. Morgan turns her head away, looking rather annoyed.
'I've been telling this guy to get lost God-knows how many times already, Vina, but this visit really takes the cake.'
'I thank you for entrusting the rebuilding of Auchterigg to me.' The noble forces out a slavish smile as he avoids Morgan. 'I had previously called upon your manor several times, but your friend here didn't even allow me past the doorway. I simply had to give this to you in person, or I wouldn't be able to sleep at night!'
Before Vina can even reply, he slowly opens up the extravagant case he is carrying, revealing its contents.
'A... speed bag?'
Though it is just about recognizable by its shape, this 'speed bag' almost makes Vina break out in confused laughter. What should be a simple punching bag made of coarse fabric attached to a rebound platform had been covered in dark blue velvet and embroidered in gold with Victoria's coat of arms. Even more ridiculous was the complex ornamentation at its attachment point.
'I'd heard you appreciated a good round of fisticuffs in your youth, so I asked the most skilled craftsmen of Londinium to make you this speed bag. It's even got a few humble ideas of my own, like how the colors of the bag match with your esteemed Holy Orb of Order. Does it not signify the eternal union of your will and the heading of our fair nation?'
The nobleman finds himself panting for breath after his lengthy bout of flattery, tugging at his necktie to give his pudgy neck some air.
'Have you been studying pugilism as well, Earl Caspar?'
'Why yes, of course!' The earl's eyes begin to shine.
Vina walks over to an empty platform, hanging up the earl's gift.
'If it pleases you, my lord. As this is your gift to me, it is only right that you have the first strike.'
The earl's face pales, but it would not do to refuse such kindness. He can but roll up his sleeves and softly throw a punch at the bag. It sways only slightly.
'Put a little more force into it, my lord.'
'But I can't, Madam Speaker! If the decorations get scratched—'
Vina does not wait for him to finish speaking before driving a fist straight into the bag. It bumps up against the platform, the golden lions adorning its peak snapping in twain. Upon seeing such destruction, the earl stamps his feet in panic.
One punch, then another. With each strike, the ornamentation shatters, sending countless fragments falling to the ground, so fast the earl cannot pick them all up.
'I... I spent a lot of good money on that!' The earl's face is a bright ruddy red. 'If you didn't like my gift, Madam Speaker, you didn't have to shame me like this!'
'Hardly, Earl Caspar. I actually rather like it. It's probably the finest speed bag I've ever used, once you strip it of the impractical parts. Much like you, my lord. When I look past your frippery and finery, I am reminded of your many contributions to the city's planning in your younger days. If you wish to find me, I will most often be in my office. On that note, don't forget to bring your project plans.'
Vina halts her onslaught, looking at the bag. It continues swaying out of inertia, the golden coat of arms sewn onto it a blur.
'The Holy Orb of Order is esteemed by the people not because of its extravagance, but rather, because of the miracle of civilization our ancestors wrought.
'But it is clear that this current age of ours can hardly be called a miracle.
'Which is why, my lord, I shall hang this here, and allow all passers-by to give it a good drubbing.
'If there comes a day when it no longer sways, I hope it is not because people hold it in esteem...
'But because of their heartfelt approval of this coat of arms, made up of all Victorians.'

LINKAGE.voiceText: I did this all the time back in magic school, and I've mastered how to use all your magical tools, so you can leave everything to me! ...Someone blew up that Originium flashlight? *ahem* Well, it wasn't me!
Canned sandworm? Lemon fin-mint noon tea? Sea Terror jerky?... NOOO! NO, NO, ABSOLUTELY NOT! ABSOLUTELY NOT!

Here, your summary on healing magic compared to restorative Arts. What? You thought I'd take longer to finish? Heh-heh! Back in school, when I was developing a new healing magic, I'd read through tons of papers like that every day. So the next time you have any work like this, just let me handle it!

Seventh Night's Awakened'? 'Fiend of the Night'? Do you really have members with such titles? Sounds like they walked straight out of some ancient legend. Awakened in a banquet of blood and darkness, a lonely moon glimmering in his blood-red pupils, surrounded by countless... Huh? Who was that man being dragged away by the ear?

My gosh, these vegetables are so fresh! No soil at all, just water? I never knew you could garden with such devices! Having one of these in the dungeon would solve everything! ...You need electricity to run it...? Well, I'll pedal a whole generator if that's what it takes!

It's true Familiar Creation is a dangerous magic, but I saw those children in the Medical Department and... They saw me as a mighty sorceress from the dungeon! And the one who can summon these little things to play with them! Aww, look how much they love it.

Just a moment ago, I saw Laios eating yet another monster I've never seen. It was tall as a half-foot, covered in thorns, and it squirted poison. Doctor, how long until food poisoning symptoms show? Never mind, I'll just pay a visit to the Medical Department and get prepared beforehand...

I learned how to make this straw grasshopper in a handicraft class. When we go back, I'll give it to Falin. The first time we hanged out together, she caught a grasshopper live, and she took me to see a real dungeon, and we ate raspberries... That was the day we became friends. I'll always remember it.

Doctor, can you show me how you use that thing you call a camera? I want to take a photograph of us—you, Laios and everyone. When we go back, I'll show it to Falin and tell her about each one of you. Am—am I doing it right? Laios, huddle up a little more. Three, two, one,  cheese—
...I wonder if my sleeping bag's still on the fifth floor... and the really valuable soap... *snzzz*... *snzzz*...
Thank you for helping us in finding a way back! Oh, yes, and my party may not look it but they're all wonderful people, and if they do anything strange, er, please try and forgive them...
Is this really the time rewind magic which allows you to relive the past? On a scale this big? How is it done? Can you teach me?
So in other words, I have the permissions now to borrow all the books on advanced Originium Arts theory? Wow! Thank you!
When I tell Falin about everything that's happened to us, she's sure to be excited... And that's just one more reason we have to make it back, and save her!
Magic tome, staff, repair tools... Done. Everything's packed and I'm ready to go.
Huh? Wait a moment, our leader's always been Laios.
Let's go. As long we have a battle plan, I can make it work.
Don't worry, I just ate my fill. My mana is in tip-top shape.
Take it easy. Just leave it to me.
Do you want me to ready a magic circle?
I've never seen all these monsters before...
Over there, right?
Ever since my last familiar channeling, my arm's been sore...
Fall back, let me handle this! I'll wipe them all out!
Exhausting your mana is dangerous. Be careful how you plan your tactics, you know.
I can see the monsters! Just give me a moment to aim...!
Heh-heh! And THAT'S why I was top of my class.
I know for a fact Rhodes Island has regular cuisine! Why are Laios and Senshi still rushing to cook up the monsters we defeat?!
Phew, still alive. I almost ended up a full-course meal for the monsters...
AHHHHHH! RUN FOR IT!!
I have to say, it's just like a dungeon in here...
EYAARGH! ...Oh, thank heavens, I thought you were a man-eating plant!
Are you heading to the Library too? Excellent, let's go together!
Arknights.

It feels like it was just yesterday that we got here. I've already gotten the hang of that camera you showed me how to use! Right, we should take another photo today, with all my new friends—a big group photo altogether. Falin will love hearing all our stories!
Doctor, how did you sleep last night? If you've been having bad dreams, then you want to check for Nightmares in your pillow—that's what we do before sleeping in the dungeon!

It took me forever to pick out your gift. As a huge, huge fan of The Daltian Clan, this one hits all the same notes, and the narrative and writing style are superb. Promise me this, Doctor, you WILL read it! Very well, it's yours—the classic romance tale, Love on Terra!

I studied the theory of maladies and injuries in magic school, and took up developing healing magic as well. I know just how excruciating it is to battle with a seemingly incurable disease. Doctor, if you're ever in need, I'll be there to give all the help I can.

handbook.profile:
Marcille, the mage of Laios's party.
She claims to have unexpectedly arrived on Terra while trying to rescue her friend Falin in a dungeon. Now on Rhodes Island seeking a way home while providing medical and magic assistance.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Marcille shows no sign of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] Undisclosed
The Medical Department has agreed not to disclose the relevant data.
handbook.promotionRecord:
The fortune teller at the Sami market took Marcille's hand and said a lot of baffling things, before discovering she had no money on her and turning to the next tourist. Chilchuck scoffed at this and mocked her for being an easy mark.
Later that night, Laios's party decides to huddle up for the warmth to sleep through the freezing cold. Half-awake, Marcille seems to see a figure under the moonlight, appearing to be foolishly digging up the soil, with a filthy face, leaves stuck in their hair, and a small pile of berries picked from the Myrkwood on hand, as if right about to taste them.
Marcille was about to quickly shout a reminder not to eat unknown fruits found in the forest, only to realize that there is nothing there but her companions fast asleep, the figure from before nowhere to be found.
A gust of cold wind blows into the tree hollow and Marcille wraps her blanket tightly around her as she prepares to return to sleep. A small snowflake appears before her, carried by the wind, and it stays for a long time before melting.
She suddenly recalls something the fortune teller said, in-between their wild ramblings: if you see a snowflake in Sami that does not melt, it is the person you wanted to see the most, talking to you.
archives:
Marcille is a mage from Laios's party. Terra is home to many adventurers, but we are curious about these few calling themselves 'dungeon adventurers'. She herself makes it clear that a strong physique is not a requirement: Marcille often tires herself out before the others when on long field missions, and has barely passed most of our physical exams. By contrast, the 'magic' she uses (which could be understood as a form of Originium Arts) is quite powerful, and during missions, no matter what the task requires, she will often raise her hand, saying 'I can do this! Let me do it!' before beautifully casting a suitable magic spell.
Compared to most operators who specialize only in one type of Arts, Marcille's repertoire of magic is quite diverse. Explosions or blinding light spells for offense, healing or barriers for support, summoning 'familiars', the ability to walk on water, and so on. In comparison, her lack of physical strength seems trivial.
However, we must add a strange asterisk to this: while she is well known for her poor physical fitness, operators fond of hanging out or exercising on the streets have recently reported sightings of Marcille executing difficult-to-perform maneuvers while shouting things like 'Not eating that! No way!' Aciddrop has evaluated her to 'possibly have a talent for street dancing' and has invited her to join in street events, so perhaps we will see a new side of Marcille in the near future.

The Rhodes Island library boasts a huge range of books, and operators who enjoy reading spend lots of time there, Marcille included. In just a few weeks, she seems to have already finished every theoretical work on Originium Arts, compiling a thick collection of personal notes. Operator Skyfire, who was substitute teaching a class for reserve operators, was shown her notes and commented that 'they're so easy to understand that everyone in class ought to read them too.'
Marcille only smiled at this evaluation and said: 'I did pretty good back in my magic school after all.' She also mentioned that she strove not only to advance healing magic, but has also studied the creation of harmless dungeons. Every spell she uses in the dungeon was something she studied, and it is a pity that no one in her party understands the vast knowledge required for such a feat, or realizes how powerful she actually is. Regardless, she is currently very excited at the prospect of studying a new system of magic, and is happy to share her notes on dungeon magic with our operators, hoping that everyone can learn from each other and find their own breakthroughs. Naturally, her notes were also recommended to the reserve operators as reference materials.
Soon after, the 'Marcille's drafts incident' was all everyone talked about.
A reserve operator reportedly found a page crammed with dense writing among Marcille's notes, and thought it could help her understand Arts, but after scrutinizing it she handed it to her teacher Skyfire, red-faced. Skyfire read it, then brought it to Orchid, who called over Midnight and the rest of Team A6 to discuss it until the sun rose. What exactly did Midnight do that could have informed Marcille of his past identity as the 'Devil of the Eastern Night' in Higashi, and also caused her to weave him and more than a dozen operators, including the Doctor, into a complex web of relationships, full of jealousy, hope, respect, control, exploitation, as well as love and hate?
Regardless, Marcille's desire for knowledge and her skills at both theory and practice make her a role model for all operators.

For some reason, Marcille has recently immersed herself in hobbies one could say are completely unrelated to returning to the dungeon.
For example, she has joined the handicraft club and learned to weave grasshoppers from straw, followed veteran operators into the wilderness to identify various fruits on Terra while gathering all kinds of berries for everyone, and learned to use a camera as she spent a whole day sitting beside Scene and capturing the sights while out on field missions, ultimately taking group shots of Laios's party along with other operators.
When an operator from HR brought her recommendation letters from Leithanian universities and Columbian research institutes, they found her on the deck carefully weaving a grasshopper from straw, next to a small plate of raspberries and a bunch of previous grasshoppers that weren't quite as good as the one in her hands. She gladly accepted HR's suggestion to rely on her 'mage' identity and her outstanding abilities to enter those institutes and receive more help on their quest to return home, and explained to the somewhat puzzled operator that her recent obsession with these unrelated hobbies was because she wanted to share what she encountered on Terra with Falin. When they finally rescue her, she intends to present them all one by one and talk about what they experienced here.
'Laios is actually more anxious than he looks. And Chilchuck won't say it, but he's already planned and optimized all our routes for the dungeon... So instead of being depressed and worried, I'm hoping to make some beautiful plans for our future too.'
Marcille checks her freshly weaved grasshopper as she speaks, and then shows the HR operator her progress. 'The first attempt was totally unrecognizable, but now it really looks like a grasshopper. I can teach Falin how to make one too, when the day comes... I can't wait to see her again!'

Joining the Rhodes Island Medical Department requires not only ample physiological know-how, but more importantly, a kind heart. Marcille passed this strict test and became one of the department's cooperating operators. She's also conducted comparative studies on her own healing magic and Terra's restorative Arts, to both enrich her knowledge of medical theory and help our Medic operators reach breakthroughs in curing various ailments.
This has taken quite a lot of her time.
We are extremely grateful to her for proactively participating in our tests and using the time she could have spent finding a way home instead assisting us in our research of various diseases. We are grateful to her for creating all kinds of adorable familiars to cheer up the children's ward, while paying special attention to Ceobe's condition.
We once asked her why she does all this, and she replied simply that she had already been studying diseases and trauma in her magic school and was used to developing new healing techniques. As Rhodes Island is helping them find a way home, she wants to return the favor by helping our patients.
That said, what she does for us goes far beyond 'returning the favor'.
Our guess is that, when Laios's party first met Ceobe in the wastes, perhaps Marcille was not yet aware of Oripathy and its consequences. And once she was, she chose to help us as much as she could, even making us a promise: If we could find a way for them to travel to and from Terra, she would definitely return to continue helping us study Oripathy. She wishes to see Ceobe and the other patients on Rhodes Island for as long as she can.

modules.moduleName: Book Collection of the Best Magician
modules.moduleDescription:
From Marcille's reading notes...
I sat in on some 'Originium Arts' lectures. It's what they call magic here, and there are several different schools of it—my explosion magic falls under the School of Evocation. When it was Skyfire's turn to demonstrate, the class suggested we compare the differences between our magic. Afterwards, I caught the whiff of barbecue—they shared a skewer with me and made me swear not to tell Skyfire. I think she knew anyway, because the temperature around her shot up noticeably. Not to mention, it was cold that day, to the point Mint invited me to tag-team hug Skyfire. She was wonderfully warm at first, but quickly got a little too toasty!
Familiar summoning falls under the School of Transmutation, which is where Originium energy is used to alter something's physical composition. The class was dying to see my familiars against Mudrock's Colossi in a tug-of-war, which we refused. However, someone mentioned a game called 'beast arenas', which aren't contests of brute strength, but a magician's wisdom and skill—now this we couldn't refuse. After eventually bringing a box into the room, we made our miniature familiar and 'rockbeast' respectively. Still, Mudrock didn't even need to lift a finger to control hers! I worked my butt off trying to win!
......
While listening to them chat after class, I discovered that Yan's Chief of Lungmen is reputedly extremely handsome, and his wife is the princess of a neighboring country. Not only does she ride motorbikes, but she also has a personal ninja maid! With love blossoming amidst the intricacies of politics, they must have faced countless challenges to be together. The family head even dispatched a ninja to capture the princess. The sight of the chief and the princess together in love moved the stoic and loyal ninja, prompting her to aid them, even if it meant sacrificing herself. On a dark and stormy night, the chief carved a bloody path with his sword to reach the captive princess's chambers. They dashed to her motorbike and screeched away from their pursuers into the night. The ninja, gravely injured while covering for them, faintly smiled as she watched them ride away and then closed her eyes... There's no doubt about it—that's exactly how it happened! And obviously, the chief and the princess went back later to save the ninja!
I know the bookstall here has a tale of their love in stock. I'm going to get my hands on it!
......
I was only expecting a casual read. I had no idea of the truth... I'm noting down their profiles while I can!
Wei Yenwu: The elder brother of Yan's Lung. Carries a red longsword on him. No one expected he'd fall in love at first sight with a foreign lady.
Fumizuki: The Princess of Higashi. A free soul determined to rule her own life.
Shirayuki: Loyal ninja. Would do anything for her princess.
I'm bringing Falin this novel along with all the books on Arts theory! I just know she'll love it!

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Your desk needs tidying up? It doesn't look messy at all. Much better than my study, hehe. Don't worry, no mess is too much for me. Truth is, I can't think straight in a tidy room.

Come on! It's just midnight, too early for bedtime. In Sargon, the days are super hot, so our 'day' only really starts when the sun goes down. Staying up messes with your circadian rhythm? Pfft, big deal. It's worth it when you see the lotuses blooming at sunrise.

My younger brother and I were born into a family of court historians, the Guardian of the King’s Secret. We grew up surrounded by stacks of scrolls handed down from our ancestors. As kids, we didn't get how valuable they were and just fought over the ones with more pictures. Thinking back, the pictures weren't half as fun as our fights.

That's a figurine of the Shah on my desk. He's basically treated like a god in Sargon. I remember trawling across the entire desert just to dig up the relics he left behind... I came back empty-handed though... But, it's okay. I still felt good about getting to bring his figurine to visit the places he'd been.

The pattern on my hood? It's my family's emblem. As the Shahanshah's personally appointed historians, our duty is to see and faithfully record everything that happens. Although... there are times when they prefer us to be silent witnesses.

Doctor, there's a Juncus pen that has been passed down for generations in my family. It has documented many extraordinary lives and left its mark on treasured scrolls and manuscripts. I'm thinking, Doctor, if I were to be handed down that pen... How about I start with the stories of all its previous owners?

Hey, Doctor! I brought back a whole bunch of souvenirs for you. A few amulets, several volumes of supernatural tales, and a golden— Hey, don't swat it! The locals consider this bug a divine emissary that keeps travelers safe on their journeys, so promise you'll take good care of it!

Doctor, excavation work isn't as exciting as everyone thinks it is. It's mostly tedious and repetitive labor. If you really want to build a career on it, the best way is to either have a kindred spirit by your side, or a good rival to push you. That’s how you achieve more, and go further.

Hey, Doctor. Wanna look around the bottom of this pit? Give me your hand. Careful! Now, this dirt might seem unimpressive, only going up to your knees, but buried under it are traces of the people who lived here centuries ago. It's difficult to explain, but the land remembers all that humanity does, and all the choices we make.

Too relaxed to say anything? Hehe, of course you are! This is the soothing incense I brought from home. One whiff is enough to… Asleep already? Did I use too much? Oops... I did... now the Doctor's gonna be out for a whole day.

Greetings, Doctor. On behalf of my exalted Padishah, I am here to negotiate with you on a collaboration project within his dominion. My name is Djerwnapekhaper Saciut Hatshepsut, but... my friends all call me Pepe.
Um, could we just hire the warrior in the recording to teach me in person? I'm not used to learning like this…
Now this is new, I was always the one giving out rewards.
A promotion? Alright, then I'll bestow an honorary title in return. Don't underestimate its power! From now on, no one will be able to hinder you in my father's domain.
With lightning and habūb, my hammer will rebuke the intruders and their greed.
Are you ready to join me on this journey to uncover history long-buried?
I have prayed to the gods, and They have revealed to me an auspicious omen! We'll find something good this time.
Whoa, you robbers actually dare show yourselves before me?!
Take note: you can never be too gentle when cleaning relics!
If we run into tomb robbers, hehe... Hammer time!
Woah, woah! Let me down more slowly. There are fragile artifacts down there!
Don't rush me! Lemme get a nice, big stretch before I squeeze down this hole.
Too late to run now, nasty little thief!
Put that down. Your filthy hands desecrate it.
You've got guts, trying to steal this!
Rawr! I'm gonna stamp a lotus on your head!
Doctor, once these results are published, your name will sit alongside mine for all eternity.
Now this is a shocking discovery! Any ideas how we might celebrate this, Doctor?
It's not much, but at least those thieves won't profane this sacred site so easily again.
How should we piece together these fragments…? Ow, my head hurts...
You better not leave me here on my own. I might get curious and go tapping around with my hammer, which could lead to me seeing stuff I shouldn't, you know.
Hey! Do NOT undo the bow on my back!
I smell nice? But I don't usually wear perfume… Oh, it's probably just this lotus.
Arknights.

Ssh, no talking. Let the new year's first ray of sunlight bathe your face and body, feel its cozy warmth and gentle touch… Hmm... Doctor, the previous year is now history, all that suffering and joy—The sun just carried it away.
Greetings, Doctor.

Happy birthday, Doctor! Careful what you wish for, though, Sargonian legends tell of crafty gods who will grant any wish, but at an unreasonable price! Better yet, just tell me your wish and I'll try to grant it!

Doctor, if the conditions are right, some traces of us will survive long into the future. When those who come after us find the vestiges we left behind, it'll be like we're smiling at them across time! So, Doctor, let's put on our best smiles! For now, and for our friends waiting in the eons to come.
