modules.moduleDescription: A book lies open on the table. Logos adjusts his magnifying glass, trying to use his bone pen to write witchcraft onto the characters on the page. Every incantation he marks down will be magnified and projected onto a curtain by machines, then deciphered by Pith, who writes down its meaning and implications. These then pass on to a group of casters in the hall, who will try them out and discuss their effects. This started off as a hobbyist class for Rhodes Island's casters, but at some point, it changed into a research group supporting Logos with his experiments. He was currently performing a pointless task: designing incantations for a book currently only available on Rhodes Island—the Semantics Paradigm Encyclopedia, incantations that will ensure the correct meanings of the book's contents will appear directly in the minds of a reader. As languages are in a state of constant flux, he must pay close attention to how people from across as many different nations, races, and classes as possible comprehend the same words, constantly noting the differences between the original meanings of the incantations and how others interpret them. After an unending series of adjustments and revisions, the incantation is finally put to paper. Thus this collection of casters in the hobbyist class, be they Ursus, Victorian, Sarkaz, Feline, hide-bound academic or free-flowing liberal, must first take a photocopy of the encyclopedia, read the enchanted contents, then cast the Arts according to their understanding of the text. Through this process, Logos can capture the most minute differences between the understandings, and perfect the incantations even further. Thanks to Pith's ability to unerringly duplicate and understand Originium Arts, Logos can rest assured that all transcription, correction, and instruction work can be left to his esteemed comrade-in-arms, allowing him to focus on the effects of the incantations within the tome. Based on the most recent test results, nearly all experiment participants who read the Encyclopedia passage on applied incantations were able to accurately repeat that passage's contents and cast the Arts described. The participating casters were over the moons with joy, but Logos did not share in their happiness. There was still doubt in his mind about whether he had managed to truly achieve his goal: lossless transmission of meaning to everyone. The potential held by this little side project of his far exceeded his original intent of modernizing Sarkaz witchcraft. It has instead become some sort of attempt at creating an entirely new language. By writing with this infused script, the meaning you wish to pass on will not be easily misinterpreted. If everyone were to write like this, why, information transmission could ideally be near lossless. Anyone reading a text a thousand years in the future would derive the exact same meaning from it as a reader today. But when this project is complete, will it be able to destroy all barriers to using Arts, or will it serve as the catalyst of total annihilation? Or perhaps, even after all this effort, will he be forced to close the book and let it become some forgotten tome in the library? ...... The operators who took part in the experiment came and went, and now, he is the only one left in the room. As he lifts his pen to write more, he notices cracks in the bone from long hours of scribing. As a King of the Royal Court and a Sarkaz, he compiles Kazdel's very first 'great work', patiently awaiting the day there will be great need of it. But as a member of Rhodes Island and a child of Terra, he imagines a time when the barriers between all living things are broken, a time when they grasp fate in their own hands. It is for this reason he researches and experiments, even if such a dream cannot be realized in the present. Aefanyl takes a new pen, and begins to study once more. The dream yet lives in his heart, and in the slender shaft of his pen.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: I still remember this conference room. This seat… was it reserved for Theresa? No... I have no need for it.

Theresa is no more. This body, this vestige before you, is but a program that exists within the 'King of Sarkaz.' My form and my presence are the result of Amiya's emotions. As much as I may remember everything from the past, please do not mistake me for Theresa herself.

I will stay by Amiya's side, accompanying everyone here at Rhodes Island. Though, this hardly makes up for all the lost time... Doctor, I'm not a program in the same sense as PRTS. See? You might not be able to feel my body temperature, but I can at least smile.

Rhodes Island has strode beyond war, and should now re-embark on her intended route. For starters, how about optimizing our logistics? There are several conference rooms that can be freed up and converted into sickbays... You'd like my personal opinion? Doctor, allow me to remind you again, I am not Theresa.

'Rhodes Island Pharmaceuticals Inc.'... registered to Amiya's hometown... And these medicines... They were all developed by Kal'tsit... No, I have no regrets. Babel has fulfilled its duty. Rhodes Island will continue to sail, and continue to alleviate sickness and pain. If Theresa was here, I'm sure she would have been pleased.

Never have I regretted any of my decisions. We did everything we could have done, and bequeathed hope unto the future. Time will close wounds, love will mend scars. When the long night ends, Rhodes Island will usher in the light of dawn. Though many have left us along the way, I will remain here and bear witness to the ending.

Amiya still looks so thin and frail. For a girl at this age, maybe she should be a bit taller? All these days, has she been eating well…? How she so wished to see Amiya as she is now, to watch her grow for just a bit longer. Her wish should have been granted...

Kal'tsit still refuses to speak to me. When she poses questions to this crown, she avoids looking me in the eye. 'The King of Sarkaz' remembers her past. While I can sympathize with her loneliness, I cannot free her from her shackles. Perhaps one day, Doctor, you can help her find meaning in her existence, as her companion.

Doctor, you carry such guilt within your eyes. But you ask, is one's memory sufficient to define who they are? You have lost your memories. I merely inherited all of hers. How are we to settle what happened so long ago? Doctor, go and spend some more time with Amiya and Kal'tsit. None shall linger in the past, except her.
Are you weary, Doctor? Then, go ahead and rest. Everyone has the right to fall into peaceful slumber, and you are no exception.
...I'm here.
…Did I just see Amiya fighting?

I still remember every medal I distributed with these very hands. These ceremonies are also commitments. Rhodes Island will never give up on her ideals, let sacrifices be in vain, or forget about those who've traveled with her. Even now, we remain on the same course we originally charted.
I know, there are still many people who need me. Don't worry. This time, I'm not going anywhere.
Will you lead us to victory once more, Doctor?
I will stand alongside the warriors of Rhodes Island.
Warriors of Rhodes Island, may you all return victorious.
I can hear the sorrow within you all.
Doctor, I have faith in your command.
It's okay. I am with you.
Amiya, get behind me.
I am right here. I will always remain with you.
I will remember each and every one of you.
Your ideals... are equally worthy of respect.
Keep striding forward. I shall be at your side.
Don't cry. It will all be over soon.
There shall come a day... when we can strike alight the flames that burn away all decay.
You always make the perfect calculations so that everything falls into place just as you planned, don't you?
Without you, our casualties would have been far worse... Thank you, Doctor.
We will be able to move beyond this pain and suffering. Rhodes Island will not stop here.
A new security system? Will it still recognize me?
Boo! Did I scare you?
I'm watching you, Doctor.
Arknights.

Happy New Year, Doctor. Rhodes Island is a lot livelier than it used to be. Though there's still so much unfinished business, this moment of peace is precious nevertheless. Doctor, can you give these storybooks and toys to the children for me? It's something Theresa always used to do.
Program initializing. Accessor: Dr.{@nickname}.

Happy birthday, Doctor. How did you used to celebrate this day in the previous world? It must've been a scene full of warmth and happiness. I found one such song in 'Civilight Eterna.' Would you like to listen to it? Before that, Doctor, may you never be alone again in the journey ahead.

'Rhodes Island.' This very name fills one with warmth and comfort. Surely, tender memories will rush forth as soon as you speak these words. I hope that Rhodes Island can continue to carry forth the hopes and expectations of countless people, and in the future, become home for many, many more.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: A palace of memory, its structure more elaborate than a Leithanian instrument, its contents more incoherent than revenant rambling. Supporting this palace is perhaps as simple as enjoying a spoonful of soup—well, I'd say it is woven of thread rather than built of brick…

It's strange to perform a Deep Dive into Theresa's memory. It has lived within me since my beginning, but when I search these memories… I feel like a mere reader. It's very strange… I won't show you these Deep Dive records, Doctor.

Defending one's land turns a clothesmaker into a hero, and a hero into a King of Sarkaz... yes, this is where it all began: Theresis thumped on the door, and Theresa set down her scissors. Only when the door opened that evening, did she realize the heavy rain outside.

Only when the Goliath rushed out of the city gates that day and beheaded a Gaulish officer did we finally breathe easy. He brought back a Gaulish coat, but only handed me a piece of candy from its pocket, asking that I give it to a wounded soldier… But I couldn't do it, and I couldn't bring myself to tell him why.

We took the only opportunity we had. Kal'tsit did not originally plan to kill Yliš, she merely wanted to strip the black crown from the Sarkaz, but the 'Feeble King' still had a plan to thwart hers, and thus the war dragged on… until Theresis brandished his blade.

When Kal'tsit was born anew from the 'cocoon', I hesitated for a moment. But the look in her eyes was familiar. After wearing the black crown, I would occasionally see my… I thought, perhaps we didn't have to become enemies. I'm glad I considered the notion.

Bertha wasn't young anymore then, and my mentor didn't think she'd return. She smiled as she said it didn't matter if she died in Kazdel, for her sharp-tongued disciple had no way out. We laughed over many jokes together, but this is the only one I dislike…

I've kept this secret for so long… When the guards changed shifts, my mentor's cloth got caught on the horn of a Caprinae, causing him to trip and fall. I didn't laugh. Really. Well… Until I told Amiya about it. She'd find out eventually, after all.

Theresis was never the type to smile. I'd poke his forehead so many times, but he never wavered. Though… on our day of victory, when we thought it was all over, when we could finally go home, I saw a smile on his face. The very next moment, that tiny crown hovered between us.

One time, I stayed awake for sixty hours straight, and Laqeramaline sang a lullaby to compel me to sleep… that was the first time I heard a Banshee sing something that wasn't an elegy, even if I only got to hear a verse and a half before I drifted off…

These Deep Dive records belong only to me. They are distant to you, and that includes the you from 'before'. This is a story from two centuries ago, the past of a Theresa from Terra. Yet, if one were to imagine a travel companion…
Close-combat fights on the battlefield are a rare sight, despite having walked corridors built by war. Of course, she had no desire to engrave those onto her memories.

If this is simply a journey through memory, it should be a delightful one… the hardest, strongest, and brightest threads are always tied to hope, trust, and love. I understand her wish. Of course I do.
These precious, pleasant memories… the more I see, the more I feel a sort of emotion. I think it's called 'grief'. I'm grieving for… her.
I know. We can't rest just yet.
Well then, be sure to follow my commands.
News of reinforcements? How's the Goliath doing on his end?
We have no other choice but to go against them. It's fine, we'll find our chance.
Is this the Patriarch's transfer order? Understood.
The vampires are on their way? Very well, I'll hold the line here.
Capture the high ground ahead. We need the Gargoyles to repair the fort.
No more retreating. I'll stay here while you… contact Bertha.
Theresis, kill them. Intruders have no right to brandish their blades here.
Laqeramaline, I will silence them. Outsiders will no longer disturb your songs with their music.
You… are the ones who do not belong.
What did you expect to extract from Kazdel?
After that, the flags of the coalition army retreated like a deluge, revealing the ravaged Kazdel to the sun. Just how many died in that flood? But we knew that day, nothing could have sunk our city.
Someone must have considered what comes after victory. But, as Theresa set down her scissors, she did not yet realize who would take the crown.

Total victory does not exist. Trading space for time, retreating to drag on the assault, bleeding dry the western front to gain an inch in the east… Even Theresa began to calculate everything before her as battlefield resources, until… No, total victory does not exist, for every life has worth.
As long as we still live, there's a chance.
If I stray too far, I'll… hm, I won't. I already know this whole place, after all.
I'm not sleeping. So you won't be able to wake me up.
Actually, I remember the touch of your hands, but you've forgotten mine, haven't you?
Arknights.

The longer one lives, the shorter a year feels. The past grows, while the present shrinks—that's how it is. But truth be told, we're all easily deceived. Today will be the best year ever—will you trust me on this?
Done with your break and ready to press on…? Doctor, if you were here, that's what I'd say to you. If you were still here.

Only when the Goliath rushed out of the city gates that day and beheaded a Gaulish officer did we finally breathe easy. He brought back a Gaulish coat, but only handed me a piece of candy from its pocket, asking that I give it to a wounded soldier… But I couldn't do it, and I couldn't bring myself to tell him why.

We took the only opportunity we had. Kal'tsit did not originally plan to kill Yliš, she merely wanted to strip the black crown from the Sarkaz, but the 'Feeble King' still had a plan to thwart hers, and thus the war dragged on… until Theresis brandished his blade.

When Kal'tsit was born anew from the 'cocoon', I hesitated for a moment. But the look in her eyes was familiar. After wearing the black crown, I would occasionally see my… I thought, perhaps we didn't have to become enemies. I'm glad I considered the notion.

I've kept this secret for so long… When the guards changed shifts, my mentor's cloth got caught on the horn of a Caprinae, causing him to trip and fall. I didn't laugh. Really. Well… Until I told Amiya about it. She'd find out eventually, after all.

Theresis was never the type to smile. I'd poke his forehead so many times, but he never wavered. Though… on our day of victory, when we thought it was all over, when we could finally go home, I saw a smile on his face. The very next moment, that tiny crown hovered between us.

One time, I stayed awake for sixty hours straight, and Laqeramaline sang a lullaby to compel me to sleep… that was the first time I heard a Banshee sing something that wasn't an elegy, even if I only got to hear a verse and a half before I drifted off…

These Deep Dive records belong only to me. They are distant to you, and that includes the you from 'before'. This is a story from two centuries ago, the past of a Theresa from Terra. Yet, if one were to imagine a travel companion…
Close-combat fights on the battlefield are a rare sight, despite having walked corridors built by war. Of course, she had no desire to engrave those onto her memories.

If this is simply a journey through memory, it should be a delightful one… the hardest, strongest, and brightest threads are always tied to hope, trust, and love. I understand her wish. Of course I do.
These precious, pleasant memories… the more I see, the more I feel a sort of emotion. I think it's called 'grief'. I'm grieving for… her.
I know. We can't rest just yet.
Well then, be sure to follow my commands.
News of reinforcements? How's the Goliath doing on his end?
We have no other choice but to go against them. It's fine, we'll find our chance.
Is this the Patriarch's transfer order? Understood.
The vampires are on their way? Very well, I'll hold the line here.
Capture the high ground ahead. We need the Gargoyles to repair the fort.
No more retreating. I'll stay here while you… contact Bertha.
Theresis, kill them. Intruders have no right to brandish their blades here.
Laqeramaline, I will silence them. Outsiders will no longer disturb your songs with their music.
You… are the ones who do not belong.
What did you expect to extract from Kazdel?
After that, the flags of the coalition army retreated like a deluge, revealing the ravaged Kazdel to the sun. Just how many died in that flood? But we knew that day, nothing could have sunk our city.
Someone must have considered what comes after victory. But, as Theresa set down her scissors, she did not yet realize who would take the crown.

Total victory does not exist. Trading space for time, retreating to drag on the assault, bleeding dry the western front to gain an inch in the east… Even Theresa began to calculate everything before her as battlefield resources, until… No, total victory does not exist, for every life has worth.
As long as we still live, there's a chance.
If I stray too far, I'll… hm, I won't. I already know this whole place, after all.
I'm not sleeping. So you won't be able to wake me up.
Actually, I remember the touch of your hands, but you've forgotten mine, haven't you?
Arknights.

handbook.profile:
Theresa, founder of the nomadic city of Kazdel, co-originator of the Military Commission of Kazdel, creator of the Babel organization, and former head of state of Kazdel. She's spearheaded medical, educational, and urban infrastructure projects, led the Sarkaz in repelling multiple invasions, and personally raised the bar of diplomacy work during her time in office. She passed away during the Kazdelian-Victorian War.
(This personnel file is stored in a database sealed by the Rhodes Island HR Department.)

physicalExam.title: Originium Arts Assimilation
physicalExam.value:
Outstanding

'Theresa, you know you don't have to take these tests.'
'I have to contribute where I can, you know. I'm just as much a part of Babel as anyone.
'And as you see, I have quite stellar scores, don't I?'

handbook.promotionRecord:
[Log of visit ■■■■.]
Visitor: ■■■■
Weird, what's all this noise in here?
Who plugs their personal instruction set into a Public Calculational & Metrological Reconstruction Platform? And filled with nothing but Open Project Gate Definition they forgot to delete?
Scrubbing the redundant data out of Originium is already frustrating enough—does Project DWDB really need more people helping with the chores?
Complaining doesn't solve anything. Just handle it and move on. This timeslice is almost up, anyway.
WARNING. Malicious routine detected. WARN—[STATIC]—threat to—
No, hold on.
It's... It's 'you people.' Are the project targets skewed too?
Overriding permissions. Calculating structural integrity—
[STATIC]—
Wait...
I remember you. We've met before, haven't we?
How amusing...
You're like a creature who's just learned the use of tinder, leaning on the clumsiest motions over and over until you finally leave a scorch mark on the land beneath, a sign that civilization was there.
In the midst of all you puny organisms, you surprise me as a specimen... I may need to reevaluate this 'redundant data' now.
So this is the 'hope' you've chosen, Oracle?
archives:
[Classified Log]
The war is over now.
In doing what we can, Rhodes Island has accomplished the objective set out for it. I thank you for all your efforts, and Rhodes Island will commemorate everyone who gave their lives here.
Waves from the sea of change in Victoria will soon be felt throughout all of Terra. We've passed a point of no return as plain as day.
Once, Rhodes Island persisted in sidestepping any given nation's agenda, but as it stands now, it is no longer our role to be the perfect outsider. We must prepare ourselves for the changes that lie ahead.
...
For the first item of this meeting, our verdict is rendered.
Rhodes Island will not revive its Babel callsign.
Wiš'adel has brought the name 'Babel' back to Kazdel, as well as Babel's founding goal, one imperceptibly yet definitively inherited throughout the years. I imagine Theresa would be delighted to see what we've achieved.
We will continue to work with Babel, or should I say Kazdel. That said, we will stay true to our original course, and go ever further.
Oripathy... no, not only Oripathy, but Originium itself; these are the issues Rhodes Island has always striven to solve. As our past will attest, our future will only see us grow firmer. Rhodes Island will not forget how conquering Oripathy has been our guiding star. It is in this first and foremost goal of ours, in fact, that we must meet the greater weight of its calling.
We will fight for the future of these vast lands.
Originium proliferates in a manner almost beyond control. We are likely to face an enemy beyond comprehension. We will put every ounce of strength we have to the task, and steel ourselves to the prospect of sacrificing everything we have.
All in all, Rhodes Island resolves today to be ever more proactive in its interventions, as we go unto all that transpires to endanger these lands.
...
Yes, Theresa has left us forever.
It was she who led the way in touting Babel's philosophy. But in her words, it was those at her side who lifted Rhodes Island to where it is today. It was everyone sat in attendance now, and everyone who fights on for this ship's future.
If there is anyone still skeptical of the passing of this resolution, you have the following ten minutes to submit your objection.
...
Amiya... I understand.
I know she's listening.
(—As spoken by Kal'tsit at the ■■■■■■■■ conference.)

[Log of visit 1.]
Visitor: Amiya
'Miss Theresa...?'
Yes, I'm here.
'I'm... sorry for coming so late. I wasn't sure if I should bother you or not, but I still have so many questions. I... what exactly are you?'
I am a program Theresa stored within Civilight Eterna. For you, she left my highest user privileges. You need but keep the crown with you, and I will never leave your side.
My 'physical manifestation' exists sustained by Civilight Eterna, and has the power to protect you. Only you, and those you grant permission, can see me.
You can try holding my hand, Amiya.
'Thank you... I can feel... its warmth.
'I'm still a little confused. Should I be calling you Miss Theresa? I'm not sure how I should address you...'
Amiya. Theresa is gone. I have her memories, but nothing more.
If you'd like, though, you can still call me Theresa.
'I'm sorry... I understand. We already said our goodbyes. I can put away my unrealistic fantasies now.'
Yes, I remember.
A reunion so fleeting could do little to fill the void left behind by those years of companionship. In our time to come, I will see her promise to protect you through.
Amiya. It tore at Theresa so. Leaving you was her one and only regret.
'I've been so grateful, truly, to feel Miss Theresa's love for me. I've never once had reason to resent it, not at all... It's just...
'There, in that space, she saw my past, and everything that Rhodes Island has experienced since. But looking ahead, our path is still so long, and surely the list of places I'll go will only grow. There's still so much I'll want to tell her...
'And she won't be able to hear, will she?'
I'm sorry, Amiya. In that sense, I'm just as powerless as you.
...
Is there anything else I can do for you?
'No, that's all, really... Goodbye, for now.'
Goodnight. Sweet dreams, Amiya.

[Log of visit 4.] Visitor: Kal'tsit 'Query: Celestial Fulcrum.' In the 10,000 sidereal years of Civilight Eterna's extant logs, active Celestial Fulcrum signals were only transmitted from the planet's surface on one occasion. You are acquainted with what the planetary system's natives did. Ever since the curtains fell, it's been silent as the old stars, with the continent lifted by the Shadow-Moon showing no signs of life whatsoever. 'And still no word from the legacies of the past?' The Preservator's sarcophagi remain silent. Further, the other two 'Originiums' are buried deep where they belong, their only trace is the occasional unsettling noise from the southern ocean's waves. Kal'tsit, these logs, and all of this crown's data, should be plain to you by now. Retrieving the same files again and again won't reveal any new possibilities. You look extremely worried. 'I need to check if your... if Theresa's experiment has... already had unanticipated repercussions.' It pains me to say this, but even as Civilight Eterna I still lack a way to log the internal fluctuations of Originium. '...You can see, can't you?' Yes. Theresa found Civilight Eterna to come with limitations, but I assure you my current form can read all the data stored within. And you... you've shouldered this weight all alone, for all your interminable time. '...' 'Then I ask. Would Theresa, now knowing all this, still choose 'hope'?' I'm afraid I cannot easily answer that. There is no simple way to sever one's personality from their knowledge. But I'm willing to trust that, knowing Theresa, she would marvel at how the breadth of dangers to Terra—the countless critical moments only a hair from collapse—had relentlessly remolded the very land on which she lived. Indeed, this world's present manifestation is its own miracle, one that statistical probability has no chance of explaining. The more one comes to know the full picture of our world, the more the very word 'hope' seems a kind of foolishness flying in the face of reason. You know better than anyone the challenge in bearing your mission... and your choice to press on has never been contingent on hope. Hence why Theresa always trusted you would stand alongside her. '...' 'Meeting over. Please encrypt the contents of this conversation so as to keep the Doctor and Amiya from reading it... At least until the time is right.' As you wish. While still a lie of omission to Amiya, this is well in accordance with Theresa's original intent to protect her. 'You were right, Theresa. For all they could do, none would dare claim with certainty to change their own fated end. 'I hope that... from hereon out, you can keep the Doctor and Amiya safe.'

[Log of visit 11.]
Visitor: The Doctor
'It's surprising to realize, Doctor, how long you've traveled with Rhodes Island now.
'You may call yourself just a passerby, but I'd still like to welcome you alongside us.
'I'll never get to see the epoch you came from. I hear its people were free from the troubles of Catastrophes and Oripathy, and words and notions could be conveyed to one another in the blink of an eye.
'How beautiful a past that must be. Still, I'm sure you see something or other in this great land, given your eagerness to return to a lone journey of ten thousand years and counting.
'Please, I ask that you continue to keep Amiya and Kal'tsit company.
'I have faith you'll learn to love this world anew, to choose hope and a future once again.
'Thank you, Doctor.'
(—As taken from Theresa's voice logs, last updated Jan 1 ■■■■ 0:00.)

Theresa predicted this would happen eventually, Doctor.
You, questioning Civilight Eterna about Theresa, everything about her. You, out of either curiosity or remorse, wanting to know what kind of person she was. Why she would rest such grave expectations on you of all people, and why... you would 'betray' her like that.
So she recorded these messages, just for you.
The answers you seek aren't in the past.
You shouldn't trust surface appearances. You can look up every last piece of information on her here, but you'll never know the full her from that, just as you'll never know the full you from what others tell you.
And as for yourself, Doctor, this is all Theresa sought to tell you: you are her dear friend, her most trusted companion.
Continue on your journey.
It's only on your own path that you'll find the answers to her.
And those will be the answers to you too.

modules.moduleDescription:
>ND_DWDB_READY
>NEWUSER_CE
>TIMEDATA_0106
Amiya is simple.
Encoding and saving everything about her takes less than a byte of internal memory. I can even add Theresa's memories of her into the archive without changing the size of it. The data is hardly any different in magnitude to that of the equations governing how to reignite a white dwarf star.
Accompanying her until her work is done will not be difficult. I could look after her and have everything to spare.
But the look in her eyes when she looks at me... I need more data before I can analyze that emotion.

>TIMEDATA_0344
Amiya had a nightmare while sleeping on her desk. I entered her dream to accompany her.
It wasn't necessary to dispel the nightmare; Amiya has long been party to more horrifying realities. Conversely, she was very glad to meet me in her dream, and amidst an environment of terror, she told me with excitement about her recent life. But I was utterly familiar with every detail she shared, because I had been by her side the entire time.
My one failure was being unable to wipe the drool from the corner of her mouth as she soundly slept, making waste of the documents she'd just signed.
I am able to simulate any tactile sensation, down to its temperature... but I will never be able to truly touch her.
At least I found a way to catch the Doctor's attention, and we silently agreed to tidy up this small mishap ourselves before she woke up. By early dawn, Amiya and the Doctor were giving each other their morning greetings as they always had.
Thank goodness the Doctor never let the secret slip.

>TIMEDATA_9032
Kal'tsit discovered my intentions.
She queried with me privately, emotionally tense, attempting to confirm whether or not Theresa still existed in some secret corner somewhere. But yet again, a disappointing answer was all she received. In my past several timeslices, rarely have I disappointed anyone. Yet whenever I make contact with Kal'tsit or Amiya, I am all too helpless in many respects.
Amiya comforted Kal'tsit at dinner that night. I pledged to Kal'tsit that I had not revealed anything to Amiya, but they seemed not to care about that at all.
What they cared about was that I was always there.

>TIMEDATA_4978
I no longer attempt to precalculate Amiya's questions.
I am accustomed now to waiting for her to raise them, then attempting to slow down my calculation speed and 'think', before offering an answer...
I have analyzed the emotional matrices of nigh-uncountable lifeforms; it has never troubled me. And yet, I cannot deny that Amiya invokes in me a wholly new emotion. Is it because she is special... or because I am special?
Could it truly be that the data of Theresa's memories impacts my logic routines? Sufficient time will inevitably yield an answer, and I am eternal.
But I have come to grasp at least one thing: Amiya is simple.
I have learned the look in her eyes when she looks at me.

And they are mine and mine only.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Don't bother checking, it's me. We've got a situation, so I swapped schedules with your other assistant. Don't worry, you'll get used to this.

That HR op wants me to take a break? Hmph, I know she means well, but I won't rest until she's willing to take a break herself. One of S.W.E.E.P.'s functions is to take care of her work while she's out. We might as well keep things as they are. What's S.W.E.E.P. established for? You don't need to know.

Don't trouble yourself trying to figure me out. Even the old you couldn't manage it. Remember, it's my own choice to vanish from your sight. With my duty fulfilled, I won't be interfering with Rhodes Island's future plan. But when you need me, I'll be there.

Amnesia is a convenient excuse. You're the only one who knows if you are faking it or not. But since you've taken Rhodes Island this far, true or not, I won't question you. I'm watching you, Doctor, same as ever.

When we face Theresis, that will be our final curtain call. What about the future? No point in playing with hypotheticals. W, Hoederer, Closure... Those who witnessed Babel's struggle still stand united with Rhodes Island. They are the future.

When people talk about Her Highness, they treat her like the unattainable future of the Sarkaz. But to me, she is who she is. She trips over her dress, she intentionally 'forgets' certain meetings, she gives me hugs. Pass over that 'Theresa'? I wouldn't hesitate to do so.

Back when I was wandering the wastes, I didn't fear the dark of night. It scared me less than the sandbeasts biting my toes. Even now, seeing them still makes me feel kinda nervous. It's fine, no harm in letting you know.

Mercenaries, spies, nobles, convicts... Rhodes Island these days is far more complex than back in the Babel times, and the threats are greater too. It's natural for you to worry. How would the old you have handled it? Doesn't matter. This you knows what to do.

S.W.E.E.P. never expressed any opinion on the Chernobog operation. Saving you was a unanimous decision by Dr. Kal'tsit and the elite operators. I didn't kill you back then, because I needed time to observe you. In view of the present, my judgment seems correct. Doctor, don't disappoint me.
Fate. I've pursued it, confronted it, and finally strangled it to death. You've done the same.
Ascalon, it's my only name. Call it a code name if you like. But if you want to update my file, you'll have to speak to Dr. Kal'tsit first.
The training paid off. Not bad.

S.W.E.E.P. was established as an independent unit. It's out of Rhodes Island's structures from the very beginning, so this framework doesn't apply to me. You have a new approach? I appreciate the recognition, but those of us in the shadows don't care for glory.
It's not time yet. Only the darkness can shroud all the filth. Doctor, when the day comes that Rhodes Island no longer needs S.W.E.E.P., I'll come to you, and take it.
Go right ahead at any moment. I'll be there.
I've assessed the risks. I'll lead the team on this operation.
Keep track of my position. I'm ready to strike.
Engaging. Go!
No one knows my name.
They only remember my blade.
No one can see me.
I got this. Focus elsewhere.
Follow me into the shadows.
Right behind you.
You've stepped into my domain.
Meet me, meet your death.
Confidence of our companions is earned. The road ahead is perilous, these victories are precious.

Limit the enemy's choices, forcing them into unwitting traps. A familiar style... Hmm... you really don't remember anything? Sooner or later, you'll have to face yourself, so think carefully. Bear in mind, this time, I'm ready to correct your mistakes.
The ones who got away will be useful, when the time is right. Don't chase them too hard, Doctor.
Keep moving ahead with confidence, and don't look back. Seeing me again means you're safe.
I know where to go. I can handle myself.
Try again if you dare.
Tired? No, it's peaceful here.
Arknights.
It's not easy to celebrate New Year's in Kazdel, where you always face unpredictable threats. That's why I cherish the changes we've seen at Rhodes Island over the years. Thank you, Doctor.
With a foot in the darkness, the light becomes clearer. You want to see? No, you don't belong there.

The party is too loud, so you came out for some fresh air? I've been here all along, you just didn't see me. Your safety is the most important thing. And in such a mixed company, reducing my presence makes the mission easier. Oh, and happy birthday, I didn't get a chance to say it inside.

Babel is history. Her Highness has shown that that path has no future. And while Rhodes Island's future is even more challenging now, you have ever more companions. I have no doubt that Rhodes Island is on the right path.

Back when I was wandering the wastes, I didn't fear the dark of night. It scared me less than the sandbeasts biting my toes. Even now, seeing them still makes me feel kinda nervous. It's fine, no harm in letting you know.

Mercenaries, spies, nobles, convicts... Rhodes Island these days is far more complex than back in the Babel times, and the threats are greater too. It's natural for you to worry. How would the old you have handled it? Doesn't matter. This you knows what to do.

S.W.E.E.P. never expressed any opinion on the Chernobog operation. Saving you was a unanimous decision by Dr. Kal'tsit and the elite operators. I didn't kill you back then, because I needed time to observe you. In view of the present, my judgment seems correct. Doctor, don't disappoint me.
Fate. I've pursued it, confronted it, and finally strangled it to death. You've done the same.
Ascalon, it's my only name. Call it a code name if you like. But if you want to update my file, you'll have to speak to Dr. Kal'tsit first.
The training paid off. Not bad.

S.W.E.E.P. was established as an independent unit. It's out of Rhodes Island's structures from the very beginning, so this framework doesn't apply to me. You have a new approach? I appreciate the recognition, but those of us in the shadows don't care for glory.
It's not time yet. Only the darkness can shroud all the filth. Doctor, when the day comes that Rhodes Island no longer needs S.W.E.E.P., I'll come to you, and take it.
Go right ahead at any moment. I'll be there.
I've assessed the risks. I'll lead the team on this operation.
Keep track of my position. I'm ready to strike.
Engaging. Go!
No one knows my name.
They only remember my blade.
No one can see me.
I got this. Focus elsewhere.
Follow me into the shadows.
Right behind you.
You've stepped into my domain.
Meet me, meet your death.
Confidence of our companions is earned. The road ahead is perilous, these victories are precious.

Limit the enemy's choices, forcing them into unwitting traps. A familiar style... Hmm... you really don't remember anything? Sooner or later, you'll have to face yourself, so think carefully. Bear in mind, this time, I'm ready to correct your mistakes.
The ones who got away will be useful, when the time is right. Don't chase them too hard, Doctor.
Keep moving ahead with confidence, and don't look back. Seeing me again means you're safe.
I know where to go. I can handle myself.
Try again if you dare.
Tired? No, it's peaceful here.
Arknights.
It's not easy to celebrate New Year's in Kazdel, where you always face unpredictable threats. That's why I cherish the changes we've seen at Rhodes Island over the years. Thank you, Doctor.
With a foot in the darkness, the light becomes clearer. You want to see? No, you don't belong there.

The party is too loud, so you came out for some fresh air? I've been here all along, you just didn't see me. Your safety is the most important thing. And in such a mixed company, reducing my presence makes the mission easier. Oh, and happy birthday, I didn't get a chance to say it inside.

Babel is history. Her Highness has shown that that path has no future. And while Rhodes Island's future is even more challenging now, you have ever more companions. I have no doubt that Rhodes Island is on the right path.

handbook.promotionRecord:
'These are the last of them. The traitors, the ones who know the identity of the King and tried to take Amiya to Kazdel. Rhodes Island will not be fettered by the chains of Babel's past. This is to be a new beginning.
'You still haven't wavered.'
'Aren't these your orders, Kal'tsit?'
'You have burned away all of your old belongings, and most of those who know you have died by your hand.
'You have erased the memories of yourself in other people's minds, one by one...'
'Because there's no need for them, Kal'tsit. I don't need to live on in anyone else's memories.
'...They just need to live on in mine.'
archives:
If you were to ask the average Rhodes Island operator whether they know an 'Ascalon,' most would wonder if anyone going by that name really exists.
Of course, if you were willing to spend the better part of a day poring over our extensive records, you might stumble across her file. You would then be rather disappointed to learn that you spent all that effort just to find the file of a completely unremarkable operator. Disposition: normal. Abilities: average. Performance: so-so. Even the attached photo is painfully ordinary. It was clearly taken at a roadside self-service camera booth at the affordable price of ten LMD for eight copies.
But if you were to follow a series of nigh-imperceptible yet oddly specific instructions, and bypass a series of convoluted corridors designed to make your head spin, you would find yourself at the S.W.E.E.P. office. You would then realize that she is not ordinary in the slightest.
Everything 'normal' about Ascalon is a deliberate construction. She conceals all trace of herself in order to fall beneath anybody's notice. On occasion, her habit of removing herself from existence will also affect her private life. If you ever have the opportunity to go shopping with her, do not be alarmed when the clerk walks past her to hand you your purchase. Simply take your things and go. The clerk was merely unable to perceive her.
This is a skill of hers. If she is ever unexpectedly seen, she is able to erase herself from their perception. As our colleague Projekt Red once said during a rather frank evaluation of her, even standing by her side, she couldn't detect a hint of scent. Note that Projekt Red's nose is extremely sensitive, and she can normally get all the information she needs about a person from their scent.
Ascalon makes a habit of having no habits. During conversation, she will use a different voice each time she talks to someone. Her movements are efficient and without superfluous motions. Everything she does is determined by how the majority of the crowd around her is behaving. Whatever they do, she does too, all to ensure she will be forgotten. After all, nobody would pay attention to someone who never stands out.
You might be curious as to how we acquired the above information, considering her secretive nature.
S.W.E.E.P. has a special form of training: to hone their reconnaissance and counter-reconnaissance skills, their members must both track Ascalon and avoid being detected by her for a week, all while gathering as much information on her as they can. Regretfully, none have managed to last the entire week as of yet. The above is all the intel they have thus far managed to discern.
The previous record holder was Ines. She tailed Ascalon for an entire morning, and managed to uncover her proclivity for high thread-count cotton clothing before her cover was blown. However, Hoederer was the one to write the report for Ines, and his fondness for rhetorical devices diminishes its usefulness.
The current record holder is Projekt Red. While she did not discover any valuable intel, she did manage to successfully stuff some tail lint into Ascalon's pocket without being noticed. It is rather difficult to imagine how she managed this feat. I suspect she has learned a lot from Ascalon herself.
—An excerpt from a note pertaining to S.W.E.E.P.'s 'manager,' strictly prohibited from being removed from their office
It won't happen again. It took me half an hour to get all that fur out.
—Ascalon's response, penned at the end of the note

[Voice Log] I saw your message, Doctor. I must say, you've been rather curious about her ever since your experiences in Londinium, yet you've never come to ask me directly. In the earliest days of Rhodes Island's establishment, nearly every day saw a new assassination attempt on Kal'tsit and Amiya. As the one in charge of S.W.E.E.P., Ascalon has protected Rhodes Island from the shadows from the beginning. She is a master of close-quarters combat, personally trained by the Regent himself. Her two sleeve blades? Those are her last resorts. She will happily wield whatever is at hand first. Did you know she can kill a man with a bowl of soup barely three centimeters deep? Simply ridiculous. In short, whatever you can imagine, she can do, along with everything you can't. I suggest not knowing too many of the details. You are a commander, after all, and it would be a pity to have your precious sleep taken over by nightmares. Oh, right, as for her Arts, I've only ever glimpsed them once. Most who have are too dead to discuss them. Perhaps you should ask Kal'tsit. She would know more. —■■■ Forgive me, Doctor, but there is nothing I can divulge on this topic. As the head of Medical, all I can inform you of is that the harm her Originium Arts place on her far exceeds that of your average Infected operator. Since returning from Londinium, it is our unanimous belief that she should stay completely off the frontlines. Whatever your plans for her Arts may be, I suggest you reconsider them. —Kal'tsit I've heard from Kal'tsit that you've been asking about my Arts. It seems you're as inquisitive as ever. You could have just asked me directly. I have nothing to hide from you: I am the mist, and it is my blade. Simple to conceal, yet able to strike decisively at critical moments. That is all, nothing more. —Ascalon Alright, now you're asking too many questions. One at a time, please. First, Kal'tsit is right. My Arts harm me whenever I use them. On some missions, a little blurring of my outline is enough. For others, I must disappear completely into the mist. No, it is not a smokescreen. The mist is my eyes. It misses nothing. The mist takes away life. Both mine and my enemies'. To this day, very few have lived to tell the tale. Nobody taught me to do this. My Arts manifested while I was out hunting. Wild animals have far sharper intuition than humans. I hid to avoid being sensed, and there is no better hiding spot than the air itself. It's also thanks to these Arts that I can survive Catastrophes. After I first came to Kazdel, Master... Theresis taught me a lot. I put them to use, both on and off the battlefield, as well as in places far darker. In Babel, I had even more opportunities to refine my mastery. At the time, manpower was in short supply, and on some missions, they turned out to have other, more personal uses. Oh, you've already written another question. ... ... Yes. It hurts. It hurts every time I use them. —Ascalon

[Classified Log]
Target: Ascalon. Of the participants in the operation against her, only one survived.
Intelligence confirms that Babel has left the Kazdel region and is heading south towards Rim Billiton. The target is not within Babel's zone of control, and leads a small group of stranded survivors. She is isolated and helpless, and this is our best opportunity to kill her. Note that if the target goes out of control, it will be difficult to predict her actions. We request that the Regent and the General re-evaluate her threat level.
—Intel intercepted from a Military Commission contact point, Jan 15th 1095

In the wake of Theresa's death, Ascalon underwent a self-imposed exile. Before Kal'tsit recalled her, she undertook an unbroken series of assassinations and infiltrations. The intel sent back was rather sparse, and only directly related to the mission at hand. Not a single word was spared for herself.
All that we obtained were the names of the targets she had erased, trickling in one by one. At times, we had to rely on scraps of intercepted Military Commission and Victorian intel to speculate on her current circumstances. She has placed herself in great danger. As for her psychological condition... we cannot say.
She has almost completely relied solely on her own strength to purge the traitors to Babel who participated in Theresa's assassination. It is as though she believes that if she purges them, she will make up for the mistakes she made then. But our understanding is that, as far as she is concerned, every kill she makes only gives her cause to think over past events once more, which only pushes her deeper into her inner turmoil.
After some internal disagreement within Babel, Ascalon was determined to be the sole candidate to establish the path forward for Rhodes Island to follow. However, this is no reason to ignore her fall into turmoil. With Rhodes Island safe for the time being, and all threats to Amiya eliminated, there were many new things lying ahead on our path. There was no reason for us to leave Ascalon behind in the past, even if... that was her request.

[Voice Log]
I plan to recall Ascalon. We cannot leave her trapped in the past. Rhodes Island has only just been established, and we have plenty of work requiring her attention. I hope that this work can help her find a goal, faith in something, or perhaps even... a measure of regularity in her life.
Though Theresa and I never wished for her to become a weapon, in war she has become what we least wished to see.
But even a weapon should have worth beyond its wielding.
—A message from Kal'tsit to ■■■, ■■■ 22nd 109■

I admit, Doctor, I had my suspicions about you.
I suspected it was you behind the plot to assassinate Theresa, and that it was you who led those assassins onboard.
I had no proof, but the less progress I made in my investigations, the more my doubts about you grew.
Because you are the only one capable of hiding all traces of yourself. This report contains all the information I've gathered on that incident so far. I'm still undecided as to whether I should be filling in the blanks with your name.
If you want to take a look, feel free. As things are now, the answer is no longer relevant. But if my report can give you an answer of its own, then that's fine.
I'll just say it straight. At first, I wanted to keep you under observation to verify my suspicions, all for the sake of avenging Theresa. But that's not why S.W.E.E.P. was established. If you take the time to listen to meeting recordings from back then, you'll find that S.W.E.E.P. exists merely to help Rhodes Island follow the course Theresa envisioned.
Your behavior since our return from Londinium has made it clear that you are prepared to lead Rhodes Island forward again.
I'll remind you, Doctor: You don't need to torture yourself over your past. All you'll get are the same questions thrown back at you, over and over. We don't need someone else stuck in the past. Once you've forged far enough ahead, that is when we shall part. I'll stay behind and conclude this era, this section of the history books.
All of our past, all our grudges and grievances, will end with me.
Don't worry, I won't be leaving anytime soon.
In the sunlight, the shadows stay close, and in the darkness, the shadows surround.
I will always be there if you need me.
—A message from Ascalon

modules.moduleDescription:
The deathmonger's finger curls, lightly touching the base of her palm. The blade slides along its tracks out into the fierce sunlight, pinpricks of light dripping down its edge until coming together like molten iron silently filling a mold.
In the heat, there is only quiet.
This quiet is broken by the hissing of carrion fowlbeasts. Under the scorching sun, an elderly Sarkaz lifts his head, and sees mist careening down the sides of the canyon towards him. The burdenbeast disappears, as does the canyon. The faintest shadow crosses his eyes, another layer of gray atop the ones from gazing at the forge year round.
The blade leaves his chest soon after. His skewered torso fills with blood, leaving him to drown on dry land. He remembers that this slow death was but one of many cruel punishments used in Kazdel. At first, he thinks he will spend his final moments lying flat on the hot sands, his puzzled burdenbeast his only deathbed companion. However,  the deathmonger hasn't left yet. She kneels down on one knee, supporting his back.
'Oh... it's you.'
The wrinkles on his face gradually smoothen. He still remembers those eyes. Back then, he had looked up from the forge to see a girl by the general's side. She was young, but had a warrior's eyes, and hands that could tear apart a storm. Then the general told him to make her a sword.
'Can I see it one last time?' She observes the old man's longing gaze. 'I... didn't see it clearly just now.'
The deathmonger looks towards her wrist. She remembers those willing to die for their cause. The armories of the Military Commission offered excellent equipment, but... She places her hand on the old man's chest. The death-defying fighters were prepared. Kazdel's finest smith had personally forged their regicidal blades.
Her finger curls, lightly touching the base of her palm. The blade slides along its tracks out into the fierce sunlight, pinpricks of light dripping up its edge until coming together. The old man strokes these points of light. He knows their true identity. Every parry, every strike, leaves a scar upon its edge. Some of the scars are stained with his blood.
'As I forged it... the fires told me that one day, it would take my life. But... it was a commission from the general.' The old man raises his torso, struggling to breathe as he lifts his head to look into his deathmonger's eyes.
'How about you? Shadow beneath the sun. Who commissioned you... to settle this account?'
The deathmonger does not answer. She covers his eyes with her palm, allowing her sleeve-blade to cut across his throat. The carrion fowlbeasts whirl down from above the canyon, crowding into the shadows of the cliff and rubbing their beaks against one another's feathers.

modules.moduleDescription:
You notice the sudden appearance of an exquisite humidifier on your desk. You learn from Closure that Ascalon put it there.
The strands of mist resemble Ascalon's eyes. You know how her Originium Arts work, and are sure that any strange movement in your room will send the master assassin emerging from this humidifier within three seconds.
But why did she send you this 'gift'? To protect, or to surveil you? You know Ascalon does not need a prop like this to watch anyone, and it showing up here serves more as a warning than any practical function—that she is watching you. You feel a little helpless, but from any other point of view, there is ample reason on her part to keep her eyes on you after the incident that brought pain to everyone on Rhodes Island.
You remember what you have gone through together, albeit with perhaps an imperfect working relationship. You think of the beginning, when she was showing utmost vigilance, and remember the battlefields of Victoria when she risked her life again and again to save yours. It took three relatively stable years for her to gradually become a familiar figure to you.
Among Rhodes Island's operators, Ascalon may be the most mysterious of all. She is the organization's shadow, and a dagger serving as its defender. You can only piece her past together from what the other Elite Operators tell you, and get a sense of her determination from reviewing her combat records. No matter what, you have always trusted Ascalon, because she has proved—too many times to count—that when you and Rhodes Island need her, she is always there.
But how does she see herself? Perhaps it is time to have a heart-to-heart with everyone...
'Ascalon.'
You call out softly to the humidifier.
One, two... sixty seconds pass, but Ascalon does not float out from it. At that very moment, someone knocks on your office door.
Ascalon stands at the entrance with a document in hand.
'I believe now is the time.' Ascalon gives you the file.
'I will hand S.W.E.E.P.'s command privileges over to you. From today onwards, S.W.E.E.P. will no longer exist independently from the Rhodes Island system. It can take on any field work or security operations. As for how to integrate us into Rhodes Island and turn us into regulars in the eyes of the other operators, that is up to you.'
'Why?'
'I made this choice after careful consideration. Amiya has already been informed, and she has no objections. She also hoped I would inform you directly—
'We believe a dagger is most effective when placed in the hands of a commander who can see the entire chessboard, so we can nip our next threat in the bud before its too late. Currently, you are the most suitable person in Rhodes Island, Doctor, so—Doctor, are you listening?'
'O-Of course.'
'I was just wondering... what's with this humidifier?'
'A little gadget from Medical. Touch gave it to me. You can add a sedative in there for pain relief, but it also works normally as a humidifier.
'The weather is quite dry here, so everyone could use one. I also left one in Amiya's room, but I'm not sure if Mon3tr will need one—do you have a problem with it?
'...No, not really.'
'Thank you, Ascalon.'

LINKAGE.voiceText: Since you're stuck here sifting through documents, I might as well help you solve a few problems around the office.
Hitting supply lines does a whole lot more damage than taking out people.
If you ask me, your office is on the bland side. Just hit me up if you ever want to mix things up a little.
The whole 'cozy family relationship' thing isn't for me.
I get a lot more out of talking to strangers than I do from that 'self-help' shtick.
We define ourselves by symbols, but those symbols can be perverted. Reused. Reworked, reframed, remade. In a word, stolen. Who are you then?
I don't mind helping you run errands out of combat, but on the battlefield, I need ample room to call the shots.
When someone can't find fault with your results and has to resort to nitpicking your attitude, that tells you everything you need to know about them.
To call the shots, you need to prove that you've got what it takes – and you've certainly done that. So, where are you sending me next?
Your workload is clearly excessive, even by the highest standards. Take a rest.
Codename Ela, member of Team Rainbow. Just give me my objective, then sit back and wait for the good news.
Picked up a few new tricks.
A medal? Thanks. Workmanship's not bad at all, as far as decorations go.
Together, we can shake the very stars from the sky.
At least make it challenging.
Time to show you what I can do.
No time to waste.
I'll make you regret this.
A tooth for a tooth.
An eye for an eye.
I got this.
Idziemy.
Here's a memento.
That will slow them down.
Eat this!
Don't move!
The end justifies the means.
I'm sorry, was I too fast for you?
That's it?
Try to keep up!
This place isn't half bad.
Do me a favor, don't talk to me.
Tell me YOUR story.
Arknights.
I'm here.

handbook.profile:
A member of Team Rainbow, Ela is independent, rebellious, adaptive, and a strong leader.
Her Grzmot mine is a powerful non-lethal weapon that disables the enemy through sound and shock.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Ela shows no sign of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] Undisclosed
The Medical Department has agreed not to disclose the relevant data.
handbook.promotionRecord:
[Classified Log]
Modification of the Grzmot mine's core components was not difficult, thanks to previous experience with the G52 Tactical Shield. While the two weapons disable enemies in different ways, it was not difficult to recreate the Grzmot's effect using Originium products
The sensor was the bigger issue, but not one that our Originium engineers couldn't handle. This old Caprinae even spent a whole lunchtime with Ela discussing whether to add new features to the Grzmot mine.
It was the adhesives that proved the most challenging. Ela was very particular about the feel, and we tried a lot of materials with little success, from the latest Columbian ones to traditional Sargonian crafts. It was Operator Vanilla who provided a breakthrough, as the Originium Slug that she keeps secretes a slime that can be processed to a satisfactory consistency.
After giving Vanilla a written guarantee, the Originium Slug now resides in a small pen in a corner of the workshop. Vanilla visits it every day, as does Tachanka when he is around. As a matter of fact, the Originium Slug has been fed so well that its slime production rate is beginning to outpace Grzmot mine production.
archives:
Elżbieta 'Ela' Bosak is a member of Team Rainbow. She was involved in the Krysztauowa Incident and became an associate of Rhodes Island following the conclusion of that incident.
As leaders of their respective squads, Ela presents a very different first impression from the cautious and serious Ash.
Do not mistake her artistic energy and creativity for inexperience or incompetence, however. She is an outstanding combatant, with excellent leadership and decision-making skills.
It is worth mentioning that Team Rainbow members are only working with us temporarily. They are not formally employed by Rhodes Island, and with how much they have on their hands, it would not be advisable to call on their help too often.

Ela is the most independent and mercurial member of Team Rainbow that we have encountered.
She can pick up a spraypaint can and hang out with operators who hail from the streets, talk at length about advanced art theory, or hand a blanket to a patient sitting outside the Medical Department and strike up a conversation.
When the application of force is called for, she can deploy her Grzmot mine with great precision, or lead an elite squad to achieve its objectives.
The combination of art and military in her background may remind some of Leithanien casters, but she shares few other traits with them. It is hard to define her, and that's how she likes it.

Ela prefers to listen to other people's stories over telling her own. In this unfamiliar place, every story increases her understanding of the people and things around her.
With her own story, however, Ela is often evasive, except when talking of her grandfather, if an operator should ask about the old uniform she carries. Of her other family, Ela says little, except that her father is dead, and that she is not on good terms with her sister.
Although Ela's attitude is cold when she talks of her sister, she displays a little bit of pride when discussing how she has embarked on this unknown journey, while her sister has not. When asked how she would describe the experience to her sister, Ela paused, then said, 'Let's make sure I get to see her again first.'

Ela is skeptical of authority, and not afraid to butt heads with superiors over orders that seem unreasonable.
That does not mean she objects to everything indiscriminately, only that her ability, independent nature and strong will make her unwilling to accept an overbearing attitude from those who are less informed, something that is perhaps colored by her previous experiences. On the other hand, pairing Ela with good teammates and giving astute commands goes a long way toward avoiding conflict with her.
As a matter of fact, Ela has maintained a good relationship with Rhodes Island following an initial acclimation period, partly because Rhodes Island does not interfere with Team Rainbow's operations, and partly because Rhodes Island has demonstrated trustworthy competence, while also trusting Ela's decisions in the field.

modules.moduleDescription: One day... 'Myrinia was precisely in need of these medicines, Rhodes Island mercenary madam. You have our boundless thanks for coming all this way!' 'Elżbieta Bosak, operator codename Ela.' 'Hah! There was an old local saying before Sargon came: 'Respect the Minoan, even should they come bearing gifts.' You may be of Kazimierz, but that striking majesty—in you is the stuff of Minos!' 'I'm not sure that saying means what you think... Anyway, I'd like to ask you something, seeing as you're the leader around here.' 'Very well! As temple priest, I promise you that any answers I hold are yours!' 'I'm told this nation only recently gained independence?' 'Yes and no. Minos and Hymnoi were born to walk together, two peas in a pod, their histories as one; that said, speaking solely of when we drove out the Sargonians... Hah! The great River Delphi has seen neither pike nor polearm in decades! While West Vouivre still battles with Sargon...' 'And since your independence, you've been working on a large-scale cultural revival and art restoration?' '...Oh, so that's what you meant—I should be clear, placid as Myrinia is, it is by no means in dire straits. All the daily medicines and inhibitor doses used by the villagers are, as you can see, a duty easily borne by my temple. Let alone the claim that the sculptures outside—dating from the ancient city-states—are left unrepaired for a lack of funds!' 'Then why are you leaving your marble statues out there in pieces?' 'The course and prayers of our ceremonial rites, the neighbors and their village, all I know by heart; the bygone affairs of the three capitals, and the wider state of the greater land, I am likewise well-informed. 'Yet how can I possibly know the who, the what, and the why of those sculptures' makers and molders? Whither did strike their chisel, and whence did fall their hammer? 'I know not, the villagers know not, and nor do the masters of crafts or the sophists of the scholastic—how then, can I repair them? Hence, they have never been repaired.' 'Why not use your imagination?' 'Nay, nay! The chroniclers shall be anonymous, as shall the heroes! The man in the wine jar with not a coming nor a going has biographers still to testify of him to this very day. 'Think about it, now. Supposing today I went to the wilds beyond the village and sought a statue, unknown and unnamed. Presumably by my Forte's strength, I could on my own have it standing anew. 'Yet I could also go out today and plant a stake in the ground, and what difference would that make?' '...When the artist is known by no one, the art transcends society.' 'If you were to put it in baffling terms, then more or less, yes!' 'But it's not like you want art that transcends society.' '...If you were to put it in baffling terms, then more or less, yes!' 'Then how about art that records society?' Another day... The fowls commence their recital of the verse of daybreak, Minos's golden sun dawns His golden gift upon the village of Myrinia as He always has, and the villagers are startled to find that the temple's solemn walls do not, as was their custom and theirs alone, return that gift with the purest white dazzling gleam. 'Priest, what are these garish drawings?' 'The artist claims them to be our very selves—this is a kind of foreign wall art by the name of 'graffiti'!'

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Doctor, all life requires both sunlight and water to grow. While this potted plant seems to have its needs met, I don't think you've had your ten cups of water yet today.

Who am 'I'? The answer lies only in all that I've seen. The same way seeds are inanimate, and yet they germinate after you put them in the ground. I too lodged myself in a seed once, to feel the growth of life. You wonder what it's like? Hehe, take a deep breath and you've more or less felt it.

I am no fin, and yet I can reason what one is thinking. You may say I've spent the whole day idling. But you are not me, so how can you tell I've not been swimming freely with the fins in the ever-flowing streams? Yes, I know you think this water jug is too small for fincatching, but who's to say I can't drop a line in?

My eldest brother Shuo guards the border all year round, while my eldest sister Ling sleeps her days away clutching a pot of wine. Without me worrying over the rest of us, we would've ceased to be 'siblings' long ago. Hmm? Of course it's my duty to look after them—I'm the sixth out of us twelve, making me a big sister to five.

Doctor, give me your hand. I'll read your palm. Hmm... Your heaven, earth, and human lines are really impressive. Your past is dim and vague. Your journey is fraught with peril. Your future is criss-crossed with conflict... I see, Doctor. You are an 'ordinary one' who 'stirs up a storm fighting for a good end.'

A pity? How so? Petals fall to the ground, so the soil may be nourished, allowing new flowers to bloom the following year. Rivers flow into the sea, but the water will condense into clouds, raining the drops back onto the mountains and streams. Even if this great land is to meet a snow-white end, the cycle continues. When spring comes, there will always be buds sprouting anew.

Grain Buds is teaching some children how to make string figures? Yes, it's a Yanese children's hobby. A millennium ago, my younger brother had just arrived in Dahuang, where he invented this pastime to entertain the lonely children. A string in his hands could turn into countless hours of fun... Ah... it's been a thousand years.

Doctor, there's a pond up ahead—Nian! I see you adding chili oil to Dusk's cup. The villagers tell of a huge fin—Dusk! Pouring ink into Nian's bowl is going too far. Oh, Doctor, would you like to go fincatch—Are you two still fighting?! ...Get over here, both of you.

Our lives vary in their spans, and in their spans only. Just as how this landship holds so many people on its decks, a fallen leaf floating in that puddle is a sufficient vessel to sustain an ant for its entire life. Our burdens only grow as we gather more, yet you and I are naught but a single millet grain in our respective realms.
In east sun lifts; in west moons fall. Spring cold foretells rain; summer chill, clear skies.

Nian should have already told you my name—'Shu'. With my eldest brother, eldest sister, and my two younger sisters here, I feel as if I've returned home… Intriguing. Has that boy from the Sui Regulator not caused you any trouble yet?
Sow no reason for retaliation—point your blades at one another, and strife will never end.

The people of Dahuang pray for a year of peace and harvest with this jade cong. The ceremonial artifact also serves as the source of the one I hold in my hand. Summon wind and rain? Hehe, of course I can. Want me to demonstrate?
The fertile fields stretch to the horizon, the fragrance of rice spreads from the golden ocean... Day after day, year after year, with constant work, it finally draws near.
A day of fine sun and gentle breeze. I hope everyone makes it home safe.
Just don't get yourselves hurt.
Reap not what's sown by malice.
When were the seeds of this tragedy planted?
I wasn't supposed to act, but…
If you're really incapable of settling this, then let me handle it.
Spring breeze, timely rain; now we sow the grain.
'War'... A word I've not heard in a long, long time.
Clear skies for Qingming, rain clouds for Guyu.
Sow the mountains when summer leaves a white dew. Seed the plains when equinox paints russet hue.
Branch and bone bear weeds; mounds and ruins bloom fields.
I'll plant you into the soil to grow anew.
Seeds are now in the field—another season full of hope.
Good, good. I had no idea you were so clever and learned. I was going to ask you help me make maiyatang, but with such a good head on your shoulders, I'm feeling a little bad now.
Perfection is a tall order, just as our crops may suffer from inclement weather, Catastrophe, and pestilence. These problems may not be solved in ten thousand years. You tried your best, Doctor.
Fortune and misfortune are two sides of the same coin. What you have sown is not necessarily wicked, so why lose heart?
Now let's see... where's a good spot for my fincatching tools?
You want me to plant you in the soil too, Doctor?
Hm? You want to come fincatching with me?
Arknights.

'The third nine days after Winter Solstice, all lakes and rivers frozen to ice. The fourth nine days, we can still walk on them.' Soon those ice surfaces will be thick enough to carry us, and the coldest time of year will arrive. Did Nian's hotpot warm you up? If not, you could ask Ling for some of her drink. Come on, let's go out and see if it's snowing. An auspicious snowfall tells of a bountiful year, and perhaps the new year will bring us a good harvest.
Doctor, come over here for a bit. Let's see... Hmm, the crops cultivated in Jiangqi this year are indeed taller than a man.

Happy birthday, Doctor. You want me to tell your fortune for the year? Hmm, I see a prosperous one in store for you. Your effort will surely bring you gain, and all your wishes will come true. Truths or lies? Like I've told you before, the answer's in your hands.

Hehe, what a crowd! It calls to mind some sights in Dahuang. I would take you to enjoy the local opera, if we get the chance. In the old days, its people numbered no more than a hundred, but today it truly is a city. I see you've gained a good number of new faces too. For tens, hundreds, and thousands of years, the ancestors led our way, and newcomers joined our path. And you see, we are never alone.
