handbook.profile: Jessica Brynley, after departing from Blacksteel HQ for personal reasons, chose to go to the frontier to become a sheriff. Currently, she provides assistance to Rhodes Island as a partnered operator in the local branch office.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Jessica shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.19 u/L
Jessica's BOCD has increased from before, but is still in the safe range. However, she has been out on the frontier for quite some time, and is often exposed to Originium products without proper protective measures, so we need to pay close attention to her.

'I'm actually more worried about her old injuries than about her getting infected.'
––Medical Operator from the Frontier Branch Office
handbook.promotionRecord:
'That's correct, Doctor. I participated in an armed robbery on the Davistown bank. That's just a fact, and I have nothing to dispute.'
The girl looks at you and rubs her hands together anxiously.
'However, I'm not on the frontier to serve out a sentence. I wasn't charged with any crime.
'Not because I was motivated by wanting to help the locals being extorted by the bank, but rather because... I'm not allowed to be guilty. Because Blacksteel operators cannot be guilty. Because members of the Brynley family cannot be guilty...'
The girl holds up a teapot in her hands and gives the tea leaves floating on the surface a blow, but accidentally cuts her lip on the container's broken rim.
'...You want to know if I plan to stay out here forever?
'Umm... I think I do. Because here, every choice I make belongs not to Jessica of Blacksteel, or to Jessica of the Brynley family.'
Wiping the streaks of blood from the corner of her lips with her fingers, the girl smiles shyly at you.
'They belong to me alone.'
archives:
We don't know precisely why Jessica set aside her mercenary career, and Blacksteel isn't particularly forthcoming about it. Whenever we bring it up, the person in charge always seems say something evasive before quickly changing the subject. However, it is true that Jessica has long been dissatisfied with Blacksteel's tough, uncompromising way of doing things, which the operators familiar with her had all noticed to some extent. On several occasions she has returned to Rhodes Island from a Blacksteel mission without outwardly displaying any negative emotions, but would instead lock herself in her room and not communicate with anyone for days at a time.
Afterwards, when we found out that she had been disciplined for disobeying her superiors, we realized that her differences with the PMC would be difficult to reconcile. This clash came to a head during a mission in the forested belt of Eastern Columbia, resulting in Jessica walking away from Blacksteel and her career, turning her back on both Fort Barron and the Brynley family to start over in a brand new land.
Fortunately, our partnership with her does not end simply because she severed ties with Blacksteel. The burdenbeast station she established on the frontier works together with our branch office to deliver medicine to remote areas that cannot otherwise be reached by vehicle, ensuring that sick pioneers can still get medication in a timely manner, while Jessica also needed funding to establish a frontier camp.
We are extremely pleased to be working together with her once again. While she may appear soft and shy on the surface, deep down she is actually tough and resilient. She also has a lot of empathy and is keenly aware of the emotions of others. These rare qualities allow her to comfort those who've suffered from various traumas, but also make her more susceptible to their emotions. It often takes her a long time to escape from that pain and sadness. Even more unfortunate is the fact that she stubbornly chooses to face everything alone. Despite everything she's witnessed and endured as a mercenary, Jessica has always been reluctant to share her experiences—not that it's our place to pry. But just by closely observing her behavior, we do believe that she's doing much better now.
At least, she now rarely isolates herself in the shooting range after returning to the landship from the frontier.

'Before officially participating in Blacksteel's field missions, Jessica had been working as a weapons tester in the Equipment and Applied Technology Department. There, she was exposed to a wide array of cutting-edge weaponry, and got to know many veterans retired from the Armed Personnel Dispatch Department. They were all experienced and could provide constructive advice during the weapons development process, and it's clear that Jessica has been heavily influenced by them, on top of her other experiences. Not only is she accustomed to using various weapons, but she's also proficient at modifying and improving them.'
'Uh huh.'
'In terms of weapon selection, Jessica prefers to carry a Blacksteel Model 1094 pneumatic handgun, a high-performance weapon representing the pinnacle of Blacksteel's sophisticated weapons R&D. As soon as it launched, it became the most popular gun of the year, beloved by mercenaries. But when faced with more complex situations, she will turn to a self-modified assault rifle, which is extremely accurate, powerful, and easy to assemble and disassemble quickly.'
'Uh huh.'
'Aside from those two commonly-used firearms, the presence of ships and armored vehicles in some extreme combat environments can pose serious difficulties. That's when she turns to a Raythean heavy-duty anti-armor/anti-ship cannon. And the accompanying tactical shield also takes mobility into account and can be used as a gun mount in addition to its basic protective function. Plus, the space inside the shield can be used to store additional small arms, ammunition, and other military equipment.'
'Uh huh.'
'But as you know, the battlefield is constantly shifting and requires thorough preparation each and every time, so Jessica tends to bring her entire arsenal with her, which greatly tests her load-bearing capabilities and arm strength. Now that she's out on the frontier, where the outdoor combat can be harsh and fierce bandits show up in convoys to rob supplies, she needs to carry not only her gear, but also extra supplies and—'
'Uh huh... So you're saying that's why you lost to her in 47 arm-wrestling contests in a row, even though you claim you can bench press 200 kilos. Gotcha.'
'......'
'Uh huh...?'
'Graaah––!'
––Excerpts from an everyday conversation between HR Operators

'Bernie Brynley and his wife already had a son and two daughters when they went on to have a third daughter in Jessica. As the family's youngest, everyone doted on her; not only were her parents extremely loving, but her brother and sisters were very close to her as well. There are reports that several of her promotions at Blacksteel were due to her family's support.
'While we don't know what sort of crime Jessica Brynley committed to get sent out to the frontier, it makes sense for a pampered rich girl who never learned right from wrong to be capable of just about anything. Yesterday, when confronted by doubtful reporters, Bernie Brynley still tried to defend his daughter, throwing his dignity to the wayside and screaming at them.'
'Bank robbery?! Where the hell did you hear that nonsense? Utterly ridiculous. Are you implying that there's a bank robber in MY family?'
'You'd best watch your mouth, sir. That's my daughter you're trying to slander!'
––Excerpts from the morning news of a Columbian TV station

'Their coverage of me was so one-sided.'
Turning off the TV, the girl looked back and addressed the operator behind her.
'Yeah, I agree. You're not like that at all, Jessica. Everyone here knows that.'
'No, that's not what I meant. They didn't even mention my grandfather, even though he was the one closest to me.'
'Huh? THAT'S what's bothering you?'
'Yeah. When he was with me, he didn't act like an elder at all, more like a playmate. When I was little, my favorite thing to do was sit in his arms and listen to him brag about his adventures out on the frontier, back when he was a soldier.
'Whenever he was done, he'd find his tie smeared with puree and cream. But that's just how it was. I was really little at the time. I was always eating, and would also crawl around all over the place... He really was the best grandfather ever.'
'What happened afterward?'
'Well... I grew up, and went off to secondary school in Victoria. Then he suddenly fell ill, and by the time I made it back home, he had already passed. I only had time to lay a bouquet of flowers in front of his tombstone.'
'I... I'm so sorry...'
'Don't apologize, I'm the one who brought it up. I'd never blame you for that.
'It's just nice having someone I can talk to about him...'
––Excerpts from a conversation between two operators while watching the morning news.

Everyone was shocked when they met Jessica out on the frontier. The girl in front of them was wearing coarse trousers and a plaid shirt, and behind her followed a neighing herd of burdenbeasts. She was riding barefoot on the lead beast, her skin flushed by the sun. If not for that familiar gun at her waist, nobody would've recognized that she was the same operator who used to work with us aboard the landship. After learning that we'd pass through the camp she was living in on our way to our destination, she offered to give us a ride. Quite fortunate for us, actually, since we were worried about damaging our vehicle at the time.
Atop the burdenbeasts, we headed up the river into a woodland. There, we discovered what life was like for her after leaving Blacksteel: in the middle of the night, several insects got through the tent's damage fabric. Be it the noisy buzzing of their wings or the itchy bumps from their bites, everyone was so fed up that they were swatting them one-by-one. But Jessica didn't seem to mind at all. She was simply curled up in a makeshift cot of two chairs pushed together, sleeping soundly. When an insect landed on her eyelid and left a huge bump behind, she simply rubbed it unconsciously before falling back into a deep slumber.
This one night was but a sliver of Jessica's hard-knock life. Not only did she need to deal with complex issues around the camp on a daily basis, she also had to deal with bandits and beasts periodically coming to harass her. Fortunately, she doesn't have to endure these things alone, as there are many people supporting her: the Elafia cook responsible for the camp's meals has exceptional skills, and even the most unpalatable ingredients are delicious in her hands; the old man tending the campfire has dexterous hands, and repaired our vehicle for us; there is also a girl there who is good with numbers, and is in charge of all the camp's finances; in addition, there's a Sankta hunter who's as good at herding livestock as he is ill-mannered, and he and Jessica take turns ensuring the security of the camp. Through everyone's mutual support, the newly-established camp quickly got on track and invited other pioneers to join.
Before we left, Jessica pointed to a forest in the distance and said this:
'We plan to buy a nice pine forest. On the frontier, logging is a relative secure industry, and good-quality white pine can be sold in a nomadic city for two hundred certs per cubic yard. That'll give us enough funds to build a small logging plate. Once we have a nomadic plate, everyone's lives will be that much better.'
As she spoke, her eyes let out a soft shine before becoming placid and calm again. During this whole exchange, her gaze remained fixed on that forest, not wavering for a moment.

modules.moduleDescription:
Holding her grandpa's hand, she climbs her way up onto the luxurious bureau.
'Alright, Jess, now before we start drawing, remember, first we clean our hands. No cake crumbs, no cookie crumbs.'
'I did! What are we gonna draw, Grandpa?'
'Ooh... lookit here, I got a certificate, from when ol' Grandpa came back from the frontier. But they forgot to draw me a darn picture of the place. How about you help me fill that in, Jessica?'
'Uhh... I've never been to the frontier, though...'
'Your brother and your sisters went a whole bunch with your dad, didn't they? They ever tell you what was out there?'
'They said the frontier's got nothing, but also said it's all... 'ripe for the picking.' I heard that, Grandpa, 'ripe for the picking,' but how do I draw it? I'm kind of lost...'
'Aw, heck, they love to teach you some strange old words. Say, forget that, how about you draw something the likes of which they've never seen. I'll teach you. Remember how I told you of the Seven Bastards of the wastes, those catapulting Liberi robbers?'
'Oh, yeah, yeah!'
'Remember what that big ol' cactus was shaped like?'
'Huge in every direction, like a mangler!'
'Remember why tumbleweeds make a good wild bonfire?'
'They're brambly and thin and they catch with a spark!'
'Remember how to ride a burdenbeast?'
'Pull the reins tight and straddle that saddle!'
'Attagirl, Jessica. You always wanted to know more, see more, just like your brother and sisters? You ask me, I bet my bottom dollar you'll be just like them once you're as grown up as them, oh the things you'll know and see. But Grandpa's personal little tales, I've not yet told a soul but you, Jessica. They don't know 'em—heck, your dad doesn't know 'em.'
'Okay! When they come back, I'll tell them, then I'll show them my picture, and it's gonna blow their socks off! 'Wow, Jessica, you heard stories we never got to hear!''
......
She pulls the burdenbeast's reins, straddles the saddle, and unfolds an old sheet of paper in the light of the sinking sun.
Just about below the edge of the wastes, its last warm rays shine through the paper. A sheen, she might swear, casts over faded fountain ink.
The old man trots his burdenback alongside her. She yanks the reins tight, and settles back in her seat.
'What's that you're peeking at, Jessica?'
'It's... a picture, something I drew when I was real young, of the frontier.'
'You came out here as a kid? Never mentioned that.'
'No, I just had someone describe it to me. Held my hand while I was drawing.'
'Not half bad, all things considered. Hell of a 'canvas' too.'
'This is his certificate, the one who showed me how to draw it. He was my grandfather.'
'Your grandfather. A hero of the states?'
'Yeah... a hero of the states. And a hero of mine.'

modules.moduleDescription:
'Jessica...'
She hid behind the sheriff, watching the unexpected visitor in the tent.
The man's clothes were tattered and his face dirty. He looked like a broken linen bag that had been dragged through mud. The desk had been ransacked.
'Stay away!'
The desperate man clutched his knife with black and withered fingers. There were black crystals on them.
She should be afraid, but she saw the sheriff lower her hand, very close to her gun.
She remembered how she ran into a mangler in the wild last month, which had surprised her with no time to react.
That's when she heard a loud crack, and saw the mangler fall lifeless to the ground. The sheriff then put her gun back in its holster, and pulled her into her embrace.
She was not afraid. She knew the sheriff could easily do to this man what she did to the mangler.
But the sheriff did not make a move.
'...Do you like cocoa?'
'...What?'
'The kids and I love it too. We always buy some whenever the caravans pass by. But the water in the bottle has gotten cool, hasn't it? Hot cocoa will taste better.'
Her eyes followed the sheriff's pointing finger. A mug sat serenely amidst the mess on the table, a small torn-open packet next to it.
'We're having barbecue and beer at the camp tonight. We'll have hot cocoa too. Would you care to join us?'
She heard the sheriff say to the man.

A new face joined the campfire that night.
'How'd you know he wasn't a bad guy?'
'I don't. That's why I'm keeping a close eye on him.'
'Mom said there are loads of bad people out on the frontier...'
'And loads of people who need help, too. Harsh weather, few supplies, dangerous wildlife... Life on the frontier is hard. People are scared, which is why they take up arms.'
The sheriff patted her head.
She had the same look in her eyes as when she closed the eyes of the mangler.
'Sometimes you don't get a choice. But right here, right now, where it's within my power... it's my hope that a cup of hot cocoa can do more than a bullet.'
The girl returned to the campfire, still harboring doubts.
At first, the man who may or may not be a bad guy simply devoured the food on his plate and glared at anyone who looked at him too long. But when the others began to sing, she saw him listening for a while before beginning to hum softly.
I wandered here alone, not a penny to my name♪
My hometown far behind me, miles and miles away♪

skins.name: A Picnic Before A Long Trip

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Were you looking for these documents, Professor? Here you are. I personally believe that some of these theories aren't explained in enough detail. If you wanted a springboard for your ideas, I suggest referencing these two papers. I've added some of my own commentary, so feel free to look it over.

The little lamb didn't go away even after the volcano erupted. It's actually been staying with me the whole time, and sometimes gets into trouble. H-Hey, you can't go standing on the Doctor's head! That's terribly rude! Sorry, Professor. Um, Can you see the little lamb? It's right here, hand to the right, and then down a little. Yeah, you're petting it right now.

This coat was Mom's old protective gear. Professor Keller once told me, this mark came from a sudden burst of magma. It almost left a scar on her, but Mom just laughed, saying she had good luck. If I were to go on an expedition with her, I'd probably need to be the one to lead.

Shh. Here, Professor, I snuck these over! I saw it all – you were muttering about how badly you wanted some snacks earlier, right? I've actually gotten pretty good at reading lips. Not to brag, but I might be better than Rhodes Island's intelligence agents by now. But, just maybe.

I'm getting ready to head out, Professor. Another volcano is about to become active. While luck is still on my side, I need to go a bit farther, a bit deeper. I want to wear the brightly-colored ornaments, and get to the truth in the hot magma, just like Mom and Dad did.

Professor, in a few days, I'll be going to Leithanien to attend a press conference and the premiere of my documentary. Our research is too obscure for the ordinary people who want to learn about volcanoes. But I still hope that one day, I can use this method to show everyone the beauty of volcanoes.

Frostleaf has been going to Mousse's book club a lot these days. Earthspirit and Provence have been trekking far and wide. I've been exploring more volcanoes... Professor, I still remember those early days, when Mousse was so nervous she couldn't even talk, and Frostleaf was always alone. But look at them now... they're getting better.

Hehe, Mr. Kahn's letter just arrived. He says he's really mad that Professor Keller and I went rowing on a sulfuric acid lake without protective gear. Mom and Dad did crazy things just like that before they had me, and they didn't bring Professor Keller along. So this time, so I took her with me!

One moment, Professor, I'm changing out my hearing aid battery. Hmm? You're... Did you forget, Professor? I can read lips now. Besides, the sign you want should be like this, then this. What you just did was 'I have been suppressed by the volcano.'
Phew... Even without my hearing aid, I can still pick up the little sounds of Professor's breathing…

Professor, I'm back, and I brought some souvenirs for you. I'll send them over to Dr. Kal'tsit and Amiya in a bit. I also managed to get a good amount of new data and specimens from Siesta's volcanic eruption. Would you like to come and take a look with me?
A volcano's every change and movement is fleeting. Only by capturing them on camera are we able to preserve every last detail.

Our documentaries are being taken seriously? That's great! During my inspections in recent years, I've seen a lot of governments that don't trust our judgment and won't allocate resources to evacuate the residents. I hope I'll be able to make a difference.
I know what you want to say, Professor, but I've never made my expeditions hard for myself. Starting from the smallest example, I bet you've never fried a fowlbeast egg over lava before, but I have!
How about a slice of lava cake before we head out? It was one of Mom's traditions.
Volcano field investigations are extremely dangerous. Everyone, please follow my instructions.
Please double check your protective gear. Also, remember to keep a safe distance from the lava, and give regular status reports.
Relax, volcano. We're just here to collect a few precious samples. Please don't get mad.
This time, we can make up for the missing data in the last report.
Don't worry about me, Professor. I've scaled a lot more volcanoes than you can imagine.
Volcanic soot contains lots of Originium particles. Let's not stay too long.
Magma will dredge up Originium veins. Keep your distance.
Melt away, life-depriving stone...
Ashes from volcanoes, they consume and erase, then nourish and propagate.
Those particles have no place here. I'll send them away.
Oh, flowing magma, please slow your steps.
We are one step closer to the truth of this land, Professor.
Perhaps there will still be people gazing across this volcano a century from now. Their footprints will cover ours, and the seeds buried beneath the ash will bloom into even more beautiful flowers...
Why…? I'm not seeing any errors in the formula or the data... Um? I think I see something surfing through the lava...?
Phew... Thankfully, the volcano didn't want to keep me that badly.
Professor, I brought the documents you asked me about.
I heard you coming, Professor. I recognized your footsteps.
Professor, I know how good you are at learning. I can tell you're doing the wrong sign on purpose just to make me laugh!
Arknights.

A pebble encounters countless other pebbles during its life. They will collide with each other and become magma. When they reach critical temperature, they erupt. In the end, they turn into the ash that nourishes new life. We're just like these little pebbles, Professor– Oh! Why didn't you tell me the fireworks already started?!
Professor, the fault lines of mountain ranges and trenches are quietly moving beneath our feet. Little by little, they inch us closer to the volcanoes we hope to visit.

The obsidian in this brooch comes from a volcano you haven't climbed yet. When you're not busy, we can go volcano-climbing. We'll visit the volcanoes one by one. And you'll know exactly which volcano I'm talking about once you get to the top. The scenery up there is magnificent, and the other half of your present is waiting for you.

Professor, I read in a book that after thousands of years, we will all re-enter this land's cycle. Maybe I'll become a little plume of magma, reshaping the land along its rock formations. When that time comes, I'll be able to forever look out across the land, with what nourished me, nestling up against me.

That's terribly rude! Sorry, Professor. Um, Can you see the little lamb? It's right here, hand to the right, and then down a little. Yeah, you're petting it right now.

This coat was Mom's old protective gear. Professor Keller once told me, this mark came from a sudden burst of magma. It almost left a scar on her, but Mom just laughed, saying she had good luck. If I were to go on an expedition with her, I'd probably need to be the one to lead.

Shh. Here, Professor, I snuck these over! I saw it all – you were muttering about how badly you wanted some snacks earlier, right? I've actually gotten pretty good at reading lips. Not to brag, but I might be better than Rhodes Island's intelligence agents by now. But, just maybe.

I'm getting ready to head out, Professor. Another volcano is about to become active. While luck is still on my side, I need to go a bit farther, a bit deeper. I want to wear the brightly-colored ornaments, and get to the truth in the hot magma, just like Mom and Dad did.

Professor, in a few days, I'll be going to Leithanien to attend a press conference and the premiere of my documentary. Our research is too obscure for the ordinary people who want to learn about volcanoes. But I still hope that one day, I can use this method to show everyone the beauty of volcanoes.

Frostleaf has been going to Mousse's book club a lot these days. Earthspirit and Provence have been trekking far and wide. I've been exploring more volcanoes... Professor, I still remember those early days, when Mousse was so nervous she couldn't even talk, and Frostleaf was always alone. But look at them now... they're getting better.

Hehe, Mr. Kahn's letter just arrived. He says he's really mad that Professor Keller and I went rowing on a sulfuric acid lake without protective gear. Mom and Dad did crazy things just like that before they had me, and they didn't bring Professor Keller along. So this time, so I took her with me!

One moment, Professor, I'm changing out my hearing aid battery. Hmm? You're... Did you forget, Professor? I can read lips now. Besides, the sign you want should be like this, then this. What you just did was 'I have been suppressed by the volcano.'
Phew... Even without my hearing aid, I can still pick up the little sounds of Professor's breathing…

Professor, I'm back, and I brought some souvenirs for you. I'll send them over to Dr. Kal'tsit and Amiya in a bit. I also managed to get a good amount of new data and specimens from Siesta's volcanic eruption. Would you like to come and take a look with me?
A volcano's every change and movement is fleeting. Only by capturing them on camera are we able to preserve every last detail.

Our documentaries are being taken seriously? That's great! During my inspections in recent years, I've seen a lot of governments that don't trust our judgment and won't allocate resources to evacuate the residents. I hope I'll be able to make a difference.
I know what you want to say, Professor, but I've never made my expeditions hard for myself. Starting from the smallest example, I bet you've never fried a fowlbeast egg over lava before, but I have!
How about a slice of lava cake before we head out? It was one of Mom's traditions.
Volcano field investigations are extremely dangerous. Everyone, please follow my instructions.
Please double check your protective gear. Also, remember to keep a safe distance from the lava, and give regular status reports.
Relax, volcano. We're just here to collect a few precious samples. Please don't get mad.
This time, we can make up for the missing data in the last report.
Don't worry about me, Professor. I've scaled a lot more volcanoes than you can imagine.
Volcanic soot contains lots of Originium particles. Let's not stay too long.
Magma will dredge up Originium veins. Keep your distance.
Melt away, life-depriving stone...
Ashes from volcanoes, they consume and erase, then nourish and propagate.
Those particles have no place here. I'll send them away.
Oh, flowing magma, please slow your steps.
We are one step closer to the truth of this land, Professor.
Perhaps there will still be people gazing across this volcano a century from now. Their footprints will cover ours, and the seeds buried beneath the ash will bloom into even more beautiful flowers...
Why…? I'm not seeing any errors in the formula or the data... Um? I think I see something surfing through the lava...?
Phew... Thankfully, the volcano didn't want to keep me that badly.
Professor, I brought the documents you asked me about.
I heard you coming, Professor. I recognized your footsteps.
Professor, I know how good you are at learning. I can tell you're doing the wrong sign on purpose just to make me laugh!
Arknights.

A pebble encounters countless other pebbles during its life. They will collide with each other and become magma. When they reach critical temperature, they erupt. In the end, they turn into the ash that nourishes new life. We're just like these little pebbles, Professor– Oh! Why didn't you tell me the fireworks already started?!
Professor, the fault lines of mountain ranges and trenches are quietly moving beneath our feet. Little by little, they inch us closer to the volcanoes we hope to visit.

The obsidian in this brooch comes from a volcano you haven't climbed yet. When you're not busy, we can go volcano-climbing. We'll visit the volcanoes one by one. And you'll know exactly which volcano I'm talking about once you get to the top. The scenery up there is magnificent, and the other half of your present is waiting for you.

Professor, I read in a book that after thousands of years, we will all re-enter this land's cycle. Maybe I'll become a little plume of magma, reshaping the land along its rock formations. When that time comes, I'll be able to forever look out across the land, with what nourished me, nestling up against me.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Mmm~I smell whipped cream. Look, the lambs have started their picnic over there. Care to join them with me, Professor?

Professor, would you like to try this cupcake I made? It's got a small piece of berry, some cream I scooped from a bigger cake, and the plate is a vine leaf… Why is there a lamb hiding in your hood...? This must be one of Dolly's pranks.

What do you think of my dress, Professor? Is the ribbon tied right? The lambs invited me to a party, but all they gave me to wear was a big ball of wool! Rather naughty of them, don't you think? It's been so long since I danced in a dress. I'm worried I might have some trouble. Would you mind practicing with me?

Hm? What was that, Professor? Sorry, I didn't quite catch that, please wait a second... My, how did this wool get in my ear? It must have slipped when I was playing hide-and-seek with the lambs! Go ahead, Professor, I can hear you now.

We've come pretty far, haven't we, Professor? A little fowlbeast brought me a rock from an acid lake. A little musbeast led me across an ocean of pink. And I even went aboard a great ship made of love and warmth. With these treasures, I don't feel at all lonely.

Do you like this cake, Professor? It's not just a regular cake. The base is made of love and dedication. The cream is distilled from our adventures. Various emotions are sprinkled as a finishing touch. And I've placed it in a box made of memories. It took me a long time to learn to bake a cake like this, Professor. I hope you'll remember the taste forever.
The little lambs can't wait to take us out to play again. What did you think of the chocolate lava in that volcano earlier? I much prefer the crystal candy from the thermal lake myself.

Phew. Looks like the sun's about to set. If only we could catch up with it, then the picnic could go on a little longer. How nice it would be if we could dance in a circle and sing. Pretty sun, warm sun, why you set so soon? Please stay, please wait, for time is such a boon♪

Cotton drifting on♪ We fly like clouds and chase the sun♪ Over the lava spout♪ We can't stop while the sun is out♪ Slow down if you please♪ You need to grant our wishes three♪ North Wind, make us rain♪ Bloom hot flowers from pebble grains♪
Shh... Listen carefully, Professor. That's the sound of flowers blooming... So soft and gentle. I'm glad I can hear it.
Is this a dream? A cozy, cloud-white dream?
I wonder if anyone recorded the picnics, too?
The flowers will not wither, and the sunlight will be forever warm. If only we could stay in this moment…
Look, professor! The hills are covered with Volcano Watchers! It's beautiful! Ah, mom and dad are there, too! Hm? You don't see them?
The picnic's about to begin.
Yes? You're putting me in charge of the picnic?
Come quick, Professor! There's still a ripe berry on that vine!
The little lambs say it's fun to roll around on the clouds. Do you think we can go for a picnic up there?
I hear fowlbeasts flapping their wings.
The rainbow bridge rises between the clouds.
The lava surges on, never turning back.
A pebble returns to her hometown.
A cotton candy cloud, drizzled in azure sky syrup.
A sweet-and-sour rainbow, dipped in golden sunshine.
A refreshing breeze, mixed into bubbling soda.
Sleep now, and fall into a sweet dream.
Hand in hand we stride, singing atop the gentle clouds.
Ring-a-ding-ding, when the flowers gently fall, the berries you can haul.
Oops, be careful now. Sudden shrinking takes some getting used to. Try not to trip and fall, okay?
Oh my, who knocked over the cake stand? The lambs' faces are covered in cream!
Can I bring the cake in?
Hey, quit it, little lamb. Oh, it's you, professor.
The lambs and I have matching bow ties. Aren't they pretty?
Arknights.

I think it's snowing on those hills in the distance… Are you cold, Professor? The fairy tales say you can spin snow into nice, soft robes. Those who wear them will sleep the gentlest of sleeps. I hope you too will have sweet dreams tonight.
Professor, since we've shrunk and the desserts haven't... Maybe we can keep eating as much as we want?

You've finally reached the top of the volcano, Professor. This is the view I've always wanted to show you... Why are you dreaming of me? Hehe, it's my way of telling you what I want to say. Happy birthday, Professor.

Mhmm... It's so quiet here. The sun is as warm as ever, and the breeze is always gentle. Professor, we may go on separate journeys from here, but don't worry. Even if we part ways for now, there will come a day when we meet again.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: 不行，我不想这么早睡觉，我们三个难得聚在一起，能不能再像小时候那样，挤在一起分享童话故事？我有一个故事想讲给你们听——是关于两朵暖洋洋的火山云的。
从前有两团云，一团背着沉沉的火山，另一团带着能遮挡雨水的小伞。它们不记得自己从哪里来，也不知道自己要去哪里，它们的心中只有一个念头：找到那颗不小心被它们弄丢的小石头。
两团云在大地上飘荡，询问了偶遇的航船，翻找过粉色的夕阳，终于，它们找到那颗小石头——它现在也是一朵小小的云了。接下来该怎么办呢？三朵云想了想，决定一起回到大地，变成赤红的花。
后来，高山变成湖泊，岩层断裂又张开，暖洋洋的火山云又回到了温暖的地下。它们在那里化成了一朵朵小小的岩浆，顺着岩层走过大地，永远依偎在彼此的身旁。
好啦好啦我的耳朵都要起茧子啦，我知道你们在学校里一直都是第一名和第二名，谁也不服谁这才认识的，怎么现在还在争呀？你们在我的心中都是第一名啦！不要再吵啦，一起看书吧！
文件就放在柜子上吧？噗，早上研讨会的介绍词念到“瑙曼教授、瑙曼教授，以及瑙曼博士”时，学校的老教授就忍不住笑了出来，等我也成为“瑙曼教授”，不知道那时的介绍人会不会舌头打结呢？
哎呀，妈妈，我现在还不想睡。你在我这个年纪已经完成了很多研究，而我现在却没能有这样的成绩，我担心自己永远也追不上你的脚步……一步一步来就好吗？呜……我会的。
咳咳，瑙曼教授，为了奖励你完成“每日陪阿黛尔学习源石技艺”这项任务，特此颁发奖状，奖品是——哎呀妈妈你别偷笑呀——一杯妈妈教我做的，专门加了榛子糖浆的热巧克力！
呼……我的童话讲完了，说完了所有想说的话，也喝到了热巧克力，我今天已经很满足啦……那么，我可以安心睡下了。晚安啦，爸爸妈妈。
……爸爸，妈妈，你们相信那颗小石头，她后来变成了漂亮的火山云吗？
欸，好困……爸爸妈妈，你们没做完的研究，我花了好久才全部完成的，我终于，终于……呼……呼……
相册里的这座火山我从没见过，将来我们还有机会一起去吗？
咦，奇怪，这次岩浆岩分布的状况和以往都不同，数据还有明显的波动……嗯？多利先生，不可以在采集样本的时候冲浪啦！
咳咳，今天是我被授予教授职称的日子，我一路追随着父母的脚步，我——哎呀我怎么在你们面前模拟一下都紧张了？爸爸妈妈不许笑我啦！
来啦来啦，童话书已经准备好啦。
小黑羊们，乖乖坐好，要听我的指挥哦！
就像小时候一起看童话那样，这次换我来为你们讲吧？
背着火山的云朵和带着雨伞的云朵诞生于岩浆，在天空中相遇。
“别担心，”它们说，“岩浆不会再烫伤我们。”
“往前走吧，”它们说，“搭乘上升的气浪。”
云朵飞啊飞，大地的心脏在它们的身下缓缓地跳动。
云朵飘啊飘，地壳的血液在它们的眼中静静地流淌。
一团小小的云朵，诞生在它们相拥的怀中。
“我们多么幸运……”两朵云无声地感叹。
“我们已然看到了最美的风景，还得到了最珍贵的宝物。”
它们相拥在一起，成为一片最灿烂的云霞。
而后，一位好奇的探险者踏上了那座灿烂云霞之下的火山。他惊喜地发现，原本布满砂石的山麓，不知何时开满了红色的花朵。
故事的最后，探险者在这里留下了一串脚印，他拍了拍身上的尘土，继续追随着前人的足迹，去往更高、更远的地方了。
唔，结局吗……我还没有想好，这个童话的结尾，交由明晚的我们继续想象吧？
哎呀小黑羊，想听故事就要乖乖坐好，不要打断我呀！
哈哈，我小时候在你们的办公室里画的涂鸦还在呀？
多利先生，不要再调皮了哦？
好吧我承认，是我偷吃了熔岩蛋糕，不要再挠我啦！
明日方舟。
哎呀，我想起来了！有一年你们在外面考察赶不回来，写信叮嘱我多看看窗外——我以为那是烟花，但回想起来，它们圆滚滚的，还会蹦来蹦去，其实是多利先生在陪我，逗我开心吧？
像小时候窝在沙发里，给我讲故事那样。
前辈，祝您生日快乐。这段时间，我正久违地和父母一起实地考察，还发现了不少罕见的标本，随信赠上一颗我发现的纯净黑曜石，希望它能把我的幸福也传递给您~
大地拥有的时光是如此地漫长，或许我们穷尽一生，都无法解开关于火山的所有谜题。等到我也变老了，我们的足迹会遍布全泰拉的火山吗？我们做的研究，会帮到更多的人吗？

handbook.profile: Eyjafjalla, Volcanologist and Catastrophe Messenger. In recent years, she has participated in the production of multiple documentaries and written and published multiple books on volcanoes. She continues to receive treatment at Rhodes Island and undertakes a variety of activities, including Catastrophe research, as needed.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Originium crystals distributed across surface of body, confirmed Infected by medical examination.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 11%
Occurrences of deafness and blurred vision have become more frequent.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.59u/L
With Rhodes Island having brought her condition under control, Operator Eyjafjalla's Blood Originium-Crystal Density has not seen a significant increase.

'Dr. Keller... My numbers haven't gone up. I'm not lying! We can't delay this field survey... Please! Believe me!'
handbook.promotionRecord:
Eyjafjalla's health isn't the best right now, but she still insists on climbing the Unna Volcano.
As her assistants, there was nothing we could do to talk her out of it...
Even before we reached the mountain, she was already starting to pass out from fatigue. She couldn't even hear us warning her. I know that Unna has seen a clear fluctuation across all indicators, and it's in prime observation condition, but pushing herself like that without regard for her own health is clearly against the most basic rules she taught us herself.
Worried about her, we've been following her.
The residents of the village all seem to know her very well. While still at the foot of the mountain, we rested a little and reorganized. Perhaps I should've tried to talk to her again...
......
We finally made it to the summit, but Eyjafjalla didn't start recording data right away.
Instead she dug a shallow hole and buried... a small rock.
Is something going to grow from this?
There are also the garlands of flowers she's been holding onto the whole time, and she kept hugging them tight even though she almost tripped a couple times. But suddenly, those two garlands just up and fluttered away. What a shame! Even though there wasn't any wind at all.
Still, I don't think I've ever seen her look so gratified...
archives:
After returning from her trip, Eyjafjalla slowly recounted to her fellow operators all her experiences during her time away. And when telling those stories, each and every piece of volcanic rock has an interesting factoid behind it: rocks with lots of holes can float in water, and sometimes even make noise; the distribution of obsidian is closely related to magma activity, and their hidden luster has other meanings to it; etc.
At the same time, our operators have also noticed that, while her hearing loss used to be a barrier to communication, it has since become much easier to talk to her. Whenever they tell her that her condition must have improved, she just keeps smiling as she always does and tells them with a bit of pride that, while her hearing has deteriorated to the point where she can now only hear with hearing aids in a quiet environment, they're finding it easier to talk to her because she learned to read lips.
'Hearing aids really don't help me understand that much anymore, so I usually rely on both them and lip reading to understand what everyone is saying. Is it that hard to tell if you're not watching for it?
'Sometimes, after I tell others about my condition, they start to look at me kind of differently. It's not that I want to be treated differently or earn anyone's sympathy. All I really need is for everyone to interact with me as usual.'
The worrying thing is that we occasionally have operators visit Medical and tell us that they saw her talking alone by herself, and that she sometimes even seemed a little angry. They were afraid to interrupt her, but were nonetheless worried that perhaps her condition has worsened in some strange way...

Few are aware of the concept of a 'Sovereign of Beasts.' When interacting with humans, they are usually treated as either a human with distinctive traits or some kind of supernatural ruler. The natural characteristics demonstrated by these Sovereigns are also quite distinct from Terra's existing creatures. Recently, there has also been a string of strange occurrences aboard Rhodes Island, and we surmise that this is the work of a Sov■■■ (A long string of sheep hoofprints can be seen here; the letters are illegible)
—■■■(Another string of hoofprints}

'Skyfire told me they were scared to death when I got lost in the wilderness again, but they didn't expect me to suddenly appear out of nowhere in the crossroads they were in, alone. But I had a pink, fluffy critter lead me there. It even took a bite out of my book!'
'Pink, fluffy critters? They've been showing up whenever I play my guitar! Gotta say, they have great taste in music. Even when I'm jamming out in the wind, they stand out there with me, up against the gales and unleashing life! Wish they'd stop eating my strings, though.'
'Outta the way, outta the way~ Metal Crabs coming through~ These chubby little guys seem to be having a lot of fun with somebody lately; their body weight is back to normal now! I even found these pink furballs stuck to their claws. Any of you know whose pet they belong to?'
—Rhodes Island Cafeteria audio recording

Warning
Following the disappearance of instruction materials and food stockpiles in September, the instructors have found the following discipline violations during the October inspection:
Using Originium Arts to play with toys, suspending them midair and sending them flying around; the inexplicable disappearance of ice cream ingredients meant for classes; skateboarding on the deck outside of set hours and hiding as soon as the instructors arrive.
Offending operators should report to the instructors' office immediately to acknowledge and rectify their mistakes, as well as uphold all rules and regulations to prevent further offenses.
—Dur-nar

Give me my motherf■■in' limited edition vinyls back!
—■■ (Unknown penguin footprint on the wall)

A few days later, after a significant increase in incidents involving 'strange pink silhouettes,' Eyjafjalla had no choice but to leave her laboratory and spend what little time and energy she has dealing with the problems caused by the stealthy sheep, apologizing to everyone one-by-one, and helping everyone touch those invisible mischievous animals.
That said, it's apparent that she's also enjoying this.

Dr. Kahn:
You have my sincerest gratitude.
I know that if it weren't for your assistance in the beginning, I would likely not have received such quality healthcare. Over the past few years, I have persistently worked to complete the volcano expedition. I feel that as a volcanologist and a daughter taking over her parents' unfinished research, this is a life goal I must complete. In spite of your numerous letters, I have insisted on continuing down this path, and I apologize for making you worry.
I also know that you have been trying to uncover the truth of all those years ago, and that you've been protecting me time and again by trying to keep me from getting too involved. If it weren't for your persistence and care, I would never have learned what actually happened back then. Although the vacation itself may have helped alleviate my worries, it was you, the truth that you worked so hard to give me, and Dr. Keller's frankness in the end that truly gave me the relief I needed.
I will come visit you in Leithanien in the near future. My mother used to tell me that you would sometimes be upset when your experiments went wrong, and that you'd need my parents to bring a cake to your lab to comfort you... I really want to tell you that we can't completely prevent accidents. All we can do is hold on to every meaningful bit of time we have. I really hope you were able to finally calm down, and that you could tell me any old stories about my parents.
—Adele

Adele:
I have given this a lot of thought, but I finally decided to write you this letter. I want you to know that I am truly grateful to you.
I had decided many years ago that I would never again climb a volcano, and that this museum would be my final memento to Magna and Katia.
At first, I invited you to participate in the museum and Mt. Siesta's affairs because my work required it, and also because you are Magna and Katia's child. I had intended to retire from all research and work pertaining to volcanoes after bringing this matter to completion. I couldn't face you, nor could I face Kahn's question. I had been wondering: if I'd chosen to make them stay as well, would they not have been caught in that pyroclastic flow and lost their lives? However, I never expected you to have never questioned my involvement nor resented me.
I'm sorry, Adele. I was too harsh on you before, and it was partly because I was afraid I'd be reminded of the time I spent with your parents. My memories with them were once a heavy burden to me, but thanks to you, I can finally bring myself to put them into words again, and share them with you as simply fun anecdotes.
I await your next letter, and am preparing for our next expedition together.
—Keller

Upon her return to Rhodes Island, Eyjafjalla immediately began to gather all the data she had kept at Rhodes Island and send them to Siesta's Volcano Museum, as well as prepare for future joint research projects with Lady Keller. Naturally, we were a little worried. After all, she had been working with volcanoes both from closer distances and more often over the past few years, all to complete the project that her parents were unable to finish. This is no doubt detrimental to her health. Our Medical operators often tried to talk her out of participating in surveys, but she would always tell us a story she heard when she was still a child: of a sickly scientist bedridden with illness, but who didn't hesitate to spend what little strength she had left to continue her research. In the end, she reached a conclusion, and closed her eyes. She asked us a question: If you were that scientist, at the final days of your life, would you rather climb a summit or spend your remaining time in bed, peacefully with your family? We were unable to give Eyjafjalla an answer, but perhaps her answer would be to achieve both. Compared to others who've made significant breakthroughs in the field of volcanology, she is still very young. Some races can live past a hundred years, perhaps even longer, while others live a much more fleeting life. However, the length of one's life does not determine its worth. Judging from the data and research papers she's managed to put together in her dorm room, we can't help but be awestruck at how much she's already fit into her short life, and she is continually adding more. 'There are many secrets hidden across the lands under our feet. Each insignificant rock has endured far more time than even the oldest Savra. 'Underneath layers upon layers of strata, there is a chamber of magma that is ever flowing at unimaginable temperatures, while the strata themselves are slowly moving and constantly crushing one another. We once made the bold assumption that perhaps the seas were once tall mountains, and that the earth currently beneath our feet could perhaps have once reached even the clouds above. When, after traveling hundreds of thousands of miles, the earth that once saw the skies, or the bottom of the ocean, finally encounters its compatriot, they release a most radiant and blazing light. 'Throughout this process, my parents lifted their heads and pondered just what exactly it is that boils our lands' bloodstreams. And now, I am following their footsteps and walking the path they once did, to seek an answer from the land. The footsteps of future generations will likewise trample over ours as they continue down this path. 'This is the meaning of our lives.' —The opening monologue of the volcano documentary One Step After Another, as narrated by Eyjafjalla

modules.moduleDescription:
[Recording: Bubbling lava]
Title: Volcano's Breathing
Description:
When the Mount Siesta stopped erupting, Professor Keller and I climbed up the volcano once again to finish our last data collection.
After we recorded this sound of bubbling lava, Professor Keller suddenly suggested that we sit for a while at the mountaintop.
She gazed at the already ash-grey Siesta and I saw her eyes swell up with tears. She mentioned something about the future of the Volcano Museum of Siesta and her plans for retirement, which would very likely be delayed. I knew that she wanted me to visit Siesta as much as possible in the future—not just for research.

[Recording: Singing with music]
Title: Singing at a Cake Shop
Description:
It's been a while since I last came back, and I had this feeling that this little town was stuck in time and nothing was ever going to change.
However, I accidentally noticed that the cake shop Mom used to like so much had finished its renovation and reopened. A lot of musicians even came to the courtyard, holding impromptu performances.
I heard a very familiar melody that day and went up close, and the singer invited me to join them! *Sighs* It was a pity I couldn't remember the lyrics and wasn't quite sure which part everyone was singing, so I just struggled to hum along... Hope I wasn't off-key too much.

[Recording: An academic talk]
Title: On-campus Seminar
Description:
I brought the data from Mount Siesta back to Wilhelm University and met with Dr. Kahn and other scholars there. Dr. Kahn seemed a little unsettled. I told him it was not a big deal, but by the looks of it, that wasn't much help.
Thankfully, after some small talk, we started discussing research on volcanoes, and Dr. Kahn finally found peace and became more relaxed.
The seminar was exciting. No one seemed to care that we were not in a classroom, laboratory, or meeting room, but just standing on a path on campus.
It felt really nice.

[Recording: Ripped audio from a childhood video]
Title: I Still Remember That Wish
Description:
I left the university and came back home.
I changed the curtains, threw away some old stuff I didn't need anymore, and found a childhood video in the process. It was a shame that most of the content was damaged. Fortunately, the soundtracks were intact, so I got to rip them and re-record them onto this tape.
I heard Mom and Dad singing me the birthday song and encouraging me to make a wish. Of course, I didn't say it out loud, but I still remember it—
Now I'm on my way to making it come true.

[Recording: Friends' laughing]
Title: A Welcome Party For Me!
Description:
I returned aboard for my regular check-up after settling everything at home. It'd been a long time since I last left Rhodes Island, and guess what? People held a welcome party for me!
Provence and Angelina caused a little chaos when they set off the firework tubes and accidentally knocked down a huge pile of dolls. Then next thing I remember was little lambs coming from nowhere and rampaging all about... It was a disaster. But everyone was laughing so hard.
I really hope these kinds of moments can last longer.

[Recording: N/A]
Title: Untitled
Description:
For the next field investigation.
I'd love to keep more recordings if I have the chance—the sound of lava, wind, rain, and the people around me.

modules.moduleDescription:
[Name] Marshmallow 3
[Description] Radiation-induced mutations in Volcano Watchers stable after four generations of selective breeding, resulting in an early floral transition phenotype that retains positive traits of the original lineage, allowing for transplant during the flowering period. Rapid color change in stem cross-section observed when soil Originium levels above threshold, allowing for quicker detection of impending volcanic eruption compared to previous petal observation method.
[Cultivation and Management] To ensure sample quality and quantity, and to maintain consistency with field environment, the research team employed genetic resource preservation, with regular cultivation managed by specialists with the support of Wilhelm University's College of Geology and the Rhodes Island office in New Siesta. Regular reviews are still required to ensure smooth cultivation and breeding. See the appendix for details.
[Addendum] Staff reported that some kind of creature had been chewing the plants, but nothing appeared on the camera feeds. After a review, Adele provided the following recommendations:
1. Put fresh grass, fruit, and ice cream on a dining table. There should be different fruits and ice cream each day, with no repetition in any given week;
2. Keep the break room TV on at all times. Tune it to Siestan Traffic at 8 A.M., Volcano's Kitchen (Junior Edition) at noon, and Love in Siesta at 8 P.M. daily (program updated on a regular basis);
3. Check your personal belongings daily; if anything is missing, place extra marshmallows on the dining table the following day and check your own pocket the day after. Report and hand in any unknown items you find.
For staff members who were still skeptical, Adele left these words—
'There's no malice in it; they're just curious. Sometimes I can't help but think... The lava running down the mountainside when a volcano erupts is like the land's exposed blood vessel. You can almost hear a massive heart beating underground, trying to tell us something, only we don't understand yet. Perhaps they, like us, are hoping that these flowers will grow and evolve, and translate the language of Terra for us.'

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Alright, chop chop. Finish your work during your coffee break so the rest of your day is all coffee break!
It's a holiday, so of course I gotta dress a little more casual. I may not have taken as many field missions these past few years, but I still passed the L.G.D.'s physical exams, in high heels.

If Rhodes Island's looking for business partners, you can definitely trust these companies. Hey! Why are you looking at me like that? I'm just genuinely listing off my recommendations. You're making it look like I'm plotting a hostile takeover of Rhodes Island. If I'm actually planning an M&A... I just need to talk you round, right?

Ahem... I've taken a glance at our recent mission records. Looks like Rhodes Island's tactics have got more professional over the past few years. Not bad, not bad... Excuse me?! What's wrong with your former training consultant checking your operators' records? I absolutely have not been looking at Ch'en's files!

It's not really a big deal, being L.G.D. chief. I've got a little more on my shoulders, a little more to worry about, and I can put myself in Ch'en's shoes a little more now... Oh, let me reiterate: I'm taking over the L.G.D., not taking over for Ch'en! If that stupid Lung came back right now, she'd have to call me 'Chief.'

I may have left my family's company, but I still deal in business every now and then. It's a way to build Lungmen, so there's no need to avoid the subject. And now that I've figured out what I need to do, I don't find my grandfather so scary anymore. Hmhm, Once you've made use of your fears, that's when you've truly conquered them, right?

The new Siesta's an interesting place. Even without its beaches and volcano, it's still worth a visit for its sky pools and natural springs. My investment there has resulted in pretty decent returns too. Doctor, if you find the time, you should go and see for yourself. Heading back to a place you haven't been in a while... might be just like a reunion with an old friend.

Things are looking up for the trading company I'm running with Bison. Transporting one country's goods to another, sharing the cultures of places afar, these are the charms of commerce. Many are afraid of breaking barriers, but, Doctor, I'm sure we can find common ground.

Is this the last document you have? Alright! You really kept me waiting this time, but finally, time for supper! I know this new place that's not so bad. It's on me tonigh—Oh, You don't want me spending money? Umm... alright, then it's on you. I know some other places.
Rawr... Ahem... You finished your work?

handbook.profile:
Swire, Commissioner of the Lungmen Guard Department.
Returning from her holiday in Siesta, she is currently providing Rhodes Island assistance in her capacity as a private individual, and based on her own judgment.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Swire shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.13u/L
Operator Swire rarely comes into contact with Originium.
handbook.promotionRecord:
Lungmen Guard Department Letter of Appointment
Per resolution, Beatrix Schwire is hereby appointed the Commissioner of the Lungmen Guard Department.
It is my wish that you uphold the public order in Lungmen and the peace enjoyed by its citizenry. 
Signed
Wei Yenwu, Chief of Lungmen

Swire holds the thin letter of appointment in her hand and solemnly puts it away in her drawer. The thinness of the paper and the simplicity of its words weighed heavily in her hands.
archives:
Compared to before her promotion to L.G.D. Commissioner, Swire has had little opportunity to visit Rhodes Island, and the few visits she does make have been relatively shorter. In the Training Room, she often simply gives a few words of advice to the training operators, and completely dodges any mention of Lungmen when conversing our operators. At most she occasionally brings up the logistics company she and Bison founded together in Siesta, as well as her magnum opus there—the waterpark.
But ever since she was promoted to commissioner, she rarely seems to show up together with Operator Hoshiguma.
Some veteran operators couldn't help but wonder if her promotion created a rift between the two, but every time the subject is brought up, she would suddenly get emotional and complain that although Hoshiguma seems like last person to mind such formalities, she'd always call her 'Commissioner Swire,' both in public and private. Even when the two of them happen to bump into each other at the elevators, Hoshiguma intentionally avoids her with a solemn expression, instead of accompanying her. This has left Swire dumbfounded. Although Hoshiguma has always dismissed this as a method to avoid arousing suspicion, Swire clearly did not accept this answer.
Out of an abundance of caution, our operators now restrict the topics of their everyday conversations to Lungmen's dining scene. Supposedly, Swire recommends places ranging from local street stalls to high end restaurants with exorbitant prices. While on deployment in Lungmen, our operators sometimes catch her having late night snacks at the street stalls. They would merely wave at each other before going back to their meals, with the lights of the L.G.D. Commissioner's office illuminating the night sky in the distance.

Swire isn't one to shy away from talking about her investments in Siesta.
She once just happened to walk by Engineering with her waterpark expansion blueprints in tow and ask for some free tips, completely going against any business logic. She also met up with Snowsant as she was returning from a field mission, told her she 'wanted the chief designer to participate in the ribbon cutting ceremony,' and shoved a few more designs into her hands while she was at it.
Under her leadership, her waterpark was successfully built to blueprint, and has proven to be no less exciting than the Obsidian Festival. It draws crowds of visitors with no end in sight, and there are even plans to expand. Thanks to this one trip, Snowsant managed to finally amass the funding she's been trying to obtain for years—as well as a multitude of design patents—while Swire and Bison have at last found their footing in Terra's cutthroat international logistics and trade industry.
Mountaincomm Trade is currently in a period of stable expansion, and their international business's success in Siesta has given the two young entrepreneurs the confidence to continue. Their next stop, Lungmen—Yan's most important commercial port—is also waiting to be taken to new heights. Though compared to their ultimate goal of connecting all the lands together, the two of them are merely taking a small step forward. However, this one, firm step has already roused the echoes of time.
'What's the point in following the older generation's asses only to fight over what they leave behind? If I'm getting into business, I may as well break into a new market. I can do more than uphold the order in Lungmen. I have the power to build it.'
The many parties within the Lungmen Chamber of Commerce are even now bickering amongst themselves. Even the scaffolding used to build Siesta's new towers is covered with their corporations' names in large letters. Siesta is facing a transition, and so is Swire. And both have satisfactory answers to offer.

On her journey home from Siesta, Swire received a total of three letters.
One was neat and stately, with heavy strokes that nearly penetrate the paper.
'Adams has read your last letter. He was elated, and he both approves of the Mountaincomm Trade business and has high expectations of you.'
......
'However, considering that you now hold an important position, it is paramount that you exercise prudence, maintain the appropriate demeanor, and refrain from making any ostentatious displays in public. This should go without saying. Now that your vacation is over, I must ask that you return to your duties at the L.G.D. with all haste.
'Further, your grandfather's condition has been deteriorating by the day. He is eager to see his granddaughter. Please pay him a visit as soon as possible.'
—Wei Yenwu
Another has beautiful handwriting, and even the paper itself gives off a pleasant aroma.
'I heard that your grandfather coughed up blood and fainted while watching your childhood tapes. I visited him in the hospital, but he was asleep. The doctor wasn't very optimistic about his condition.
'I know you two have never gotten along, but blood is thicker than water. There must be something he wants to tell you before he goes. Stop playing around all day and come back to see him as soon as you can. Think of it as giving yourself closure. You owe yourself that much. Don't end up regretting your decisions.'
—Lin Yühsia
Another letter has strokes as heavy as the first, though its handwriting is much cruder. The sender also practically dove towards Swire with the letter.
'Nei zek laan taan mao, I heard you pissed nei ah je off so much that he just up and zau maai?!'
—Hoshiguma

Swire held Hoshiguma down, and then continued her journey to Lungmen.
The conversation in that extravagant sickroom between Swire and Old Mr. Schwire, her grandfather, will forever remain a secret to everyone else. However, the moment she closed the door, a satisfied laugh could be heard in the hallway, creeping through the door.
A few months later, Swire, his heir apparent, announced she would leave the Schwire Group. That afternoon, she attended the Lungmen Guard Department's promotion ceremony and was promoted to the role of commissioner—the police chief.

There is a desk in the L.G.D. senior superintendents' office that has sat empty for two years. Thanks to Swire's promotion, there will now be another empty desk. When the last senior superintendent left, she didn't take any of her belongings with her. This time, Swire put them all away in a paper box labeled with the name of their owner: Ch'en Hui-chieh.

Catalogue of Desktop Items
Ch'en Hui-chieh:
Felt-tip pen, previous years' documents pertaining to the Lungmen Infected, water cup.
Swire:
Business contract, letter from Lin, evidence bag, L.G.D. holiday attendance schedule, police work policy adjustment suggestions, situation analyses...
Also a bowl of finball soup, still hot; I'll bring it over in a moment.

The officers sometimes privately discuss how Swire's leadership compares to Ch'en's. Superintendent Ch'en always led the charge, and always capably divvied up the tasks among everyone. Those who worked under her would breathe a long sigh after missions and find themselves unable to loosen up for the better part of a day. On the other hand, Swire requires everyone to handle multiple tasks at once, but all the officers agree that, even at their most busy, the work is never unmanageable. No matter how many problems there are, they can always feel a clear through line in their work. This line threads together every problem and reaches the core of it all. But long story short, 'It's like both of them have eight brains each. If I were in their position, I'd be dead the first day on the job.'
Aside from her work at the L.G.D., Mountaincomm Trade, which Swire founded with Bison, has expanded rapidly from only a small factory in a corner of Lungmen, allowing the city to gain an even firmer foothold in Terra's international trade as Yan's premier city of commerce. Lungmen's public order and economy are both undergoing rapid development. Swire still sits in her office, and her desk is just as messy and cluttered as before, but no one would ever claim that she got where she is because of the Schwire Group's backing, or that she took over for somebody. She is where she deserves to be, and is doing a terrific job, too.

'Young Ch'en's chase may have guided her onto a different path, but it's clear that this girl is a better fit for the role... The kids have their own paths to walk, and they're all well on their way now. Remember how you were worried sick all those years ago? Now you'll admit they're capable, right?'
'She is indeed doing a fine job. I can rest easy knowing the L.G.D. is in her capable hands.'
'You should watch your back, though. She might even be eyeing your Lungmen Chief seat.'
'She'll have to work much harder for it, then. Us old bones aren't THAT old yet—Hey, your beard got in my bowl!'
—A casual conversation between two old men drinking tea in Lungmen's night market

modules.moduleDescription:
'With unsurpassed strategic thinking, a mindset for acute initiative, and an attitude showing they care about the human side of things, Mountaincomm Trade has opened up international markets, injecting new life into Siesta's economy and marketplace. I quote Beatrix Schwire's own words—the value of business is in building connections, and the greatest activity a business can undertake is connecting with the future.'
—Award speech, Siesta's 1099 Annual Award for Outstanding Figures in Business
Ceylon Doykos personally awarded Swire this medal at Siesta City Hall's annual dinner, and now it's just one of a jumble of keepsakes she's brought back from Siesta to Lungmen.
'You went to Siesta for a holiday, and took this home with you?' Hoshiguma asks curiously, poring over the Columbian on the certificate.
'The greatest activity a business can undertake is connecting with the future'—I'm putting that in my autobiography.'
'This certificate really tells a wild story... And you managed to do all this in just under two months? What does 'opened up international markets' mean exactly?'
'Siesta's coffee beans were moving slow this year, so I made a few friends and sold off a massive shipment to Kazimierz—did you want to try some? I still have some in my bag.'
'And can you translate 'an attitude that shows they care about the human side of things'?'
'I did a little investing, and got the volcanic hot springs there transformed into a waterpark. Everyone seemed to take quite a liking.'
'Okay, and 'a mindset for acute initiative' refers to...'
'There were an awful lot of firms warring for Siesta's urban construction. Winning the final bid obviously took doing a little something to stand out.'
'So how did you win?'
'On vacation. Which is where that story is staying.'
'Uh-huh...'
'Stop reading that and help me sort my gifts out. This surfboard is for you, here's a volcanic mud cleanser for that stinky rat, here's a vinyl for that puk gaai lung—you know what, she can fetch it herself when she gets back—and here's some fruit cans for old Wei...'
The two spend all afternoon sorting through the pile of memorabilia, until finally, the only thing left lying forlornly on the ground is that medal.
'Are you putting this on display? I don't know, your cabinet's already full with all your other awards...'
'Forget it, this one can be a present for that sick old tiger—I'm visiting the hospital tomorrow, so I'll just give it to him myself.' Swire puts the medal away in her handbag, then stretches delightedly.
'As the representative of Lungmen's future, I'm going to go connect with him.'

modules.moduleDescription:
Pinned Casual Chat Group (4)
16:26
Guma: i'm hungry. what's for dinner?
Swire: Let's eat somewhere nice. How about the Lungmen Grand Hotel at 8:00 PM? You guys have to try their new poon choi. It's made traditionally, but the ingredients come from a new trade route that Mountaincomm Trade just opened. You'll get flavors from Rim Billiton to Sargon, and it's all super fresh. It even comes with a bottle of wine from Sami!
Swire: Bison and I worked really hard to get this supply line up and running, so you all have to come! @Stinky Rat
Stinky Rat: Am I invited?
17:09
Guma: i'm starving. can we just go now?
Swire: There aren't any seats yet. Have a snack to tide you over!
18:32
Guma: so hungry...
19:20
Guma: starving...
19:58
Stinky Rat: Something just came up. You guys eat first.
20:08
Swire: Huh?
Swire: What about Hoshiguma?
20:23
Swire: It's been ages since we all last met up—we HAVE to eat together. Finish up whatever it is you're doing, then decide where we're going to eat!
20:41
Swire: So, what are we gonna eat?
21:19
Swire: What are we eating tonight???
Swire: Lin Yühsia, I can see you on read! Hurry up and pick a place!
Stinky Rat: I just finished up. Besides, you're the one who put out that 'Director Swire's Lungmen Food Guide'. It's been blaring nonstop on TV for three days. And I'm the one that has to pick the restaurant?
Guma: sorry, emergency mission. done now. i'll eat whatever, as long as there's meat. i'm so hungry i could eat a burdenbeast
Stinky Rat: How about the night market? 'Right next to the shopping district, featuring specialty items from all over Terra. Shop at all of Terra, only in Lungmen!' Pretty good marketing copy, don't you think?
Swire: Great choice! I have to promote my work, after all!
Guma: doesn't sound like much meat. pass
Swire: The volcanic mud cleansing face mask I gave you is on sale there too, @Stinky Rat. And the surfboard @Guma.
Swire: Bison and I bargained day and night, and now they cost almost the same as they do in Siesta. Smart, huh?
Guma: don't wanna eat a surfboard
Stinky Rat: How about the Global Commerce Park? It's second on your food guide list.
Swire: That could work. We're working to attract investors over there, and we have a lot of international vendors now. The food's good too.
Guma: i want meat, and that's over half an hour away. i'll starve on the way
Swire: Well that's a shame. Young folks love that place—it's a top date spot!
Stinky Rat: Enough!
Stinky Rat: Final offer: the noodle cart behind the L.G.D. station. If that's no good, you two can starve.
Guma: fine by me
Swire: Fine by me.
21:30
Swire: Wait, Lin Yühsia, how did you get my food guide? Weren't you complaining about my TV ads?
Stinky Rat: I just grabbed one. Is that a problem?
21:33
Stinky Rat: How come the noodle cart isn't on your food guide?
Swire: I wanted to include it, but the owner refused. He said something about how he didn't want his humble stall to be viewed as a sellout and lose its authenticity.
Swire: Which is great, in my opinion. In the end, that's what Lungmen is all about.
21:38
Guma: i've already ordered. hurry up
23:35
Guma: why hasn't chen read a single message?
Swire: Try the intercity net. She's probably standing on a pile of hay in the middle of nowhere, holding up her terminal to catch a signal.
—New Message—
Puk Gaai Lung: ...
Puk Gaai Lung: It's a pile of rocks.
Puk Gaai Lung: I'm back in Lungmen. I'm up for noodles.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Close your eyes, don't rush to open them. They may feel slightly hot, that's normal... Shh, stay calm, I crushed some herbs to help your eyes relax. You must have been staring at some dangerous thing. I do that a lot, trust me.

A guide...? I guess Simone is a better fit for the job. She's also a veteran hunter like me, so I know you'll be in good hands, and won't get into... trouble. There have been some misunderstandings and a few tribes now turn me away. Just remember, if anyone tells you I'm a man eater, they're lying.

Hands off. I've told you before, no one gets to touch my bow. Not you, not the smiths. You don't have the skills to hunt shadows in the depth of Sami, so you shouldn't draw their attention. I know your kind, I know you're curious. I'll just repeat myself over, over, and over again until I get through to you.

Check the logs from the research teams. See? These little hornbeasts are friends, they're harmless. And this kind of snow needs Arts to control, so call me if you run into some. Good, go ahead and add some notes to these pictures, you're pretty clever. Why the look? Is it so strange that I know how to use electronics?

You all are strange, just like Magallan, insisting on comprehending the land on your own terms. I've seen your hard work, you'll come to know the whole of Sami as you see her in your dreams someday.
