What are you looking at me for? You want to hear my opinion, or no? Hmph. Who knows, I could've said you did a pretty good job.
I smell danger—did someone spray perfume? No? Then we've got enemies on our tail, so let's move it.
Too bright! I need a cubby-hole with no light on it… That's how I like it, got a problem?
Have you washed your hands? I'm not being difficult, I just finished organizing my collection, you know. And you should probably go wash them again in a moment.
No comment. Yeah, you didn't ask yet, but that doesn't affect my answer… Oh, fine, you look like you're dying to ask, just ask—no, seriously, what were you going to ask? Tell me!
Arknights.

I'm not a fan of kholodets or pirozhki on New Year's, but I do like the tradition where you write your wish on a piece of paper and burn it. I used to write 'somewhere to live', and then I met Antosha. Then I changed it to 'a full belly', and now I'm here. What do I write these days? I'm not telling you!
This is strange, I feel like someone's staring at me… Oh, just in time! Look, can you check if something's weird with your desk humidifier? Nothing? No way, no way, my intuition's always correct!

*sigh* You found me. I was trying to leave this here before you got to the office. Here, it's a rag doll, I sewed it to look like you. Isn't it cute? I know you're looking out for me all the time, so happy birthday! What do you mean you're not used to me talking this way? Hey! Explain that to me!

'Path'. That's a word Antosha kept teaching to me. He wanted to explain the meaning inside of it, but Matvey would never let him—he always said just being told it wouldn't help you understand it. You have to see it and walk it for yourself. Doctor, I've seen a lot on Rhodes Island, and I want to keep walking a long way still.

EN.voiceText: Me, your assistant? You want to split your work with a sick little girl? Even if she can't read well? Or are you just keeping an eye on me in case I cause another fuss? No, I'm not complaining. You're the boss.

How come you're so much taller than me? If I stare at you really hard while you're napping, will you get nightmares? Would you even notice? Tch, that's no fun. Can you give me some thumbtacks to play with? I promise you won't feel them—*ahem* I promise I won't stick them in you!

It's super stuffy in the mobility layer of Deity Grypherburg. I used to go down there to clean the Originium piping, and I found tons of dead beetles and butterflies—it's okay, I don't have them on me. *sigh* I was so dumb when I was little. I used to think I had it better than a bug. But being down there just proves we had it the exact same.

I don't want to talk right now. I'm not moody, I'm just—I'm tired or something, okay? I'm thinking, it's nothing to do with you. I don't want any snacks, stop talking to me! *sigh* Now I lost my train of thought! Show me what snacks you've got? Never mind, wanna go to the vending machine and buy something?
Bored, bored, bored. Why is all this 'paperwork' the saaaame? Is this all you ever look at all day…? I pity you. Wanna play marbles? No, these are mine, they're not for you, go get your own.

This fowlbeast doesn't have a name. What do you mean 'why'? It's not my pet, and it's not being sold at market. Why does it need a name? I don't know why it hangs around me, it's not like it wants food or warmth. Maybe it will be gone tomorrow. Can't say anything for sure.

Did you find who stole the razor from the stationeries? I'm sorry for you. You're right, though, people just can't resist shiny things. Matvey's reading journal says some nobles will even hire hitmen just to loot necklaces for them—no, I'm not saying I stole it.

Biscuits and tea—are you trying to bribe me? You want me to make up with someone? Who? Her? You're not getting it, I don't hate Rosalind, but you know she almost beat Antosha into slug paste? No, I'm not making that up. Also, if you really want to bribe me, trade me razors, sewing pins, or moth specimens.

The book Matvey gave me? No, it's nothing heavy, it's just things he and Antosha went through. I'm a very slow reader, or well, to be honest, I'm just not very willing to read it. I know what you're about to ask. Yes, I miss them, and I always will. And I wish he could be reading it to me.
Aj-aj-aj, I didn't mean to scare you, I've been standing here watching you for ages—yeah, since the moment you fell asleep, something wrong with that?

You, you're Sonya's boss? Just call me Ukusik. Sonya says you're the real deal, but you don't look like the type who could beat her. Relax, no worries, I'll help if you find yourself in a fight—Is something funny?
What shop sold this to you? I've never seen a movie look so clear, and there's no weird watermark either… What, this isn't a pirated version? And it's not a movie?!

Is this for me? The design's so old-looking. Are you sure you got the right one—ohhh, it's a promotion medal, okay, thank you then. A speech? Uh, alright, 'keep at it'. Maybe you can get me a prettier one next time.

Another medal? I approve. Now all that's missing for a perfect day is a spell of rain. Check the weather forecast? *sigh* This newspaper is a costume prop. Are you really asking about Grypherburg's weather from eight years ago?
*hiss*—Nobody warned me there'd be this many people.
Stop staring at me. All of you can just go do your thing.

There'll always be people who need to tear down others' feelings, and there'll always be a need for someone to heal those wounded spirits—everyone here's made sacrifices, haven't they? Don't worry, I'll heal them up.
Shh—keep it down. Enemy movements? Don't ask me, I just wanted quiet.
This'll do. Quit hesitating.
You're the boss. You make the calls.
Ayyyye-aye.
Surrrrre thing.
I know you can handle the pain, but try this now—isn't that better?
Hey! No hitting my patients! What? They're not ours?
Yeah, sock 'em! I've got you, go for it!
I'll stitch your wounds up. Relax, I can sew you nice and pretty.

handbook.profile: Ukusik, formerly of the Grypherburg underground society 'the Unbound'. She joined the Grypherburg branch of Rhodes Island at Operator Zima's recommendation, and works in intelligence gathering and first-aid. She receives regular Oripathy treatment and general education at Rhodes Island HQ at the request of Leto, who serves as her guardian.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 8%
Originium crystals are visible on Operator Ukusik's limbs and torso, along with chronic skin lesions. Imaging tests reveal presence of a small amount of Originium crystals in her upper respiratory tracts.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.27u/L
Ukusik suffers from organ damage from untreated early-stage Oripathy, contracted from an extended period of manual labor in high-Originium environments without proper protection or treatment. She has been cooperative with treatment since arriving on Rhodes Island, which has improved her condition.
handbook.promotionRecord:
'Why are you staring at me like that?'
'You're hurt.'
'This? Nah, it's nothing, just a little cut on the finger. Nothing to get your feathers ruffled about.'
'Sounds like you've been through a lot.'
'I've seen lots of people die... Bet you didn't expect that, huh? Hehe.'
'There's no need to force yourself to smile when you're sad.'
'I feel weird, like there's something in my head—did you do that?'
'No need to be scared. I just helped you smooth over your emotions. You should feel something different now.'
'I feel like my cheeks are hot.'
'Anything else?'
'My nose is tingling.'
'Is it the smoke from the new year fireworks?'
'No, it's because... bad things happened last new year... Why am I telling you this?'
'There's nothing strange about it. We're both Liberi from Ursus, and we both happen to be sitting on the same bench at the new year's party.'
'It's so hard being a Liberi in Ursus...'
'Almost as hard as it is finding a quiet corner at the Rhodes Island new year's party. There's joy and excitement everywhere.'
'That doesn't sound like something you'd want to get away from.'
'Then why are you here?' The older Liberi gently stroked Ukusik's hair with her mechanical arm.
Ukusik pouted, saying, 'I keep feeling like I shouldn't be happy.'
'I see. You know, there's a saying that a heart has two rooms. Happiness lives in one of them, but she's always worried about being too loud and waking up Pain who lives next door.'
'Hm? That's not what they tell me in my general education courses... But keep going...'
'But in truth, when you feel happy, you don't know what's living next door. Maybe Pain has already moved out. Maybe it's just an empty room.'
'Maybe, but how can I know for sure?'
'Well, what we need is a key.' The older Liberi gives her a small badge with a big smile on the front, an antenna on top, and a word etched on it.
'Courage.' Ukusik reads it aloud.
'Courage is the key. Open the door to the next room and maybe you'll find that it's empty. That no one's there to scold you for laughing too loud, and that you can put all the words you wanted to say but never got to in there.'
The older Liberi looks up. 'Oh, my teammates are looking for me. I should head over.'
'Wait! How do I find you again if I want to talk?'
'Don't worry, I'll find you first,' the older Liberi smiles. 'Besides, do you see that antenna on the badge I gave you? You can talk to it any time you want.'
Ukusik ran her finger over the 'Courage' badge, and suddenly got the urge to talk to the tables and chairs in the counseling room.
archives:
Her mother died on a dirty bed after giving birth to her. Her father died in a gambler's alley after abandoning her.
At the age of three, she was 'recruited' into the Grypherburg pipe cleaners with other children her age, crawling through pipelines filled with Originium crystals with nothing but a rope and a steel brush taller than her. Growing up in the cramped and hot pipes, she soon grew used to the darkness, but never her peers' unanimous silence. She saw far too many tiny creatures that died in the pipelines, and collected the hard, round shells of insects like wealthy children collected jewelry.
The 'Captain', an old man missing at least one tooth, collected the wages from their employer and gave them a few measly pieces of rye bread, drinking the rest of the money away—as old Ursines in Grypherburg are prone to doing. One day, he got drunk and forgot to lower the rope ladder for the children waiting in the pipes.
She saw her peers trample each other, fighting for breathable air higher up, most of them suffocating from inhaling an excess of poisonous fumes. She saw... that the lips of the dead children were ripe and red, and their faces a 'healthy' rosy color, forming what resembled a happy smile.
She survived by climbing over their corpses and breathing what little fresh air came in through the gap in the hole cover.
She was barely conscious by the time the old man woke up and remembered them, but she had to wait for him to haggle with the pipeline manager before he would open the cover.
The old man went down into the well himself, too cheap to hire cleaners. She awoke on the ground above, and gazed down coldly at the man's figure, the smell of alcohol still wafting from him...
She closed the cover, locking the old man in with the dead, then walked away—What? Don't ask me. How am I supposed to know where she went after that?
You thought I was talking about myself? No, 'she' is a friend of mine. Her name's Sveta Goreva. My name's Ukusik. It's not the same at all.
—Excerpt from 'My Best Friend', Operator Ukusik's impromptu presentation at her writing class's end-of-course party

The black fowlbeast that followed Ukusik to Rhodes Island caused a bit of commotion when she first arrived. She swore she had set it free outside Grypherburg, and had no idea how it followed her here. The fowlbeast had no name. Ukusik insisted it was not her pet and denied any responsibility for taking care of it. She was also completely unaware of its rarity. [Entry Name]: Rare Northern Black Fowlbeast [Distribution]: Mostly seen in Ursus's Far North mining district and the edges of Sami's southern pine forests, occasionally appearing near the routes of nomadic plates. [Rarity]: Very Rare The Rare Northern Black Fowlbeast is a medium-sized sedentary fowlbeast, with adults reaching around 25-30cm in length. Its body is covered in dense, matte soot-black feathers. It has a short and strong beak, and its eyes are typically yellow in color. Tiny Originium fragments are often found on the edges of its flight feathers. It is unknown whether this is a symptom of Oripathy infection, or the result of its unique metabolism. The Rare Northern Black Fowlbeast is able to mimic environmental sounds, particularly industrial noises. It is unclear what purpose this mimicry serves. Perhaps it is simply a form of play. Due to its rarity and cautious nature, taking a clear photo of one has become a popular challenge for fowlbeast photographers. —Encyclopedia Ursinia: Rare Flora and Fauna (4th Edition) [Audio Log] I'm recording this so people will stop asking me how I got it! First, I didn't 'get' it. It just landed on my head when I was crying for Matvey! Maybe it wanted to drink the salt from my tears. No, I don't know anything about its habits. I've never seen it eat or drink, and it never lets me know before it leaves to do whatever it does. I'm guessing it has a nest next to some factory furnace, because sometimes it feels hot to the touch, like charcoal, when it shows up. Imitating sounds? Is that a thing it can do? All I remember is that one time I dreamed about two people talking about complicated things, saying stuff like 'this land is a glass sphere lying upon an opaque black velvet blanket'... When I woke up, it was sitting next to my bed staring at me, cocking its little head. You want to take a photo of it? Suit yourself, just keep me out of it. As for the guys who fainted, better luck next time. Shortly before Ukusik's arrival, some fowlbeast photography afficionados amongst the operators had learned that there were potentially Rare Northern Black Fowlbeasts nearby. They quickly formed an expedition to conquer this highest peak of fowlwatching. After a week in the wilderness, Operator Scene was the first to get a photo of the beast. Though the quality of the photo was far from her usual standard, it was more than enough reason for the expedition to celebrate—that is, until they returned to the Rhodes Island living area and saw a dozen operators surrounding Ukusik with the fowl perched upon her shoulder, taking photos with anything from cameras, to personal terminals, to even security monitors. Several members of the expedition fainted from a combination of shock and fatigue. Scene managed to maintain her composure, though somehow forgot to remove the lens cover when someone invited her to take a photo of them next to the haughty Rare Northern Black Fowlbeast. Something seems... different about the fowlbeast on Ukusik's shoulder. Did you notice how it doesn't have any Originium fragments on it? —Member of photography expedition

[Registration Application Log]
Time: 1102-■-■ 13:21
Applicant: Leto
Request: Change Operator Ukusik's registered guardian from [None] to [Leto]

[Audio Log]
What d'you mean, 'respect the child's wishes'? Wait, wait, that's not what this is about—I'm not her mom, I just want to make sure she's taken care of, and that there'll be somebody to pick up after her when she gets in trouble at Rhodes Island.
What do you mean 'she hasn't gotten into trouble yet'? Hah, just you wait.
—Leto

[Audio Log]
No mediation! This has nothing to do with her not letting me eat candy before bed... This is a life and death matter! It looked like she almost punched Antosha's soul out of him! How could I not be mad at her? Yeah, I know she protected me, but that’s a different matter.
Anyway, I don't want her as my guardian!
—Ukusik

[Application Review]
Time: 1102-■-■ 09:01
Reviewer: HR
Decision: Operator Leto's application for guardianship of Operator Ukusik has been rejected due to opposition from Ukusik herself. Her guardianship will be decided at a later time.

[Communication from Operator Zima]
Stop humoring the girl, and stop letting Leto humor her either!
There's a lot of work to do at the Grypherburg office. If she doesn't want Leto as her guardian, you can put down my name. But tell her that if my name's on the form, she'll have to be my sparring partner too.
P.S. If you can get her to open up, ask her how Leto managed to get through the pipe... those two just wouldn't tell me!

[Registration Application Log]
Time: 1102-■-■ 23:33
Applicant: Ukusik
Request: Change Operator Ukusik's registered guardian from [None] to [Leto]

[Audio Log]
Like I said, she's not a bad girl. She just doesn't get the complicated stuff yet, like why friends might get into a fight with friends, or why a family member doesn't come back home... Me, when I was her age? Hah, I was so much more mature than she is!
Is this where I sign?
Wait, what do you mean by dormitory hygiene violations? Has she been hiding bugs in the sheets again?
Damaged goods at the Procurement Center... Teacher-Guardian meeting for missing her writing lesson homework... Get your butt over here, Ukusik!
—Leto

At the Doctor and Amiya's request, Medical arranged counseling for individuals involved in the Katorga Incident, but Ukusik steadfastly refused to talk, dodging questions with jokes, feigned crying, and acting cute, refusing to face her trauma—for which we could hardly fault her.
The turning point came on the second day of the new year, when Ukusik came to the counseling room of her own accord on her day off. She picked the lock, sat down on the sofa, and started talking to the furniture.
We are unsure whether she intentionally turned on the interview recorder, but the camera and microphone worked, and they recorded everything that happened.

[Audio Log]
...I didn't tell you about the house, did I?
I asked Yura and the others. No one knew how a poor kid like Matvey managed to build his own house. But the day they were released from jail, it was Matvey who told the expelled and... what's the word again... disenfranchised students to come with him. They built new floors and even a courtyard, and the place became the headquarter of the Unbound. They had other bases later, but eventually they went back to that house...
Matvey said there were rumors that the place was used to bury dead people, which was why it was left empty, but all he found when he was digging the foundation was a few Originium scraps—nothing to be scared about.
Oh, yeah, Originium. Antosha saw the rocks on me from the start, but no one said anything. I used to think that black rocks were the dirtiest, but after hearing them talk about all the amazing things the Infected have done, I began to feel like black rocks were the cleanest. Nothing to be afraid of.
I learned that Matvey died in the lockdown zone in 110■, and ■■ just told me the latest news about Antosha a couple of days ago. What would Matvey say if he were still alive and knew what Antosha is accomplishing? Maybe he'd say, 'Our friends are walking the right path.'
I think that's from a song. I heard Matvey hum it to himself when he was sharpening a knife in the kitchen in the sunlight, when I was sorting stolen coins by value on the table. Whenever Antosha came back, the first thing he did, whether he was hurt or not, was call out the names of everyone in the house. Matvey never answered back, only nodded—it was a strange feeling. I don't even know what to call it, because it all seemed so strange.
How long did I spend in that house?
Let me think, November, December... Wait, just forty days?
No, how could that be?
Just forty days...
But it felt like—

modules.moduleDescription:
Ukusik had been gazing at the illegible line for a while now, but still could not figure out what the words were.
Of the next row, only the first half is left: Ukusik, you—
Clap.
Ukusik closed the notebook that she had rescued from the fire. The two names on the cover were intact.
'A gift from Antosha and Matvey.'
Ukusik sighed and turned off her bedside lamp.

'Not hungry?' Leto watched as Ukusik stirred her porridge with a spoon.
'I'm practicing how to write.'
'Well, someone's eager, huh?'
'I need to learn how to write these words, so I can ask the teacher what they mean.'
Leto took a closer look at the trails Ukusik was making on the surface of her porridge.
'What's that? Learning a new language?'
'No!'

In the evening, Ukusik stood on Rhodes Island's outdoor terrace, raising a piece of paper to the wind and letting it be blown into various shapes. Then she let go and let the wind blow her eyes dry, but found someone standing behind her as she prepared to leave.
'Raidian?'
Raidian combed Ukusik's ear plumage with a practiced hand and said, 'I picked this up outside.'
It was Ukusik's writing class exam, with a few scribbles next to the full-marks score.
'Not even the teacher recognized those words.' Ukusik's eyes grew wet again. 'Matvey said he and Antosha wrote so much for me, but I couldn't read any of it!'
Raidian did not interrupt her.
'All those stories he never told me, all his adventures with Antosha, even the poem he wrote for my next birthday! He said he wrote it in the notebook! Why couldn't he have given it to me sooner? Why let it fall into a fire? I could have protected it! I could have protected them!'
Raidian hugged Ukusik to calm her down. She knew what she needed most right now.
'I'm sorry, Ukusik, I can't read those words either,' she said. 'However...'

Ukusik turned on the lamp again.
She opened the notebook.
Once again, she looked at the tattered papers.
The writings on the page began to move, forming familiar letters that said, 'Ukusik, you got first-place today! That's way better than we did when we were your age.'
Ukusik laughed.
'What are you laughing at? It's time for bed. Don't tell me you want a bedtime story?'
Ukusik nodded.
'Alright. Let Antosha tell you how he managed to offend every professor in the faculty on his very first day after getting into college...'
Ukusik closed her eyelids and watched the story emerge before her mind's eye as sleep overpowered her. Before she fell asleep, she forced her eyes open and took one last look at the three woolen dolls she had made in crafts class. Raidian was right, she thought—
'However, they can be any words you want them to be, and have any meaning you want them to have. They belong to you, and they'll always be with you.'

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: I hear strange noises in my headphones when I walk into this office… Doctor, is there a problem with the wiring of your audio equipment? Oh, it's the counter-surveillance system? Sorry, I'll turn off my equipment.

It's windy outside again. When I was a child in Bresk, I always worried about high winds putting out the fire at night. For many years, the sound of the Far North winds woke me from my dreams—does it still happen? Of course not, I'm awake right now. Oh, that's not what you meant?

No, nothing I don't understand. The documents are very clearly written. I look puzzled? Oh, that's because my horns aren't balanced, so it's less tiring if I tilt my head. Are you interested in my redesigned antenna? I can share the blueprints—Oh… nope, it doesn't hurt.

I often see you deep in thought. I envy you. My thoughts are shallow, and so I often realize things after the fact. Examples? Well, for example, it was only when I heard about the news in the Far North that I realized the fact. I'd been accepted into the Imperial College of Science and Engineering, just because it benefited the Grand Duchess politically. Ironic, isn't it?

The people in the cities thought they could keep the tragedy of the mines outside their doors. They're wrong. The city doesn't belong to them. Even their doors don't belong to them. I can hear the footsteps constantly following me, from Breskenoy to Grypherburg.

I met Mantra and found that voice when I came to this place. She and Raidian are remarkable women. Oh, no, I'm not here to ask for an autograph. But I do have a couple of microphones in my collection, just saying…

I used to read the proverb of the day on my college's student council radio. One day, I didn't have time to make preparations, so I read my own work. Word got out somehow, and an angry student came to demand that I read his work too. Yes, it was Rania.

Start recording. There's a lot of paperwork yet to be done, so the scheduled long-range communications test will have to be delayed—were you looking for me? Just making an audio diary. Mind if I continue? I hope I won't be interrupted again tomorrow. End recording.

I tried to call for help from the outside after being shut inside the quarantine zone, but heard only silence. The anxiety had me vomiting on a daily basis. But it turned out there was someone beside me listening all that time. Fedya—actually, how should I call him?
I can play relaxing music for you if you need to sleep. Don't worry, I have my headphones, it won't disturb me.

I remember you, Doctor. That unusual high-frequency waveform that appeared in Rhodes Island's encrypted signals. Just call me Botani, that's how everyone else calls me. It means 'bookworm', and I take it as a compliment.
I can't see the screen very well—whoa, there's even more static on it when I approach! Is it because of interference? Give me a minute to turn off my equipment. Well, more like a dozen minutes.
A commendation for me? Thank you. I once captured a Rhodes Island commendation message in an attic corner at my college. I never thought at the time that I would earn such a commendation myself.

I appreciate the recognition, even if I don't know if I actually deserve it. The same medal carries different weight on different people. There is much that I have to learn from Mantra and the others.
Operation channel connected. Beginning test.
Botani here. Beginning timecode check.
All units, maintain radio silence. We are leaving.
Target acquired.
Listening in.
Waiting for response.
Coordinates synced.
Botani ready.
Listen, hear the winds of the Far North behind us!
Look, see the torch in your hands!
Remember, know why we fight!
Shout, that they might hear our voice!
Radio silence lifted. We can cheer now, Doctor. It's a victory worth celebrating. Botani, over and out.
Good work, Doctor. Botani, over and out.
Botani, over and out.
Botani to all, Botani to all. Hear my voice, and I'll guide you to safety.
The soft humming of machines running… it's comforting.
Hey, did you hear something?
Don't touch that horn. No, it won't shock you, but it sends a terrible noise into my mind—ah, you believed me.
Arknights.
Somehow, New Year lights here feel warmer than in Grypherburg, and the wind gentler. Look, some operators are already dancing… would you like to try? I just picked up a new song that you might like.
How are you doing, Doctor? The report is on your desk. Would you like me to read it to you? Ahem. Today's news—

Put on my headphones, Doctor! Do you hear a strange beeping? Can you note it down for me? Thanks! Hm, it sounds like some kind of message. Seems like it translates to—aha! It says 'Happy Birthday!' The cake's still on its way, though.

With the call from the Far North that was heard all over Ursus, I realized that just listening was not enough. Change can only come by making more sound, and letting more people hear it. Even if we can only change a little bit at a time, Rhodes Island will be with us, yes?

No, nothing I don't understand. The documents are very clearly written. I look puzzled? Oh, that's because my horns aren't balanced, so it's less tiring if I tilt my head. Are you interested in my redesigned antenna? I can share the blueprints—Oh… nope, it doesn't hurt.

I often see you deep in thought. I envy you. My thoughts are shallow, and so I often realize things after the fact. Examples? Well, for example, it was only when I heard about the news in the Far North that I realized the fact. I'd been accepted into the Imperial College of Science and Engineering, just because it benefited the Grand Duchess politically. Ironic, isn't it?

The people in the cities thought they could keep the tragedy of the mines outside their doors. They're wrong. The city doesn't belong to them. Even their doors don't belong to them. I can hear the footsteps constantly following me, from Breskenoy to Grypherburg.

I met Mantra and found that voice when I came to this place. She and Raidian are remarkable women. Oh, no, I'm not here to ask for an autograph. But I do have a couple of microphones in my collection, just saying…

I used to read the proverb of the day on my college's student council radio. One day, I didn't have time to make preparations, so I read my own work. Word got out somehow, and an angry student came to demand that I read his work too. Yes, it was Rania.

Start recording. There's a lot of paperwork yet to be done, so the scheduled long-range communications test will have to be delayed—were you looking for me? Just making an audio diary. Mind if I continue? I hope I won't be interrupted again tomorrow. End recording.

I tried to call for help from the outside after being shut inside the quarantine zone, but heard only silence. The anxiety had me vomiting on a daily basis. But it turned out there was someone beside me listening all that time. Fedya—actually, how should I call him?
I can play relaxing music for you if you need to sleep. Don't worry, I have my headphones, it won't disturb me.

I remember you, Doctor. That unusual high-frequency waveform that appeared in Rhodes Island's encrypted signals. Just call me Botani, that's how everyone else calls me. It means 'bookworm', and I take it as a compliment.
I can't see the screen very well—whoa, there's even more static on it when I approach! Is it because of interference? Give me a minute to turn off my equipment. Well, more like a dozen minutes.
A commendation for me? Thank you. I once captured a Rhodes Island commendation message in an attic corner at my college. I never thought at the time that I would earn such a commendation myself.

I appreciate the recognition, even if I don't know if I actually deserve it. The same medal carries different weight on different people. There is much that I have to learn from Mantra and the others.
Operation channel connected. Beginning test.
Botani here. Beginning timecode check.
All units, maintain radio silence. We are leaving.
Target acquired.
Listening in.
Waiting for response.
Coordinates synced.
Botani ready.
Listen, hear the winds of the Far North behind us!
Look, see the torch in your hands!
Remember, know why we fight!
Shout, that they might hear our voice!
Radio silence lifted. We can cheer now, Doctor. It's a victory worth celebrating. Botani, over and out.
Good work, Doctor. Botani, over and out.
Botani, over and out.
Botani to all, Botani to all. Hear my voice, and I'll guide you to safety.
The soft humming of machines running… it's comforting.
Hey, did you hear something?
Don't touch that horn. No, it won't shock you, but it sends a terrible noise into my mind—ah, you believed me.
Arknights.
Somehow, New Year lights here feel warmer than in Grypherburg, and the wind gentler. Look, some operators are already dancing… would you like to try? I just picked up a new song that you might like.
How are you doing, Doctor? The report is on your desk. Would you like me to read it to you? Ahem. Today's news—

Put on my headphones, Doctor! Do you hear a strange beeping? Can you note it down for me? Thanks! Hm, it sounds like some kind of message. Seems like it translates to—aha! It says 'Happy Birthday!' The cake's still on its way, though.

With the call from the Far North that was heard all over Ursus, I realized that just listening was not enough. Change can only come by making more sound, and letting more people hear it. Even if we can only change a little bit at a time, Rhodes Island will be with us, yes?

handbook.profile: Botani, also known as Tishinna Viktorovna Belyaeva, is a former student of the Imperial College of Science and Engineering in Grypherburg. After withdrawing from school, she joined Rhodes Island by Operator Zima's recommendation, continuing to study Originium communications while participating in field missions.

handbook.promotionRecord:
Tishinna, my dear child, I hope this letter finds you well.
Thank you for telling me your new address and providing recent updates, which has set my anxious heart at ease.
There is nothing to worry about at home. The weather in Bresk is still the same, but at least I'm getting your letters, and flour and vegetables remain affordable. As for your suggestion of moving, I thought long and hard about it, but our address is the only information on us that your sister has. All I hope is for both my children to come home safe and sound... Will you forgive me, Tishinna?
I've been in touch with this 'Rhodes Island' you mentioned. They're nice people, though they always wear a stern expression, and they put on these 'Third Bureau' uniforms to avoid suspicion. It must be hard work. They visit weekly, bringing food and fabric, and taking with them some old things you left behind. Last time they took the letters you sent back, saying they would have to be destroyed to ensure secrecy. I'm also not sure why you asked them to send the toys you brought from Sami to Rhodes Island... Maybe you still have memories of the place. By the way, they were asking me whether you've been in contact with your old friend. How was I to know? They even wrote down the name of the friend, like they were concerned I couldn't hear clearly. How kind of them!
How did you meet this Fedya fellow anyway? How is he? Why haven't you told me about him before?
Your mother (who is eager to know more about your story with your 'old friend')
archives:
Tishinna Viktorovna Belyaeva is not the name Botani was born with, but it is the name that stayed with her the longest.
The award displayed on the wall, the fading photo framed in gemstone, and the thick stack of penalty decisions all bear witness to important moments in Tishinna's life.
For a long time, she thought she was lucky to be admitted to the Imperial College of Science and Engineering in Grypherburg under a generous scholarship from Grand Duchess Elisaveta, even receiving an invitation to the Grand Duchess's solemn manor. Where, to her bewilderment, she was made to stand by the fireplace for an hour, watching the Grand Duchess speak to her advisers without being granted an audience, or even a single glance. It felt very cold outside when she left that building.
The Imperial College of Science and Engineering was also a far cry from what Tishinna had dreamed of. It was a garden of wealthy nobility, where the unruly children of aristocrats were sent to spend a few years, whereupon they became 'intellectuals'. There was no place there for a commoner from Bresk, and an Elafia at that. Indeed, there were hardly any non-Ursine students at the school. Tishinna often found herself locked out of her room at night, or having to search for her shoes and scarf early in the morning because they had mysteriously gone missing.
She eventually took up residence in a storage room at the library, which was open 24/7. This earned her the nickname 'Botani'—derived from 'botanik', or 'bookworm'—but also a place of peace and quiet. At the library, she found a notebook belonging to one Ksenia Markovna Nelidova, which seemed to be a survival guide from a non-Ursine student. Times had changed, and many of the locations and people in the notebook were no longer relevant, but Tishinna found courage in it nonetheless. Books had always been better teachers to her: following the guidance of professional textbooks, she created the communications device she had long sought, even modifying her own antler to hear signals from afar.
Then, everything changed one night.
The cries from the Far North drowned her. She tried to tell others what she heard, but found that she had no voice, and thus no power to bring about change. Listening to the voices from the Far North, she felt the pain of snowflakes cutting her skin open, and finally realized why the Grand Duchess had summoned her that day only to ignore her.
It was all so simple. It was the same reason she was admitted into this college for aristocrats: the Grand Duchess needed an example of her benevolence. All she needed from Tishinna was for her to be seen walking into the manor and spending an hour inside, so that the people would praise the kindness and benevolence of their Grand Duchess. What she thought had been the product of her hard work and good fortune was no more than a political show.
Since that night, Tishinna's name began to frequent the school's penalty notices, while the nickname 'Botani' she had been mocked with began to spread amongst the students trying to speak out for the tragedy in the far north.

Botani finally met Mantra and Raidian in Rhodes Island once things had settled down, even receiving a microphone autographed by Raidian. After learning that Team Mantra's members held open seminars on the effective use of long-range communications Arts, Botani could often be seen in Engineering's presentation room, hoping to sit in on one. I learned a lot from those seminars. It seemed like the attendees didn't know each other very well, sitting apart from each other. I don't have a very good memory for faces, so I didn't have the courage to greet unfamiliar colleagues either. In fact, I couldn't even tell who were supposed to be the lecturers and who were the students. Fortunately, that situation did not last for long. One day, the lecturers came to quiz me after I had just performed some repairs on my antenna. Their questions were quite difficult, and I saw the disappointment on their faces when I failed to answer one... After that, I began spending my nights studying in my room, trying to keep up with them. I suppose I did well enough, and I felt the benefit of this unique form of education. I learned a lot of new things. As far as surprises... I found there were far more lecturers than students at these seminars, and for some reason they all liked to question me. —Operator Botani I went to the Engineering Department's presentation room too. I thought the Team Mantra seminars were only a legend, but they turned out to be real! Botani didn't look like she liked to talk, so we only sat around, none of us daring to ask questions. Then one day, the antenna on her head quivered, and I realized it was a sign for us to ask questions, so I went up to her! Her Ursine accent left a deep impression on me. She spoke methodically at a careful pace, and whenever I asked a question lacking in rigor, she stopped to let me think for myself. I would have to go back to my room and think about it all night, then she would tell me the correct answer the following day. In a matter of weeks, the other new engineers and I felt we made significant progress in our technical and theoretical knowledge. We wrote a joint letter of appreciation to Mantra, thanking her for the help her team had given us. —An engineering operator So is that why no one came to the seminars?! Everyone went to the presentation room—I was waiting for them in the break room! Isn't it an Engineering tradition to discuss academic problems in the break room? Did I misunderstand something? Well, whatever, I'll just hide this letter before the captain finds out... She asked you to give it to me? She knew?! —Operator Elysium

Tishinna Viktorovna Belyaeva is the name Botani has used for the longest, but it is not the name she was born with.
Her original name came from the frost and springs of Sami, given to her by her sister, which she claims is untranslatable into any other language.
A shadow came over her eyes as she brought up her sister.
Her sister was not like her at all, not even like their mother. One day, her sister took her to see the ice springs, only to leave her alone in the snow-covered woods. She called her sister's name in panic and dug a shallow hole in the ground, trying to hide herself in it... She does not recall how long she spent in the dark woods, for her memory stopped there. Much later, her sister told her by the fireside that she had been watching her from a short distance away. When asked why she didn't answer, her sister said she had not pronounced her name correctly. She looked into her sister's eyes and saw only disappointment.

After that time in the forest, my sister gave me an intercom she made herself, and taught me how to tune it to a special channel, how to speak into it, and how to receive a response.
I was too young to understand what she was doing. Our mother may have noticed, but she never told me.
The day we moved away from Sami, my sister stopped walking and said, 'This is as far as I go.'
She was speaking in Sami. She said she could go no further with my mother and me. I wanted to go with her, but she said no. She said I had an Ursine name, and that I could no longer go back with her. Mother said nothing. All she did was weep.
I remember holding the intercom my sister gave me. I remembered that if I wanted to find her, all I needed to do was call her name on that channel, and she would appear and tell me which syllable I had mispronounced.
So I turned on the intercom, but I didn't know what to say—I couldn't remember her Sami name. It was as though everything I knew about Sami was disappearing from my memory. In a panic, I cried the name in Ursine that would become mine for many years to come.
My sister did not stop, and disappeared into the snow. Would she have stayed if I had called her name correctly, with the correct pronunciation? I don't know.
I lost the intercom. Maybe Mother threw it away. I wanted to get another one.
—Audio recording from a counseling session, used with Operator Botani's permission

Rhodes Island took in many survivors of the Katorga Incident, providing them psychological support.
Botani was the most cooperative of those who eventually joined Rhodes Island, and the first to consent to the use of the Self-Diagnosis and Treatment of Trauma Using Exposure Therapy Recorder β, and to share her data with the Medical Department.
Indeed, Medical found her nonchalance on the matter abnormal.

[Audio Log]
(Noise)
...? More EM interference... Did that recording save?
The bad news is that I couldn't find the Save Recording button, and I'm not comfortable with disassembling the machine. The good news is that there's still 2% power left, and it should auto-save before turning off... right? I should keep talking. I've told you how I became trapped in the lockdown zone and how I got out with Sonya and the others. What else can I tell you?
Do I really need to tell you how I hid in a wardrobe for three days and how I cried for help in a voice so low that only I could hear it? Or... should I talk about... how I took a life...
(Heavy breathing)
No... no.
I... I didn't do it on purpose. At least, not the first time. He was... swinging a knife, like he didn't feel pain.
I just... I just wanted to live. I didn't want to keep hiding in that wardrobe. There were bloody scratch marks on the back panel... someone had died there before I hid in it.
No one could hear me. Nothing I did meant anything. Katorga was... a coffin for the living.
(Vomiting sounds)
...I'm sorry.
How do I delete this recording?
People are dying... why am I talking to myself here?
No, this is not how it should be—
(Recording interrupted)

Botani submitted this audio, admitting that she had accidentally destroyed the SDTTETR β in an outburst, and was only able to extract a partial recording from the storage media.
She also submitted a broken dagger, which she said she took from the wardrobe. She does not know who it belonged to, whether it was used in self-defense, and certainly not what happened to its previous owner. She had taken the broken blade out of a vague sense of responsibility. She survived, yet she dared not look back. In her own words, looking back was 'like sleeping wrong: it makes it really hurt to turn around. But it'll stop hurting eventually—it's just a matter of time. Now that the time has come, I feel like I can finally let it go... but I don't know who to give it to. Will you take it?

By the way, I'd like to ask about the intellectual property rights for the SDTTETR β. While my attempts to repair it failed, I did manage to create small audio recorders imitating its core structure. Do I need to pay royalties to Closure? I'll only use them to make personal journals, since I found that I seem to respond well to this sort of self-conversation therapy. At least I'm making my voice heard to myself.
—Operator Botani

modules.moduleDescription:
I hear someone call my name. The voice comes from afar, and keeps me awake.
It comes at the appointed hour every night. Sometimes I wait for it at the table with a cup of coffee. I don't know if I'm hallucinating or not. I would rather believe it's some kind of signal interference. Medical gave me medicine to calm my nerves and help me sleep, but I don't actually need it.
Here it is again.
The voice is familiar. I go through everyone in my memory, but none match. Mother's voice is gentler. My childhood friend died of pneumonia at the age of six. As for my sister, she never called to me like that—
My sister would simply gaze into my eyes, as though trying to peer into my soul, then turn around and leave... No, what was it that just came back to me?
Cold air so dry it makes you sneeze. Was it Bresk? I could not forget that warm hallway. I was gazing at the Grand Duchess's back, waiting for her to emerge from the shadows, so that I could clasp those hands again. I waited a long time, but she never moved. Perhaps she only needed the people to see me walk into her palace, nothing more. Was it someone on the streets calling out to me then?
No, that wasn't it.
Perhaps it was in Grypherburg, from back when I walked onto the campus of the Imperial College of Science and Engineering with my acceptance letter in hand. I wasn't the only commoner to be dropped into this garden of aristocracy as a political performance, but I was the only Elafia. I stood in the courtyard, smiling at a tree they had imported from Yan at great expense. The nobles had donated five heaters for it, yet it still failed to survive even one blooming season. Was it from that time? I had picked up a white petal on the ground, but someone from an upper floor called out to me, just to laugh at the antler that I had modified into an antenna...
No. I look at my empty coffee cup, my thoughts at a standstill. A face seems to be reflected in the porcelain bottom.
I feel the wind and snow brush past my cheeks. It's as though I've gone back to the day I parted ways with my sister. I fell down in the snow, clasping the small intercom she had given me. I tuned it to the channel she had told me about, and opened my mouth, but didn't know what to say—
Beg? Apologize? Accuse? No, none of them. There wasn't a single word on Terra that belonged to me at the time, other than my own name.
'Tishinna Viktorovna Belyaeva!'
I hear my own voice, the voice I shouted with back then, twenty years later.
I remember my unfinished thesis. Perhaps the signals we emit never truly disappear. They echo in the Originium particles in the air, the soil, and the water. Signals from Originium Arts may grow weaker over time, but they never truly disappear.
They echo in your life for years, decades, even centuries, until you capture them again. I hear my cry from when I was five, the appreciation speech I read for the Grand Duchess, my mutterings in the attic during finals, and, from Katorga...
I see the formless signals surround me like the starry heavens, unintentional greetings from the past to the present. The days of my life I have experienced have never truly left me.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: That's everything that needs doing done! Anything else you need me to handle, like your schedule, your finances… What do you mean, you can't let me touch those?! Why not? I'm good with those too!
I saw that, Doctor. What's that you're hiding behind your back? Is it a soft drink? You shouldn't drink so much of that stuff, it'll rot your teeth. I'm confiscating it.

I ran into the Saluzzo Vino bigshot in the corridor just now. If I ever have the chance, I'd like to have a meal with him, and if I get really lucky, I'd like to talk business with him. Of course I'm not scared of him. He's like me. Everything we do, we do for our families—'Family comes first, after all'. I think he should get where I'm coming from.

handbook.profile: Ripresa, manager of a well-known orchestra in Nuova Volsinii who contacted us after observing that many with positions of power in the city have ties to Rhodes Island, in the hope of increasing exposure for her orchestra. She participates in certain field missions at her own request.
handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 6%
A small distribution of Originium crystals is present on Operator Ripresa's thigh.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.25u/L
Operator Ripresa contracted Originium at a young age. Her condition is currently under control.
handbook.promotionRecord:
Maestro Czerny,
I hope this letter finds you well.
I apologize for not being able to visit you personally, as I have been busy with the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra's performances lately. I am writing today to share with you some changes that have happened recently, and ask something of you.
Yesterday, I ran into a Caprinae at the end of her wits holding an instrument case, saying that she came from Leithanien to Nuova Volsinii, just like the other members that Mama Paola recruited. I didn't understand a lot of what she said, but I feel there must be many people like Mama Paola who couldn't play the music they wanted to back home. This woman really loved the piece you wrote for us, and so I asked her to stay as second violist.
You may have already guessed what I want to ask... We already have a violist, but I wanted her to stay, and to give her a place in that piece that belongs to her.
I know you wrote it for our particular orchestra, which is why I didn't want her to just play in unison with the other violist—it would make her feel redundant, not to mention that the performance would deviate from your original concept. I want the composition to truly respond to her, just as it did for the others, but I'm not Mama Paola, and I'm still learning the art of composition.
So I would like to ask if you could make some arrangements to the piece, so that the second violist has a distinct and unique significance. Whether it be the voicing, the structure, or anything else you see fit, I am willing to put my full faith in whatever you decide.
Actually, she doesn't yet know that we're inviting her to stay... I was shadowing her before writing this letter, and I saw her go to a music store to ask about selling her instrument. Please, I don't want her to give up music! I'll try to get her to perform with us until you write back.
I look forward to your reply!
Liesel
archives:
Czerny had had enough. For the fourth time, Ripresa had given him a new tape after her piano lesson.
The first, a piano etude, could be justified as homework, but the next was a trombone solo, followed by an oboe and bassoon duet. This one was apparently the percussion section from a symphony movement. Ripresa was a motivated student, a quick study, and diligent with her practice. Other students in the studio said she must be a huge fan of Professor Czerny, and at one point Czerny would have agreed.
'Did you need something from me, Frau Liesel?'
'Oh, um... I've always been very interested in your compositional style...'
'That's not what I'm talking about. You've taken enough of my lessons to be familiar with my style, and I've heard enough of your tapes to get a feel for them. I must certainly compliment you on your choice of repertoire. Now, what do you want from me?'
Ripresa blinked for a few seconds before taking out a few video tapes from her bag.
'Well, Maestro Czerny, these are recordings of the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra's performances, a small chamber orchestra of around twenty members that I currently direct...'
Ripresa's description gave Czerny food for thought. He recalled his most recent schedule to check whether he had time to make a trip to Nuova Volsinii. A Leithanian orchestra? What sort of chemistry could he form with them as a pianist? Czerny cleared his throat, interrupting Ripresa's monologue.
'I would be happy to work with your orchestra—'
'Really?! Thank you! About the composition's style—our members agreed that we would prefer a hopeful work to a melancholic one. With Maestro Czerny writing it, I'm sure our performance will deliver hope to our listeners' hearts!'
'...Composition?'
Czerny swallowed the words 'performing as a pianist' as Ripresa continued to describe her request. Her ideas for the new composition were very specific, and the recordings were sufficiently vivid that a melody gradually took form in his mind as she spoke.

Czerny's new work was unsurprisingly a massive hit in Nuova Volsinii at its premiere by the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra. We deliberated on whether to tell Ripresa that she could simply come forward with any requests she has, without resorting to her old negotiation tactics from Nuova Volsinii. But she seems to enjoy the process very much. Perhaps it is not such a bad thing after all, to let her do things her way.

Certain strange rumors came to our attention as HR performed its background check on Operator Ripresa. When we inquired with Operator Bellone on this, he simply smiled and said, 'She's good to her famiglia.'
The theater that the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra had partnered with was closed for investigation following the murder of the musician Paola Memminger, forcing the orchestra to seek out other venues in Nuova Volsinii.
Their agreement with the new theater was initially only a temporary lease, but extra costs were incurred as rehearsals intensified, which were borne by the venue under the rental agreement. Meanwhile, the orchestra would have difficulty finding a new venue on short notice if the agreement were terminated, locking the two parties in a stalemate.
Rather than avoid the issue, Ripresa set about reviewing rehearsal records and expenses incurred, putting together a list of the extra costs and incorporating them into their budget in her capacity as the orchestra's representative. It was not an easy decision for an orchestra in transition, and Ripresa had to redistribute a budget that was already tight to begin with, incurring additional risks in the process, but she decided to take on the expense knowing that the orchestra risked more than monetary loss if the partnership were terminated.
In interviews, HR learned that the venue was surprised by her decision.
It kept the partnership intact, and the two sides began negotiations on future billing and usage. While a stable long-term partnership is as yet uncertain, the pressing issues have been resolved without escalation, as Ripresa has consistently done in any matter involving the orchestra's interests.
At the end of the investigation, we were still unable to clearly define her actions. She did not seem to be trying to expand her influence, but rather appeared to take on responsibility for any issue as a matter of habit, acting less like a representative and more like a...
'That petite Caprinae resolved the conflict between the vicious foreigners and our famiglia like the Godmother!'
While inputting the data, the investigator could not help but recall certain rumors from the early stages of the investigation.

One consistent theme from our interviews with members of the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra was that many of them had begun to identify themselves as Nuova Volsinians, or more specifically as 'members of the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra of Nuova Volsinii'.
Most of them came to Siracusa as exiles from Leithanien, harboring both bitterness towards Leithanien and wariness towards Siracusa. They struggled in Siracusa's cities despite their talents in music and Arts, and many even gave up on music. After all, music that was rejected by Leithanien would not necessarily fare much better in Siracusa. It was only when Paola Memminger brought them together that they finally found their home.
After her death, the members faced uncertainty about more than just personnel or venue, but also about their own futures. They mentioned that, for the first time, they were faced with the reality that without a steady anchor holding it all together, they could dissolve and scatter at any moment. Leaving was always a realistic option.
Things changed when Ripresa took over.
She did not attempt to define the orchestra's identity, nor did she emphasize to its members what they ought to represent. She simply performed the duties that seemed mundane, but were very important: ensuring that rehearsals continued on schedule, checking the details of their rental agreements with venues, and making contingency plans to avoid potential conflict. As things began to settle down, something changed subtly in the mentality of the members, nudging them towards putting down roots in the city. The members offered various answers when we asked the reason, but they all pointed to the same thing: Liesel was here, and she would conduct them tomorrow.
Notably, this shift in identity did not come from any clear gesture of acceptance by the city, but from the orchestra itself. For its members, 'Schwarzervorhang' was no longer just a collection of musicians, but a community they lived in, one in which they did not have to explain where they came from, nor constantly prepare for where to go next.
For what was perhaps the first time since they left Leithanien, the people who came together because of Paola had a home, one that they did not need to check on constantly, and one that was not easily lost. All thanks to the leadership of Paola's foster daughter.

'I was sitting in the gallery when the Caprinae who killed Mama Paola was sentenced by Judge Lavinia. He stood there with an impassive expression and freely admitted his crime. To him, she was a stranger—no more than a symbol, one that was incompatible with the narrative he believed in. For a long time after the trial, I had a hard time accepting the whole thing.
'She never preached sedition the way the killer said she did. She didn't gather us to oppose anything. From the beginning, all she told me and the other members was that we should tell the truth, not be afraid, and enjoy the music we love... I just don't understand how it turned out this way. I don't understand, so I need to do something.
'Revenge? Oh, not at all! The case is closed, and the culprit has received his punishment. The other members are all of the same mind on this. What I feel I must do is... well, maybe it's an impulsive act, but I feel like Mama Paola did nothing wrong, nor did anybody in the orchestra. I don't want anyone to have to change their way of life just because someone else doesn't like it. We'll continue to live this way. In fact, we'll live even freer and let the Leithanians suffer on their own. We'll play the music we want to play, and only the music we want to play.
If you ask me whether I have a grudge against the killer... he took my mother from me and hurt my family. Of course I have a grudge. But I won't let him or people like him ruin my life. I think that's what she would have wanted.'

[Classified Log]
Grimmacht's voice is silent. The shadow of Gaul appears in the clouds. Ewigegnade is cleansing Leithanien of all disharmony, and her iron fists reach beyond the borders of Leithanien. Rhodes Island must be vigilant, and consider its next move carefully.

modules.moduleDescription:
The conductor's baton brushes past the last note on the score, and the performance concludes to fervent applause. As usual, Liesel turns around to bow, but someone in the audience catches her eye. It is a Caprinae woman, around the same age as Paola, with both anxiety and suppressed joy in her eyes, as though she were listening to some distant melody only she could hear.
Why would this bright, uplifting piece bring about such emotions? It was Paola's favorite work, and Liesel had pestered her for months before she figured out the details, for she had been fascinated by the music's freedom and spontaneity, unbound like a dancer upon the vast plains. Paola had told her not to be obsessed with accuracy, but to imagine the floating sensation of being thrown to the clouds...
'Thank you. I thought I would never hear music like that again.
'I used to hear such melodies from street corners in my hometown. It was the most unrestrained sound I'd ever heard. But then the wandering musician was chased off by the guards.
'The musicians of the spires say that such dissonance is an affront to art, that it is only beautiful to the untrained.
'But... is beauty something that can be so arbitrarily defined?'
The woman falls silent. There seemed to be some kind of unspeakable pain there, hidden where Liesel could not tread. Perhaps it was the very reason Paola came to Nuovo Volsinii. She recalls Paola's comments in the margins of a copied score:
Expression and beauty are not privileges, and nothing can stop true passion. Do not be fazed by criticism and scrutiny. Express yourself to your heart's delight, and we shall meet in equality. Passion will create unity, and we will come together to make new things.
Liesel had not understood at the time. All she knew was that the words were beautiful and warm, just like Paola herself. Now, seeing the longing and sorrow in this woman's eyes, she realizes that the reason this piece was Paola's favorite was not because of the beauty of the music itself, but because it represented the voices of the musicians who loved music, and Paola's own vision when she founded the orchestra. Everyone who expresses themselves through their instrument deserves to be listened to.
This brings her one step closer to Paola.
'My mother left Leithanien, brought this music here, and taught it to me. Now that it's where people can hear it, this orchestra will make sure it deserves to be heard.'
Liesel extends her hand.
'Welcome to Nuova Volsinii. We'll perform it again next time.'
The woman smiles, a faint smile as if her doubts have faded away.
'Thank you... I'll come again.'
As Liesel watches the woman leave, she recalls how Paola stood upon the podium, and the dedication on the score—
To all musicians.
Liesel Memminger takes a deep breath and looks up.
She must prepare for tomorrow's performance.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: You can leave the meeting minutes to me, Doctor. I'm very good at shorthand—You can't read my writing? Oh, sorry. I'll do my best to write neatly.

The head of Medical wants to have a chat with my master? That might be difficult… That elderly man—he wanders all around as he practices, so meeting him even once isn't easy. Why do I call him that? He has healing hands, but he's got a haggard face and a stick-thin body, though he'll still give you a kindly look now and then, just like any other elder.

There's an old saying in Yan: 'A house with ginger, illness won't linger.' Fresh ginger is warming, able to induce sweating that relieves external symptoms while expelling cold from the stomach. Don't be a picky eater, Doctor. You really can't eat it? Well, ginger and jujube tea, ginger cystymilk curd, and ginger honey water will also do. Just wait here while I brew a pot.

The Shen Jing, Cu Bing, and Zhen Gui. Yes, that's them. Just leave them on my table. Thanks. Why do I bring all these books with me? Go ahead and laugh, Doctor. Despite my many years of medical internship, there are many things in the books which I don't fully understand.

My master would always say that late nights are harmful and deplete your qi, and that you must never indulge in them. But… I would often wake in the middle of the night to see him sitting alone by the candle, lost in thought. I believe you and he are very similar.

Dandelions have medicinal properties; the Yanese use them to make decoctions, while Columbians make similar tisanes. But their effects would remain obscure without proper research. *sigh* There are countless medicinals out there, and I want to learn about all the wonders they hold, but I… No, there's still my master. He'll be able to do it.

Look over here, Doctor! Fwoo—Haha, they're dandelions a coworker at the Convalescent Garden sent over. Would you like to try blowing on one? Oh, right, remember to make a wish when you do. Who knows, it might come true in a few days.

I'm not Yanese, I've just followed my master around for a long time, so the way he speaks and lives rubbing off on me was inevitable… My hometown? Why don't you take a guess? A hint? The farthest point these dandelions can fly. That's where my hometown is.

These bells on my staff aren't just for show. Our travels often took us through the wastes, and the chime of the bells bring people in arduous straits some measure of hope. 'I vow to save all sentient life from suffering.' This is why my master carries on, and what makes him weary. Me? I don't have such grand aspirations, but I'll do my best to keep up.
The decoction worked wonders… It's dandelion season, Doctor, you'll need a little something to clear the sinuses. Rest well, now.

Hello, you can call me Taraxacum. My master sent me here for an exchange study, and also to tell his brothers and sisters that he is well. Me? I am simply his coachman, with a little knowledge of medicine.
No theory without practice, no practice without theory.
A promotion? Does that mean I get to be a master myself? Haha, just kidding. I know I still have a long way to go.

Another promotion? Doctor, healers should have calm minds and concrete goals, and should not have wants or desires. I don't think I really merit such a—My diligent practice deserves commendation? Well… If that's your logic, then the one who really deserves commendation is you, Doctor.
I've prepared forty-three common prescriptions. Whatever ails you, I'll have the medicine for it.
Everyone, relax. I've already studied the battlefield in detail.
Sickness requires swift treatment.
'See the suffering of others as if your own'… I know your weak spots. Forgive me.
The medicines are mixed.
Medical equipment ready.
Afraid I can't do much about that tongue of yours.
Going to need to look up what's wrong with your pulse.
Illness is unpredictable. This will be… tricky.
Prescriptions are adaptive, so let's add an extra ingredient!
Since it's being stubborn… Let's change how we're administering the meds!
I understand the symptoms now. Don't worry, I won't make even the slightest mistake.
Most meticulous.
What a perfect prescription.
Something must have gone wrong with my Medicine Pot… I'll need to ask Engineering for help when we're back.
Let's go back and get some rest, Doctor.
Now where… would Master's siblings be…
The medicine's just been brewed. Careful not to burn yourself!
So, Doctor, out of all these medical texts on the table, which do you feel like memorizing first?
Arknights.

A New Year's custom calls for customized herbal teas. Care for a cup, Doctor? Bitter? No, shouldn't be. Lungmen herbal tea is different from ordinary decoctions… Dried tangerine peel, lotus leaves, and honeysuckle, all steamed to remove the astringency. That sounds like a decoction? It's not! It really is just regular herbal tea!
Would you like something off the grill, Doctor? Though it might be too heaty… Huh?

Sit here, Doctor. No need to be so nervous. Today is your birthday, and I learned some Yanese tui na massage techniques from my master. You're always hunched over your desk, so your back, shoulders and neck must ache a lot. Here, a-and here… Well, how's that? Feels great, doesn't it!

Don't worry, I've already filed away all the case files. Phew… I hope that one day, there won't be a market for these medicines! Ah, I'm not trying to put a curse on your company or anything. I was just thinking, if there ever comes a day when these cases were gathering dust, wouldn't that mean everyone will be healthy?
