He'll be able to do it.

Look over here, Doctor! Fwoo—Haha, they're dandelions a coworker at the Convalescent Garden sent over. Would you like to try blowing on one? Oh, right, remember to make a wish when you do. Who knows, it might come true in a few days.

I'm not Yanese, I've just followed my master around for a long time, so the way he speaks and lives rubbing off on me was inevitable… My hometown? Why don't you take a guess? A hint? The farthest point these dandelions can fly. That's where my hometown is.

These bells on my staff aren't just for show. Our travels often took us through the wastes, and the chime of the bells bring people in arduous straits some measure of hope. 'I vow to save all sentient life from suffering.' This is why my master carries on, and what makes him weary. Me? I don't have such grand aspirations, but I'll do my best to keep up.
The decoction worked wonders… It's dandelion season, Doctor, you'll need a little something to clear the sinuses. Rest well, now.

Hello, you can call me Taraxacum. My master sent me here for an exchange study, and also to tell his brothers and sisters that he is well. Me? I am simply his coachman, with a little knowledge of medicine.
No theory without practice, no practice without theory.
A promotion? Does that mean I get to be a master myself? Haha, just kidding. I know I still have a long way to go.

Another promotion? Doctor, healers should have calm minds and concrete goals, and should not have wants or desires. I don't think I really merit such a—My diligent practice deserves commendation? Well… If that's your logic, then the one who really deserves commendation is you, Doctor.
I've prepared forty-three common prescriptions. Whatever ails you, I'll have the medicine for it.
Everyone, relax. I've already studied the battlefield in detail.
Sickness requires swift treatment.
'See the suffering of others as if your own'… I know your weak spots. Forgive me.
The medicines are mixed.
Medical equipment ready.
Afraid I can't do much about that tongue of yours.
Going to need to look up what's wrong with your pulse.
Illness is unpredictable. This will be… tricky.
Prescriptions are adaptive, so let's add an extra ingredient!
Since it's being stubborn… Let's change how we're administering the meds!
I understand the symptoms now. Don't worry, I won't make even the slightest mistake.
Most meticulous.
What a perfect prescription.
Something must have gone wrong with my Medicine Pot… I'll need to ask Engineering for help when we're back.
Let's go back and get some rest, Doctor.
Now where… would Master's siblings be…
The medicine's just been brewed. Careful not to burn yourself!
So, Doctor, out of all these medical texts on the table, which do you feel like memorizing first?
Arknights.

A New Year's custom calls for customized herbal teas. Care for a cup, Doctor? Bitter? No, shouldn't be. Lungmen herbal tea is different from ordinary decoctions… Dried tangerine peel, lotus leaves, and honeysuckle, all steamed to remove the astringency. That sounds like a decoction? It's not! It really is just regular herbal tea!
Would you like something off the grill, Doctor? Though it might be too heaty… Huh?

Sit here, Doctor. No need to be so nervous. Today is your birthday, and I learned some Yanese tui na massage techniques from my master. You're always hunched over your desk, so your back, shoulders and neck must ache a lot. Here, a-and here… Well, how's that? Feels great, doesn't it!

Don't worry, I've already filed away all the case files. Phew… I hope that one day, there won't be a market for these medicines! Ah, I'm not trying to put a curse on your company or anything. I was just thinking, if there ever comes a day when these cases were gathering dust, wouldn't that mean everyone will be healthy?

handbook.profile: A native of Sargon, Taraxacum is a wandering medical apprentice with considerable experience driving burdenbeast carts. He is currently stationed on Rhodes Island for academic exchange and study, providing everyday medical services on a temporary contract.
handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 7%
No obvious Originium crystallization has been observed on Operator Taraxacum's body.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.2u/L
Operator Taraxacum's work frequently takes him into high-risk areas. While he has a fairly strong awareness of protective measures and medical knowledge, regular checkups are still recommended to prevent his condition from deteriorating.

Don't worry, he's got Number Ten looking after him.
—A certain warm-hearted person who showed up to watch the checkup
handbook.promotionRecord:
'I want a Yanese name too!'
'What's that? Cart Boy is not good enough for you?'
'That's not a name!'
'Why not?'
'Fine, I'll call you Old Doctor from now on.'
'...Ahem.'
The night wind through the desert was chilly. The gaunt doctor gazed toward the northeast where Yan was. The snow must have fallen a few times already.
'...Feng Xu.'
'Feng Xu?'
'You didn't want to stay in your homeland, and insisted on wandering the land with me. 'Feng Xu' means the dandelion seeds drifting in the wind, and it describes you perfectly.
'Doesn't that make the name sound sad?'
'It could also be a name that represents freedom.'
'Freedom... did you come to Sargon all the way from Yan in search of freedom?'
...
'I read a Yanese poem this morning.'
'Tell me about it.'
'Life is like dandelion seeds in the wind; all the joys and sorrows scattered. It's like the poem was talking about my name!'
'...Has there been more joy or more sorrow in your life?'
'Joy, of course!'
'...Why do you say that?'
'I'm standing here listening to you talk about difficult things, rather than sleeping under the sand, or being turned into a rock by Oripathy. Am I not the lucky one? That means I have so much more joy in my life than I have sorrow!'
'Ahem... it seems you have too much time on your hands. Have you memorized all the medicine books?'
'I'll get to it right now!'
archives:
'Don't worry, Taraxacum is getting along quite well with the others. He brought some Victorian gummies for the kids when he came to Medical yesterday.'

Nian had talked about Taraxacum before he came to Rhodes Island, telling us that he was a student of her younger brother's, a highly skilled Yanese physician. Many operators from Yan assumed Taraxacum must be a native of Yan as well, and prepared 'homeland' treats such as spring tea from Lungmen and rock tea from Shangshu. It was thus a big surprise to everyone to see Taraxacum in the flesh.
While Taraxacum's appearance was obviously not Yanese, he spoke the language fluently, with an elegant if slightly archaic vocabulary. He knew the regions and seasons of all the teas, and had good knowledge of the associated local customs and traditions. When asked if he had spent a lot of time in Yan, Taraxacum said he had passed through the country, but never taken up residence there.
Though he was not a fellow countryman, Taraxacum nevertheless quickly became friends with the Yanese operators. After all, he could make authentic Lungmen herbal tea, and knew the recipes for all the traditional healthy snacks.

[Letter addressed to Nian]
I hope this letter finds you well, sister.
...
There is one more thing. I hear you have frequently visited Rhodes Island in recent years. I have seen their medicine on my journeys, and would like to pay a personal visit, but I am about to travel to a very dangerous area, so I have sent Taraxacum to Rhodes Island ahead of me. Look out for him if you have the time. If not... try to keep him in one piece.

Two pieces of equipment carried by Taraxacum caught the attention of other operators during weapon registration. An inspection revealed the detailed designs of their components: the core unit of the 'Medicine Pot' casting staff was sculpted in the style of ancient Sargonian jewelry, while the medicine storage equipment in the shape of a dandelion seed head is reminiscent of portable medical equipment used on the battlefield. The three decorative chimes seem to originate from a market near the borders of Yan, and the skateboard that can briefly fly while carrying a person was clearly inspired by trending Columbian flying machines. It took a few days for Engineering to ascertain the two weapons' safety—meanwhile, inquiries with local branches reveal an exact match between the parts' places of origin, and Taraxacum's self-report of his recent travels. Surprisingly, this young Kuranta boy has already journeyed across almost half of Terra with his teacher. We were even more surprised by his statement that he carries his jet skateboard in order to deliver medicine to patients more quickly. We believed his story because he always seemed serious about things, until we saw him excitedly sign up for the on-deck capture-the-flag game, only to be forced to forfeit when his skateboard malfunctioned. The real kicker is that he snuck into the kitchen after the competition and devoured five servings of Yanese barbecue, paying no heed at all to the healthy eating that he normally preaches... Maybe the kid just likes to skate. Say, did he go off to take lessons from Aciddrop again? [Rhodes Island Library Borrowing Log] Date: Feb 16 User: Taraxacum Item: Basic Principles of Flying Machines, Overview of Levitation Technology Taraxacum? Yes, he's been coming into Engineering, but he really knows nothing about engineering... What's he doing there? You saw his jet skateboard and casting staff, right? They're pretty fine, alright. Apparently, both were gifts from his Yanese teacher, so he has to try to maintain them himself when his teacher's not around. Seems like a pretty trendy teacher, if he can make a jet skateboard. But Taraxacum also said his teacher was old... Well, he's probably a trendy old guy, like Chongyue. —On-duty Engineering Operator

Taraxacum's favorite haunt is the hospital. Medical Department staff told us that Taraxacum was not particularly impressive when he first arrived: his medical knowledge was quite haphazard, causing concerns for the department head. But he demonstrated outstanding aptitude when it came to practical work, and was easily able to follow Dr. Warfarin's instructions, even when she was using technical jargon. We learned that this was the result of his instruction under his mentor. According to Taraxacum, his teacher rarely spoke or gave him systematic instruction in medical knowledge, but always took him along on patient visits, giving him the opportunity to observe and learn. Taraxacum was also periodically given a thick stack of ancient Yanese medical books, telling him to study them himself and ask questions if there was anything he did not understand. Taraxacum gradually grew into the role of assistant, and accumulated considerable clinical experience, though his education was somewhat antiquated by the standards of modern systematic medicine. It seems his teacher Fāng, younger brother of Nian's, shares a few common features with Dusk, especially when she first came to Rhodes Island. Was Dr. Fāng a reclusive hermit, just like Dusk? 'What's my master like? I guess he does sound like the kind of reclusive sages you find in Yanese dramas, but he's actually quite familiar with modern medical technology and equipment! Then why am I so unfamiliar with the medical department's instruments? Well... I don't get a lot of chances to see new stuff, always being on the road with my master! Besides—' He strokes the beard that he does not have. 'Master Fāng said: You haven't even mastered the basic Yanese medical books yet. The newer stuff can wait...'

[From the Candleholder Archives] July 1st, 9am The proxy has entered Sargon, providing basic medical assistance to villages he passed. No unusual activity. July 21st, 9pm The proxy has entered the northwest desert, where a small Catastrophe had recently struck. Fāng is looking for survivors... July 22nd, 5am A young boy around the age of seven ran into the village carrying a handful of herbs. He had gone into the hills after the Catastrophe, in search of medicinal herbs known to the locals through oral tradition. Fāng said the herbs might soothe the pain, but would be of little help in saving lives. The boy himself is in serious condition. September 21st Two months have passed since the last entry. The boy has recovered. As for the others... there is little time left for them. Fāng has done all that he could, giving the boy a chance to say goodbye to his family. September 23rd, 6pm The proxy has left the village, but the boy continues to follow and cannot be persuaded to turn back. It is not my place to judge their actions... but Fāng has seen the same scene too many times, even during my tenure as his Candleholder alone. He must not allow his compassion to run unchecked. He cannot help everyone... On the other hand, there are no other survivors in the village. Could the boy really survive in this desert, if he does not follow Fāng? October 26th The proxy has tacitly consented to the boy following him. His true intentions are unknown at this time. 'I've consented to you following me this far.' —Comment in a corner of the page November 7th Fāng has given the boy a Yanese name—'Feng Xu', a nickname for the plant Taraxacum, otherwise known as dandelion. He has permitted the boy to observe him at work. Despite his youth, the boy seems to have experience in operating vehicles. It was his suggestion that helped us avoid a spot of quicksand this morning... 'Verify the boy's identity, and his intentions for coming into contact with the proxy.' Verification complete. No irregularities were found. Feng Xu's personal statement is attached: I... I just didn't know what to do. I simply wanted to survive, no matter what... I'll drive carts and pick herbs for you and Master. I'll do anything... anything that I can help with! ...Are you Master's bodyguard? You follow him all the time, but hardly ever talk to him... 'Sui Regulator'? Master said the word 'Sui' means time... an organization that regulates time? Yan is such a strange land. [Final Page] Many years have passed since. It is almost time for me to retire, though my heart is at ease, knowing that there will be someone there to take care of Fāng... Feng Xu is almost as tall as Fāng now. 'Thank you for everything.' —Comment in a corner of the page

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: It is good that you can handle paperwork on your own. As we are now in cooperation, I shall point out any mistakes within these documents. This contingency plan, for instance. I do not believe my name should be under the column labeled 'Pending Repair'?

Those who wish to stop the fighting may wield weapons, but their hearts are filled with kindness. Only dunces who adore conflict would see this as an empty threat… Unskilled in battle? Haha, no, no. Rather, it is an unwillingness to fight. Non-aggression first requires a capacity for aggression. In times of need, this crossbow shall reveal its full might.

It was no easy task bringing this war to a peaceful end. But the things the people of Yan must consider are far from over. How shall the annals about this war be written? How shall that one weiqi stone be judged…? Alas, all the myriad tales of this land had to first be scribed and sung by the people who lived through them.

Doctor, that Nian girl has come to find me in a rush, no doubt to continue our discussion on the remodeling plan, so I shall have to excuse myself. Hmm? That's not why? She just needs one more mahjong player? Feh, smiths should be focused on their craft, on hammering and smelting techniques. Imagine indulging in such wanton pleasures—I shall have to give her a good talking to.

That is the girl who barred ten thousand men with a single sword that day? Not bad. She possesses backbone most chivalrous. She asks for no more than 'justice', but that is such a heavy word, heavier than thirty thousand catties… Though her principles be high, in the end, she shall suffer for them.

Reading about the history of Yan? This book's usage of words such as 'campaign' or 'suppression' is of some interest. I am weary of violence, but I do not completely reject it. Fending off bandits, defending one's home, toppling tyrants, castigating the wicked… Such battles are unavoidable. What I tire of is the unjust war.

The younglings of your Engineering Department oft flee to my workshop when they are idle. It is good that they are so eager to learn, but so many components they discard after only one or two uses. Such wastefulness must be disciplined. What? It's junk? Says who? Allow me to provide them a demonstration!

To peer at the mounts, rivers, lakes, and ponds, and learn of all natural laws they hold… That was the creed of that old carpenter. 'Tis a pity people only remember his wondrous mechanisms, and not his desire to create a better world. Even his apprentices and disciples have become the way they are now. One's intentions can easily change, for the human heart is but a thread of silk. One cannot be inattentive.

Take this burr puzzle. I simply cannot figure out this toy myself… It should be no problem for a dexterous crafter? Haha, the more you ponder its trick, the more agitated your heart grows, until eventually, you forget even the most basic, simplest solutions. Which is why I say no need to overthink it.
Falling into a dream? The hungry must be fed, the cold must be clothed, the weary must be given rest… This Rhodes Island… At times, it truly does resemble an age of peace.
It is my pleasure to finally meet you. I am Ju, a craftsman. We have met before? Haha, perhaps you have met with my creations. Or perhaps, it is simply two lovers of truth recognizing one another.
Skillful use of arms to douse a fire. Beautiful. Precise.
Those with ability are commended. Rhodes Island's ways are proper.

How do you treat those different from you? Rhodes Island's answer has given me much to chew upon. Ahem… My prior frankness was due to candor and determination. Though the world may change, my heart does not. You are much the same.
This battlefield… Just like before.
Listen to me: use defense for offense, use stillness against movement.
With blades drawn, stride forward, you noble hearts.
String your bows, nock your arrows. Harm not those repentant.
With faultless reasoning comes your duty's perfection.
Neither great victory nor great defeat is the way of truth.
All my eyes see are they who seek the unreachable, milling in confusion…
Hold fast to a corner, thus aggressing without attacking.
With fell of swoop, remove all absurdity.
With flash of thought, extinguish all suffering.
With shift of step, separate all falsity.
To insist upon violence is… improper.
A victory of words, effortless yet bloodless. Very good.
A victory with few deaths can comfort the heart.
Though your foe remains, do not chase them like mad beasts.
I shall use other means to defend us. You retreat first.
Cleanliness and neatness are good. If you were to dismantle this couch, you shall save yourself much hassle.
Is aught the matter?
Take care not to startle the fowlbeasts on my shoulder.
Arknights.

I am uninterested in careful consideration of elaborate displays. 'Tis a rare holiday, so this cannon in my hand can prove its worth today! See its radiance, the power of its shock! Hoho, there is no opportunity on normal days to act so rashly. Still just standing there? Not lively enough for you? The next round shall be yours, then.
Shall we discuss whatever ingenious ideas you have?

This thing they call time is too difficult for me to perceive. Perhaps the day of your birth can be used as a different sort of marker along this long journey… Is this what you eat on a marker day? Ahem. Though I often speak of being economical, today is different. Let us have Little Carpenter fetch you a couple of Ding Feng Lou's best dishes!

Dedication to truth is not easy, to walk righteously is especially hard, but what you do, so unlike ordinary folk, is difficult beyond measure. The road under your feet may not be solid, but do not forget to take the time to look behind you. Those following you will happily brave flame and blade for you, unafraid of death… Me? Haha, I count myself among them.

This battlefield… Just like before.
Listen to me: use defense for offense, use stillness against movement.
With blades drawn, stride forward, you noble hearts.
String your bows, nock your arrows. Harm not those repentant.
With faultless reasoning comes your duty's perfection.
Neither great victory nor great defeat is the way of truth.
All my eyes see are they who seek the unreachable, milling in confusion…
Hold fast to a corner, thus aggressing without attacking.
With fell of swoop, remove all absurdity.
With flash of thought, extinguish all suffering.
With shift of step, separate all falsity.
To insist upon violence is… improper.
A victory of words, effortless yet bloodless. Very good.
A victory with few deaths can comfort the heart.
Though your foe remains, do not chase them like mad beasts.
I shall use other means to defend us. You retreat first.
Cleanliness and neatness are good. If you were to dismantle this couch, you shall save yourself much hassle.

Take care not to startle the fowlbeasts on my shoulder.
Arknights.

Hoho, there is no opportunity on normal days to act so rashly. Still just standing there? Not lively enough for you? The next round shall be yours, then.
Shall we discuss whatever ingenious ideas you have?

This thing they call time is too difficult for me to perceive. Perhaps the day of your birth can be used as a different sort of marker along this long journey… Is this what you eat on a marker day? Ahem. Though I often speak of being economical, today is different. Let us have Little Carpenter fetch you a couple of Ding Feng Lou's best dishes!

Dedication to truth is not easy, to walk righteously is especially hard, but what you do, so unlike ordinary folk, is difficult beyond measure. Haha, I count myself among them.

handbook.profile: Ju, an unemployed wanderer who roams the wilderness of Yan. He has vast experience and knowledge, and his unique nature gives him considerable historical value. He is at Rhodes Island at the Doctor's invitation, serving as an engineering consultant.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
A joint examination by the Medical and Engineering Departments indicates high torso density with no presence of abnormal shadows. Originium granule readings in the circulation and motor systems are within normal parameters and show no signs of activity. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Machine-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Ju's parts were calibrated and carefully reassembled during the examination.

[Coolant Originium-Crystal Density] 0.005u/L
We are happy to announce that Ju has shared his body's detailed damping data with us, providing significant assistance to the Engineering Department's maintenance work!

It took seventeen checks before Ju told us that there was no need to conduct further examinations, as the equipment was not malfunctioning. It was blatantly obvious that he just wanted to study the equipment...
—A Medical Department Operator
handbook.promotionRecord:
Ju left the Shanhaizhong, but his rules remained.
The principles that he often repeated, demonstrated by example, and etched upon bamboo slips and his followers' hearts, formed an invisible barrier that continued to protect the Shanhaizhong after his departure.
When he was still there, however, the rules were alive too. They grew with his words and deeds, adapted to changing times, and could be tailored to the context. Ju was able to determine when to be strict and when to be flexible, who to trust and who to be on guard against, which principles were temporary and which were fundamental.
The rules died when he left. The Shanhaizhong carried on his teachings, living in the wilds that he made, and were unable to respond to lawless violence and unbound malice.
Principles become dogma when removed from their context. Ju's followers remembered every word he said, but not necessarily the spirit behind them. Their descendants may treat his teachings as scripture, but the message inevitably deviated from the original meaning as it was passed from one generation to the next.
Ju understood this limitation well. He could protect a city or a community, but not everything. He could teach a person or a group, but he could not ensure that his teachings were properly understood and utilized. His life is long, but not eternal. Feranmuts are powerful, but not omnipresent.
Ju has thought about whether it would have been better if they had never followed him and never formed the Shanhaizhong. Perhaps they would have found their own respective paths, and perhaps they would not have died in the name of his teachings.
But would they really have had a better fate, if they had never met him?
He does not know the answer. Maybe there isn't one.
Rules become forgotten or distorted; perhaps people need to learn to love each other by their own instincts.

I don't ask for my ideals to be remembered. It's enough to know that they have made someone suffer less and commit less evil, sometime, somewhere.
—Ju
archives:
Ju's examination was conducted under the curious gaze of many eyes. We tried to explore his secrets, but other than basic mechanics, there seemed to be little in common between his body and modern technology. We have yet to ascertain how it works, but by his own claims, he spent much of his 'new life' wandering the farmlands of Yan—this was the truth behind the household tale of the 'machine man' that has scared many a Yanese child. Ju himself views it from a different perspective: he believes he has done a good thing by stimulating people's curiosity toward the unknown.

As Ju's body can be freely disassembled, Engineering recommended that we publish details of several incidents in order to mitigate the impact that an 'accidental' loss of parts may have on other operators.

Incident 1: An engineering operator inquired about the structure of Ju's head at their first meeting, for research purposes. Ju proceeded to remove his head and gave a detailed lecture. The operator froze for ten minutes, terminated all research into Ju, and received psychological counseling at the Medical Department.

Incident 2: During maintenance work, an operator discovered a row of fingers on the worktable and assumed that a safety incident had occurred. Ju apologized for the misunderstanding and promised to arrange the fingers in the shape of a smiley face next time to avoid unnecessary panic.

Incident 3: The Logistics Department reported that an operator found a mechanical arm on the edge of a training field early in the morning, tapping the ground rhythmically with its index finger. On-duty personnel investigated the incident after they heard the operator's screams. An investigation revealed that Ju had left his arm behind to let it watch other operators train for him and learn from their techniques when he finished the calibration checks the night before, and had forgotten to retrieve it.

[Analysis report of current data on Ju]
File Number: 0375687
Classification Level: ■■

This is an unusual investigation: the entity sitting opposite us is not flesh and blood, but a mechanical body made from countless intricate components, containing the consciousness and memories of an ancient Yanese Feranmut. Ju's form was destroyed in the war, and his current vessel was built during a time that he claims was 'insignificant'. When asked why he kept it, Ju said, 'Taking human form is one way to understand humanity.' This helped us understand the importance of Ju's principles to himself—his current form may be considered an extension of his ideals and philosophy. We can see an inkling of this from the Sui Regulator's files:
From a worldly perspective, the result of an attack is determined by victory and defeat, and that is how history is written. But Ju seeks to answer a more fundamental question: What is victory? To Ju, the nature of attack lies in a lack of mutual love. People loved themselves but not others; they loved their community, but did not care about other communities. As such, they viewed others from a perspective of pillage rather than respect, destroying cities, killing people, expanding territory, and flexing their power. But the dead do not come back to life, shattered families cannot be repaired, and trampled pride cannot be restored. The victor stands atop a mountain of bones, basking in glory earned with blood. In the course of history, war is abstracted into a conflict of interests between nations or factions, but Ju sees war through the lens of each individual victim. Children who lost their father, mothers who buried their sons, survivors despairing amongst the ruins... they are not numbers, nor pieces on a chessboard.
Ju told us, 'The victor does not love.' Indeed, he believes that anyone engaged in victory and defeat cannot love.
Ju spoke of wars that became far more than what the instigators expected—a campaign that began under the banner of justice became an indiscriminate massacre; an act of self-defense became another invasion. War has its own logic and rarely stops when the one who began it pleases. Those who partake in it become drawn into its logic, and are driven to do things they would not have under ordinary circumstances, regardless of the ideals they once held.
Based on what we know, Ju and his followers participated in several actions to stop war. These were not grand events filled with fanfare—they simply arrived on scene before the siege began and attempted to persuade the belligerents to lay down arms. Sometimes it worked, sometimes it didn't. At times, they helped poorly defended cities improve their defenses. At others, he went alone to beseech the aggressor to stop the conflict. He cares nothing for personal gain and loss, only for the hope that human dignity would not be trampled by martial strength.
For Ju, victory is not the vanquishing of the foe, but the elimination of hostility. It is not about occupying territory, but winning over people's hearts. Those who rely on violence may win this day, but they are simply setting the stage for their defeat tomorrow. The same applies to the war between humanity and Feranmut. Ju could not stop it, but at least he provided a standard to judge right and wrong, a framework for reflection. The power of thought is already being exercised if people ask themselves whether peaceful coexistence is truly a fleeting dream when they take up arms.
At the close of the meeting, Ju told us that he does not expect his ideals to change everything. He has only done what he thinks should be done, following in his own nature. His ideas are like seeds—people centuries later will not remember which seed grew into the great tree, but hope will live on as long as it exists.

In the beginning, when the primal void first gave way to order, people urgently sought peace and plenty, and the learned folks of the time traveled the land to express their convictions. Some advocated ruling through courtesy, others through law. Some said the government should be quiet and stay out of everyday life, others saw strength and strategy as the way. It was a time of chaos, yet in chaos there was vitality; a time of conflict, yet through conflict came progress. Different schools had different ideas, but all harbored the same hope of making the land a better place.
It was an era that was never seen again.

It was a time of infinite possibilities. Perhaps there was a chance for humanity to coexist peacefully with Feranmuts, but it was buried by Its will and obsession.
—Ju

The war for which Sui was responsible drove an irreparable rift between humanity and Feranmuts. New schools of thought had risen prior to the war, emphasizing defense against external threats and securing internal order, distinction between close and distant relationships, and a clearly delineated hierarchy, but all of them came down to emphasizing the existential threat that the difference between humanity and Feranmuts represented. The House of Yan is built upon the decline of the Feranmuts, and so the people must be united and order established, building consensus for the great campaign to come.
In such a climate, Ju's idea of 'universal love' was akin to heresy, scorned for being a pipe dream that ignored the realities of life and the selfishness of humanity. Meanwhile, those who were moved by Ju's ideals and became his followers continued to pursue this distant dream, despite being few in number. Stubborn and rational, they became known as the Shanhaizhong.
But being a Feranmut was a 'sin' in itself. Ju knew that he would only bring doom to his followers if he stayed with them. As the shadow of war spread to the land that he and humanity had developed together, his existence became a sword that hung above the heads of the Shanhaizhong. When war came, the Shanhaizhong lost Ju and were scattered, but they survived.
Centuries passed. The Shanhaizhong have changed. Some offshoots have faded into history, while others have drifted from their ideals over the years. Ju's teachings have become abridged, distorted, or mixed with other ideologies, becoming unrecognizable.
Ju understands the reasons for the change. Hate begets hate, and blood begets blood. 'Centuries' is a long time, enough to turn the most gentle of ideals radical... Obsession can claim even Feranmuts, never mind humans.
These people view Ju with veneration, confusion, and barely disguised disappointment. They expected a leader who would lead them to victory, but all Ju could offer was principles that had been cast aside centuries ago. He is not surprised—he knows that his ideas will never become mainstream, be it past or present.

Ju is not the only one who seeks a path of peace under heaven. Unlike Ju, Hou's ideals are only seen in fragments, often in the form of allegories that are absurd yet thought-provoking. Some see him as a cynical ne'er-do-well, others an idle hermit, but a select few see something deeper in his satire and castigation.
Every encounter between Ju and Hou has ended in a lengthy argument. Their differences seem to be fundamental—Ju advocated for active engagement with the world, changing things with universal love and non-aggression, while Hou thought that such hard work was futile, and it was better to let nature take its course and distance oneself from things.
Ju saw humans as easily deceived and prone to selfishness, and that order would eventually become the accessory of violence if humans were left to judge right or wrong based on their own preferences, turning it into a tool for the strong to oppress the weak. Only by appealing to a higher order that does not easily change can justice find its home, just as craftsmen make vessels from specifications, which in turn are born out of practice.
Meanwhile, Hou sees Ju's attempts to communicate peace through pure rationality as a source of conflict unto itself. For every person who advocates for universal love, there is another who advocates for partial love. For every person who advocates for non-aggression, there is another who advocates for conquest. The more heated the debate of right or wrong, the more chaotic things become. It would be better to forget the differences and let everything settle itself according to fate and nature.
For his part, Ju has long understood that Hou's was a path of compromise and transcendence. It demands that people set aside their obsessions and differences, to be one with heaven and earth through serenity and non-action. Fundamentally, both paths lead to harmonious coexistence, only Ju wants to overcome the barriers separating people with universal love, while Hou wants to eliminate them through transcendence. Their methods may be very different, but there has never been a dispute about each other's goals. They both know that, ultimately, their paths converge upon the same destination.
One of Hou's allegories talks about a great tree with soft and gnarled wood that was no good for building or furniture. No one bothered to cut it down because of its uselessness, and so it lived to a ripe old age, offering its vast canopy shade as shelter. He said that Ju devoted all his life to what was 'useful', such as elaborate and effective siege defense equipment, and concise teachings of a greater good, all efforts that point toward something tangible and actionable. But even the strongest walls can be breached, and the most elaborate equipment solved. The arts of siege defense may protect against one attack, but not the endless greed and hatred of man.
Siege defense equipment will no longer be necessary when people truly forsake aggression. Ju understands this, and it is precisely what he is seeking. The ideal of peace, the mentality of non-aggression, abhorrence of violence—these things can neither be built nor defended, but they are the foundation of all that is material. One is pragmatic, the other transcendent; one wants people to set aside their selfishness and love others as they love themselves; the other wants people to forget there is a difference between oneself and others. Their ideals are so different, and they will continue to think back to the sentiments that their differences created many years into the future. Those arguments only truly carry weight when they come from the mouths of the debaters.

modules.moduleDescription:
He senses an unprecedented blockage. Looking down, He notices the water flowing by His left ribs has been reduced by thirty percent. Curious to find out why, He approaches the field, clad in a blue robe. In the distance, an unfinished dirt dam stretches across the narrowest part of the valley, with water already pooling behind it. It is His interest rather than His ire that is piqued.
'Water's seeping from the rocks, so we'll open a channel that flows down to the mouth.' Atop the dam, a craftsman dressed in brown directs the others, probably their leader.
'Why do you want to cut off the river's flow?' He steps forward and asks.
The craftsman wipes the sweat off his brow. 'To prevent a disaster from happening, of course.'
'Disaster?'
'This mountain region is prone to both droughts and floods, but with a dam, we can control the flow, and store or release the water when needed.'
'But the river has followed nature's course unabated since antiquity. Now you force it to go where you please. Do you not fear angering the river god?'
Some of the others laugh at this, but the craftsman answers coolly: 'The river has its paths to follow, and so do we. Until now, it's taken away our basic right to live, while the gods haven't cared a whit. So it's up to us to change how the river flows.'
For the next few days, He watches silently from the side as the crew toils day and night to reinforce the dam. The craftsman turns around to joke: 'Sir, you stare at us all day, but you look less like a scholar keen for knowledge, and more like an expressionless scarefowl out in the field.' He does not answer, and continues His silent watch.
One month later, a spring rain suddenly descends on the unfinished dam. The workers with the craftsman carry more dirt over, drive piles into the ground, and secure it all with bamboo rope with all the effort they can muster. But the resulting flash flood from the rain sends a muddy wave towards the dam, forcing a rift open. Immediately they rush forward to plug the crack despite risking their own lives. Seeing this, He casually flips His palm over, and the rushing water slows down. They take advantage of this momentary lull to fill the gap with every heavy object they can find. When the rain finally stops, the dam is battered, yet stands. The craftsman heaves a sigh of relief and turns around to see the scholar, still watching him silently in His pristine blue robes.
'We'll have to thank the river god for showing us mercy this time.'
'River god? Shouldn't you be thanking yourselves? Does that not make more sense to you?'
'No.' The craftsman shakes his head. 'I can tell what happened earlier was pure luck and nothing else. 'As for where the luck came from—'
He straightens his back and points at the river behind the dam, gradually slowing down: 'If the sky clears up, we'll open the sluice gates tomorrow and let the water flow. Rest assured, O river god, we're not trying to stop the river, but simply requesting that it flow according to the rules—the seasons.'
'If you say so.' He turns around, about to leave.
'A moment, sir.'
'I keep seeing you wandering around the dam recently. If you could allow me a guess, you have a genuine interest in our creation? If I'm right, why don't you stay?
'Stay here, go to the fields, and see what we've made. Visit our group... and see the path we humans have paved for ourselves.'
'Oh?' He pauses, then turns back.
'Of course, if you'd rather be the scarefowl in the field and wish only to silently watch others from behind, there's nothing wrong with that either.
'Though I'm just curious if you're unwilling to measure it yourself—
'Just how much does this mortal way actually weigh?'

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: What might you want my help with, Doctor? Why don't you decide?

Here's the operational report from the Athenius branch office over the last two quarters. You'll be able to gloss what you need from the summary… Hm? You want to hear me report in detail? Now that would take quite some time. Things have been eventful for me, since my return to Minos.

Doctor! Visiting the Convalescent Garden? Perfect, we can catch up while we—hmm? Is that… Podenco? Did she move her entire bed into the greenhouse? *sigh* I'm barely aboard these days, Doctor. Keep an eye on her so she doesn't overwork herself, please?

All the new names are gradually outnumbering the old on the Garden's guestbook… When melilotus ripens, its slender pods can fire its seeds a great distance away. So too has Rhodes Island ripened… Melancholy? Me? Well, for all you know, I'm only waxing poetic as Minoans do.

Going back to Minos isn't without its own headaches. Minoans all think their dreams of heroism are dashed the moment they contract Oripathy. They become totally apathetic. They hardly even bother with treatment… Do you know what? I'd have those wandering bards touring the Three Poleis, singing tales of how Infected can become heroes too!

People can't help absorbing themselves in their own proficiencies, can they? That's what being a perfumer is for me, and I spent the longest time sheltering within it when I came aboard Rhodes Island. These days… Now that I know I'm made of more than that, I think it's finally, truly become mine.

Origanon, thyme, Athos's parsley... It's back to keeping the Minoan plants I knew best of all in my seed pouch. I used to keep such a distance from these, and now they're in my hands again… These seeds haven't changed a bit, but young Lena would be shocked by just how she's grown.

Me and… Lydia? Oh, dear, I didn't expect that name to come from you… Well, she's one of my cousins, a bit of a dependent type. If you want to know more about her, I can tell you, certainly. But if you want a story, well, I can't say the way it ends is very fun.

Doctor, your fragrance today isn't quite the same as the usual. Did something happen? Or, did you run out of the perfume I gave you…? If it's the latter, then tell me beforehand from now on. How else will I top you off in time?
Doctor? Oh, and you're not even using lavender today. Let's see, I'll just put you on break for the next two hours… Hmm? What on Terra are all these deferred holidays for?

I'm back, Doctor. Oh, these boronias on your desk are fresh. It seems Podenco's been minding you and the Convalescent Garden well. Anyhow, I'm back on Rhodes Island for a spell. Home for the holidays, I might say… No, no, that's a joke.
Oh… You seem to make more sense to me now, Doctor. I used to think you were a little slapdash here and there, but now I see how almost frighteningly meticulous you are.

When I first took over the Convalescent Garden, I had every intention to spend the rest of my life here, never to leave again… Whenever I intend that, fate points me in a different direction. Still, I'm starting to grow fond of how the 'unexpected' feels.

My odyssey to Minos wasn't as hard as I thought it'd be. It only struck me, when I was standing in front of my family again, just how… old all those old pains had really become. Not worth dwelling on any longer. Now I'm the perfumer Lena of Rhodes Island, and that suits me just splendid.
Certainly. Remember to have everyone double-check their supplies.
Of course. I'm getting quite comfortable in the lead now.
I'll look after you, everyone.
Remember to put safety first.
Doctor?
Someone's deep in thought, Doctor.
I'm in position. Assistance is at the ready.
Don't worry, everyone. I have your positions confirmed.
Deep breaths. Let the odor molecules enter your circulatory system.
I know it stings, but this'll promote your blood flow.
Calm, now. Give your lungs time to exchange those gases.
I know it's bitter, but this'll help ignore the pain.
Mm-hmm… there it is, that incense. I smell it about you from time to time after a high-risk mission. Oh, I've missed it so, Doctor.
I might like to learn your knack for seeing the big picture… Say, in exchange for a 'present', how about you explain it to me when we get back? I have a lot more to mentally juggle these days.
You might need to destress a little, Doctor… Don't let your nerves pull you thin.
Doctor, give the order. I'll conduct the evacuation… Don't let it get to you now, it's alright.
And I'm home.
Today's scent? It's cardamom.
Keep this up, Doctor, and before long you'll have my scent on you.
Arknights.

New Year's certainly takes me back. They light the colossal torch in Athenius, but I think I much prefer to see the white smoke of Rhodes Island as it sails… You think I just wanted to see you? Oh, my, you have seen right through me.
Good morning, Doctor… Oh, my, still half-asleep. Hold on… Give this a smell? How's that, nice and awake now?

Could I invite you to the greenhouse, Doctor? I've been growing a flower that just so happens to be blooming today… What are you laughing about—right, fine, it doesn't 'just so happen'. But there you go, that's my present. Now, will you come to the greenhouse and collect it?

It was through being 'lent' Rhodes Island's ideals that Lena Athopoulou could become 'Dr. Lena'. It's the kind of future that the young Lena could never have imagined, and yet it's better than I ever dared dream… I get to be here with you all, doing the right thing. I couldn't be happier with that.

I'm back, Doctor. Oh, these boronias on your desk are fresh. It seems Podenco's been minding you and the Convalescent Garden well. Anyhow, I'm back on Rhodes Island for a spell. Home for the holidays, I might say… No, no, that's a joke.
Oh… You seem to make more sense to me now, Doctor. I used to think you were a little slapdash here and there, but now I see how almost frighteningly meticulous you are.

When I first took over the Convalescent Garden, I had every intention to spend the rest of my life here, never to leave again… Whenever I intend that, fate points me in a different direction. Still, I'm starting to grow fond of how the 'unexpected' feels.

My odyssey to Minos wasn't as hard as I thought it'd be. It only struck me, when I was standing in front of my family again, just how… old all those old pains had really become. Not worth dwelling on any longer. Now I'm the perfumer Lena of Rhodes Island, and that suits me just splendid.
Certainly. Remember to have everyone double-check their supplies.
Of course. I'm getting quite comfortable in the lead now.
I'll look after you, everyone.
Remember to put safety first.
Doctor?
Someone's deep in thought, Doctor.
I'm in position. Assistance is at the ready.
Don't worry, everyone. I have your positions confirmed.
Deep breaths. Let the odor molecules enter your circulatory system.
I know it stings, but this'll promote your blood flow.
Calm, now. Give your lungs time to exchange those gases.
I know it's bitter, but this'll help ignore the pain.
Mm-hmm… there it is, that incense. I smell it about you from time to time after a high-risk mission. Oh, I've missed it so, Doctor.
I might like to learn your knack for seeing the big picture… Say, in exchange for a 'present', how about you explain it to me when we get back? I have a lot more to mentally juggle these days.
You might need to destress a little, Doctor… Don't let your nerves pull you thin.
Doctor, give the order. I'll conduct the evacuation… Don't let it get to you now, it's alright.
And I'm home.
Today's scent? It's cardamom.
Keep this up, Doctor, and before long you'll have my scent on you.
Arknights.

New Year's certainly takes me back. They light the colossal torch in Athenius, but I think I much prefer to see the white smoke of Rhodes Island as it sails… You think I just wanted to see you? Oh, my, you have seen right through me.
Good morning, Doctor… Oh, my, still half-asleep. Hold on… Give this a smell? How's that, nice and awake now?

Could I invite you to the greenhouse, Doctor? I've been growing a flower that just so happens to be blooming today… What are you laughing about—right, fine, it doesn't 'just so happen'. But there you go, that's my present. Now, will you come to the greenhouse and collect it?

It was through being 'lent' Rhodes Island's ideals that Lena Athopoulou could become 'Dr. Lena'. It's the kind of future that the young Lena could never have imagined, and yet it's better than I ever dared dream… I get to be here with you all, doing the right thing. I couldn't be happier with that.

handbook.profile: The Doctor and the Medical Department have approved 'Perfumer' Lena's request for temporary assignment to the Minos region, where she will direct the newly established Athenius office in establishing a local system for Oripathy treatment. Operator Podenco will supervise the Convalescent Garden while Lena is away.
handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 3%
Minor infection. Crystal formations have not been observed on the surface of the body.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.2u/L
Operator possesses significant medical knowledge and cooperates with treatment. Her condition is under control.

Certain herbal remedies have been demonstrated to be effective in containing the progression of Oripathy. While the medical benefit of fragrances in Oripathy treatment has not been established, it can certainly have a relaxing effect, or allow the subject to temporarily set aside deeply-rooted biases. As an Infected from Minos, she has a more personal understanding of the interaction between psychology and Oripathy than you and I.
—Warfarin
handbook.promotionRecord:
Lena wrinkled her nose. The corridor smelled strange. She had returned briefly from the Athenius branch office, and her ride back to Minos was leaving in twenty minutes, but she smelled something burning as she passed near the Convalescent Garden. The smell was acrid and aggressive, not like ordinary fire, more like some kind of Originium Arts. An enemy attack? But there was also a familiar scent, some kind of bright and sunny flower. The names of a dozen flowers flashed across Lena's mind, but none of them seemed to be the answer. Then she heard scattered sounds coming from behind the garden's door, and the smell grew even more chaotic, without rhyme or reason. For the first time, Lena found herself at a loss as to what was happening behind the door. The unfamiliar sound and smell made her uneasy, but this was the Convalescent Garden, the garden she had built with her own two hands. Lena clutched her staff and pulled the door open sharply—
'So... it was your handiwork I smelled, Podenco?'
'Yes! It's a brand-new essence I developed while you were away!'
'Was it part of the plan to have Beanstalk's metal crab run around with various fragrances?'
'Yes! It helped hide the scent of the small cake from you. Peacake had a lot of fun too!'
'Was Flamebringer in on the surprise as well?'
'He made a charred smell as part of the disguise. Said it was repayment for the flower seeds you gave him!'
Lena shook her head, but her ears betrayed her joy at how a group of operators who had only met because of Rhodes Island and the Convalescent Garden went through all this trouble just to fool her sense of smell and give her a surprise. She blew out the candles, and found herself in no particular hurry to go back to her other home. Why not spend a little more time with her friends here in the garden?
archives:
A caladium plant on one of the Convalescent Garden's shelves was the first to notice that something was off with Lena. Highly sensitive to changes in moisture, the plant had heretofore received the most tender care possible in the greenhouse, but now the edges of the leaves had begun to grow yellow, only returning to their previous color when Podenco discovered the issue and recalibrated the humidifier. Numerous minor incidents like this continued to occur throughout the week—pruning shears not being returned to their proper place, pesticide cans being filled with water, plant names spelled wrong on fragrance tags... When Podenco witnessed the normally steady and dependable Lena mix up pepper and cardamom, resulting in a sneezing fit, she was convinced of one thing: her performance evaluation had begun.
Lena had always been meticulous about the Convalescent Garden, after all. She hardly ever made errors, and would certainly not break the rules that she herself had set. She had built the garden from a few seeds and design books that she brought from her homeland, carefully picking the right flowers to grow, and developing it into a space for fragrance therapy. It was a labor of love, her pride, and one of the most popular hangouts for Rhodes Island operators.
It thus came as a shock when Podenco anxiously completed her seventeenth 'evaluation item', and learned that Lena was leaving to become the supervisor of the Athenius office. Perhaps this trip home had special meaning to Lena, or perhaps she received a letter from an old acquaintance inviting her to reveal some hidden past... Podenco realized that Lena was testing whether she was ready to take over management of the Convalescent Garden, which implied that Lena was likely not coming back. The empathetic Perro sniffled as she expressed her worries to an HR operator while preparing a parting gift for Lena.

Why am I going back to Minos? Heh, tell Podenco not to overthink it. I knew Rhodes Island was going to establish a new office in Athenius, and it just made perfect sense that I should be involved. I was a little concerned about what would happen to the garden, but she has been particularly passionate about her work lately. It would have been a much harder decision if not for her. Huh? A performance evaluation? Oh dear, I didn't even realize I've been causing so much trouble for her... I suppose the prospect of returning home has made me nervous.
—Lena's explanation when submitting her disembarkment application

Many came to see the scion of the famous Athopoulou family when the Rhodes Island office was first established. From her botanical fragrance, to her gentle words, to the meticulous craftsmanship of her dress... everything about her was the very image of a well-bred young lady. She took young patients into the hills to pick herbs on sunny days, teaching them about the leaves and roots of medicinal plants, and the process that turned them into medicine to relieve pain. She told children who feared that their illness would prevent them from becoming heroes that they themselves would be the first person they saved, and it would be their first step on the path to becoming a hero.
Surprisingly, Dr. Lena has received mixed reviews in the office's recent patient surveys. One patient complained that she had banned her from drinking, catching her in under thirty minutes no matter which establishment she went to and preventing her from emulating Bacchus the Drunken Hero. Another lamented that he could not do the work he loved anymore, as he was no longer allowed to swing a hammer with his Originium-covered arm to make weapons in the traditional manner.
Most patients did not believe that the gentle doctor would use forceful measures, until one day a hulking and ferocious patient came rushing out of the consultation room to complain about her at the front desk. The man, a well-known ruffian, claimed that she had insulted his veneration of Heraces, and was trying to record his name in a book so that everyone would know he was a weak Infected. But he quickly lowered his raised fist at the sight of her coming out of the consultation room with her staff in hand, calmly explaining that registration was necessary for the establishment of an emergency medical system, and that the man's actions had demonstrated that he does not truly venerate the heroes, only the muscles that allowed him to bully the weak. She prescribed medicine for the troublemaker, and a bottle of pheromones labeled 'Your Heroic Spirit'.
The concept of 'hero' is a vague one, and everyone's understanding of 'heroic spirit' is different. The idea that Oripathy saps the heroic spirit, an ancient saying of unknown origin, has become a widespread belief in Minos. Even without discrimination from others, those suffering from Oripathy will leave the temples of their own accord, abandon their dreams, and even turn to a life of crime. Fortunately, operators at the office know that all they need to do with patients who have given in to despair is drag them into Lena's consultation room, and their dependable supervisor will use the fragrances of plants to calm her countrymen down.

The HR operator lost his way when he came to the 'Mountain-Rimmed Garden' for the first time. When he asked two Athenians where to find the supervisor of the local office, one said that the 'Flora of Athopoulou' was the only Oripathy doctor he knew, before being interrupted by his companion, who said, 'Do not compare an Infected to a hero, even if Dr. Lena has indeed done a lot for us.'
Flora is one of the heroes worshipped by Minoans, the legendary gardener of the 'Mountain-Rimmed Garden'. It is said that she had a superhuman affinity for plants, being instinctively in tune with the breath of nature, even bringing back dead flowers to life. She is the patron hero of Minoans who worked with plants, herbs, and perfumes, and Operator Perfumer's family was no exception. The Athopoulous were once one of the most famous families of Athenius, one that both gardeners and fashion-seeking merchants depended on. The family has long since fallen from its high perch, and most of its members have left Athenius, but there are many who still remember the former head of the family, Steros Athopoulou, and his daughter who left for distant lands at a young age.
Having learned of this past, the HR operator now sat in Perfumer's consultation room, listening to grateful patients call her the 'Flora of Athopoulou'. Seeing no reaction from Lena, the curious operator asked if she felt uncomfortable with the title. She looked surprised for a moment, then answered in the negative.
Returning to the office months later, the operator found that patients were no longer calling Lena by that lengthy title. A short distance away, a smartly dressed, gray-haired Vulpo with a cold expression on her face was writing up a citizen who had committed an offense. She stopped the operator when she saw the Rhodes Island's logo on his clothes, and their conversation was recorded as follows:
'How much do you know about Lena—or rather, 'Operator Perfumer'? How much do you know about the Athopoulou family?
'You've heard what the patients called her... you asked her how she felt? Hah, did you expect her to tell you the truth?
'Of course she was used to it. For the better part of two decades, she sat at the breakfast table every morning hearing her father sing her praises, calling her the brightest the family had ever seen and the 'Flora of Athopoulou', as if those words would do more to help her grow than the cystymilk on the table.
'Of course she could always let go of her past. Most of the family have left Athenius at my 'behest', but why remind her of those days when she was kept chained by training and rules? ...Even if she might not think of it the same way.
'Anyway, I've dealt with the matter. No one will bring it up ever again.
'Why? Because as a former member of the family, I hated the name Athopoulou as much as she did, that's all.'

A medic found a special notebook in the flowerbeds at the branch office, recording the common and scientific names of plants, as well as short comments written in Minoan—a little dictionary of plants, so to speak. She initially thought it was written by a child who idolized Lena, but it was Lena herself who showed up at the lost-and-found. Lena told the curious operator that she had indeed written those notes herself; however, their purpose was not so much to remember, but to forget.
Lena left Athenius years ago under unspoken pressure from her family, attempting to restart her perfuming career and botany studies elsewhere, but ran into difficulties with communication. The language and naming conventions of the Minoans were shaped by their love of poetry and stories, so without an actual physical object, it was impossible to explain to a Victorian merchant what a 'Reflection of Narcissus' was, and she had a hard time progressing her perfuming work until she memorized the names of plants in the common tongue.
'This was the most basic thing, and what I would tell any Minoan child who wanted to follow in my footsteps. But the truth is, I never spoke the names of plants in Minoan after I left my homeland... I hated them.' The operator's impression of Lena had always been one of polite gentleness. She rarely if ever recalled Lena directly expressing her like or dislike of something. Yet it seems her return to Minos—this 'home' that once rejected her—had caused her to abandon her restraint. 'The scientific naming of plants is structured and objective, reflecting a precise truth, such as their family, genus and species, their discoverer, and their characteristics. Minoan names for plants are vague and ambiguous, full of meticulous poetry. I understand its beauty as well as anyone, but I also understand how it causes people to place expectations upon those names.'
Having grown up shouldering the expectations of her family, it was fortuitous that Lena had a natural affinity for plants and nature. She gladly accepted coursework far beyond what was reasonable for a child, the massive amount of plant names and etymology she was expected to memorize, and her father's pop quizzes, all in the name of her love and passion. At the time, she did not understand the compromise that her harmonious relationship with her family was built upon. Not until she left Athenius and saw flowers from her homeland again did she realize the burden that all the names and stories of plants she memorized had become. She could no longer find it in herself to call them by the names she once knew them by.
On this return to her homeland, and in her communications with patients, Lena once again hears the stories and names of plants that she spent more than a decade memorizing. But she understands that her patients are calling to her in the same way she might instinctively say the name of a familiar plant in Minoan as she gathers herbs in the forests of Athenius alone. The burdens of the past are lifted, and she once again flips through the 'dictionary', communicating with Minoans in the words they are most familiar with. She is now able and willing to extend a helping hand.

modules.moduleDescription:
Perhaps it's homesickness, my dear Lydia. Recently, I've been recalling the days when I'd lead you around the garden and teach you how to tell the plants apart. I am ashamed to say that only long after I left Athenius did I realize there are times when perfumes are of no use.
'The Convalescent Garden is just as it sounds: a garden of flowers that cast a spell on me, and where I thought the scent of Athenius still lingered. Only when I went to a real battlefield, when I visited those makeshift hospitals with all their medical supplies exhausted, did I try mixing soothing perfumes for the wounded. But no matter how strong the scent, they could not mask the stench of gunsmoke, blood, and necrosis.
'Oripathy patients also contribute to my feelings of helplessness. I no longer remember how it felt when I got infected, but I do remember wanting you to take that valuable plant back. But on Rhodes Island, I've seen so many tormented by Oripathy... I do not regret what I did, but I too hope no one else will go through the pain I have experienced.
'Perfumes remain important to me, and are my distinctive trait as a doctor. I will continue to delve deeper into our Minoan botanical traditions. That has always been my goal, and whether I inherit the Athopoulou family or not has no bearing on the matter. But our traditions... You must be aware of how much we, be it our family or Minos as a whole, differ from 'today'. There are pros and cons, but I believe we must face them head-on to fully understand why they exist in the first place.
'I left Athenius filled with hatred, and while I've been feeling nostalgia for a long time, still I harbored hesitation. I didn't know what to think or do when I met you or our parents again. But as of now, I will no longer doubt myself. I will return home as a doctor, and perform a doctor's duties.'
Lena puts down her pen and seals the letter, destined to never be sent. She is less than a day's journey away from Athenius, so very close to her homeland. A faint mix of thyme and marjoram wafts through the sky, like the twin moons breathing gently in the night.
She starts packing her belongings, organizing her frequently used medicine, and testing the Rhodes Island-issued stethoscope and detector bands, before finally putting away the perfume bottle she's always had. Her past self wouldn't have brought so many things on a trip, but the more she practices, the more items she packs. Essential and heavy, but they also put her at ease.
Surely her hometown has changed a lot, as well as the kin she was once close to. But some things will never change.
Doctor Lena Athopoulou is returning to Athenius.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: This type of work is not my wheelhouse. I'll do my best, if you can explain it. What should I give you for teaching me? Well, my students bring me beans, grapes, and fins. Would any of those be appropriate?

Is it possible for Rhodes Island to adjust course five degrees to the west? Following this river would bring us across a floodplain. It may not affect Rhodes, but the vegetation there is fragile. The river would... no, I would thank you.
You can come out now, Doctor. The Medical people have left, but I'm sure they'll be back. Why are you avoiding them…? Me? Why bother wasting time treating Oripathy. Every day I still live is a gift.

Medjehtiqedti came looking for you. Remember to get back to her... why are you staring at me like that? I know what kind of place Rhodes Island is, and I won't do anything to the Sargonians here. But don't try telling me to 'empty the bottomless cup of hate' or whatever.

If you ever get to visit Athenius, I could take you for a morning cruise on the Delphi Canal. The city is cool and quiet, with few people on the streets and few boats on the rivers. The sun rises over the temple and upon the canal, glimmering in the morning mist… I hope Minos never changes.

Athenius is not my home. The Sargonians destroyed my home. The Delphi Canal is wonderful, undoubtedly. But even the real Delphi River cannot replace the memory of my river back home, the night-veiled water where the fincatching lamps sway with the current… my first river.

—Oh! …Sorry, Doctor. Did you knock the cup over? I'll clean it up. Sorry if I spooked you, it's just the sudden sound provoked me… I'm fine. Just didn't sleep well after hearing armored burdenbeast hooves in my dreams last night.

Where are you taking me, Doctor? This way leads to the Medical Department, and I don't think you're scheduled for an exam today. I came to repay my debt to Rhodes Island for saving my life, not to get treatment… Alright, if you insist.

I've seen off too many young people who deserved to live longer than me… when I think about how this sort of thing could happen again, I feel… fear. But why do I see the same fear in your eyes, Doctor?
What burdens you so heavily?
The Doctor, is it? Lena said I would find you here. Give me an order, if you need me to do something. Just don't put me together with any Sargonians. It's better for everyone that way.
Did you give the orders in all these battles?
