handbook.profile: Xanthos, former dockmaster and ferryman at the Delphi Canal in Athenius. Resigned after the relic exchange ceremony at the First Temple and was referred to Rhodes Island for Oripathy treatment by Operator Perfumer, providing services as a Guard Operator.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Originium crystals distributed across surface of body, confirmed Infected by medical examination.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 18%
High level of infection, clear signs of Originium infection on his forearm.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.41u/L
Infection has entered mid-stage with clear signs of spreading. Timely treatment at Rhodes Island has been able to keep his condition under control, to an extent.

Operator Varkáris's condition is serious: in addition to Oripathy, there are also numerous scars on his body and burn marks from artillery fire on his face. They are apparently the aftermath of his time fighting the Sargonians with the guerrillas. While we do not know the details, we can easily imagine how intense the battles must have been.
handbook.promotionRecord:
The wounds that Sargon left behind in Minos have yet to fully heal, even in the nomadic city of Athenius, far from the border. Scholars continue to piece together the cultural heritage of Minos prior to the Sargonian occupation, the priests relying on a mix of legend and imagination to recreate the ceremonies and rituals of the past. Ruins of classical buildings litter the streets; few remain intact.
We do not care about that, said the Athenians. We were free. We would build a new glory with our own hands, so long as the spirit of the heroes lived on in our hearts. Athenians smiled, put on plays on the streets, and sang at temple ceremonies, as though they had forgotten the suffering of the past—until Xanthos, the dockmaster, delivered his speech to the people of Athenius at the First Temple.
We do not care, say the Athenians now. We do not care how strong our foe is, nor the price we must pay for freedom, but we will remember the hardships along the way, and remain vigilant of our foe's cunning. And we will not forget to lay a white flower at the graves of our fallen kin.
archives:
HR and Medical were on high alert following the arrival of Xanthos on Rhodes Island. While Rhodes Island has no shortage of operators who hail from countries in conflict with each other, no one calls the Sarkaz 'devils' here, nor do Kazimierzians go for the throats of every Ursine they see. But Xanthos's situation was different. Everyone had heard what happened in Athenius, and the atmosphere at the Medical Department was particularly tense whenever Xanthos came in.
He turned out to be surprisingly well-behaved, and the terrifying scene of Xanthos vs. Dr. Gavial that Lena was worried about enough to specifically warn us of never happened. People were relieved, and perhaps they began to let their guard down.
That was when the accident happened.
Dr. Warfarin had obtained a rare blood sample and was working overtime to study it, messing up the shifts and forgetting to make sure that Dr. Gavial was not on duty when Xanthos came in, resulting in the two of them coming into contact with one another. One was oblivious and the other seemingly unconcerned, but everyone else was quite panicking. Dr. Gavial read the latest checkup report, saw that Xanthos was taking his medication as instructed—bringing his condition under control—and patted his shoulder in approval, with considerable force. Everybody quite freaked out, but Xanthos said nothing. His face was hidden under his mask, but if he took it off, one would probably find a complicated expression on his face. No violence ensued, though, and Dr. Warfarin stopped worrying about staggering the shifts.
Rumors that Operator Narantuya had invited Xanthos to rob Sargonian caravans in the desert with her remain unsubstantiated, as Narantuya had promised us that she had left behind her life of banditry once and for all. All we know is that they did indeed leave the ship together once, but had returned by the time we found out, and refused to talk about what they went out to do, or what happened in the desert.
What we do know is that Xanthos has successfully integrated into Rhodes Island, and there is no concern that he will act aggressively toward operators from Sargon.

Xanthos is definitely cut from the same cloth as Aspasia alright! He's a solid survivor and a fighter—not as good as me of course, but good enough to survive in the desert. Too bad he doesn't want to become my subordinate, but I won't give up so easily!
—Narantuya

By Minoan standards, Xanthos is quite reserved—stiff even. We know that Minoans love drama, as citizen-organized performances are a frequent sight on the streets of Athenius, and Minoan villages often jointly hold small drama festivals during agricultural off-seasons. Xanthos, however, seems to have little interest in it. It is not that he does not know the stories of the heroes—he responds to citations of the legends in conversations—but his own words are always brief and succinct, never quoting proverbs or fables. His upbringing may have something to do with it: Xanthos was raised in a small village in southern Minos, near the border with Sargon. Life was hard even without Sargonian raids. His father died when he was very young, and he inherited his father's work as ferryman. He spent most of his time on the river, and his emotions flowed like the river, never rising or falling by too much. But the river was also fickle, and he had to be vigilant at all times, never letting his guard down. His taciturn and cautious manner is the result of such a life. This is not to imply that he has no hobbies: he has told us that reading poetry was his way of relaxing in those rare moments of leisure. The reasoning was that poems are relatively short, and do not make you forget the time or to monitor the condition of the river. Xanthos showed some interest when I invited him to join our Poetry Club, but began to hesitate upon learning that we get together and recite poems in front of other club members, apparently not used to group activities. My praise of his speech at the First Temple of Athenius seemed to have the opposite effect, as he looked visibly uncomfortable, though I was eventually able to convince him to come. That night, we read poems that we wrote ourselves, and engaged in some impromptu group poetry. Someone brought wine, which I had reservations about, though I must admit that good wine can indeed do wonders for the atmosphere. Once we got a little tipsy, we began to sing while someone played accompaniment, ending on a high note with the climax of the Kerespereia. Xanthos sat in a corner throughout, listening quietly and touching none of the wine (most admirably!), looking somewhat out of place. He continued to attend the meetings, sitting quietly in a corner as he did the first time, saying little except nodding on occasion upon hearing a particularly well-crafted verse. He seems to prefer sentimental odes to narrative epics, and takes a particular liking to the works of a certain female poet from Antisa. It seems that his appearance belies a much more delicate nature. —Erato, in Rhodes Island Poetry Club Report

The training of a priest is a serious matter in Minos. Children found to have the proper aptitude are sent to the temples to receive education and training at the age of ten, studying with a dozen other children of the same age. They are responsible for everyday cleaning and maintenance, while also studying the classics and learning about the heroes and their associated rituals. They also have to study scientific knowledge associated with the temple, as well as accumulate management and administrative experience, all in preparation for a career in the priesthood. The process can take more than a decade, until trainees pass their exams to become full-fledged acolytes. The priests of Minos are therefore among its most talented and educated people.
When we learned that Xanthos's apprentice in Athenius was a former trainee acolyte, we began to wonder—did this mean Xanthos possessed knowledge that rivaled the temples? There was, of course, an element of self-interest in our curiosity: there are patients of every age group at Rhodes Island, including young children who had to abandon their education because of their condition, and we wanted to give them an opportunity to continue learning.
Xanthos seemed to smile wryly behind his mask.
'Lykeion knew much more than I do, in terms of professional knowledge. I dealt with issues that occurred on the river through experience and instinct, accumulated through observation and memorization, while he understood the principles behind them, and could draw on such knowledge to understand things that he had never seen before. It was practical experience that he lacked... but the real reason I took him in as an apprentice was that he needed a reason to keep living after I saved... after he contracted Oripathy. I didn't need a caregiver or companion, but he needed something to fill his life, in order to find the strength to keep going. I'm glad that he's found a new goal.'
Xanthos was humble and did not immediately agree to take on apprentices at Rhodes Island, but we have noticed that he has a way with children, guiding them to fulfill their potential while showing remarkable patience. He tells stories of heroes to crying young patients, competes with Popukar to see who can cut planks faster using a chainsaw (and his oar), and steers Bubble and Ceobe to keep the corridor clear when they are playing in the hallways. Perhaps it comes from his experience observing the river—'one can only sail far and easy by going with the flow,' in his own words—or perhaps he is simply a natural educator.

You want to know about my life in the marshes? It wasn't like what you might find in pastoral poems. Ferrying in the marshes was not like ferrying in Athenius. It was not a simple matter of going from one side of the river to the other. Our village was surrounded by the river. Essentially, we lived in the river. The river was the most important part of life in the marshes; master the river, and you master the marshes. It was formed from rainfall and meltwater from the peaks of Mt. Hymnoi. Spring was the season for planting and irrigation, as the snow began to melt and rainfall declined. I ferried people back and forth between the village and nearby small plots of farmland, separated by the river, while keeping an eye on the snowline in the distant mountains, looking out for sudden floods. Summer was when meltwater was at its highest, the busiest season for irrigation. People guided water into the fields, and harvested young reeds which were used for weaving. Autumn was the season of harvest, with increased rainfall and reduced meltwater. The crops in the fields had to be harvested quickly, and reeds that had grown hard harvested for reserves. The river was calm in winter—villagers used harvested reeds to make handicrafts, and repaired farm tools and houses, while I ferried people between our village and neighboring villages. Reeds were a frequent sight on the river, growing along the river and marshes, forming narrow passages that only those who knew the river well could navigate successfully. Only those few could ferry the others to where fins and fowlbeasts were in abundance. Reeds were versatile materials that could be woven into baskets, mats, even houses and their foundations. We used reeds to mark out areas in the river, and filled them with reed stalks to make floating plates on which we built our homes. It may seem primitive to people used to the nomadic cities, but it was flexible and adaptable to any changes in the river. When Ithakos came, he taught us how to connect these reed plates to create large public areas, upon which we built a little temple and lit a fire that belonged to us... Life was hard, and far from affluent, but it holds a special place in my heart, not only because of the memories of home and my deceased friends and relatives, but also because it was a life that was within my grasp. All I needed to do every day was to understand the river beneath me. The river has since dried up, but it continues to flow in my heart. Having lost sight of my own heart from loss, I'm trying to understand it now, trying to tame it. Perhaps this will allow me to once again grasp my own life.

modules.moduleDescription:
The sky isn't dark yet, but he begins to set up camp. There is no need to rush, he tells himself.
He has resigned from his ferryman job, even though the citizens of Athenius voted to have him stay. With his apprentice gone, he no longer has any time-sensitive responsibilities on his shoulders.
This freedom terrifies him and he knows it: he's slowing down. Compared to when he left his homeland five years ago, the land seems no different now—desolate and quiet. The clearly depicted river on the tattered map in his hand was gone without a trace.
The priest said that snowmelt will eventually form new rivers, but all he sees now is desolation.
An indistinct fear creeps into his heart once more, an emotion he has long been acquainted with. Ever since he embarked on this journey home, when he arrived in Athenius with Ithakos's blood-soaked robes and stayed after the priest invited him to, he had been caught in its clutches. It was the fear that kept him there with no way to return home, that had him unleash his rage and hatred upon the Sargonians. What can he even do if he goes home and realizes the past is gone forever? What else can he chase after?
By now the sky is completely dark. He lowers his oar and retrieves the lantern hanging on it. Old and riddled with signs of wear, yet it follows him everywhere. It used to be an ordinary oil lamp, but Ithakos had modified it to run on Originium and added a windproof case designed with latches that could be easily opened for a soft light to guide him home. He still remembers that night. He was adding notes to the river map based on his observations, as Ithakos hammered away on his workbench nearby to improve the lantern.
Finally, he works up a slight smile as he carefully wipes the dirt off the lantern and tries to open the case—but fails to.
It is stuck. This has never happened before. He dares not use force, nor does he know how to repair it, so he can only gently turn it over. Cold sweat forms beneath his mask and on his back as fear returns. After leaving Ithakos's armor and Arts Unit to the guerillas and leaving his bloody chiton to Athenius, this is the last item he owns with any connection to him. If he loses even this, then what should he—
Click.
The lantern opens up.
A thin fiber falls out of it.
He breathes a sigh of relief as he raises the lantern to the river map. After a long silence, he remembers to look at the fiber, surprising himself when he realizes it is the top of a reed. Perhaps the wind blew it over the night before, or in the morning, and he only now noticed its presence.
Just as he only now realizes how soft the black earth is beneath him—though the rivers have yet to return, the annelids in the soil were already weaving through the ground in his absence, and the reeds of the rivers and marshes are once again regaining their moisture.
At daybreak he can go even further, he thinks.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: You're not seriously expecting me to give you a tour of your own office! C'mon, I'm getting you out of this place! I'll cart you out, if I have to!

It's more than just cannibals banished from Rusthammer over there, we got Catastrophe cultists infesting the place, all in the name of the living Originium forest… Guh, most of my clients would be asking me to take them there by this point. Where's your sense of curiosity?! You wait here, I'll get us some water before I tell you more!

Eh, no biggie even if you didn't bail me out, that prison wasn't so bad. I accidentally ruined the reputations of enough travel agencies, I had plenty of companies trying to get me thrown in jail, but thanks to them, my Terran Travels 'Free Lodgings' Guidebook has a few new entries.

Doesn't matter how much money you've got or how hard the job is, I'm not gonna charge you an arm and a leg if you're feeling something like the Bleached Wasteland. If your idea's good enough, the only consideration I'll need is you bringing yourself along, buuut if you just wanna go into the restricted areas to snap pics with the warning signs, then that'll cost ya!

Look, I might be a rulebreaker, but even I've got standards! Standards like, 'make sure the client comes out without a scratch'! If I didn't keep to that sort of ironclad rule, I'd never have thought to fight off a whole manglerbeast by myself, haha…

It doesn't have to be a restricted area, y'know. It's not like I'm into getting shocked by electric fences. If you believe an ancient secret passage is hidden in Rhodes Island's toilets, then I'd be happy to take you there. However many skeptics there are on this land is the number of places worth going.

What? My tie's all wrinkly? Oh, that's because I used it to wipe too many of my clients' tears. Sad tears, emotional tears, happy tears… Travel has this mysterious effect on people. So, when am I gonna make you cry?

'Traces of civilization among the stars', 'fleets wandering through subspace', huh… It's not that I don't believe you, I just don't understand any of it! Even if you were some crusty old man on a sickbed, delirious with fever instead of the Doctor, I'd believe you. The real question is, when are we gonna get to see them?

Atatatatata—enough outta you! Everybody knows Oripathy's incurable, but should someone working all day and all night to cure it really be saying that? I've still got lots of 'you can't go there' places I want to check out, so I'll leave the 'you can't cure that' diseases to you.
So you're the kind of client who contemplates life anytime, anywhere.
Allow me to introduce you to our travel agency! I'm the president, and you're the staff. So, where are we off to?
Do we really have to watch recordings of places we've been the whole way through?
Pfft! Since when did tour guides get promotions? It's like a musbeast getting a 'Best Street Cleaner' award.
The gold-star tour guide—exclusively recognized by the mysterious pharma corp which deals with politicians all across Terra! Who knows how many clients I'll draw with a reputation like that!
I've never brought a group this big before.
Hey, stick close to my guide flag, okay? No wandering off, or you'll get lost.
Hey, you don't need to stick that close! I climbed up this tree to scout the place, okay?!
Whew, something stinks! Means I know where the enemy is!
Hey, listen! I got something to say!
I'm here, I'm here! Explanation time!
Doctor, get up here! The view's amazing!
Can't let them pass? I'm used to that sorta thing!
'Please note: breaking into restricted areas will not give you superpowers!'
'Ammo is expensive, so there will be no warning shots!'
'Warning: continuing onwards may lead to missile barrage!'
Y'know, these noisy loudspeakers are pretty handy for scaring people.
Told you, not a single hair harmed. Can't really call this place a 'death zone' anymore now, can you?
Alright, group dismissed! Make sure to tell your friends all about me when you get home!
These guys are way too pro at escaping! I should sue them for infringing on my patented techniques!
Look, it's no big deal, let's just run first!
There don't happen to be any secret areas you're not allowed into here, are there?
Gee, you poke like a needlefly, Doctor!
If you want a group huddle, how about a trip to Sami with me?
Arknights.

Pfft, okay, enough jumping around, Doctor. There aren't actually any Sargonian tribes who gather around Originium clusters doing headstand dances to greet the new year, I was just teasing you. But to make sure your jumping doesn't go to waste, my New Year's resolution is to bring you somewhere that actually has a custom like that!
So, figured out where you wanna go, Doctor?

Happy happy birthday to you! Can you guess what's so special about today? It's the day you graduate from working in a teeny-tiny space to traipsing across all of Terra! I can't believe that after all these years, you're still pacing around the same little office! Today, you're coming with me! Outside! On a trip!

Oooh… It's good that everyone has dreams like this, means the two of us won't be running out of work to do any time soon. You're in charge of making the dreams people have come true, while I'm in charge of the same, but for the dreams people are too scared to have. We're like the two bits of bread in a sandwich!

But to make sure your jumping doesn't go to waste, my New Year's resolution is to bring you somewhere that actually has a custom like that!
So, figured out where you wanna go, Doctor?

Happy happy birthday to you! Can you guess what's so special about today? It's the day you graduate from working in a teeny-tiny space to traipsing across all of Terra! I can't believe that after all these years, you're still pacing around the same little office! Today, you're coming with me! Outside! On a trip!

Oooh… It's good that everyone has dreams like this, means the two of us won't be running out of work to do any time soon. You're in charge of making the dreams people have come true, while I'm in charge of the same, but for the dreams people are too scared to have. We're like the two bits of bread in a sandwich!

handbook.promotionRecord:
Rusthammer 'Fiends Gang' camp, forty-three kilometers east of Lake Sulligan. Two people were tied up and hung upside-down from an arch made of bones.
'Are you REALLY sure about this, Ferne? This ain't a movie where the cavalry come riding to the rescue in the nick of time! You saw that blind devil yourself! He could break my neck with his fingers! Are you SURE you made the arrangements? Are you REALLY sure those people are coming? Say something already! We're gonna die!'
'Hm... I never realized that this is how the land looks upside-down.'
'?'
'Say, don't those houses look like boats when they're upside down?'
'We've only got a few more minutes left to live, and this is what you wanna talk about?'
'It's precisely because we've only got a few more minutes that I wanna take a good long look.'
Two minutes later, an armored ambulance with the words 'Mandrake International Wilderness Rescue' charged through the west-side fence, and the crew pointed three ballistae at the executioner who was polishing his blade. Meanwhile, on the east side of the camp, a man wearing a metal bucket on his head leisurely got off his burdenbeast and waved at the crew of the ambulance, gesturing that there was still room for negotiation.
'You know, upside-down trees look kinda like toilet brushes.'
archives:
[Industry Commentary: Braving the Forbidden—Reform or Rehash?]
There seems to be little point in talking about 'forbidden' areas in a land that is 90% uninhabited.
On this land tilled by Catastrophe for thousands of years, even wilderness level enough for nomadic cities to traverse is rare, much less fertile soil suited for farming. For city-dwellers who think fowlbeast meat is grown in supermarkets directly in their packages, ready to be cooked, the nomadic cities and the wilderness visible from their routes are the entirety of Terra. They do not think of other places as 'distant' or 'dangerous', because they do not think of those places at all.
As such, 'travel' in the traditional sense is more like a vacation. Caravan International Travel Agency can take you to Sami, but all you will see is a well-furnished Sami-style resort village. It will feel no different from a Columbian nomadic city, at least once you spend a few days acclimating to the cold.
In recent years, however, Columbian tourism has become fascinated with the forbidden. News reports of the wealthy hiring guides to take them into forbidden areas are a regular occurrence, and travel agencies have started marketing these 'forbidden tours'. Naturally, the authorities responded by stepping up their control of such areas. Last year, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Arts Units, and Originium, the Columbian Park Police, and the army's Mobile Cavalry came to an accord regarding management division of the Bleached Wasteland, drafting a patrol route that fully covers the region.
As for the reason...

'It's true that enforcement has gotten stricter, but that has nothing to do with those so-called 'forbidden tours'. Two tour guides dressed up in military uniforms pretend to check your papers, then you take a few photos in a place that looks empty enough—that's all that 'forbidden tour' crap is about.
'If you want to see caverns with naturally occurring liquefied Originium, or Feranmut carcasses lying in the desert—the stuff you'd have to risk your hide to see...
'Then look for Ferne Barn.
'Me? Forget it, I'm not taking anyone with me, no way.
'Ferne's the only one with the skills AND the willingness to bring people along. You wanna go, find her.'
—Operator Asbestos, when asked about 'forbidden tours'

Ferne Barn, citizen of Columbia.
Investigation reveals that she has registered more than twenty accounts with seven banks in fifteen different Columbian nomadic cities, using different identities.
After tracking the cashflow of these accounts, we found Ferne's spending patterns to be extremely suspicious. Virtually all expenses are for medical bills, medicine, luxury items, antiques, as well as fines and bails paid to law enforcement authorities. There are no signs of spending on any ordinary items, be it food, clothing, housing, or any basic daily necessities.
Therefore, we believe that this 'Ferne Barn' does not actually exist: she is simply a persona created by criminal organizations to facilitate their illicit activities...
—Internal Revenue Department Investigative Report

When I first saw the operator who was to serve as my guide on the mission, she was crawling on top of her dorm room's closet. She tossed me a package before I asked.
'Here! Your onboarding equipment!' She said.
It was a bunch of junk. Broken telephone wires, tattered tarp pieces, safety ropes that had lost their buckles—and looked like they might have already taken a few lives—and plastic ties that looked straight out of a scrap heap.
'What's the matter? I gave you the best stuff!' She looked downright proud.
I pointed at the tattered tarp, then at myself, and shot her a doubtful look.
'...Ah! I forgot to give you scissors! One moment.'
Suddenly, I understood. She was wearing the same equipment she gave me: a telephone wire as a hair tie, a piece of tarp as her skirt, a safety rope as her belt, and used plastic ties to fasten her protective gear and communicator. This junk was her agency's 'equipment'.
As I took out my wallet, I saw her smile disappear.
'Please put that away. This agency does not require its employees to foot the bill.'
But she didn't even have the money for proper equipment!
'It's called smart spending! You gotta build connections with doctors and medicine dealers in case a customer gets sick or gets hurt, and you wanna be in the good graces of the ATAO, Rangers, and Mobile Cavalry officials so they don't arrest or 'accidentally' shoot your clients! That's where the money goes. As for equipment... what's the problem? Is the hair tie inconvenient? Is the belt not solid enough?'
—Rhodes Island Field Operator Report

After a long and drawn-out process, the Trimounts City Administration finally announced that they were closing the investigation into the recent incidents.
With reluctance written all over his face, a city spokesman admitted that the 'savage' (who was smashing walnuts with a briefcase as the spokesman emphasized the word), two meters tall and with indecipherable symbols painted all over his face with solidified Originium crystal, and who answered any questions with manglerbeast-like growling, was indeed a senior accountant of United Donuts Group whose papers were all in order.
The Administration had to admit another failure in just two weeks: they failed in stopping this 'senior accountant' from riding into the wilderness atop of a box truck containing one thousand two hundred hard-shelled briefcases. Fifty kilometers north of the end of the Trimounts route, in a forest that exists in a strange state of symbiosis with active Originium, the lives of one thousand two hundred natives unknown to Columbia were about to change dramatically. With these one thousand two hundred hard-shelled briefcases, they would be able to easily crack open the mutated Originium slugs indigenous to the area, which were their main source of nutrition. The one who brought such a wonderful tool back to the tribe would become a hero. He would be able to have the first pick of the freshest Originium slugs, and his tribe would build a statue of him with solidified Originium crystal.
The man himself, however, seemed to have different ideas.
Soon, the two meter-tall 'senior accountant' was once again spotted on the streets of Trimounts. Quickly encircled by a swarm of excited reporters and the sulking city spokesman who kept cursing at the sight of this grand comeback, the man took out, with a proud look on his face, two calculators and began to play an unfathomable beat on the buttons. Apparently, he enjoyed creating chaos in this unfamiliar city far more than accepting his tribesmen's tribute of Originium slugflesh.
City Administration officials submitted multiple requests to authorize a warrant, but all of those reports to their normally swift and decisive superior went unanswered. After one week, they finally lost patience and kicked down the door to their boss's office, only to find it empty. Seventy kilometers east of the end of the Trimouts route, in a Durin-occupied ruin deep under a metal megastructure, their boss was muttering drunkenly with a cup of strong mushroom wine in his hand.

Few know that a guide by the name of Ferne Barn was behind all this, from the flawless paperwork of the 'senior accountant', to the silent disappearance of a City Administration official. For her part, Ferne seemed uninterested in this farce of her own making. Was it a prank, a social experiment, a marketing ploy, or a show? Ferne never said a thing, even when speculation was at its peak.
The reporters might be fascinated by the presence of a savage on the streets of the city of progress, and the officials might be devastated that their superior had been reduced to a drunkard living in ruins with the Durin, but Ferne simply found it utterly natural that anyone might want to be anywhere and lead any kind of life.

'Is it strange for me to think that way? ...I guess it might be. But the job of a guide is to fulfill those dreams, isn't it?'

Our living room was always filled with children listening to Dad's stories when I came back from school.
None of the children came to Dad's funeral, but there was an uninvited guest who interrupted the ritual with blaring sirens. A potbellied cop poked his head out of the patrol car, saying he had received complaints from parents about someone by the name of Martin Barn, who deceived children with tales of gold-scaled sandbeasts and the like—
The cop stopped mid-sentence, took a look at us, then at the name on the coffin, and left without another word.
Sheriff Jones of Trenton—I nailed the name to the wall when I founded the travel agency, hoping to prove to him one day that Dad wasn't a scammer, and gold-scaled sandbeasts were real.
In the last few years, I proved a lot of things to a lot of people. Some didn't believe there were nomadic cities outside of Columbia, some believed the Pioneers' treasure was hidden in the Bleached Wasteland... I let them see the truth with their own eyes, but was never able to prove the existence of gold-scaled sandbeasts.
I had theories. The steppe-dwelling sandbeasts usually have multiple layers of backfins in order to blend into their surroundings, which could easily be mistaken for scales at a distance. Maybe sandbeasts that dwell in golden steppes rich in Originium really do look like they have golden scales. Another theory was that the people of Rim Billiton had tamed small sandbeasts for use in the mines—the capillaries in their backfins can help with determining air conditions in the tunnels, and people sometimes would paste golden foil on their backfins for easier identification. Was that what Dad saw?
It makes sense, doesn't it? But there's no proof. It helps people understand how these stories could come about, but it doesn't stop them from thinking Dad was lying.
Besides, Sheriff Jones passed away two years ago.
—Ferne Barn, on a rare occasion when she spoke about her father

Sandbeasts are small, fluffy animals, while gold-scaled sandbeasts exist only as drawings in picture books, or as curiosities in tabloid columns. And for many years, Martin Barn was the sole supplier of such columns for the Columbian tabloid industry.
Columbian archives consider such tabloids to be beneath them, and Ferne never saw those columns again after Martin passed away. That is, until she came to Rhodes Island.
The column on the page was accompanied by a shoddy illustration of a gold-scaled sandbeast, which looked like someone had copied and pasted the texture of a pineapple. The newspaper had become creased with age, but someone had carefully flattened the creases before pasting the cutting in a notebook. The Cautus with bangs like a pinwheel cookie gazed intently into Ferne's eyes.
'You want me to help you find this creature?'
The Cautus nodded fervently.
'You believe it exists?'
The Cautus cocked her head in confusion. She said she did not know whether she believed in it or not. It wasn't a question she had even thought about.
She had simply heard a story and wanted to see it for herself.
The Cautus asked if whether she believed in it or not was important. Should she?
'No, it's not important. Let's go find it!'

modules.moduleDescription:
You know, I'm serious about throwing my life away for love. That's why I came here.' The man shifts uncomfortably in his chair.
'I know.'
'But well, it's really hard to pull off.' The man continues shifting around awkwardly. Ferne scratches her head. She is quite sure she hasn't left any thumbtacks on the chair.
'I know.'
'I'm sure you also know how nice the folks here are, and that there's plenty of cops. The lake she jumped in back then is now a popular tourist spot, so even if I entertained the thought, someone's just gonna call the cops to dredge me up and save my life. So if you're gonna help me end my life for love, you'll have to clear the whole place out first, and that's impossible, so—' The man shoots an earnest look at Ferne. She feels that rather than imploring her to take his request, he is hoping she will refuse.
'Yeah, I know. But I can manage that much.'
'......' The man slinks silently into his chair. Ferne can clearly see he is more terrified than relieved to hear her response.
'But on one condition.'
'Is it money? Well, you know I don't got much. So how about we just—' The man suddenly springs up from his seat, as if desperately clutching his last chance to live.
'No, not money! Didn't you write hundreds of apology letters since she passed? Go find them all.'

The next day, the man stands on the very same rock where his lover had jumped into the lake from, all those years ago. As Ferne had promised, no one else is present at this scenic spot to save him. Every step he takes is underlined by a shrill clinking of chains, connecting his feet to a huge sack filled with his letters of remorse.
At first, he had approached the unassuming guide wanting to hear a firm 'no', in the hopes of putting a stop to his suicidal ideation. So how did it turn out like this?
He knows he can no longer run at this point. It was his long-lasting guilt over many years that brought him here, and he wouldn't be able to live with himself if he ran away now.
The man heaves a long sigh, and jumps down.

The lake water is very cold.
Now, has he stayed true to her? Has he stayed true to himself?
He does not know.
All he knows is how cold the water is. Is this the cold ending she wanted when she threw herself into the lake?
He does not want it one bit.
The man struggles in desperation, wishing he had never talked to that guide. If his feet weren't shackled to that sack full of letters, he'd still have a chance—
'Cough—Hack!'
A large sturdy net lifts him up from the water. Ferne, who should have left long ago, appears and winks at him.
'You... I... where are the chains? And the sack?'
'Underwater.'
'Then my suicide, I—'
'If you still really want to, then you'll have to make a separate request. But I remember your original one wasn't about that. It was about helping someone get over their guilt and delivering an apology.'

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: We're filing project papers? You're kidding me. Why sit here sifting through the stuff we've already done…? There're denied proposals too? Then what the heck are we sitting here looking at dead trees for?

Let me guess. No, don't spoil it for me. Is this a smart head massager, or an autonomic pressure regulator cap, or a holographic environmental monitoring device…? It's just a normal hood? Well, dream bigger! Spot me some funding, and I'll do you a full suit worthy of the Head of Rhodes Island.

Yeah, I deal in contraband, but think—what am I 'violating'? They'd outlaw toothpaste if you paid 'em enough to make it Schedule 1. What kind of system is that? I'm trying to rescue the nice stuff from a contraband warehouse, you're trying to sell good drugs on the open market. You and me, we work the same.

Get a load of this, Doc! I rustled up an RGB frill-wig ahead of the summit on Originium goods regulations! Look, this thing changes color on its own, it… what? The summit started half an hour ago? Pfff. That's fine, I still gotta dip into the toybox. I'll deal with the summit later.

It's not all eggheads at Propeller Paradise. Look at me, I learned all my physics from teaching toys. If I can make it in there, pretty much anyone with a brain can. I'm just out to match people with little fellas that work for them. Can you imagine anything better than that?

Check that out. The stars. Glittering like a blanket over the sky. Make fun of me if you want, but when I was a kid, I'd hold this blanket full of holes over my head, stand under a light, look up to pretend I was stargazing. It was dumb. But life's about feeling out one dumb idea after another until you hit on something and feel like you've got your future. Right?

What am I doing hanging upside-down from the ceiling? Ha! Well, you looked hot enough to boil in that suit, and my propeller here pulls double-duty as a fan, doesn't it? Y'know, excuse me in advance for this, but it's geniuses like you that stump me the most. How come you've got the brains to study a terminal disease, but you don't think to install yourself a better air conditioner?

Back in Tkaronto, when I saw you squatting in the corner of your detention cell, chilling out studying the mushrooms, I knew the ATAO didn't get you, you were just playing the ATAO. And now here I am, business partner with a whiz like you. Goes to show I'm the real deal. And that I didn't put extra meat in your prison meals for nothing.

Wait, what did you just call me? 'Friend'? Nooo no no no, I've used that word on a lot of people before, but not between us, you understand? I don't want to sully my most dependable associate with the kind of relationship that breaks down when you don't like the same food.

One of these days, I've gotta figure out a way to suck out all the wasted nutrients from the morons who can't use their brains, and then redirect them into you, so you can stop spending all this time sleeping.

Want one, Doc? Here, I got a light. It's just an Originium firework, but you ain't seen nothing yet. Cut a deal today, and I'll get it to you tomorrow. Gordon Tannen, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Arts Units, and Originium, at your service.
I got some bodycam footage from the gangs we busted back in my frontier days. Want it?
This is a real deal promotion medal, and not my consolation prize for playing patsy, right? Hey, then this IS my first one ever. You wanna pop the champagne?
I tell you what, this Rhodes Island joint's got potential to become the next Propeller Paradise! A few more of those promotions and I'll bring you along to make it happen… *burp*!
You guys on the transport crew for my little fellas? Then I'll bring a few extra crates.
You guys remember one thing: When you kick the door down, kick like you mean it! I'll handle the rest.
Oh, high-explosive Originite grenade, my beloved, you'll waste away in the warehouse no longer. I'll blow you up so good the whole continent's gonna hear you scream.
Get on your knees, now! What, never seen an ATAO agent lay down the law before?!
Don't sweat it, I catch your drift.
What, got a report for me?
Keep it simple. Doesn't matter where you put me, I'm still headed for the skies.
Stand a little further in, Doc. I can see your hood from here.
Don't touch me! You gonna fix my hazmat suit too? It's called sense.
No more hollering! What if I fill my data wrong? It's called courtesy.
Get up! How do I test-fire if you're lying down? It's called responsibility.
Quit playing dead! One more round, new weapon! It's called a control!

handbook.profile: Gordon Tannen, born in Columbia, was promoted to Chief Inspector of the Columbian Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Arts Units, and Originium following the Propeller Paradise Incident. He has also been restored to his position as Chief Executive of Propeller Paradise. He has entered into cooperation with Rhodes Island to secure legitimate channels for our Oripathy medicine to enter the Columbian market, while also representing Propeller Paradise in our joint aerospace research.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be non-infected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Skybox shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.13u/L
Operator Skybox regularly comes into contact with Originium products, resulting in heightened risk of infection.

Hope that suit of his doesn't start leaking Originium. He doesn't take it off even when he sleeps...
—Space Fin 054
handbook.promotionRecord:
A normally stoic Rhodes Island medic broke down in tears when he saw Rhodes Island medicine on the shelf of a Columbian drugstore.
In just six months, Rhodes Island's Oripathy medicine made rapid inroads into the Columbian market, which had been secluded itself for more than a decade. There is a long way to go until prices drop to a level affordable by the average Infected, but no one can deny that it is a huge first step.
Gordon Tannen, Chief Inspector of the ATAO, has never shunned any opportunity to flaunt his well-deserved pride as chief architect of this development. Following the incarceration of Gustave, former head of the ATAO, and the subsequent changing of the guard at the agency, Gordon Tannen has strengthened his own position while intentionally shredding the relationships that a certain corporation built into the ATAO for the purpose of enacting stringent Oripathy drug laws, enabling its monopoly.
However, rather than emphasize the help he rendered to Rhodes Island, Gordon boasts more often about 'building great things together with the Doctor'. Operators not in the know might believe him to be one of the Babel-era veteran, an elite operator operating undercover, after hearing him boast for two hours straight.
In fact, his first encounter with the Doctor was in Tkaronto four years ago, in an ATAO detention cell. Gordon had been working the border checkpoints for three years, and his only job in Tkaronto was to bring meals to the prisoners in the cells. At the same time, the Doctor had turned themself in in order to get the the ATAO to crack down on Mama John's, which had set a trap for Rhodes Island.
The dealings between the two of them began when the Doctor noticed a few extra meatballs in the dinner that Gordon brought.

'ATAO has every means at its disposal, and ATAO never fails. It's like a portable Arts unit with ready-to-cast Arts installed. All you need to do is aim and shoot, and anyone can buy one of those at an outdoor equipment shop for the price of a few hundred certs.
'The president can use it. Maylander can use it. Capitalists can use it. So why not us?
'That was the most important lesson I learned from the Doctor spending three days behind bars. And all it took was a few meatballs.'
archives:
[Excerpt from the Propeller Paradise Administration Rules for Secretaries]
......
04. Anticipate the boss's needs and serve tea at the right time by listening to the boss's voice and observing the scales around his mouth.
22. Respect your boss!! Stop bringing tea whenever you think he's thirsty. You're his secretary, not his mom! Stop treating him like a kid!
......
09. Do not interrupt the boss, argue with the boss, or steal the boss's words in front of other people. Actually, just shut your mouth, there's no need for you to talk.
15. Immediately remind the boss if he makes a mistake during a negotiation. If you don't, it's your fault if anything goes wrong.
......
12. Know your boss, and communicate his intentions with absolute faithfulness when negotiating, for you are his personal representative.
17. Use your brain when negotiating, don't just communicate his intentions. No one will take you seriously if they can tell you're just repeating what your boss said.
......

'Did you really spend six months under Mr. Tannen as his secretary, Mercia? Is it really possible to follow all these rules at the same time?'
'Yes. It just takes more effort. But there is also a way to make him forget all these rules and work with you in a different way.'
'Really?'
'Pay close attention to his outfit, his little robot, and all the Originium equipment and Arts units he fiddles with. Express as much interest as you can feign.'
'...And then?'
'And then, you just deal with him like you would deal with the most talkative boy in class when you were in elementary school.'
—Conversation between Mercia, former secretary to the Chief Executive of Propeller Paradise, and her successor

[Interview from the documentary Bluebeard and the Great Toothpaste Prohibition] When we talked about 'toothpaste tubes', we were talking about vehicle coolant pipes. When the Great Toothpaste Prohibition was first enacted, we filled the tubes with toothpaste and smuggled it from Kazimierz into Columbia. No one would find out unless you took the vehicle apart. You could only fool the ATAO for so long, though. Within six months, every checkpoint on the Columbian border had trained casters posted, and all it took was a wave of their wand to expose the goods. It was around that time that the name 'Bluebeard' started making its rounds. He was a mysterious figure who never showed his face, but it didn't matter. No one ever saw Mr. Max during the Revolutionary War, either. What mattered was that Bluebeard could help us avoid the checks. From anti-Arts coating to invisible tubes... he always had a way. Everybody knew the toothpaste hero who defied the authorities. They were singing songs about him: 'You can have my smokes and you can have my booze, but you can't have Bluebeard's toothpaste tube.' And you'd hear people boasting about brushing teeth with Bluebeard every night. What happened next? Heh, he sold us out and went into the ATAO. Some said he got bought out, other said he was coerced, but all we know is that we never heard from our toothpaste hero Bluebeard again. —A truck driver who worked as a smuggler during the Great Toothpaste Prohibition Gordon unabashedly describes his job at the ATAO as 'racing natives, refugees, and smugglers at the border checkpoints.' Border checkpoints are high-speed mobile platforms owned by the ATAO. They are little more than the size of a truck, but their speed is real, and smugglers call them 'toilets running with sirens blaring'. Gordon's primary responsibility at the ATAO was overseeing one such checkpoint, by himself all year round, chasing natives, refugees, and smugglers that crossed the border, and either negotiating with or fighting them until he retrieved the Originium hallucinogens from their false teeth, or the live Originium slugs from their tails. His biggest achievement over the years was confiscating a crown with a hundred thirty-two foldartals pasted on it, owned by a Sami snowpriest. Three years passed before Gordon returned from the border checkpoints to the nomadic cities. At Tkaronto port, he was stopped by an excited young reporter who wanted to know if he was the outlaw hero Bluebeard. As Gordon got away from the reporter, he said: 'Sure, people were putting 'Originium' on everything they could think of, and you could say that the president guided Originium fever in the direction he wanted. But why did it have to be toothpaste? 'Took me three years to figure it out. Someone had the bright idea to corner the dental hygiene market with Originium floss, so he called on every favor he could to get this crazy prohibition through Congress. Buying and selling toothpaste was banned the next day. 'That's how the rules of ATAO came about. The rules that some people bleed to protect, and others bleed to defy. How does fighting them make you any kind of hero?'

I thought it was a thief when someone knocked on the door late at night, but it was a strangely dressed Savra who called himself Gordon Tannen. I remembered that my father had kept cursing that name the last time he came home, as though he were his actual son.
Gordon seemed very interested in everything in my house. The warped floorboards, the leaky roof, mom's red and swollen eyes, and my Gaulish accent that I could never fix. That, and my name: Gustave Baune. When Dad left, it was like he took Mom's soul with him. She missed him so much she changed my name to be the same as his, but I could never become him. He was the head of the ATAO, while I was a loser who was good for nothing but cleaning people's cars. When she begged him to give me a job at the ATAO, he slapped her.
Dad left because we weren't good enough for him. That, I accepted, but I didn't need pity from someone who WAS good enough for him... This Gordon, looking down at us from on high.
Thankfully, he didn't say much. Indeed, he didn't say anything at all for ten minutes, as we sat around a table silently, to the sound of Mom crying. He finally opened his mouth right when I was about to see him out.
'You won't be seeing your dad again. Treason. Life sentence.'
I already knew. The courts had sent a letter.
'You're allowed to change your name under Columbian law. Come find me if you want to change it back, or to something else.'
What he gave me was not a business card, but a bottle opener with a propeller on it, and the words 'Propeller Paradise' displayed prominently.
—Marlin Baune (formerly Gustave Baune), son of Gustave, former head of ATAO, in an interview with Maylander

'Gordon Tannen. You deny any private dealings with the traitor Gustave, but you have met with his son, Marlin Baune, multiple times following his incarceration, even inviting him to a tour of Propeller Paradise, where you were sighted drinking and partying with him. What is your explanation?'
'I was Gustave's former subordinate, and he was Gustave's son, so me visiting him means that I had dealings with Gustave—is that what you're implying?'
'Maylander cannot eliminate the possibility.'
'Wow, it's that easy working at Maylander? Okay, I'm reporting that pineapple pizza is evidence of a conspiracy between Siesta and Siracusa. When do I get my paycheck from you guys?'
'......'
'Listen, man. That kid Marlin cleaned cars for people in that border town for a decade. He's even smoother dealing with foreigners than I am. The only reason he's still cleaning cars is because old Gustave saw him as a disgrace. And what's worse, made the kid believe it himself. Let me tell you what I'm gonna do with him. I'm gonna open a bottle of champagne with him, and then I'm gonna get him a job at ATAO working at the city checkpoint, where he's gonna shine like he's never shined before. That's how ATAO's gonna be from now on. No freaking glory and no freaking shame. You got the chops, you got the job.'
—Interview with Gordon Tannen by Maylander investigators

Welcome to the Sky Conqueror solo exhibition. I am your guide, Space Fin 054. The tour is about to begin. Please turn off your mobile terminals. The first exhibit is a video disc set of the classic 70s drama, Sandwalker. Sandwalker, which depicts the exploits of a free-spirited Kuranta warrior, instilled a certain idea of freedom in an entire generation. Students often skipped class to play 'Sandwalker' on school grounds. Young Gordon did not join the other children's games after watching Sandwalker. But one afternoon, several trucks from a nearby construction site drove onto the school grounds, and turned it into a sea of sand in front of the stunned security guards. Nobody knows how Gordon fooled the foreman and security, but everyone remembers how he put on a cardboard helmet and raised his arm triumphantly before charging into the sea of sand. The schoolchildren had two hours of unprecedented fun before Gordon was dragged into the principal's office. Gordon said, 'If you're already skipping class, why settle for standing on the playground spouting lines from the show?' ...... Exhibit 13 is a game disc released in 1082 by Blue Box Co., Columbia. Gordon's approach to gaming is unusual. While this game is not considered particularly difficult, he played through each stage multiple times until he reached the inventory limit for all equipment and items, before challenging the final boss. The plan was to use this wealth of items to overcome the boss with ease. However, game discs at the time had a short lifespan, and it broke down when Gordon reached the final stage, so he never managed to beat the game. Gordon said, 'What's the point of reaching the boss if I don't crush him the first time?' ...... Finally, we have here a shrub from Sargon. Originally a tiny bud picked from a wooden stick, it has now entered its fifth generation under the nurturing of Gordon's 'Growth-Encouraging Loudspeaker' and 'Nutrition Lightbulb'. Today, every street tree in Propeller Paradise is a descendant of the original bud. Another 100 saplings have been sent to Rhine Lab, in the hopes that this tree that survived the harsh environment of the foehn hotlands can become the first plant to grow outside the Starpod. The item previously belonged to an explorer Gordon described as 'a hateful free spirit'. He apparently declined an invitation from the explorer to travel together, not because he was uninterested in going where no one had gone before, but because he saw no point in unburdened exploration. Gordon said, 'That budding stick would be nothing but a stylish walking stick in your hands. Give it to me, and I'll show you a moving forest the next time you see it.' ...... 'Excellent, Five-Four. Absolutely perfect. You finally understand my needs.' 'When will this exhibition be held, Sky Conqueror?' 'There's no rush. When I pry all of Columbia off the face of Terra and conquer the skies with everyone with super propellers.... that'll be the day. For now, your mission is to recite those descriptions to me every night before bedtime.'

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: You want me to watch over your work, like I keep an eye on my siblings while they do their homework? Sure. I'll make you run ten laps in the snow if you don't finish on time.

Whoa! Head up, chest out, swing your tail—good! Treating my disease is something that deserves the greatest gratitude a hunter can give. Look how this leporibeast snorts and kicks! It's the strongest that I've hunted. I'm not sure why the medics won't accept it…

Apology Letter: I'm sorry, instructor. A hunter takes only what she needs. If she fails to kill with one single shot, it is not hunting, only meaningless killing. This is the rule that Kjeragandr set for the snowy mountains… and the reason I put a hole in the training target, I guess…

Legends tell of a creature that points the way for hunters lost in the blizzards. It is mysterious and beautiful—no, not this one on my shoulder. It got lost while following me, hoping to pick up scraps from my hunt. I call it the Rift Cloudbeast. Cool, isn't it? Wait, no, no, no, not the Doctor's hood! You can't eat that!

The craftsmen know that Kjeragandr's eyes must be deep, for She sees a thousand miles. Her hands must be delicate, for She heals whatever wounds She touches. But these ideas were formed from our sculpting, one chisel at a time. At the end of the day, tomorrow depends on our own eyes and hands.

When I go back, I'll tell my siblings that Oripathy isn't something to be feared. Their big sister is strong as ever and still carries her heavy crossbow around. Oripathy isn't a punishment from Kjeragandr. She guides and does not punish…

Doctor, help me put the strand from the left side on top of the one in the middle, then do the same with the hair on the right side and weave them together—no, it's all wrong again! This is completely different from how the Saintess did it… do you actually know how to braid hair, Doctor?

You get punished when you do something bad. The Rift Cloudbeast stole your snacks because I didn't keep a good eye on it. We'll banish ourselves, according to the rules of my house. Don't try to stop me—huh? You're saying the rule here for cloudbeasts is just three days of petting time with you? You're the master of this house, and you wouldn't lie to me. Here you go!

You want to go hunting with me? Alright, let me first step up my training… why? There's no way you can track anything in the snowy mountains on your own. I'll need to get strong enough to carry you on my back the whole way.
Kjeragandr on high, hear my prayer… keep them safe, keep them healthy.
I came because the Saintess says you can treat my disease. Do you need a hunter? I can take out a beast three times the height of a grown man with a single shot!
Everyone's really good!
What's this badge for? Oh… I get paid more when I have it? I see! Thank you!
I don't quite understand what the health exam report says, but I know I haven't gotten worse. You saved my life, and Kjeragandr's blessings will be with you.
Do you need help hunting game?
Stay close. The snowy mountains can be dangerous to newcomers.
Shh. Don't disturb the beasts.
Look at the tracks they left in the snow…
Do you see the game?
Do you hear footsteps?
I have bait.
Hide your smell.
Broken icicles… we've got a big one.
Fresh dung, not yet covered in snow… it was here not long ago.
Set the trap, and wait…
One shot, one kill.
I've never seen a quarry this big… did we really catch it?
By Kjeragandr, we have our game. Let's go home!
Rift Cloudbeast, go find some herbs that can stop bleeding!
Let's go, Doctor! The smell of blood will draw more beasts!
Mm… it's warm here. Almost too warm!
Whoa! Careful, I strike back on reflex!
Oh no, the Rift Cloudbeast is chewing on your hood again…
Arknights.

Thank you for letting me bring my siblings here to celebrate the new year! They don't get to leave Kjerag very often and they're really enjoying their time here. I'm taking them to try the special dishes that the other Operators have prepared. Thank you so much!
Doctor, have you seen the Rift Cloudbeast anywhere? I've been looking for it since morning. It ate my breakfast.

I don't know what a working adult like you might want for your birthday, but I gave a chain like this to my parents before, made from the tooth of the first quarry I hunted. They were very happy. This bead chain will keep you safe. Happy birthday, Doctor.

This was the walking stick that I used on my pilgrimage to Mount Karlan with the Saintess. I took it to bathe in the purest lake water, and in the first ray of dawn atop the peak. May it keep you safe on your path towards the future you seek.

handbook.profile:
Snow Hunter comes from an offshoot of Kjerag's Clan Paleroche that went into the mountains, where they have lived as hunters for generations, passing down the craft of carving Kjeragandr sculptures.
With her experience of hunting in the snowy mountains, she demonstrates excellent athleticism. She currently receives treatment at Rhodes Island after a hunting accident left her with Oripathy, and is assigned to field missions at her own request.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Originium crystals distributed across surface of body, confirmed Infected by medical examination.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 6%
Originium crystals are present on Operator Snow Hunter's arm.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.16u/L
Operator Snow Hunter is still developing physically. She demonstrates excellent physical abilities as a result of her active lifestyle in the mountains, but continued observation is needed to prevent deterioration of Oripathy symptoms.

[Rift Cloudbeast Health Examination Report]
The Rift Cloudbeast is in good health with no signs of Oripathy, but is slightly overweight. Consider reducing daily food intake.
handbook.promotionRecord:
Kjeragandr on high, hear my prayer.
Let your blessings be upon my mother,
and my father,
and my brother and sister.
Let your blessings be upon those who have helped me, those who have cared for me, those who walk with me.
Bear witness, Kjeragandr on high, that my life will be my own, no matter what hardships await.
archives: With our experience in onboarding operators from different countries, plus having received a heads-up from Pramanix ahead of time, we were confident that Snow Hunter's background as a huntress in Kjerag would not present any particular difficulty, and that she would successfully integrate into Rhodes Island within a month. However, what had happened was truly unprecedented— One day, when it was time for a regular checkup, the medical operator opened the door to find a fine leporibeast standing by Snow Hunter's bed, huffing and kicking its front hooves. With great ceremony, she placed its reins into the medic's hands, saying it was a gift of gratitude for treating her condition. The medic, who was allergic to animal fur, began sneezing non-stop, but Snow Hunter mistook the tears in her eyes for tears of joy. The medical department spent three days deliberating what to do with this energetic leporibeast, and eventually resolved to ask Snow Hunter to return it to the wilderness when they found it trying to nibble at the medical equipment. Snow Hunter could not understand why and looked hurt that her gift was rejected: to her, that was the highest show of gratitude she could offer. After further dialogue, she learned that the common token of gratitude among the hunters would be good enough for this kind of situation: a bundle of meat jerky, savory and well-salted. This mountain delicacy was shared within the entire medical department to rave reviews. Perhaps there is still room for improvement in our Getting Started at Rhodes Island: Guidelines for New Operators.

Of all the legends of Kjerag, the 'mysterious creature of the mountains' is the one that Snow Hunter gets asked the most about. Legend has it that mysterious, beautiful creatures dwell on the mountains, appearing before those who lose their way in the storm, showing them the way home. It is said that many hunters owe their lives to these creatures, and Snow Hunter just happens to have a little white creature with her. According to her, however, it was she who saved the creature, Rift Cloudbeast, while out on a hunt, and shared her limited food with the weakened beastling for days.
Many operators were confused as to why she had to cut her own portion of food. Why not hunt more often? Was it because of the difficulties of hunting in a snowstorm? Snow Hunter's answer was that this was one of Kjeragandr's rules: Every being in the mountains, including the hunters, are part of Kjeragandr, sharing in Her soul in an eternal cycle of life. As such, they take only what they need. To take any more lives would be unnecessary killing. She could not do more hunting than necessary just for the Rift Cloudbeast, but she could also not stand idly by and watch it die, so she chose to share her own food with this being, who shared in Kjeragandr's blessing.
The Rift Cloudbeast seems completely oblivious to all of this, enjoying the comfort of Snow Hunter's quarters and occasionally playing with the Kjeragandr sculptures on the desk, which she hand-sculpted, a craft she has been studying since the day she started hunting on her own.
She steadfastly believes that Kjeragandr will protect her, her family, and everyone.

Many operators know of the three great clans of Kjerag, and the history of conflict between them. Snow Hunter comes from the Paleroche clan, while Pramanix, who introduced her to Rhodes Island, comes from the Silverash clan. The two of them seem to enjoy a good relationship with each other: Snow Hunter will sometimes ask Pramanix to braid her hair, while Pramanix often tells the story of how Snow Hunter saved her life and treated her wound. If not for her treatment, the wound on her right leg would likely force her to leave the harsh environment of Kjerag and live somewhere else. Besides, they can often be seen praying together as well.
Operators who see this might think that the feud between Clan Paleroche and Clan Silverash has been exaggerated, and that the younger generation is no longer concerned with their contentious past, but SilverAsh's presence is a reminder that not all is water under the bridge—
While operators going to visit Pramanix would normally pass by SilverAsh's room nearby, Snow Hunter prefers to go the long way around, avoiding going near his room.
She has told us that she does not know much about the history of the three clans. All she knows is that roaring trains have intruded into the quiet forests, and that the animals that used to live there were forced to flee their homes, leaving behind the carcasses of the ones that died of fright and hunger. It was against such a backdrop that she rescued the Rift Cloudbeast. She does not understand why people would pave concrete on Kjeragandr's body or dig a hole in it, causing a Catastrophe to befall them, which is how she lost her father.

It took a long time before Snow Hunter became comfortable talking about her father.
To her, her father was a great hunter, able to kill beasts several times his size with a single bolt and return safely from the mountains in a raging snowstorm. He was also a great craftsman who sculpted beautiful Kjeragandr sculptures with his callused fingers, supporting the family after her mother passed away. After she came down with Oripathy, it was her father who reassured her that he would find a way to cure her, that she would not need to worry about the future. But he himself died in the Catastrophe at the train station, and she found out through his effects that he had been acting as a spy to buy medicine for her.
She could not even find someone to blame. Did Kjeragandr punish her father for his betrayal? Was it her that made him betray his faith? Was she the one who was ultimately responsible for all this?
Snow Hunter found herself beset with anger and bewilderment. She had accompanied the Saintess on her Pilgrimage to find an answer from Kjeragandr, but she never knew what she was actually hoping for. Did she want Kjeragandr to show Herself in all Her glory to expel the outsiders who had drawn their swords? Did she want Kjeragandr to shower Her blessings on her arm and heal her Oripathy? Or did she want Kjeragandr to blow away the snowstorms, and let her quarry run docilely into her bolts? And after that, what then?
Snow Hunter vaguely realized that this was not what she wanted in her prayers to Kjeragandr, that this was not how blessings and divine punishments worked. She had no way to know what her father was thinking when his faith was shattered, and what internal struggle he might have had when he made the choice. But she remembered the solemn expression on his face when he inspected his sculptures, and the joy and love he showed every time he brought her medicine. At the end of the day, he was simply a father who wanted his child to live well, and he had already paid the price.
'Emotions are such complicated things. There are many things I still don't understand.' This was what Snow Hunter said to us in the end. What we do know is that she is firm and resolute as she faces the path ahead. Her past experience and the teachings of Kjeragandr will undoubtedly guide her path when she feels lost, helping her walk towards a brighter future one step at a time.

modules.moduleDescription:
'When's Sir Arctosz gonna give us new hunting gear? Hey, Joanna, still using that spring trap your old man gave you a while back? How's the hunting lately, getting enough to eat?'
'Joanna's twice the hunter you are. She's perfectly fine using older traps and crossbows. You need to train harder, not hope for shiny new contraptions.'
'Well, what d'you want me to do? If I started training right now until I'm as good as her, all the animals on the mountain would've run off already, and all that training would go to waste.'
'The railroad construction shouldn't affect the forest for too much longer... Hmm, have you considered moving down the mountain? I heard old Hans followed his son and daughter-in-law to the city recently.'
The villagers chatter away about the rumblings of the trains through the forest, the long level roads and the many marketplaces those roads connect to. Joanna sits to the side, adjusting her old spring trap. There are dark, minute gouges between its iron teeth thanks to many years of use, but its clasp remains nimble. She does not speak, simply retightening the trap in silence. She uses her fingertips to push down on the spring, ensuring its jaws still mesh together. Soon, she waves goodbye to the villagers as she begins today's hunt.
The sky is darkening, and a narrow hollow mars the vast snowfield, a shivering cloudbeast reclining within. The trap is not far, so it was most likely lured over by the scent of bait. A cloudbeast this young should not be out alone like this. Its fur has not yet lengthened, and its claws lack the length and strength to grasp. It must have wandered off from its kin. It tries to move forward, but the frigid wind forces it to curl up even tighter.
Joanna crouches down, packing up the trap. She makes no move to capture the young beast, instead taking out some jerky and breaking off a small piece to gently place on the ground. She knows that with no one to care for this cloudbeast, it will not survive the cold night. She looks at the trembling beastling, a complex bitterness welling up in her chest.
Has Dad come back from the train station yet? A thought suddenly comes to Joanna. Maybe one day, her family will move down the mountain too. Maybe one day, her dad will agree to work at the crafting hall, where he can keep carving statues of Kjeragandr in a workshop... Kjeragandr's body stands as tall as ever, the endless freezing winds whistling past as they always have, and the spring trap her dad gave her still works great. It's not like everyone really needs new tools or a new place to be. Why does it feel like the more the land moves forward, the less people can actually hold onto? Joanna cradles the beastling, tucking it inside her jacket. It snuggles against her, the tips of its fur dripping with melted snow. The touch of cold water against her chest jolts her. She looks down at the weak cloudbeast. It seems to have settled down a little.
'Let's leave it for tomorrow. I'll go hunting with everyone then. There's always a way.' A faint pulse beats against Joanna's chest. The snowy path under her stretches on in peaceful silence.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Doctor, would you like to study the languages and lifestyles of tribal Sargon with me? It'll be harder than combat training, for sure.
I bear a duty to my tribe, and I will see it through to the end. Tribal heritage is a pretty distant thing to a girl who grew up in Columbia, but the doubts of a few lords ameer won't discourage me!
Isn't Kestrel's weapon just awesome? The way she wields it is so different from any other weapon. I'd love to spar with her, to learn her style, when I get the chance.
Uh… thank you. I'm having a hard time getting used to this Sargonian alcohol. I miss Columbian kale soda.
That's true. I've lost a few fights with those ameeri guards, and sometimes it wasn't even close. But there's still time, I'll get my chance.

The padishahs and local warriors look down on Columbian composite swords, just because they're designed for urban combat. But I'll show them the potential of combining modern technology with traditional tactics someday.
Remember, it's vital to stay hydrated, Doctor. Once you spend a whole month in the wilds of Sargon, during the dry season, without seeing so much as the mirage of an oasis… you'll get it.

At first, there weren't many tribes who believed I'm actually descended from the Qarnsayf. Can't blame them, considering how the legend has faded from history. You believed me from the start? Oh… I mean, thank you…

My dream is to host a martial arts tournament in Sargon, and gather all the warriors from all the lands, so they can share in the glory of the Qarnsayf. You should come too, and bring the best of Rhodes Island with you! Yeah, it's a promise, Doctor!
You can rest safely here. We're not in the wilds.
Hello, Doctor. I'm Hadiya, descendant of the Sargonian Qarnsayf tribe. I've come to study at Rhodes Island in order to overcome the challenges that the wilds have set for me.
Sargon warriors say that combat is the way to grow, but I can learn in this way too. Let's get started.
I'm still a very long way from my goal, but please accept my gratitude.
You honor my tribe when you honor me. Thank you for the recognition.
An opportunity to try out some new moves.
Like the wilds of Sargon, the battlefield is more dangerous than it looks. Make sure you know what you're doing.
Is your equipment ready? It all comes down to this—time to fight!
Which weapon would you like to be on the receiving end of?
My turn, finally.
What tactics do you want me to use?
I hope it's a worthy foe.
Do you know what these horns signify?
In the name of the Qarnsayf!
In the name of the wilds!
I have more than one weapon.
Take this!
I always knew I would win a memorable victory someday.
Victories like these are what Sargonian warriors live for.
No, I can't be content with the limitations of my sword. For the sake of my tribe.
Defeat is but the herald of victory. Let's pull back for now.
Ah… It's been a long time since I've had a solid roof over my head.
Be careful, or my horns might hurt you.
Curious about my sword? Here, try it out. Oh, and be careful about the spring blade in the staff.
Arknights.

Happy New Year, Doctor. How would you like to celebrate the holiday? Are we going with Sargonian tradition, or Columbian custom, or do you have some other arrangement in mind? Either way, I'm with you.
What challenge do you have for me today, Doctor?

Today is your birthday, and I think it would do you good to set work aside for a while and go out for a walk. The landscapes of Sargon are spectacular, but you didn't seem to have time for them. Come, consider today's excursion my gift to you.
Looks like we're both a step closer to our goal. Let's celebrate this with a Columbian high-five! We've got a long way to go in the days to come.
