handbook.promotionRecord:
[Classified Log]
I must admit that no equipment has troubled me more than the Gemini Replicator. At first sight, I thought it would be easier to deal with than those strange guns that Team Rainbow carries. After all, even Redmark mercenaries get their hands on holographic projectors.
Imagine my surprise when I found that the Gemini Replicator did not rely on any Originium Arts, and performed far better than any holographic projector I have ever seen.
There is little I could do with it, other than adapt it for Originium batteries. Honestly, I'm more worried that I might break the sensitive equipment inside—not that it's as fragile as it looks at first sight, but I'm very interested in its design principles. I hope to learn more about it from Iana.

That's not a reason to fail to show up to work. I'm cutting your pay if I catch you having tea with Iana again when you should be working.
—Closure
archives:
Nienke 'Iana' Meijer is a member of Team Rainbow. She was involved in the Krysztauowa Incident and became an associate of Rhodes Island following the conclusion of that incident.
Iana has demonstrated impressive tactical acumen and processing of battlefield intelligence. While much of her background remains unknown, we hypothesize that she is a highly experienced intelligence operative.
He response to this hypothesis was a laugh.
'Well, I guess it's not entirely wrong. But the intelligence that I'm most interested in is usually thousands of kilometers away.' As she spoke, she aimed and fired, scoring a bullseye on a target fifty meters away.
Each member of Team Rainbow brings to the table their own set of specialized skills. That said, given they have not formalized any long-term contract with Rhodes Island, it would be advisable not to call on them for too many missions.

Of the eight members of Team Rainbow who have established contact with Rhodes Island, none is more curious than Iana.
The other members focus their efforts on specific fields, such as Doc with Oripathy, and Blitz with languages, but Iana is like an extraction device running 24/7, passionately taking in knowledge from everywhere and every walk of life, and not just at a surface level either; she processes and analyzes a massive amount of data, arriving at certain unique perspectives.
Her tireless effort seems more befitting of a curious researcher than an intelligence operative.

Iana's engineering and surveying skills are beyond our comprehension. Even without access to the equipment that she is used to, she managed to cobble together some makeshift devices with the help of the Engineering Department.
That equipment was almost immediately put to good use. Even though it was very different from the technology that Iana is familiar with, her surveying equipment helped Rhodes Island detect and avoid newly-created adverse terrain that had not yet been mapped, giving us more time to resupply.
'All systems are complementary, if you know how to connect them.' Other engineers have also began to adopt Iana's favorite saying.

[Classified Log]
Iana's physical examination revealed below-average vision, another symptom of the genetic condition that causes her to lack skin and hair color pigments. Her condition has only made her more determined and confident, and more aware of the discrimination and exclusion faced by those suffering from illness.
She thus feels a natural affinity with the Infected, a sense of empathy that, for the Infected, is sometimes even more important than a dose of suppressant.

modules.moduleDescription: 'Commence voice recording. Rhodes Island, Team Rainbow, codename: Iana. Internal team comms, confidential. 'Uh, X days since the transfer incident—I'll fill that in once I get back to base—and 41 days since beginning experiments in Sargon. 'While sun was up, retrieved all cameras we deployed on the first day. Currently loading obtained images into terminals. Terminals here can only do wired connections to the server, and the server in my car isn't powerful enough to handle my processing needs, so any specific analysis needs to wait until I get back to base. 'I brought along my eyes and brain too, so while it's loading I've been going through these photos manually since sunup. That way I can at least get some preliminary hypotheses going, and can to some extent inspect and verify the results we've previously observed elsewhere. 'The Columbians—I mean, Terran Columbians—recently launched an experimental device that's likely a high-energy particle beam. Opened a hole in the sky. 'The sky is fake' will probably end up as common sense and popular opinion. 'Meanwhile, our own experiment seems likely to help infer the coherence and uniformity of this false sky. 'Just examining the photos with the naked eye, the stars demonstrate clear discontinuities between different times and regions. Far worse than what the literature describes. Conclusion waiting on main server analysis, but I estimate it won't be too far from my first instinct. 'This implies the sky has no coherence whatsoever, and is essentially more of a regional projection originating from outside. I have a few other conjectures as well. 'That said, I still have confidence in the terrestrial planet hypothesis—ordinary optical surveys support this. While most locals may not be able to give a full justification, universally they have an awareness—they've likely never seen the sea their whole lives, but they know the land beneath them is actually round. 'The people here understand wireless technology, but their signals seem unable to reach this planet's ionosphere. Their alternative is a sort of linked relay: ultra-high bandwidth, energy cost practically negligible. But it appears that because of this, they've never tried to use medium-wave signals for long-range wireless communication. I can't tell just from the literature whether the issue is with the D or F layer—of course, this assumes Terra has atmospheric and sunlight conditions comparable to Earth. I personally think this is extremely likely. 'Their technology, the way it shifts, and the root of its development may seem completely unlike ours, but counterintuitively there are similarities too. '...... 'Actually, I replicated Karl Jansky's experiment here. Nobody seems to have thought of it, so it fell to me to do it for them. Couldn't help myself, sorry. 'These local Terrans don't know where we merry few came from, but their curiosity in the world outside this planetarium is growing as I speak. 'And I want to help them. I want to be one of the explorers. 'I've always wanted to, no matter where. '...... 'Alright, let's see what signals the antenna's picking up... 'Huh? 'This intensity, this... period... 'What is this?'

LINKAGE.voiceText: Right... Let me know if you need anything.
Watch out. There are a lot of dangerous materials in the workroom.
Engineering Department... Not bad. The head of the department, though... A bit too talkative.
I like machines. They don't talk, but they're always honest with their readings.
Chaos is only an enemy if you're unable to adapt.
When the approaching chaos endangers your loved ones, the thing to do isn't to protect them. It's... to keep them as far away from you as possible.
No, my comms equipment's fine. Nothing to worry.
You want me to say something? Uh, that's the hardest part.
My hometown? There... the sky is blue, and all the buildings under it are blue, too.
Good... I'll find something to do.
Rainbow Operator, codename Fuze. I've said everything I need to. Let's get to it.
No problem. I'll find some time to watch them.
Good. Thank you.
Do I need to give some crowd a speech? No? Good.
At your command.
Do exactly as I say.
Enough talk. Now we act.
Матрёшка готов поручить.
Focus on the task at hand.
Remember our objectives.
Lower your voice.
Remain silent.
With me!
Remain alert.
Stay focused.
Hold position.
Every action builds our chances to win.
Asset secured.
On your feet, your wounds are not fatal.
Move, right now!
This place isn't bad.
Don't do that...
I made some pilaf. Want some?
Arknights.
Hey...

handbook.promotionRecord:
[Classified Log]
The principles of the Cluster Charge are simple: Set it on the wall, drill through it, then launch the explosives one by one. It's not at all hard to understand.
In practice, however, there is no shortage of obstacles. Originium explosives of equal mass simply do not have the same destructive power. Drilling through a wall is easier said than done, as I already learned when working with Ash, while the Cluster Charge also works very differently from Breaching Rounds. But the hardest part was launching the explosives one by one: how do you ensure that the Originium explosives do not detonate too early or too late? It's about as easy as running 5km through the Infy Icefield naked.
The more I deal with Fuze, the more curious I get about what's in his head, especially when he quickly comes up with solutions for something that you've been banging your head against for a long time. At least Closure doesn't give you that sense of inferiority, even if she does nag.
And then he comes to me asking how a simple Originium-powered hand-warmer works. We're even now!
archives:
Shuhrat 'Fuze' Kessikbayev is a member of Team Rainbow. He was involved in the Krysztauowa Incident and became an associate of Rhodes Island following the conclusion of that incident.
The expert engineer is a man of few words, who excels at using explosives to achieve tactical goals. He demonstrated high anti-personnel and anti-materiel performance, as well as considerable combat experience.
It is worth mentioning that Team Rainbow members are only working with us temporarily. They are not formally employed by Rhodes Island, and with how much they have on their hands, it would not be advisable to call on their help too often.

Just because Fuze doesn't like to talk doesn't mean he's not thinking. He is in fact a quick and flexible thinker, who is not afraid to voice his opinions in tactical meetings. His taciturn nature and tendency toward unexpected action can lead to misunderstandings in certain cases, however.
While the members of Team Rainbow are used to Fuze's personality, we should take it into account when assigning Fuze alongside other Rhodes Island operators, in particular encouraging them to communicate with him. He may be silent as a lump of iron, but it is a lump of iron that surges with the currents of inspiration, waiting for the opportunity to spark into action.

Fuze is an expert at creating chaos, and with it, opportunity. Although Team Rainbow has faced more than their usual share of chaos lately, he has remained his quiet and reliable self.
Seeing a two meter-tall Forte use a hammer to smash through a wall that he had planned to blast open seems to have dealt a small blow to his self-confidence, though the rest of his teammates may see it as a 'necessary adjustment', particularly those like Ash who established contact with Rhodes Island earlier. They say it's something that will pass, perhaps even inspire Fuze to new inventions.

Fuze's quiet nature could not hide his interest in the Engineering Department. He applied for and was granted his own workshop, in which he spends most of his time at Rhodes Island, maintaining and testing his weapons and those of his teammates.
In one incident, Fuze rescued a twelve year-old Infected boy and brought him to Rhodes Island. Having witnessed the Cluster Charge in action, the boy was fascinated, and wanted to trade his doll for a Matryoshka.
Fuze spent an afternoon in the workshop, and emerged with what looked like an ordinary wooden doll.
The boy looked disappointed, until Fuze pressed a button in the same way that he would activate a Cluster Charge, and the wooden doll flew apart, leaving behind one that was identical, but smaller. And again. And again.
The boy was overjoyed at the imitation, but Fuze patted his head and told him that it was no imitation; this, he said, was the true 'Matryoshka'.

modules.moduleDescription:
'Buddy, you are NOT a chatty type, huh!'
After the gazillionth attempt to start up a conversation without getting a reaction, the Cautus worker in a yellow pair-o'-ears helmet stops operating his control panel and gives the man beside him a pat on the shoulders. With the machine kicked into auto anyway, it's not like it needs nannying.
Seeming to recognize as much, the man finally turns his head. His eyes are hidden behind a black visor, barely discernible. He remains silent, and simply extends two fingers on his right hand and gives his own helmet a few taps.
'Go on and say somethin', will ya? Saaaaay—woooords—'
Throughout this temporary worksite echoes the rumble of Originium electronics, more often than not a soundboard to rival a nomadic plate's engine layer. But the voicebox of a Rim Billy worker, like the workers themselves, is filled with a power that cuts through just about everything.
The man appears a little confused. He feels around behind him, then unexpectedly pulls out a mirror. He takes a glance at his own reflection, then raps on his helmet again in the same manner as before.
The worker doesn't get to respond before he sees, out of nowhere on the man's visor, a smiley face positioned right between where his eyes would be. There's a line of Victorian text below too, split by his nose into halves. The left side reads 'I'M SHY,' and the right, 'AND QUIET.'
The worker tries as hard as he can to keep a straight face. His lower lip twitches side to side, his teeth grind over each other, and he doesn't leak a single word.
But soon, he can't hold in anymore, snorts, and begins to laugh.
'Probe has reached scheduled depth. Drill decelerating. Prepare to turn off and take samples.'
That's an announcement from Control Center 2. It sits 80m straight above them, and 50m above that are the natural caves of Camp 2 and tracks to the auxiliary shafts. Another 600m up is the surface, and outside from there are the Targangils Mountains for miles and miles forever.
The drill mentioned in the announcement is a fair way deeper into the earth than they are.
'—Hold on, Number 2 is too deep. Abnormal tremors in 2's shaft walls. Calling emergency stop!' The second announcement comes hot on the heels of the first, as if some kind of prank.
Something unwelcome has been welcomed. The worker throws himself onto the control panel, pounding a fist on the largest, roundest red button of them all. It's the one to emergency-dump the drill and inject extra polymer prep into the shaft walls.
But the injector doesn't respond, and the Originium electronics continue to roar.
A ginormous thud echoes through the worksite, seemingly not from deeper depths, but from times long, long ago.
One thud becomes two, then three, then a string of them. The two watch as even the wall outside them finally begins to experience its own fierce tremors.
Number 2 has drilled too deep and awakened something, and that something is heading for the sunlight.
'Detonating all Cluster Charges!' The worker's never heard this voice before, but in an instant discerns that it has to be the man's shout.
Perhaps because of this shout, or perhaps because of what it triggers elsewhere...
The tremors cease. Silence seems to reign again for a while, until there comes another announcement urging evacuation.
'Your tender said 'use of Originium explosives forbidden', so here I am.'
This may be the second time the man's opened his mouth today, and his voice is far quieter than a moment ago.
'There's issues with your emergency injector system. Once we're up top, come with me to tell them, and then I'll take a look.'
'Er. Right. You got it.'
After experiencing an accident whose true severity will only be known later, a conversation finally ensues.
'...What's with that light-up stuff in your visor though, eh? That's one hell of a lark, buddy.'

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Here are the documents. If that's all, I'll be going... The stain on that sheet? Oh, that's, uh... I guess I did spill something when I was having a couple of drinks last night. Haha... Damn, I put it in the middle of the stack, how'd you catch it...?

Do cultured folks like you even drink? Come, come, let's take a swig together, okay? Climb the hills in the dark, cross the desert in a storm. Now we gather in the oasis, drinking all the finest booze… Hehehe, oh, my friend, let's return to our homeland…

Why are you all wrapped up like that on such a warm day? You'll be drenched in sweat. Hey you! Yes, you! Why don't you take off that jacket? A true warrior isn't afraid to show the results of hard training!

'Operator'? No, I'm a warrior of Rhodes Island. Don't worry, it's not because I can't let go of the past, but because I want to defend the present. I'll train new warriors for you... same as I was taken in and raised back on the sands.

I once took in some war orphans. They begged me to teach them how to use a sword to get revenge. I agreed, and they succeeded, but at the cost of their lives… Many years ago, the chief taught me that the sword is only for protection.

The war took the lives of everyone in my tribe. My friends blocked blows with their bodies, and the chief's blood dripped onto my head... Me and the other children set out on a path of revenge. I'm the only one left. No one and nothing else. Only me.

The mark I'm drawing on your forearm? It's a 'bite mark'. Look, I have one too. The chief carved it into my skin herself. She said that those who have undergone the trial of blood and pain become the bravest warriors. The mark brings us strength.

I've taken plenty of hits both in battle and in the mines, but not many left marks. I used to think I was lucky, but now I wish I wasn't. I want the scars to help me remember certain people and things. Death brings back nothing, you know. I have to stay alive, and carry them myself.

Is it snowing on that peak...? Ohh... Guess what, Doctor? I had a dream last night about sleeping in the chief's arms when I was first taken in. She stroked my forehead gently, and her palm was like the sun-scorched sand, warm and rough. They've never seen the snow. Now I see it for them.
It's a beautiful day out there. I had a good nap, and a good dream, for once.
I choose to stand here, and so the land beneath my feet is my home.
No need, I'll grab my weapon and shield and head to the training grounds.
It's a warrior's duty, no need to thank me... Wha? Blushing? Of course I'm not blushing. How could you even tell I'm blushing through my tan?
Thanks, Doctor... I'll take this medal back to my homeland. The spring there has dried up, but it will continue to bless me, and they will know that I'm still fighting.
Love, friends, hearth. That's what a warrior lives for.
Warriors! Your courage will bring glory.
Don't eat too much before a battle, unless you want to throw it all up.
Now we fight!
I'm well prepared!
My sword is honed.
You're not getting past me!
I see them.
Victory or death!
We will defend our home!
The enemy will never see our backs!
Raise your weapons and shields! Not one step back!
This is the home that we defend. This is where they die.
The invaders' swords cut their own throats. An end they deserve.
Haha, it is an honor to die defending my home.
My homeland, my friends, my love... they're all waiting for me.
The heck? No alcohol here...? Huh? What's that in my mug? It's just some b… umm... bubbly barley juice.
Hey! Hands off.
Hahaha! Oh, I hate being tickled…
Arknights.
The strongest liquor for the bravest warrior. This one is mine, Doctor. If you really want it... devour this whole roasted game, and you'll be our hero for the day!
Yo, Doctor, you sure you don't need to sun a bit?
I made this horn out of the sands of my tribal homeland. A new warrior blows her victory horn after her first battle. It's like the cry of a newborn, celebrating her arrival into the world.

I first saw Rhodes Island sailing in the distance when I was at the branch office. The rumbling of the ship and the tremor of the sands... it's like my chief was whispering in my ear: You've found another place worth fighting for.

handbook.profile: Formerly a warrior of a Szubat-Arsalan tribe in Sargon, Kestrel and her siblings were enslaved by the local lord ameer's army. Encountering Rhodes Island personnel during her escape, she was able to return to the mines and rescue the other workers. She later joined Rhodes Island and is currently employed at the Sargonian branch, receiving treatment while participating in field missions.
handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 3.7%
Operator Kestrel shows signs of mild Oripathy infection, but leads a life that is little different from the uninfected.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.26u/L
Working in dangerous Originium mines without proper protection has had a significant impact on Operator Kestrel's health. Her BOCD is well above normal levels and requires regular monitoring. While we have instructed her to take it easy in her everyday life, it seems unlikely that she would be willing to sit around all day. The best we can do is recommend that she avoids high-risk field missions.

The people of her tribe had a custom of painting 'bite marks' with mineral paint. It remains to be seen whether this has a negative effect on her condition.
- Warfarin, Medical Department
handbook.promotionRecord:
The sun is setting.
Kestrel stands up from the roof of the office building she had been lying on, pulls out her horn, and blows it towards the setting sun.
She had explained to curious operators that the horn symbolized the celebration of victory, or the passing of a peaceful and quiet day.
Today's horn is particularly long, because this is her first day at the office as an official operator of Rhodes Island.
Kestrel blows it a little longer for the important events in her life.
The first time was her very first victory in battle. Their armies charged downhill and routed the Lord Ameer's soldiers. She had volunteered to be the vanguard, and saved the life of her friend with the sword her chief had taught her to wield. That day, she learned what it meant to be a comrade, and she blew her horn longer.
The second was when she led the slave revolt through the mine shafts, filled with fog and enemies. She took the rear guard, fighting off pursuers all night, until she saw with her own eyes that the miners had reached safety. That day, she learned that the purpose of the sword was to protect, and she blew her horn longer.
This is the third time.
archives:
Kestrel is a Sargonian warrior who is as straightforward as they come.
She began frequenting the training room shortly after arriving at headquarters, confidently walking in like she had always been a regular. Her relationship with the combat experts of Rhodes Island began with a clash of weapons, putting on a show of Sargonian tribal swordplay that the operators in the training room had never seen before. They eagerly invited her to come back for more.
Her favorite hangout is the bar; although she has been warned against excessive drinking, she can often be spotted doing so from dusk to dawn at the bar for weeks on end. Ultimately, the Medical Department decided to bring her in by force, but Kestrel refused the 'treatment'; being under the influence only seemed to make her sword strike faster and harder. Treatment finally began when her training room friends arrived and successfully restrained her with great effort, only for everyone to realize that treatment was unnecessary after all: unlike most drunks who deny being drunk, Kestrel was, in fact, unimpaired. If anything, the alcohol had only served to hone her swordsmanship.

[Medical Department Audio Log]
'That Kestrel, from Sargon. Can you believe what her tests show?'
'What do you mean?'
'Do you know how much she drinks? Yet it doesn't seem to have any effect on her vitals.'
'Wish I were like that.'

Many Rhodes Island operators have their fair share of scars, which serves as a way to introduce themselves.
'I got this during the Sarkaz Civil War...'
'I got this during Columbia's Great Expansion...'
'I got this when I hit my head on a table when I was three!'
'That doesn't count!'
Kestrel was rather reticent about this topic at first, as the trials of her past left no visible marks on her skin. This bothered her, as she saw scars from battle as something to be proud of.
As she began to blend in, she realized that her 'bite marks' serve equally well as a conversation starter. When asked about the meaning of a 'guardian bite mark', she ended up giving a lecture about the meanings of various marks.
'What would Rhodes Island's bite mark embody?'
'That depends on what Rhodes Island is about.'
'Let's say... 'future'.'
'My tribe didn't have that kind of mark, but we can invent one.'
Kestrel began inventing her first 'bite mark' after receiving such a request. Shutting herself in her room, she spent two days drawing up the pattern, and hung it up in the cafeteria to the sound of cheering.
As the crowd came forward to embrace her, she felt, for the first time, that she had truly been accepted.
She still thinks back to the people and events of her past, but no longer finds her lack of scars to be a handicap. Rather, she is happy to share the origins of her 'bite marks,' and to carry on the tradition of her people in her new home.

Medical checks revealed nothing of particular note. We suspect that painting these 'bite marks' with mineral paints may have something to do with how external trauma leaves no mark on her skin, but no firm conclusions have been reached for now.
- Warfarin, Medical Department

Kestrels holds great respect for the tribal chief who brought her up.
By tradition, women of the tribe undergo trials to become defenders of hearth and home. The chief was the one who took the homeless Kestrel in and raised her to become a brave warrior. She was a beautiful and kind leader who taught her tribe to turn abandoned ruins into settlements with plenty of water and rich soil.
The threat of the Lord Ameer was constantly looming over their heads, though. In order to oppose the Lord Ameer, the chief traveled to numerous other tribes to build alliances, taking Kestrel along with her. In her free time, she discussed with the young Kestrel what kinds of body paint looked best, and gave Kestrel 'bite marks' symbolizing 'Protection.'
Kestrel learned that the chief preferred white for 'bite marks'.
In subsequent years, she used the 'bite mark' that her mentor gave her, in her favorite color, while fighting a hopeless war against the Lord Ameer's soldiers with the few comrades she had left, until she was the only one left.

A psychological assessment was performed on Operator Kestrel to mitigate potential risks in field missions.
We learned through interviews that revenge became her purpose after the destruction of her tribe, but that it came to a stop at some point.
According to her, during her stint in the mines, she took in some children who had also been enslaved in the mines. At their request, she agreed to teach them to use a blade in order to take revenge for their families.
However, she had underestimated the price of revenge. Witnessing the deaths of those children led her to look back on the purpose she had pursued for so many years, and the results that came of it. No longer obsessed with vengeance, she turned her sights back to the original connotations of 'Protection,' and began to see inciting revenge as an evil.
She came to the conclusion that her current life matters more, and that Rhodes Island is her new home that she must protect. As such, she has requested a reassignment to the Sargonian branch to participate in field missions.
We must inform the Sargonian office ahead of time to keep an eye on Kestrel's condition in the field, investigate any faction that has a history with her, and require her to regularly return to HQ for psychological evaluation and Oripathy monitoring.

Kestrel still has many mysteries, as there are details in her personal history that can no longer be verified, and her own account is sometimes confused or fragmented. It must be emphasized, however, that this is no reason not to put our trust in her.
- HR Department Note

modules.moduleDescription:
Making distance from a ruin they personally set alight, Kestrel takes her group back to their initial gathering point. The fire rages on, and even when the skies open up, the rain can't even touch the flames before it steams away midair, leaving only the sound of crackling.
Breaking the silence, someone asks Kestrel. 'Boss, how many did you kill today?'
'Can't remember.'
'Who would remember after the heat of battle how many they killed, youngster?' a weary voice adds. 'To survive is already a job well done.'
Kestrel lets the topic lapse, but that twisted face comes to mind. The one of an 'old acquaintance' scared shitless. The one she closed in on with every step. The one with no alternative but to jump from the roof. The one who left her only that face, one moment before melting into the sea of flames.
She knew who that was. The assassin who murdered her friend.
'Still, this victory's worth celebrating. Today, we wiped out a few more of the killers who slaughtered our people.' Kestrel comes to a stop, looks back, sees the descendants she's brought along. The distant flames flicker in her eyes.
They raise a cheer, but Kestrel doesn't smile.
'So how many killers to go?' asks again the one who broke the silence.
Kestrel gazes over. It's a girl, still young. If the tribe still was, she would never be part of these fighters. She would be living her youth, a bright one, a happy one.
Oh. That's right. She doesn't even have a 'bite mark'.
'You showed a great display today. I've now decided you should be rewarded with a 'bite mark.' Kestrel fails to directly answer the girl's question. 'While we return, you can think about what style of mark you'd like.'
'Really?'
A feeling hits Kestrel. She's had this conversation. She was the girl before her. She, the girl, before the tribe's chief, the one who raised her—the one who was dearest to her, the one who outlined, over her left shoulder, the very first band of her 'bite mark'.
Kestrel can't help but hug that shoulder tight, the warm memory almost abating the cold rainy eve, but it's only a moment before she comes to. For they, stood in the rain, are waiting for her.
'Really—now let's get back to the gathering point quick. I'll find the box, and then you'll be able to choose.'
The group begins to slowly move, their figures gradually melting into the dark of night, never to be seen again.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: I looked after the stockbeasts in Dahuang, so I'm looking after you here, of course. You'll have to listen to me, work hard, and rest on time. Let's see... It's rest time now. Let's head out and have some fun!

Of course I know what the stockbeasts are saying. The beastlings in Dahuang always talk to me about things like what kind of snacks they want or who they like, and I sneak them a little help. This apple? A stockbeast asked for it, obviously. I'm just tasting it for them, making sure it's sweet enough.

Zuo Le is Candlestick, the Record Keeper is Inkbrush, that blinged out guy is Megaphone, and you're Wisehead. I also know a Tall Shades and Smiley Sharpshooter! Oh, and Amiya is the best! We made a promise to come up with a better nickname for you together.

Shu made me this fowlbeast whistle, and whenever I wanna tell the stockbeasts to go home, I give it a blow. Sometimes, when Dahuang feels empty, I sit down on the street corner to play it. People come and go, and my whistle's my goodbye and hello.

Dahuang's operas are sung in different dialects. That commemorates the farmers who came to our rescue a few centuries ago. They were from all across Yan, farming here for generations. They're why Dahuang fields are so fertile and prosperous now. I'm really proud that I can play the accompaniment on my flute here every year!

When I first stood on the terraces, I could only see the aqueducts, but after the farmlands were raised, I could see the edge of the city, and now that Shu brought me here, I can see the horizon from the top deck. Megaphone tells me that Baba and Mama will come back someday, but when, exactly?

Could you draw a line over my head...? I'm not standing on my tiptoes! I'm not stretching my neck out, either! Are you done? Let's see. See? I told you I got taller! Maybe I'll be taller than Xiaohe next year! Let's see how tall you are. Minus your hood and shoes, you... come up to my shoulders!

When I'm in a bad mood, I sometimes go to the embankment to play my flute. There's a woodcutter there who yelled at me every time, but he always quieted down as soon as I played this song. He even hummed along. That was the first time I saw him smile! Like I said, I'm really good at the flute.

The farmers say that the stockbeasts live by following water and grass. Fowlbeasts fly freely in the sky, but they always eventually land in the fields. I know what that means now.  Everyone has a field to call their own. Rhodes Island is your field, and you are the fowlbeast that will come back to land, isn't that right?
Hm... You fell asleep...? You really fell asleep...? Hehe, have this coat then. Have a good dream. I'm off to have some fun!
Shu brought me here to hang! I think I wrote my name on a document she was supposed to sign...? She said it was fine, though. Now that I've signed it, I get to come here to hang out all the time!
...Wah! I'd never fall asleep in class, Laoshi...! Huh? It's you.

I developed a way to train stockbeasts to identify foods based on their smell. The Tianshi Bureaus gave me a medal for it. It doesn't have a serial number, but it says how amazing I am! And now I have this one you gave me. I'm putting them next to each other.

I got taller again, right? By the time I'm as tall as you, the people of Dahuang will definitely have cultivated the seeds they want. When that happens, I'll invite you to come sit with us in the fields. The rice flowers are gonna look even better then!
Is it time to do pest control again? I'm the best at catching these nasty little things!
Trust me. I know I can do it extra good.
Listen up, get your boots on, and tread lightly!
Everybody ready?
Qui-Qui-Quick! The pests are getting away.
I saw them hiding in the bushes there!
Nice. They didn't see us.
None of you are getting away this time!
Hah, I got you!
Come any closer, and I'll whap your heads with my flute!
Not so fast now, huh!
And don't ever come back to our fields!
Come on, let's go! We need to hurry and tell Shu. She's going to be so happy with me.
Next year, the year after, and the year after that... One day, the whole of Dahuang will live without fear of Catastrophes or pests, and we'll have stack our harvests as high as Heaven for Shennong.
It's okay. We've been through Catastrophes much worse than this. This one's just a little setback. We'll work harder next season!
We're in trouble... I'll go get the Tianshi to help us!
I want to sneak out when the landship docks. Can you keep it from Shu?
These buns aren't for you to grab!
Have you learned to play the song I taught you?
Arknights.

Here. A multigrain fragrance sachet! It's made by blending some grains and medicinal herbs. Keep it on you, and you're guaranteed peace and good health for the rest of the year. And you should definitely have a bowl of multigrain rice with multigrain beer. The farmers always tell me how good the multigrain beer tastes, but when I took a sip—It was so spicy and bitter!
I have the basket ready. Should we head to the fields to catch mudfins together?

I made you a bowl of noodles. Give it a try. When I was still a kid, Shu always made me a bowl of longevity noodles for my birthday. An entire bowl made up of a single noodle. She always added a fried egg over easy too. I think this one might be overcooked, though. It might... have turned into a bowl of gruel.

I saw Rhodes Island splitting the sandstorm and sailing here. It felt just like the first time I saw Dahuang's new buildings, how they protected the fields from the Catastrophe. As long as everyone works together, no matter if it's a Catastrophe or anything else, there's always a way, right?

When I first stood on the terraces, I could only see the aqueducts, but after the farmlands were raised, I could see the edge of the city, and now that Shu brought me here, I can see the horizon from the top deck. Megaphone tells me that Baba and Mama will come back someday, but when, exactly?

Could you draw a line over my head...? I'm not standing on my tiptoes! I'm not stretching my neck out, either! Are you done? Let's see. See? I told you I got taller! Maybe I'll be taller than Xiaohe next year! Let's see how tall you are. Minus your hood and shoes, you... come up to my shoulders!

When I'm in a bad mood, I sometimes go to the embankment to play my flute. There's a woodcutter there who yelled at me every time, but he always quieted down as soon as I played this song. He even hummed along. That was the first time I saw him smile! Like I said, I'm really good at the flute.

The farmers say that the stockbeasts live by following water and grass. Fowlbeasts fly freely in the sky, but they always eventually land in the fields. I know what that means now.  Everyone has a field to call their own. Rhodes Island is your field, and you are the fowlbeast that will come back to land, isn't that right?
Hm... You fell asleep...? You really fell asleep...? Hehe, have this coat then. Have a good dream. I'm off to have some fun!
Shu brought me here to hang! I think I wrote my name on a document she was supposed to sign...? She said it was fine, though. Now that I've signed it, I get to come here to hang out all the time!
...Wah! I'd never fall asleep in class, Laoshi...! Huh? It's you.

I developed a way to train stockbeasts to identify foods based on their smell. The Tianshi Bureaus gave me a medal for it. It doesn't have a serial number, but it says how amazing I am! And now I have this one you gave me. I'm putting them next to each other.

I got taller again, right? By the time I'm as tall as you, the people of Dahuang will definitely have cultivated the seeds they want. When that happens, I'll invite you to come sit with us in the fields. The rice flowers are gonna look even better then!
Is it time to do pest control again? I'm the best at catching these nasty little things!
Trust me. I know I can do it extra good.
Listen up, get your boots on, and tread lightly!
Everybody ready?
Qui-Qui-Quick! The pests are getting away.
I saw them hiding in the bushes there!
Nice. They didn't see us.
None of you are getting away this time!
Hah, I got you!
Come any closer, and I'll whap your heads with my flute!
Not so fast now, huh!
And don't ever come back to our fields!
Come on, let's go! We need to hurry and tell Shu. She's going to be so happy with me.
Next year, the year after, and the year after that... One day, the whole of Dahuang will live without fear of Catastrophes or pests, and we'll have stack our harvests as high as Heaven for Shennong.
It's okay. We've been through Catastrophes much worse than this. This one's just a little setback. We'll work harder next season!
We're in trouble... I'll go get the Tianshi to help us!
I want to sneak out when the landship docks. Can you keep it from Shu?
These buns aren't for you to grab!
Have you learned to play the song I taught you?
Arknights.

Here. A multigrain fragrance sachet! It's made by blending some grains and medicinal herbs. Keep it on you, and you're guaranteed peace and good health for the rest of the year. And you should definitely have a bowl of multigrain rice with multigrain beer. The farmers always tell me how good the multigrain beer tastes, but when I took a sip—It was so spicy and bitter!
I have the basket ready. Should we head to the fields to catch mudfins together?

I made you a bowl of noodles. Give it a try. When I was still a kid, Shu always made me a bowl of longevity noodles for my birthday. An entire bowl made up of a single noodle. She always added a fried egg over easy too. I think this one might be overcooked, though. It might... have turned into a bowl of gruel.

I saw Rhodes Island splitting the sandstorm and sailing here. It felt just like the first time I saw Dahuang's new buildings, how they protected the fields from the Catastrophe. As long as everyone works together, no matter if it's a Catastrophe or anything else, there's always a way, right?

handbook.profile: Grain Buds is an ordinary girl from Dahuang, an important agricultural settlement in the north of Yan. She has considerable experience handling stockbeasts, and followed Shu to Rhodes Island where she now stays as a temporary visitor.

handbook.promotionRecord:
'Grain... Buds.'
The stockbeast-herding girl sits atop a pile of straw and slowly reads out her name. 'The Xiangzhang said my parents gave me this name. Grain Buds are what you call the seeds when they're starting to turn full but haven't completely ripened yet. It means I'll be healthy and grow up teeming with hope!'
The woodcutter, still with somewhat lifeless-looking eyes, sits unsteadily on the pile of straw as well. His back is stiff and straight, his legs appear uncomfortable, and he holds tightly onto his Tianshi ruler. Evidently, the girl had dragged him here.
'Give me your hand. I'll write my name. You just read along!'
The man's coarse, thick fingers were pried open by the young girl's small hand to reveal his palm. She stuck out a finger and started writing. The woodcutter thought it was ticklish. He did as the girl said and opened his mouth to laboriously let out some sounds.
'Grain...'
'Grain— Buds.'
'Gra... Grain... Grain— Buds.'
'Yep, that's right! Put them together like that. Grain— Buds. My name!'
'Grain... Grain Buds.'
The woodcutter lowered his head and gently moved his lips.
'Grain Buds.'
The girl leapt in joy, her whole head covered with straw. 'Mute Uncle! You can say my name!'
archives:
Outstanding Farmer of Dahuang, Honorary Stockbeast Breeding Expert, Honorary Rice Planting Master, Excellency in Stockbeast Feed Research...
Upon repeated verification, the above honors were all found to be genuine.
Grain Buds always puts all her effort into doing the things she is capable of.
Having grown up in Dahuang, she's been infected by the residents' gung-ho attitude toward farming since a young age, and believes that to put food on the table, you have to earn your keep. Before she was even as tall as a hoe, she was already imitating the farmers and planting seeds. Unable to bear the sight, the elderly farmers instead sent her to feed the stockbeasts, only to find that they behaved especially well around her, almost as if they were on the same wavelength. As such, she was able to manage the massive ranches there in a very organized and tidy manner.
Grain Buds has kept herself busy even after coming aboard Rhodes Island as a visitor. She's developed new recipes with the logistics operators at the cafeteria, helped care for the plants at the Convalescent Garden, and naturally never forgets to give every one of the new friends she's made here an easy-to-remember and pleasant-sounding nickname. Many medical operators have noted their work stress greatly decreasing thanks to her being around to look after juvenile patients and comfort them when receiving injections or medicine.
'Guess it's easier for kids around the same age to hit it off...'
'Or maybe she thinks she's still taking care of stockbeasts...?'

Rhodes Island is already home to a number of so-called animal experts, and it is not at all uncommon for beasts to be trained to complete certain tasks. That said, none have ever dared to claim to able to speak to animals. Until Grain Buds, that is.
She insisted on demonstrating her talents: First, she found a lost storm cloudbeast on the top deck by 'communicating' with another cloudbeast. Next, she used a flute to command a few metal crabs to pick up the food waste scattered about the kitchen (Beanstalk insists that her crabs had always known how to do this). Finally, she even attempted to bring a couple of slumberfeet to help insomnia patients get to sleep, only to fall asleep herself in the hallway instead. From this, we cannot completely rule out the possibility that she does actually have some sort of strange ability.
According to herself, there was this one time when she was five years old that she got lost and went outside the city. The farmers couldn't find her anywhere, and just as everyone was at wit's end, an old stockbeast waded across the river with her sitting on its back. Ever since, she has been very close to stockbeasts, and over time she found she was able to understand the 'words' of all kinds of animals. The stockbeasts would tell her which orchard had the sweetest fruits, the traveling fowlbeasts would tell her that the flowers were in full bloom in the south, etc. When Grain Buds speaks vividly about the colorful land filled with wonder in her childlike tone, she is always able to pique the curiosity of her listeners.
'How did the stockbeast know the way back?'
'How wide was the river?'
'What's a city full of farms like?'
The listeners gather around her and bombard her with questions. She seems to have an endless number of amazing stories to tell as well. For example, there was the 'gang war' between stockbeasts, the stockbeast and fowlbeast who befriended each other and ran away together, the fin who swam all across Yan on an adventure... Does it matter if they're true? Just imagining the countryside depicted in her stories is enough to stir one's emotions.

Aside from her ability to talk to animals, Grain Buds is most proud of her flute skills. She would proudly tell others how she performed for Dahuang's operas year after year. With her small bamboo flute, she is able to play a variety of distinct melodies, from grand accompaniments pairing with the operas' epic scenes, to melodious tunes to send resting stockbeasts peacefully to sleep. Everyone who has heard her flute has been astonished to see such a seemingly frail girl exert so much energy in one go. She is always happy to use her flute to bring comfort to those around her, and she also loves to, in her own words, 'write' new melodies according to her mood. Her tunes are all uplifting and pleasing to the ear, and He Sheng occasionally writes lyrics to them. The farmers toiling in the fields would always sing along whenever they heard the music. And just like that, the two of them created a number of childlike folk songs that spread throughout Dahuang. In her hazy memories, she once heard her mother playing a reed whistle, but her 'Tianshi duties' took her away from Dahuang before she could teach her daughter how to make one. Later, she learned how to make the whistles herself as well as how to play the bamboo flute. The girl learned to play more and more music, yet her parents never returned. To this day, her melodious flute can still be heard by Dahuang's riverbank, awaiting the return of faraway travelers. [Classified Log] '...Therefore, a Chamber of Heaven's Designs shall be established roughly a hundred li to the north of Dahuang in preparation for the demonic threat.' '...Its forces shall consist of those gifted in Originium Arts as selected by each Tianshi Bureau. Those who enter the Chamber of Heaven's Designs, each possessing great skills and a firm resolve, shall train at length and be ready for battle at all times. After a year, only half shall remain. After another year, less than one-tenth shall remain. This shall continue year after year.' 'The scourge of the demon first and foremost robs one of his mind, and by the time one finds his mind even slightly clouded, it is already too late. Countless have been buried in the north to ensure the survival of their fellows. Relatively few instead live out their years with their minds clouded, rendered incapable of coherent speech for the rest of their lives. Skeletally thin, not even their old acquaintances can recognize them...' —Excerpts pertaining to Dahuang, from a history of Yan requiring a very high clearance level

To those who live on these lands, the word 'homeland' is a transient concept.
No one knows when their home will be destroyed by Catastrophe. Nomadic cities travel everywhere, and villages continue to migrate ceaselessly. What exactly is a 'homeland'? Is it the skyscrapers going up day after day in the nomadic cities, or is it the rubble left behind in the Catastrophes' wake?
Yet there are still those who, regardless of the price, have continued to guard a swath of land important to them for thousands of years. Such a long-lasting defense of the same area is extraordinarily rare.
Such is the place where Grain Buds was born and raised. Having seen all the fields and the men and women working them from a young age, she knows every blade of grass and every tree like the back of her hand; she remembers every crop in every field; she remembers which grasses each kind of stockbeast likes to eat; she remembers how she once fell from a tree and hurt her leg, and He Sheng carried her home on his back across half of Dahuang under the setting sun... The land incorporates the history and memories of the people here, and it becomes part of them. That's how the people and the land are connected.
Which is why she too is holding the fort here, watching the crops grow green and then yellow, before they are harvested and new seeds are sown anew. She watches the fields grow larger and larger, as the stockbeasts around her grow bit by bit. She sits atop a stockbeast's back, playing her flute to guide the passing caravans as well as sending travelers from afar on their way.

modules.moduleDescription:
May 10th
It feels like I'm going in circles. These so-called 'social activities' keep dragging me back to Dahuang. Not only does the weather not suit me, I can barely understand their accent, and I heard that their pickled vegetables are super super salty! I don't know how I'm going to make it an entire year.
As I expected, nothing's gone right since I arrived. I thought I could at least talk to people, but I keep tripping over my own tongue. Not only can nobody understand a word I say, but the stockbeasts keep running away from me!

May 21st
I've run into a strange young girl, standing tiptoe atop the backs of the stockbeasts. She jumped around on top of them, and at first glance you'd think she was a fowlbeast that had fallen into the herd. There I was, one leg sunk deep in the mud while my other foot is barely covered, trudging through the muck, when she started laughing at me.
'Sillyhead!', she said.
Me...?
'Take off your shoes!'
Eh?
'I'll teach you how to walk on top of the stockbeasts so you don't have to go through the mud.'
I got thrown off the stockbeasts' backs eight times that day, and I'm sure I ate more mud than rice by dinner time. She thumped me across my back, her plumage flapping about as she laughed. Though my luck may be bad, looking at her smiling face makes me feel that there's nothing that can hold me down for long.

July 8th
That girl was crouching down by the stockbeast pen this time, swaying her head as she played her flute to the herd.
'Hey, Claypot! Come, quick!'
Who...?
'You're new here, right Claypot? I forgot to tell you last time, but my name's Grain Buds!'
Oh, was she talking to me?
'Do you want to learn how to talk to stockbeasts? I'd say I'm better at it than anyone in all of Yan!'
She held my face in one hand, while holding a stockbeast's in the other, and told us to look into each other's eyes. That day might be the first time I realized a stockbeast's bright, intelligent eyes possess the same basic range of emotions as any man. Since then, the stockbeasts really did stop running away from the sound of my voice. I never expected someone like me—who's always getting chased and nipped by tuskbeasts—to suddenly have a group of animal friends.

October 4th
I was out searching for Grain Buds when I ran into her along with another youth who appeared to be a schoolboy. They were playing some odd game where they threw small pieces of bone.
'Claypot! Come play with us!'
Oh, alright...
'He's 'Big Buffalo', have you two not met before?'
I'm afraid not...
'These were left over from Shu's stew! I don't really know all the rules myself, so you'll have to explain, Big Buffalo!'
I had no idea that you could turn stockbeast leg bones into toys. A shame I was so clumsy, though. I couldn't catch the bones for quite a long while, and kept accidentally flinging them at their heads instead. Big Buffalo was a nice guy. Didn't talk much, just like me. However, every time he went off to work, he wanted to bring me along. Sometimes Grain Buds would lie down on a stockbeast's back, or hang from a tree. Sometimes she would help us out with work, and other times she would drag us off to play. Out here in the boundless fields, it almost felt like we were a family.

May 20th
As I was leaving Dahuang by car, a group of stockbeasts wandering the fields walked past. Looking at their chubby figures fade into the distance behind us, I suddenly began to feel uneasy, just like I did a year ago when I left home by myself to come to Dahuang. Setting aside not being able to see Dahuang's fields and stockbeasts any longer, would I be able to find friends as good as Grain Buds and Big Buffalo at school? I don't know how I'm going to make it through the next two school years.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: I've arranged the incoming documents just the way you like them, and added a few labels for categorization. Feel free to use them to find what you need. If only my master was so organized... Oh, it's nothing, just an idle musing.

Wait, there's a bug on your collar. Don't worry, it's a green lacewing, a helpful sort. They hunt the pests that eat our crops. Look at the wings on this cute little guy, the color of jade. Really beautiful... My master always jokes that if I didn't become a farmer, I could've been an entomologist.

Low clouds bring rain, high clouds bring fair skies.' See that cloud down by the horizon? That's a cumulus... The proverbs may not always be right, but they do have reference value. Using that one, you predict that tomorrow will be clear, but with strong winds and lightning? You might be a Catastrophologist, but just how did you come to that conclusion?

I've read that 'Tianshi' means 'to be a role model for the generations to come, and to search for perpetual truth.' I used to think I could never live up to that, but after seeing some of my seniors befuddled from time to time... Maybe I've been overthinking it. There may be a saying more suitable for me: 'Focus on your search, and learn for the sake of the people'.

I once challenged myself to a fast, but I ended up fainting on the fourth day. Still, my master said this was not true hunger. I didn't know what it was like to go hungry for years on end, so I could not possibly understand. I hope there comes a time when no one has to know that feeling.

I've gotten tanned again, you say? No big deal, every farmer worth his salt ends up dark as a chestnut. So long as we accomplish our goal, so long as we see our  crops prosper in the contaminated soil, and the hard work of so many bears fruit, then it's all good. Me? I don't need to be there to see it. If the people keep walking the right path, that's enough for me.

Oh, did you need me for something? Just a second, I need to braid my hair again. When I was younger, I grew out this 'rice stalk braid' as a prayer for peace. Now I spend a lot of time managing it every day. Back then, Grain Buds always thought I was a girl thanks to this braid...

The crops grown in Dahuang have a much better texture and taste than others. If you get a chance, I'd love to show you about the city. You wonder if they could supply Rhodes Island with food? Um, that's a little... I-I'm afraid that you'll need to discuss that with the proper authorities. It's not up to me.

These seeds occasionally fall onto the ship. Oftentimes I gather them up and wait like this on the solid ground, closing my eyes and feeling which way the wind is blowing. There, once the breeze rises, I let them go, and those seeds find someplace to take root all on their own.
The wind rises...

Why am I called 'Wanqing'? It's one of the breeds of rice that my master cultivated in Dahuang. Others include Fanglao #3, the waterlogging-resilient one, Zaoyou #8, the quick-ripening one, and Kangdong #11, the frost-resistant one... 'Wanqing' means wide, and it sounds the most like a proper name.
Everyone looks so well-mannered around here, it's hard to imagine that they're so fierce in battle...

The rating standards of the Tianshi Bureaus seem to stipulate that you can use evaluations from exchange visits in their assessments... Excuse me Doctor, is Rhodes Island able to provide an officially-stamped study visit certificate?

I've consulted with my master. As long as Rhodes Island agrees to sign a contract of cooperation with the Tianshi Bureaus, I'll get to offer my assistance as an advisor on experimental crop fields. We both do what we can for the sake of the many, and we'd be delighted to support your goals.
Initial environmental survey completed. Nothing abnormal. We're good to go.
I hope everyone takes my commands seriously. Let’s get this done right.
If we cross any farmland, watch where you step.
I'm a student of the Tianshi Bureaus. I won't hold you back.
Here! Er, I mean I'm in position.
Tell me what you require, and I will deliver.
I've finished construction of the refinement system. Deployment point confirmed.
We're in a complex environment. Don't go off on your own or you might get disoriented.
With the aid of the wind, we too can soar through the skies.
Watch your step, don't hurt the crops.
The landscape here is tricky. Only step where I step.
Until we can confirm that this area is safe, I will hold this position.
Ensuring the harvest isn't easy. I hope to pass on the torch of our ideals.
Just as the farms never rest, there will always be new growth from the ground, and there will always be those who wish to follow in our footsteps.
Let's try that one again. The tiniest oversight leads to different experimental outcomes, and you can't let an error cloud your conclusions.
Success is the fruit of a thousand failures. Experiments under the Tianshi Bureaus are the same. Don't be discouraged, Doctor.
Ever since I got here, there haven't been any leftovers? Of course. Waste not, want not.
Who—Ah, my braid hit you? I am truly sorry...
I reassemble my Tianshi apparatus while I wait for my experiments to finish. My record is twelve seconds. Would you like to try?
Arknights.

The poems I read when I was little always compared winter snow to a thick blanket. The seedlings sleep beneath the snows, ready to welcome the spring days with new life. Dahuang is always busy this time of year. People my age go to the frozen rivers and throw firecrackers at the frost while covering their ears. Grain Buds always shouts the loudest. Would you like to give it a try?
Doctor, I'm pretty sure I heard this cactus say 'I was already watered yesterday—'.

I'll make this one exception since it's your birthday, Doctor. I'll stand to the side and watch. But you'll want to keep your lower body firmly planted. For people who are unfamiliar with this Tianshi apparatus, they could very easily get pulled into the air by the kite, so keep your center of gravity low... Hey! Hey! Geez... The Doctor is flying...

At first I didn't really understand why my master wanted me to go on a study visit to a pharmaceutical company. But after spending all this time here, I've come to realize that you're all just like the people of Dahuang. We're both fighting to help the desperate, to save lives in danger of fading away. We walk the same path, Doctor.

handbook.profile: Wanqing, real name He Sheng, an Agricultural Tianshi apprentice of the Yanese Tianshi Bureaus. Produced significant research results in many Dahuang planting projects. Introduced to Rhodes Island by Shu, he is now on the landship as an exchange student and Logistics Operator.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Wanqing shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.12u/L
Operator Wanqing is very meticulous about following protection procedures when handling Originium.
handbook.promotionRecord:
The Tianshi Bureaus have a tradition of conducting apprenticeship ceremonies whenever a young student passes their exams. They are formally placed under the care of a senior Tianshi, and the ceremonies they hold, large or small, will give some insight into their mentor's character. During Wanqing's apprenticeship ceremony, Shu gave him only a single verdant seedling.
'In the past, these ceremonies would require three bows and nine kowtows, but that's rather out of fashion these days. Take this rice seedling and plant it beneath you. We can consider it your mark of respect. I cannot teach you much myself, for all the knowledge that you wish to learn ultimately springs forth from the soil.'
Wanqing did not fully understand this, but respectfully stooped to plant the seedling in the soil beneath him. When he raised his head, he saw the endless, fertile fields, and the calming greenery that grew within them.
From that moment on, he began to put down his roots.
archives:
While many operators on Rhodes Island are familiar with the farming life, a scholar specialized in agricultural research is still rare enough to turn heads.
'Is it true that you'd need to be hunched over plowing a field every day, all year round?'
'I heard that during the harvest season, everyone from little kids to grannies get their sickles out to reap wheat as far as the eye can see, from dawn until dusk.'
Under the sympathetic yet admiring gazes of everyone around him, Wanqing shyly scratches his head before earnestly introducing himself. Dahuang is Yan's foremost center for agricultural research. There, the entire process is mechanized. From sowing seeds to harvesting crops, from spreading fertilizer to spraying pesticides, every step is handled by Originium machinery. It is said that there are even plates that not a single person need set foot on all year. As Wanqing speaks, he takes out all sorts of Tianshi apparatuses, displaying high-precision agricultural Originium devices we have never seen before. He also decides to show off a painstakingly-choreographed performance by his 'Sky Pole' drones...
Since time immemorial, Yan has always found it incredibly important to track agricultural yield. Countless lives are built upon that foundation of tiny seeds. Which is why an entire group of Tianshis like Wanqing dedicate themselves to agricultural research, unceasingly developing more efficient planting methods and higher quality grains. Despite their sophisticated equipment though, their research is hardly a walk in the park. Whether carefully selecting which plants in their fields meet their requirements, or imitating remote environments without access to Originium machinery, toil cannot be avoided. It is a tough life, as can be seen in Wanqing's young but toned arms and the calluses poking through his gloves. It is this sort of work that the Nongye Tianshis of Dahuang perform year after year, after which the finest seeds from their programs are sent to every corner of the country, carrying with them the wishes of their creators for a successful germination.
When asked whether he is proud of his work, Wanqing finds it hard to hide his embarrassment.
'It's hard to think about anything but farming when you're out in the field... I'm pleased whenever we get a bumper crop, and getting to see everyone eating their fill, well, that makes me happy too.'

In Yan, a Tianshi is an occupation that commands respect, but demands great responsibility in turn. To become part of this elite group, one needs to pass the Tianshi Bureaus' grueling exams.
They require not only outstanding talent in Arts, but also a deep pool of specialized knowledge. Thanks to Wanqing's exceptional exam results at the young age of fifteen, an exception was made for him, and he was placed under the tutelage of a senior Nongye Tianshi, Shu. Only a handful of test-takers in all of Yan meet that standard. Some suspected cheating at first, but suspicions were quickly dispelled once his performance at the Tianshi Bureaus became clear. Not only were his academic scores once-in-a-generation, his first crop breeding experiment yielded promising results. Only three years after entering the Bureaus, he'd already taken on several fellow Tianshis as students.
However, Wanqing was by no means a child prodigy. Even now, he is somewhat slow to pick up new techniques, a fact reflected in the courses he takes while on Rhodes Island. His tutor, Shu, who is just as kind as he is, says: 'using your mind always means being a touch slower than those around you, and your limbs will always be a touch slower than your mind.' Instead, he was able to achieve such amazing scores thanks to his unusual concentration and focus. As he himself puts it, if he runs into an issue while on the job, he'll simply think of a way to solve it. Thoughts such as 'maybe I could take a shortcut?' or 'what happens if I can't fix this?' never even cross his mind. While that sounds simple, it is actually quite difficult for most people to work without mulling over the consequences. 'For every step, plan three further' is an ancient Yanese saying for a reason, and its people are naturally disposed towards caution and forward planning, while always keeping an escape route in mind. This, too, can be considered a form of instinctive wisdom. However, only those who able to completely immerse themselves in the act of moving forward are able to arrive at their chosen destination.
'In earlier eras, crops still needed to be harvested by hand. More experienced farmers would tell younger ones, in all seriousness, that they must never raise their heads as they worked. Seeing the full fields stretching out to the horizon would demotivate even the hardest worker. But if you only see the stalk in your hand, then, well, you need only cut a single stalk.' Wanqing is rather serious when sharing his experiences with others, without a hint of arrogance or pride in his voice.
'While being able to focus like that is a rather rare trait, it's not always an appropriate one. Once, Wanqing accidentally broke an automatic door by bumping into it, and he silently took it on himself to fix it. By the time someone found him, he'd been at it for a full twenty-four hours... Can someone make sure to help him out the next time this happens? I'm scared that he'll starve to death.'

When Wanqing was registering as an operator, he came up with his codename in almost no time at all.
Dahuang focuses on several distinct problems plaguing the farmers of Yan, and is host to multiple experimental crops, each with their own name. For example, a crop bred for colder climates is named 'Kangdong', or 'Frost Resister'. If a descendant of this crop shows marked improvement during further experimentation, it would be named 'Kangdong #2'. In addition, there is also 'Zaoyou' ('Early Excellence'), 'Fanglao' ('Flood Defender'), 'Chuibudao' ('Unblowable'), 'Esichong' ('Pest Starver'), etc etc. These simple names entrust a simple hope into each and every variant. Of special note is 'Wanqing', or 'Vast Expanse'.
Since time immemorial, people have been fighting with Catastrophes for land. Catastrophes destroy buildings and farmland alike, and soil contaminated with Originium is extremely difficult to grow crops in. As such, in ancient times, Catastrophes were usually followed by famine. Since the invention of the nomadic city, most scholars of agriculture have focused on increasing the yields of food grown on nomadic plates. However, the Tianshis of the Dahuang persist in trying to breed crops resistant to Originium. But despite their long efforts, countless academics have deemed it futile.
The Dahuang Tianshis believe that limited space is a fundamental flaw of nomadic plates, and that though their research has been slow, it is only by exploiting the vast unused tracts of land that all the people of the lands can eat their fill. Generation upon generation of Tianshis have contributed, breeding crops that could tolerate more and more Originium activity. Five percent grew to fifteen percent, which blossomed further into twenty-five percent. Now though, progress is made only in fractions of a percent, with the rate of improvement inversely proportional to the time put into the experiments. Great leaps in tolerance seem to be a thing of the past. According to the Tianshis participating in the research, one could dedicate their entire life with no results to show for it, denied a place in the annals of history.
Wanqing is just one such nameless Tianshi.
'People have asked if I'm afraid I'll never see my experiments bear fruit. I used to be... because I felt that anything I did needed a result, any result, so I could face myself in the end. But I think I see the bigger picture now. A man's life may be all too short, but the road he walks is long. It isn't the destination that's the result. It's the path you follow, and the footsteps that you leave behind.'

In modern times, 'starvation' is a rather foreign concept to most of us.
It is more than simply having to endure until the cafeteria opens for dinner because you missed lunch, or skipping a few meals for two or three days straight during a tough mission. Rather, it is the inability to obtain sufficient nutrition for a long period of time, and the pain, suffering, and despair that comes along with it. Such an experience is beyond our imagination, and the same can be said for Wanqing. However, the records of withered crops and the photos of famished crowds in his textbooks have stamped themselves into his mind's eye.
He returned to the village ruins up the large river outside the city. The ruins could very well have been his 'hometown', and he knew that his biological parents, and possibly others in his family, could easily have been in one of those starving crowds in the books. They, too, had experienced suffering unlike anything he could imagine.
Wanqing was a fortunate child, being set adrift in a basket along the river at the tender age of two, sent by the wind and the flowing waters to Dahuang, like a seed blown by the breeze and coming to rest in a rice paddy. Thankfully, he survived the experience. As the farmers would tell him, after several years of poor harvests, the year he floated in saw Dahuang a bumper crop. And that is the story of how Wanqing came to the city, where he spent his childhood after being taken in by the kind-hearted farmers. One day he would eat at a house on the east side of the village, the next he would eat on the west side. He would run madly on the ridges between rice paddies, pulling along his kite. He would clamber up the greenhouses and back down again. All in all, he was just like any other child born in Dahuang. He might not be great with words, but he remembers their kindness, deep in his heart. Ever since then, he's treated the day summer began that year as his birthday. And as if by divine providence, ten years since his fateful landing, he was back in that very same paddy, gathering the rice fortunate enough to break through to a new level of Originium tolerance.
He brings the seeds, bred with his own hands, alongside him as he sets off once more on the endless road, sending them to every corner of Yan. Wherever the wind takes these seeds, hope sprouts.

modules.moduleDescription:
'He Sheng—'
He Sheng leaps from the earthen slope, turning his head wildly. He rises in a hurry and his thread spool falls into the water, leaving his paper kite cut in the shape of a fowlbeast's tail to become nothing but a tiny dot in the pale blue sky in the blink of an eye, disappearing before his eyes as it follows the river's current.
He Sheng himself was brought to Dahuang by this very river. Were it not for the strong wind that guided him to the shore's embrace, were it not for the sharp, attentive eyes of the farmer hauling sandbags, a babe of not even two years would surely have met with disaster. The Tianshis and the farmers had discussed arrangements for him throughout the night, sent for instructions from the Ministry of Revenue, and even dispatched a Messenger to head directly upstream. However, that year the north had suffered floods after a great drought, while the south was buffeted by a vicious Catastrophe, and so the search for his parents had borne no fruit.
Since then, he was known as He Sheng, and he was considered born in Dahuang.
He grew up atop the crop ridges. He grew up by the water pumps. He grew up on top of the mobile greenhouse frames. He grew up in the Tianshi dormitories and the farmers' courtyards. He grew up in the service channels between the artificial canals. He remembered Tianshi Shu giving palm readings to the children his age, then dabbing a drop of wine onto their foreheads. He remembered sitting atop the backs of stockbeasts alongside Grain Buds, surveying the container ships reminiscent of small mountains slowly entering the waterways, leaving for distant Baizao, Shangshu, or perhaps Danyan to the north. He also remembered one time that an experimental field of high-sugar crops spontaneously combusted, and Dahuang was filled with the inescapable sickly-sweet scent of boiling syrup for a month.
He Sheng rubs his eyes and spots the old farmers he's known since childhood rushing towards him. 'You've passed your exams,' they shout along with his name, joy plastered across their faces. 'You've passed your exams, and Tianshi Shu said she'd take you on as an apprentice!' Behind them, a small stockbeast languidly chews on the fresh grass, a brand-new metal ruler tied to its back alongside a silver kite. A strong wind pushes him towards the crowd, while little bells jingled and jangled amidst the hubbub that had swallowed up heaven and earth.
He jumps down from the slope, running beside the Yiwei plate's canal, pulling a silver wind behind him.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Coming, coming! Warmy coming in with warmth! Huh...? Sheesh, Doctor! No calling me a little potlid like Lanns!

Doctor, do you smell that? Hehe, it's the smell of my sweet pear and vegetables soup, slow cooked to perfection! I said it before, I'm gonna cook the best meals to cure everyone's Oripathy! Huff, huff—It's not so hot anymore. Give it a try, won'tcha? If you don't, everyone else will eat it right up!

Rhodes Island is such a big, biiiig transport, and it has a kinda different furnace than the one at the factory... Oh, I just went to the engine level. The boiler man there thought I was lost and took me back up. I was fine down there, though. I'm used to the heat.

Come, Doctor. Hurry up and eat. No need to worry about me. It cheers me right up to see people enjoying their food. Aw, you still want to share with me? Okay, I'll clean this plate! Om nom nom... Wha? You were just picking out things you don't want to eat? Well alright then.

I made this bracelet from bottle tree leaves. I can keep them fresh for a short while. Hehe, didn't think my Arts could be used like this, did you? Oh, Don't worry, it'll only be for a short while. I won't keep it going for too long, or they'll get tired, too. We should let them be. The withering will come slowly.

Dad liked to collect the carrots we had left to carve into small animals. Doctor, do you think Ray will like this carrot sandbeast? Ah! I think I carved a little too deep. I'm still not very good at this, not like Dad. If only he'd taught me a bit longer...

Doctor, look! The lady at Medical gave me a plaster with pears on it! Rhodes Island has so many Infected. It's the same back home, but we didn't live so well. And I had nowhere to go... Doctor, Is it a bad thing to be an Infected?

Deep in the pitch darkness, those warm breaths slowly got colder...' That's how Ray told her sandbeast stories. I've heard the workers saying stuff like that ever since the accident. They were kind of hard to understand at first, but I know what they mean now.

Yeah, it hurts a lot when my Oripathy flares up. And I'm worried I could go out of control, too. Huff... Hufffff... Doctor, want to try a bite of stewed pear? It doesn't cure Oripathy, but it's sweet. When life's all hard and bitter, we need something sweet! Hehe, does it taste good? Alright, I'll take this to Lanns now.
Doctor? Are you feeling warmer? Have a good sleep now. I'm right here.
Nice to see you again, Doctor. Do you miss Billy stew? I was just heading to the aft kitchen with Lanns— Hey! I'm not a little potlid. Don't call me Potlid!
Whoa... Did you command all these battles, Doctor? You're amazing…
I-I got promoted? Does that mean I can ask Closure to buy some more authentic ingredients?
Thanks for your recognition, Doctor! I'll do what I can to bring even more warmth to the people! Um... Actually, what I mean is... I'm glad I can help out!
I'm all set.
Huh? I'm the head chef today?
S-Slow down... Wait for me!
They're not part of a good breakfast!
I'm here to help.
Fire up the barbie.
Light and gentle…
This place feels a little too cool…
Sparky spark, hop n' jump!
Little flames, shake n' dance!
Roast their tummies!
Shh, it's burning quietly.
Everyone did such a great job... I'll make a big stew to reward them!
Hm—Smells so good. Today was another huge success!
We spilled a lot out of the pot. What a shame...
I wasn't paying attention, it's all burnt...
This room's so warm… Hm? You can adjust the temperature with this panel?
Huff—huff—Didn't burn you, did I?
I'm not— Okay, if it's what you want to call me, Doctor, then no worries. I am a little potlid.
Arknights.

Happy New Year, Doctor! Do you want to go up to the deck to watch the fireworks together? Uh... It's not Arts. It's real fireworks. Everybody at Rhodes Island pitched in to make it happen! Shh—Do you hear that?
Doctor, are you eating good today?

Happy birthday, Doctor! Lanns and I made you a carrot cake! Oh… You've already got lots of cake from the others? Okay... Yes? You could eat a few slices and share the rest with Amiya and Savage? Haha, That's great! I'll light some candles!

When I was still small, I had so, so many wishes, but Dad only ever wished for me to grow up happily... Now I understand. I need to be happy first, then I'll wait for my other wishes to slowly come true. Doctor, make sure you'll be happy too, during this new year onboard Rhodes Island.
