handbook.promotionRecord:
When not on a mission, La Pluma often heads to the ship's bar - but she goes there not to indulge in drinks, but to mix them.
While in Dossoles, La Pluma worked as a bartender at a small bar, and she brought her craft over to Rhodes Island.
As the intersection between the three cultures of Bolívar, Leithanien, and Columbia, Dossoles has provided a variety of rich experiences for La Pluma as she honed her craft, and her bartending has reached quite a high level.
Furthermore, La Pluma's taciturn nature may normally seem like a character flaw, but as a bartender, the same trait unexpectedly makes her become a good listener. After all, people who want someone to talk to often aren't looking for answer, but sometimes just want to listen to themselves.
All of this has gradually made La Pluma more popular with the aficionados and drunkards among operators. Whenever she takes on her role behind the bar, the evening at Rhodes Island is guaranteed to be livelier.
archives:
A Liberi woman who seems rather spaced out.
She rarely expresses her wants, seldom takes the initiative to talk to others, and through her daily interactions, gives off the impression of being rather air-headed. As such, when she first joined, some operators assumed that HR had made a mistake, but this misunderstanding will generally be dispelled after seeing her in battle.
In combat, La Pluma displays a concentration that seems completely at odds with her normal air-headedness, carries out the commander's orders on the battlefield absolutely and without fail, and successfully achieves them most of the time. The stark contrast between this side of her and her normal demeanor has left a deep impression upon many a squad leader who had taken her on a mission.

La Pluma's real name is Rafaela Silva, and her father was Pancho's comrade-in-arms. Due to her mother's early death and the lax discipline of the True Bolívarians, she followed her father and grew up in the military. Because of her docile and charming personality, many of the soldiers saw her as their shining jewel.
The True Bolívarans is an independent government established by the locals to resist the coalition government and the Singas government. From Dobermann's perspective, their army is extremely rugged, but lacks clear organization and discipline. La Pluma grew up in this environment that emphasized the values of loyalty and rapport, and setting aside the big picture, she should've been quite happy - if not for the battle that claimed the lives of her father as well as three thousand other soldiers.
In regards to the specific details surrounding that battle, Pancho did not want to mention any more about it to La Pluma and Tequila, as they were not firsthand witnesses. Furthermore, Dobermann was still a part of the coalition government at the time. The three concurrent governments of Bolívar were not unified in their intelligence and they all regulated the relevant information as it could easily be used to discredit them. Therefore, it is difficult for us to collect accurate information. From the accounts of two individuals in tandem with the intelligence gathered by Tequila, we suspect that this episode was carried out to persecute Pancho, one of the heads of the True Bolívarians's hawkish faction at the time, and this persecution cost the lives of three thousand innocent soldiers.

We were surprised that someone as young as La Pluma would enlist in such a plan when she has virtually no knowledge of Bolívar's domestic affairs. This inevitably reflects poorly upon Tequila as well as her surrogate father, Pancho.
Of course, this is hardly true in reality.
From the beginning, both Tequila and Pancho believed that La Pluma should be kept away from the conflict, so at least after they came to Dossoles, they chose to conduct their activities without La Pluma. However, as the three of them were still family, La Pluma would eventually discover all of these activities.
According to La Pluma's own account, she gave them the cold shoulder for two weeks until they agreed to let her join. According to Tequila, this outcome was the result of his deliberation, followed by days of pleading Pancho.
After all, as La Pluma's sworn brother, he knew that although his sister was obedient, her obedience was built on what she perceived as a mutually trusting relationship. She is willing to obey the words of those she relies on, but at the same time, she is unwilling to accept being excluded even if the other party was acting out of good intentions; even moreso if they were acting on good intentions, she would reject that even more. For her, sharing both happiness and hardship are most important than anything else, a mindset that may also be related to her childhood and her experiences becoming Pancho's adopted daughter.
Of course, since she chose to join the plan, we can't ignore her status as a rebel against the Dossoles City government. Setting aside the fact that ignorance is no justification for her actions, if she simply sees her family ties as the sole criteria for the actions she takes, then she is perhaps even more terrifying than Tequila, who has full knowledge of what he is doing.
La Pluma is aware of this, and though she is kind-hearted, she has even stronger convictions in her views of Pancho's actions than Tequila. As a youth who grew up amidst the flames of war, she has not seen fewer wars than Tequila, and her views of war may not even necessarily be shallower than his. In fact, even Dobermann said that the youth of Bolívar notwithstanding, even she did not know how to stop war except with more war, until she left Bolívar.
For a young woman like La Pluma, the way Pancho did things was perfectly normal. Rather, we should see Tequila's ideology, which has become shaky as a result of Candela's influence, as an outlier.
Rhodes Island has no right or authority to weigh in on the political situation of Bolívar, nor does it intend to judge whether Candela or Pancho is correct. We can only learn what is truly happening in that land from the people of Bolívar.
Perhaps nobody can cast that judgment, and only time will provide an answer.

The Pancho described by La Pluma is quite different from the person in the records obtained from local areas by the Dossoles City Office, as well as from Ch'en's and Tequila's accounts.
It portrays the image of an elderly father who cares deeply about his son and daughter, but does not know how to express it.
With no outsiders around, La Pluma likes to snuggle up to Pancho's side and ask him many questions. At these times, Pancho will pat her head while slowly explaining that she may not yet understand these things. She is willing to listen nevertheless, and these moments have become some of her most treasured.
Furthermore, in conversations with the Doctor, La Pluma has mentioned more than once Pancho's disappointment as well as pride in both Tequila and himself.
He is disappointed that as his son continues to work under Mayor Candela, his ideals inevitably become tainted, and he can see his son wavering.
However, he is proud that his son has undoubtedly matured and is doing well in all aspects, and feels happy from the bottom of his heart when others mention how his son is doing.
He even said that he actually hoped for Tequila and La Pluma to leave Dossoles before he began his plan, so that no matter what happened to Dossoles, his two children would have nothing to do with it.
Of course, he may have never said these words to Tequila, or Tequila might have not taken such words seriously. Such is the nature of the father-and-son relationship. Inadvertently, they've become strangers who know each other better than anyone else.
Originally, La Pluma didn't plan to leave Dossoles with Tequila, wanting to stay behind to look after Pancho. Only when Pancho told her to leave did she decide to go with Tequila, though the relationship between the two siblings has become strained as a result of Pancho's affairs.
There's not much we can do about this, since family affairs tend to be complicated and peoples' rationales can be convoluted. However, her closeness with the Doctor may yet be a good first step. After all, since we accepted her as one of her own here at Rhodes Island, she also hopes to find a new life as well as her own path.

modules.moduleDescription:
Why do people like to drink?
When Rafaela first began her bartending job, the question floated to her mind from time to time.
She can always ask her papá when she has a question. But this is a work thing—Papá usually barely talks to her about his work, so likewise, she'd better not ask him about hers.
And she doesn't want to ask her hermano about it.
Especially not her hermano.
So she'll ask a customer! People are always coming and going in Dossoles, but in just a short time, Rafaela's learned to recognize a lot of regulars, and they all like to talk to her.
According to the person dancing wildly to the jota while calling her 'Rafa' and 'chica' at the top of their lungs, you drink for the color, the mouthfeel, the taste, and for a moment of joy.
But according to the person calling her 'Señorita Silva' while leaning on the bar counter, sluggishly lifting a hand as they sing fado, you drink just to forget and be free from your worries for a while.
'Thanks for asking,' they add more often than not.
Rafaela isn't sure if she comprehended all these answers, but she makes sure to remember every one. It's how it should be, she thinks.
Times change.
As the landship sails, there's a regular thrumming all throughout the hold. Rafaela hasn't gotten used to this noise yet—after all, it's nothing like fowlbeast chirps or beating waves—but she doesn't react badly to it at all.
She's asked another operator before, and now she knows this is how it should be on the ship.
In the landship, music is more varied too, with lots she's never heard before.
Even so, the person who dances wildly while calling her 'Rafa' and 'chica' at the top of their lungs is still there. When she meets this kind of person, she does as they request, and squeezes some of the sweetest fruit juice into their drinks, adding some of the most bracing syrup. But at the same time, she secretly dilutes these flavors until they make for the coolest, most reinvigorating flavors. She gives whoever's drinking it a moment of joy, and all the wake-up they need to bask in that joy.
And there's still the person who calls her 'Señorita Silva' and 'Miss La Pluma' while leaning on the bar counter, sluggishly lifting a hand. When she meets this kind of person, she does as they quietly ask her, and pulls the strongest, most biting bottles from the racks to pour into their glass. But at the same time, she doesn't forget to mix in a little of the finest pedigree, sourced locally from Logroño. She watches them down a glass of bitter drink, but knows the taste left behind won't be totally astringent.
'Thank you,' they say in approval more often than not. Sometimes she nods, but feels strange about it, so other times she just doesn't nod at all.
Of course, this method of mixology isn't entirely described in the Dossoles Guide to Cocktails, but she makes a note of it in there herself.
And she's already given the book away to someone who deserves it. She may not have it anymore, but she's learned it by heart.
Rafaela feels that this way is good.
This is how it should be.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Good work, Doctor. Why don't you take a break? Oh, don't worry, I'm already done with the report… Haha, there's no need for a compliment. It's really not a big deal, I've simply become experienced with these things.

Wait, wait, Doctor, s-stop tugging, I'll take them out myself! There, all the cards I hid up my sleeves. Haha, I figured you'd see right through me. If we get a chance to go to Dossoles, I'll show you some even more interesting things.

Every time I talk to Miss Ch'en, as well as that Miss Lin, I get all nervous. Man, I really don't want to get beaten up again… What, you can't tell? Well, Doctor, here, check out my palms. They're all sweaty!

Yo, Doctor, fancy seeing you here. Looking for someone? Oh, Rafaela? I'm afraid I don't know where she is either. Guess you can tell, without the old man here, we have very little to say to each other.

My old man threw me into the army reserves when I was just a kid. We were all kids, really. Some of us had burning ambitions, but I'd say most of us didn't even know what we wanted. Life was tough, and we were just looking for a way out, nothing more.

Dossoles should be in good hands with Miss Candela. As for the old man, he's better off behind bars for now. He needs to calm down and reflect on his actions. You see, Doctor, when I agreed to help him one last time,  it was my way of trying to find answers,  and sort out my thoughts. Now... I've found my answers.

When we first arrived in Dossoles, Rafaela and I were still very young. We quickly adapted to life there, but the old man still insisted on his integrity and his old ideology... Can't do anything about it, but I figure I should at least try to help.

Doctor, here's the mission report from last time. I've already handled the follow-ups. Ah, don't worry, there won't be any problems. It'd be a real bummer if something unexpected happened and ruined our carefully laid plans. I'm not about to allow that.

So how about it, Doctor? Did you draw the card you wanted? Aw, better luck next time! Though I should say, in a game of chance, there's nothing less reliable than luck. But rest assured, if you're ever in need of it, I'll deliver luck right into your hands.
Doctor, I'll put all the materials I've organized over here. Hm? Asleep… Look at all the important documents you left lying here... You must trust me a whole lot…
Hello there, are you the Doctor? Great, you're just as recognizable as Miss Ch'en said you'd be. Oh, right, I should pick out a code name, then? Hmm... Let's go with Tequila! Sounds pretty nice, eh?
I'm supposed to try this move myself? That… seems painful.
A promotion? Already? Whoa… thanks a million. In any case, without further ado, let's talk about future changes to my work…

When Miss Ch'en brought me in, I never thought I'd see a day like this. So, does that mean I'm one of your most capable subordinates? Haha, it's not a joke, whether you need me to be a tour guide or something else, you can rest easy knowing you're in good hands.
OK, Got it. Leave it to me.
I'm in charge of the squad? Haha, I appreciate the trust…
Follow my lead. Be careful, and don't fall behind.
Come, let us show our guests some hospitality.
Need my help with anything?
Awaiting orders.
Sorry, this path is closed for business.
Pardon me, I'd like you all to stop right there.
Don't get worked up, let's talk first.
Violence isn't really my thing, but well…
Negotiation Failed.
Begone.
You even managed to anticipate their ambush, Doctor! I guess there's no shame in them losing like that. I still have much to learn.
Everything's taken care of, Doctor... How did I take care of it? Doctor, do you really need to hear that?
Phew, that was a close one. Are you alright, Doctor? Yeah… A few of 'em got away. Let me see…
Let's retreat for now! We'll live to fight another day!
Ah, so this is the dorm... Mind if I give it a makeover, and buy some little decorations for it?
Tsk... What the… Oh, it's you, Doctor.
It was raining out there just now, and my hair got a little wet... Sorry, Doctor, could you pass me that towel?
Arknights.

Happy new year, Doctor! My new cards are here, so, how about a game? Entertainment at Rhodes Island is nothing compared to Dossoles, sure, but as long as you've got me, we'll manage. I know a thing or two about creating a festive atmosphere.
How are you feeling today? Want to head out for a bit?
Here, Doctor, a birthday present for you. Guess what's in the box… Hey, no, don't shake it so hard! It's expensive, and we'll have nothing to drink if you break it!

For those who seek change but set off on the wrong foot, no matter how flashy their appearance, they will always lack substance. That's why I appreciate Rhodes Island and its work. Salud, Doctor, to us both finding the right path forward.

handbook.profile:
The former deputy director of the International Trade Management Department of Dossoles, real name Ernesto Salas, was dismissed during the riots in Dossoles City. After that, he was recommended to Rhodes Island by Operator Ch'en, and joined after passing the test.
He was taken to Rhodes Island by a person who had clashed with him just a few days prior. Even in the face of such an embarrassing situation, he still behaved as if nothing had happened, maintaining a friendly and jovial social atmosphere along the way. Truly, Operator Tequila is a rare diplomatic talent fitting for one who serves the Mayor of Dossoles.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Tequila shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.15 u/L
Operator Tequila frequently comes in contact with Originium... or something related to Originium, and this may be related to his prior job. There is a certain risk of infection, and will require careful follow-up observations.


'The way this one tries to fool his way through everything with a smile makes me concerned for his safety. In every way a person can be, he is very unsafe.'
—Sussurro
handbook.promotionRecord:
The personality that we observed in this young man is not quite as sunny and hearty as the side he displays. We were able to discover this without much difficulty when he didn't try to cover it up from us too much.
Operator Tequila thinks about both his own experiences and also the experiences of the people around him to a great extent, and to be able to maintain this is rare indeed. Obviously, Ernesto disagrees with some of Old Pancho's ideas, but nevertheless, chose to aid his father throughout the Dossoles incident.
As for Ernesto Salas, the turmoil of Dossoles and the failure of Pancho Salas was a turning point that helped him make up his mind. Now, the youth have convinced themselves that they've freed themselves from the will and control of the previous generation, and are determined to pave their own way.
This way may branch off in a completely different direction than the last generation, but Ernesto has always admitted that he belongs to Bolívar and will likely return there in the future. If there are more young people like him, the situation in Bolívar may experience new change as well.
This young man is trying to grasp his own destiny, and we are keenly interested in seeing where this leads him.
archives:
After arriving at Rhodes Island, Operator Tequila seemed to adapt to his new lifestyle quickly and easily.
Leveraging his excellent interpersonal skills, he can insert himself into any conversation without breaking the flow, and is able to communicate smoothly and amicably with everyone. Operator Tequila even mediated in some disputes, to remarkable results. He always uses a disarming attitude, cleverly proposing solutions that are amenable to everyone.
His outstanding communication abilities seem innate and do not seem to burden him. Some operators compared Tequila to other operators who are good communicators and were surprised to find that Operator Tequila always seems to have a hearty smile and a friendly attitude. Nobody seems to have ever seen Operator Tequila display any negative emotions.
However, there is no such thing as a person who never experiences negative emotions, and some of the operators who've been in contact with him are persistently worried about this.

The young Perro named Ernesto Salas was born into a military family in Bolívar. His father, Pancho Salas, joined the 'True Bolívarians' local resistance force because of his patriotic ideals, leaving behind his wife and his son.
During the long years during which his father never came home, fighting for Bolívar's independence, Mrs. Salas suffered from a vicious illness that claimed her life after a prolonged struggle that almost lasted a year, leaving the young Ernesto alone. It was not until Ernesto had finished taking care of his mother's funeral that Pancho Salas suddenly appeared at his doorstep.
After that, his father took Ernesto away from his hometown and followed the army through Bolívar. He was sent to join a True Bolívarians prep team, receiving professional military training along with a group of similarly-aged youths. After suffering defeat on the battlefield eight years ago, the old soldier brought Ernesto and Rafaela to Dossoles after three years of drifting and laid dormant within the city, hoping to stage a comeback.
Compared to Operator La Pluma, who is more pure-hearted, Ernesto has a substantially deeper and more complex view on many things. His five years of living in Dossoles allowed the young man to fully integrate into the city, and the ideas of indulging in freedom and the supremacy of hedonism have had a profound influence upon him. His experiences working under the Mayor have undoubtedly changed his viewpoints regarding various matters.

Operator Tequila quickly accomplished two things at Rhodes Island:
First, he improved the wine-tasting ability of many operators. In his spare time, he occasionally appears in the bar to introduce various wines to the other operators, finding something suiting their tastes. When a bartender is present, his sister La Pluma in particular, he demonstrates his knowledge of mixed drinks as well and introduces them to other patrons. After all, it is well known that though La Pluma is an excellent bartender, she seldom takes the initiative to talk.
Second, after joining Rhodes Island, he found that the company does not object to operators maintaining their own interests outside of work, and as such, he planned to continue operating his weapons shop on the ship — unlike the situation in Dossoles, the mobility of the Rhodes Island landship makes it easier to purchase high-quality equipment from various places. In front of the operators who come to his doorstep as customers, Tequila provides serious recommendations to each guest depending on their actual circumstances and needs. Furthermore, Tequila seems to have made significant inroads with the skilled craftspeople of Rhodes Island, and perhaps the modification and customization of weapons will soon be on the agenda.

From the two things above, Operator Tequila clearly demonstrated an adept and ingenious ability to leverage his social skills, bringing his entrepreneurial temperament along with him, well-deserving of his former job as the deputy director of the Dossoles International Trade Management Department.
However, there are certain individuals in Rhodes Island who he struggles to get along with, and Dobermann, an operator from Bolívar, is one such individual. The atmosphere between Tequila and Dobermann was rather tense when they first met. However, Dobermann, who hailed from the same country as him, had more convoluted experiences there than he did, and had a more profound understanding of Bolívar, ironically may have understood Tequila, who hides all kinds of complex thoughts behind a smile, better than anyone else at Rhodes Island. In fact, Dobermann easily saw through his facade and came to regard him as a young man from the same motherland, worthy of nurturing, and keeps a close eye on him. This makes Dobermann one of the few people who can make Tequila visibly squirm.

[Classified Log]
Regarding the events that occurred during the Dossoles championship, Operator Ch'en has already briefly explained the causes and consequences to us in a report, specifically mentioning why she would recommend Tequila and Rafaela to Rhodes Island.
Pancho Salas's long-planned plot fell short, and he will spend a long time in prison as a result. However, Mayor Candela Sanchez saw the championship as a great boon for viewership, and as a result, granted amnesty to all the people participating in the plot with the exception of Pancho, instead removing them from their posts and exiling them, an irony not lost upon us.
The siblings, Tequila and La Pluma, were faced with an uncertain future, and Operator Ch'en, after great deliberation, finally decided to recommend the two of them to Rhodes Island. Ch'en believed that she was in no position to pass judgment on Tequila's actions, and also recognized that Tequila was undergoing his own internal struggle. As such, she gave Ernesto the option of trying to apply to Rhodes Island through the newly-established regional branch in Dossoles. In the end, Tequila and La Pluma came to Rhodes Island together.
What must be noted is that if Ernest was the type of person who could disregard the lives of civilians in order to further his own ends, Rhodes Island absolutely would have turned him down.
However, we can rely on Ch'en's pieced-together account of the incident to understand some of Ernesto's thought process. Old Pancho's plan was very difficult to execute, and in order to enable him to smoothly coordinate with the available outside forces, Ernesto, who was in placed in charge of directing the operation, had to attract the attention of the Mayor as well as that of other unexpected players. He had to instigate a certain degree of panic within Dossoles, and also needed to apply sufficient psychological duress on Mayor Candela. To accomplish these ends, Ernesto commanded his subordinates to place a considerable amount of explosives in residential areas... Ch'en's views on these actions are as follows: At that time, the residential area had been temporarily expropriated due to the championship being held, and all residents had been evacuated before the games. In theory, that area would've been the least populated place in Dossoles during that time.
Of course, this is not to say that Ernesto's guilt should be lessened in any capacity, nor is this to defend him. However, after taking stock of the situation after the fact, we can at least make a definite conclusion:
Ernesto Salas was not interested in creating a moving heap of rubble. Nor did he want corpses strewn everywhere.
Perhaps as a result of the wars he had seen in his youth and his knowledge of their cruelty, Ernesto did not want to become like the armies in his memories, treating corpses and destruction as trophies to be shown off.

modules.moduleDescription:
'Mr. Ernesto, before this trip, I never imagined what a charming city Dossoles could be.'
Inside a luxurious parlor, a man raises a glass to Ernesto, making no effort to hide the joyous surprise on his face.
'It's wonderful to hear that you like the city, Mr. Charles.'
Ernesto's face also bears a cheerful smile, and he raises a glass to meet the other.
The communication terminal buzzes. Ernesto silently glances down at the screen, and leaks a slight frown.
But soon he returns to his previously nonchalant look, as if nothing had happened, and begins introducing the room's decorations to Charles. Afterwards, as Charles appreciates the art on display, Ernesto deftly sweeps a hand over his guest's wine glass, sprinkling a transparent powder into the drink.
A few minutes later, when a bodyguard receives a notification and knocks to enter the room, Charles is deep asleep on the sofa while Ernesto wears a helpless look on his face—
'Mr. Charles isn't used to the climate here in Dossoles, so I believe he won't be able to perform on stage today.'
The young bodyguard becomes nervous, 'Then... What should we do now, director? Mr. Charles is one of the show's headline acts.'
'He should recover by tomorrow, I'll take his place later this afternoon.' Ernesto pats the bodyguard on the shoulder to assure him.
He does not wait for him to respond before leaving.
Returning to his room, Ernesto opens a suitcase lying quietly in a corner. The bottom compartment contains various documents and office stationery he usually uses—all neatly arranged and normal-looking—until he opens a hidden compartment filled with weapons.
After choosing one suitable for covert operations and hiding it on his person, Ernesto turns around to open the closet. Inside is a complete costume for performances.
The news he just received earlier came from his father's underlings—behind Charles is a big deal between Mayor Candela and the Columbian entertainment industry, and a group of exiled soldiers are plotting to kill Charles and ruin the deal.
He has no plans to ruin it, but nor does he intend to have the soldiers return empty handed.
Standing before a mirror, Ernesto changes into his costume while imagining the actions every party might take. When he snaps back to reality, he notices a rather stern look on his face.
'Enough, Ernesto. You're the one who decided to give yourself so much trouble.' As he speaks, he picks up the microphone next to him. 'The audience at least is innocent, so let them enjoy themselves.'
He takes a deep breath, faces his reflection, and flashes his signature beaming smile.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: All done now. Um… do you mind if I read my manga here?
A-ah. I'm just not cut out for real life relationships… On SNS, all I gotta do is send a request to make friends. Reality is such a nightmare.
Utage was my classmate in middle school, and the one who introduced me here. We're… friends, I guess, but Doctor, be warned, riajuus are terrifying!
Eh? Why send messages when we're face to face? Uh, cuz, you know, it's easier that way…

Back in Higashi, I saw Koga election vans on the street a bunch. Their representative is kinda hot... Um, but I don't understand much about that whole side of things, so usually I just voted whatever.

My family says that we all came out of the sea onto dry land forever ago, and that's how we settled down. Would I wanna go back into the sea? Mmnn... honestly, I don't really care.  As long as they don't get Oripathy, life's pretty good in Higashi.
There's some trouble lately. I hear things between us and the Kougon guys up north are getting heated again. This sucks... I wonder if their latest games will make it through…
Um… Doctor, do you think my hobbies are weird or anything? When I was young, the other kids would make fun of me, calling me gross and gloomy. Hmph. Who cares what they said, I certainly don't.

Doctoooor! I'll lend you this game, this manga, and this CD! They're masterpieces that I handpicked, so once you go through them, we'll be otaku buddies for life! We will have so much to talk about. If you're into other genres, just say the word. Better yet, just come over and pick something you like.
Not now, pal, I'm busy right here! Just one more hit... one more hit and he's down! Perfect! Got the rare drop!
I'm Kirara. Nice to meet you... Uh… um… If you don't need anything else, can I leave?
Wow, that's cool… Uhhhh, the ultimate's name's kinda cringe though.
A promotion? As in a job promotion? Ugh, a middle management job is gonna kill me.

I just want to thank everyone for, uh, sticking by me all this time. I realize that, uh some things are better… said in person than by text... So, um, I guess... Tha-that's all I want to say! Thank you!
If you want a support, maybe I can help out… I guess.
...Huh? Me? Captain? Really? Are you serious?
Alright. Begin quest.
Ah. Look over there. Enemy came right out of the tall grass.
Whuh? Started already?
Hfff... ha…
Oh boy, I'm kinda nervous.
Woah, the mangas do not lie.
Feels like I'm smurfing here.
Just like this, right? Okay.
Give me five minutes.
Wait… That move was pretty awesome, huh?
Uso! I've seen no-damage runs, but this is on a whole new level!
Mission Accomplished. Phew… it's done.
Aaarrnngh, missed, darn. No save scumming in real life. I guess…
That's it, time to remake.
If it's an option, I'd like to just stay in my room forever…
Whah! Aaaahh, wrong button... this round is lost.
Oh, hey, Doctor. What? Got an action game you want me to take over?
Arknights.

First off, please do not invite me to anything today without a good reason. Nothing's wrong, it's just…urgh, you wouldn't get it—the terror of having to say Happy New Year to strangers at a party. Besides, I've decided to just dorm it up and play games all day. You're always welcome by the way, Doctor.
Good stuff in the login rewards today.

Happy Birthday, got you a dedicated pager. Just press this button and mine will light up. It also works vice-versa. Hehe. This way, you can reach me whenever you want a game buddy! Um, friends do this with each other, right? This is, like, a normal friend thing?

As an Infected, I get to live a stable life, and I can still read manga and play games outside of work… I never thought a fantasy like this could come true. Maybe there are more dreams that I can make real… Say, Doctor, let's take on the world, together.

handbook.profile: Higashi student Kirara, chose to leave home due to her Oripathy. After sending out an SOS message to her former classmates, she got a reply from Utage and sought treatment from Rhodes Island following instructions. Has a considerable understanding of electronic equipment. Presently providing assistance to Rhodes Island with broadcast communications and equipment maintenance.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 5%
Operator Kirara has been infected by Originium, with minor amounts of crystals visible on the surface of her body.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.17u/L
Kirara's infection was only an accident. In daily life, she rarely comes into contact with Originium. So long as her situation holds steady, the chance of her condition worsening is particularly small.
handbook.promotionRecord:
There is always some way to clear a game.
So long as one makes the right choices, the people in the screen will turn to them and smile. So long as one strives hard enough, the enemy can be defeated and a good ending welcomed.
But reality...
There are no retries in reality. Reality has no choice that reliably wins others over and earns one smiles. Failures in reality cannot be done over, and that is why we dread and are scared of ruining everything.
But, if one has companions willing to confront the elements with them, face the trials together...
Just maybe, things are no longer as scary as when one was all alone.
archives:
Kirara comes from a small-scale nomadic city in the south of Higashi, falling under the jurisdiction of Mitsumoto, the southern ruling bloc. The town borders the sea, the surrounding land level, rich in resources in all respects, and so a commercial economy has developed, trading fairly closely with its surrounding city regions.
At the same time, since it lies far from Higashi's internal two-power line of contention, Kirara's hometown has been less affected by the dispute. Prior to Kirara's own unfortunate contraction of Oripathy, she had been living a proper, stable life as a student should have, her only worry about the tumult of war being whether games produced by the north could make it safely across the chaos zone, for a smooth delivery by their hired shinobi.

As a patient who was introduced by Operator Utage, it never occurred to Kirara at the outset to find work at Rhodes Island, and become a formal Operator like her classmate Utage. For the introverted girl, Rhodes Island offering her treatment for Oripathy also gave her somewhere to stay for a while, and for the money she paid as compensation, it was quite a worthwhile deal. At first, that's all it was.
However, plans are where the little things always go awry. While the Higashi girl would shut herself in her room the majority of the time, using SMS in place of verbal dialogue, and making maximum efforts possible to avoid interacting directly with others, on her occasional 'outings,' she'd always come back having helped some operators while she was out, at times resolving some minor issues with electronic equipment, or being entrusted ad-hoc with instructing operators on how to work appliances, and once she'd even been pursued with inquiries for a walkthrough of a popular game at the time... In short, before Kirara herself even realized it, she was already on fairly good terms with our operators.
We very quickly sent a formal invitation to this Higashi girl, inviting her to become one.
Gratefully, fearful of strangers as she was, she didn't decline.

In Higashi, lineages of Ægir that migrated in and settled down like Kirara's are not uncommon to see. In contrast to our understanding of Iberia's internal situation, Higashi's Ægir by and large have not been faced with overt exclusion, putting down roots in the country without a problem. In the present day, Kirara's own recognition of herself tells the tale—without any weight to it, she can say 'I'm just a normal Higashi girl, that's all.'
However, as is plain to see, stemming from different environs in upbringing, Kirara and other Higashi operators—for example, Operator Matoimaru—have differing conceptions of many things, despite being fellow Higashi.

'The north? Uh... I'm not too clued in about what Kougon's like, but I hear everyone's pretty old-timey there?'
When Kirara introduced her homeland Higashi to us, she raised the subject of its two ceaselessly warring powers, each one occupying one half of the country, exerting their governances on familially unified grounds.
'Mitsumoto didn't seem as heavily armed as the guys over there.' When regarding the contrast in power between her own home faction and the opposition, Kirara first skirted around the topic, only conceding after a while that 'if the fight started, then on a face-to-face battlefield it'd be pretty hard to win... b—but, direct conflict isn't the only thing that goes into who wins and loses! Besides, it's not like it's just war and life's on pause. When it comes to economy, openness and good atmosphere—livability, that's it—then it's us who come out on top, right? Uh, not that they're bad or anything, just, that's how I feel about it at least.'
Beyond this, the Higashi girl also somewhat regretfully, and somewhat barbedly stated:
'Honestly, if we could just not fight, then let's not. The past few years have been pretty good. Been peaceful for a while. Sometimes I buy games from over there and shinobi even deliver them straight to me. But after I heard about it, it seemed kind of difficult to say. Um. I'm not really sure, I don't get it much myself.'
'I heard the eight families used to be one, but then they disagreed on something and that's why they've been split across ever since... *sigh* Honestly, isn't it kind of an overdone premise? What's the point? It's just a bunch of brothers infighting, isn't it?'

Operator Kirara's interests and hobbies are startlingly expansive, with a major love for all niche entertainment comprised in novels, manga, games, etc.—though she had no choice but to leave her home, Kirara insisted on bringing more than half her collection with her, leaving people speechless. Aside from that, music is also one of Kirara's passions; before catching Oripathy, Kirara used to have a part-time job at a bar near her home, and putting on music to fit each day's mood was one of her daily joys.
Per her own absorptions, Kirara has spent considerable time and energy, even at times near the point of foregoing sleep and food, throwing her whole devotion into games or manga. The shut-off manner in which she refused interaction initially worried people, but as we've spent more time knowing her, we've been quick to realize that it's not that Kirara truly opposes interacting with people, but rather, it's a self-defense mechanism of sorts, stemming from a mentality of fearing being hurt.
This fear is closely related to Kirara's experiences as a child. During childhood, her reserved character and her interests unlike those of the children around her led to her being bullied. The experience of being ostracized still has an effect on Kirara to this day; she fears that when she bares her own soul and displays her true self, she may well be rejected or attacked, and so she has preemptively avoided contact with others.
However, should you break past Kirara's inner defenses, and be recognized as a close friend, it'll be clear for anyone to see that the true way she treats people is sincere, passionate, and without any reservation.

modules.moduleDescription:
Thank you for purchasing We Will Survive 3 Online. The following is a brief rundown of the game.

■ Primer
We Will Survive 3 Online is an RPG that includes both competitive and cooperative gameplay. Players will play as and control different characters in-game, raising their survival rank, and battling with other players to win the Survivals.
Of course, joining forces will also be necessary throughout many points in the game, so this is a game to enjoy with your friends.

■ Controls
Players must use a controller compatible with the console when controlling their chosen character.
If you have multiple people playing, have more controllers ready.

■ Items
All items within the game can be obtained either through exploring the wild or through crafting.
Once obtained, items can be stored in your backpack. Backpack space is limited, so you can trade any items you don't need at the moment with your friends in-game, and you can opt to just send them as gifts too.
Each item you collect also unlocks its illustration in the guidebook. If you want to unlock them all and unlock the secret achievement, get trading with players!

■ Competition Phase
Don't forget, your ultimate goal is victory in the Survivals!
Merry cooperation goes hand-in-hand with the struggle to compete afterwards! Use your survival skills to contest and loot other players' resources. Out in the wild, you can also lie in ambush, or directly challenge people, initiating one-on-one battles with other players!
The higher a player's survival rank, the bigger the advantage in the fight! Decide who amongst you will be the champion of the Survivals!

With that, you should now have a decent understanding of the game. Invite your friends, plunge into a colorful world, and have a fun time playing together!

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Do you think me Lady of the Office? This is work for grown-ups.

Don't take Iris's songs so literally. They're meant for the young ones, you know. What? Yes, I'm the guard with the scissors—what about it? Chop-chop? That's the sound of me making clothes—what did YOU think it was? Huh... adults, honestly. So eager to assume the worst.
Preservation techniques? Huh, fat chance. Even Iris hasn't the faintest clue about how I safekeep things. Why should I let YOU know?
Let me introduce Annie to you. She's my very best friend, and another 'me.'

Don't ask me. I don't know why the Castle takes deposits from everywhere, just to send them back out. Granny wants me doing it, so I do. Don't you know? I hear adults call that work. It's when someone has to do it.

Annie's just the quiet sort, nothing at all like me. C-Controlling her? What are you talking about? She's a whole person, she goes where she wants to! She's only by my side because she likes being with me. That's what best friends do. Isn't it, Annie? 'Mm.'

With all the children here, it's no wonder Iris doesn't want to leave. Hrmm... if this carries on, we'd be better off plonking the whole Castle of Dreams here onto Rhodes Island. That'd save so much time and effort.

Good girl this and good girl that, are you saying that I'm not good?—Well, I suppose sometimes you can't just do as you please. You have to 'act' a little, Granny says. Act how? Well... 'My greetings to you. I come from the County of Linton. Bena is my name.' Something like that, you know!

Granny brought me into the Castle when I was young, and I grew up there, and once she retired, I took over her whole job. What could I have in common with Iris, Little Miss Heir-to-the-Castle? What, you think I'm jealous? Dream on! Iris has to watch her figure, but me? I can eat all I want without putting on a pound!
'Rest soundly. Doctor.' Who cares about that Doctor? Come on, let's go out and play! 'Alright.'
I'm Bena, and I was here to fetch an idiot who went out and forgot to come home. But I hear she still has things to do, so I'll just stay a while and keep her company.
Oh, you can't show something this violent to Annie and me.
Ah-hah! See, you do know how to play by children's rules!
Annie, are you ready? We're going to show this hooded hoodlum what our Arts are made of! 'Alright, Bena.'
Two people for a single job. This won't be tricky.
Attention, please! Annie's told me of some brilliant ideas.
Let's just take it like a walk in the forest.
So you want to pull these toys apart too?
Hehehee.
Don't you rush me!
Annie, don't go too far.
Have to be careful, now.
It's trimming time!
Chop-chop!
Whatever breaks needs a fixing.
If there's no fixing it, smash it to pieces.
What did you expect? I'm a dab hand at doing bad things to bad people!
No one else in need of a trim?
Leave the rest to the adults, then. We're going home.
Annie, where are you?!
Hang on, this room's a little small. We're two people here.
Wagh!
Annie's off on an adventure. Want to come along?
Arknights.

Well, happy New Year to you. Annie and I are taking our crack at the Yanese lantern tradition. This one's for Granny, may she live a long and healthy life. And this one's for you, may you... err... you know what, make your own wish...
Hey, no hiding things! What's that you're playing with?

It just baffles me! How can you all be so happy to have your birthdays? One year older is one year further from your childhood innocence. Honestly... here, a new pillow for you. Take it and dream sweet dreams. I wish that you keep that child at heart of yours alive... forever and ever.

It's all over the shop today, isn't it! Let me take some photos for you. One, two... Good, these merry moments are safe and sound now. If you ever want to relive the memories of today, just come see me at the Castle.

handbook.profile:
Specialist Operator Bena, retained aboard Rhodes Island after her attempt to bring Iris back to Victoria turned out fruitless.
Uses unique doll manipulation techniques, able to demonstrate a special strategic value on the battlefield.
Considering her age and her own wishes, only to be deployed under special circumstances.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Bena shows no signs of Originium infection, and neither does Annie.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.14u/L
Operator Bena rarely comes into contact with Originium, and Annie also usually does not.

'Who wrote that last part in her test results? Who's Annie?' —Anonymous Medical Department operator
handbook.promotionRecord:
Bena has extreme hands-on proficiency. All the clothes you see her as well as Annie wearing were personally made by herself. We've heard that in the Castle is an age-old library, and Bena's childhood was, outside of completing what tasks her Granny gave her, spent in that library reading whatever books she wanted to. She had too solitary a life in the past, to the extent that when she discovered techniques in a book that could enable her to 'make' her own true friend, she threw all her time into it without hesitation, and the ultimate crystallization of these techniques is Annie herself. Not a single person in the Castle was surprised by the appearance of Annie; to them, 'everything in fairytales is possible,' yet she'd need an explanation if she were meeting anyone outside the Castle—
'A doll' is the pretense Bena gives. Bena often needs to use Originium Arts and manual ability to protect Annie, and in this regard, there is no difference between her and a doll. That said, those who pay attention will note that the Caprinae and the doll's conversations seem more than anything to be another sort of 'act.' Both have long since understood the other's actions, they know the other's tastes, and making displays of communication is really just a way of relief during daily life, or to alleviate surrounding people's doubts and fears. That perspective is one reasoned through the lens of medical observation by the doctor that carries out Bena's scans. From it, we can infer that when Bena says Annie is 'another me,' she's not lying whatsoever.
'We have queried the relevant Medical Department Operator with resulting testimony that the above speculation has no empirical evidence. Deletion suggested.' —Anonymous high-ranking administrative personnel
archives:
After Iris came to Rhodes Island, a Cautus visitor would often come to carry away what children wanted safekept. But one day, this Cautus visitor brought a Caprinae from Victoria who directly sought out Iris, chattered with her for more than an hour, and then applied to stay aboard just like Iris had. From her vexed, scheming expressions, it's plain to see that she's confident Rhodes Island is using some underhanded method to curtail Iris's freedom. After conducting an 'investigation' aboard that stretched out over two months, she found no evidence to support her view; our Cautus friend and Iris helped out in resolving this misunderstanding, and ultimately, she conceded her own failure of judgment. However, she did not return directly to Victoria, instead having the Cautus leave and then staying aboard along with Iris. The 'public' account is that she feels she should be of company to Iris until she fulfills her own responsibility, but the truth?
'There are riches of toys in the playroom here, and plenty of people to play with. What's the harm in me staying for a while?' After finishing registering herself and becoming an interim Operator Caprinae—so Bena said.

Like Iris, interim Operator Bena asks the children whether they have anything they can't keep safe for long, and hands it to her Cautus associate to take back to Victoria. However, the way she gains trust is unlike Iris. To put it this way: Iris looks after the other children like an older sibling, while Bena plays together with the children, becoming one of them. With the help of her doll Annie, Bena is easily able to slip into the children's conversational circles, and is further able to put on an 'act' in front of others of her own volition, 'imitating' all sorts of personalities. If the Doctor hadn't punctured her 'act' the first time they met, she would be giving the Doctor a completely different character and tone of voice now.
Owing to her consummate 'acting,' Bena is often able to 'obtain' more belongings than Iris does. That said, she's not competing with Iris for anything, only treating this as a sort of work, something she must do. Bena is always willing to do more for the Castle's long-retired 'Granny'—this is one of the few things she will readily admit.

'After Bena boarded, Iris's routine with that mysterious Cautus changed. Now she takes everything to Bena first, the two of them are alone for a bit, and then Iris comes out with the things again and hands them over. Why? What on Terra is Bena up to?' —Excerpt from the failed Iris investigation records

Bena doesn't shy from telling others just what her duty in the Castle is. Just as we'd conjectured, she is the one in charge of the preservation technique for belongings, and through her handling, the lifespans of things sent to the Castle can far exceed the original limit of their existence. However, should anyone attempt to look into details of her technique, she will make use of every childlike technique to avoid talking about the particulars, including but not limited to: dour refusal, blank ignorance, instant lapse of memory, etc., etc. Thanks to her reactions being far too amusing for their own good, some go out of their way to raise this topic with her, but anyone Bena or Annie sees through will soon suffer the practical tomfoolery of a little Caprinae and her doll together. At this stage, one can put the Caprinae prankmaster out of their mind, because most of the time, the one putting plans into practice is the ordinarily quiet, unspeaking doll Annie.
'I'm warning you, never, ever treat Annie as some ordinary doll. She—forgive me for using 'she' rather than 'it' to refer to Annie—she can speak, think, is capable of lone operation far from Bena, and aside from clear spherical joints and a notable gap in personality, fundamentally differs none from Bena at all. Moreover, though she's reserved with speech, her curiosity is exuberant. When not by Bena's side, she'll roam about Rhodes Island wherever on her own, and should she find something interesting, she'll stay there and quietly watch, saying nothing. People are frequently startled by Annie, and some inquisitive people will instruct Annie personally. At times, Annie will be so absorbed in observation that she'll forget to return to Bena's side, who as a master of sorts will scramble about Rhodes Island searching for her doll, then finally find her Annie nestled in some room focused on something all too keenly.'
'I know the description above might not seem too frightening. That's because I've only written about how Annie ordinarily acts. If you antagonize her and Bena, Bena will tell Annie absolutely every last horrid idea off the top of her head, and Annie will then spend days, possibly even up to months, carrying these plans out on you without a break.'
'Believe me, you don't want to try. In terms of build and potential to harm, she has Morte beat by miles.'
—Independently compiled by a Rhodes Island archivist Operator

Roam, lost lamb, without a way, so worn and parched her stomach brays.
Home so far, kindred unknown, name all gone, lost years ago.
Roam, lost lamb, without a way, not even loved by Feline may.
Come a night with stormy rain, thunder and lightning fierce—
The little lamb sits 'neath the eaves, with hollow belly's fears.
And plop! she hears from somewhere off, a person's tripped and fell—
An oldly lady, rushing home, has slipped, and is unwell.
No-one around this roaring rain takes note, or has a mind to pay—
'Oh Granny, Granny, are you fine? Is everything okay?'
The little lamb, her heart so warm, lone helper from afar—
'Thank you, thank you, little lamb, so darling kind you are.
The rain is pouring, quickly now—go home and bless your soul—'
Yet great and vast the city runs, the lamb without abode.
'Come to my house, then, come with me. Take rest beyond the rain.'
She shakes off dry, she nods, and goes to Granny's place to stay.
A basket full of ripe red fruit, she hands the lamb to bear—
The apples, slicked, perfume so sweet, her mind so wide aware.
She swallows down her hunger, by her shoulder lifts the weave—
And once at Granny's door, the rain has soaked her to a freeze.
But Granny doesn't mind, and brings her to the dining space—
'Sit now, darling little lamb, sit down and take your place.
I'm off upstairs to take a bath. I'll be right back posthaste.'
Then Granny leaves behind the lamb, to sit there all alone.
The food is rich, laid wide in front—her mind and stomach groan.
She swallows down another ache, and waits for Granny wise.
She waits, and waits, and waits until she faints from hunger's cries.
She wakes again after some time, now lying in a bed.
She's clean and dry, and by her side, all wondrous food is spread.
She's filled with such a warmth inside, and Granny's tickled pink—
'Eat, now, eat, poor little lamb, there's no more need to think.
You'll never want for food or drink, if you come by my side.'
'Oh, why? Oh, why?' the lamb now asks, and asks again, eyes wide.
'Because, my dear, once storms clears up, the apples washed by rain—
Are sweetest of them all.' And Granny laughs, and laughs away.
—Extract from 'The Jeffreys Collection of Fairytales New and Old'

'Granny said this was a fairytale from Victoria's past. But why do I feel like it's about me?' —Bena
'The story's older than Granny.' —Annie

modules.moduleName: The Jeffreys Collection of Fairytales New and Old, Hardback Edition
modules.moduleDescription:
Once upon a time, in a forest far far away, there was a castle.
And in that castle, there lived a child.
Come the wee hours of each morning, the child would take bread from the pantry, and draw water from the well, from which he would sup for the day.
Once the sun set, he would go to the bedroom, and fall soundly asleep on the bed.
Each day came like the last, and each year the one before.
The forest outside the castle was gloomy and deep, where the wild-beasts never ceased to snarl and bay.
But this did not reach the child—
For the hardy castle protected him.
Yet there is a time for every castle to crumble.
Though the child strived hither and thither to mend the holes, the cracks grew greater and greater.
How it confounded the child!
One day, a witch rang the bell at the castle door.
The child had never opened this door before.
He dreaded all that lay outside, from the pit of his stomach.
Yet he could not help but hear the witch beseech him, and in his kindness he let her into the castle.
The food of the castle was barely enough for the child to subsist, but still he shared a half of his meal with the witch.
Come days later, the witch sought out the child.
She was much pleased with the child's choice, and so she pledged to him:
—I may grant you a wish.
A wish! The child began to think.
He would like to mend the castle, and continue his life from before.
But after the witch was gone, suppose the castle were to fall apart again; whatever would he do?

He thought and thought, until finally a perfect wish came to him:
—I want to take the castle with me, away from the forest.

Hence, the child set upon the journey of his—
And behind him was his tiny little castle, which seemed to look very much like him, and which forever protected him.

—The Child's Castle, selected from The Jeffreys Collection of Fairytales New and Old

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: You need me for something? Hah... Look at all these papers on the desk, each one filled with words. Just the sight of them makes me want to cut them up!

Hfph—haah... Leave me alone. I'm trying to feel my new technique. Aren't techniques meant to be conceived, you say? Hmph, not for me. I just need to quiet down and feel it with my heart. When the time comes, my technique will naturally unfold on my blade.

That ninja... She may evade your eyes, but she cannot fool my senses. I know not what she schemes, but I can promise you I shall not engage her here and now. However, if I find her trying to harm my master... You won't be able to stop my blade.

Who says my eye sight is poor? Heh! This medical report is utter nonsense. If you doubt me, send your strongest, swiftest warriors, and as many as you want. Have them attack me from any direction all at once. If they can make it anywhere close to my body, I'll accept defeat.

It hurts my head to hear righteous principles. Especially when those hypocrites go on and on like preaching scriptures. Hmph, the principles in their mouths are just fancy garbage. For benefit, they will stab even their family in the back. These shameless cowards, my katana will slice them apart!

I've seen winters like that many times. The snow would turn red the moment it hit the ground. My enemies were everywhere. Lying, sitting... I never saw their faces, nor did I care to. My face and chest felt cold, but my hands gripping my blade were warm. Tsk, why am I even telling you all this? Just forget what I said.

Um? How many times have I told you? Don't stand in front of me all of a sudden! What? You wanted me to see you better? You're a strange fellow. I don't need to look at you to know it's you. You think I would just let anybody come this close to me?
Dr.{@nickname}, you remind me of my master when you get serious. I suppose it's because… both you and her compel yourselves to go forward in chase of a grand, ambitious goal.

My master had me come to Rhodes Island for some peace and quiet. Yet how can I find peace, when the flames of war still rage in my homeland? Nonetheless, as a general, you have my respect. Dr.{@nickname}, while under your command, I shall fight by your side and slay all that stands in your way!
Hmm… The air here is nice and cool. Hey you, move over a bit. Let me lie down for a while too.
Akafuyu, samurai, the strongest you'll find. Worrying about my katana? Haha, unlucky for you, I carry it with me wherever I go. You better keep your distance if you are scared.
Oi oi, I'm already strong enough. Stop wasting my time!
I don't need anyone's approval. However, I appreciate your gesture, and will repay the favor with my katana.
Heh, if those guys were here, we'd be out drinking and celebrating. How about this, Dr.{@nickname}. YOU come with me! We'll drink till we drop tonight!
Let's get going already. My katana is starting to rust.
Now we're talking! All of you, with me!
Now! To battle!
No matter who, I shall slay them by my katana!
I'm here.
I've been waiting to slay.
Off to the front!
You will feel my blade!
Now… I strike!
Come one, slay one! Come a thousand, slay all!
Not only your head, I will cut your will to fight!
My katana knows its targets.
Where are the foes actually worth fighting?
Hardly a challenge. I barely broke a sweat.
Some enemies got through? Impossible. There's no way I didn't see them.
I won't run away. My blade has not failed me, I can still fight!
What a small room! Don't keep me waiting in here for too long! I might just draw my katana!
Hmph... You see, if you were my enemy, I would already have sliced you in half.
Come on, let's get ourselves all the ale and meat!
Arknights.

Happy New Year, and why so late to rise? I'm already back from my training. Let me tell you, think of a wish. On the first day of the new year, make 1,000 sword swings. Then that wish will come true. Do not ask whether it's true! It's real, as long as you believe it.
Yo, Doctor, how about some katana training together?

Oh? Today's your birthday, Dr.{@nickname}? Haha! Come, I'll take you for ale and meat! Honestly, why stay quiet about a day so important? Hm? You wonder what I would've gotten you if I knew? Well, need you ask? Better ale and even more meat!

Never have I asked you what we fight for, yes? Stop, no need for an answer. Words are the least reliable of all. I only care that you've considered the question, and considered it well. Lead us forth on a just path, Doctor, and I assure you my katana will be sharp enough to cut through all.

handbook.profile: Akafuyu, a swordsman from Higashi, is the successor of the Nobukage-ryu Iai-suemonogiri Kenpou. Aside from her mastery of traditional swordsmanship, she also possesses excellent modern combat and tactical abilities. Given how distinctively extraordinary she is as an individual, it will take some time for her to familiarize herself with Rhodes Island's combat style.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Akafuyu shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.13u/L
Operator Akafuyu rarely comes into contact with Originium.

That gal wakes up before daylight and starts training every day without exception... How can she not be in good shape? Argh, I wanna arm wrestle with her... If I get to fight her, that's even better!
—Gavial
handbook.promotionRecord:
'She is smart and hard-working.
I looked after her for all these years not because I wanted her to do battle for me or take my place as my successor.
I wanted her to not be tied down by the flames of war before her. I wish for her to find her own meaning of battle. I hope she will come to understand that we will one day face even greater perils.
I ask of you, please help her. I know you can do it.'
archives:
Regular physical exams show that Akafuyu's vision is much worse than average. Further tests and examinations confirm that this is not a result of Oripathy or other diseases, and current technologies are unable to correct her vision.
Akafuyu denies her vision is impaired, and, in actuality, her performance on the battlefield is exceptional; she has shown herself to be more perceptive than your average person. Clearly, her other, heightened senses and her combat skills make up for her decreased vision.
The benefits they provide in her daily life is evidently minimal, however. If you ever find her in the hallway running into the wall head on, try not to point it out to her, lest she gets angry because of that.

Akafuyu tends to be somewhat old-school with her living habits. She wakes up as soon as the sun rises before practicing her swordsmanship, eating her meals, and heading to bed at nightfall if there is nothing else to attend to.
What is surprising is that she is not the kind of person who is completely removed from modern lifestyles. When she hangs out with her fellow Higashi operators, she would often loudly compliment Utage's trendy nails and defeat everyone else in video games, especially action games.
'You think I'm the kind of girl who does nothing but battle? Besides ale and grub, we, too, like to hang out and game after training! Action games improve your ability to react as a commander. Don't you know that? What? How do I play games when I can barely see? What is that supposed to mean? I can see fine! And haven't you heard the best action games are all rhythm games?'
It seems that, with the right amount of mass appeal, no barriers can stop popular cultural works proliferating, no matter where.

Akafuyu has never attempted to hide her upbringing.
'Yeah, I'm that asshole's bastard child, and what about it? He's never admitted it anywhere. My name's been Akafuyu since I was five. Whatever my surname is, it hasn't a thing to do with him one bit.'
She was born into one of Higashi's eight distinguished families. As the illegitimate child of a noble, she was entrusted to and raised in a shrine. She was considered to be a stubborn, unruly child as she rarely obeyed any instructions. As such, she was often punished. When she was five, she met an elder from her family and was subsequently taken in by her. Under her care, she began to receive training in swordsmanship and military tactics, slowly becoming a formidable military leader. For all this time, she has never forgotten who her blood father was, but there was only ever one family member whom she trusted and one master whom she followed.
Out of consideration that Akafuyu is unwilling to have anything more to do with her blood father, his surname will remain redacted in this record.

[Classified Log]
Akafuyu is not just a swordsman; she is also a general of the military.
When the Bloodpeak Campaign came to a conclusion, Higashi found itself in another civil conflict. During the conflict, there was a general in service of the Mitsumoto faction of the Southern Court who, unhappy with her brother, the family head, stirring up a new civil conflict, chose to defect to the north and thus helping bring this conflict to a fast conclusion. Though there was a truce, it did not mean there was an everlasting peace. In the twenty years since, the two courts found themselves in frequent clashes, and the flames of war raged incessantly. In particular, the defected general was the target of multiple assassination attempts by the south. This general is Akafuyu's aunt and also the master she serves.
For years, Akafuyu led a squadron that has braved through hell and high water on the battlefield until she had a close brush with death when she found herself fallen into the enemy's trap. Although she emerged unscathed, as the commander, she was exiled by the Northern Court for the failure. She left Higashi behind and eventually found her way to Rhodes Island.
Despite being exiled by the only master she has ever trusted, Akafuyu had no complaints about the punishment she received. She still firmly believes that she will one day return to Higashi to show her master how far she has come and to fight and bring an end to the war for her master's ideals.
What Akafuyu doesn't know, however, is that, contrary to her belief, it was no mere coincidence that she received an invitation to Rhodes Island. As per the client's request, this record shall remain hidden from the operator's eyes.

Additional remark: Owing to the above, direct, one-on-one contact between Akafuyu and operator Shirayuki should be kept to a minimum.

modules.moduleDescription:
Kirara glances at Akafuyu sitting in front of the TV.
'Why are you suddenly so interested in this thing? You've been stealing looks at it.' Akafuyu doesn't turn around, but simply removes a shoulder guard with one hand and tosses it to Kirara. Her eyesight may be poor, but she's so aware of her surroundings, she might as well have a camera in her back.
'This armor...'
'It's an heirloom. It's not valuable. My master doesn't go out to fight much, so it was bequeathed to me.'
'Um, the design...'
'It's a very special shape to the armor. In the old days, each family had its own style.'
Kirara touches the shoulder guard and compares it to the armor in her game. She starts to think the developers must know of Akafuyu.
'Someone asked me almost the same question before, a little girl about your age. She would ask me under her breath, 'Captain, is your armor made of some high-tech material? Can it really withstand a grenade blast?' Ha, she might have thought I was some antique.'
'So, can it?'
'Don't be a fool. It's hard, sure, but it's just a piece of metal. You'd do better training hard and listening to your commander. She knew that, of course. Still, this armor has saved me plenty of times. Look, the pit that jumps right out at you there, that crossbow bolt almost pierced clean through my arm. Oh, and she was there in the last battle, standing next to me. Damned near died.'
Kirara suddenly loses interest in the topic.
The heavy feeling on her knees reminds her that this shoulder guard is supposed to be unique, representing an era of glory passed from one generation to the next, still thick with the stench of war and sacrifice.
But now, it's a rare item in a popular game, and any player can get it, if they pay enough.
Akafuyu stands up. Kirara decides to hurry over and take out the freshly purchased game disc before Akafuyu notices.
'By the way, do you have a minute?' Akafuyu walks towards her, 'I just killed the final boss without taking any damage. Can you upload the recording to that forum you like? Oh, and put my name on it, so you-know-who doesn't miss it...'
Kirara only now notices the game on the screen. The main character is holding a wooden sword with the lowest ATK, wearing almost no armor, except... the piece currently resting on her knees.
'Does it... bother you?'
'What? Oh, that it's my armor? If someday the people of Higashi know it from a game, rather then from a battlefield... then it can only mean that the war is finally over.' Akafuyu takes back the shoulder guard and slots it neatly into place, 'I've waited too long for that day.'

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Let's just burn 'em. You weren't gonna give those papers a second look anyway.
If you wanted me to lay defenses in here, I'd break up the floor for starters. Not that I mind, it's for you to think about.
Got twps from Royal Guard knocking about, have you? Heh, ain't that interesting.
Calibrate the sight? Nah, materials I ordered last should be here almost, I'll make the arrows first... Oh, push off, out my way.

Most who leave Vouivre don't agree with the mercenary life in Sargon. Move to Victoria, end up doing something else instead, they do. Like... factory-working, farming, you know. Having their own little touch of land.

You could probably tell, but I didn't use to be artillery. Mainly studied recon, infiltration, CQC, all that. Did not bloody take to it, and the instructors wouldn't let me switch courses, so I dropped out, simple as. What's the point in learning things you hate?
Oh, you're helpless! How am I going to the workshop wearing this?!

It's meant for attacking nomadic cities, this weapon. Using it to help you lot cope with skirmishers? It's like a hatchet to a cupcake. Let me try hitting a city or two sometime for practice, won't you?

Don't you think these crystals on my shoulder here match well with my hair color? I like my off-the-shoulder clothes too, so it's perfect. Shame, though, it would've been nice if they covered the whole way like that Siracusan Messenger girl.
I'll be heading back to sort stuff out, then. No point wasting time on this rotter.
Arianrot, codename Toddifons. I don't like working for ordinary people, so I've got my fingers crossed you show me something unusual.
Boring. Off we go.
What goes on in those Logistics' minds? Oh, look what Arianrot made, let's just grab it and... For me? Tch, fine. I accept. Your feelings are loud and clear. Thanks, see you.
You've seen a Draco's flames before, I bet you anything. You ever imagined, the sight of them raining down on your enemy? I can make that your reality!
I'm listening.
Work's on. Focus.
You lot go ahead. I've got things to prepare.
Visibility clear. Awaiting orders.
Still not done?
Iawn?
Mounting complete.
In position.
I don't need visuals. Give me the map.
This area is cleared. Next!
Nothing remains once the arrows rain!
Ha! Fire wouldn't go out while there's something left to burn!
There's only so many who can make this thing shine—guess you're one of them.
Out without too much ash on me. Gwych.
Ammo's more precious than that little lot. Deal with 'em yourself.
Still good to move? We're heading home. Grab on.
Like this titchy bit of space is enough? Let's break this wall down and I'll have the whole area behind, Diolch.
Think it through before you put your hand out.
Go on if you need something. Don't wait for me to change my contacts, I can hear you whatever color they are.
Arknights.

Yeah, New Year's, there's a party, the whole song and dance, I get it. And that's why I'm sitting right here, having a drink with my magazines, while you carry on moaning and whinging. Trust me, that's my happy times.
So it's you. If you need something, out with it.

Oh? Birthday, then, today. How about we head deckside to celebrate? I'll give you my little siege ballista, can set off some massive fireworks? Oh, too dangerous? Tch, you sopping wet blanket. Whatever, off to the shops then, pick you out a proper present. Well? Get changed already, we're off.

Oripathy comes second, I've said that. If I'm not able to do what I like, that's not life no matter how long it drags out. And you know, being here, Rhodes Island, I always get a crack at something interesting. I half like it working with you lot. So don't you ever go letting me down.
