That Suzuran girl I turned down just now, I wonder if I've been too harsh on her... She was kind enough to invite me to her tea party, but socializing isn't really my forte…
My body is frail, frailer than most others'. To die a young death, to forsake all my pasts, then to be born anew… 'Rejuvenation'… such is the cruel fate of mine…
Memories dissipate as spumes on shore. The pains, the joys, the pasts I don't want to let go… nothing will be there as I look back.
Though my memory fails to serve me, I can still sense the unspeakable flowing within my blood. Stay away from the sea, Doctor. It'll be a nightmare devouring us all. It is… fear itself.

I do wonder sometimes what 'mortality' is to those with true longevity, like Dr. Warfarin and her people. For them to shed not a tear when bidding farewell to the departed, is it only because theirs have long run dry?
Doctor, could you take these flowers to the children in the ward, for me? Yes, just like always, place them by their bedsides… Thank you, for helping keep this secret.

Doctor, come quickly, we need to find Closure! It seems Thorns and his companions have burst a water pipe open in the corridor, and Weedy is furious now! I'm soaked to the skin... Um, I seem—like I'm enjoying myself? Wh-What do you mean?!

Every time I watch a film, I keep the ticket stub afterward. These leftover vestiges always serve to me as a reminder, even if the contents would be lost to me... Doctor, could you come watch a film with me? I'd like to preserve the time I've passed with you, too.
Sleep sound, Doctor... By the time you wake, will you have forgotten about me?
Code name… Whisperain. A roving doctor, nothing more. If possible, please take me as a traveler lodging under the eaves in rain. You needn't pay me much mind…
In the face of such fierce combat, I worry... I wouldn't be able to survive.
Thank you very much. But I hope you treat me the same as always...

Those sorrows I could not wash away with one death—I always feel like they're strands, wisps, winding about my skin... Doctor, you've come to forget the past too—could you maybe understand this feeling?
Please leave the assistive work to me.
I'm the leader...? That's a little…
Please keep with me. Don't go too far.
Please be careful, everyone. Protect yourselves and stay safe.
Very well.
Injections are ready.
Come to me if you get wounded.
Let me dispel the pain.
Disinfection comes first.
Do not be afraid.
My treatment will not hurt.
I know this scent of death well.
Sleep tight... May the rainfall shelter all dreams.
This is how their story ends. Tragedies, one following another...
Leave the pursuit for later. I'd like to see everyone treated first.
I'm sorry, I could have fulfilled my role better…
Such a peaceful place this is. I can hear the patter of rainfall.
You startled me…
D-Don't move, please! Something got my hair…
Arknights.

Elysium, Thorns, please stop blowing your noisemakers, quite a few operators are already staring at you... Ah, Happy New Year, Doctor. The New Year at Rhodes Island truly is so vigorous... Was I ever this happy to celebrate in the past? I'm afraid I no longer remember.
What will we be doing today, Doctor?

Happy birthday, Doctor. Amnesiac as you are, you still haven't forgotten the meaning of this day, which tells me a lot. In that case, would you like to keep the stub of a movie ticket with your birthday on it?

Please, allow me to sit out here on my own. It doesn't feel quite right being a part of this ship's commemoration day, given that I don't know when I might depart... That being said, I will always remember the sound of rain pattering on the deck. There's little else like it.

handbook.profile:
The Iberia-born roving doctor, Whisperain, never stays in one place for too long. Records of her work in the area remain all throughout Kazimierz, Sami and the like. Her patients appear to have received treatment from her while she passed by, and in her seemingly aimless wandering, she's rescued more than a few from the brink.  
Since she administered treatment to a mid-mission team of Operators met by chance, she is now an ad hoc member of the Medical Department as an accompanying doctor, journeying together with Rhodes Island for the short-term.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected. 

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Whisperain shows no signs of Originium infection. 

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.10u/L
Operator Whisperain is exceptionally attentive—even rigorous—in defending herself, and rarely comes into contact with Originium or related products. 

What's going on here? How could her body become so frail...? Never mind Oripathy, even a bad fever could cost her her life! Ugh, with her constitution, she had no business running amok outside all this time.   
—Warfarin
handbook.promotionRecord:
To want to flee for fear of harm is a very normal thing. 
Our biological instincts bind us to innately fear pain. Perhaps there are people with the willpower to overcome these fears, or perhaps there are people long numbed to them through all their torment, but we must recognize—fear is a normal thing, escaping is a normal thing, and these cannot be criticized. 
The question is, where does blind escape lead you, and who can truly flee from their pain? 
Luckily, there are people on Rhodes Island who will reach their hand out to her, and people who can make her want to try stepping out of her own world. 
Perhaps, what she lacked right now was only a bit of courage.
archives:
Just like Miss Whisperain said, she's a traveler who happened across Rhodes Island by chance. After aiding a few Rhodes Island operators, her dune buggy malfunctioned and left her stranded in the middle of the barrens. The Rhodes Island landship picked up on the distress signal, and so went to rescue her.  
As a traveling doctor, Miss Whisperain had no set destination at all. There was no doubt she fulfilled high standards as a Medic, with her expertise above all else being first aid in various emergency situations. Once we considered Miss Whisperain's circumstances, we sent her an invitation. Rhodes Island wouldn't restrict her staying or going, but if her own interests aligned, she could act as a provisional Medic Operator in joint with Rhodes Island's operations before she left.   
After several days of hesitation, Miss Whisperain accepted our proposal.

The Medical Department's routine health inspections have made it clear that Miss Whisperain is not in good condition. In summary, she is in no way suited to activity as a traveling doctor. 
This verdict is completely objective. Her exam numbers show that every index of Miss Whisperain's health falls below average compared to any healthy person. Her immune system requires particular attention, having reached a dangerous state. Oripathy has not infected her frail body, despite its rampant spread across this world and all its people. Yet, frail is still the only word that appropriately describes Miss Whisperain's constitution.   
We're not sure why Miss Whisperain doesn't choose to settle down in a city suited to her, but rather continues to walk the world's four corners, never calling a single place home for long. Regardless, while Miss Whisperain lodges for the time being at Rhodes Island, the Medical Department has suggested she be a medical worker onboard the ship, minimizing unnecessary field missions and avoiding further burden on her body.

Miss Whisperain is hardly ever seen or heard of in social settings. This is not purely due to her reserved, shy nature— rather, she actively takes deliberate pains to avoid contact with others.  
In response to contact from gregarious operators, Miss Whisperain is typically evasive. From the faint sorrow and vexation in the little talk she makes, and the struggle and expectation seen behind her glasslike eyes, you can tell Miss Whisperain isn't distant by nature. There's just some innate reason she has, and so she chooses to be apart from the crowd, to close herself off from others.  
However, there seem to be signs of a turn for the better, in the time since she joined Rhodes Island. Though the roving doctor still avoided any involvement with others at all costs, Rhodes Island's cast of operators isn't short of warmth, and life aboard the ship always seemed to hide all kinds of 'accidents' to tie her up in... and after enough 'accidents,' we can say that our present Miss Whisperain lets much more of a rich array of moods show than the one that first joined us. And by her side, little by little, more familiar faces have started showing up.  
Though it perplexes her and she's helpless in the face of them, one can see that Miss Whisperain doesn't sincerely reject the bubbling, lively little mishaps that happen around her.

Outside of medical work, Miss Whisperain spends most of her free time at the library or AV cabin. Among those quiet indoor amusements, moving pictures are her most beloved. Her expertise in film appreciation is nigh unparalleled.  
Her angle is nothing like a critic's, fussing and picking and passing judgment. Miss Whisperain throws herself whole into the film, learning a work's characters' emotions by firsthand experience. The sentimental roving doctor's natural heart is fine-woven and sensitive, highly empathetic towards others, and this becomes even more apparent when she's picture-watching. Miss Whisperain can often be influenced by strong emotions, writing out vivid, piercing impressions of what she watches, and these reviews have been well-received across the ship, esteemed by many movie-loving Operators as a viewer's guidebook.   
For each film she's seen at a regular screening, as a memoir, Miss Whisperain will hold onto the cinema ticket's stub. To the roving doctor, this act seems to hold a special kind of sense, each ticket stub representing some memory she doesn't want to forget.  

[Classified Log]
Setting aside her innate frailty, by her own disclosure, we've ascertained that Miss Whisperain falls under a very rare branch of the Ægir, possessing an extraordinary constitution. Under the effect of the race's characteristics, this type of Ægirian is exceptionally frail. When the body is incapable of enduring its environment or has been gravely wounded, it will relapse to a young stage, losing its prior memories and maturing anew.  
After several examinations, the Medical Department arrived at a conclusion, and this rather strange conclusion seemed to fit with Miss Whisperain's own confessions. Her mentions of 'rejuvenation' during conversation were not truly in the sense of longevity, but referred to a biological differentiation, transformation and regression. 
It was precisely because memory loss accompanied each of her 'deaths' that Miss Whisperain began to dread forming connections with people, scared that her own deaths and their oblivions would come to harm the people around her. For the keenly sensitive Miss Whisperain, it's hard to bear.

modules.moduleDescription:
On that rainy day, a young traveler came through our door, breathing faintly to us that she wished to shelter from the rain.
It was around that time that the children in the village had fallen sick one after another, and my precious Veitch wasn't lucky enough to be spared. We all muttered how it was some devil's witchcraft silently spreading about, and so we all kept our houses tightly shut. But we didn't have the heart to throw a single frail woman back into the wild in the rainstorm, so we agreed to let her in.
The first moment she laid eyes on Veitch, she sensed something was wrong. She was prudent as we worked through his symptoms with her, and she asked how the village at large was doing, before revealing herself to be a roving doctor.
'This is no Originium Arts; it's an illness. The soil and wellwater is contaminated, and the children are the first to be sick; as the poisoning builds up over time, the adults will come to show symptoms too.'
She opened her suitcase, and mixed a medicine with practiced hands. As she did, she spoke. 'I'm sorry. All I can give myself is a temporary first aid, but the only way to cure an illness such as this is to be away from the contamination's source, and convalesce through medication in the long-term. If possible, I'd ask you to tell all the village that they should move away from here.'
'But this is our home,' my husband said with worry. 'Even if this soil will harm us, where are we going to shelter if we leave here?'
The doctor said nothing more. She worked in simple silence.

The weather had cleared up the next day, and I found the doctor just as she was about to leave. On the door was stuck a wild flower, a kind that grew anywhere. In that instant, a faint memory of someone seemed to match with her in my head.
'I remember you, doctor. I've met you before.'
'I was still in a small town on the outer edge of a nomadic city. You'd make home visits to everyone, and you always secretly handed out fresh flowers to us children... I was behind the curtains watching, I remember seeing from there.'
'That was decades ago by now. My mother caught Oripathy, see and we were driven out... and I've gone from a child to a married woman now, I know you wouldn't recognize me. But, well, you look about the same now, compared to all the way back then.'
I told her how grateful I was for her, from the bottom of my heart, for she cured me of my fever when I was young, and now she'd saved my own child too. Yet the look on her face was at first blank, then became so sorrowful, as if she was close to weeping.
'No, please... don't go on any further. Just treat me as though I'd never visited before.'

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: I can be your assistant, but is it okay if I do some craft work here?
Doctor, if you like excitement, you should probably stay in Siracusa for a while. You won't enjoy it so much after that.
Considering his personality, sometimes even I wonder why no one's beaten Chiave to death yet.
Doctor, are you interested in DIY? See, the three of us actually design and make our own weapons and outfits. You could join us sometime, if you want.
After cleaning up Chiave’s messes so many times, I’ve realized something: If you want real power, you’ll need to rely on more than just violence.
In Siracusa, most people my age just want to join a famiglia, but there are plenty more who would rather live an honest life instead. Sometimes, I think those are the strongest of us all.
(Yawn) …Oh, sorry, Doctor, I didn't get much sleep last night. Rhodes Island is way too safe. It's taking some time to get used to.
Chiave, Broca, and me. The three of us are like brothers, and we've done all kinds of things together. But, sometimes, I really wonder if this really is the life for us.

To tell you the truth, I wanted to be a public servant when I was a kid. Up until my dad made me pick up a weapon for the first time, that is. I don't mind drifting around with the other two, but I always felt like I was missing something, and I know what it is now. I wanted to become as strong-willed as you are, Doctor.

handbook.profile:
Aosta, former Siracusan mafioso, later became a member of Chiave's gang. 
After a particular incident, he joined Rhodes Island along with his leader, Chiave, and is now active as a front-line attacker.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Originium crystals distributed across surface of body, confirmed Infected by medical examination.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests have shown the outlines of his internal organs to be indistinct due to abnormal shadows. Originium granules have been detected in his circulatory system, confirming him to be infected with Oripathy. 

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 5%
Small traces of infection are visible on the surface of the body. 

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.23u/L
Operator Aosta didn't begin treatment until his infection had spread to a considerable extent. All other indicators are normal, which goes to show he leads a healthy lifestyle. Thanks to this, his condition isn't very severe.
archives:
Although he tends to keep quiet, Aosta is a dependable Lupo whose demeanor is almost impeccable. 
He may sound a little street with his vocabulary at times, but it's hard to believe he used to be one of Chiave's underlings. 
He's cautious, and he thinks his problems through. That has earned him excellent appraisals from all the operators he's teamed up with.

According to Aosta, his work ethic is a product of his time with Chiave.
Indeed, Aosta is careful, if you're feeling generous, but less charitably, he's way too anxious. It's astonishing to see someone as young as him possess such a pessimistic personality, but when you look at Chiave, this perhaps may not be so strange.
Chiave made all the decisions about what to do, Aosta decided how to go about doing them, and Broca did all the hard work. It's clear they made it this far in no small part thanks to Aosta's meticulous planning.

Aosta is the most skilled in handicraft of this trio. 
More specifically, he has experience in everything from simple origami to complex sewing. If there's anything he hasn't tried his hand at making before, he's able to make something fairly close after just a few glances. 
It's a talent rarely seen here in Rhodes Island—we've also got no plans to hire a full-time tailor here—and that has made him hugely popular among our female operators. He's become far busier outside of his deployments. It doesn't seem like he minds at all, though. He's taken on a variety of requests, and he even seems to be enjoying the work.

Out of the three, Aosta is the only one who has an understanding of Siracusa's inner workings as a country. 
Even though he grew up in Siracusa and never traveled abroad, he still understood Siracusa's uniqueness. As we all know, the way Siracusa operates is fundamentally different from how other countries are run. There, the families run the show behind all public affairs. 
Thanks to this unique characteristic, life in Siracusa is quite strange even in this diverse world, and Aosta understands clearly that the Siracusan lifestyle is not what people of other origins would consider normal. 
It's difficult to say what makes a normal lifestyle and what doesn't. However, when the authorities avoid getting involved with the wars between families, it's safe to say that life in Siracusa can hardly be called normal. 
Aosta knows so much about the environment he grew up in, and still manages to harbor such doubts about the place. You don't come across people like that often. The good thing about this is that he was able to adjust to life in Rhodes Island very quickly. Unlike Chiave, who took a very long time just to accept and follow the rules here.

modules.moduleDescription:
The night streets of Locomotiva City are teeming with armed thugs. Their target is hiding in an alley.
'Aosta, I have an idea. Let's put on wigs, change our clothes, and slip out of the city with the acrobats.'
'Shh, keep your voice down. You'll blow our cover!'
'Hey, I'm serious; I've really thought this one through! We just smashed a pie right in the face of the most notorious don in Locomotiva City—and honestly, he deserved it. But we didn't have time to grab even a single coin before running. Now we're lost, and the streets are full of people ready to turn us into mincemeat. If we don't do something, we're done for.'
'We're not lost. This is the back alley behind Baron's Pub, and there's an abandoned warehouse right across the street. We can hide there temporarily. There's even a working landline inside.' Aosta pulls a city map from his waist pouch.
'And what is this wobbly line here?'
'Our escape route—the one you just ran along!'
'Broca... did you know he planned all this?!'
'No, but it doesn't surprise me.'
'You mentioned a landline—who are you planning to call, anyway?'
'The guy who gave us meds last time. Our car's still with him.' As he speaks, Aosta takes out a business card from his pouch with the words 'Straightedge, Rhodes Island Operator' printed on it.
'I could help him remodel that boring office of his as payment.'
'We were caught off guard the last time we had to flee,' Aosta says, taking out a few coins from his pouch, 'I'm not going unprepared this time.'
'Aosta! You said you didn't have any money for my modding supplies, but you were hiding cash! What else do you got in that pouch? Probably not anything good to eat, though. Ugh... I'm starving. Is there any meat we could roast in that abandoned warehouse?'
Aosta opens his pouch again and takes out two candies in plain packaging.
'I'll never say you're like my mom again! But... only two? If there's one for both of us, what about you?'
'I'm not hungry.'
'There's that mom tone again...'
'Shut up and eat the candy. Do I have to unwrap it for you?'
'Alright...'
He tears open the candies and throws the wrappers to the ground. Chiave's expression shifts from gratitude to confusion to disgust.
'Ugh! What is this?! It tastes awful!'
The white-haired Lupo, who had remained stoic and serious throughout their escape, finally breaks into a smile.
'It's booger-flavored trick candy, to curb your appetite.' He raises a finger. 'The thugs outside have thinned out. Are you ready, you two? On the count of three, we dash for that warehouse.'

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Some burdenbeasts won't drag themselves to work until they're whipped. But you're different, Doctor, you're way smarter than a beast, isn't that true?

Doctor. Just to put any little misunderstandings to rest, let me say this now. Maria might call me her aunt, but that's only because I'm higher in the family. I'm still young. I'm not much older than her. And, I'm still not married. Clear?
A spat between me and Dobermann...? Oh, don't worry, she's a top-of-the-top instructor, I know that. We've just had a bit of a… bit of a difference on how we like to train our people, that's all.

There's plenty at Rhodes Island who pack personality AND strength. You could pick anyone, turn them into competition knights, and have every eye in the room on them... Well, maybe let's not stir that pot.
Doctor, can I borrow you? I just want you to help me carry some things. What things, you ask? Well... Hmm... all sorts of random things I buy when the mood strikes me.

My injury...? Well, I'm not setting foot in that arena ever again, and I've long since learned to get along with my right hand. So let's not worry yourself, okay? Or maybe... you're just being polite, Doctor? Tiptoeing around saying I can't fight at operator standards, huh?

My little Maria, she just runs away to the Engineering Department any time she's free. Such a headstrong girl she is, I never know what to say. Where did I go wrong that she ended up like this...? Well, whatever. Compared to forcing herself to arm up and do what she doesn't want to, life is better this way.

Hm…? Oh, Hello, Doctor. No, I've just been feeling a little empty. Margaret never needs my fussing, Maria's found what she wants to do here, but... what about me...? Oh, gosh, what am I saying? Don't you worry about me, Doctor. I'm fine.

Doctor, we don't get along half bad, but you don't just lie there and leave it all up to me, not in your wildest dreams. I hate danger plenty, but layabouts leave a bad taste in my mouth. Though, when your back's against the wall... Well, we can talk about it then!
Someone's easygoing, eh? Alright then, I'll let you nap for ten minutes.
Ahh, this is Rhodes Island, is it? I'm Whislash Zofia. As a former competition knight of Kazimierz, trust me when I say I'll whip your operators into shape.
I've never even heard of fighting like this before!

handbook.profile:
Whislash Zofia, former competitive Kazimierz Knight. In family terms, Operators Nearl and Blemishine's aunt on their father's side. Has reached the Final 16 of the Majors before. Was left-handed in the past, but owing to some impairment, has switched to using her right hand. 
Though atrophied in combat compared to her peak, she holds unique insight and a rare talent in training others, currently folding herself into the Instructor lineup headed by Dobermann. Training Operators is her day-to-day priority, only joining any missions as required.

archives:
The distantly removed aunt of Nearl and Blemishine. A Kuranta madam with a domineering streak. 
Possesses bountiful Kazimierz assets from her winnings in the competition knight circuit, but seems not to take much interest in her own wealth. 
She's got no ill will at all, but when chatting with her, you may invariably feel she projects a sort of arrogance. As long as you push past that first impression of yours, getting along with her is easy as could be.

At the outset, Whislash had a prolonged dispute with Dobermann, which at its root was due to their conflicting views on the training of operators. 
Dobermann, of military birth, believes that operators should be required to attain what she sees as average proficiency for a combatant, afterwards earning the right to choose how they develop themselves. Whislash of competition knight lineage, however, doesn't care at all whether operators meet a uniform average, instead aspiring to bring each operator's own characteristics to their maximum potential. 
Neither's way of thinking is wrong, but even so, Dobermann and Whislash are both particularly stubborn. They were at an impasse for a while, before finally taking a meeting and reaching a compromise. 
Though perhaps they came to understand each other while butting heads. Ever since then, their relationship's gotten pretty good. You might hear them talking tactics from time to time now, or even just eating meals together.

While she is Nearl and Blemishine's aunt, Zofia the Whislash does not take the surname Nearl. Strictly speaking, she cannot, since her standing is as a branch member of the Nearl family, which bars her from directly taking up the name. 
But this was policy for the Nearl family at its shining peak. Following Nearl's exile, it might've been simple enough, with all that she possessed, to seize the title of Nearl if she so wished. 
Mind you, Whislash did not. 
One part of it was her sisterly relationship with Maria. The other, as she saw it, was that the Nearl name held hallowed significance. 
In a certain sense, her opinion overlaps with a true direct relative of Nearl's and Blemishine's, their uncle, Młynar—'This is not a name I'd tarnish with such underhandedness.' 
Though, sure enough, they define 'tarnishing' in different ways. 
Unlike Młynar, Zofia does not reject the idea of the competition knight itself. Put another way, she accepts at least its existence—but does not err in her forthright and sporting approach to dueling, which she took to the competition as humble representative of the Nearl family. Unwilling to bow to any sponsors or firms, she went from start to finish lacking any favorable provisions or equipment, until the Final 16 brought her journey to an end. Even now, despite that gulf in equipment taking her left hand out of action indefinitely, she has no regrets. None—come the Major, she wants to make sure Blemishine continues to fight as she once did.  
It's plain how in Whislash's heart of hearts, her honor as a member of the Nearl family is unbreakable, and anyone could see how she looks after Nearl and Blemishine. When joining, she even assured us that if Rhodes Island wasn't fit for purpose, she'd prefer to take Nearl and Blemishine with her to raise them herself. We've had some personnel envy the sisters in a way, having an elder who cares for them like that.

When joining us, it seemed that as long as Nearl and Blemishine were doing well, Whislash wouldn't have any issue with us. But as time passed, as other operators arrived, and showed her ever more ways of life from ever more corners of Terra... chatting with the Doctor one day, she posed a question she'd never thought of asking before—somehow, she'd never considered what she wanted to do herself.  
Safeguarding the Nearl family name, looking after Nearl and Blemishine. These were what she wanted to do, but somehow not all she wanted to do. 
Ever since Nearl was cast out, she'd found a new purpose for herself. Maria had jumped headlong into her beloved engineering. The name of Nearl was all but safe. Once everything she'd worried about no longer needed her, the realization struck her—she had no idea what should come next. 
Blessedly, the operators of Rhodes Island not only reminded her of life's variety, but that the vast majority of it was open to try herself. After a short period of haziness, Whislash decided to continue as an Instructor on the one hand, while trying all sorts of new things she'd never imagined on the other. She could seek out her new purpose in life. After all, she's young, life's long, and it's not like there's a rush.

modules.moduleDescription:
Even before the match, Zofia knew that she had a long way to go if she were to defeat the Fissure Knight, but it wasn't until she actually had to fight the Fissure Knight that she knew how fatal the gap between them was.
She heard that her opponent had staff who reviewed all of her previous matches and had been trained by coaches bearing the same weapon and comparable stature to her. In effect, her opponent already knows her like the back of his own hand.
She had also heard that the Fissure's armor was forged specifically to take on her weapon of choice in battle. Not only does this armor make it difficult for her to get a good grasp with her whislash, any attack she manages to land isn't going to hurt her opponent in any way.
On the other hand, the blades yielded by her opponent have both been treated to give them fine cutting abilities.
She used to think these were just rumors. Alas, it all turned out to be true.
Zofia is starting to get discouraged. After all, her last few matches have all resulted in her defeat.
How many companies are there sponsoring Fissure? Are there really tens of thousands of people racking their brains together just to figure out how to take on the Whislash Knight?
She needs to find a way to get herself out of this, lest she gets defeated yet again.
Did Nearl use to fight all by herself as she is doing now?
Did she waver and hesitate when she found herself at a disadvantage?
She knows the answer, and she also knows very well that she is not Nearl.
When her techniques, weapons, and armor are unable to give her any advantages, the only things she has to rely on are the same things that led Nearl to victory.
Conviction and determination.
She starts switching up her attack patterns, even using techniques that she has not yet completely mastered.
She's relying more on her blade than her whislash to attack.
Now, Zofia the Whislash has a clear objective:
She must confuse her opponent.
She must wait for her opponent to become distracted for even a second.
She must snatch his weapon away with her whislash.
And before its threads snap, she must strike her opponent down!

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Doctor, anything I can help with?

Ahhh... A hot shower every day is a blessing... After I got infected and had to move all over the place, it was hard for me to take a hot shower. Besides, the food here is decent. Oh, I just love Rhodes Island!

'April'? 'April' is a song about spring. The lyrics describe the feeling of lying on the grass on a warm spring day, looking up at the sky and letting your mind wander. Wanna hear it, Doctor? I'm sure you'll love it.
Strange, where's my lip gloss...? Oh, right. I lent it to Rope. Nah yeah, I was gonna teach her to do makeup. She's a fine looking girl. I bet she'll be even cuter after a little sprucing up.

Back in Rim Billiton, the companies promise a pension for the Infected, but you only get scraps in the end. And it's hard to find a job... Good thing I decided to try Rhodes Island as soon as I saw the ad. I feel appreciated around here.

After I got infected, people started asking me things like 'what's an Infected wearing such bright colors for' and 'what's an Infected listening to music for'... And my answer's always the same: 'It's what I like.'

Back in Rim Billiton, I was a professional hunter. I had to keep the beasts away from the city and sometimes escort company people. But… after I got Oripathy, I lost my job and had to hunt on my own for a living. It was real rough…

My parents died in a mining accident when I was little, and I grew up on a company pension, so I was always real grateful to the company. I figured getting Oripathy was my own dumb fault... But there's more to it than that, isn't there, Doctor?

Doing something for the Infected... I never thought about it before. I mean, it's hard enough to keep yourself alive. But after coming to Rhodes Island, I decided I wanted to try to do something not just for myself, but for everyone who suffers like me.
Doctor, if you wanna nap, I can lend you my earplugs.
Gosh, Rhodes Island has great pay and benefits… Oh, sorry, Doctor, I'm just a little shocked. My codename is April. Nah yeah, it's the name of my favorite song.
Wow, the professionals here are really something.
Wha? A raise...? Oh, it's not that I'm disappointed, I'm stoked! It's just been a long, long time since anyone told me I was doing a good job.

Back in Rim Billiton, I liked to sit on the roof and listen to my music while I watched the whole city go by. Now, I can see even more from the bridge of Rhodes Island. I'd call that a silver lining after getting infected, Doctor.
All righty!
Follow close now, everyone!
Here we go!
Earphones on, let's get started!
My bow is ready!
Who's the target?
Nice visibility.
Leave it to me.
Let's put on some Billy Bounce.
Now this is a good rhythm!
I've got a lock on you.
This one won't miss!
Such a tough battle! Doctor, need some slow music to calm your nerves?
Didn't miss a single one.
Doctor, a few got away, should we chase them?
Doctor, go, I'll cover you!
No matter how much I wander around Rhodes Island, it still feels so big.
Huh?
Hmm, the Doctor should be in the office right now...
Arknights.

Around this time of the year, I was usually in the wilderness all by myself, trying to get warm by the campfire, watching the fireworks in the cities far away. handbook.profile:
A hunter from Rim Billiton, lost her job due to Oripathy before making her way to Rhodes Island. 
Has never received formal training. All indicators read average. Her previous occupation suggested an affinity for sniper training, and she currently serves as a Sniper Operator.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Originium crystals distributed across surface of body, confirmed Infected by medical examination.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests have shown the outlines of her internal organs to be indistinct due to abnormal shadows. Originium granules have been detected in her circulatory system, confirming her to be infected with Oripathy.

 [Cell-Originium Assimilation] 5%
Some mild crystallization visible on her back. 

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.17u/L
The Operator reports she avoided dangerous environments with significant Originium exposure risk, but living in such poor conditions for so long ultimately caused her infection to worsen.
archives:
She has a real urban feel to her, always going around with her stereo playing.
Very extroverted, she gets along with everyone. 
She is always looking to improve her lot in life, and follows trends closely. She is often seen chatting with Utage and Orchid.

Because of the highly developed mining industry in Rim Billiton, the population is more likely to be exposed to Originium than in other countries. So most Rim Billiton companies have some kind of benefits structure for employees who get infected on the job to encourage them to work without fear. 
But April's experience shows that not every company does provide such benefits. Or maybe because of a general revulsion for Infected people, the lower level functionaries of these companies may not have an interest in caring for them, no matter what policies the upper management may put in place to keep people working.
Whether April was forced out of Rim Billiton because her benefits weren't worth the paper they were printed on, or because a bad actor worked against her, we can't know. And it's clear she hasn't investigated it herself. Of course, it doesn't really matter, in the end. Even if it is the latter, it wouldn't be easy for April to go recover what is owed her, considering the situation of the Infected.

If Rhodes Island held an interior decorating competition (we won't), then April would likely take the prize. 
Rhodes Island dormitories have a very plain design, serving only to provide occupants with a basic standard of living. Most operators have no further interest in design. But the company does not have any regulations against operators making interior modifications, as long as they don't damage the landship. In fact, Rhodes Island encourages them to do just that, in hopes of improving their lives. So while most operators live in very plain surroundings, there are some with a lot of character, and April's are among the best. 
Her room is exquisitely decorated. Posters, knick knacks, flower pots, and such all give the place a lively atmosphere, well-suited to her personality. We're very glad to see her adapting to and even loving life at Rhodes Island.

There is a common misconception that once someone becomes Infected, they will then speak for the Infected, and always side with the Infected. 
The truth is obviously different. Sudden changes are always difficult to accept. One who does try to accept such changes should be commended for her open-mindedness. But we shouldn't condemn someone for failing to accept the drastic, sudden change that is Oripathy infection.
Not everyone would openly accept her identity as an Infected person, and every new Rhodes Island operator will receive psychological counseling about that identity to avoid excessive burdens and conflicts over the course of her work. 
This is of particular concern for operators who come from civilian backgrounds like April, for whom discrimination against the Infected is deeply rooted. We must acknowledge the reality that some people, completely without malice, grow up in an environment that teaches them to dehumanize the Infected. And that these people, even if they become Infected themselves, do not see the Infected as peers. It is difficult to reverse that perception. 
Luckily, April's cheerful disposition and open-minded personality did her well. While she had some ingrained discrimination against the Infected and some resultant self-loathing, she quickly shed these ideas thanks to our counseling and the general environment of life in Rhodes Island. She immediately began to think about how she could help others who also suffered like her. While she may not be that impressive in combat, April's outlook and thinking are worthy of emulation.

modules.moduleDescription: April climbs onto the roof. The school is deserted at night, seeming to acquiesce to her intrusion. The vast streets can be seen from the roof of this building, as well as the spotlights shone skyward from the gym several blocks out. Unlike Rim Billiton, there's no stench of slag on the evening breeze, nor the dust Rhodes Island so often faces in storms while sailing the wilds. It's clean, and strange for it. Her field mission concluded two hours ago. She made sure to put on her favorite band's bracelet as she set out from the Rhodes office. Had a whole disguise on and everything. Still got stopped outside the venue. 'Our tickets aren't for sale to the Infected. We need to ensure the safety of our other concertgoers,' the worker said, while taking a cautious step back. 'Sorry.' Yeah, figures I'd get caught, she ruefully thinks, stood below the looming white gymnasium walls. Infected have their own neighborhoods, their own perimeter walls, and their own checkpoints. Rhodes Island spent a week of classes teaching her that Oripathy wasn't something you could transmit just by brushing past someone else, but it's not like she can teach the whole city that. Oh well. She's on the roof, right here, right now. She takes off her headphones. Rhythmic cheers and shrieks pour out of the circular venue, indistinct by the time they reach her ears. They're a lot like the calls she used to hear from the mines. In this moment, they echo the beat of her heart. She reaches a hand out towards the spotlights in the sky, almost able to feel the air shaking. Even though that concert venue all bedazzled with lights feels as far away as the moon. In that sea of noise, an extremely familiar intro faintly reaches her, every note mixed in with the city's clamor. She needs to be careful. She can't get spotted. But she still waves her braceleted hand in time with the music, lightly singing as she does. So lucky I got to apply for this field mission, seriously, she thinks.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Can I read any of the books here? I can read all of them?  Oh, thank you! I'll be careful! I won't mess them up!
Ah, sorry, please don't go touching my book. It might bite your hand if you do. No, really, I'm not joking, I'm serious. Look! I even have to tie it shut like this.
Doctor, do you know where the library is? I asked someone just now, but they were talking too fast. It was hard to understand.
Skyfire, um, Skyfire, wait for me! Uwwhh, please don't walk so fast... I promise I won't run off halfway this time, I promise!

I like reading, but I like hanging out with everyone too! It makes me so happy when I can be with the people I like. Also, don't be fooled. I'm really good at sporty stuff! Especially climbing trees. I can climb super high!

I got some new inspiration after talking to Miss Eyjafjalla today! She's very well-researched on environmental geology. Thank goodness my group's research wasn't stopped because of my accident. Heheh! If I get results this time, I can reapply to the Institution to resume my studies.

Skyfire is an alumna from my university. She graduated soon after I entered since she skipped a year, but even still, she did look after me... Oh, speaking of! She's also the one who introduced me to Rhodes Island! It's thanks to her I'm receiving treatment here.
Um, I suppose I've been following you around, haven't I? I mean, I feel really at ease when I'm around you, so I just unconsciously... A-Am I annoying you, Doctor? Do you want me to go away?

Doctor, this is for you. I found it on the way back, and so many more pretty-looking stones just like it! But, well... that was before I realized I'd gotten separated from the others. Mm? The ore chunk on your desk from before? I put that there too, yes. Did you like it, Doctor?
Nnh... mmmmnnh... there! Ah, Doctor! Sorry! Did I wake you up? There was a bug on your head, so I just, um—did it hurt? I can shush it better!
Thank you for helping me move all these books! Just leave them here, please. Oh, my codename is Mint. What's yours? Doctor? Wait, so you're the Doctor? Skyfire was telling me about you!
Wow... incredible! Everyone's so incredible!
Are there any rewards for promotion? Can I borrow even more books than before?
Doctor, come sit down here. How is it? The sun feels really nice, right? Eheheh. This is my secret base. I love it here more than anywhere. Don't tell anyone else about it, okay?
Got it. Are you coming with us, Doctor?
Wait! You want me as the leader?
We're off.
Are those our enemies, then?
Mmmm… Whuh? What? Yes, I'm listening!
Yep! Leave it to me.
One, two—whoopsie-daisy.
Please don't get in our way!
Take that!
Please calm down a little!
I've got you now.
Would you like to see some of my magic?
Everything went just like you said it would, Doctor! Amazing...!
Phew... it's over. We can finally head back now.
It doesn't look like any more are coming for us... This is fine for now, right?
We can't, it's too dangerous... Doctor, you need to get away!
Um, to tell the truth, I'd be alright sleeping in the library too.
Yah!
Ah! Doctor, would you like to read with me? It's really comfortable sitting here.
Arknights.

Hm... I'm starting to miss my mum and dad. Skyfire has been away from home for so long. Maybe I should ask her how she manages... Oh, Doctor. Will a Messenger visit Rhodes Island today? I have a letter I'd like to post.
So this is where you were, Doctor! Found you.

Doctor, here's a book as a present. Happy birthday! Look, I illustrated the cover myself. I'm always gathering minerals, and these ones have been recent favorites of mine. I looked for paints with lusters as close as I could get! And I have the actual rocks to give you too, of course. What do you think, Doctor? Go on, it's all for you.

I wish I could participate in more research projects. My instructor and teammates always take such good care of me. They're worried my illness could get worse if I push myself too hard, so they don't let me join them on the surveys... I must get better at Rhodes Island so I can go back and focus on my research.

JP.voiceText: Can I read any of the books here? I can read all of them?  Oh, thank you! I'll be careful! I won't mess them up!
Ah, sorry, please don't go touching my book. It might bite your hand if you do. No, really, I'm not joking, I'm serious. Look! I even have to tie it shut like this.
Doctor, do you know where the library is? I asked someone just now, but they were talking too fast. It was hard to understand.
Skyfire, um, Skyfire, wait for me! Uwwhh, please don't walk so fast... I promise I won't run off halfway this time, I promise!

I like reading, but I like hanging out with everyone too! It makes me so happy when I can be with the people I like. Also, don't be fooled. I'm really good at sporty stuff! Especially climbing trees. I can climb super high!

I got some new inspiration after talking to Miss Eyjafjalla today! She's very well-researched on environmental geology. Thank goodness my group's research wasn't stopped because of my accident. Heheh! If I get results this time, I can reapply to the Institution to resume my studies.

Skyfire is an alumna from my university. She graduated soon after I entered since she skipped a year, but even still, she did look after me... Oh, speaking of! She's also the one who introduced me to Rhodes Island! It's thanks to her I'm receiving treatment here.
Um, I suppose I've been following you around, haven't I? I mean, I feel really at ease when I'm around you, so I just unconsciously... A-Am I annoying you, Doctor? Do you want me to go away?

Doctor, this is for you. I found it on the way back, and so many more pretty-looking stones just like it! But, well... that was before I realized I'd gotten separated from the others. Mm? The ore chunk on your desk from before? I put that there too, yes. Did you like it, Doctor?
Nnh... mmmmnnh... there! Ah, Doctor! Sorry! Did I wake you up? There was a bug on your head, so I just, um—did it hurt? I can shush it better!
Thank you for helping me move all these books! Just leave them here, please. Oh, my codename is Mint. What's yours? Doctor? Wait, so you're the Doctor? Skyfire was telling me about you!
Wow... incredible! Everyone's so incredible!
Are there any rewards for promotion? Can I borrow even more books than before?
Doctor, come sit down here. How is it? The sun feels really nice, right? Eheheh. This is my secret base. I love it here more than anywhere. Don't tell anyone else about it, okay?
Got it. Are you coming with us, Doctor?
Wait! You want me as the leader?
We're off.
Are those our enemies, then?
Mmmm… Whuh? What? Yes, I'm listening!
Yep! Leave it to me.
One, two—whoopsie-daisy.
Please don't get in our way!
Take that!
Please calm down a little!
I've got you now.
Would you like to see some of my magic?
Everything went just like you said it would, Doctor! Amazing...!
Phew... it's over. We can finally head back now.
It doesn't look like any more are coming for us... This is fine for now, right?
We can't, it's too dangerous... Doctor, you need to get away!
Um, to tell the truth, I'd be alright sleeping in the library too.
Yah!
Ah! Doctor, would you like to read with me? It's really comfortable sitting here.
Arknights.

Hm... I'm starting to miss my mum and dad. Skyfire has been away from home for so long. Maybe I should ask her how she manages... Oh, Doctor. Will a Messenger visit Rhodes Island today? I have a letter I'd like to post.
So this is where you were, Doctor! Found you.

Doctor, here's a book as a present. Happy birthday! Look, I illustrated the cover myself. I'm always gathering minerals, and these ones have been recent favorites of mine. I looked for paints with lusters as close as I could get! And I have the actual rocks to give you too, of course. What do you think, Doctor? Go on, it's all for you.

I wish I could participate in more research projects. My instructor and teammates always take such good care of me. They're worried my illness could get worse if I push myself too hard, so they don't let me join them on the surveys... I must get better at Rhodes Island so I can go back and focus on my research.

handbook.profile:
Mint is a Caster affiliated with the Victorian Institution for Higher Studies, specializing in geology, frequently participating in investigative field projects. She contracted Oripathy on an expedition and was referred by Operator Skyfire to Rhodes Island for consultation. 
She currently receives treatment at Rhodes Island while assisting with Originium research, environmental and geological observation, and related services.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Originium crystals distributed across surface of body, confirmed Infected by medical examination.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests have shown the outlines of her internal organs to be indistinct due to abnormal shadows. Originium granules have been detected in her circulatory system, confirming her to be infected with Oripathy. 

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 4%
Small traces of infection visible on surface of body. Severity of condition is mild and notably stable. 

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.17u/L
Operator Mint often works deep within danger zones. Despite strict safety measures, risk of aggravation remains present. We recommend she receives regular checkups.
handbook.promotionRecord:
Mint likes hiding in her secret bases and reading in silence, and she likes fooling around together with her friends. She likes to climb trees. She likes adventures. She likes every last new and novel thing. 
She might tiptoe as she follows behind her friends, and she might suddenly get distracted by something and go bounding off instead. 
Should you ever receive a small present from her, be it as little as a misshapen piece of ore with mud still stuck to it, take it. Accept it. Without a doubt, it's something she's fond of, and regardless of how, she'd like for you to share in it too.
archives:
With her backgroundin the Victorian Institution for Higher Studies, and being introduced to Rhodes Island by Operator Skyfire, many Operators who had not yet met Mint could not help but have certain preconceptions about her. 
Regardless, once they met the new Victorian for themselves, they quickly realized she was not an elite in the vein of Operator Skyfire. This isn't to say Operator Mint isn't outstanding; rather, she and Skyfire are two completely separate sorts. She looks quiet and proper at first glance, but in truth she bursts with a curious spirit and a lively step. Compared to her senior Skyfire, a cream-of-the-crop Caster who gained her qualifications from school and promptly graduated, Mint values her research in geological fields much more. 
It's no surprise that when the time came to decide where she wanted to go, Mint chose to stick around and further her studies, continuing her pursuit of cutting-edge geological research. It was on such a pivotal field investigation that she came to contract Oripathy.

The new Feline girl has a book that'll bite you. 
Once Mint came to Rhodes Island, the rumor swiftly followed, spreading like wildfire amongst the younger Operators. 
Mint does indeed hold an Arts unit, one fashioned into the form of a book, that together with her staff helps her to make full, free use of her Originium Arts. Mint usually has the 'book' bound with a specially made tie, so as not to cause any accidents. It's as the rumors say—the book will bite people. If someone randomly flips its pages, they'll very likely set off its built-in retaliative mechanisms. It won't cause any life-threatening harm, but according to Mint, 'Its bites hurt so much. It's even worse than stubbing your little toe.' 
Mint says she happened upon the book at an old marketplace near school, where all the shops sold old books and worn knick-knacks that had probably traded hands countless times, and where no shortage of questionably-legal goods moved around under wraps. 
'Don't go in there expecting anything. People who treat it as one great treasure hunt by and large end up buying complete useless rubbish, ' stated Operator Skyfire on this topic. 'If you honest-to-God know how to find something nice, you'll find it. If you can't see a thing's true worth, tough. That's the only way. '

Operator Mint's sense of curiosity is extremely strong. 
Most Institution scholars have passion to embrace as they seek the verities of their matters, and Mint is no exception. Though most of the time she comes off simply as polite and sweet, Mint's natural-born curiosity and hunger for knowledge is impossible to hide, and it didn't take long to show once she arrived at Rhodes Island. 
She spent the first couple of days 'exploring' most areas of the ship provided to Operators, before selecting a few lesser trodden places to act as her own secret bases. She's taken to life at Rhodes Island very quickly. 
However, her wildly scattering curiosity has definitely invited trouble at times. 
One thing that worries people is while doing something, Mint is distractable. Of course, this isn't to say she has no sense of priority. When a directly pressing matter is at hand, Mint focuses and spares no detail until it's done, but the moment the most critical part is finished, she loosens up, and it's then that something else can easily steal her attention. 
For example, after a mission, she might be lured away by some novel ore or Originium-infected creature, and will wander off from her team without realizing it until she's lost in the dead of the wilderness... That has happened more than once. 
And if this continues without any mediation or regulation, we fear that Operator Skyfire, who already loses her temper whenever it happens, will sooner or later burn the ship out from the inside.

Mint doesn't seem to be too bothered by her own Oripathy. 
Her infection was completely unforeseen. At the time, a group of scholars had made due preparations and entered a deep fault left by a Catastrophe. Exploration there went without a hitch—only as they withdrew, the ground beneath Mint's footing subsided, and the rest is history. 
Mint herself cares less about her illness, a lost cause as it is, and much more about if she's obtained some good samples for experimentation, or whether she's onto any breakthrough discoveries. Those are what really matter to her. 
After all, geological research has always been part and parcel of all sorts of dangerous environments. No matter the stringent safety measures, no one can guarantee an accident will never occur. Mint and all the researchers with her were all aware of this. It was with a fundamental understanding of the risk that they made their choices. 
Operator Mint has never once been regretful.

modules.moduleDescription:
The forty-second time Mint wanders off is the time she resolves, as other operators keep telling her, to train herself to stay focused.
After picking up more than a few items from the flea market, her training commences.
-METRONOME. The shop says Leithanians use this little tool when beginning to learn music, in order to help them grasp tempo. But conversely, '100 Ways to Up Your Concentration' says having a regular sound playing helps focus your attention, as people will map out the thoughts in their head to the rhythm, thus untangling their logic. 'Tick, tock, tick, tock, tick, tock, pebbles, twigs, outside, everywhere, pretty, favorite, I want to look, I'll look right now...'
-SOUND BATH. 'Bathed in pure, long, and gentle tones, you will come to find serenity, and concentrate upon the self.' '*ding*—' It... sounds like Pramanix's bell, it's so reassuring... I wonder if this was from Kjerag too? I remember there was a holy mountain there, since Cliffheart's told me heaps about the place. I'd like to visit too one day, sooner or later—I'm sure there'd be so much geological knowledge to pick up on! The Black Flow's on the bucket list too. Maybe I should consult Asbestos about it beforehand? That door she has looks so hefty...
-ATTENTION SPAN TRAINING CARDS. This one's a present from Skyfire after she heard I was starting attention training. 'Suitable for children ages 3-5. WARNING: CHOKING HAZARD.' Why did she buy me this?
-BANDAGES FOR WHEN A BOOK BITES. These aren't to do with attention training, I simply saw them on the table just now and put them in here with everything else, hehe.
-PEBBLE. Saga told me that to concentrate on but one thing before thee, one item, be it even the most mundane and unremarkable stone, would settle thee down, and see that thou wouldst ponder the primitive and true. She led me through some meditation, to focus my attention, but eventually... the natto gohan was just too tasty to resist.
Then comes the forty-third time she's wandered off. Her attention training is declared a failure, and consequently her journaling ends there. The final item noted is a fire extinguisher.
-FIRE EXTINGUISHER. I put out the flames that started from Skyfire flaring up. I think... I think it's better than any other tool at addressing the most frightening consequences of being unfocused...
Ohh... but still, I have to make a proper apology...

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: File management? Alright, then. Teach me how. Okay... Sort them first. Like this? Then put them in order, by date… Uh. I tore the paper… S-Sorry. I didn't mean to.

Some of the people here. Don't you think they're a little too tall? No, I don't care. Not actually. How tall you are and how strong you are don't relate. I just need to bring every last one of them down.
What's my tribe gonna do now that I'm gone? That's a dumb question. See who has the bigger fists. The biggest is the new leader. Then they're done. That's it.

I heard a lot about Gavial. Like how she can crush a rock with her abs, and tear a raging beast apart with one hand. Is she actually that strong? Stronger than Chief Blaze? Warfarin said if I get treatment from Gavial, I'll know firsthand how strong she is. It's worth a try... Hm? Doctor, why are you stopping me?
I came here to get stronger, and that hasn't changed. Not just Chief Blaze and Gavial, there's a lot of people here worth challenging... What? I look happy? You're right. I sort of like being here.

The Rhodes Islanders. They all think too much. You too, Doctor. You have to think about so many things every day. You must be tired. You're not? You have to do it? Hmm, I guess that's true. handbook.profile:
Flint, Sargon tribal warrior, began building her combat experience from the moment she was first able to put up her fists. She has mastered a martial arts style based on swift and precise punches. 
She is currently here on the recommendation of a certain elite operator whose identity has been withheld, and became a Rhodes Island Guard Operator after passing the examination.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected. 

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Flint shows no signs of Originium infection. 

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.05u/L
Operator Flint rarely comes into contact with Originium. She might not even know what Originium is in the first place. 

What am I supposed to be looking for? She's the picture of health! 
—Gavial
handbook.promotionRecord:
To Flint, most people think too much and wind themselves up too tight. Especially the people of Rhodes Island, some of them propping themselves up while they keep working. They make so little sense to her. 
'If you're tired, go take a break!'
So she says. And when she says it, warrior that she is, she's usually already prepared to safeguard you from any danger as you rest.

Only, you worry how the warrior of the rainforest hasn't yet fully grasped just how vast, and broad, this world is. She still needs more time to understand this. Just how much in this world can be solved with her fists alone, and just how many things we're powerless to do anything about.
archives:
The one Blaze brought back with her went and picked another fight with an Operator in the training center today. 
To preface, Rhodes Island has built up a healthy collection of operators, each different in their own ways, with no shortage of misfits among them. There have been plenty of times where a single flippant comment made someone throw down right in the corridor. Sorting out all those scuffles is a pain, but the fact that they happen in the first place doesn't really surprise anyone. Operator Flint's case, however, is somewhat distinct from this. 
We've had a lot of operators who've 'compared notes' on physical combat with Flint testify that actually, the fights that unfolded between them were with both sides' mutual discretion and consent. No bad blood at play, no clash that sparked a conflict. In most situations, this short girl stares straight at her target, walks over to them, opens her mouth, and lets loose some strange syllabic utterances. The two then recognize something implicit in the other's gaze, and then put up their dukes. 
'I didn't understand what she was saying. But there was no wickedness in her eyes.' -The words of Operator Broca.

Prior to arriving at Rhodes Island, Operator Flint was completely unable to speak several common languages. According to Flint, the common tongues were much like the native languages that evolved freely in the unregulated lands of Sargon, making it almost impossible for her to keep track of. Thus, following her arrival at Rhodes Island, studying common languages has become an important part of her schedule in order to facilitate smooth communication in day-to-day life. 
The common languages are not particularly difficult to learn, and a persuasive word from Gavial to Flint about taking daily language courses proved to be key. 
'What, don't you wanna be able to chat up Blaze?'
That was all it took. It worked better than anything anyone else had to say, and Flint began to study seriously. 

[Voice Log]
'So what do we do until she learns? There's nobody else around who can make sense of her native dialect. Do we just wave our hands at her?' 
'Oh. Don't you worry about that.'
'What's not to worry about?! Missions! What do we do about missions? Okay, do we use body language to give her orders in the middle of the battlefield, too?'
'Relax, relax. All accounted for when they put the squad together, don't you worry. See, the Doctor's already kinda sorta picked up a little bit of that weird Sargon blah-blah whatever it is!'

Operator Flint is a Liberi who was raised in the rainforest. The tribe of Liberi she comes from is naturally of small stature, and it's apparent that their physical fitness compared to other Liberi falls slightly short. One need not even start comparing them to the wealth of combative, healthily robust races surrounding them. This is why Flint's tribe has always had a relatively tough time living in the rainforest. These challenges persisted up until Flint reached the age where she could run and jump, at which point she promptly picked and won a fight with two Archosauria who substantially outclassed her. She beat them on their own ground. 
Flint's fists are fast and tricky. Where she falls short in terms of naturally endowed strength, her race's superiority in speed makes up handily for the deficiency. Her fighting style differs from any boxer with a grounding in theory. She wields her fists to knock her opponent down, pure and simple, and they carry an almost illusory sense of the freedom and danger of the rainforest. 
As the tallest and strongest warrior in her tribe, Flint was always quite confident of her own build, even proud of it, until she came into contact with other, much taller peoples. Once she came to the realization that most of the entire outside world's population was of much greater stature than her, Flint was quick to give up her arrogance born of ignorance, and she began seeking out new challenges. She went to find those stronger than herself, challenge them, harden and mold herself, improve herself, until she could beat them. 
Do not underestimate her for her size. No Sargon warrior ever feared a challenge. 

[Addendum by file author]
I will refrain from putting her relationship with the taller operators into words. On the other hand, she gets along with our operators of Durin origin. No question about that.

One might expect that in their reverence for might and strength, the Tiacauh would be impulsive and unruly. But we must admit their conduct is full of great fervor, candor and a masterful valor. Operator Flint is an archetypal example of this. 
As Flint sees it, there is nothing that can't be settled with her fists some way or another. Back in Flint's old stomping grounds, you'd often catch a glimpse of Tiacauh people who'd been wrestling with each other just a moment ago, who'd stood themselves up straight, shook hands and made peace with each other the very next second. After that handshake, they might wrap their arms around each other's shoulders and go off to eat together. Though, generally, they'll get into another fight because of something else altogether before they can sit down. 
In addition, the Liberi people to which Flint belongs have a love for flowers that far exceeds the norm. Their preference is especially for lushly colored specimens, which can be often found adorning their homes. Operator Flint holds the fundamental notion that flowers are something found everywhere, and freely pickable as one wishes. Even now, living in Rhodes Island's colossus of rebar and iron sheeting, she continues to think so. 
As Miss Perfumer's greenhouse steadily drew in the horticulture enthusiasts one after another, a great mystery reared its head. Flowers would often be picked without warning. As the days went on, the gardeners whose plants went missing ultimately formed an alliance, agreeing once and for all to teach the delinquent flower-picker a lesson they'd never forget. 
Before they set out a real action plan, Operator Flamebringer's meticulously cultivated bonsai was burgled overnight—a crucial breakthrough. The concerned parties fought each other bitterly that next day, and finally, under the oppressive gaze of Dr. Gavial, they reluctantly shook hands and made their own peace. 

At least Operator Flint now understands. Unlike the rainforest, abundant with vegetation, she should refrain from picking the flowers she finds growing within Rhodes Island. The greenhouse's keeper has allowed Flint the use of a small flowerbed. You can find the Tiacauh stooping next to it from time to time, her hands, so often closed in fists, carefully pulling the weeds, looking forward to seeing the flowers bloom.

modules.moduleDescription:
Soon to return to Acahualla, Kemar takes her flashcards with her. The handwriting's kind of immature, and she doesn't need them to remember what the words mean now, but still she hooks them on her belt, the well-worn eyelet fraying day by day.
'These ones, I brought from home. The rest, I picked on the outside,' replied Kemar once upon a time, when a Rhodes operator was curious about the flowers on her cards. At first, they were how the girl of the rainforest learned her way through other languages—they fascinated her since she was young. Tender little plants. As enrapturing as a flying fist, and they called to her the way the wild things did.
On a certain level, these flowers held more strength than any brave warrior. Their names and stories were some of the earliest things Kemar knew by heart: learning how the people beyond the rainforest colored the four seasons with them, interpreted their lives with them. What describes these flowers now are no longer unfamiliar words, but a ring of keys, hung on her waist, opening each of Terra's doors alongside her.
'Look well, it's our tribe's tallest, mightiest warrior! Her footprints are left in places even our imaginations couldn't reach! And now, she's back!' Kemar parts the grass weave over the doorway, and is met head on with the eager chatter of her tribesfolk, in her native language. Eventually, she stirs; in this most familiar of rainforests, she'll never be needing any 'key'.
The tribe's kiddies mill around Kemar, jabbing zealously at all the names on her flashcards' flowers, pestering her to tell all her stories from beyond the forest.
'Beyond the rainforest... it's very wide.'
Kemar recalls the most exciting moment of her own language-learning. Not the first time she understood a spoken word. Not being able to fluently converse with Big Boss Blaze. It was when she realized she could finally explain to others, coherently and clearly, the things that all the flowers of her home represented.
'...But don't let me tell you about it. You should all go see it for yourself!
'And then face off with the people outside, and tell them... let them know how mighty we are.' Kemar flips back to the very first flashcard, pressed with a flower of the rainforest. Its power to live is unwavering, and its power to adapt is unrivalled. Rainforest, prairie, or barrens, it will bloom more avidly, more ardently than all.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Gavial doesn't do this kind of work, and nobody in the tribe wants to do this stuff either. So, that's why I help out a bit when I have the time.
If there's no trainee nurse at the Medical Department, I can give it a try. I have some basic nursing knowledge.
Doctor, this pen seems to be out of ink. Oh, wait! Please don't throw that out! If it's not too much to ask... Um... could I have that?
I can't dig up the floors on Rhodes Island? There's no buried treasure? But where are all your precious things, then? Locked inside rooms? Oh, that's too bad…
My tail's gotten even bigger. If this keeps up, everyone's going to hate me for sure. Wuh... What do I do…?

Some people are born strong and cool, others, smart. For me, I've got a big tail... Since we can't choose what we're born with, let's embrace our uniqueness and make the most of it. Um, of course, if you could help me out every now and then, Doctor... that would be best.

I understand Gavial skipping work, but why would she skip a meal? Could something be bothering her so much that even she has to hide? And no one else even noticed. I'm the only one who can save her! Ah, Doctor, good thing you're here. Can you help me with something?

Are you sure you want to see what's inside my backpack? Okay... I haven't organized it in a while so it might be kind of messy. Let's see… An amber wrapped in a leaf. A loose fang...? A bloodstained black crystal... and a stack of autographs?! Uh, Doctor, that's all for today! Sorry, but we're done here!

She shines with such brilliance that I can't help but stare, even as her flames scorch my eyes dry. That's my Gavial, she shines like the sun. Oh, by the way, I came across that passage in a book and thought it sounded nice, so I memorized it. It really fits Gavial, doesn't it?
I'll leave this dreamcatcher over here… May you have a pure and peaceful dream, Doctor.
Hello, Doctor. Er, I'm not here to cause trouble. I'm here to… to... Study! Right, study. No reason for me to stay home alone if Gavial is here, right?
Hmm... Maybe I should just practice on the battlefield, I guess…
Thank you for giving me such a pretty badge, Doctor. What? It's a promotion badge? Ah, uh, y-you sure...? A-A-Am I really qualified to have this?
I'll be worthy of this flag one day, I swear I will.
I'll watch and learn, Doctor. It would be great if I could actually master some of your skills…
You're leaving it to me? Really?
Let's go. We are gonna F… um… beat them up!
Wait, I'm not ready yet!
Please not me, please not me…
Maybe I'll have a go…
H-Here I go!
Who needs beating? Come over!
C-Come on, you can do this!
A little more, a little more!
Haah!
Wh-Who's next!
I got beaten like that before, by you, Doctor.
We won, yay.
Phew, my back's sore. I need a break.
I'm sorry... so sorry…
Ah! Please don't throw that away yet. Can you leave it to me? I'll take care of it.
M-My tail...
Want to try Sargonian barbecue? I'll work the grill, you just enjoy the food, Doctor.
Arknights.
If today's a holiday, does that mean I can take the day off? Haghhh… Oh, where's Gavial? Have you seen her, Doctor? If I've got a free day, of course I'm going to spend it with Gavial!
Hnngh... Doctor…

Doctor! I brought you a birthday present! Umm... huh? Wh-Where did it go? I hid it behind my back so I could surprise you. How could it go missing...? Wahh… Oh! Here it is! It was stuck under my tail... Sorry about that, and happy birthday to you, Doctor. Hehe.

Doctor, I got a paper slip from the fortune box, and it says if I say five positive words to a plant every day, it will grow even bigger. Let me try it with this one! Tail, backpack, barbecue, sweet dreams... And... Gavial. Hehe... Doctor! Why are you laughing at me?

handbook.profile:
Tomimi, an Archosauria from the Acahualla region of Sargon, is a friend and supporter to Gavial. She tried all sorts of radical ways to prevent Gavial from returning to Rhodes Island, but upon her failure, instead accompanied Gavial back to Rhodes Island.
She assumes the responsibilities of a Caster but often forgets that she is a Caster. Nevertheless, given her excellent performance on the battlefield, there are no plans to have her switch operator roles.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected. 

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
'This one's the exact same as before, pure and unblemished.' 

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.14u/L
'Is she actually listening to me when I say she needs to exercise? Not bad.' 

'I pretty much already know everything about Tomimi—— Though this would be the first time I gave her a physical exam.' ——Gavial
'The physical exam went smoothly, but her heartbeat was abnormally fast and that confounded the data.' ——Gavial
handbook.promotionRecord:
A (partial) list of items in the backpack Tomimi made for herself:

A piece of amber wrapped in leaves.
'A neat thing I found on my first expedition. Holding it right now makes me happy.' 

A fired clay wad, slightly deformed 
'The first time Gavial and I tried to make pottery. She squeezed it a bit too hard and it got a bit deformed.' 

A fang that fell out when I was growing
'Mama always said this was my lucky tooth, so I've always kept it in my bag.' 

The woven bag I kept my collectibles in when I was younger
'It's really sturdy and can still last a really long time!' 

Gavial's signature, cut out from various places (erasure marks visible)
'...I want more.' 

Doctor's badge
'Doctor gave this to me. I can become smarter if I keep it with me.' 

A stack of dreamcatchers
'To give to people who can't sleep well.' 

'Praise the Sun'
'A really interesting book. I'll read a bit more tonight.' 

Adventure package
'Has all sorts of neat stuff inside it, very useful for when adventuring.' 

Field medic kit
'Still learning how to use it. After that, I'll be able to help Gavial whenever she needs it.'
