CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Structural design, industrial R&D, scientific research. You name it, and I can do it, Doctor.

The Engineering Department never approve my proposals. Do they have any bias toward me? What should I do... Oh! Actually, Doctor, would you please submit this suggestion on improvement for me? It's a deal then!
There are many workshops like mine in Rhine Lab, but what takes others six weeks to finish, I can have it done in one. I'm not boasting!
DO NOT interrupt me when I'm doing my research, or I'll have my Meeboos bite you! And I will bite you too!
At night I'm always full of inspiration... and the… urgency to sleep! No, I can't bear it... Where's the pillow... I need to rest...

Hm? Why are these cuties called Meeboos? That's because they go 'meeee-boooo' when they boot up. So I named them after that. Fitting, don't you think? Just listen and you'll get it. You press this switch to... NONONONO, That's the self-destruct button! Ahhhhhh run！
That girl who just passed by... that was Silence, right? If only back then... Oh, sorry, the non-disclosure agreement is still in effect. I should keep my mouth shut.
I feel kinda empty when I've got nothing to do... I guess that's just how engineers are. I bet even you have to idle your time away on occasion, Doctor. Huh? You don't?

Doctor, may I request... No! Not 10 square meters! I asked for too much last time, so this time... all I need is 3! W-Wait! Don't leave yet! 1 square meter, just 1 more for my research will do! Please, Doctor, I'm begging you...
Geez... where's the coffeemaker... Oh, there it is... You want some too, Doctor?
Lutra Workshop of Rhine Lab, at your service. Yup, I run the workshop on my own. No assistance needed. Amazing, right?
This structure... Interesting. I'll look into it.
This raise came just in time! I can afford to upgrade my equipment now.
I promised that you'd not be disappointed. Now look what I have! Surely kept my end of the bargain, didn't I?
Time to go, Meeboos!
Commanding both Operators and my Meeboos at the same time is a bit much even for me...
Hopefully we can get some useful experiment data!
Come on, Meeboo, show them what Rhine Lab's technology can do!
Whoa!
Careful! Be gentle with it!
Handle with care!
Precision equipment isn't cheap!
Get 'em, Meeboo #3!
Bite 'em, Meeboo!
If anything breaks, just make another one!
My Meeboos are more than just machines!
Come on, Meeboo! Show everyone your victory dance!
Nice! We practically rolled over them!
The device is slightly damaged. I'll fix it in no time.
Oh no! My Meeboo...! I'll need to make more...
Now I want a new workshop!
Whuah?! Hey, I'm working here!
Doctor, let me touch your head! Inspiration can strike, you know!
Arknights.

Happy New Year, Doctor! I love New Year's, there's always so much to eat when you go out, even if you miss the canteen's dinner time! I wish every day could be like that... Ouch! Alright, fine Meeboo, I'll eat on time, you're hurting me!
Heya, Doctor!
Your birthday present? A literal piece of cake! Here's a cake sample, complete with blueprint, recipe, and a mass-production line ready for full rollout! How's that?

What is research for, Doctor? My former coworkers say I can be surprisingly shallow, but if I were only in it for the money or fame, there are better ways. I just want to help advance technology, even by a little bit. And here, I can do that.

handbook.profile: Mayer was born in Columbia and is a member of Rhine Lab. She is the inventor of the 'Meeboo' wire control system. She is outstandingly capable and runs her own workshop called 'Lutra.' She is currently working with Rhodes Island to provide assistance with construction, planning, and development.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this Operator is believed to be non-infected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0% 
Operator shows no signs of infection at this time.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.12u/L 
Operator has been in long-term contact with Originium and frequently works to process it. However, due to strict adherence to safety protocols, Operator has not yet displayed any signs of Oripathy.
handbook.promotionRecord: So far, a total of 80 Meeboos have been constructed by Mayer. 20 of them are serving in Mayer's squad, while the others have been disassembled for various reasons. All available components have been installed on these models in service and are uniquely named by Mayer on their respective nameplates. Of the 20 Meeboos in service, there remains a single one with an unknown serial number that Mayer uses both as a mobile workbench and an experimental prototype. Despite its advanced functions, it is unarmed and useless for combat.
archives: Mayer frequently encountered Silence at Rhine headquarters since she was responsible for preparing, installing, and commissioning experimental devices for her. This was up until Silence abruptly disappeared which in turn caused this project to be terminated. Mayer often feels a sense of regret when reminded of this instance but had she known the true goal of the project, she would have pulled the plug herself.

Mayer possesses just the right mixture of a scientist's meticulous thinking and an engineer's hands-on mentality. If there's any downside to this, it's that she never has enough time. If you don't believe it, take a look in her personal dictionary. The word 'idle' is missing.

Mayer's head contains a multitude of, shall we say, volatile ideas, which makes it no surprise when she creates something eccentric. Out of her countless inventions, her prized and most cherished 'masterpiece' is 'Meeboo.' Mayer diligently creates nameplates for each individual 'Meeboo' and carefully cleans up its wreckage after it's served its purpose. It is clear that she pours her heart and soul into the maintenance and operation of each Meeboo, despite their mechanical origins.

Since Meeboos take up so much space, Mayer's workshop is extremely cramped, causing her to devise ways to expand it. Despite having a room twice as large as anyone else's, she has managed to run out of space after increasing Meeboo production. Mayer has begged the Doctor to increase her room's size. That request was denied by the logistics department out of fairness towards others. Despite this ban on room expansion, the Doctor nonetheless granted her extra space in the hangar to allow her to continue the production of her Meeboos.

modules.moduleDescription:
Multithreading enhancements—Completed
Meeboos maintenance—Completed
Detonate and Recycle circuitry—Completed
System upgrade—Completed
Undisclosed plan—In early development stages
......
Closure's AI buggies are so amazing.
I want them! I really want them! And I want all my Meeboos be like that!!!
A whole squadron of Meeboos that does what I want by themselves. Heh... hahah.
......
Closure did say that she doesn't have all of the code and computational logic figured out, and that she still has to rely on Rhodes Island's core for part of its upkeep.
It wouldn't feel right to reuse technology that I don't understand, so I will just make my own.
Meeboos' service efficiency has improved quite a bit lately, and their Detonate and Recycle rate has been stable. I'd say the research on it has come pretty far.
Next up—Research on Meeboos' automation logic...
The learning device's been installed on Meeboos No. *unknown number* for a while now, and it's made some progress.
That is, if opening the door for guests counts as progress, haha...
Given what a complex environment the battlefield is, I'm afraid sending it there will affect its operations.
But if I don't take it there, it won't collect any data either...
......
I ended up bringing it with me. I've backed up all the data and logged down all the hardware specifications.
If... Just if... If it ends up getting wrecked and written off, I'll have to come up with some kind of way to squeeze some compensation and a few days off out of the Doctor.
Then I'll have to spend half a year again to build a new one...
Please, let there be some kind of breakthrough! Just a little will do!!
This isn't for the old guys at Engineering or myself.
It's for your own good, Meeboos!
If there comes a day you reach the AIs' level, what should I say to you?
Oh, whatever. We've been friends for so long, I guess both of us know deep in our hearts what we want to say to each other.
Right, Meeboos?
—Excerpts from 'Meeboos Maintenance Diary' by Mayer Stony, Lutra Workshop Member of Rhine Lab Engineering Department

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Umm… Leave it to me. I'm used to observing the traces left behind by other people's work, and experiencing the persistence, joy and excitement therein. I can see the commitment in your to-do list, Doctor.

Are you looking for the source of the music? It's the musical enchantment on this cup. Most music in Leithanian cities are created with Arts. From statues to fountains to murals, virtually anything can become a device for playing music. Would you care for a drink? I recommend this song to pair with anything alcoholic.

Sorry. Criticism of music is best left to listeners and creators. I'm simply a tuner with perfect pitch, and I know my place. They say one only understands the importance of talent once one has worked hard. Well, I know I have no talent, so there's no need for me to work that hard.

I come from a small town where tourism is the main industry. I designed the music of every nook and cranny in the marketplace, so the melody will follow you with every step you take. Oh, there is even a famous blindfolded musical pathfinding competition with a decent prize pool. You should have a go, Doctor. Me? No, I'm one of the judges.

Can you take a look at this proposal? Basically, I'll set Arts to play different background music in different areas, which will improve everyone's experience at leisure and work. I've left this area empty, because I thought you should set your own playlist for sleepless nights.

'Turning the marketplace into a splendid bastion of culture'? That's just the copywriter spinning words around. All I am is a humble tuner. But you can find so many examples of remarkable creativity cast aside in a forgotten corner, unnoticed by others. I do my little part in gathering them up and playing them for children to appreciate.

This group photo…? I… was troubled by my lack of talent at the time. I hung it in my room to remind myself to live without regret. Oh, I didn't explain why I'm not in the photo, did I? Well... I never graduated.

Shh! Can you hear my flowers? I added musical Arts to the flowers sent to Medical, and I'm one piece away from completing the suite. I don't want the patients to suffer any regret, because in their eyes, I'm a healer too. It's not always recovery that makes patients happy, if I am not wrong.

Medical says they want to help me find the reason I can't sing in tune. I know it's not an illness, but the result of being scorned by those who live atop the spires. I don't like the feeling of expectations placed on me. Fortunately, it is possible to tune out the noise, and tuners never have regrets.
Sorry, I didn't mean it. Perhaps the duet was a little too hypnotizing?
Don't worry, I've entrusted my work in Leithanien to my colleagues there. I'm afraid you're mistaken, they're inveterate workaholics, just like me.
It's very complex, like a passionate fugue.
I'm being recognized? Simply for doing my job? Okay. I have quite a few colleagues in Leithanien. I think they will be very interested in joining Rhodes Island. Care to consider it, Doctor?

The journey helped me see clearly and understand it. The wonderful music of the cities comes not from god-given talent, but the concerted effort of tireless tuners. That's what I aspire to be—one whose work is ordinary, unremarkable, but indispensable.
I'll be in tune with you.
Do you need me… to give the cue?
The horn sounds. Now, beat the drums.
It's time to cut the noise.
Here. I'm listening.
Eh? What did you say?
Oh, it's my turn.
I'll give it a try.
Ready, four-four time.
Too low. From the top.
Let the arpeggio cascade.
This is my range.
They gave up before we got to the cadence. Looks like the program doesn't need to be too long.
This is an elegy for them to mourn themselves.
It's not such a bad thing to rush through a passage that's out-of-tune.
Ugh! I need to wash my ears out.
Quiet, like a sheet of paper without notes or staff lines. I'll set it up.
I can hear you, you know.
My horns are not a percussion instrument, Doctor.
Arknights.

The celebration can wait. I'm maintaining the musical order of the festival; those who work behind the scenes only get to enjoy the celebrations after the curtain falls. It's not that I don't like a lively scene; my blessings are with everyone, in each and every note. The tuner does not leave until the music has ended.
Hello, Doctor. Here's a special suite of music for you to play on deck. A little applause would make it even more pleasing.

Happy birthday, Doctor. My gift is imbued with musical Arts, playing back a song cover I performed myself. I'm sure the original is much better and… actually in tune. But I guarantee this song is more memorable than any other.

It used to be hard for me to ignore regret. I tried, only to realize it wasn't really necessary. A rousing melody can stay in the climax, and a settled note is no longer noise, just as everyone on Rhodes Island has found their home.

handbook.profile: Akkord, real name Tonia Klang, is a tuner hailing from a remote Leithanian town. She was referred to Rhodes Island for treatment after contracting Oripathy in a soundfield core overload accident caused by a snowstorm. She currently helps out with Rhodes Island's music scene, while assisting in battle as a caster.
handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 3%
Small traces of infection are visible on the surface of the body.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.22u/L
Akkord contracted Oripathy early, and comes into contact with Originium components regularly in her work, but she observes proper protection and is diligent about receiving treatment. Her condition is currently stable with no sign of infection spreading.
handbook.promotionRecord:
Tonia rarely participated in her class's creative showcases while at school. Her notebooks were filled with strange symbols, arrows, and overlapping waveforms, but rarely complete melodies. Her classmates used instruments or song to create musical Arts, but she preferred a little audio recorder, carrying it through streets, markets, and old workshops, collecting those authentic sounds around her—the knocking of hammer on metal, the low humming of winds gliding past the eaves on a snowy night, or the screeching sound of trains braking as sparks fly. She broke the sounds down into fundamental vibrations, and attempted to recreate their texture and temperature with Arts. To most of her peers and teachers, it was an act of documentation, not creation, a mosaic lacking in soul. Tonia never argued. All she did was put away her device and walk down from the stage after each showcase with her head bowed, through scattered applause and silent skepticism from the crowd.
Years later, Tonia was in the Rhodes Island workshop, testing a piece of audio equipment. She knocked it lightly with a tuning fork, listening to the echoes bounce inside the casing. The monitor next to it flashed; the curved line on the screen fluctuated. In a split second, it looked just like the waves she wrote in her notebook in her youth.
Tonia gazed upon the curved line. Her fingertip stayed on the knob, as though trying to capture a familiar feeling—neither melody nor rhythm, but a position that gave her certainty that the sound belonged to her. The equipment hummed, and she bowed her head again to record the sound in her recorder. Tonia was not sure what she could eventually do with the collected sounds, but was in no hurry to answer the question.
archives:
Operator Akkord has a habit of 'listening' in her daily work and inspections. She explains it as capturing the specific frequencies of the target's soundfield, and adding 'tags' to them in her notes.
The relationship between this behavior and her tuning work is unclear, but maintenance logs across different cities show a pattern: When Akkord notices any changes in the subject's tags, she will instantly check the audio facilities in the subject's block, make necessary adjustments, or perform extra inspections around the area.
The Medical Department is reserving judgment on the uniqueness of her hearing. Assessors believe it is not absolute pitch in the traditional sense of the word, but an identification method based on perception and experience.
It must be noted that Akkord has never publicly discussed the specific relationship between her tags and the tagged subjects, and her notes contain no decipherable information.
On the whole, we do not believe there are significant risks associated with this habit at this time, though continued observation is recommended regarding why and how she uses this ability in special missions.

The town's train station was always noisy at dusk. Miners chatting and laughing as they return from work, children chasing each other over the tracks, and the fires of smelters roaring in the distance. Tonia slowly pushed her old soundfield tuner through the crowd. It was a heavy machine with creaking gears that sounded like they could fall apart at any moment. She was headed towards the broadcasting speakers at the town square, which had become distorted by age and sounded like they had been put through sand and rubble.
The people in town were not particularly hostile to her, nor were they particularly friendly. She was one of those people who don't do 'real work'. To the townsfolk, a little bit of Arts was all that was needed if some facility in town broke down, and they were not entirely wrong. As such, they did not bother to ask Tonia for help most of the time.
'Doesn't seem like her Arts got any better, even after she got infected.'
'I heard her grades were pretty ordinary. Didn't inherit her father's musical talent, I guess.'
'Then what's the point of getting infected—'
'Shh, don't say that...'
Tonia pretended not to hear these comments around town. She simply inserted her tuner's pin into the speakers, and turned the knob to minimize the noise while listening. Slowly but steadily, she tuned the sound of wind, furnaces, and footsteps into the waveform, until the screechiness was gone, and the broadcast sounded nice and smooth again.
Only a few nearby miners seemed to notice that the ambient sounds had become more pleasant. They nodded but said nothing to Tonia, as if they were simply acknowledging something that was always supposed to happen. Tonia put away the machine and pushed it away. She knew she was neither a scholar nor a smith, and she would not leave any signature or adage on her work, like the ones on the plaques hung up in the town hall. Even in such a remote town, in the most ordinary workshop, the people only spoke of the strongest and most worthy to be remembered. However, Tonia heard the weak and strong sounds just the same. Even the tiniest tremolo could not escape her.
Tonia felt herself stripped from familiar society and systems, layer by layer—on the results board at school, in the soundfield accident that snowy night... Sometimes she felt she had gotten used to the things that happened to her. What other choice was there? But she was happy, for the soundfield in the square was now in harmony, and she saw a few fowlbeasts perch on the station's window sill, a sight she had not seen for a while.
'How to get the musical Arts on the murals to resonate better with the cries of fowlbeasts... I should come back tomorrow and re-tune it.'
Tonia thought as she pushed the tuner on the way back.

'Is this... music theory? Or some kind of performance instruction?'
At the operator's question, Akkord realized she had dropped her old notebook. The operator who picked it up was reading through it with admiration in her eyes. The cover of the notebook was so worn that it had become glossy, while the edges of the pages had curled up from frequent turning. Akkord felt a tinge of embarrassment, unsure whether to take the notebook back, or answer the question.
'The wind swirling in the notches of the stone spires creates sounds that do not belong to the original tune. If they are not eliminated, they could spread through the town along the cracks of the spire.'
'Music flowing through the seams of copper tubes may become sharpened due to contraction in the cold. Mixing in wooden harmonies will make it less piercing.'
'In rainy season, the rhythms caused by water dripping at the old clock tower may distort the soundfield, requiring regular maintenance, or passages with a different texture to counterbalance it...'
Only a few wall lights remained on in the archives, casting their light on the paper. The operator read through the notebook carefully with curiosity: There was nothing like music theory or intricate formulae, but only casually written tips and guidelines, combining Arts knowledge and everyday experience.
'Just some informal adjustment tricks. Nothing significant,' answered Akkord.
'But these are really useful! They would be great teaching materials. Not that I know much about music, but I know you always use musical Arts in the right situations, without any clashing melodies...'
Teaching materials? Akkord was not listening to the latter half of what the operator was saying. She was thinking that such teaching materials were unneeded in Leithanien, as there were no special Arts in the notes, nor would they be considered musical creations. On this ship, however, someone was reading them quietly under the lights, even treating them as genuine knowledge.
Akkord recalled the nights in Zwillingstürme, how the nameless tuners restored the harmony of the city's soundfield. Now, on this behemoth far away from home, she realized that these experiences, which she thought nobody cared about, could at least make other tuners feel less lonely.
'Can I try tuning the musical equipment in my room by following your notes?'
The sound coming from beside her pulled Akkord back from the city's music to the Rhodes Island archive room. She smiled bashfully and nodded. Perhaps, these experiences she thought nobody cared about would spread even beyond the tuners.

[Audio Log]
'...On the count of three, we'll start singing together.'
'One, two, three—'
'......'
'Goodness, who just went up into the atmosphere?'
'It wasn't me... Wait, maybe it was? Sorry, I always seem to lose the key when I'm nervous.'
'Heh, I wish I brought earplugs!'
'Stop laughing, you sang even worse than I did! You dragged me off-key!'
'Alright, alright. None of you were especially in harmony just now.'
'Yeah, I know we're tone-deaf, Akkord...'
'I was talking about the hesitation in your voices. Try think it this way: When you're out of tune, you're just in different positions. Some go up, some go down, some go here, some go there. And that's what gives a song its range, right?'
'The audience must see us as a flock of squawking fowlbeasts.'
'Fowlbeasts seem so in harmony when they're together, don't they? I don't think they discuss how to sing beforehand, or care about how others want them to sing. They just sing the way they want.'
'Is it really the same thing?'
'Of course.'
'......'
'How do you want us to sing, then, Akkord? We're performing in front of the whole ship in one hour.'
'Sing what you can. It's my job to get these different voices in different positions together in the same place without stepping on each other's toes.'
'Isn't that... cheating?'
'No, I'm simply reigning in stray sounds and getting them to walk together. You have a bright soprano, but you're too scared to let it come out. You, you have a solid bass like a rock. No need to be scared, I'll catch it. As for you, you have a beautiful tone, and you're the one who put your heart and soul into these lyrics. All you need to do is sing what you want to express.'
'Are you really talking about us, Akkord? You make it sound as though... all of us could be useful.'
'Not just useful. Indispensable. You all enjoyed the process of writing the song, didn't you? You stand here now because you love it. All you need to do is sing what you love. Besides, Maestro Czerny wrote this song for you to sing together.'
'What if it still sounds bad?'
'All the more reason to sing out loud, so that no one can ignore how bad it sounds. Of course, I'll probably have to go with you to beg for permission to hold another event...'
'Haha... alright, let's try again?'
'Let's try again. All you need to do is open your mouths. Leave the rest to me.'

modules.moduleName: The Music Box of A Burdenbeast
modules.moduleDescription:
The fields of northern Leithanien are shrouded in a thin blue mist come evening time. The wind blows gently, sending the white flowers scattered across the meadows tumbling as they please.
Tonia has come to gather flowers in place of the town pharmacist, imbuing their petals with pleasant music. They were exceedingly simple Arts, requiring only the marking of miniature symbols into the petals' vasculature. As they sway in the wind, the flowers will play a lingering melody. She crouches down, placing the imbued flowers into her basket one after the other.
An aged burdenbeast strolls by the pasture fence, approaching the basket for a sniff before immediately munching on one of the imbued flowers. There is no time for Tonia to stop it. All she can do is listen to the notes spilling out of its throat. After a few steps forward, it too seems to realize that the sound is emanating from its own body. It stops and swivels its ears, constantly letting out brays of its own as it tries to respond to this miraculous melody. The notes warble as the tune is pushed out of its mouth by its breathing, thrumming to the beat of its slow steps under the darkening sky.
It is not long before the stockbeasts in the pasture lift their heads in agitation. They soon calm down, gathering by the one musical burdenbeast, but rather than seeming like they are following a leader, it is more like they have recognized a sensation they have not felt in a very long time: the calm before the snowstorm, the crackling of melting streams, and the touch of a refreshingly warm breeze under the afternoon sun. The ranch owner pushes open the door, intending to disperse the gathering, but upon seeing the odd serenity, he stops. The wind, the stamping of hooves, and the distant cries of fowlbeasts are all mellowed by the gentle melody.
Tonia stands by the field. She had meant to return to the pharmacist already, to hand in the flowers and complete her task. But now, she watches the aged burdenbeast as if it were some clumsy musician, slowly performing in the twilight. There is no grand opera at play here, only scattered, isolated voices that have found each other once more. Here and now, they have become the language of the land thanks to this chance reunion.
The flowers' melody was only meant to have played for a moment in the wind, but within the burdenbeast's body, the notes seem to have found a new path to follow. As the curtain of night falls, they deepen and soften. Tonia suddenly realizes she has forgotten to record this new melody. But she also feels that, even if the petals have melted away within the burdenbeast, the notes shall not fade. They will remain in the memory of the herd, like a seed hidden within the flowing of the wind, the stillness of the snow, and between the breaths of the fields.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: The data from Experiment 36? Second cabinet from the left, in the blue folder. The error report? The document at the very top of the pile behind you. As for the mathematical formulae, they are in the left drawer of your desk. Are there any other files you need? Please, feel free to ask for my help.

Please don't mind me, Rhodes Island's laboratories are excellent, and there have been zero issues with the equipment. I keep rearranging it because… Ahem, I never thought I would have a workbench of my own again.

Oh! My apologies for bumping into you, my glasses fogged up suddenly… I thought I could walk back to my workbench like this, but I was carrying so many things, I had no free hand to wipe my glasses. I'll just stand here until they clear up…

Do I need help? No, I am fine, I know how to key data into the terminal. It's just that… Once this data is in the terminal's system, others can delete it or classify it with a press of a button. Writing it down on paper allows me to feel a little more relaxed.

The polar nights of Ursus are near-endless, to the degree that even if I were to light every lamp, I would still find myself yearning desperately for the tiniest sliver of daylight, the faintest glimmer of hope. Perhaps I followed you here thinking only of proving myself more than a failure in life.

Back in the Far North, I thought that by following you, I would escape that endless expanse of ice and snow. Even if I were to leave a suicide note, it would have only made for kindling. I had to go with you. You people are mad for doing what you did in Ursus. But perhaps I, too, have long fallen to madness.

Back in Chernobog, Professor Ilia would try to cram knowledge into my brain as quickly as possible, Director Kal'tsit and the others would perform their calculations without rest, while every day I lived in fear of the punishments I would suffer for any mistake… Who would have thought those would be the best days of my life?

'The youngest of the genius researchers'. I once held such a title with pride, but if you were to swing a pick anywhere in the Far North and break the frozen earth, you would find the Originium dust the corpses of those geniuses have become. At times, I am glad I managed to escape that place... but have I truly escaped?

Alcohol is a fine thing. It warms the body and dulls the mind, and you need not think about whatever is happening outside... It is too warm here, and I do not rely on it to get through the day now. What should I rely on next, Doctor? Can you tell me?
I am simply transcribing some data, and you have fallen asleep. Is the sound of my writing really so soothing?
I thank all of Rhodes Island, Doctor, for taking me in, and I also thank you for… giving me a laboratory where I will not be disturbed.
It seems I am not the only one giving everything to survive. Everyone does the same.
Receiving such a formal memo scared me half to death, but thankfully, it was not a directive to cease my experiments… You have my deepest gratitude, Doctor. I shall continue with my research.

I have been looking for you all day, Doctor. Look, my paper was published in a Columbian journal. My research is heading in the right direction! Huh? I am smiling, am I…? It seems I truly am happy now.
The materials are ready.
I am to oversee this project? Understood.
Readings are coming through… Beginning recording and graphing.
Remember, sample the data every twenty minutes.
What is your hypothesis?
Do you have a new conjecture?
Control group ready.
Initiating data collection.
Removing outliers.
Calculating standard deviation.
Marking significant trends.
Performing data derivation.
L-Look, Doctor! We succeeded! Has… Has the day finally come?
The hypothesis holds. The report will be on your desk shortly.
I will begin investigating the error at once. You may put your faith in me.
A failure? No, no, no, how could this be? Please, a little more time! I promise no more problems next time!
Such a warm room…
Oh?! Sorry, I thought you were someone else. Forgive me for hitting you with that file…
Would you care for a warm cup of tea?
Arknights.

We never celebrated this holiday when I was at the research institute. The passage of time held no special meaning to us, aside from the little headway we were making on our projects. But now… I wish to believe it means the day I see results is all the more closer.
Hello, Doctor. The experiment is proceeding smoothly. Here. I used hot tea to keep my mind clear and warm myself back in Ursus.

While I do think preparing a birthday present for my superior is somewhat odd, it is still something I would like to do. It was you who gave me the hope I needed to continue with my research, starting when you chose to enter that mine in search of remaining specimens… I have been grateful to you ever since.

Here at Rhodes Island, my research enjoys success after success, and the sick benefit from better medicines developed on my results. The fact that these things actually happen here has swept me off my feet countless times… Seeing my work come to fruition, and how it makes this place a better one, has left me greatly satisfied.

Arknights.

We never celebrated this holiday when I was at the research institute. The passage of time held no special meaning to us, aside from the little headway we were making on our projects. But now… I wish to believe it means the day I see results is all the more closer.
Hello, Doctor. The experiment is proceeding smoothly. Here. I used hot tea to keep my mind clear and warm myself back in Ursus.

While I do think preparing a birthday present for my superior is somewhat odd, it is still something I would like to do. It was you who gave me the hope I needed to continue with my research, starting when you chose to enter that mine in search of remaining specimens… I have been grateful to you ever since.

Here at Rhodes Island, my research enjoys success after success, and the sick benefit from better medicines developed on my results. The fact that these things actually happen here has swept me off my feet countless times… Seeing my work come to fruition, and how it makes this place a better one, has left me greatly satisfied.

RUS.voiceText: The data from Experiment 36? Second cabinet from the left, in the blue folder. The error report? The document at the very top of the pile behind you. As for the mathematical formulae, they are in the left drawer of your desk. Are there any other files you need? Please, feel free to ask for my help.

Please don't mind me, Rhodes Island's laboratories are excellent, and there have been zero issues with the equipment. I keep rearranging it because… Ahem, I never thought I would have a workbench of my own again.

Oh! My apologies for bumping into you, my glasses fogged up suddenly… I thought I could walk back to my workbench like this, but I was carrying so many things, I had no free hand to wipe my glasses. I'll just stand here until they clear up…

Do I need help? No, I am fine, I know how to key data into the terminal. It's just that… Once this data is in the terminal's system, others can delete it or classify it with a press of a button. Writing it down on paper allows me to feel a little more relaxed.

The polar nights of Ursus are near-endless, to the degree that even if I were to light every lamp, I would still find myself yearning desperately for the tiniest sliver of daylight, the faintest glimmer of hope. Perhaps I followed you here thinking only of proving myself more than a failure in life.

Back in the Far North, I thought that by following you, I would escape that endless expanse of ice and snow. Even if I were to leave a suicide note, it would have only made for kindling. I had to go with you. You people are mad for doing what you did in Ursus. But perhaps I, too, have long fallen to madness.

Back in Chernobog, Professor Ilia would try to cram knowledge into my brain as quickly as possible, Director Kal'tsit and the others would perform their calculations without rest, while every day I lived in fear of the punishments I would suffer for any mistake… Who would have thought those would be the best days of my life?

'The youngest of the genius researchers'. I once held such a title with pride, but if you were to swing a pick anywhere in the Far North and break the frozen earth, you would find the Originium dust the corpses of those geniuses have become. At times, I am glad I managed to escape that place... but have I truly escaped?

Alcohol is a fine thing. It warms the body and dulls the mind, and you need not think about whatever is happening outside... It is too warm here, and I do not rely on it to get through the day now. What should I rely on next, Doctor? Can you tell me?
I am simply transcribing some data, and you have fallen asleep. Is the sound of my writing really so soothing?
I thank all of Rhodes Island, Doctor, for taking me in, and I also thank you for… giving me a laboratory where I will not be disturbed.
It seems I am not the only one giving everything to survive. Everyone does the same.
Receiving such a formal memo scared me half to death, but thankfully, it was not a directive to cease my experiments… You have my deepest gratitude, Doctor. I shall continue with my research.

I have been looking for you all day, Doctor. Look, my paper was published in a Columbian journal. My research is heading in the right direction! Huh? I am smiling, am I…? It seems I truly am happy now.
The materials are ready.
I am to oversee this project? Understood.

archives:
[Onboarding Memo]
To Medical: Please be aware that we previously found a large quantity of vodka and sedatives in Operator Snegurochka's luggage during security checks.
—HR Operator

[Health Examination Memo]
Operator Snegurochka's health checkup revealed nothing out of the ordinary, but she showed clear signs of evading my gaze during psychological evaluation. I added two assessments because of this, but failed to find any issues. All her answers indicate that she is emotionally stable.
Out of respect for patient privacy, we have limited our actions to general advice. We will continue to maintain communications in follow-up work.
—Medical Operator
[Addendum]
Snegurochka admitted that she was very on edge during the period after she joined Rhodes Island.
The vodka she hid in her luggage was discovered by security personnel on her first day, while Medical bombarded her with questions to evaluate her psychological condition during her health examination the very next day. She understood full well that our intentions were not malicious, as well as why we asked those questions, but she was afraid that revealing her true self would result in rejection.
She could not admit to others that she drank enough coffee to throw up on a daily basis in order to stimulate herself. Or that only the pain caused by the reaction between vodka and sedatives could trigger her survival instincts when she is most depressed. While this is undoubtedly harmful to her body, controlling dosage is exactly what her job entails, and she is very good at it, for better or worse. As such, she spends her days between extreme alacrity and deep stupor, acting the part of a normal person who is only a little bit depressed, a little bit muddled.
She knew full well what kind of diagnosis our questions would lead to, and so she avoided any answers that could lead to the 'wrong' result, despite promising to answer truthfully.
She had to act normal and ordinary, just like she did in the labs.
—Record from counseling interview 11

Snegurochka has been sober for a week.
At the lab, she used to spend half of her salary on vodka, driving to the sole liquor shop within twenty km on her only day off of the week. One crate of 750ml vodka would last her just about one week.
Before she came to Rhodes Island, she knew that we had a bar, but feared that its offerings would not be strong enough for her needs. Therefore, outside of a few everyday items that were absolutely necessary, she spent the rest of her luggage allowance on distilled vodka.
She found her decision justified the first time she passed by Just One More Pint. The mood at the door was sweet and slightly tipsy, a far cry from the powerful, sledgehammer-like feeling of Ursine pubs. So she swore an oath to herself never to set foot inside.
Giving up on Just One More Pint meant that Snegurochka had to ration her vodka carefully. Rhodes Island was nowhere near as stressful as the lab, and she worked half the hours she used to. She would not need to paralyze herself with alcohol quite so much, so she should be able to cut her drinking by half, meaning the two crates of vodka she brought would last her a month, giving her enough time to find new supplies...
Her plan soon hit a rock. Apparently, stress was not the only cause of her alcoholism, and with Rhodes Island's shorter hours, she found she had that much more time to drink. With her usual habit of spending all her time off work drinking, the vodka she had counted on lasting a month was gone in two weeks.
For a full week, Snegurochka went without alcohol. She was in a daze, and often wondered if she had actually been drinking, for she felt as though she had a constant hangover and wanted to throw up, even though the only thing she drank was water.

Exhausted and leaning against the wall, she stood before the bar that she once looked down on, reason and craving locked in a desperate inner struggle.
'Snegurochka? Would you like something?'
A gentle voice extended an olive branch.
'I...'
Snegurochka slowly raised a finger—
She took a deep breath, and a sweet scent mixed with the aroma of alcohol filled her nostrils.
'I... No, I'm trying to quit drinking.'
The proud, stubborn Ursine resolutely walked towards the Medical Department.

Snegurochka was assigned a corner by the wall at her own request.
Unlike the messy desks of other operators, her desk is immaculately clean. As though it does not belong to her, she never places any private items on it, and only uses disposable paper cups for water.
This may seem strange to the operators of Rhodes Island, but it would be perfectly normal in the labs of Ursus, where junior researchers are not given their own desks. It is quite common for several researchers to huddle around a single tiny wooden desk. Sometimes, during an animated discussion, someone might say, 'Let's talk over at that desk,' which was her cue to exit the discussion and return to the instruments with her notebook, pretending to be writing down the readings.
Snegurochka had no idea what to do with this two-meter-long desk. The files went into the cabinet next to it, while her notebook came with her to her room at the end of the day. She had gotten too accustomed to standing in front of the instruments all day, running tests while reading her colleagues' papers.
She began observing her new colleagues' desks, hoping to find inspiration. Some have practically built a wall out of experiment documents, some have a small potted plant on their desks, while others have a rack of the latest music records... She managed to persuade herself that not all places are as dull and oppressed as Ursus. Perhaps there was something she could do to make her desk her own.
Three months after she joined Rhodes Island, Snegurochka mustered the courage to put something belonging to herself on the desk—a bright, custom-made sun lamp.
Warm light filled the room when she turned it on for the first time, and she found her heart finally settling for the first time.
She likes the sun, as a matter of fact, and if asked again would not have chosen this dark corner by the wall.

'What game will we play today, Ksenia—'
'No games today.'
Ksenia frowns and looks up at the sky beyond the walls, a thick pile of documents in her hands.
'Did they kick you out again?'
'...Yeah.'
'It's alright, Ksenia. They didn't let me join either—'
'We're different, Lyudmila. You're still a child.
'Meanwhile, I've been chosen by the empire. I should be striving to work on even more complex projects and achieve results that will impress everyone.'
'You're not even that much older than me. One, two, three...'
Lyudmila looks at her hands, but she did not pay attention in math class a few days ago, and cannot figure out what the number is.
Ksenia gazes at the tightly-shut window of the lab, and mutters at a volume only she can hear—
'Next time, I'll make sure I get the answer.'
...
'You know about Kal'tsit's death?'
Lyudmila leans against the wall, gazing at Ksenia, who is standing in front of Kal'tsit's desk.
The setting sun shines through the window into Kal'tsit's office. Ksenia stands in the shadows, and Lyudmila cannot see her expression.
'I heard they hid it from you because they were worried you wouldn't take it well.
'No need for you to feel anger or regret. All I wanted was to see her face-to-face, but even when I did, she never gave me a straight answer.
'Our questions were never answered.'
'No... I don't have any questions for her.'
Ksenia's answer surprised Lyudmila.
'I stood here for a long time, thinking long and hard about what I wanted to ask her, but never found the answer.
'I'm a researcher, an independent academic. When I have a question, I should let the data provide me the answer. Director Kal'tsit's the one who taught me that.
'As for my life... In the days since I left Chernobog, I realized that my failure wasn't her fault, nor your father's. It was only because of my own incompetence...'
'Why can't it be Ursus's fault?!'
Lyudmila interrupts Ksenia, glaring at her.
'Everyone in Ursus—you, me, my father... we all walked the wrong path for too long.
'I had so many questions I wanted her to answer, but then she was just gone.'
'You seem angry, Lyudmila.'
Ksenia takes a step forward, and Lyudmila finally sees her face.
'...And you're crying, Ksenia.
'What exactly did we go through, all these years?'

modules.moduleDescription:
Ksenia,
I have reviewed your report on the physical nature of the Sarcophagus.
There were no issues with the way the experiment was conducted, and the selection of control groups was appropriate. The reason you failed to get the results you expected was because of certain biases in the direction of the experiment.
However, I do not see anything associated with the Sarcophagus in your recent schedule. Based on your equipment and system access logs, I have reason to believe that this experiment was not conducted with the approval of Ilia, your supervisor.
This is dangerous and ill-advised, Ksenia.
As a graduate of the Imperial College of Science and Engineering, you must be aware that those with high intelligence have a tendency towards becoming trapped by their own obsessions. The cutting edge of science has no shortage of madmen.
Sarcophagus research is still in its infancy, its potential and risks unclear. We do not yet know what it can bring us. For the safety of the experiment, as well as your own, I am revoking your high-level privileges and denying you access to the associated data.
Do not take this as a denial of your abilities. On the contrary, I fear you will make a breakthrough and find yourself trapped.
Ilia and I have spent much time discussing your development. Your university research focused on energy applications because the ICSE reassigned you to that major, and you accepted their plan. It is exactly the reason Ilia chose you. Too many researchers here have eyes only for that ultimate laurel, a place in the history of theoretical science, without consideration for the kind of impact their results will have on the people who live upon this land.
As a scientist, you are conscientious and bold, but sometimes prone to impatience. Enclosed you will find a research project that I have worked on for many years, but never managed to finish. Feel free to pick it up where I left off. You will earn the gratitude of far more than just myself, if you are able to make a breakthrough.
You are still young, and your career just begun. Have patience, and take heart.
—Kal'tsit

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: Thirty-two, then thirty... three? Oh, Doctor? Wait, where was I? Hmm, I've been away half an hour? No worries, almost done. The fiftieth document from the left... one, two... don't worry, I'm the best counter at my escort association.

In this line of work, encountering odd clients comes with the territory. There was this one time when I was hired to escort a gentleman, he insisted I carry him on my back down a muddy road. I agreed, but said only after terminating our escort contract, because I couldn't defend him while carrying someone on my back.

Doctor, take some of these. My family came by during their escort job and brought me some treats from back home. What? We're under attack? Wait, you mean... them? Uh, hey, don't smoke on the landship. Put your shoes on and mind your manners! Don't glare at people like that! Ahem, Doctor... let me introduce you to my family.

I'll ask the local bandit boss about the situation here. No, we're not exactly friends, but we sort of pay this toll of theirs. Does that sound like we're in cahoots with the bandits? Hahah, it's just a way we can both make a living. Nobody wants unnecessary bloodshed, if we can help it.

I got the crystals on my hand from a highwayman. His legs were shaking and I thought I could talk him out of it, but his mind was made up. When I discarded his Originium explosive, we both got caught in the blast. In the end, I left him some money for his sick child's treatment. As for my own condition, I got used to it long ago.

Not every bandit manages to make the move to an honest escort life. Some have walked the way of the bandit for too long to change, many of them were aunts and uncles who watched me grow up. I couldn't look them in the eye when I had to show them out, but people must keep moving forward, right?

What are you eating? Give me a bite; I haven't eaten yet. Ran into a righteous volunteer on the way, he was collecting relief funds for his hometown that got hit by a Catastrophe, so I gave him all my money. A scam? Maybe, but I don't need more money than I can spend, and I can always sock him if it turns out he was lying. It's not like I'll ever starve with you around.

My swords? This one was given by my adoptive mother. The other was hers—she threw it in my face the day she left. The blood was everywhere. I had tried to convince her to retire from banditry and join the escort business, but she saw it as a betrayal. People... when goals differ, they are quick to call it treachery. She raised me, after all.

Once I no longer have to worry about the escort association, I want to go wander the jianghu, to see what's out there. Want to come along, Doctor? Where to? Haven't thought about it yet. What matters is wandering free like a fowlbeast, traveling only with my two swords, drawing them at the first sign of injustice, and drinking and singing to my heart's delight.

Want some dried plums, Doctor? I always eat one when I get sleepy on the night shift. A piece of green plum with no sugar added works better than pinching my thigh. Haha, look at your face! You look like the plum just bit you.

You're the Doctor of Rhodes Island? I've heard so much about you. I sign this, and you'll be an official friend of Windscoot. Any help you might need, just— er... no, I know how to write my name. It's—where do I sign?
My eyelids, they're stuck... Doc, just step on my tail. It's fine, just stomp!
Just like when I wore my escort association's badge for the first time. Gotta keep my head bowed and tail tucked. I won't let you lose face, Doc!

There was this time I picked up a cloudbeast on a solo escort mission. We traveled together for a while. But just before entering the city, I set it free, afraid customers might see it and think I was soft. Now, I suppose I wouldn't be afraid to keep such a companion.
Three bulkies, twelve mid-sized… all set. Huh, why is there one more here? Did I count wrong?
Everyone, keep an eye open, your sword at hand and uniform on. Safety first.
The fortune stick reads 'very lucky'! Only took one, two... five draws to get it. What a good sign! Let's go!
They've got guts, coming at us like this. Don't they recognize our banner? Guess we're in for a fight.
Just tell me which one to cleave.
Just tell me where to go.
In position. Awaiting your command.
Give the signal and I'll do it.
Don't pick a fight if you're not prepared to get punched.
A few broken bones would be a good lesson for you.
Want my goods, none; else my life, one. Come and take it if you dare!
I've already drawn my swords. You can beg for your life after we've fought.
We're friends for life from this day on, Doctor. One word from you and I'll rush to your aid, even if I'm on the other side of Terra—that's a promise.
The goods are intact, and everyone's unhurt! Ahhh, damn it!—I've dreamed of having such a reliable escort leader as you, Doctor.

Look at him run! He even lost his shoes, hahaha! As long as the goods are safe, that's all that matters. Bandits never forget an ass-kicking. Next time they hear our association's escort chant, they'll stay far away.
I'll keep them at bay while you go get backup. Want my goods? Over my dead body!

handbook.profile: Windscoot does year-round armed escort work in Shangshu and its surrounding areas in Yan. He came to Rhodes Island for Oripathy treatment, and signed a cooperation agreement to expand his escort business, providing medicine transportation and talent recommendation services to Rhodes Island.

basicInfo.title: Infection Status
basicInfo.value: Originium crystals distributed across surface of body, confirmed Infected by medical examination.

handbook.clinicalAnalysis:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 4%
Small distribution of Originium crystals can be seen on the left hand.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.14u/L
Operator Windscoot seldom comes into contact with Originium, and does a good job at keeping his condition under control.

Operator Windscoot attended our Originium Protection Course on time, and earnestly took down many notes despite his difficulty doing so. Apparently, he has a group of people to teach what he's learned here.
—A Medic Operator
handbook.promotionRecord: 'A-Ahem! Uncles and aunties, if you insist on having the youth chime in, then look at these two numbers on the wall. Which one is bigger, and by how much?' 'That's 1 above and 5 below. 5's obviously bigger than 1!' 'Bah, you should be looking at the first number. 4 on top, 3 below. Top one's bigger!' 'Hahaha! Makes sense. Well, I won't keep you all guessing. The numbers above are the Gang of Justice's income for the year, while the numbers below are the escort firm's.' 'Aiya! Which one's bigger then?!' 'Look, isn't the bottom number longer than the one on top? Our escort firm earns way more than when we were still in the gang. Almost ten times as much! ...Basically, it's a TON of money! Look, everyone. It's possible to walk the right path and have a good life! ...Y-You guys agree, right?' The dinner table observes a moment of silence before bursting into laughter. 'Hahaha! Just look at this brat, working his ass off because he's scared we'll go back to being bandits! I hope you aren't spending all your time worrying about that?!' '...Haha, of course not. I'll drink first as a toast to all your hard work in the coming year!' —A conversation from the escort firm's annual new year's eve dinner
archives:
[Rhodes Island Assistance Log]
Rhodes Island's Medical Department received an unusual request for help. A patient had given up on her plans to continue school in Leithanien, but received a sum of money this morning from an unknown source, accompanied by a note haphazardly filled with misspellings of 'Schulgeld'—'Tuition fees' in Leithanian.
Oddly enough, she asked her acquaintances for any information on where the money came from, to no avail. We later came to learn that the only time she might bump into a stranger is when she practices her violin every morning.
So on the next day, we tried waiting by the open space where she was practicing, just to see if her benefactor would show up. As the violin played, a window from the adjacent Training Room opened up. We ran over and looked in, only to startle Operator Windscoot, who was quietly training.
'Ah... hah, I don't get music, but I like it. My tail goes everywhere every time I hear her violin, like I'm tipsy. So when I heard she couldn't further her studies, I just impulsively...'
The investigation into this international act of chivalry stopped here, with a gratifying finale: The patient accepted Windscoot's assistance, and they both agreed he would get his money back in a few years, with Rhodes Island serving as the intermediary. Windscoot also sincerely accepted our boss's criticism over this small disturbance. This was actually not the first time he had done a quiet act of 'charity'!
'When you're always wandering, upholding justice is the name of the game.' Operator Windscoot spread out his hands like it was the natural thing to do, with no apparent intention to reflect on his headstrong actions.

SOMETHING BIG IN STORE?!
Additionally, the infamous Gang of Justice, known for their efficient intimidation tactics and record of 32 robberies in three days without a single casualty under their belt, has not attempted any robberies for 15 days straight. An informant who wishes to remain anonymous claims a Gang of Justice member told him they're about to 'score big', but no one knows what the gang has in store, when other gangs have been keeping a low profile with the current spotlight on highway robbery investigations.
—Excerpt from the first March issue of 'Shancheng's Jianghu tip-offs'

TURNING A NEW LEAF OR UP TO SOMETHING WORSE?
A new flag with 'Escort' written on it hangs at the foot of a mountain, and behind it stands a group of fierce, familiar faces—members of the Gang of Justice who claimed they would 'score big'. Are these brigands possibly planning to pivot into armed escort work?! This writer approached them to pose the question, only to discover their fee is abnormally low for such services. Is this a front for something more sinister? Will their clients find their pockets emptied after taking up their cheap offer?
—Excerpt from the third March issue of 'Shancheng's Jianghu tip-offs'

MYSTERIOUS FELINE RETURNS
After two weeks, the Gang of Justice's escort team has returned to the foot of the mountain. The former bandits actually handed over the entrusted goods to the consignee and received their reward without any shenanigans? It is worth noting that the escort team is led by a young yet unfamiliar face, absent from the history of the gang's various activities. An informant tells us this person used to live with the gang, goes by 'Windscoot' in the jianghu, and returned to the gang after having left for several years. Is this individual related to the Gang of Justice's sudden transformation from bandits into a formal escort firm? This writer shall continue to keep a close eye on the matter.
—Excerpt from the second April issue of 'Shancheng's Jianghu tip-offs'

The merchant frowned as he entered the escort firm. That's what they called it anyway, yet it looked like a bandit den. Idle escorts squatted on the ground, and their gazes made the merchant's hair stand on end. The young man who welcomed him is enthusiastic, but so clumsy that he struggled to even produce a shipping bill. The merchant had had enough, and turned around to leave. The young man chased him all the way to the front door, stammering a request for his business card, and promising the escort firm would improve within a month.
A month later, the young man actually showed up at the merchant's office, introducing the escort firm in a green but practiced manner. With trust and doubt evenly matched in his mind, the merchant followed the young man back. As he walked through the door, he heard the young man cough right before two rows of bodyguards greeted him with a unified roar and their backs bent 90 degrees.
Floored by their sincerity, the merchant began working with them. On his third visit, he ran into a client stirring up trouble, who seemed to be waving his unsigned bill, flatly denying that the delivery happened. The troublemaker provoked the young man by saying: 'Hit me, then! Or are you scared? Spineless coward!' The young man's brows knit tighter and he suddenly raised a fist—to apologize, and even compensate the troublemaker. The client grabbed the compensation fee, sighed, and left disappointed. Only then did the young man realize that what the other party wanted was not just monetary compensation.
'I didn't realize what he wanted, but... I decided I'd try my best to avoid resorting to violence to solve my problems.' The young man smiled awkwardly.
Was that a professional scammer sent to bully the young escort agency? Or someone from their peers in the industry trying to challenge them? No one knew. Anyway, when the merchant contacted the escort firm again, he found out the young man had given every escort team leader a terminal. They also straightened out their handover process—confirm and sign, every step now flowing as easily as one breathes. The escort firm born from a bandit den had metamorphosed into a proper business.
The merchant could not help but ask: 'How did you manage all that? I mean like, everything.'
The young man who had always managed to handle everything with ease now scratched his head, lost in thought, unsure where to begin.

[Operator Windscoot's Personal History]
Age 2: Picked up by a gang, with the day they picked me up treated as my birthday.
Age 10: They begged the school down the mountain for half a day until they finally let me study there. Later, I helped the weak wherever I went, handled my classmates who were being bullies, but was treated as the top bully and expelled.
Age 11 to 17: Too embarrassed to return to the gang, I wandered the jianghu.
Age 18: Heard rumors that the gang back home was opening an escort firm, so I rushed back. I've been working there ever since.

When we questioned Windscoot about the details, he showed a cheerful candidness unique to jianghu adventurers. His mouth twists experiences unworthy of celebration into interesting tales, and it often drew laughter from us. However, when we were organizing our records later, we realized there was still a blank period between his return home and the escort firm's founding. We had indeed asked about that, and he seemed to... just when did he skip over the questions?

[Collection details of a certain Yanese agency]
By chance we obtained a payment record showing that Windscoot had paid off fines for several captured bandits. These bandits seem to belong to the gang that took him in when he was a toddler, but their names do not appear in the escort firm's employee roster.

[Rhodes Island Weapon Maintenance Log]
'Can you not tell the difference between your blades? Why do you always send the same one to me?'
'I maintain the other one myself. Oh, don't get me wrong, it's not that I don't trust your craft. It's just, the other blade's owner is super fierce and nitpicky. She once gave me a beating when she wasn't satisfied. And I mean a real beatdown!'
'Huh, so the other blade isn't yours?'
'I'm just keeping it safe for now. One day I'll be able to return it.'

modules.moduleDescription:
After a huge ruckus, the two elders from Gang of Justice reluctantly depart, leaving the place in a mess—wooden chairs smashed over heads, shattered windows broken with bodies, and their iconic wooden sign on the door with 'Yi', or 'justice', written on it, now split into two pieces stuck in the ground.
'Anyone who was injured should head inside to get patched up. Everyone else help me clean up the mess. If any of our customers see this, they're going to be scared away.' Windscoot says this as he takes the lead and grabs a broom with one hand, his other pressing on a cut on his forearm.
'Hey, kid. You're the one who should go get patched up. If you hadn't blocked that blow for me, my head would've been split open.'
'It's just a little cut, I'm not afraid of blood—okay, okay! Enough glaring at me, uncle. I'll go wrap it up once I'm done cleaning.'
The former bandits begin to clumsily clean up the mess. Today their 'escort agency' has far less members than when they were bandits, and the situation seems much more somber after this bout of chaos. Someone picks up the broken 'Yi' and says: 'Are we gonna toss our Justice away just like that?'
Windscoot takes the broken sign and sighs without speaking. The Gang of Justice had broken up, and the escort agency's business was unlikely to improve. Was everything he had done so far the right thing to do?
'Hey,' The uncle jabs at him, 'You did nothing wrong. It was those two who extorted our customers. If they'd carried on with it, it would've been hard for us to continue this line of work.'
'Exactly! I finally learned to read a few words recently too. Wouldn't it all go to waste if our agency goes bankrupt?!'
'And all those super-hard-to-remember passcodes too!'
'Don't get me even started. Those damn traffic rules keep giving me fines round the clock! I won't forgive anyone who makes all my effort go to waste!'
'Haha, isn't that because you're too dumb?'
The crowd chats about the efforts they've put into their new lives, filling the air with laughs. Windscoot unfurrows his brow, and pats his own head, as if trying to expel the hesitation within himself.
The next day, the wooden 'Yi' sign appears again at the escort agency's entrance.
'For now, I just stuck them back together with some nails. I'll make a new one when I have time.' Windscoot returns to his usual cheerful tone.
'Nah, don't bother! This is a pretty unique look. Look at the top and bottom halves—now they're joined even closer than before!'
'Exactly, isn't it the trend these days to have, uh, a logo or whatever? We should trademark it!' Sounds of agreement follow.
'Really? I'll go find someone to turn it into an actual logo then, and print it on our clothes and gear. But remember: you asked for this, so no refusing to wear your future uniforms.'
Windscoot's beaming smile draws a crowd of complaints. Learning to write up orders, practicing martial arts, keeping proper accounts—everyone is busy getting the escort agency on the right track.

CN_MANDARIN.voiceText: You want me to help you sort these files? Alright... And double check the numbers too? Sure, leave it to me.

Wow... There's a lot of people heading up on deck... What? Someone jumped off the bridge and they're organizing a rescue? But I didn't see anything like that when I was flying... W-Wait, they might be looking for me! Ohhh no, I've gotta clean up this mess! How am I gonna explain...?

Have you ever seen the land stars, Doctor? When I was flying over the frontier, the scattered bonfires were like stars sprinkled across the wilderness. Animals migrate to find a new place to live, but those Pioneers... I wonder if they dream of a nice, warm home?

Yes, this is a monitoring device. l'll stick it onto a fowlbeast, and then adjust the rhythm of my breathing to the data it sends over. That way, I won't disturb the flock while I'm flying. Ah, sorry, I'm babbling again... Umm... Any other questions, Doctor?

As a kid, I was really scared of the featherless monster fowls in the stories. They were always snatching up children. Even hearing the chirping of a real fowlbeast got me shaking. But after the first time I got plucked off the ground for real, after I got to see the whole land from above, I was never scared again. Um, you don't believe I got carried off by a fowlbeast? B-but it really did happen...

I learned some painful lessons on my first test flight. I lost my balance and almost flew straight into a cliff. It's all thanks to my glider that I survived. There's nothing left of it now, only these tattered strips of blue and purple. But I tie them on before every flight.

Once, I had an Originium slug pulled out of its shell and plopped down right in front of me. Can you guess who gave it to me? It was a mother fowlbeast hen. She decided I was one of her chicks, but I never saw her again once I left the forest... Well, I'll try to finish the slug soup, it's the least I can do.

I record my voice, so I can play it back to the fowlbeasts and get them to slowly see me as one of their own. 'Gah gah' means 'look at me', 'Ah-kah' is 'run away'… Hehe, it's all guesses, really, but you learned them pretty quick.

That's the entire pre-flight checklist. Come on, Doctor, I'll be taking you up for a quick loop around. Don't worry, no need to be scared, I'll hold you tight the whole way through. Eh? Ah, uh, no, wh-what I mean is... We'll be strapped together while we're flying, so you can relax. I'm not going to drop you.
Doctor, this file... Oh, you're asleep? Go ahead and rest up, then. I'll come back later.
Hello, Doctor, I'm Operator Contrail. Nice to meet you—you remember seeing a photo of me flying with a fowlbeast flock in the news? I-I'm glad you remember me…
On my next flight, I'll try this super-tricky barrel roll…
Thanks, Doctor... I love the medal. I'll hang it up with the pendants showcasing my successful test flights.
'Though it may fall a hundred thousand times, a chick still yearns for its first flight.' I've loved those words ever since I first read them. Doctor, do you think... I've grown?
Okay, I'll fly echelon.
Alright... I'll navigate then.
I'm not afraid.
Let me check the wind direction first.
Propulsion units and emergency ejection equipment, check. All systems go.
Ready for take-off.
In the pipe, five by five.
All units, watch for my signal.
Turbulence incoming.
On me, stay in formation.
Brace yourselves, cumulonimbus ahead.
Is that fog...? Oh, just condensation on my glasses.
A perfect flight record... Next time, we can try somewhere even further.
The two long white plumes up in the sky...? Yeah, those are mine.
Looks like there's still room for improvement... Maybe I should add a multi-speed pursuit module.
It's okay, Doctor... Anyone could run into a storm. Let's rest up for the night and try again when the weather clears.
The setting sun, some floating feathers, a sea of clouds stretching out into the distance... No, not a painting, it's the view out the window.
Oh, Doctor. Go right ahead…
There's a black cloud in the corner of the test flight photo? Th-That's my tail…
Arknights.

You're looking for peace and quiet on the deck too, Doctor? I'm still not too good with crowds, so I wrote all my New Year's greetings down on cards. I didn't have any other plans tonight, so I was just gonna stand here and look up at the night sky... Sure, we can look together.
I don't have any test flights planned for today, Doctor... You just wanted to chat? Alright, you've got my ear.

This multicolored, feathered wobble doll... It means you should live life to the fullest and never give up. Huh? No, I'm not saying you should get all round and, and, and plump like this, and I'm definitely not saying you're too stingy... Ummm, I'm sorry, I'm bad at picking out gifts... Oh... You were joking? You're teasing me again, Doctor...

Starting from Columbia, twisting and turning all the way to Rim Billiton. Rhodes Island's following a long and windy course, just like a migratory fowlbeast. I'll be your wingman, but more than the destination, I'm excited for what I'll find along the way. You too, right, Doctor?
